Eggers draws from the literature and seemingly all major screen adaptations of Stoker's novel to portray the definitive tale of the Vampyr.

Eggers and cinematographer Jarin Blaschke capture the gothic atmosphere on delicate 35mm film and turn Nosferatu from being merely visually stunning to a crawling seductive shadow. The relentless pace and score sail through the considerable runtime like the Plague-carrying ship crossing the stormy sea.

The ensemble cast bring a raw energetic dread that is freed from the often boring constraints of acting in period dramas. I must sing particularly the praises of Lily-Rose Depp and Bill Skarsgård who are entangled in a deadly dance from beginning to end.

If I may list but one single flaw, it's that Eggers' Nosferatu is victim of Hollywood's own plague: remakes. If you've seen the 1922 version, this treads (albeit with masterful craftmanship) the exact same beats. Thus, my decision to give 9/10 instead of a perfect score.

reviews.author: aazaidy
reviews.body: Robert Eggers screenplay of Nosferatu absolutely supersedes that of any vampire horror genre film. Its a concoction of perfect proportions. From the beginning to it's very end, the story is starkly riveting. Now the quaint dilemma is whether the screenwriting surpasses the prolific acting of the Cast or vice versa. William Dafoe will as usual not let you down and so can be said about Bill Skarsgard alongwith Nicholas Hoult and Lily Rose Depp. Read some reviews being critical of the story but it's a vampire themed picture and if you like that you will find no respite from staying engrossed. Period, I haven't seen any vampire horror movie which is so good in it's screenplay. Kudos to Eggers and the entire cast.

reviews.author: danfradley-37658
reviews.body:
Tone was dark throughout, acting for me wasn't the best in parts, expect from Defoe who is always amazing. Story could have been put together better, set design & costumes for me were spectacular, the moaning scenes seemed abit out of tone with the rest of the movie which it didn't need, overall an enjoyable watch, feel like I need to watch it again...

Rare you get to this type of horror movie with the constant re hash of the same old haunted house movies that get forced out these days.

I'm of the age where I haven't watched any older adaptations of a vampire film, but watching this made me want to go back and watch them.

reviews.author: DoNotComeToTheCinemaDepressed
reviews.body:
Just Got Out of a Dolby Cinema Screening Of Nosferatu.

👌Incredible Film, it was Constantly Interesting to Watch.

🦇🌟 - Lilly Rose Depp, A Perfect Casting imo, her facial structure, namely her Cheek Bones & Forehead, gave the character an Uncanny Presence on screen, Which of course is a perfect fit for this particular film. Also, her performance was very strong, she absolutely went for it full force.

🦇🌟 - Nicholas Hoult, another great performance, those scenes with him and Nosferatu were so good to watch. And also he realised Lilly's rose Depp characters energy, and through realisation, he responded and matched her Energy.

🦇 ✨ - All of the other Performances, Aaron Taylor Johnson, Bill Skarsgaard(a little bit on him below), Emma Corrin, Willem Dafoe, Ralph Ineson, were all Anywhere from Good to Great Performances. All of them were operating at the very top level.

🦇 🎥 - The Storytelling & The Look & Feel of the Film. It's Just Brilliant All Around. The Shot Compositions, Screen Transitions & Fantastical Moments, for instance the Horse Carriage Scenes, the Colour Grading and Contrast, the Lighting, the slow build storytelling, the Performances. Everything. It's So Well Executed.

🦇👌 - Due to the Nature of the Performances, the Shot Compositions, the framing, the film had a distant nature to it. Because of that, it gave the film this slightly fantastical feel to it(and even more so when Nosferatu was around, his height, his movement and Sound Design was at times Amazing to Watch and hear) yet at the same time, an actuality to it, which I thought was brilliant in execution.

👌 - The Ending and Realisation of Nosferatu as he lay on top of Ellen and looking directly at the camera to the audience as the score hits in the background and as the realisation comes to pass.

Overall, this is a Magnificent Films of Cinema, I don't think Robert Eggers will hit this level again, that was it.

reviews.author: evan-spitzer
reviews.body:
There is not a lot technically wrong with what is script and plot wise a faithful remake of the classic german expressionist film. There are beautiful shots, some great acting, and legitimately grotesque and fantastic imagery.

But to what end? This film has very little new to say and, in my experience of it, ultimately very little purpose. Its nowhere as camp and entertaining as, for example, the 1992 Coppola Dracula adaptation, and unlike that film, this film sticks so close to accuracy that by the second half of the film the gimmick is tired and you know exactly where the story is going. That is the problem with remaking a film that was just a copy of another film or story. If you know either Dracula or Nosferatu, there was nothing keeping you interested in where things were going or what would happen.

Even more, Nosferatu (1922) is already the artsy remake of Dracula, with images from that have stuck with me, even though I am not sure I have seen it even more than once. So what is new to taking Nosferatu and making a visually stunning version, there is little truly memorable that Eggers pulls off in this, beyond images that I truly do not want to see (i.e. The very uncomfortable ending, lacking in beauty as the film did not earn the feeling of poetry, but bares so much resemblance to reality). Most of the images that are staggering are from the 1922 original. The only place I would single out is the fantastic setting of meeting the Count at his table, excellent mood, but soon wears off the more we see the count (not crazy about the moster prosthetics as they get more and more lit).

Similar to the Northman, Eggers and his backers, lack the courage to hire native language speakers as well. I would have loved to see this film with top tier German actors using authentic time accurate dialects. I ca not believe that the audiences that are attracted to Eggers work would begrudge subtitles if it adds to the immersion; instead we get mostly posh British voices mispronouncing every German name. The old english and wickie accents in his previous successes really brings the world together in a way that these past two have not for me.

Another major issue for me while watching was the issue of tone. Was this trying to be a realistic but heightened drama set with Nosferatu as the background, or maybe was it having fun and letting you escape into a fantastic world of odd and disturbing imagery? The acting was so fantastic in its sincerity, but the situations and cinematography undercut the notion that these are real people we should feel real emotions for. The backgrounds feel staged and emblematic in a way that works great, but the acting was of a different level and so they just do not mesh together. It would have been interesting to play the known story but the vampire nature is less obvious (then the you are not believing my truth odd subplot would make more sense) or else just play up the camp to a level where it is fun and not just bleak and dower.

The final point I will make is that Eggers' schtick of sticking to historical material and giving it a beautiful rendering with surrealist mood works great when the underlying material is actually historical, as mentioned, this is knock off Dracula from its conception a century ago, so there is not the historical weight that The VVitch, nor the folktale feel of the Lighthouse, in both of those, they feel familiar, but we genuinely don't know where they are going. The boredom for me came when I felt I knew where the story was going, and I had gotten a feel for the extent of where the visuals would go.

reviews.author: RK_Zissou
reviews.body:
I am a Robert Eggers fan so I had high hopes for Nosferatu. It did not disappoint!

Also a sucker (!) for anything vampire and gothic.

This movie was entertaining, a lot of fun with some creepy and dark elements thrown in for good measure.

Visually it was perfect.

Performances - to be honest I had some doubts about Lily-Rose Depp but she was good...not outstanding but also not bad. She gave it her all and this showed.

I also had doubts about Bill Skarsgård but he really shined in his role as Count Orlok. The voice! Fantastic! The moustache, the coat...everything was bang on in the approach to this character.

Of course Willem Dafoe was brilliant.

I will be viewing again.

reviews.author: anastasiiaparakhnevych
reviews.body:
I expected something different, something more complex and horrifying, but still left the cinema satisfied with what I had seen.

It's a solid one-time watch. A bit naive, a bit old-fashioned, with a bit daring heroes, but still reflective of the time in which the events take place.

I suppose that, a hundred years ago, people would have been terrified by a plot with an almighty evil bringing death wherever it goes. These days, for me personally, it's impossible to be even slightly scared by such things.

With incredible cinematography, the events unfold in a somewhat sluggish (or, perhaps better said, lingering) manner. While this doesn't make the movie bad, it doesn't keep the viewer on the edge of their seat. Instead, it allows time to appreciate the setting details and the atmosphere they create.

The actors' performances are solid, the costumes, setting, and audio effects are great - there's literally nothing to complain about.

But would I rewatch it? Probably not.

reviews.author: jasonbloom-10630
reviews.body:
No other words to describe this trash other than horrible.

The dialogue alone sounded like it came from a high schooler trying to pass an AP English exam.

The pacing was utterly dreadful, the acting was abysmal, the fake accents were even worse.

Don't go in to this movie expecting excellence as it is so acclaimed. But go into it with the expectation of arthouse garbage. It's like going to a wine tasting where everyone there has no idea what fine wine is but will willingly pass off prison toilet wine as the finest they had ever tasted and all their monocle bearing snobs will ho-ho-ho at their whimsy for detecting the taste of forest floor.

This film needs to be deleted from my memory.

reviews.author: chenp-54708
reviews.body:
Once again, Robert Eggers strikes back with creating another masterful and artful take on the classic story of Nosferatu with a new mind, and creeps.

Filled with gorgeous production, camerawork, and direction, Eggers explores the dreadness, creepiness and slow-burn feel horror of vampires, blood, terror, and the creepiness of the period times within its characters and surroundings. Offering a gothic vibe horror story that is filled with gorgeous and haunting atmospheres, production designs, lightening, and tension throughout. Including some really grand make-up and practical effects being used throughout the movie.

The narrative follows what the original Nosferatu tale goes, but with his direction and style, its new take, atmosphere, and vibe creates a whole new level which offers some slow, yet, genuine creepy vibes throughout. I can't say enough about the camerawork because it's gorgeous, especially since there are certain sequences and dialogue deliveries that are still burned into my memory, and that sent chills through the spine. All of the performances are great and the characters are interesting, although, compared to his previous works, the characters aren't too individually and emotionally connectable or sorts which is one flaw I have with this movie.

Upon leaving my screening, I overheard audiences saying it wasn't scary and it's a bit dull. I understand opinions or subjective but sometimes, horror movies really brings some questionable audiences that baffles me.

Eggers never relies on cliches of horror, rather approaching with fresh breathes and new creepy vibes throughout with his works. I won't say this is my favorite Eggers work, but I'm so happy to see Eggers continuing to make great works of art.

reviews.author: mrmurr9909
reviews.body:
I try to write these reviews before I read any others. But in this case I rushed to see what other users wrote so we could share excitement. Unfortunately, yet again, there are far too many folks digging for something to criticize vs. Truly appreciating what was accomplished here.

Eggers delivers a work of art that is important for the horror genre, for period pieces, for originality, and for an example of what a large budget film outside of remakes and comic book lore can be.

But above all, this film is important for cinema. A journey and tale that chills, excites, humors, and seduces. A holiday film not rooted in Disney algorithms or targeted to get every family member in the seat. Instead, this move offers all that cinema should be: pure entertainment and beauty.

I did not share the same qualms others had with the story, but even if I did I feel Eggers' attention to detail outshines anything folks would say the story lacked. The grey and black tones splashed with orange fire and golden sunlight. The wide shots of countryside, mountains, and canyons. The dialect. The sets. The costumes. There isn't a single director using their canvas to produce what Eggers has in his previous films, and somehow he 1-ups each of his earlier films with Nosferatu.

I thoroughly enjoyed every moment of this film and can't wait to see it again. I'm also beyond excited to follow Eggers in his journey forward. This is the type of film that is keeping the cinema alive and I am glad it exceeded my expectations.

reviews.author: carlsw
reviews.body: I grew up watching (real) Vampire movies, and every time a new one comes out I jump on the opportunity to see it. Although I did not see the original, I loved the new twist this one put on the Vamp story, and how it ties in to actual historical events. This is not a mockery of the story but a real addition to the history and mystery behind the Vamp legend. The detail around the dress, language, and location gave the story itself more validity. I didn't feel like the movie was adding fluff or unneeded action battles to keep the audience awake. The editing seemed choppy at times but I understand that everyone doesn't want to sit through a 3 hour movie. If you are a Vamp fan then you will not be disappointed.

reviews.author: borisenkovdenis
reviews.body: Nosferatu! You won't believe it, but I just learned that this word means "vampire" in ancient Roman. I never watched the 1922 film adaptation, but I enjoyed Francis Ford Coppola's 1992 film "Dracula". What can I say about our new 2024 film? It's simply magnificent! It combines drama, mysticism and horror. The scenery is amazing: Germany of 1837 is magnificently recreated, a cozy Romanian village pleased, a gypsy camp and village huts create an amazing atmosphere. The acting is top notch, the narrative is imbued with fear and tension. I will also note the impressive horror elements; the melody penetrates the very soul. At some points it was so scary that I wanted to scream. Comparing the characters with Coppola's adaptation, I got a little distracted, and, frankly, I envy those who haven't seen the adaptations of Bram Stoker's "Dracula" yet - for them, this film will be a real discovery. I give it a solid ten!

reviews.author: Plastic_Giraffe
reviews.body:
I had high hopes going into this. Sadly, this movie was a sloppy mess.

While visually pleasing, it failed to capture my attention. It felt more like a slide show, rather than a cinematographic experience crafted with intention and nuance. Just regurgitating what we've seen before, adding nothing memorable.

The same with regards to storytelling, it added nothing to what its (vastly superior) predecessors offer.

Worst of all, the acting, with few solid performances, lots of disjointed scenes, people just throwing dialogue lines at each other, and some nonsensical, cringy moments.

I can easily sum up Count Orlok in one word, since nothing else stuck: mouthbreather. That's it. What a caricature.

Lily Rose-Depp is just not a good actress and and was way in over her head. She did quite well in some aspects (physical expression of the seizures), but most of the time, she was just off, when delivering her lines. Zero chemistry, no good sense for timing. It was more highschool theatre than professional craft. And I remember one or two scenes that just made me laugh out loud (not apppreciated by my fellow movie goers), it was so ridiculous and try hard.

Her anaemic look fits the role quite well, but there was no spark at all, neither with the other actors, nor to capture the audience.

I'd say the same for Nicolas Hoult. Both had their moments, but overall rather poor casting & directing.

Bad movie, probably because we expected more. I'm definitely projecting my grievances too much at the nepo baby, -I think overall the acting was not good.

My friend and I both have an interest in cinema, but for this one, each of us had (literally) only one or two sentences to say afterwards and that was it. Utterly forgettable, and felt like a robbery (time more than money).

If you asked me about Nosferatu 2024, my answer would be "I've seen it."

reviews.author: harishnj
reviews.body:
Robert Eggers' "Nosferatu" (2024) is a chilling and atmospheric masterpiece that pays homage to F. W. Murnau's silent classic while infusing it with his own distinctive vision. This film is a visual feast, a haunting exploration of darkness and dread, and a testament to the enduring power of vampire lore.

Lily-Rose Depp delivers a mesmerizing performance as Ellen Hutter, the young woman tormented by the shadow of Count Orlok. Her portrayal of innocence, fear, and burgeoning strength is captivating, anchoring the film's emotional core.

The film's production design is nothing short of breathtaking. Eggers meticulously recreates the 19th-century setting with stunning detail, immersing viewers in a world of gothic architecture, shadowy landscapes, and eerie candlelit interiors. The cinematography is equally impressive, with stark contrasts and haunting compositions that evoke a sense of timeless dread.

The score is a masterpiece in its own right, with its haunting melodies and unsettling soundscapes perfectly complementing the film's atmospheric visuals. The music amplifies the tension and suspense, creating a truly immersive and unforgettable cinematic experience.

While the film's deliberate pacing may not appeal to all viewers, it effectively builds a sense of creeping dread and allows for a deeper exploration of the characters' psychological states. Eggers masterfully balances moments of quiet suspense with shocking bursts of violence and disturbing imagery.

"Nosferatu" (2024) is a must-watch for fans of horror, gothic cinema, and anyone who appreciates a visually stunning and emotionally resonant film. It's a haunting and unforgettable reimagining of a classic tale that will stay with you long after the credits roll.

reviews.author: Stay_away_from_the_Metropol
reviews.body:
Strong, strong movie but probably my least favorite Eggers offering thus far. Well, it's most comparable to The Witch in a multitude of ways, and on par with that, but I feel I would choose that simply because it was one of a kind. All of his other films are wildly original. This one kind of felt like "Why did you actually decide to make this when you could have made another unique film?"

Gorgeous looking movie. Paced very tastefully, but it feels as if Eggers chose coming off as tasteful over striving for entertainment. Though the movie was great overall, it dragged in the middle, and certainly could have used a solid 20-30 minutes cut from it. The middle portion is also the only portion that begins to feel rather cliche and formulaic, a bit too "this feels too much like too many other movies".

The last half hour was definitely the strongest portion in my opinion, and served as quite redeeming. I especially loved the finale - it is exquisite from all angles, but especially visually, and in its direction. I admit I could watch the ending over and over. It's quite incredible.

Another of the films only flaws would be in the casting/acting, in my opinion. While Nicolas Hoult held it all down very, very well. And I still can't believe that was Bill Skaarsgard - he is completely unidentifiable as Orlok, Aaron Taylor-Johnson and especially Lily Rose-Depp were unfortunately inconsistent. While they both had some very strong moments, for every impressive moment, there were just as many that were impossible to take seriously. And while they're both very talented, with a gothic tale meant to be this dramatic, romantic, and tragic - these moments of acting imperfection take away from the potential trance that this movie should otherwise have you in. Herzog's Nosferatu was great because it was one of the most dreamlike films I've ever seen - the whole thing plays like a fever dream and it's never broken - this is the way I feel a Nosferatu film should play. While Eggers' version certainly has its effective sequences, it, much like the aforementioned performances, does not remain consistent in this regard.

Those criticisms aside, Eggers' Nosferatu is still a very strong film. The environments, music, sound design, imagery, and most of the dialogue are excellent. There is much to love about this movie, as is the case with all of Eggers' work. Though it felt slow, I do admittedly already have the desire to see some of the sequences again. Of course, Willem Dafoe was also perfection, and the real show-stealer was the rat-king henchman under the spell of his dark lord. I can't access his name right now cuz I'm on an airplane as I write this, but he was the best part of the entire cast. Let me also say, this is better than 90% of contemporary American horror films, so that too is something to celebrate.

reviews.author: kristina-56908
reviews.body: This is NOT a vampire movie, it has necrophilia, weird unneeded sex scenes. The accents were so heavy and hard to understand. The movie itself was not scary in any way, everything was so dim and dark making it hard to see. There's a character in there that I still don't understand the point of. You can tell it was a male director the way they choose to focus on women's breast for no other reason than just to have it in the movie. Two people got up and left after 20 minutes. Then once the movie ended half the theater laughed in disbelief of how awful it was. I am so sad and disappointed that we actually wasted our money to watch it. Please do yourself a favor and skip this movie, you are not missing out whatsoever.

reviews.author: vaterian
reviews.body:
The vampire tale ever told. The classic by this film is an arthouse masterpiece in how it is shot, acted, written and made overall.

The acting was better than great. This is the first film I have seen with Lily-Rose, Johnny Depp's daughter, starring as Ellen and it was phenomenal. There were times when she was lamentably subtle while other times, she can be unpredictably scary with how she physically acts. Nicholas Hoult was intense as Thomas; he plays scared and mild-mannered so perfectly that you too are fearful of what is to come. Willem Dafoe is always a delight to see on-screen, especially since he has become a regular actor of Eggers.

Bill Skarsgard was fantastic as Count Orlok and thought he was scarier than his portrayal of Pennywise from 'It'. The make-up work on him was meticulously solid, yet at the same time, stays loyal to the original 1922 look. This brings me to my favourite scene when we are introduced to Orlok in the dining hall, where he is mostly covered in shadows. Even though we do not see much of Orlok throughout the film, it leaves much to the imagination. Every time he spoke to Thomas, it always made you feel uneasy. The most effective jump scare comes from Skarsgard's Orlok and they will still get you, even on the second or third watch. The horror also lies in the build-up, the actors' performances and how it was shot.

I have been enjoying Robert Egger's films more and more with each one he has directed. Watching Nosferatu, you can clearly tell he has done his research on the source material. The cinematography is very gorgeous and thorough, even during the close-up shots. Despite the monochrome palette, the production value is high-quality in the designs of its town settings and Victorian apparel that actors wore. The aesthetic was pretty gothic, yet very natural as well from the look of everything. How it was set up and framed is memorable..

reviews.author: mcgill_krm
reviews.body:
I went into the theater today, with the hope that I would be transported back in time. Call it a Festivus or a Christmas miracle, but I was transported to another time and place.

Where the streets smelled of sewer and the rats stewed in their own filth. To a place that was utterly offensive in every way. Yet, it somehow managed to be beautiful. The cinematography was beyond my wildest imagination and the acting was superb. The makeup department alone should get a standing ovation.

The Count was grotesquely beautiful and a job well done to the Bill Skarsgard. I found myself forgetting who actually played the Count. The role was portrayed so seamless. I felt, in that moment, that the Count was lurking around the corner.

I highly recommend this masterpiece of cinema!!

reviews.author: jared-25331
reviews.body:
Nosferatu (2024) is the modern day remake of the 1922 silent black and white movie of the same name from Germany. Now this is a movie I've been excited about for a long time. First, Robert Eggers is one of my favorite filmmakers working today and I've loved all three of his previous movies. Second, I was excited to see what he was going to bring to the table with this modern day version of that movie. Well I just got done watching this movie and this is easily one of the best movies of 2024.

Positives for Nosferatu (2024): This is easily the best work Robert Eggers has done up to this point in his career. I love the old school approach he took with this movie where it has that Classic Universal Monsters and gothic feel when it comes to the movie's atmosphere. In a time where a lot of movies are starting to feel the same in terms of filmmaking, this felt like a fresh breathe of air. The production value with the set design and costumes is immaculate where it feels like you're being transported in a different timeline while also having that modern day feel that makes the movie more accessible to modern day audiences. As with any of Robert Eggers movies, the performances from the cast are phenomenal and everyone is given it their all here. Lily-Rose Depp gives a star making performance as Ellen and she is worthy of a nomination and win for Best Actress at the Oscars, you know if the Academy will allow it given their treatment to the horror genre in the past. She is required to do a lot in this movie whether you're talking about the way she delivers her dialogue and her physical performance. Nicholas Hoult is also awesome as Thomas Hutter in what has been a phenomenal 2024 for this guy and I can't wait to see him as Lex Luthor in Superman (2025) next year. Willem Dafoe is another standout here, but then again this guy is always bringing it in almost every movie he's ever been in. Bill Skarsgard was phenomenal as Count Orlok and this is easily the best that this guy has ever been in his career. I love how he's being kept in the shadows for most of the runtime and you can still feel his presence. The way hoe he delivers dialogue with his voice is so creepy and disturbing which gives the sense of dread and terror that is about to come. I even love the look for Count Orlok in this movie where it also feels like a very transformative performance. And finally, I loved the slow-burn approach to the movie where it does feel long while also keeping you invested with a lot of compelling stuff in the movie.

Overall, Nosferatu (2024) is another phenomenal cinematic masterpiece from Robert Eggers. This is not only one of the best movies of 2024, this is easily one of the best horror movies I've watched in my life.

reviews.author: maria_b_tanner
reviews.body: Mesmerized from the beginning. We could not take our eyes off the screen! The entire ambiance of the film was perfect and creepy without being over the top. Lily Rose Depp was great and makes you for get the previous disaster she starred in. . We saw the original Nosferatu from 1922 just a few weeks ago but this one tells the whole story. I finally understand the connection between Nosferatu and Ellen. After the film was over we just sat in our seats just in awe. The first word out of our mouths WOW. I highly, highly recommend this movie. I would actually see it again and pay more attention to details that may be hard to catch the first time.

reviews.author: FilmAlicia
reviews.body:
Gorgeous sets, splendid costumes, beautiful cinematography and a good cast do not a great Gothic horror story make.

"Nosferatu: A Symphony of Horror," the 1922 silent F. W. Murnau classic starring Max Shrek, is apparently one of Robert Eggers's favorite films, and his reimagining of the classic film, 2024's "Nosferatu" includes nods to both the original and to Werner Herzog's excellent 1979 remake.

Having seen two of Eggers's other movies, "The Witch," and "The Northman," which were praised by critics for his effort to do authentic and highly atmospheric recreations of historic periods, for me the actual stories sometimes descended into silliness, as, for example, in "The Northman," when two enemies fight to the death on the slopes of an active volcano while both are completely nude.

"Nosferatu" is centered around the deeply troubled heroine, Ellen Hutter, played in this version by Lily-Rose Depp. However, if you are looking for a Gothic tale of a beautiful, cursed woman contorting her lovely features in the throes of possession by a dark force, John Logan's great series, "Penny Dreadful," already did it better, with the character of Vanessa Ives, played by the inimitable Eva Greene.

I had the distinct feeling which watching Lily-Rose Depp's acting in "Nosferatu" that Depp had seen and admired Greene's fearless performance in "Penny Dreadful," but lacked the acting chops to pull a similar feat off.

Eggers doesn't do subtlety, and subtlety usually works better for horror. His conception of Count Orlok was unlike any other that we have seen previously, including the voice, and it might have worked for some people, but it didn't work for me, no disrespect to Bill Skarsgard's performance as Orlok intended.

For the remainder of the cast, I thought Nicholas Hoult, Willem Dafoe and Aaron Taylor-Johnson were particularly good. Worth seeing, but the 1922 version is still the definitive "Nosferatu."

reviews.author: frydfairy
reviews.body:
The new Nosferatu is a stunning homage to the 1922 classic, capturing the haunting beauty and gothic atmosphere of the original while enhancing it with mesmerizing visuals. The use of lighting and shadows was truly remarkable, adding depth and tension that felt like a natural extension of the silent film's aesthetic.

While there were some slower parts, they mirrored the pacing of the original, perhaps intentionally. The slower moments didn't detract from the experience but instead gave way to suspenseful, nail-biting sequences. The jump scares were surprisingly effective-something that's hard to pull off for seasoned horror fans-and the score amplified the tension throughout, keeping me captivated for nearly the entire runtime.

Skarsgård delivered a spellbinding performance, transforming himself into a truly unrecognizable and chilling Nosferatu. His mastery of language and dialect was entrancing, and the supporting cast's overdramatized performances felt like a loving nod to the theatrical style of the 1920s.

From beginning to end, the film exuded fear, trepidation, and an underlying sense of tragedy. The ending, in particular, was a masterpiece-a heartbreakingly beautiful shot that lingers in the mind long after the credits roll.

Overall, this Nosferatu met and exceeded my expectations. It's a must-see for fans of the original and those who appreciate gothic horror. I'll definitely be watching this again.

reviews.author: valentincostea-18698
reviews.body:
I absolutely loved the first thirty minutes. The brutal start and amazing shots, with characters resembling real human relationships. After that, everything felt off. The actors gave their best, but the characters were dull, making it clear that beautiful cinematography alone can't salvage a lackluster movie.

The only engaging subplot was about Nosferatu's human helper and the lengthy names Dafoe's character came up with. Though the actors did their best, they were constrained by an empty script that focused too little on what the characters would genuinely feel. There were some great scenes portraying fear, but love, friendship, acceptance, and surprise were barely touched upon.

In summary, a movie with a dull plot, but great actors, dull characters, and stunning visuals.

reviews.author: linistea
reviews.body: Watching Nosferatu in cinema was an immersive sensory and archetypal experience, suspending the contact with the rational world. Good unsettling physical acting to represent the encounter between the body and the beyond body forces. Good unsettling voice taking you out of the world. And one of the best phrases heard this year in a movie coming from the cabalist doctor (William Dafoe) about having to face the evil inside so you don't have to face the evil outside. And the final scene, a reminder that the completion of the self comes after the integration, taking in (both scary and joyful) the shadow.

reviews.author: sjo-15
reviews.body:
I was looking forward to this. I wanted it to be great. I am a fan of Nicolas Hoult - hes been in some interesting and varied stuff.

I found it slow and a bit boring and more than a bit silly. Taking itself very serious. So serious that in a few scenes that were particularly silly I could not help but laugh out loud at the silliness, as did my companion.

The ending, in particular, drew disbelieving gasps and chuckles from the audience, and not in a good way. My impression was that many people found it to be just daft. Never a good way to end a film viewing. There was no buzz afterwards.

Its bit like someone took Bram Stoker's Dracula from the 90's and painstakingly removed the interesting characters and came up with this dull saga.

Its also pretty unpleasant in places, not necessarily a bad thing I suppose.

Switching between black and white and colour isn't dramatic, its irritating.

The plot jumps a bit. One minute someone is dieing the next they are up and about and seemingly cured.

Willem Dafoe was like a breath of fresh air - finally someone with commanding screen presence. Simon McBurney was entertaining too. These two stood out.

Ultimately, for me, I think this film will be sadly forgettable and a disappointment.

reviews.author: robertmortimer-16398
reviews.body:
The script, athmosphere, tension, cinematography, sound design, acting and directing are all great and everything come together in an awesome and beautiful way!

Great performances from all the actors, especially from Lily Rose Depp and Bill Skarsgård!

I would not be suprised if this movie wins an Oscar for best cinematography, even the acting categories would have a shot!

Robert Eggers is a king at building athmosphere, tension and suspense, which he maintain throughout the whole movie.

So at last, it's really worth watching this horror masterpiece on the big screen! Don't wait until it's out on the streaming services!

reviews.author: sampsoncs
reviews.body: I didn't get to watch all of it, had to deal with an emergency and 2 two minute bathroom breaks, but this movie out did whatever preconceived notions of a remake of a classic. A must see in the theater. This is the first time I've posted a review on here. I own hundreds of DVD's and love many movies. In fact, of the original Nosferatu is a classic and this one will be a classic too. The cast is great William DaFoe is excellent as always and Bill Skarsgard performance as Count Orlok is outstanding, he is on his way to greatness. I watched it in Curacao it was in English with Spanish subtitles. Again a must see in a theater.

reviews.author: mgw-19433
reviews.body: Visually this movie was remarkable. The setting of the movie makes for the perfect aesthetic of a gothic horror movie. It feels like every scene something is popping off the screen whether visually or literally. I felt Lily Rose Depp was perfect for this role and she was incredible with her body language and facial expressions. Her quote of "does evil come from within or from beyond" was such a good quote the way she delivers it and it's a great metaphor for the movie. Willem Dafoe as usual is perfect for these type of movies and roles, he comes into the movie at a point when it needs another injection of life and he delivers. Lastly Skarsgaard was really dialed in as Nosferatu, his presence and voice stood out and really took the movie to another level.

reviews.author: ianplaceme
reviews.body:
Before I dive into my review, it's actually insane how so many people do not realize that Nosferatu was intentionally a slightly modified version of Dracula.

The original 1922 film was not able to get Bram Stokers authorization and in turn renamed characters and changed minor plot details to avoid copyright lawsuits (which they ultimately still had to battle). To that end, it's crazy that so many people leaving reviews are claiming this is a copy of Coppola's Dracula.

It's a copy of Dracula, which Coppola also took from Bram Stoker. All in all, kinda shameful to see so many people focusing their reviews on this moot point. Now that we've cleared up the 95% of reviews on here lacking the necessary context, I'll turn to my actual review of this legitimate masterpiece.

It goes without saying that Eggers is one of the best directors in modern filmmaking. All of his films have been able to achieve a visceral atmosphere of dread and impending doom that leaves mindful watchers in angst and discomfort (the fun kind) throughout the whole movie.

Nosferatu is unequivocally his best work yet. The tension and atmosphere throughout the movie is palpable. I felt uneasy by the sheer darkness of the sets whenever Count Orlock was on screen. His mere image and presence made me uncomfortable throughout the entire movie. However, I thought the voicing by Skarsgard was a fairly generic Eastern European impression but that's a minor concession to make.

An important callout in Eggers' work is that all of his films have been able to masterfully utilize a small cast that carries the film entirely (look no further than The Lighthouse). The same goes for Nosferatu, each character was perfectly casted and carried the majority of the film with a few extras and minor speaking roles thrown in the mix. I was particularly impressed with Lily Rose-Depp, Nicholas Hoult, and one of the greatest actors ever to live, Willem Dafoe.

I could truly go on and on about this film and why it's exceptional in nearly every sense. Ultimately you need to have the proper context of the Dracula/Nosferatu relationship, go in with an open mind, and enjoy the best film of 2024.

reviews.author: natebclapp
reviews.body: I have never been so terrified by a movie that I felt the need to leave the theater. Nosferatu is deeply unsettling, creating a real sense of panic within the audience. The atmosphere was dark and depressing, and the jump scares were very effective. The performances by all of the actors, especially by Lily Rose Depp, were extraordinarily haunting. I was covering my eyes at every turn, hoping that the story would stop advancing in the direction it was going. It was a brilliant adaptation of such a memorable classic. Just be prepared to be scared. Its themes of religion and death were interesting and thought provoking, capturing what the fear of death truly feels like.

reviews.author: Josephpr1990
reviews.body:
Yesterday (11-01-2025) I saw this film at Movies@ in Dundrum, Dublin, Ireland. It's a good film but it's still very scary. It has some very disturbing moments that can cause jumpscares. Some of them gave me a fright! I'd rather not watch it before bedtime when it comes out on DVD, Blu-Ray and any streaming services like Netflix, it may give me nightmares!

Its acting is great especially from Bill Skarsgard and Lily-Rose Depp themselves.

We know it is a remake of F. W. Murnau's 1922 German silent film Nosferatu, itself inspired by Bram Stoker's 1897 novel Dracula.

If you're a fan of vampires like Dracula, you'll like this film.

reviews.author: P-Dawg_
reviews.body: Don't normally write reviews but this is one I have been waiting on for quite some time. First, the visual/audio experience was outstanding and worth the cost of admission alone. Orlok has a disgusting presence which is effective at least early in the film. Acting was great, particularly Skarsgard and Hoult, as well as Depps physical performance. The negatives: the plot was weak, especially when considering the source material. I never felt like I had a solid grasp on Orlok's motivations or the complexities of his relationship with Ellen. The count also becomes progressively less scary/interesting and the finale just sort of comes out of nowhere without a true climax. Outside of thomas, I was minimally invested in any of the characters and I found Ellen's character confusing, like did she sort of have this planned? I have no idea. If it had a great story, which exists with Stoker's work, that could have made up for lack of depth in other areas. It just seems like modern movies absolutely nail the visuals/atmosphere but abandon storytelling. Again, this is a very good movie and worth seeing in theaters, but does not come close to Coppolas 1992 film, which is much more coherent.

reviews.author: sgildea-78306
reviews.body:
Nosferatu is a gorgeously shot movie.

The lighting, the cinematography and the effects are all of the highest standard.

The acting is great all round and Skarsgard is truly unrecognisable and evil in the role of the vampire.

Lily Depp is great in her role which carries the movie really.

The story is well worn though. But as this is a remake then there's nothing to really quibble about there other than it might be too familiar for some.

However a slight difference is this really is focused on Lily Depp's character Ellen.

In fact it's fair to say this movie could have been called Ellen instead! But that's not a bad thing as the part is played brilliantly.

There's some jump scares, gore, nudity and creepy moments.

All essential for a good vampire film.

And the ending is class.

reviews.author: jacloax
reviews.body: Yes. I love movies. No. I am nothing near a critic or reviewer. I was totally engrossed in this movie. The cinematography was fantastic. The acting was great, intentionally melodramatic. I was very much on the edge of my seat, anxious to see what would happen next and how it would be portrayed. A few "gross" scenes, though not a gross movie overall. I'm not sure they completely stuck the landing. As the movie approaches the end, you know what is going to happen, waiting for the anticipated conclusion to... conclude. That is a bit of a break from my eager anticipation for what was coming next through most of the movie. A minor quibble with a fantastic movie. If you enjoy a slow burn or gothic horror, or just something a little different, go see it. You won't be sorry.

reviews.author: saimariejohnson
reviews.body:
Nosferatu is a stunning cinematic delivery into a Gothic story of pure splendor that is a visual delight for the eyes in every possible way.

Then comes the amazing and stunningly shocking performance that Lily-rose Depp gave definitely proving that she has gotten the talent from her father to deliver the kind of performances that Gothic horror necessitates in order for it to be delivered properly to an audience.

An example of this is in fact that no CGI was used in the creation of this film and lily Rosa's iconic acting in the moment where she goes into a seizure and begins quaking is so believable that you truly do think that she's about to convulse and this is actually happening to her.

Next, comes Bill Skarsgard in one of the most phenomenal unrecognizable rules I've ever seen him and however the heroine voice that he delivered comparing it to the things that he's done in the past especially with the iconic voice that he gave to Pennywise it was clear to see he put a great deal of time and effort and ensuring that the accuracy of his voice and accent depicted that of a Romanian nobleman in such a way that it gave the character So much more depth even for the lack of visualization since he was mostly covered in shadow until his great reveal.

Nicholas Hoult and Aaron Taylor Johnson also did great in their respective roles but I will say I load Aaron Taylor Johnson in this role and that is a credit to his acting because the character in my opinion was meant to be hated. Willem Dafoe offers a sense of levity at moments in this movie and yet brings everything together in such a way that the ending delivery is not only perfect for the story line but also bitter sweet I truly think that Robert Eggers has delivered us a masterpiece of cinematic art in this film comparable to Francis Ford Coppola's Bram Stoker's Dracula from the 90s this is one of the best Gothic films I have seen in a long time.

As a Gothic enthusiast and a lover of Gothic literature classic art and film I give this movie a masterpiece stellar 5 star review.

reviews.author: HOLYDIVER575
reviews.body: Where do I start? Top notch visuals. Incredible performances. A nicely paced story. You know, the opposite of many of the movies released these days. There was an old school feel about this film. A classic gothic tale of a story that has had various versions/retellings since the dawn of time. The portrayal of Nosferatu by Bill Skarsgård was the best I've seen in decades. He took the role seriously and it shows onscreen. The entire cast known and unknown to me were stellar. Did not rely on other films as a blueprint. It created something that will last the test of time. This is a film you're going to want to see again. I already bought tickets for Saturday. Just watch and enjoy.

reviews.author: simonlangbakke-88873
reviews.body:
Main roles were acted out great, but the Kraven/Kickass guy felt like he was overacting or out of place in some scenes.

The aesthetic and mood was amazing and the editing from the original was nicely modernised to say the least.

I didn't watch it for the cool aesthetics or visuals from the 19 hundreds, but I came for Nosferatu!

Sadly he was nowhere to be found. Yes in spirit and motives he may have been the same, but as a movie which I expected to capitalise on the image of Nosferatu I was completely let down.

Instead of the famous Nosferatu I found the Führer from Der Untergang. Everything from the voice, dialect, moustache and sideparted hair. What a waste...

reviews.author: mtthwjstvns
reviews.body:
The title is all that needs to be said about this film. If you consider yourself to be a cinephile, a movie fanatic, a connoisseur, etc. Then you HAVE to go to your local theatre and go check out the masterpiece they Eggers has brought to the big screen. I've never seen anything like this absolute gem. The acting, the cinematography, the lighting, the eerieness. Every single thing about this movie is absolutely phenomenal. This is easily my new favorite horror movie of all time, and quite possibly a top 5 movie of all time for me. It's been quite some time since a film lived up to the huge expectations I had for it, and God did Eggers meet my expectations and then surpassed them drastically.

Go. See. This. Movie.

reviews.author: bardavidi
reviews.body: Nosferatu 2024 excels in honoring the original, down to its painstaking use of candles as lighting, rat "actors" and set building - but at the same time - it chains itself needlessly to the source material, unfortunately, at the expense of giving the cast an opportunity to act with a modern psychological understanding of their own characters' motives instead of merely reviving a pre-exsiting interpretation of Victorian times and German Cinema. The only actor either immune to this instruction or permitted to "world build" is Willem Dafou, who gives the film its most original performance, despite playing the "Van Helsing" archetype as an odd duck.

reviews.author: jaredkjacoby
reviews.body:
Taking place in 1838 in Wisborg, Germany, Thomas Hutter wants to improve his financial situation for him and his wife Ellen by accepting a commission from Herr Knock who wants to sell a home in Wisborg to Count Orlok. Meanwhile, Ellen senses a vampire pursuing and haunting her constantly and she persists Hutter to not go on his journey. Hutter travels to Transylvania and he quickly realizes the monster he is dealing with while Ellen deals with more hauntings.

Nosferatu is a messed up movie and for that, it makes for an incredibly compelling horror movie. This is the kind of film that will crawl under the audience's skin. To put it lightly, it is about this horrifying vampire who plays sexually sadistic mind games on this poor girl and her husband is tricked to go help get this vampire a home nearby their home. The original movie has some scary scenes and atmosphere, but it could be cheesy at times and there is no graphic content. Here? It is a part of the story to emphasize how sadistic Count Orlok is with his torture of not just Ellen, but everyone he encounters. This is what builds the dark atmosphere of the movie of a guy who can just get in your head and dreams making life hell.

Speaking of atmosphere, Robert Eggers has done a masterful job building the atmosphere here from the very first scene to the last. This is gothic horror at its best as far as the imagery and the tension goes. There is always the feeling on Hutter's journey that something is not quite right with this strange person he is about to meet. The first time he meets Orlok is definitely one of the most intense moments in the film with the way the camera moves and how the conversation between Hutter and Orlok goes. I could feel the anxiety Hutter felt at that moment. This movie has the best and most chilling atmosphere of any horror film of the year with not a single moment to relax.

Performances in this movie are top-notch. I barely recognized anyone in this movie. The star of the movie is Lily-Rose Depp as Ellen. She captures the tortured mind of Ellen's situation perfectly and authentically even in scenes where she is going through freak outs. They are tough to watch because it looks like Depp is really going through trauma and not just acting. Depp is captivating in every scene she is in, especially her monologue at the beginning, her rant towards Friedrich and her interactions with Thomas. Her performance makes Ellen so much more likable and rootable giving her layers of depth and a passionate personality.

Nicholas Hoult as Thomas is no slouch either. Hoult retains the politeness of Thomas as well as his desire to help improve their financial situation. Hoult also represents a man who goes through so much and becomes broken throughout the film. I also like how Thomas is much more aware of the situation he puts himself in than in the 1922 movie because he recognizes that Orlok is no good right off the bat.

Speaking of Orlok, oh my god is he horrifying in this movie. He has the voice from hell, he mind controls both Ellen and Thomas to an extent, he feeds off of every human he comes across and he comes across as a sadist from the moment he speaks. Not to mention, he represents a freaking plague that haunts the town Thomas and Ellen live in! Nosferatu is the scariest horror movie villain of the year for his monstrous nature, his powers as a vampire and the realistic atrocities he commits. The vampire is made even scarier with the demonic voice from an unrecognizable Bill Skarsgård.

The supporting cast is phenomenal too. Willem Dafoe is the most recognizable role here as Professor von Franz, but he is a joy to watch and brought a little bit of levity to this dark story without taking away its impact. Aaron-Taylor Johnson is solid as Friedrich who becomes so well-done before the climax of the movie. Emma Corrin is great as Anna especially when interacting with Ellen. Ralph Ineson is solid as Dr. Shivers who is one of the nicer characters and Simon McBurney kills it as the creepy Knock. This cast is top tier and they help Nosferatu go from being a typical vampire story to a horror movie epic.

Production-wise, it looks incredible. The cinematography by Jarin Blaschke is breathtaking especially the longer takes, the composition of several scenes, the lighting and the different colors utilized to set the tone of the film. My favorite shot however is the very last one which I feel like will stick in my head for a while representing how messed up the story is here. The sets are fantastic and represent the gloomy situation for the town. The costumes look great, but it is the makeup and design for Nosferatu himself. That creature will give me nightmares just on its looks alone. I kind of expected a bit of a goofy version like the 1922 movie, but this version blew me away from design alone. Robert Eggers captures the gothic tone to this movie perfectly from the story to the visuals.

The musical score by Robin Carolan is terrific with just the opening music being stuck to my head. It captures the gothic horror tone of the movie and the sadder parts of the film. The credits theme definitely sticks out and I do want to listen to more of this music for sure.

Nosferatu is a fantastic movie, but it is not perfect. It is a little slow at first which makes some of the scenes at the beginning not as impactful, but when Hutter meets Orlok, that is when everything gets a lot more interesting. Also, I feel that the similar beats it follows from the 1922 movie make it a tad predictable. This is more of a nitpick because this is a faithful adaptation from what I can tell, but there are a couple changes I personally wanted to see.

Robert Eggers does it again with Nosferatu. This is a horror movie epic. The stakes are huge, the visuals are grand, the characters are all memorable and the villain is amazing. From the way the story is told to the way the film is shot, this movie is truly a work of art. Not only that, but I think it makes the original film better by giving it context that I may have missed. It makes the scenes where Orlok is messing with Ellen in the original even more haunting and less campy. Definitely check it out on the big screen because it is the perfect horror movie for this time of the year. Consider it the haunting after Christmas.

reviews.author: EllaDolez
reviews.body:
Nosferatu created an experience that felt disturbingly unique. It's balance between cheesy and unsettling amplifies the film's eerie tone. The unexpected sexual dynamic between Nosferatu and his victims is a choice that feels unnecessary. The distinctive cinematography modernizes the classic 1922 Nosferatu and Robert Eggers sheds some light on the film's creative choices.

The inclusion of real rats supports the authenticity and realism that enhances the sense of dread and the plague-ridden era. The film's reliance on sexual overtones and explicit gore suggests an effort to bridge the gap between the vampire being a folkloric figure and its attempted transformation into a modern horror icon. The choices do not entirely escape the challenge of rendering a vampire as truly frightening.

Without prior knowledge of the film's backstory, the plot can feel anticlimactic. While the film still holds attention, it is only because of its bizarre nature, having moments of strangeness and discomfort but never delivering a truly satisfying outcome. Eggers Nosferatu may not fully appeal to all, but it remains as a reimagined cinematic legacy as it lingers in the mind as unsettling and odd.

reviews.author: scorchio-14128
reviews.body: This was the first movie I've ever walked out of. I felt like I was watching softcore porn, long uncomfortable drawn out scenes of moaning that add absolutely nothing to the story. It was two hours of waiting for something to happen; ultimately being let down. I felt like I was watching a dramatic fanfiction reading while zombie Borat struggled to breathe. It wasn't even scary, just vaguely gross. Watching people wake up from a bad dream about 30 times, sweating and moaning, got boring- real fast. I cannot stress how BORING this movie is. There was absolutely no substance. I wish I could yet a refund for my time & waste of Christmas day.

reviews.author: courtneyleighmackey
reviews.body: I'm a huge horror movie critic, have seen hundreds in my life. I thought Nosferatu was incredible, a really fantastic film that perfectly captured an eerie, haunting and disgusting story. The acting from Skärsgård, Depp, Hoult and Dafoe really really stood out. The editing was immaculate and the CGI was completely passable, which is a pet peeve of mine when it comes to horrors. Prior to watching the movie, I had read that critics pointed out the pacing being bad, but I disagree. I found the pacing to be perfect, I was not bored at any point. It's 100% a must watch movie if you're a horror movie buff.

reviews.author: tschumacher-62210
reviews.body: The movie is very tense. The visuals are artistic in a way that is not at all annoying, rather well done. The violence isn't too shocking (with one specific scene aside. I'm avoiding any spoilers). The musical score keeps tension when necessary and the cinematography is absolutely perfect for this movie. I've been a fan of scary/horror/thriller movies for a very long time and this is one of two times I've been unsettled by the camera work alone. I've seen complaints about the story and to those I wonder who has and hasn't seen it heard of the past film/book. Those people are wrong and this movie is well worth your time and mine. This will not be the last time I watch this movie. Do yourself a favor and see it for yourself. In theaters if you can.

reviews.author: johnalagoz
reviews.body:
Nosferatu is a 2024 gothic horror starring Nicholas Hoult as Thomas Hutter, a man with his dogmatic but hysterically unstable partner Ellen (Lily-Rose Depp) goes on a visit to meet Count Orlok (Bill Skarsgard). But little does Thomas know he has actually unleashed a dark force of evil intent on causing blood and death to spread in an 1830s Germany. But with the help of a team dedicated to eradicate the beast, can they kill it before it's too late?

Terrifying while being engaging, Nosferatu might just have a one way ticket to being one of the best horror films of 2024. With it being hyped up ever since the project was announced does it live up to expectations? In my opinion yes, this is a effective perspective on a classic tale that has scared many for centuries and I do believe this is one of the best takes of the story ever put to screen.

The performances are a spectacle with so many characters put to such great use it makes me wonder how long Robert Eggers thought about developing them all. But Lily-Rose Depp really stands out from the rest, she was fantastic and definitely a star to look out for in the new year and Willem Dafoe was just captivating as anything with his dialogue and charisma, such a good performance here.

Then of course, Count Orlok was done so well by being this evil entity obsessed with the love of Ellen, and the deaths of many. But his voice was on point and sounded very menacing, such a good take on the vampire.

Loved all the visuals and the jumpscares where unexpected, there's absolutely nothing I could ask for this was just a flawless adaptation of a iconic story.

Overall, gothic aspects and disturbing lust makes this a watch I would highly recommend to any vampire or horror fanatic. This truly was worth the wait and I hope to see more of Robert in the near future.

Grade: A+

reviews.author: cattarinaguanais
reviews.body:
There has been a strange phenomena in the past couple of years in which we have truly lacked movies with decent cinematographic content, which is why superhero themed productions are not moving crowds to the movie theatres no more, or maybe when they manage to sell millions, still the audience seems to get unpleased and annoyed with "more of the same narrative" type of approach- it's an overused formula that works no longer.

I was somewhat under the very same impression when I watched "Nosferatu" tonight. Maybe because I have recently watched "Bram Stoker's Dracula" by F. F. Coppola during my yearly Halloween themed movies binge? Maybe because the plot is not new to me or to the audience in any ways? Maybe because knowing what Eggers is capable of, I had set myself decently-high-yet-realistic expectations, somewhat? Not the case.

Truth to be told, the Director has never failed us when it comes to creating an atmosphere, delivering an ambience like no other- and here I have to stop to properly acknowledge the beautiful, stunning, appealing Photography that has made worth my while throughout the experience. That'd be the only reason to name the movie "Nosferatu" as opposed to "Dracula", for the movie captures cinematographic (German) Expressionism perfectly. Matter of fact, the moment I got to see Lilly Rose dressed up in wedding gown, I was almost instantly taken back to her father's old pal Tim Burton's "Corpse Bride". However, it's a remake of Coppola's movie nonetheless.

It's certainly chilling, but not frightening. Suspenseful, yet not scary. Disgusting, but not gruesome. Acting is on point- I absolutely love Aaron Taylor-Johnson skeptical and pragmatic approach to the presented issue, Willem DeFoe's intensity and depth in his mad-yet-down-to-earth "Dr. Van Helsing", and Lily Rose Deep's endless, boring, repetitive lines, that she thankfully managed to deliver with so much potency and commitment, and then potency again.

I won't bother to mention how I felt like Bill's talent was completely wasted for he's used prosthetic makeup throughout the entire feature, meaning his interpretation was bodiless, faceless, merely reduced to the intensity of his voice (edited by Sound FX, of course). I was hoping we would get to see a young and charming Count Orlok at some point, just like we get to see Gary Oldman's beautiful rejuvenated face after feeding on human blood on his journey to Mina. Not the case.

The whole movie matter of fact feels a lot like it was unnecessarily extended to almost 3h of an atmosphere in which nothing much happens and when we finally get to the third act, there's absolutely no excitement. We get no disclosure and climax feels simply wasted. I got to the theatre thinking "it's going to be great"... not the case.

reviews.author: wellthatswhatithinkanyway
reviews.body:
STAR RATING: ***** Brilliant **** Very Good *** Okay ** Poor * Awful

Ellen (Lily-Rose Depp) is engaged to Thomas (Nicolas Hoult), who works on behalf of a banking firm, but finds herself plagued by haunting visions of a sinister entity, that wants to consume her for himself. Thomas is sent to a remote castle in Eastern Europe, to close a property deal with the reclusive, eccentric Count Orlok (Bill Skaarsgard), but he has ulterior motives for summoning Thomas, leading to a determining final showdown involving the crazed, eccentric Professor Von Franz (Willem Dafoe.)

The Dracula (or Nosferatu, if you rather) legend has proven to be one of the most enduring fables in filmic folklore. With the first Nosferatu film released around 1922, and various adaptations over the years since then, it continues to fascinate and captivate new generations of filmgoers, and now it is the turn of Robert Eggers to deliver his vision of the old, familiar tale, because if there was any modern day director who could do anything interesting with the story, it's hard to think of anyone else.

With Eggers at the helm, the main focus is, naturally, on the visual style and cinematography, which is an inspired angle in the Dracula fable. Here, the familiar names from Bram Stoker's original novel, have been given new, unique ones, even though if you're familiar with the story, you'll still know who they are and their relevance to the proceedings. With all this established, all that's left is the performances, beginning with Rose-Depp, who captures a shallow frailty in Ellen matched with a prodded determination, whilst Hoult convinces as a timid man forced to assert himself against the forces of evil. He already appeared as Renfield in another Dracula themed movie of recent times, so the different names here might serve him well. Skaarsgard is unrecognisable in the title role, but his Dracula is an imposing, thick voiced entity that works well. But it is, of course, Defoe, as ever, who carries the proceedings, doing his zany, wild act to brilliant effect.

It's a tale you'll have seen before, and even with different names, you'll know who they are and why they're there. It's a version carved more by atmosphere and style than any deep character development or connection, but it leaves an effective mark, Dracula, Eggers style. ****

reviews.author: joshcook-68163
reviews.body:
"Nosferatu" had the potential to be a standout horror film but fell short in key areas, leaving it slightly underwhelming. The visuals were undeniably atmospheric, with striking imagery such as the vampire's silhouette behind a curtain and the haunting shadow over the city. However, the overly dim lighting, while adding mood, often made it hard to fully appreciate the details and left certain scenes feeling unnecessarily murky.

The dialogue was another weak point. At times, it was cryptic to the point of distraction, making an otherwise solid and engaging story feel convoluted. While there's something intriguing about the ambiguity, clearer delivery could have enhanced the narrative rather than detracting from it.

The biggest issue, though, was the look of the vampire. The film wisely kept his full appearance hidden in the marketing, successfully building tension and curiosity (which I'm sure we are all grateful for). Unfortunately, the payoff was disappointing. The choice to lean into a Vlad the Impaler aesthetic, complete with a hideously prominent "Ringo Starr" moustache, was bizarre and undermined the fear factor. Worse still, the moustache appeared to obscure his fangs entirely, an essential trait for any vampire. Instead of evoking terror, the look drew confusion, pulling me out of the moment and making it difficult to take the character seriously from almost the get-go.

"Nosferatu" had moments of brilliance, but the distracting design choices and overly artsy storytelling dulled its overall impact. It's a film that lingers in your mind more for what it could have been than what it actually delivers.

reviews.author: Anurag-Shetty
reviews.body:
Nosferatu is a remake of the 1922 film of the same name. It tells the story of a disturbed young woman named Ellen Hutter(Lily-Rose Depp) & the horrifying vampire Count Orlok(Bill Skarsgard), who is obsessed with her. This leads to unspeakable terrors.

Nosferatu is a superb film. Writer-director Robert Eggers has given us a movie that is creepy throughout, has a beautiful gothic tone & maintains a growing sense of dread as we watch it. There are one or two well executed jump scares. The cinematography by Jarin Blaschke is phenomenal. Lily-Rose Depp is awe-inspiring as Ellen Hutter. Nicholas Hoult is spectacular as Thomas Hutter. Bill Skarsgard is mind-blowing as Count Orlok. Aaron Taylor-Johnson is great as Friedrich Harding. Willem Dafoe is amazing as Prof. Albin Eberhart von Franz. Emma Corrin is excellent as Anna Harding. Ralph Ineson & Simon McBurney are perfect as Dr. Wilhelm Sievers & Knock, respectively. Nosferatu is a must watch for fans of horror films & director Robert Eggers. It surpasses The Witch(2015) & The Lighthouse(2019), two of Eggers' directorial efforts. However, The Northman(2022) is still my favorite movie in Robert Eggers' filmography. Please watch Nosferatu on the big screen for maximum impact & I promise you'll be on the edge of your seat throughout! Can't wait for Robert Eggers' next film.

reviews.author: dsfgrc
reviews.body:
Very strong performances by every actor in this film make this film a good watch but it plods along with unremitting dullness. Nicolas Hoult's character says a line towards the end of the story "I don't think I can take any more of this" and I know just what he means.

It doesn't help that unfortunately, Nosferatu's words are largely unintelligible when he speaks using his native slavic accent, and is almost unintentionally comic, meaning I didn't have a clue about what was happening or where the plot was heading. When he talks in pig latin his dialogue is subtitled so that gives the audience a chance to catch up. However, for the first hour, what is being communicated is mostly descriptive and irrelevant to the plot.

Willem Dafoe's character makes everything clear, and from then on the film moves with a bit of pace and intent. Dafoe explains that there's a prophecy of a passage of three nights choas, but I am sure somehow 24 hours were omitted in reality.

The unremitting gothic treatment sledges you from the start which means by the end of the last third of the film you are simply numb with the gore and have no sensation left for the bloody final shocking act.

The Hungarian/ Roumanian village scenes reminded me of the French Revolution part in the Mel Brooks film A History of the World Part One.

This film is a lot better than I have described it and I just I wish that I had been able to enjoy the performances more and made better sense of the plot earlier.

reviews.author: sunt_liviu
reviews.body:
I've seen the movie from 1922 just before going to the cinema and all I can think about is that with the new movie they made justice to what they couldn't do back then.

What I like: The Nosferatu is more detailed and you can feel him through the screen. You understand what he wants and he feels very real.

All the other actors have depth and their story begin and ends somewhere.

Aside from the good cinematography, I felt like I was in a theater and all the actors and events were there in front of me to feel them.

What I didn't like: I didn't like how Lily-Rose Depp acted in the begining of the movie (remember how I said about theater experience? Well she felt like an amateur trying too much) but that changed going on. She really stands out in the finale and I appreciate her for that.

They removed some parts that I remember from the old movie. They could fit in the new one, so I'm not sure why they skiped them.

The night and day timeframe felt weird. Why did it took him all night to cross the city in the end? It was not New York.

Conclusion: I could tell a lot more but this is some ideas that I could think of now at the end of the movie. It was a good movie and it made justice to the original one. The actors did a great job and the cinematography was good. The movie could feel a little boring or unremarkable on laptop or tv, so please see it in theater to really enjoy it.

reviews.author: mgarratt-55519
reviews.body: Nothing special here, just another director riding on previous success to carry the ticket sales. Nosferatu left the audience restless and bored on opening night. I have never seen so many people get up and down throughout a film. Its run time while not abnormally long, felt unbearable. The opening possession moment was bland and grabbing at thin air to get the viewer's attention. Sexual possession doesn't do it for me, aside from that the other moments of possession felt generic and overdone. There was nothing unique about this film in any way it's editing to me was just ok... the script was mediocre, and the acting was alright. It would have been much more enjoyable if they sped up the story to make the runtime at most 90 minutes. Willem Defoe was acting in lighthouse pt 2. Overall it's not bad, I'm sure the film connoisseurs will love it to bits (even though it's basic as heck), but for someone looking for entertainment, this will be a drag.

reviews.author: calvarez3
reviews.body:
I'm not sure what version of this movie other reviewers have seen, or how much they are being paid to give this positive reviews. Perhaps there is pressure to view this over-stylized but ultimately empty movie and story as beautiful and meaningful to feel intellectual and classy.

It's just not good. Looking back, I honestly wish I had walked out a third of a way through, but I just kept waiting for it to get better. It is a beautiful film.... What you can see. It is a vampire film, but it is consistently too dark. Costumes and settings are beautiful. But as others have stated, when compared to Dracula, it just doesn't measure up to the overall product in terms of story, acting, costumes, cinematography, etc.

Perhaps the messaging was lost on me. Lilly Rose-Depp seems to suck the charisma out of any scene she's in. She has a keen ability to both overact and remain a bit stilted and empty in every scene she occupies. By the end, I was honestly hoping for her character's death to give me some satisfaction.

The 2 stars are for the artistry of costumes and Willem Dafoe's performance. However, even he couldn't save this doomed production. There were some other loved actors in this including Nicholas Hoult who usually nails it, but his character and the writing was just too unbearable.

Do yourself a favor and just don't subject yourself to this.
