While some here want express this movie as "boring" or just continue to critique in the most mundane and superficial opinions all I can say is this:

1. The adaption from the original black and white to now is exponentially amazing; what Eggers was able to produce and capture was astonishing and that constant atmosphere of the Dark and Other was all encompassing throughout the entire movie.

2. The true folkloric/ Occult beliefs of that time were spot on. The esoteric reality of this movie was next level.

3. Robert Eggers, as par usual, was able to capture the time period that took place and transport the viewers back to that time.

There is so much I could write, and based off of my experience and studies as an anthropologist with focus on witchcraft/shamanism/ the occult, this movie was beyond what any nay sayers proclaim this movie as.

"This movie was boring" Yeah, only if all you like are garbage new age Marvel movies, with stereotypical plots, corny embarrassing humors parts and over the top action that is distasteful.

"This movie has no plot." Okay, sure, if you have no knowledge of the original Nosferatu and all that encompasses this movie.

All the negative feedback are from stereotypical baseline people, whose opinions are shallow and without any depth.

This movie is not for some people. If you are looking for some corny action packed movie, no, this will not be for you. This is not Saw; this is not Terrifier (which I love!) This is for those who are truly into the Occult, those who truly appreciate a story or capturing a time era; this is for those who appreciate true cinematic art and true Occult Darkness. This movie is Dark, it is serious and it is solemn, as it should be. It truly captures the Vampyr or "vampire" as some would say.

All the homage paid to Coppola's Dracula is there. Both films are amazing but this for sure captures the Sinister side of everything and goes beyond a love story. This movie is Darkness and Shadow.

Eggers has been trying to make this movie for a long time and with its fruition, it does not disappoint anyone except those with shallow minds, shallow taste and mundane interests.

Hail the Vampyr!!

reviews.author: arkano22
reviews.body:
Nosferatu is to me the most convincing movie incarnation of the vampire myth to ever exist. The first half of the movie is spotless. The second half could be shortened a bit without losing substance imho, but the entire film traps you in an opressive and dark atmosphere that you won't be able to shake off for quite a while after leaving the cinema.

Photography, locations, costume design, sound design are off the charts good. Acting is also on point - I'd be hard pressed to find a problem with any of the performances.

Must say I've never been a fan of Bram Stoker's Dracula -which so many compare this film to. Coppola's interpretation of the story and characters is way too campy for my taste. Now, Nosferatu really gets it. Easily best movie of 2024 for me.

reviews.author: acanacox
reviews.body:
Cinematography: superb!

Editing: perfect Screenplay: yes!

Music:wonderful

seeing nominations coming this way with this movie! Only hope it's not too late for this upcoming Oscar's.

Give the man who did the voice for Nesferatu an Oscar! I absolutely loved how they didn't show his whole face throughout the movie. Although it would have been icing on the cake if they had revealed the face at the very end! They had half of his face shown. But in darkness. The close up of his eyes! It's like being pulled back in 1930! Perfection of cinematography skills!

I can't say more of the cinematography, the lighting, the scenery of Germany and Romania!

I will however be less polite: the main actress: I couldn't see the acting. Yes the dialogue is something from a different era but there was no emotion in her voice when speaking in calm settled scenes.

William Defoe~ there are moments where you see and hear a very familiar voice and you can't shake off his or her actual human traits and their past associations with other movies. He did better in this one and I could finally shake off his uneasy past performances of "Poor Things" and "Kinds of Kindness". And of course "Spider-Man". But with new environment and more respectable atmosphere of directing, he went away with childish/juvenile movies. He did wonders here.

Very very very pleased with the ending! Oh my!!!! That last scene of Neferatu! YESSSSS!!!!!

reviews.author: Giuseppe_Silecchia
reviews.body:
Nosferatu (2024), directed by Robert Eggers, revisits the timeless tale of Bram Stoker's Dracula with an unsettling and atmospheric gothic touch. The film explores the obsessive bond between a haunted young woman, played with ethereal fragility by Lily-Rose Depp, and a chillingly magnetic vampire, portrayed by Bill Skarsgård in a role that exudes menace and allure. As the narrative unfolds, the grimly beautiful setting and eerie cinematography draw viewers into a world where love and horror intertwine in disturbing ways.

Eggers' signature style shines through in the meticulous attention to period detail and the use of shadowy, almost painterly visuals that amplify the film's gothic tone. The atmospheric sound design and haunting score further envelop the audience in a sense of dread. However, despite these strengths, the story struggles to balance its focus on atmosphere with character depth. While Skarsgård's presence is commanding, the emotional stakes between the leads lack the depth needed to fully immerse viewers in their tragic obsession.

At 2 hours and 12 minutes, the pacing occasionally drags, with certain scenes feeling indulgent rather than essential to the narrative. The supporting cast, including Nicholas Hoult, delivers solid performances, but their roles feel underutilized in service of the central dynamic. Though Eggers' vision is undeniably captivating, the film's emotional core fails to match the weight of its visual splendor.

Nosferatu is a visually arresting reimagining of a classic tale, best appreciated by those who savor atmospheric horror with an artistic edge. While it doesn't reach the haunting depths it aspires to, it remains a compelling effort that stays true to its gothic roots.

Rating: 6/10. A beautifully crafted gothic horror that dazzles visually but falls short in emotional resonance.

reviews.author: lucaszlawns
reviews.body: As a fan of Robert Eggers, I'm thrilled to say that "Nosferatu" is a masterpiece that dives deep into gothic horror. The film's atmosphere is thick with dread, thanks to Eggers' meticulous period detail and Jarin Blaschke's haunting cinematography. Bill Skarsgård's Orlok is both terrifying and mesmerizing, redefining the vampire archetype. Lily-Rose Depp gives a breakout performance as Ellen, embodying the film's psychosexual tension. While some might find it a bit slow, the payoff in its final act is chilling, with a lingering sense of unease. Eggers has crafted a film that's both a tribute and a bold reinterpretation, making it one of the year's best horrors.

reviews.author: Frozone37
reviews.body: Nosferatu is an instant classic. Easily Eggers best and you can tell he's been thinking about making this iteration his entire life. Anyone who is complaining it is "slow" or "boring" cannot appreciate what he is doing here. The story is perfectly based. The amount of dread that he builds is incredible. Each passing frame I kept getting anxious at what was coming next. It is truly disturbing in the best possible way and the way the shots are framed make you over analyze what you're seeing. The cinematography and score are absolutely breathtaking. Skarsgård is incredible as Orlock. Lily Rose Depp is the highlight of the film. This was easily one of the best films of 2024.

reviews.author: kabisoder
reviews.body:
First off, saw this in IMAX which is always the best way to experience a film, so the quality of the sound and visuals where stunning. Cinematography and compositing does a fantastic job recreating the feeling of an old movie but with a modern touch. Costume and set design was also top level. If you did not know it, you almost couldn't have guessed it was Bill behind all that costume, and the way he changes his voice. On the actor part everyone did their thing at a solid level, never felt or can think of anything the actors could do better.

I have to admit on the first scene i got jumpscared. But after a few jumpscares throughout the story i kind of stopped reacting to the jumpscares. I don't know if im alone on that part but i think they were overused a few too many times.

The storyline is good, but for me nothing too special. Eggers goal was obviously to recreate the original Nosferatu film, and he does this very well, and he should get all the praise for the time he spend creating this. But for me the story did not really catch me.

reviews.author: cwnmrgt
reviews.body:
Nosferatu had some style with some beautiful cinematography and scenery but ultimately it was a shallow movie that lacked any real horror and had a truly unsatisfying ending, one that I personally found disturbing.

I found the acting to be good at times but overdone at others. I couldn't say any of the acting was bad but I just couldn't manage to be attached to any of the main characters. Lily-Rose Depp's performance was unnerving at first but after seeing her convulse time and again, it started to get tedious. And I couldn't even remember her name until there was about 20 minutes left in the movie. I'm not sure if this was bad writing, ineffective acting, or a combination of the two. Defoe was good as usual but his character was sort of clownish and stereotypical. The one performance I thought stood out was Ralph Inneson as Dr. Sievers. He played a very believable part in a movie full of unbelievable events.

I was also surprised at how ineffective the horror elements were. Orlok was intimidating and had some decent but some silly design choices but he was left mysterious in some ways that made him less interesting. Overall he was more of an evil and ugly physical menace as opposed to the darkly mysterious spiritual menace they seemed to want him to be. And I found myself completely not scared pretty much the entire movie, even at the jump scares. That's not normal for me. The horror just didn't work.

The writing was mostly poor but in a way that you don't really realize it until the conclusion is reached. Some sequences are so bad as to be disturbing but not in a way that makes you contemplate the deeper meaning of the story. They're disturbing in a "they really put this on screen?" sort of way.

Overall, it's a movie that's got the visuals and sounds down but falls very flat everywhere else, especially in the writing.

reviews.author: boisebookworm
reviews.body: Any time Hollywood announces a remake, the internal eye roll is strong. Very rarely is it necessary and done well. This, however, was beautifully done. It added to the original story, gave characters additional depth, and used modern technologies to create a beautiful film. There were only 2 shots in the film where there was obvious CGI at play. The soundscape was beautifully done and mixed silence and sound effects with grandiose orchestral moments and haunting gothic chants. The acting cannot be understated, everyone did exactly what they needed to as a cast and as standalone characters. The setting, costume design, and cinematography made for one of the most esthetically pleasing films I have seen in a while. Eggers is a powerhouse with his filmmaking. No, this won't be for everyone, it is long and you may not like the pacing of the plot. But it is a near perfect film with dedication to both the original source material and an obvious love of filmmaking from the cast and crew.

reviews.author: Bewareofwitches
reviews.body:
The film was incredibly gripping, building tension from start to finish and It was disturbing in the best way, keeping me scared, disgusted, and anxious. The cinematography was breathtaking and the atmosphere was perfect. Lily-Rose Depp gave an outstanding performance and I as someone who was not really sold on her acting I'm happy to say this is going to open so many role for her.

I saw Nicholas Hoult in a whole new light. Skarsgård was amazing as Count Orlok. And i could tell Eggers was really eager to tell this story cause everything was amazing.

The final scene is exactly what you'd expect from a gothic horror, occult, and haunting sensual story.

reviews.author: phesmo
reviews.body:
This is certainly a movie to be enjoyed on the big screen - cinematic, atmospheric with great use of sound and music to add dramatic effect.

It's very much a traditional telling of the vampire story, set in 18th century Germany and Transylvania. The story has parallels with Bram Stoker's Dracula and all the ingredients are there from howling wolves, a riderless horse drawn carriage, a blood sucking asthmatic Count and local peasants warning not to visit the castle. Perhaps the only change from tradition was the abundance of rats, rather than bats.

I found the first 20 minutes a little slow but then the story picks up pace and moves along quite quickly with some great set pieces along the way.

There are plenty of elements that make the movie stand out in its own right, particularly the visual look of the film, the use of shadows and muted colour - the film almost appears black and white at times, adding to the dramatic atmosphere.

There is a fair amount of blood and gore throughout the film but it isn't overly graphic or shocking and it builds tension, rather than going for cheap jump scares.

I left the cinema wanting to watch it again, which doesn't happen often.

reviews.author: isaacmizrahii
reviews.body: Cinematography...exceptionally well put together... and boring as hell... though EVERYthing about it WAS good...the acting, the sets/scenery...and i imagine the director of photography might win a number of awards for their work on this... but, already having seen my share of dracula/ vampire movies in my life, this one just didn't do all that much for me...it was, plotwise, 'paint by numbers'...so yes. It was all about the execution of the movie and no one could be faulted for liking it...in many ways it was more art than horror, though there WERE a number of grizzly scenes...but it was not, in my opinion, overdone...it did what it needed to support the story and its title character...

reviews.author: TheAffableFool
reviews.body: Perhaps we all know the story of Nosferatu. This is a remake. I would perhaps say, after watching it, that the remake was a needed one because what this film delivers is exactly what the story needed. Visually beautiful. The constant sense of dread is meticulously done. Acting is great from start to finish. My mouth was open from start to finish in amazement at what I was watching. Eggers delivers once more. I could maybe say that the movie could have been only slightly shorter if I was to criticise it slightly but this is still a complete masterpiece to me. It's a must watch for any horror fan.

reviews.author: imaxxing
reviews.body:
Nosferatu at times successfully creates the gothic atmosphere ghoulishly befitting of the infamous eldritch genre and setting. However, it struggles to tell a tale that surpasses the by-now overdone possession trope, which has aged significantly since the original classic 1922 film, released about a century ago now. What terrified the audience of the past probably only tickles the audience of the present, I felt unmoved by jump scares and the run-of-the-mill macabre imagery of spasmodic convulsions and blood. This retelling of an unauthorized adaptation of Bram Stoker's 1897 novel 'Dracula' takes the story from silent to audible, and certainly ups the visual ante - which goes without saying; but doesn't do much else. Critic and historian Kim Newman declared the original as a film that set the template for the genre of horror film; but this old-school template has since been taken in a hundred different directions, leaving the old classic feeling outshined and simple by comparison.

So many nineteenth-century horror novels work on the uncertainty of perception, with darkness, flickering firelight, huge projected shadows, mists and rains, gales and thunderstorms, all obscuring what one can see and hear. Here, the darkness of the lighting is almost always daringly low that it quickly becomes OTT; gas lamps and candles are pretty sparing, even for the early 19th century setting. It was getting to the point where it felt like shuffling around in the dark looking for a light switch, the dark was perpetual and monotonous. Count Orlok (Bill Skarsgård) sounds like he has COPD, taking belaboured inhalations between sentences that listening to his dialogue is borderline grating, the lexicon of the time is used but the Count is rarely insightful or interesting. The other characters' dialogue follows suit, bearing limited resemblance to Stoker's powerful prose. Friedrich Harding (Aaron Taylor-Johnson) and Prof. Albin Eberhart Von Franz (Willem Dafoe) and Dr. Wilhelm Sievers' (Ralph Ineson) exchange about superstition states the obvious tensions between science and magic, these tensions could have been articulated in a far more compelling way as a recurrent theme of the storytelling.

The cinematography, set design, and costume design is next level, but without a good story threading it together, these efforts are wasted. The overabundance of greys, blacks, and dark corners is intended to conceal the horrors lying in wait, but because the object of horror is quite predictable, it doesn't land quite as intended.

Overall, Nosferatu (2024) is missing the right dialogue, modern twists, and impactful screenplay to make it competitive in the modern horror genre. The film could be at least 30 minutes shorter. There are spades more 'creepy' and 'disgusting' or revulsive than truly 'scary', per se.

reviews.author: jakethesnake-18813
reviews.body: Robert Eggers is a director that I feel has potential to be a master of his craft, at least if that wasn't made apparent already. Here, with this reimagining of the timeless horror classic, he succeeds in holding true to the original while making it his own nonetheless. There's such an effective use of atmosphere in this film, and without losing comprehension, you feel as though you're in a living nightmare. Beyond that, every actor delivers. Dafoe, Depp, Hoult, Corrin, and even Aaron Taylor-Johnson deliver solid performances among many a solid cast. While there isn't one performance that I can say stands out as the best, I have to give special attention to Bill Skarsgard as Orlok! The guy proves between this and Pennywise that he'll slip into a role that demands so much and transform into an otherworldly force of terror. Overall, Eggers' Nosferatu may not be as tight in pacing as the original silent film and may contain scenes and themes that could give one the ick, but it's nonetheless a modern horror win that stands on its own!

reviews.author: paul-allaer
reviews.body:
As "Nosferatu" (2024 release; 132 min) opens, a young woman has a nightmare. We then go to "Germany 1838", and the same woman, Ellen. Is now married to Thomas, a real estate agent in Wisborg, Germany. Thomas must travel to meet Count Orlok in person, and finalize Orlok's purchase of a house in Wisborg. At this point we are less than 10 minutes into the film.

Couple of comments: this is the latest work (don't call it just a film) from writer-producer-director Robert Eggers ("The Witch", "The Lighthouse"). Here he brings the latest remake of the 1922 silent film "Nosferatu: A Symphony of Horror". There was of course the prior remake in 1979 by Werner Herzog called "Nosferatu The Vampyre". I saw that version again just the other day (my first time seeing it again in 45 years). To say that I had high expectations for the Robert Eggers version would be an understatement. The 2024 movie version is quite good, but I found it a bit lacking as compared to the 1979 version, for a number of reasons. First and foremost, the 2024 lead characters, performed by Bill Skarsgard (as Orlok/Nosferatu), Lily-Rose Depp (as Ellen), are simply not on the same level as the 1979 lead characters (performed by Klaus Kinski and Isabelle Adjani). Second, Herzog made a virtue of the minimalist approach (due to lacking a big budget) in the overall feel of the movie, to great effect. Eggers did not have that constrained (the movie's production budget was around $50 million) but it doesn't necessarily make for a better movie. Last, Eggers' version runs a little long for its own good (2 hrs. 10+ min.), whereas in the Herzog version (1 hr. 45 min), not a second is wasted. I fully realize that this is a subjective take, based solely on my own personal viewing experience of these two versions. I can certainly appreciate that others may have a very different take on it.

"Nosferatu" was released in US theaters on Christmas Day. It is currently rated 87% Certified Fresh on Rotten Tomatoes. If you are a fan of Robert Eggers' prior work, or simply a fan of the Nosferatu/Dracula character, I'd readily suggest you check this out, and draw your own conclusion.

reviews.author: axxmqmcy
reviews.body:
E went into this with rather high expectations. That being said, there were more than a few people who just left before the movie concluded, it was that bad.

In a nutshell, they remade Dracula with a vampire who liked like Freddy Nercury's corpse in TWD.

Depo' "acting" consisted mostly of imitating someone having a severe epileptic seizure. Skarsgard's accent was comically pitiful, and every actor who you've seen give great performances in the past, came across like they were in a student film.

We left the movie feeling as though we'd made our lives about 3hrs worse for wear.

I would not recommend this movie to anyone, nor would I plan to watch it again, even when it inevitably makes it to a streaming platform in about a month or so. After watching the "making of videos, I'd expected something both cinematically beautiful and a collect of engaging performances, what I got was mid-level CG and actors flipping around and sticking out throw tongues. Don't waste your time nor your money.

reviews.author: chrislawuk
reviews.body:
Like to draw attention to Lily-Rose Depp performance and the possession, which I thought was particularly good. Up there with the Exorcist!

The Nosferatu vampire draws on many from the past retellings of the story, but brings something new to the table also in with Eggers own signature. There are touches of original Nosferatu, Salems Lot, Francis Ford Coppolas Bramstokers Dracula etc. Wisely he takes best elements of each, and builds on them.

I like this version of the vampire very much, with his very human and monster characteristics combined. It makes it all the more frightening, and this is a true horror film, with maybe the scariest vampire yet to hit the silver screen.

Yes, I like Lost Boys and Fright Night etc, but they are not strictly horror. I found the 15 rating kinda surprising, but again glad it opens the movie up to a broader audience.

It is a very dark film, but very fun also as it lies clearly in the realm of fiction. 2 hrs 10 min well spent at the cinema. Great retelling of a tale, and just when you thought the genre had already had all the blood squeezed out of it. It is impressive though, that they can tell the exact same story so many times and still come up with something fresh.

reviews.author: lexva5
reviews.body: I was impressed by this version of Nosferatu. Top notch acting lends credibility to all the whole proceedings especially with the way the dialogue is structured without hampering communication with the viewer. The cinematography is excellent with all proceedings having a night or dusk feel even during the day. I did feel that it could have been shorter in some parts specifically with Thomas Hutter's stay in Nosferatu's castle and also the decimation of a particular family, the latter could have been left out. The film direction is funneling dread all through out and a kind of helplessness pervades the proceedings even though the main protagonists try to stop Orlok's ascent and the plague which eventually consumes the city, leading to the ultimate sacrifice. The concept of science versus belief is also touched in such scenario I couldn't help but feel a bit of empathy towards count Orlok at the end despite the misery he caused. I think this is due to mastery of the story and the medium and means to show it by the director. Very good atmospheric film. I also felt the film never lets its stranglehold on the viewer despite its length.

reviews.author: jacksongaming-80094
reviews.body:
Robert Eggers' Nosferatu stands as a pinnacle of cinematic artistry, achieving a level of technical brilliance that filmmakers can only aspire to.

The film opens with an extended dialogue sequence set against an all-encompassing darkness. Eggers challenges viewers not merely to adjust their eyes to the absence of light but to embrace it, prompting introspection as the narrative serves as a mirror to society.

The tale of Count Orlok has long been interpreted as a symbol of plague and societal fears. Eggers' rendition transforms this familiar narrative into a unique collage, blending the known with his distinctive vision.

This film epitomizes the culmination of Eggers' work since his 2015 debut, The Witch. Every filmmaking technique in his arsenal is not only reused but elevated to its fullest potential. While some may deem this his magnum opus, it feels like a precursor to even greater achievements.

Nosferatu is destined to be studied by fans, critics, and students for generations. Each scene is meticulously crafted, leaving audiences in awe. Lily-Rose Depp delivers a performance that merits strong Oscar consideration. This is a theatrical experience that demands to be seen on the big screen. In an era where genuine risk and artistry in filmmaking are increasingly rare, supporting such endeavors is essential.

reviews.author: kyleecoyote79
reviews.body: Lots of people crying about how similar this movie and Bram Stokes Dracula are. Well yeah, it's a vampire movie. You don't just go to the movies and only like it if it's completely different than anything you've ever seen. I mean that's cool and all but you also go to the movies to see how a director tells the story. It's an old story, that's been being told for centuries before all of us were born. A monster, a love interest and a problem. ((shrug)) Got that out of the way... When the movie ended, I said to myself "Now THAT was a good vampire movie." I was thoroughly creeped out. Orlock is scary af. Not just visually, but that feeling you get listening to him talk and knowing he's about to do some damage to somebody. The sense of dread I had almost the entire movie. I like horror because of the way it makes me feel in between the scares. This movie delivered on that. I hid behind my jacket a few times. All of the actors did an amazing job; however, I want to shout out to Lilly Depp (not like she will ever see this lol). She played that role superbly. If I lived closer than 2 hours to a movie theatre I'd go watch it again. I will be buying a physical copy when it's released. Extra special addition if there is one. Brilliant visual storytelling,

reviews.author: Mykewood
reviews.body: The film isn't bad. It's actually pretty good. It's a story most fans know, I get that. So the director put his spin on it. For me, the issue is his spin seems to be "I'll make this as disturbing & uncomfortable as possible." The monster dry humps his victims as he drains them. Aggressively. And Depp writhes around in a 3rd of her scenes like she's in heat. Her friend has her own strange "writhing around in sexual bliss moment." But these scenes are too gross/or weird to be sexy. So you're sitting there asking "Why?" I can't say I enjoyed it. But my group did spend time discuss it afterwards. So I guess part that worked.

reviews.author: jp_91
reviews.body: "Nosferatu" (2024) is the third film adaptation with this title and is based on the novel "Dracula" by Bram Stoker, which has had different adaptations with the original name around the world, not only for film, but also for television and theater. This time Robert Eggers serves as director, giving us a masterpiece, which is on par with F. W. Murnau's 1922 version and Werner Herzog's 1979 version. The cinematography accompanied by the filming locations achieve amazing visuals, a gothic visual delight, as well as excellent lighting in shadows and chiaroscuro, reminiscent of the paintings of romanticism, and the obvious and well-appreciated tributes to the cinematography of German expressionism cinema. The soundtrack is magical and eerie, a delight for the ears. The performances are sublime, Lily-Rose Depp is dramatic and shows it with her character full of emotions, Bill Skarsgård is mysterious and spooky as Count Orlok, Nicholas Hoult is incredible in his role as a man who turns out to be deranged and shows different emotions on screen, Aaron Taylor-Johnson is the actor whose ideology of his character is the antithesis of the others and is extremely realistic when showing his emotions, Emma Corrin gives a tender performance that stands out in each of her scenes, Willem Dafoe plays his eccentric and lively character incredibly, Ralph Ineson plays a focused and distant character that is fascinatingly mysterious and Simon McBurney gives a wonderful crazy performance that is grotesque. The costume design is beautiful, elegant and spooky depending on each character. The art direction is tremendous, atmospheric and above all chilling. "Nosferatu" is an excellent film in every aspect, a masterpiece that is crowned as the best horror film of 2024.

reviews.author: jimmy360kuts
reviews.body:
Beautiful is not a word that I enjoy using for a film with such a muted color pallet. However, for Robert Eggers' Nosferatu, after viewing it in it's entirety, it is the only word that comes to mind.

Eggers has constructed this film meticulously, with a precision seen in very few directors these days. Heck, more so than any previous effort he's put to screen. You can tell he enjoys working with a bigger budget and he know what to do with it as well. Lavish, gothic set design and costumes across the board. Wonderful special FX, both CG and practical makeup. The cinematography was insane. Sweeping camera shots and uncomfortable closeups, all framed in a 35mm letterbox format. It was a spectacle worth the wait, especially on the IMAX screen I saw it on.

reviews.author: youlesivanson
reviews.body: What was this movie really about? Was it a vampire story or an exorcism tale? Each genre of movie has its own unique fantasy. The mixing of genres can often be quite frustrating. I have seen Bram Stoker's Dracula But I have not seen Nosferatu (1922) or Nosferatu the Vampire (1979). So, I saw the previous two versions and was ready to watch the new one. It completely surprised me. It felt more like an exorcism movie than a vampire movie. On the other hand, the erotic scenes in the film were entirely unnecessary and out of place. I wish the movie had a different name. It would have spared me from constantly comparing and contrasting it with other films.

reviews.author: masonsaul
reviews.body:
Nosferatu builds dread beautifully and is a seriously horny vampire movie where primal lust is prioritised over swoon worthy romance with the deepest desires being unleashed in an uncomfortable fashion. It's a film that's incredibly comfortable in darkness and definitely feels like a Robert Eggers film through and through. The production values are faultless, the horror is the epitome of a slow burn and every frame is meticulously crafted, making it adult cinema at its most cinematic.

Lily-Rose Depp gives a very visceral performance as she lacks control of her own motions when nightfall comes and matches it with a resilience during the day. Everything that's been said about Bill Skarsgård is so true as he completely disappears into the role of Count Orlok with an unsettling voice and look which hides all of him. It was a wise choice to hide his appearance from all the marketing and the film takes its time to properly reveal it for maximum effectiveness.

Aaron Taylor-Johnson gets way more than expected as the epitome of an old school nobleman whose worldview is pushed to its breaking point. Nicholas Hoult excels at showing fear. He's a kind soul who senses something is off but once he actually meets Orlok it's clear he's forever changed. Willem Dafoe continues his creative partnership with Robert Eggers and it's obvious that he's having a great time doing so.

Robert Eggers' direction is satisfyingly confident as shadows are weaponized, all the horror comes from its unrelenting atmosphere and it ends on an unforgettable final shot. From beginning to end it's a gorgeous film that never ceases to amaze in how earthy and lived in this feels. Jarin Blaschke's cinematography is fantastic thanks to some almost trademark seamless long takes and Robin Carolan's score elicits chills by being suitably haunting.

reviews.author: redban02
reviews.body:
I wrote this review about 25-30 minutes after leaving the theater

I think the movie is beautifully filmed: the actors all look authentically 1800s with their costumes, hairstyles, and facial hair. They reminded me of Ebeezer Scrooge or President Van Buren. I think the actors all nail an old-world accent while still sounding understandable (the film gives Nosferatu breathing issues to make him talk slower, which helps us understand him when he talks). The setting at various parts is scenic yet atmospherically creepy. The dialogue is well-written. The plot, at times, is a quite predictable; but in fairness, the film is a remake of a movie that tracks the universally-known Dracula. Thus, I give the film a pass there

The acting is great all-around. The lead actress (Lily-Rose Depp) does a fine job of being melancholic, insane, and innocent simultaneously. Nicholas Hoult, the lead actor from Juror #2, is serviceable as the cardboard-cut husband. William Dafoe shows up as the Van Helsing character in a seemingly subtle nod to his role as a vampire in "Shadow of the Vampire," which came out about 24-25 years ago. He is excellent. Bill Skarsgard does a scary rendition of Nosferatu, though a small issue might be the mustache.

A major gripe might be the ending. I won't be giving spoilers. But the ending felt a bit anti-climatic and a little unsatisfying. The feeling was, "That's all it took to do it?" (again, I don't want to spoil anything by saying any more). I also think the movie could have cleaned up some of the threads involving the lead actress, her marriage, and her motivations. I'm still a little unsure about the opening scene, for example. The movie also contains 2 scenes that may go down as the most awkward sex scenes in cinema history

Still a good watch

9.5/10.

reviews.author: spxnmxx
reviews.body:
Delightfully poised, tenderly paced and dreadfully dark.

An absolute gem of the gothic horror genre, which honours the original rather than simply gorging from it.

So many times we are made to suffer re-makes that churn out fan fodder. This is anything but that. There is commitment to craft, there is commitment to story telling and there is commitment to horror.

The cast is strong on paper, and stronger on the screen. Lilly Rose Depp haunts her role and Willem Defoe sets ablaze every scene that he graces. Bill Skarsgaard seems to seep the rancid festering Olorf beyond the screen and into to cinema.

Throughly recommend watching this on the big screen.

reviews.author: vanderstamjeroen
reviews.body:
Robert Eggers' Nosferatu is a stunning piece of cinema that brings the gothic horror genre to life like never before. True to his style, Eggers delivers a dark and gripping story full of eerie atmosphere and occult themes. From the very start, the film pulls you into its haunting world, where every shadow and sound adds to the tension.

What makes this movie stand out is its incredible character development. The vampire isn't just scary but also strangely tragic, while the human characters feel real and complex. As the story unfolds, the creeping dread grows stronger, making it impossible to look away.

The attention to detail is amazing. The old-world setting feels authentic, and the slow pacing allows the tension to build in a way that keeps you on edge. Every moment feels carefully planned, blending beauty and horror in a way that only Eggers can.

Whether you're a fan of Eggers or new to his work, Nosferatu is an unforgettable experience. It's a beautifully made film that stays with you long after it's over-a must-watch for any horror fan.

reviews.author: ARTaylor
reviews.body:
A movie that is technically well done and features terrific acting, but also cannot escape the shadow of Bram Stoker's iconic novel.

Just like Robert Eggers other films, the movie looks fantastic. Every scene is monochromatic, reminiscent of classic silent films. The sets and costumes are all fantastic. The shadow special effects work very well, especially in the opening scene.

The actors are all great. Bill Skarsgard disappears into the role. Willem Dafoe, who previously did his own fantastic version of Orlock, plays a perfectly crazed vampire hunter and steals all the scenes he is in. Lily-Rose Depp and Nicholas Hoult are fine but overshadowed by Aaron Taylor-Johnson and Emma Corrin.

The main problem with the movie is that the story is and always has been a mere copy of Stoker's genre-defining novel. The original F. W. Murnau film had the benefit that there were no official versions of the book. When Universal came out with the official Bela Lugosi version, the original only lasted thanks to its iconic visuals. The Werner Herzog version again looked good but came out after Hammer had their famous series. Shadow of the Vampire came out following Francis Ford Coppola's faithful version, but at least brought something new to the movie. The characters are all still just renamed versions of Stoker's, performing the same roles and doing the same actions.

That's the real problem. The Nosferatu movies look good but offer nothing new. The story is basically the same when it should be breaking new ground. As they've always tried to be trademark friendly imitations when they should do something different with a gothic vampire tale. The most significant differences always has been the look of the vampire and the inclusion of the plague. The plague is something unique that perhaps should have more focus. Orlok always has been the creepier version of Dracula. The original was disturbing, Lugosi was haunting, and Oldman went creepy. This version goes for disgusting, looking more like a walking decaying corpse. It works for what it is but not always scary.

The movie does well with what its given. But it's a shame that when given the chance, the movie settles for the same story told numerous times before and better.

reviews.author: rbvakarian
reviews.body:
While this film is relatively faithful to the original 1922 screenplay, Eggers is able to make a fresh horror film within the Vampire Genre. The attention to detail for the time period & costumes make for an immersion world, keeping the viewer engaged. Eggers also succeeds in making Vampires scary again. Count Orlok is more than an undead creature of the night, but a force of nature. Orlok's foreboding and mysterious demeanor make him incompihensible to the mortal mind.

Eggers also departs from the standard horror movie cliche of jump scares and gratuitous monster shots. Orlok is a creature of shadow, and the cinematography does wonders in showing, not telling us this fact. One of the best films I've seen this year, and I look forward to future projects from this creative team.

reviews.author: shahrad
reviews.body:
A visually stunning but very stupid remake. Nowadays filmmakers go to extreme measures to do anything to be different, no matter how bad that difference is.

Poorly written, unbelievably bad actings from all casts, even Willem Dafoe. I think it's his worst performance ever. Lilly Rose Depp couldn't be more irritating. As if they were all dragged to the set and were forced to act.

However, the only great part about this emotionless adaptation is the cinematography. It's truly mesmerizing, and the only thing that keeps you going till the end. Some people left the auditorium almost in the middle of the film.

Still, Coppola's 'Bram Stoker's Dracula' is the best Dracula adaptation to me. I watched it tens of times and still can't get enough of it. Actually, I need to watch it again tonight to digest this mess!

These modern horror film makers are really overrated.

So bad!

4/10!

reviews.author: jmaxskully
reviews.body:
After coming out of the cinema having watched the movie all the way through, first words that came out of my mouth was "well that was messed up". I've seen all the original vampire movies but this was above what I expected from a Robert Eggers movie. It was raw and gut wrenching like most his movies, however it came with amazing story telling it kept me hooked all the way through. I wouldn't watch it a second time but it was still brilliant, especially with how Bill Skarsgard played Count Orlok, he was absolutely brilliant along with Lily-Rose Depp and Nicholas Hoult being the cherry on top in regards to acting this out. It really felt authentic and surreal, especially the things they did throughout the movie to get the perfect outcome.

Overall I give this an 8-8.5 and would recommend it to be watched at least once, only because this is a movie I wouldn't watch a lot like.

reviews.author: isopodsoup
reviews.body:
I saw a few complaints (as in, full media articles) that this movie is really slow paced and boring. I'm a fast paced film kind of person so that worried me when I was paying just over $40 at local mall cinema to see it with another person. It wasn't slow to me. But I can absolutely see how other people would give up halfway through for their own sanity.

The feeling is a bit weird. You KNOW the film is going slow, taking its time. But if you enjoy what it's trying to do you're still really surprised to look at your phone and see 45 minutes have passed and we've barely even introduced the main plot. It's fun, but undeniably long.

I had fun watching the modern translation of silent film acting. They hadn't really separated it from live theatre yet, so people were very dramatic. This movie tries to translate that convincingly without sounding like a stage musical or lunatics. I think it succeeds! The cinematography is bold with its lighting, clearly takes inspiration from the black and white or single colour dyed negatives of the past and even tries to modernise the filming style of the original 1920s film at many points. I really, really admire what it was aiming to do.

And, not really a spoiler, but I do appreciate how they did Orlok's makeup and modernisation. When you think about what Orlok actually IS as a nosferatu, who he is, where and when he's from. The tweaks make a lot of sense while still fitting well into his pre-existing designs.

But if you're not already a fan of Nosferatu and old films, you might not pick up on these things. The nods to silent film might seem strange and out of place in a modern world. They probably seem 'artsy fartsy' or 'weird' to others and in that case the film will be PAINFULLY slow. I couldn't make it through the first Nosferatu remake because of how the naturalistic filming made it seem so dull and slow for me personally, even though the film was objectively really well made and acted. I know the feeling of boredom even through a good story. Without those extra pieces to be giddy about, you might end up dropping it halfway through.

Give it a shot! Just, if you think it'll bore you maybe wait until it's out of theatres. Paying money to leave halfway through bored and annoyed would really ruin the experience :( Hope you enjoy it like I did!

reviews.author: gbondy-48240
reviews.body:
+2 Cinematography +2 Acting +2 Costumes +2 Set Designs
1 Plot (Overshadowed by the theatricality and weird poetic language)
+0.5 for Overall Mood & Feeling (very dark, eerie, Gothic) +0.1 Because I love Robert Eggers and want to round up to an 8. But this movie was not my favorite.

= 7.6

I went into this movie with extremely high expectations because I've been following it ever since I first saw The Witch in 2018. Since childhood, I've loved the Hollywood style of vampires with yellow/red eyes and really cool teeth. I thought Robert Eggers would have THAT ALONG WITH his amazing theatrical style that makes me feel like I'm watching a tragedy play every time! This movie did feel like a cool experimental play to me. But...

My childhood vampire stylistic expectations were not met because Robert really loves to dig into the historical and folkloric depictions rather than what Hollywood has done already, which I do admire. Of course! I should have expected something different. I knew about a certain facial quality of Orlok going in but I wanted something more coming from my childhood expectations. I wanted the evil laughs and the sadistic smiles but I didn't get any of that. He was only dark gloomy and dead the whole time. I understand it though.

Look, when you're going into a Batman movie and there are no cool, pointy ears on the mask, but like NUBS or something, you're going to be like, WHAT THE F***!? This is how I feel about vampires without pointy teeth and reflective/yellow/red eyes that's why It's not really like a 9 or 10/10 to me.

Still, this is a very groundbreaking, experimental, and extremely authentic take on the vampire horror genre as a whole. The shots and acting from everyone were breathtaking. The overall mood was very dark, eerie, suspenseful.

I wish a certain murder scene of some very innocent people was less graphic. I liked how the Witch's main most disturbing things happen OFF camera because it adds to the theatrical "HORROR BY IMAGINATION" aspect. My drama teacher taught me that all the most traumatic stuff happens off-screen with just a little on-screen hint right before.

Some of the plot was watered down by how theatrical and poetically weird everything was. This style of line delivery in some scenes watered down the believability. The Coppola/Oldman 1992 Dracula did better with plot CLARITY because it wasn't so focused on mysterious, mythical jargon. It also watered down character development. The only characters I felt like I knew were Ellen Hutter (Depp) and maybe Thomas Hutter (Hoult) a little. But everybody else felt like CARICATURES rather than CHARACTERS to me... Still really well acted and cool caricatures though.

The audience snickered at all the convulsions. I understand why. We don't need another possession movie but it was so well-acted and added a sense of struggling with the darkness inside one's soul which is always interesting to me.

But if you love history, folklore, authenticity, theatrical quality acting, and breathtaking symmetrical camera shots (and you're not looking for a favorite childhood visual aspect like cool eyes and teeth), you will love this movie. I understand why people give it a 5, and I understand why others give it a 10.

I learned that I like Robert Eggers' original material rather than adapted material. Especially adapted material THAT HAS ALREADY BEEN adapted by so many others. But I'm going to the theater to see it several more times because I'm still trying to make myself LIKE THIS MOVIE MORE. I'm sad that I feel like I have to do that.

reviews.author: RUaMovieFreak2
reviews.body: Some that went in our group have never seen the original or any of the remakes. Others have seen a few, and I have seen them all. It took 102 years to do the classic Nosferatu justice. Max Shrek would be proud. Everything was done to perfection in my opinion. The acting was great. The period costumes were fantastic, and everything visual was breathtaking. And the dark ambiance throughout made it extremely creepy and intense. If you leave to use the restroom. Do it at the one hour mark quickly. And going back in, you might want to stand and let your eyes adjust again so you don't kill yourself getting back to your seat. If you're a fan Nosferatu and the original 1922 movie. This is a must see! Rarely do horror movies get remade that are worth watching. They got this one right!

reviews.author: meganriches
reviews.body: Robert Eggars did a fantastic job on directing this movie. I thoroughly enjoyed it start to finish. The movie isn't particularly scary but has a strong sense of eeriness throughout. I definitely felt on edge and uncomfortable during a few scenes. Although there was some unnecessary prolonged nudity and sex. The acting of the cast was good, I enjoyed the characters, in particular Ellen played by Lily-Rose Depp, the costume and makeup on Skarsgärd made him hardly recognisable! The strongest element of this movie was the look of the piece and atmosphere, definitely a visual treat, beautifully crafted moody black-and-white cinematography.

reviews.author: henry8-3
reviews.body:
Based on the 1922 film and Bram Stoker's Dracula, this features the vampiric beast Count Orlok (Bill Skarsgard) who is obsessed with Ellen Hutter (Lily-Rose Depp) recently wed to Thomas Hutter (Nicholas Hoult). Hutter is sent to darkest Transylvania to get Orlok's signature on the contract to buy a run down castle in Germany. Terrified he soon realises that Orlok is after his wife, escapes by accident and finds his way back to his home in Germany whilst Orlok heads there by ship to claim Ellen. Help is at hand though in the form of eccentric Professor Von Franz (Willem Defoe)

Whilst the Dracula story is plain to see, the atmosphere and story leans rather more towards the classic Murnau film. The film does not move fast and is arguably a touch too long, particularly in the second half where the debate about Orlok's existence, what he is and how to get him tends to drift a touch. That said the overall look and feel of the film is gorgeous, if that's the right word here. The film is dark and beautiful throughout especially in the scenes featuring Nicholas Hoult's journey to and stay with Orlok, which is absolutely stunning and the German hometown overun by plague carrying rats. The performances are on the whole strong with special mentions for Lily-Rose Depp, Nicholas Hoult and Simon McBurney as Knock, the 'Renfield' character - although I can't say I was entirely convinced by Aaron Taylor-Johnson. Top of the pile though has to be Skarsgard as Orlok, he, director Eggers and the Make Up department have created one of the most ghastly, vile creatures to grace the big screen. Overall then beautiful but disturbing and not a little revolting - good stuff.

reviews.author: natebarbone
reviews.body:
I don't normally get excited about movies, but I decided to log in here just so I could write this review. I am a big fan of Robert Eggers and silent films, and thus was looking forward to seeing his take on a legendary classic. Nosferatu exceeded expectations, I was blown away. It's captivating from start to finish, and utilizes the medium of film to give you an unparalleled experience that leaves you breathless. I am still reeling from this movie and have been thinking about it since.

The performances, the music, the world design and cinematography, it's all simply perfect and envelops you into the dreaded story on screen. Lily-Rose Depp gives an unexpected, awe-inspiring performance. She has many intense yet believable emotional scenes, as well as moments of unnerving physical acting. She gave this performance everything, it must have been exhausting. Nicholas Hoult also has great emotional moments to complement hers, they bring the movie to life. Of course the scene is always stolen when Count Orlok is on screen. He should easily be enshrined in the pantheon of greatest movie monsters. Orlok is genuinely horrifying and keeps you on the edge of your seat. His entire character is one of the best and most effective horror monsters ever created. His voice is haunting and unique, his demeanor is unpredictable and sinister, and he looks simply awesome.

This experience is real horror. There is a constant sense of dread and unease throughout. It's a visceral feeling that most movies can't even attempt. The sights and sounds make you feel entranced by the vampire's curse. It is truly nightmarish and unsettling, you feel everything that the characters are going through.. The acting gets intense, but never feels over the top. Everything feels so real. The sets and costume design, the lighting, the dialogue and languages, it all works perfectly in tandem to keep you wanting more, yet still fearing what's next. The pacing keeps you in your seat for fear of missing anything. The tension building and releases are done so well, I never felt that it dragged.

The music is exceptional and I would say perfect. It is sparse and subdued, but when it hits, it works beautifully. It lingers in the background much like the pervading evil that approaches the town.

The effects all look great, and of course the titular vampire is a sight to behold. He is filmed so well as to not give too much away, but still captivate you with what you see (or what you think you can see). You get enough glimpses of his grotesque form to satisfy, and it all builds to more revelation of his hideous features. Some people are complaining about his look because it's slightly different and unexpected, but I think it is fantastic. It keeps things interesting and fresh, and is also more true to the source. I think people will come to appreciate this vampire as one of the all-time great movie monsters, and has set a precedent for what true horror monsters are. The execution of his character is simply on another level. Forget everything that you thought was scary, this Count Orlok is the embodiment of evil and takes you to places that you never imagined. Nosferatu is a nightmare on screen, and will entrance you with the vampire's curse.

reviews.author: ubasarsahin
reviews.body:
Nosferatu is visual-cinematography-acting wise stunning, undoubtedly. Shots were so intriguing and clever. Practical effects played off very well. 35mm was also a fitting choice which makes me wonder how this film would feel like on a vhs tape. Definitely loved the use of location, the gothic atmosphere and close up shots. With these terms there is nothing I can complain.

Yet, it lacks the character depth thus I couldn't get to find myself root for anyone nor anything in particular. The pace of the film dragged it a bit for me. When things were building up, slowburn side of the film didn't do it for me. I also would choose different kind of appearance for Dracula. For instance, I would've liked it if it were to be skinnier and without a mustache lol. Additionally I wish it were shorter so maybe it could have been easier to stay focused.

With its ups and downs, I legit think it was worthy watch and I'd definitely like to own it on blu-ray.

reviews.author: acclose
reviews.body:
Good potential, not enough follow through. The story skips important sections of the story and changes the vampire lore, for the worse. I feel that a more cohesive storyline would add suspense to the movie. Perhaps the editing left out the development, but it didn't really work. The actors are excellent and the movie starts well, but the middle and end leave much to be desired.

A friend of mine really liked it and thought the change was more about an old vampire story line. So, it maybe more a matter of personal taste. I think it was a wasted opportunity. Best seen on a streaming service than the theater.

reviews.author: amnatario
reviews.body: Nosferatu is definitely not your typical horror movie. The pronounced Gothic tone drives the action with remarkable intensity, setting a very unique pace. The atmosphere is masterfully crafted, effectively gripping the audience. The film's direction deserves praise. Sound and cinematography elevate the story to a frenetic pace, showcasing the quality of Nosferatu. However, the cast fell short of the film's cinematic ambition, with the seasoned Dafoe being the standout in an otherwise somewhat directionless ship. Despite this, Nosferatu easily earns its place among the good films of recent times, especially considering the weak competition 2024 has offered.

reviews.author: kambizthearchitect
reviews.body:
The 2024 rendition of Nosferatu masterfully captures the eerie, gothic essence of the original while delivering a fresh and immersive experience. The film starts with a mysterious allure, transitions into spine-chilling horror, and ends on a romantic yet peculiar note, cementing its unique place in modern horror cinema.

The standout performance is undoubtedly Count Orlok, whose otherworldly voice and chilling presence elevate the film. The acting across the board is stellar, immersing viewers in the dark, gothic atmosphere.

With its faithful homage to the original and a compelling blend of terror and artistry, Nosferatu is a must-watch for fans of classic and modern horror alike. A hauntingly beautiful experience.

reviews.author: mathieuisidro
reviews.body:
I'm often disappointed with horror, but when I saw a remake of this classic with these actors when coming out I was compelled to see it on its first day out on the big screen.

Having just walked out of the cinema, I had to reactivate my IMDb account to leave this review.

In my opinion, this was a fantastic piece of film-making, and will no doubt become a modern cult classic like Interstellar is in its own genre.

I thought it was dark, foreboding, beautifully filmed, and gave a sense of never-ending tension and despair, with solid performances from the cast.

Perfect gothic horror. 10/10.

Go see it on the biggest screen you can find!

reviews.author: uptoprasslin
reviews.body: Brilliant actors & Actresses (especially Depp, Skarsgard and Defoe), a competent screenplay, Stellar direction, Striking cinematography, Some of the best Costume design I've ever seen, immaculate vibes and most importantly it is absolutely terrifying and frankly quite upsetting. The jury is still out on the ending for me but even so I must acknowledge that there is artistic merit to the ending. You come for gothic horror and it is delivered in deliciously macabre bucketfuls. A few of the scary scenes were more funny than scary to me but they still worked fine, and Fred just fell a bit flat as a character for me. Otherwise there are just a couple minute pacing issues. This movie is so beautiful though that its flaws somehow make it more charming. I highly suggest a watch.

reviews.author: niltonstorino
reviews.body:
The latest Nosferatu revives the iconic vampire in a reinterpretation that embraces its dark and claustrophobic essence. While flawed, the film manages to honor the identity of the classic, thanks to its meticulous direction that prioritizes atmosphere and psychological tension. Its carefully crafted aesthetics stand out, but pacing issues hinder the narrative's flow, creating a mix of highs and lows in its execution.

The cinematography is the film's strongest asset, relying on dense shadows, tight spaces, and compositions that evoke constant discomfort. Every scene seems designed to convey a sense of entrapment - whether physical or emotional -enhancing Nosferatu's menacing presence. Even with limitations in makeup and visual effects, the carefully built atmosphere keeps viewers immersed, delivering moments of genuine unease.

However, the film stumbles in its narrative structure. The suspense builds slowly but takes so long to develop that the tension risks turning into impatience. When the story finally gains momentum in the last 20 minutes, everything unfolds too quickly, disrupting the previously established balance. This abrupt acceleration weakens the conclusion, which lacks the emotional impact it aims for.

Character development also falls short. While Nosferatu steals the spotlight with a magnetic presence that surprisingly evokes empathy, the other main characters feel overshadowed. Their arcs lack depth, making it difficult for the audience to connect with them on a meaningful level.

Despite its shortcomings, the film succeeds in reimagining and elevating the figure of Nosferatu. His complexity and magnetism dominate the narrative, overshadowing the surrounding flaws. The blend of psychological tension, dark aesthetics, and echoes of German Expressionism turns this version into a visually striking experience, solidifying Nosferatu as a timeless icon.

reviews.author: Mike E Monster
reviews.body: A beautifully rendered, if not entirely original, retelling of the Nosferatu tale - it, unto itself, a reshaping of author Stoker's now-iconic Dracula. Not much new ground unearthed here, but what is dug is deep in rich midnight blacks, thick grey shadows and soaked in dark warm pools of flowing crimson. Fantastic performances by the entire cast and amazing cinematography make for a near visually flawless neo Victorianesque nightmare, one that - while albeit largely familiar - is nonetheless rendered as frightening and powerful as any previous incarnation. Skarsgard is exceptional as Orlock, with the only drawback being his heavily-laden prosethics and thick mustache of the undead. The result makes for an unrecognizable actor and, more pointedly, a tad underwhelming Orlock.

reviews.author: metodico
reviews.body: In "Nosferatu" from 2024 we see a well-made work in the style of its director and interesting in many ways, but less ambitious and sometimes monotonous for not exploring new concepts in relation to the 1922 classic. Robert Eggers is one of my favorite directors today, but of all his works, Nosferatu (2024) is his weakest. It doesn't have the interesting violence scenes of "The Northman", it doesn't have the mystery of "The Witch" and it doesn't have the deep message of "The Lighthouse", it's basically Eggers getting comfortable and satisfied with following the pattern of the 1922 Classic. I couldn't give a higher rating to "Nosferatu" (2024) after I was quite critical of the fact that "Alien: Romalus" was very similar to the 1979 Classic, and although Nosferatu sells itself as a Remake, it's sad to say that Robert Eggers only did the basics for a good remake, and barely explored the technology that the 1922 film didn't have. Of course "Nosferatu" (2024) is a good film, with good performances and another interesting construction of Atmosphere by Robert Eggers, but at the same time it fails to offer something different from the 1922 work and makes the classic even more prestigious.

reviews.author: milan-zuidhof
reviews.body:
The cinematography and scene setting was terrific in the movie. It felt like all the scares and horrors came to life. That being said the plot was lacking depth despite the length of the movie, nor was the movie psychologically scary.

The movie had nice details and links to the past - or ways of thinking in the past - that could make you think.

At times the horror seemed a bit forced and scenes were made more 'scary' than they could have been to add some thrill.

The ending didn't leave me satisfied, as there was not some deeper meaning or thoughts behind the plot that could make you think further.

reviews.author: kevin_sheehan_
reviews.body:
What a film to start off the new year.

This film perfectly captures the darkness and evilness of Nosferatu/Count Orlok. It portrays him as this formidable, powerful and unbeatable force that can take control of you, even in your dreams. Hats off to Robert Eggers, his vision that he's had for years came to fruition.

The cast of this film was incredible, consisting of Lily-Rose Depp, Nicholas Hoult, Bill Skarsgård, Aaron Taylor-Johnson, Emma Corrin, Willem Dafoe and Ralph Ineson. Despite the entire cast being terrific, Lily-Rose Depp definitely stole the show with her phenomenal performance as Ellen Hutter. The sheer amount of talent she showed in this film is bound to land her a lot more big roles. Nicholas Hoult was also amazing as Thomas Hutter. The emotions he showed were fantastic, from being utterly terrified to being brave and strong. This year is truly one of his biggest years yet, and with Superman next year as well, he really is doing great. Bill Skarsgård was exceptional as Count Orlock. I'm not surprised that Robert Eggers saw him as Pennywise and then proceeded to cast him as Nosferatu, he is THE man for the job. From his accent, to his voice, to his body language, he did a phenomenal job playing the character. From the moment he came on screen he was as frightening as they come. Aaron Taylor-Johnson and Emma Corrin were both wonderful as Friedrich and Anna Harding. They both played their characters so well and with such determination. They both also portrayed their connection as husband and wife very well. Willem Dafoe was superb as always as Professor Albin Eberhart von Franz. Despite him not having as much screen time as the rest of the cast Willem Dafoe definitely leaves his mark on this film. He plays the character so well, to the point where you can really believe that he is obsessed with what he does and that the world of vampires and dark forces does nothing but intrigue him. Finally, Ralph Ineson who is extraordinarily as Dr. Wilhelm Sievers. He has such a distinctive face and voice which makes his character that much more unique and memorable. He plays the character very well and he really makes you believe he is a doctor from the 1800s.

The cinematography in this film was probably one of my favourite parts, it was absolutely incredible. Whether it's the shots overlooking the town or the shots of the Count's shadow roaming through a room, it all works so well. It's definitely some of the best cinematography I've seen this year.

The score was another one of my favourite parts of this film. It really captures the dark and evil feeling of the film, and when it's mixed with the amazing cinematography it's just impeccable.

Even though the idea of Nosferatu is scary it more fascinates me more than anything, especially because I love vampire films. But one thing that made it slightly hard to watch is all the jump scares, that I just can't do. I don't mind jump scares usually, but for some reason this film just made them so much more scary and dark. I just hate the anticipation and fear of the jump scares in this film. Nevertheless, it didn't change my opinion on it at all.

I hate to say it but this is my first Robert Egger's film, and what a first to start off with. I'll definitely be watching the rest of his filmography.

Overall, this was a terrific film and a suspenseful watch. I would definitely recommend watching it and watching it on the big screen, unless you don't like horror films.

"We are here encountering the undead plague carrier... the vampyr... Nosferatu."

reviews.author: george.schmidt
reviews.body: NOSFERATU (2024) *** Lily-Rose Depp, Nicholas Holt, Bill Skarsgard, Aaron Taylor-Johnson, Willem Dafoe, Emma Corbin, Ralph Inseln, Simon McBurney. Filmmaker Rober Eggers' Herculean task in remaking the silent horror film goes beyond iconicism and then some with its devil in the details approach for the timeless tale of the nefarious Count Orlok (an unrecognizable Skarsgard) whose stranglehold on newlywed Depp (having a field day of emotions) while her broker husband Hoult attempts to thwart his evil plans. Set in 19th century Germany and inspired by Bram Stoker's classic 'Dracula' the film outdoes itself with some truly amazing sets and production design by Beatrice Brentnerova & Craig Lathrop, respectively as well as the handsome and jaw-dropping cinematography by Jarin Blaschke. While on the whole the endeavor pays off but there's something decidedly off (i.e. Wtf is Orlok fitted with a ridiculous mustache?!) in the long run that comes-this-close to true cinematic greatness. Dafoe's Van Helsingian Prof. Von Franz is the one true spark of slightly enjoying himself as the historian more than practiced hunter in the field. And McBurney's mad-as-a-hatter turn as the Renfeldian Knock gives Dwight Frye a run for his loony money. I recommend you see this in IMAX to truly surrender to the film's wonder.

reviews.author: alexfolkesson
reviews.body:
I never thought I'd say this, but this Robert Eggers film would have been stronger if it fully embraced its pretentiousness. Sadly, it feels as though the Hollywood machine has softened its edges to appeal to a broader audience. The tension between its artistic ambitions and its more mainstream concessions creates a disjointed experience that undermines the film's potential.

One of the most glaring missteps lies in the choice of language and accents. Opting for British accents instead of German ones feels like a missed opportunity to ground the story in its proper cultural and historical context. Even more so, the film would have been far more immersive and thematically cohesive had it been in German-a decision that would have honored the original Nosferatu's legacy. This disconnect is further exacerbated by the set design, particularly the depiction of the city. While visually striking, the setting feels more akin to London or Amsterdam than a distinctly German town. In most cases, this wouldn't be an issue, but Nosferatu is so deeply rooted in its Germanic origins that this loss of specificity diminishes its atmosphere.

Another shortcoming was the design of Nosferatu himself. While Bill Skarsgård delivers a masterful performance, his character design lacks the haunting, grotesque features that define the Nosferatu archetype. A closer adherence to the original design would have amplified the film's eerie, unsettling tone and further distinguished the character as a chilling cinematic presence.

That said, the performances across the board are nothing short of outstanding. Lily-Rose Depp, Willem Dafoe, and Nicholas Hoult each bring remarkable nuance and intensity to their roles, elevating the material and delivering some of the film's most memorable moments.

In the end, while the film boasts strong performances and flashes of Eggers' signature brilliance, it feels like a work caught between two worlds-one of uncompromising artistic vision and the other of mainstream accessibility. It's a fascinating piece, but one that ultimately feels like a compromise.

reviews.author: kosmasp
reviews.body:
No pun intended - if you have seen any other Eggers movie, you are aware that he is quite good when it comes to cinematography. And yet you may have some issues with this movie - and the darkness .. literal darkness that is. On the other hand, you should be aware of him and his fondness - also when it comes to storytelling ... we are talking about quite the slow pace.

Also because I read this in a chat group I am part of: Eggers is known for pulling back and not showing us things too explicitly. That said and while I was expecting this too be way more violent .. it still has a few graphic spikes ... as in really in your face brutal stuff. Could have been "worse" (or better, depending on your viewpoint) - but I am quite certain that nothing was cut down ... Eggers does have a lot to say and I am sure he would not let producers tell him what to do.

The movie does take a few liberties ... there seems to be a bit more humor in it than in the original ... but it still is dramatic and it has a lot of suspense in it. It also seems to give or update some characters, gives them more to do ... and makes them try stuff - remember the original in Orlocks castle? Our good guy was quite passive in that situation ... Nicholas Hoult is a bit different ... and there is some planting on how he tries to act ... Kudos for that.

Also anyone who says they recognized Skarsgaard? I don't buy it ... at least not from the very first second and even less so if you had not clue he is playing Nosferatu. Eggers also has the gall to stay dark ... that is mood, but also cinematography wise. Also the pacing ... I would say that your regular cinema goer might take issue with how the movie is told ... add to that the shadows and absence of light ... well you have to dig it (do not dig it up though - sorry for the pun).

Performance wise this is exceptional, but also something you have to get used to. Lily Rose Depp ... she has some inner monologue she has to do externally ... which feels weird at first ... and also just wrong. But she does it as convincing as possible. Also the movie is one of those movies that openly tackles the sexuality of the vampire lore and myth ... the sucking of blood ... the penetrating ... it is pain and pleasure. Well for those who are into it - still, you get what I mean.

There is nudity and there are situations of moaning and other sounds that might make some people even more uncomfortable than the scene with the pigeon (you'll understand once you watch the movie). Fair warning then ... the movie does test the boundaries ... not just geographically and language wise (some German words are thrown in for good measure - Meine Herren - my gentlemen/men) ... but in almost all areas.

The movie also gives Orlock a reason - and his object of desire (again no pun intended) more to play with ... and Depp really throws herself out there ... not just physically but also mentally ... she really goes all out! She is vulnerable ... but she is also tough ... really hard to do, but she managed it.

So while it took me a bit to get into it (long beginning), I loved the way it took something known ... and made it his own ... this is not a straight remake ... and yet you can see the influences of the original ... the best way to honor an original in my humble opinion ... watch both (and maybe the Kinski Herzog one ... also definitely the movie Shadow of the Vampire) ... all are great.

reviews.author: cbrleah
reviews.body:
I didn't have strong expectations but I did enjoy this. It is basically a carbon copy of Francis Ford Coppola's Dracula, which makes it largely predictable if you're familiar with the genre and previous iterations of Nosferatu.

Unlike Coppola's Dracula, there wasn't a strong story line that connected Ellen and the Count which I think undermined the plot development and believability of the Count's obsession with her.

Generally I liked it. I've read some reviews saying how comedic it was particularly the Dafoe character, but again - if you're not familiar with the legacy of the Van Helsing character and humour than I guess you might find the role comedic rather than manic.

reviews.author: Victor_Santamaria
reviews.body:
I know it's very difficult to be original and make a good movie at this point, when it comes to this character, but putting a mustache on the count, I think it was the worst idea.

I'll be very honest. As a lover of the genre, I liked the movie. Especially at the beginning, although they could have explored and developed the real estate agent's journey to the castle a little more, his arrival and his acting performance when he meets Nosferatu are outstanding and perhaps the best or one of the best of all film adaptations.

Nosferatu promised a lot and had s few good disturbing scenes worthy of a truly bastard and which will remain for the Dracula filmography but the mustache put him in the category of I already know this guy...he looks like an uncle of mine or I see him a lot somewhere, maybe he looks like the baker or the hairdresser in my neighborhood. In addition, they made him too visible on more occasions than indicated, too obvious in contrast to the use of his own shadow.

Her scenes reminded me of the Exorcist and I found them excessive. Removing some of the intensity from her role, removing the jump scares that didn't work at all and nobody needed, focusing good old Wilem Dafoe in a different way in which he would have shined at least 20 percent of what Anthony Hopkins shined in Bram Stoker's Dracula, and removing Count Orlock's mustache would have given the film a 10 and it wouldn't have seemed so long to me; the two and a half hours were very noticeable and they shouldn't have.

reviews.author: dannyinbox123
reviews.body: It was a magnificent visual ride riddled with mystery but oh so slow and anti-climactic. The thrill was well equipped with poignant acting and visual effects. However cliche waking-up transitions all to run into a brick wall yippee dippey hoo ha. To my perspective the film was overall very attractive and disparaging to our inner evils. The creepy ties it has to contemporary lives is irrefutably horrid. The dance of dialogue and space was carefully stitched with the strings of darkness. It was a diabolical story bereft of any hope or any innuendo of holiness. The ignorant are punished. The evil is satisfied.

reviews.author: nicolamina-36384
reviews.body:
Well, first, let me start by saying that the movie wasn't very scary. However, I think this was partly because I couldn't hear all the words coming out of Dracula's mouth. This made it hard to stay fully focused. I really wish they had added subtitles when he spoke because his heavy accent made it difficult to understand most of the time.

Second, the acting was very good overall. I think the girl's performance stood out the most. She was the only character I was truly interested in, and I was happy with her acting. She delivered her role perfectly-her reactions, facial expressions, and body language were all on point. I was completely in love with her performance. Honestly, I don't think they could have found anyone better to play that role.

Finally, the protagonist-or lack thereof-was an issue for me. I don't think the movie gave anyone the title of a hero or gave us the opportunity to connect with or root for any character. I was hoping to feel something, maybe sadness, for the death of (I won't spoil), but I didn't. I didn't feel any empathy for the characters. To be honest, if all the characters in the movie had died, I wouldn't have cared or felt anything for them.

That said, the visuals, camerawork, and graphics were top-tier. I absolutely loved how they created the atmosphere in such a scary and immersive way. However, the nudity and sex scene felt completely unnecessary. Why would the guy agree to sleep with a girl he knew was possessed by Something? That part made no sense to me-completely UNNECESSARY.

Overall, it was a good movie, but it could have been much better with a stronger connection to the characters and fewer unnecessary scenes.

reviews.author: cboyles-63805
reviews.body: I still cannot decide if I liked it or not. It's def one of those movies you have to see and then you'll prolly never watch it again. I'd call it a "master piece" from how unique it was. I did jump a couple of times and it had some very "creepy" moments but all in all I was more disturbed then scared. There were several Moments I sat back in my seat thinking "ohh I did not need to see that". I enjoyed the twist on the overall dracula story and honestly, I hated dracula the first time I read or saw it on film but the twist was fun and fast (loved the Demeter movie). Idk why anyone is saying it was boring, it def wasn't. Ignore the negative story comments and just understand some of those scenes will stick with you for a long time.

reviews.author: tzzgrzkny
reviews.body: This movie was so wonderfully done, I cannot say enough good things about it!
