Not only was it true to the lore, but the historical accuracy clear down to the Romani dialect and clothing was great! The costumes were absolutely breathtaking, the scenery astounding and the cinematography was some of the best I've seen in a long time. The characters were so well done. Depp's acting was unbelievably done, she is so freaking talented I was mesmerized! Of course DaFoe was a great addition to the cast, and Skarsgard's Orlock was BRILLIANT. He was scary and gross and nasty and sexy and alluring and you hate yourself for thinking all of that lol. His voice was to die for. I saw it on Christmas, went back a couple days later, and can't wait for the third go round. This has become my favorite movie. I'm not going to go into any analysis, everyone has their own take. And being a goth who loves monsters and gothic horror, obviously I'm going to adore this as this is my jam. I hope others find it as wonderful as I did! Dear Eggers, please do more of THIS!!

reviews.author: movieman6-413-929510
reviews.body:
Nosferatu is a remake of the 1922 film of the same name. This remake is directed, written and partly produced by Robert Eggers, director of The Lighthouse, The Northman and The Witch.

Thomas Hutter (Nicholas Hoult) is hired by the more alienated Count Orlok (Bill Skarsgård). During their interactions, Count Orlok only becomes obsessed with Thomas's more troubled wife Ellen Hutter (Lily-Rose Depp), without the two actually meeting.

After his first real directorial work on The Witch, Robert Eggers already had passion and ideas to direct a remake of Nosferatu. Only after making the story a bit more modern and a bit more his own, Eggers keeps it close to the familiar story. So for people who are familiar with the original Nosferatu film, or Bram Stoker's Dracula story, the film can remain a bit on the familiar side. This way, there may be few surprises or left for some.

Robert Eggers knows how to portray the film well and appropriately, in which he has tried to use as many practical, real effects as possible. By keeping the film largely in the dark, he knows how to hide the possible CGI used. By keeping things more in the dark, the quality of some make-up effects is somewhat lost, because they are not always clearly visible until certain moments.

In addition to seeming somewhat familiar, as a connoisseur of the other stories, you can also start to compare this with this new version. Where, for example, Bram Stoker's Dracula Keanu Reeves seemed to be cast a bit wrong, Nicholas Hoult knows how to portray this almost identical role a bit better. Because the film tries to focus more on the special connection and relationship between Count Orlok and Ellen Hutter, Nicholas Hoult's character and acting are somewhat in the background of the film. Lily-Rose Depp does a good job of portraying her role, but can also be compared to Winona Ryder's role.

Bill Skarsgård is known for playing monstrous creatures in films such as his version of Pennywise from the It films. However, this role was also compared to Tim Curry, his version from the same TV mini-series. Despite the fact that he spent a long time in make-up for his version of Nosferatu and even learned to lower his voice an octave with the help of an opera coach, he is still somewhat overshadowed by Gary Oldman, who managed to make his role as Dracula iconic. Despite a different name for the character, Willem Dafoe manages to make the almost similar character of Van Helsing, who was played by Anthony Hopkins in the Bram Stoker Dracula film, his own. He also manages to provide the most entertaining scenes as an investigator who seems to know more about the case surrounding Orlok. Only his character and storyline seem to be a bit more detached from the rest of the film.

reviews.author: ogmore-59394
reviews.body:
That was immaculate.

Not too much of our villian.

He was kept in the shadows We see motivation in the villian and believability in the draw between our villian and our female lead.

Really enjoyed this film.. The tone...the pace... The tendon throughout Highly recommend.

The director has kept his stamp in this film despite the scale and subject.

Our villian was all in his voice and his shadows and mystery.

The era worked so well for the style.. If this was modern in its setting everything would have been lost. Go watch this film... It's not too long and not predictable with jump scares out any other form of cheapening.

reviews.author: Nikkiangel002
reviews.body:
I love Robert Eggers movies, and always watch then have to give myself a few days to process properly what Ive seen. I'll admit I really like this film but left abit oh... that's not what I thought but.. I done the same with The Witch which is now in my top films ever. There's so much to take in. This isn't just a film you go and see then done. As any of Eggers films... they linger after. He's a filmmaker for fans of film....

Its a stunning film, some of the scenes were genuinely breath taking. Particularly Thomas arrival to the castle. Cannot get it out of my head.

Skarsgard was amazing and completely unrecognisable as Orlok. I don't understand the hate for his look Eggers done a great job merging real lore around this era of when Vlad was alive! He's merged all the stories of vampires "nosferatu" and made his version. I actually thought it was great he didn't go down the "sexy" vampire route and thought it was great they didn't make it "hot" where they could have.

Soundtrack was so eerie and very reminiscent of The Witch.

Very well done retelling but didn't expect anything less from Robert Eggers. Deep down I knew it was going to be the perfect gothic film.

I only mark it down because I felt a few character fell flat and I was shocked Defoe was one for me!

But I can't wait to watch again... and I'm glad I seen it on the big screen to soak in those stunning visuals.

reviews.author: Tayl_or_Treat
reviews.body:
Overall, I really liked the movie! Robert Eggers did a great job putting his own spin on Nosferatu while keeping the unsettling feel of the original. The scenery, costumes, and settings were all so beautiful and set the perfect mood. It had a creepier atmosphere than the OG, with a few jump scares that were effective but didn't make it feel like a full-on horror film. I'd describe it as just really dark. Everything about it-the mood, the visuals, the storyline-was heavy.

I do have to take off a few points for the unnecessary nudity and sex scenes; they're always a little awkward to watch with family. Also, what the hell was that ending? Bill Skarsgård was fantastic as Count Orlok, but it was hard to understand some of his lines. I definitely need to rewatch it with subtitles. Nicholas Hoult was solid as Thomas Hutter, but I wasn't as impressed with Lily-Rose Depp's portrayal. I think Emma Harding, who played Anna, would have been a better fit for Ellen.

All in all though, it's a really good movie, and I'd definitely recommend checking it out!

reviews.author: jamespmeegan
reviews.body:
As a fan of horror I was excited about seeing this and overall I did enjoy it.

The dialogue in certain scenes was hard to make out, particularly those involving the count; this, coupled with some scenes coming seemingly out of nowhere, made it confusing to follow at things. This was more annoying as it was often during crucial plot sequences, which meant I only knew what was happening by deciphering and inferring things, but maybe this was intentional, who knows!?

It looked very pretty throughout, shot well - albeit sometimes too darkly in my opinion, although I get this has been done on purpose.

reviews.author: jacksonbarbara-69503
reviews.body: Watched this today at the cinema was I impressed ? I think so it's very gothic atmospheric and has a few jump out moments the posters depicting Bill Skarsgard as Nosferatu were what drew me to the film in the first place unfortunately you don't see him much ( Facially) in the film but the voice he potrays is particularly good. Lily rose Depp surprised me as an actress but I think Nicholas Hoult steals it as he plays the tormented Thomas rather well.... Ralph Ineson makes a surprise appearance as well anything with Ineson involved us a bonus ...all in all it's a gothic slice of horror but doesn't give that full bite.

reviews.author: katalist420
reviews.body:
First off, this is the years best film for me, from the editing, to the direction, to the wonderful acting and the great Cinematography and audio, this movie is near flawless.

Now, to the acting.... I knew Dafoe would do wonderful and he killed it no doubt, he is one of my favorite actors around and we have seen what he can do with this Director on the movie Lighthouse. But boy oh boy.... Lily-Rose Depp surprised the hell out of me! She was fantastic in this movie and was the star of the show (which is very hard to do along side Dafoe!).

Where did this acting from her come from? What I have seen from her in the past was very average, but the way she acts and delivers the dialogue in this movie is unreal, very good acting from the young actress.

Next up are the views and the atmosphere, some gorgeous views in this movie and also the atmosphere is thick as hell, very creepy movie. Instead of gore every few minutes, we are treated to a wonderful slow burn with great atmosphere and immersion, that really will pull you in.

I love this director and really enjoyed The VVitch & The Lighthouse, but this movie for me is his best movie, squeaking past those 2 other classics of his.

From the audio, to the acting, to the editing, to the direction, to the atmosphere, to the cinematography, this is the years best film for me and blew me away. I already had high expectations but it blew those away, very well crafted and I cannot wait for this to hit Bluray in march (I heard today it will have some extra footage and be around 3 hours? I cannot wait to see that version!)

Go see this movie asap if you can, it was a real treat, can't wait to watch it again.

reviews.author: Error404_user_not_found
reviews.body:
After my mixed feelings about Robert Eggers last film 'The Northman', I was in high anticipation of his interpretation of the original 1922 Nosferatu, a lifelong passion project of his.

Watching the film and its majestic visuals and sound, I can see Robert had everything planned out how he wanted to film it, but however it's such a shame the same couldn't be extended to the screenplay.

The casting is spot on, and there are some really great performances in there, despite some of the goofy pantomime dialogue they are asked to speak. I suspect some of that might have been trying to keep in tone of how they might have spoken during the era the film is based on. The film starts promisingly enough but its hold on me didn't last very long once Nicholas Hoult and the Count proceed to act 2 where they head away from his creepy castle and back towards Germany.

Bill Skarsgård as Count Orlok goes through quite an unbelievable transformation as an actor to embrace this version. He looks and sounds the part of a malevolent being who is supposed to strike terror into anyone who crosses his path. Unfortunately this is where it fails, as despite all the visual creepiness, the horror elements fail to land at all. At no point did I find the character terrifying like his iconic work as Pennywise the Clown.

The gimmick of Count Orlok with the voice and shadowy figure gets very tired, plus Lily-Rose Depp going through another possession episode often with erotic overtones. The ineffectiveness of this resulted in me becoming very disconnected with the film.

For a vampire film I found it largely bloodless and lacking bite and not quite the masterpiece I was expecting.

reviews.author: denzellucano
reviews.body:
Here's the translation:

The movie is visually stunning, with solid performances, although there are a few minor details that could be improved. The script and plot are decent, and it's clear that this is an original work from the director's vision, who never intended to make a 100% faithful adaptation of the original material.

I found the redesign of Orlock interesting and thoroughly enjoyed it. I understand that many people went to see the film with expectations that didn't align with what was promised, and as a result, they left disappointed. However, this could be due to a lack of understanding or ignorance about what the director was truly aiming for: creating an original work that reflects 100 years of evolution in cinema.

Although some criticize the film's slow pacing, that doesn't make it a bad movie. I believe much of this criticism comes from people who are not very familiar with cinema, its history, or the director's intent. In my opinion, it's an excellent film.

reviews.author: romanmotion
reviews.body:
In the age of instant gratification, I appreciate when a movie comes along and reminds us that good stories unfold in their own time. Nosferatu is a story that isn't in a rush and doesn't care about rushing its story. I think the story unfolds beautifully.

Nosferatu has a beautiful build up and a stunning cinematography for a dark themed horror classic. It's all about the darkness and all about the shadows and every scene is a shadow noir masterclass!

As for the story, it is a remake of the classic horror "Nosferatu" which I feel like this one plays homage to many times throughout the film if you are familiar with the original.

Nicholas Hoult brings a solid performance, Lily Rose Depp, who doesn't have a long list in her IMDB has surely made a name for herself from this film. And all the supporting cast was great including Aaron Taylor-Johnson, but hands down Willem DaFoe steals the show! Bill Skaaragard is proving he is a modern day horror all star as he has now another horror classic lead role to add to his portfolio.

When you breakdown everything, Nosferatu gives us what it promises and although at times we feel the story could speed up the process, we got to ask ourselves, what's the rush? I think it unfolds at a perfect pace with a third act that delivers!

reviews.author: kjymmrk
reviews.body:
I really wanted to like nosferatu, I did. The story and films based on Bram Stoker usually thrill me, the characters, the underlying message of obsession and possessing someone are as deep as they can get.

And I'm also a huge Robert Eggers fan but in this movie he resorted heavily on driving suspense through basic jump scares and just turning up the volume and cutting away to another scene

The acting felt like theatre, in a bad way. The only character I'd say came through was Depps daughter, all the others felt like a caricature that spilled their dialogues without understanding what they were saying

A lot of build up and when the climax was supposed to happen it held no punch whatsoever.

This movie lacks the suspense that Eggers achieved on the witch, the depth he managed to bring to life with the lighthouse, the violence he showed us in the Northman. It felt... empty, no feeling whatsoever or involvement from his cast.

A definite miss from a talented director that managed to set the bar way too high, even for himself and a clear attempt to bring a classic to this century and missed the queue of actually telling a story and just relying on dark scenes, jump scares and possibly the shallowest of interpretations that I've seen in a movie from most of his cast.

The only actor that I felt involved was Ralph Ineson whose acting on the witch is perfections and in Nosferatu he delivers a semi decent punch - that voice is something else.

Lily-rose's acting is not bad, but it's not great - she brings a lot of physical tension and she delivers some scenes masterfully but the resting victim face came thru as uninterested.

Hope Robert Eggers returns to his glory days soon and delivers something that get under your skin, he has managed to do so with every project except this snooze fest of a nod to old cinema.

reviews.author: bonnalexis
reviews.body:
I don't often write movie reviews but I felt my civic duty to warn my fellow movie goers about Nosferatu. I love movies and rarely feel picky about them but my god was this the worst movie I have ever seen- so much so that I almost walked out.

Sometimes a film is intended to make you uncomfortable but this one did so in a way that was unnecessary and boring from the get go. Every decision of the director took me out of this movie making me very aware of the camera angles, slow pacing, and consistently questioning what the hell was going on. I can count more scenes (and breastage?) than not that made little to no sense and felt unnecessary especially given the 134 minute run time.

Honestly, the only praise I can give Nosferatu is the acting. I really thought lily-rose depp and Nicholas hoult were actually quite impressive


Maybe I am a layman and maybe you'll read many critics reviews of the "stunning visuals", "incredible gothic cinematic delivery", and "powerful religious symbolism" but to that I say touch grass.

Nosferatu was a movie that gave "directed by a conceited man attempting to display his creative genius". It's a skip. Save yourself.

reviews.author: dallonthoruppro
reviews.body:
2 hours and 12 minutes of absolute boredom! WOW!

What a waste of time. Now, sure, you might say it's not boring, and if I like gothic horror I'd love this. Also incorrect. I love Gothic horror. I've been super excited to see this. The pacing is just really bad. It's not even really a horror at all. It's more of a gothic film with creepy elements. It is almost more of a Gothic drama with a vampire? Twas boring.

I can even go deeper with it, because it wasn't just the fact the movie was boring for me, a lot of the elements didn't work.

The lighting and cinematography was just too dark. I get that it's a gothic film, but there are many gothic horror that have excellent dark lighting that doesn't leave the viewer feeling blind, or struggling to see what's on screen. I couldn't imagine trying to watch this at home.

The choices made by the director/writer to have Nosferatu speak in such a slow and gruff voice really added to the frustration of how poor the lighting and the pacing were.

In a film that's supposed to build suspense, how can that happen when everything that's going on is so slow that there's no way you can build upon it?

Even the moments of high tension took so much time, that when things did happen, I was so far removed from caring about anyone in this film.

Were there Gothic elements there? Absolutely. Do I consider this a horror? No.

Just a melodrama involving a vampire Honestly. I understand how maybe the filmmaker was trying to give recognition to each vampire story that was inspired by the original Nosferatu, but even in its originality, this whole movie felt like a bunch of ideas with nowhere to go, and then the movie ended.

reviews.author: johnsage
reviews.body: I sat in a full cinema of horror fans, who all laughed out loud at the extremely poor dialogue and acting. It was so funny it actually works as a young Frankenstein type spoof. As a horror or drama however, this movie fails miserably and is sickeningly pretentious, as I watched I could imagine a room full of self important film students wooping uncontrollably, loosing themselves as the director clearly has, up there own behinds. I truly hope that the director is In fact having a joke with the audience, otherwise he's dangerously delusional to think that this movie is anything else but a steaming pile of poop. But as mentioned, it could actually be the comedy of the year!

reviews.author: daniewhite-1
reviews.body:
"Nearly Not Quite" the third major version of 'Nosferatu', itself a germanised unauthorised adaptation of the novel 'Dracula' follows on from the 1922 and 1979 versions. That's about it. There isn't much more to say. Each version stands about 50 years apart, and each itineration becomes more sexually overt, more explicit, more graphic. The demon vampire's sexual possession and possessiveness towards a somewhat unworldly woman gets more and more leerily layered with each telling.

In this version we can confirm that women don't just have boobies, they also have nipples. That's the kind of thing we are dealing with. The undead demon vampire Count has worse personal hygiene. He certainly looks more undead when unclothed. That's the level that this version has got to.

The original novel has this deeply hidden sexual tension with two young couples (who could easily be married elsewise between the four of them.) The Count and his undead brides. The Count's obsessive love for a living lass. The nighttime visitations.....

'Nosferatu' (22) added expressionism, comparative explicitness in this treatment of the Nosferatu's purposes, and Germanic/European folklore of diseases and devilment.

Then two more versions have built up the sex until its really all that this version is about. It doesn't add much of originality like the '79 version by Herzog did. It just ups the ante by another 50 odd years.

The first half is actually awful, it needs intertitles like a silent film because it is so badly acted, directed and structured that I was watching it as a comedy film ala 'Dracula: Dead and Loving it'. Not only this but the scares, tension, suspense, atmosphere and set pieces are fumbled and fudged like the film was made by an amateur director rather than an auteur. How did the director make 'hounds of hell' - wolf "children of the night" - so bland? The gypsies so uninteresting. The scenery so bland. The Count's coach so cruddy? The list goes on. At the half way stage my assessment was that the piece was poorly written, poorly directed, poorly acted, poorly staged, boringly photographed and unimpressively scored and arranged.

For the second half two things improved: Defoe got the theme and the tone with his performance (although he sounded very alike to the late actor Colin Swift.): slightly hammy. The rest of the cast, finally given something to ground their performances on, them rose to "meat" the mood. In effect Willem Defoe can take more credit that the director for the effectiveness of the casts acting.

Secondly the layering of sex got into it's stride and "revealed all" as to this films method: it's a 50 year updating of the sexually charged themes built into the 'Nosferatu' series, and indeed, literary 'Dracula'.

I rate at 3.5/10 the first half is simply dire rather than demonic; things improve as Willem Defoe gets going and as the utter simplicity of the film treatment is revealed to the audience. My stars are almost entirely for the efforts of the players in the second half of the film, with half a star extra for a couple of well lighted interior scenes and some nice fire lighting. Otherwise this 'Nosferatu' is boring and even "unfunnily" comedic to look at and to listen to.

I recommend only to fans of Willem Defoe, I am struggling to think of any other - numerous - group of film fans to label at this juncture. Perhaps a few people of very niche taste will find a bit more to lapp, lick and like.

reviews.author: berrynic-39228
reviews.body:
The cinematography, sets, costumes and soundtrack are very good but the acting is atrocious. Skarsgaard is terrible as Orlok, the voice he puts on is beyond ridiculous.

I normally love Dafoe in everything he's in but he seems to think he's in a lowbrow comedy here. Lily is just grating and excessively hammy, Emma Corrin looks like she's nearly asleep, Aaron Taylor-Johnson delivers soap opera style histrionics. Nicholas Hoult is always a likeable presence and he's just so-so. Ralph Ineson is always good but he isn't given much to work with. Only Simon McBurney gives an outstanding performance and he's hardly ever on screen.

There are a lot of reviews testifying to how frightening Nosferatu is but apart from a couple of cheap jump scares, I spent most of the time trying to stifle my laughter.

The only scary thing is that I spent twelve quid to watch this empty, pointless rubbish.

reviews.author: b_velkova
reviews.body: At the time, I liked The Witch a lot, but after that, Eggers repeatedly failed to impress me. The message of a world deeming woman's pleasure as demonic is a great one, but it has to be shown. Here, Eggers opts to have it directly recited by Miss Depp, in her little wooden voice. Otherwise, we get a few decent hysterical seizures, and I appreciated the final scene. The pigeon-eating and the plague vomit are disgusting, but there's nothing truly unsettling or even moving. The scare attempts with sudden loud noises after extended silences are downright insulting. As for the vampire-with his walrus mustache, poorly executed accent, and horse-like breathing-I'd probably burst out laughing if he tried to possess me.

reviews.author: photomotophoto
reviews.body:
I watched Nosferatu (2024) yesterday, and honestly, I wish I hadn't. I fell for the YouTube critics' rave reviews, all of them gushing in ecstasy and reverence for Eggers' work. As someone with a deep understanding of the occult, I can confidently say that the director is clearly fascinated by Aleister Crowley and chaos magic. This obsession likely explains his strange desire to remake Nosferatu.

Let's remember, the original Nosferatu (1922) hit the screens after the First World War and the devastating Spanish Flu epidemic, acting as a harbinger of a new plague for Europe-the rise of Nazism. Eggers, true to the spirit of a chaos magic practitioner, has once again timed his version well, aligning it with our current global tensions and uncertainties. However, instead of delivering a profound and relevant exploration of these themes, the film comes across as a vehicle for Eggers' personal sexual fantasies, where he, in the guise of Nosferatu, seduces young and corrupted Ellens.

Feminism Gone Awry Eggers' attempt to nod to feminism is a complete failure. Ellen, played by Lily-Rose Depp, isn't a nuanced or empowering figure-she's a lifeless, inflatable Victorian doll, designed for the entertainment of gentlemen in drawing rooms. Her character evokes no emotion beyond irritation, though the blame doesn't lie entirely with her performance. Eggers seems to have molded her into this hollow shell, devoid of agency or vitality.

The Underground Scene and Sex Magic In the U. S., kink parties and sex magic are wildly popular among the underground and creative intelligentsia-and that's fine. Rituals of eroticism and creative liberation have their place. But where is the artistry in Eggers' Nosferatu? Beyond the superficial aesthetics of chaos and gothic grandeur, the film fails to deliver anything meaningful. Instead of provoking thought or emotion, it indulges in shallow sensationalism.

Where's the Art?

Instead of a fresh or groundbreaking vision, Nosferatu feels like an awkward reflection of Eggers' private fantasies, rather than a sincere work of cinema. The film's attempt at mysticism and depth falls flat, leaving behind a sense of frustration at what could have been. While visually striking, it ultimately lacks the heart and substance to resonate beyond the surface.

Eggers' take on Nosferatu might have aimed to be bold and transformative, but it ends up being nothing more than a hollow echo of the gothic masterpiece it sought to reimagine.

reviews.author: monicakim-40126
reviews.body: I had very high expectations for this and wanted nothing more than to love it, but it was a big miss for me. From the first glimpse of Orlok all I could think of was Lemmy from Motohead, and that thought never left my head. Orlok's voice and accent were also really out of place, somewhat silly, and took away from the movie and from the character. Huge segments of the movie were so dark that I couldn't see at all what was going on and eventually stopped caring. The timeline was also weird. The very beginning skirts over young Ellen and Nosferatu in like 10 seconds. When her husband leaves it's hyped up like this epic journey that was apparently one day? I feel like the whole story was forgotten and this was more of a weak vibe.

reviews.author: pzamost
reviews.body:
There's not much you can really do to make Nosferatu better than all the other versions of it, it's the same old story told again and again just another tired vampire movie with dark shadowy scenery with the vampires undying love for some waif from his past ...whatever. This movie doesn't do much more than any of the others versions it just looks better and sounds better.

I would say Nosferatu is on par with Eggers last movie The Northman which is okay while you're watching it but 5 minutes after seeing it you couldn't remember much about it and don't get that haunting feeling you got from The Witch or The Lighthouse.

All in all if you are new to vampire movies this movie may have you enthralled but to me it was a bit of a snoozer.

reviews.author: Rageypoo
reviews.body:
This is boring. I was interested in the story up to about the halfway point, when suddenly the characters and plotlines they were building up either didn't pay off or completely disappeared.

The movie itself is gorgeous. Each scene is wonderful to look at. The shots were very well framed and enjoyable. There were times that they made certain scenes these kind of...moments that didn't need to be, and it's very obvious it felt like they were milking the moment but it came off awkward.

There were also many scenes that had similarity with the film "the exorcist" and when you watch it, you can't help but laugh. It reaally wasn't needed and felt out of place.

Some of the characters said a lot of exposition to carry the story rather than just doing it, which was disappointing. Some of the lines were put out like theatre than acting.

Overall, this was very hit and miss, and deserves an average rating at best. The story is weak and boring, and the acting while good, can't make up for bad writing.

reviews.author: karajbahal
reviews.body:
I really came to the conclusion that most of the reviewes from the journalists and critics are paid and commercial reviews.

This movie is unbelievably bad, I don't want to waste my time even writing about it but if you went to watch the movie and you came to the same conclusion, never trust the reviews anymore and be very careful with choosing the movie, because it's not just a waste of time and money, it's an insult to the viewers who come to see a good horror movie, but they leave with despair and the feeling of being deceived.

The plot is horrible, many times during the movie I laughed at how patheticly the it tries to scare, and it never could.

I asked my friend how she feels about the movie and she was just mad at the quality of the movie and said she can't believe why they make these ridiculous films.

I think the rating will come down for sure (it's 7.7 now), it's absolutely a 0 for me.

reviews.author: EdoMaliMedo
reviews.body:
Robert Eggers is one of those directors that doesn't quite follow the norm and instead utilizes his own creativity and style to make his films. The Northman, being my favorite film of 2022 gave me hope that this would be another slam dunk. Unfortunately, his style didn't help to bolster anything at all within the story of Nosferatu which has already been told many times. In fact, the movie is quite boring with the first half of the film being nearly unbearable to get through. The design of Nosferatu is needlessly decrepit and the film seems to be more erotic than scary. The character building was extremely weak and no one cared when characters died, in fact, my entire theater laughed during the "dramatic" conclusion.

Willen Dafoes character was a stand out as he nailed the slightly psychotic tinge of the character but no other character comes even close. It's clear Bill Skarsgard put in lots of effort into his role but Count Orlok is just laughable from his over exaggerated accent to his cartoonish mustache, the character looks nothing like the past iterations of Nosferatu. Lily-Rose Depp also plays her character as highly exaggerated and she often speaks as if she's writing a letter which causes the tone to come across as unserious.

No characters are memorable and the story is drawn out to the point of being exhausting. With a shorter run time and more of an emphasis on telling a story that's both faithful and entertaining, Eggers could have made his best film yet. The sound design and cinematography were amazing but it doesn't help to cover up the lackluster essence of the film.

reviews.author: toltuff-90072
reviews.body:
A lovely looking remake with a decent cast but very dull sadly

I managed to catch a screening of Herzog 70s film on Halloween and that is a much better version of the story and better than Coppola's Dracula

Klaus Kinski's performance was chilling to bone but also so subtle it was perfection

There wasn't enough of count orlok in this new film and the design was more distracting than scary, it kept reminding me of Freddie Mercury or Borat must have been the moustache

This new version is near a 1:1 remake just drawn out which makes it's quite tiresome towards the end

Willem Dafoe is brilliant but he always is and gives the dullness a lift

My advice would be watch the 1979 version instead it's far more scary without the use of cheap jump scares and enjoy Kinskis amazing performance.

reviews.author: delaniacollins-17605
reviews.body: I think the title says it all. This was the worst vampire movie I've ever seen, and I'm a B movie lover. From the dreary, colorless background, clothing, and faces to the horrible overacting and constant seizures, I wanted to leave the theater after 30 minutes. I swear I memorized the pattern in the aisle runner. Great actors put to poor use. And why, oh why does a vampire have a breathing ailment? Do vampires even need to breathe? Or grow distracting mustaches. I never go to the theater, it's been years. Now it will be never, ever again. Ruined Christmas day with this horrible, boring release.

reviews.author: arfdawg-1
reviews.body:
The Plot A gothic tale of obsession between a haunted young woman and the terrifying vampire infatuated with her, causing untold horror in its wake.

Don't believe the hype. It's a slow, atmospheric horror movie with many scenes that don't make sense and a few that are really good. The time between the good scenes drags.

I saw this on the 30th and the small theatre of 44 seats was pretty much empty.

The good scenes were with Nosferatu. Overall, the movie just isn't as good as the original, or even the Werner Herzog version.

And here's a couple of questions: why is the vampire so obsessed with Depp's daughter? AND how is it that the count needs to take a boat to his new house when the groom can leave after him and take a horse?

For me the movie was far too slow and atmospheric to be a really good movie.

reviews.author: hadchips
reviews.body: Having what was likely far too high hopes for this movie, we were highly disappointed. Not enough depth of story to be drawn out in a movie that long. Poor use of the villain, too many moments of absolutely nothing happening, with an anti-climactic ending. With the cast in place, there was so much opportunity, especially with Depp, Hoult and Dafoe. Unfortunately, they were given a script that falls flat. There was some pretty good cinematography, but far far too many scenes of waiting and wanting of something to happen. I you absolutely have to see this movie, I would highly suggest waiting until it's out on DVD or digital so you can promptly turn it off once you've met your limit.

reviews.author: TheCynIsIn
reviews.body:
After the movie, all five of us who went to see it shared that we all had wanted to leave early, as the movie was very slow and weird. We now have a "safe word" for letting everyone else know someone wants to leave early and it is "Nosferatu."

I feel that this movie combined the less good parts of Rosemary's Baby with Exorcist and older vampire movies and the way-too-dark Batman movie that I couldn't stick out. They needed to do a much better job of cutting scenes. Normally, we enjoy vampire and zombie movies, but this movie tried to combine art and gore, and could have spent the time used for "hand shadow" scenes and "Ellen convulsing" scenes to flesh out the characters better. I haven't been forbidden from picking out movies for my group after this pick, but I have been put on alert.

reviews.author: jenniffertafoya
reviews.body: It's crazy how terrible this drama movie is. Horror and drama don't mix like what's the point of this movie. It's so bad. It's best to experience a breakup than watching this terrible movie. I hated the writing and nudity scenes. What kind of movie is this? Vampire porn? Idk what's the worst movie of the year? This or the joker 2? Don't waste your time watching this movie. It's not worth it. It just don't make any sense at all. The vampire looked so terrible and bad makeup effects. Part 2 will be even worse if they do it. I wasted my whole life watching this movie. I regret it so bad. I wished I watched something else.

reviews.author: comps-784-38265
reviews.body:
First off, this is not a patch on the 1992 Dracula played by Gary Oldman, Rider, Hopkins etc Yet the scenes are very similar.

What was good : Special effects/cgi/costumes all looked good

It certainly had the cast of actors that should have delivered a good film

But it was not a good film, I sighed with relief when it finally ended.

What was bad:

First off it is far to talky talky talky for no reason. The writer clearly had an attack of verbal diarrhoea, when writing this.

To make this even worse the actors speaketh in a unfathomable manor, indicative of a bygone era, forsooth and then, with, and then, followed by and then. At one point Dafoe's character said someting how nosferfartu had to returneth to place of rest before cock-crows, that another character had to translate 'you mean he has to return to his grave before sunrise'.

Daefoe is a fine actor, but his character was bizarrely comic (unintentionally) and reminded me of the Albert Einstein in the electicity companies advert for smart meters, with Angela Ribbon (former BBC news reader)

Nosferfartu himself was more of a spitting image character by the end and certainly lost much of his 'menace'

All in all, it came across as a rather disjointed collection of scenes, that individually look cosmetically good, but do not join up well in telling the story.

No I would not endure watching this again.

reviews.author: dwd-60860
reviews.body:
I really wanted to like this movie. Great cast, great director and vampires. I was so looking forward to being scared but you are more likely to be scared watching an episode of Friends. Unfortunately, this film is a mess. When will directors learn, if we can't see it (ie. Why so dark?), it sucks. The acting is really shocking. Lily Rose Depp has a decent performance as does Bill Skarsgard. Everyone else seems to think this is a farce. Aaron Taylor-Johnson is laughable. Who knew that William Defoe was so short?

Cut to the chase, this film is not good. If you must see it, wait for it to hit your streaming service. Do not pay extra. It isn't worth it.

reviews.author: erikdj-6497
reviews.body: Slow burn was great for the first 30 minutes, then it dragged on and on and on. Till the end to lead you to a disappointing finish that left you feeling like you got snubbed of your time and money. Way too many unnecessary sex scenes and long drawn out moaning scenes with didn't convey any other feeling other then uncomfortability and a feeling of this movie is wasting my time and money. Next to no action from nosferatu himself and his shadow hand had half the audience laughing. 10% or more of the scenes in this movie could've been removed and would've done it good if they were. Nosferatu also did wayyyy too much talking to the point of it being comical and was just a poor choice in terms of direction. Not scary at all.

reviews.author: daisysu-72152
reviews.body: Each moment of this movie was difficult watch. Not horror at all. The props and costumes fail were a let down. One scene shows the characters costume collapsed. There are several scenes anyone could anticipate but not the gore. Bodies were moving and thrashing about for no apparent reason. There was not a good story line that would mask the gore. The ending was blah. Was the entire focus of this film for shock and awe. The film goes on and on and I waited for something good I could say. Just could not get into this film. If I had bought my ticket, I should have walked out and got my boy friends money back.

reviews.author: kylierempel-14472
reviews.body:
Show don't tell. This movie tried to do both and failed miserably. It borrowed a lot from 70s Nosferatu which is a much better film. There are almost no moments of silence in this movie, it just wants to explain everything to you like you're a small child that needs to be led by the hand.

Nosferatu in particular is super chatty. He wants to give you his full inner monologue. How am I supposed to be frightened of a creature that lets me know its every passing thought? If he was ever quiet I might have time to appreciate the impressive makeup on Bill Skårsgard and have time to be frightened but no he's always yapping.

The cinematography was lovely and the acting was good but that's all the good I can say about it. There was no mystique. It's a shame I really liked Lighthouse and The Witch. But save yourself the time and go watch the original and the 70s version. I rewatched them prior to watching this and they are much better films. This had ambition but was poorly conceived. It didn't trust the audience.

reviews.author: chupacabracito
reviews.body:
Pretty good, but not great. A bit disappointing, really. Having a few more gory special effects does not make it better than the original; in fact, the opposite. It needs more German Expressionism and Dutch Angle, more surreality. It was too literal about the plot, which honestly dragged a bit.

Francis Ford Coppola's "Bram Stoker's Dracula" is way better, both in artistic style and in pacing. There're a few great artistic moments, though. You'll see most in the trailer. And great period costumes, that was well done.

So, to quote my friend Lynn, this was ultimately a NOsferatu, not a YESferatu.

reviews.author: stefstars
reviews.body:
I really wanted to like this one. I'd been looking forward to it, but unfortunately, it wasn't as good as I hoped it would be. It's beautiful to look at, they successfully accomplished the Gothic aesthetic. The story didn't feel fleshed out. Granted, there's only so much they can work off of from the original incarnation of this story. Still, I feel it's enough of a "skeleton" for the writers to have fleshed out a full on story where we could've seen some important character development, rather than rushing us right into the madness.

From the start, we hear Count Orlock say that Ellen is not human - that's why he's so attracted to her. However, it's never explained why Ellen isn't human. She's your typical 1800's pretty young wife who's faithful to her husband and then starts experiencing possession (thanks to her husband making a deal with Count Orlock) and that's about it for her. I wish the movie would've shown instances in the character's life or personality that would've explained what Orlock meant when he kept insisting she wasn't human. This is the case for every other character except Count Orlock, we don't know much about them before everything starts happening and we just have to go along with it.

The strong points of this film are the set design, costume design, make-up, Bill Skarsgård and Willem Dafoe. Skarsgård does an amazing job as Count Orlock. His movements, the way he delivers his lines, he's deservingly the star of the whole thing. Willem Dafoe never misses, I can't think of a role where this man isn't amazing. It could be the dumbest film ever and if this man is in it, he's it's saving grace. In this case, Dafoe plays a character that, like Ellen, goes from 0 - 100 in terms of "going mad", but even it's not sensible, Dafoe's acting chops make it worth watching. Nicholas Hoult (who has come so far since his skins days) he was good, but I feel like he couldn't demonstrate his acting chops as much since the character he's playing didn't seem to be nothing more than a dutiful husband who's reduced to a scared wreck ? The performance that I felt was the worst one in this was Lily-Rose Depp as Ellen. I already explained the problem with her character, but Depp's over acting didn't make the situation better. She counted on her handy dandy "worried face" to get her through the film along with crying and screaming. While she may have the correct look for these kind of films, she hasn't developed great acting skills yet - despite her parents. Hoult did what he could with what he was given, but it wasn't as exaggerated and ridiculous like Depp's performance. This could serve as a good lesson for acting instructors to use to teach "what to do vs what not to do" when a character you're playing isn't written as well.

I'd watch it to appreciate the Gothic Aesthetic and to see Skarsgård's performance. Especially if you're someone who appreciates the Gothic aesthetic, I recommend it, some of the shots (especially at the end) are beautiful. But if you're watching to find a new take on the Nosferatu story to enjoy, you'll be sorely disappointed.

reviews.author: linda-glass
reviews.body: Gross on so many levels, which was all really unnecessary. The story is repetitive and slow, cinematography dark but good. The monster was so silly looking, they overdid it with this horror. Sometimes I couldn't hear what they were saying. The music was always the same and with the dark theme was rather annoying. Constantly the same thing over and over, yep we get it, too long at over 2 hours! 2 people walked out of the cinema halfway through laughing at this thing of a movie. Thr direction is very good though, and some parts are good. But overall, I say skip this one and see something else...

reviews.author: jchampany
reviews.body:
Having long been a fan of the original 1922 version of "Nosferatu", I was compelled to see the newest remake in the theater. While the cinematography was great, and there were some satisfying nods to the original Murnau film, the production at times feels somewhat ham-fisted in its attempts to cram as many spooky tropes into itself as possible.

But the film's true undoing is in the performances from Depp and Skarsgard. Both overact horribly, and both seem to approach their roles with all the tact and depth of a high-school drama student. Skarsgard's accent is particularly heinous in this regard.

While the original film was a masterpiece, this new remake is a disappointing, self-indulgent disaster.

reviews.author: mrcliff4
reviews.body:
This movie is garbage. There's very little character development and the 2nd half of the plot is very confusing. Everyone in the theater was falling asleep. The only part of this movie that scared me was when I thought it was almost over and I saw that it had 1 hour left.

Imagine the worst thing you've ever seen on the internet... I would rather watch that on repeat for 2 hours than watch this garbage movie again.

Once again, the positive reviews are bots.

I need to fill the character count so I'm just going to post lyrics to a related song:

"She's got a date at midnight, with Nosferatu. Oh baby Lily Munster, ain't got nothing on you. "

reviews.author: kgardner67
reviews.body: If I could give this farce less than 1 star I would. Made a mockery of vampire movies. Nothing redeeming about this movie I wanted to walk out of 5 minutes after it started. Had I gone alone I would have left after requesting my money back. Very very disappointing for sure. Bad movie. Don't waste your money. Only accuracy in this were the names of the characters. It was poorly told and poorly shot. Hard to see at times because the lighting was so bad. The acting was ok it was more the cinematography and gore that turned me against this film. I really wanted to see it too but walked out shaking my head.

reviews.author: hswasserman
reviews.body:
I was excited to see this film. But as with another overrated film of his, The Witch, it is just too incoherent for my tastes. It is not too much to ask for a filmmaker to produce a narrative viewers can follow and peopled by characters with whom we can sympathize or even understand.

I get that Eggers didn't want to just imitate the other two films, nor did he appear to want to emulate any other vampire films. Therefore his Orlock looks nothing like the vampire in the 1922 or 1979 versions. His idea is Orlock's soul is literally trapped inside a corpse. That doesn't really work (for me). If he's a vampire he needs to look and act like a vampire. This Orlock just looks like an ugly old man or a zombie. I didn't need to see some handsome dude in a tuxedo and cape but I didn't need or want to see this hideous old beast either. And you barely do see him. I don't think there is a single instance where we really get a good look at Orlock.

Worst of all is his voice. I have read that the actor worked hard to get the voice to where it was, but by God I could not understand a word he said. The only time I did was when he spoke in another language and there were English subtitles. I felt like the townspeople in Young Frankenstein when they couldn't understand Inspector Kemp. Frankly there is no excuse for this considering all the money they spent and all the people who worked on the film. Did no one realize it was impossible to understand Orlock?

The rest of the cast can't salvage it. Depp is certainly pretty and looks right for the role, but there is no way she or perhaps anyone could hope to make sense of her ludicrous character. And what was the sense in having someone so flat-chested go topless? Dafoe does his best to be memorable and amusing as Von Franz, but I was really bored by the time he entered the picture and ultimately his character gives us nothing we have not seen a thousand times before. Nicholas Hoult is certainly handsome and that admittedly went a long way. Lastly the actor who played Knock gave nothing to the role. When we had Dwight Frye and the brilliant Roland Topor as the vampire's servant, McBurney needed to give us more than he did.

Lastly for such a lavish production I have to say the lighting was not good. A lot of the time I could not see things very well.

reviews.author: emailrs
reviews.body:
I had great expectations for this movie from what I read in the reviews. But I have to grade this movie fair minus. The scenery in the film was decent but how the story was told in the movie was poor and boring. There were several dramatic suspenseful scenes that would cut to a different scene too quickly without letting the previous scene play out. I would wait until this movie comes on Netflix or Prime. Probably in the top 5 of my least liked Dracula movies.

It was not even close to being as good as the 1992 Dracula movie with Anthony Hopkins and Winona Ryder. The 1992 Dracula movie was very well made in every aspect.

reviews.author: galgusa13
reviews.body:
A huge disappointment. The disappointment is just as tremendous as the expectation. For what reason was this one of the movies I was most anticipating this year? To witness an undeveloped narrative and a miserable female experiencing orgasms from having a dream about a vampire with a mustache like my uncle? Trust me, just go and watch Twilight, it's much better than this.

Apart from the film's cinematography, the film is boring, not scary, the actors' acting is excellent, but the film doesn't reach a climax, it just stays in the same place for the entire two and a half hours, the first time in my life that I wanted to leave a film before it was over. And I didn't do it, which is a shame.

reviews.author: stick500
reviews.body: Super loud, extremely dark scenes, completely nonsensical plot and cuts, couldn't decipher half the female lead and the monster's dialogue, disgusting sex and vomit scenes, just awful! We walked out halfway through. Have no idea why so many think this is a good film. And I like horror films. The original Texas Chainsaw Massacre is on my top 10 list. The only scene I enjoyed in this film was near the beginning when one of the characters was walking through an 1830s market in Germany. That was it. Please don't reward Hollywood by giving them your money for this horrible film. So sorry I did after reading some positive critical reviews.

reviews.author: dgvi
reviews.body:
Ok I went in with high expectations given that I liked Robert Eggers previous film 'The Lighthouse" and I was looking forward to see what he would do with this but I was very disappointed and fell asleep towards the end.

The screenplay and dialogue were pathetic as a start and it looked like it was written by an amateur and when you have Count Orlok having to explain and talk in his scenes then it takes away from the mystery and intrigue of the character.

Also the whole cast apart from Simon McBurney just felt out of place but the wooden screenplay didn't help.

I would recommend for everyone to go watch Francis Ford Coppola's 1992 version with Gary Oldman where he delivers a masterclass in acting out Dracula.

The cinematography is beautiful in parts however but that's the only positive in this movie.

reviews.author: timesinthesun
reviews.body: Have waited in anticipation for this film. How incredibly disappointing this was. It's not a bad film, it's not a good film, that's exactly how it leaves you feeling, numb and bored. Brought nothing new to the story in it's interpretation apart from the appearance of Dracula and the unintelligible dialogue. The performances were staid and unengaging. What was the point of this film apart from cashing in on the Dracula die hards who will always go and watch anything new. It had nothing to say. Your could have easily replaced Lilly Rose Depp with a cardboard cut out, William Dafoe is now always playing some version of an eccentric nut job, and Nicholas Hoults skills were not used to any great extent.

reviews.author: nickmatveychuk
reviews.body:
I just watched the movie Nosferatu, and while it has a fantastic atmosphere, it fell short in many other areas. The film beautifully captures the eerie, gothic mood of classic horror, with impressive visuals and a haunting soundtrack that really sets the tone.

However, the plot is dull and highly predictable, leaving no room for surprises or suspense. The characters are poorly developed and feel one-dimensional, which makes it hard to connect with or care about their fates. Despite its strong atmosphere, the film lacks the depth and engagement needed to make it truly captivating.

In the end, Nosferatu is visually striking but fails to deliver a compelling story or memorable characters. It's a missed opportunity to bring fresh life to a legendary tale.

reviews.author: stevenkeithjones
reviews.body:
I struggle to see how anyone can rate this more than 3.

Its dull, ludicrous and ruins the gothic horror genre. The acting was hammy, the lighting is dark, the dialogue is stupid and the story is boring and adds nothing.

I have no idea what the aim here was but it won't linger in cinemas so if you are keen to waste a couple of hours of your life, act quickly.

Watch the original if you want atmosphere.

Watch Dracula for a production.

Watch Lassie for a better story and watch the Teletubbies for better acting.

I actually think the Count sounded like an asthmatic version of Nandor on What we do in the shadows!

reviews.author: nastyxfury
reviews.body:
I went to this movie with great expectations. As promised, the lighting and costumes are very beautiful) But this "horrific" atmosphere feels so.

But the loud, pulsating music was more annoying than creating an "alarming atmosphere," and there was so much of it that sometimes you wanted to cover your ears. Characters who yell at each other 80% of the time, this is causing irritation again.

Lily-Rose Depp was very disappointing with her acting, sometimes it seemed so inappropriate that it was almost funny. I felt so bad I wanted to leave the cinema. Some did so...

Big plus for references to the cultural features of Eastern Europe.

reviews.author: some-like-it-hot
reviews.body:
I watched Nosferatu tonight, but unfortunately, I came away rather disappointed. The film felt like a tedious experience, weighed down by a weak storyline and exaggerated performances. Nosferatu himself was neither portrayed convincingly nor introduced in a compelling way.

The dialogues were often stiff, at times even awkward, leaving little room for natural interactions. It felt as though the director wasn't in tune with modern audiences, relying instead on outdated tropes like jump scares and possession themes reminiscent of classics such as The Exorcist. However, those elements failed to bring any fresh perspective or genuine tension.

In the end, the film felt disjointed-an overly expensive ensemble cast with little cohesion or purpose. Despite its potential, Nosferatu failed to deliver the chilling allure one might expect from a vampire legend. A missed opportunity, in my view.

reviews.author: ILikeMovies-14
reviews.body:
I watched "Nosferatu" in theatres about 2 days ago. It left me and my friends heavily disappointed. Let me explain-

The movie starts with the right foot. The picture, actors, atmosphere, everything was amazing. I loved it. I was actively thinking "Man, this is a straight 10". I loved the Romanian gypsies scene and most importantly, it had mystery. This movie had possibly the best mysterious atmosphere I have ever seen, and it was spooky too!! I got scared like 2 times here and there and Nosferatu comes on scene. I am pretty sure that first time he comes on screen everyone in the theatre got goosebumps.

HOWEVER, this skyscraper peak enjoyment that the movie offers end there. Why? Some BIG reasons.

First off, it gets so repetitive and full of filler scenes that makes the viewer too familiar. It simply fades the whole mystery. No more mystery, at least it's scary, right? Right?

Previously I mentioned the 2 times I got scared in the beginning- that was it. I came and paid to watch Nosferatu, a remake of a movie that was banned because of its horror 100 years ago. I am an easy to scare person yet, this only managed to scare me twice by not being warmed up. The jumpscares were Lameeeee...

At least the movie keeps being serious? Well, hard to tell. There is one moment throughout the film (a sex scene to be more specific), that I cannot understand its purpose. It was so cringe and embarrassing, it got the room shocked (cringed shocked). All of that just to follow up with a lame jumpscare? Come on.

I try to keep this review spoiler free, therefore I won't even talk about the ending which I find completely disgusting and embarrassing. I am not a hardcore Nosferatu fan, I didn't know what I was about to watch, but is this really how it was supposed to end? Me personally I didn't like it at all. And neither of the people watching.

By the second half I keep seeing people opening their phones. It was dragged out (with the boring stuff, not the good stuff that we want to see) and it got boring. Along with those 2 extremely weird moments I felt bad for asking my friends to come with me.

At the end, we just watched a weird non-horror extremely cinematic movie. I can't really recommend it. I wouldn't watch it again (at least the second half). I liked "Smile 2" a lot more. Even "The Nun" was more consistent than this.

10- for the starting 5- overall movie.

reviews.author: RaggedEdgeReviews
reviews.body:
F. W. Murnau's 1922 Nosferatu remains a benchmark in silent cinema, blending dread and the supernatural into something both terrifying and transcendent. Robert Eggers' 2024 adaptation seemed poised to evoke similar depths of horror, yet what we are left with is a disjointed, underwhelming experience, weighed down by nepotism and shallow attempts at modern relevance.

At the center of the film's failings is Lily-Rose Depp. While the Depp name guarantees a certain level of attention, it's hard to ignore her glaring miscast as the female lead. Her wooden performance feels out of place in a role that demands gravitas from a more seasoned actor. Her character lacks the depth and emotional resonance necessary to carry the film, leaving a void where empathy and fear should have existed. Her presence feels more like a calculated marketing move than an artistic choice-a reminder of how nepotism continues to plague modern Hollywood.

Nicholas Hoult's annoying overexertion as the poor man's Jonathan Harker is equally disappointing. Hoult seems to be striving too hard for an unnerving performance, resulting in an overly mannered and theatrical portrayal. His delivery is inconsistent, veering between awkwardness and forced intensity, leaving audiences more exasperated than terrified.

Count Orlok was interesting insofar as his appearance wasn't revealed in the film's trailers or promotional art. Orlok's design aligns with Bram Stoker's original source material, but the monster here fails to terrify in the way Gary Oldman did in Francis Ford Coppola's Dracula.

Robert Eggers, known for his meticulous attention to historical detail and atmospheric storytelling, seems to have lost his way here. The film struggles to find a cohesive tone, bouncing erratically between abstract symbolism and traditional horror elements without fully committing to either. The pacing is uneven, dragging in key moments and rushing through others, leaving the audience disoriented rather than immersed.

Moreover, Eggers attempts to infuse the story with modern themes, but these efforts feel hollow and forced, failing to enrich the narrative. The film's focus on superficial style over substance ultimately reduces its impact, turning what could have been a profound exploration of existential dread into an empty exercise in gothic aesthetics.

Nosferatu is a disappointing misfire, marred by poor performances, particularly from Lily-Rose Depp, who you can't deny has benefitted from self-indulgent nepotism. Robert Eggers' usual mastery of atmosphere is absent here, replaced by hollow attempts at contemporary relevance. What remains is a film that feels disconnected from the haunting beauty and terror that should have defined this modern retelling of Nosferatu. Perhaps it was too contrived to remake a remake of a silent film that was made out of protest to a copyright claim from the Bram Stoker estate.

A squandered opportunity that leaves fans longing for the dark, visceral power of its predecessors.

reviews.author: ElJay-W
reviews.body:
It was gross. It was weird. It was badly-acted. It was inconsistently executed, badly explained. It had embedded thematic rules that it didn't even follow. Nothing was consistent. One scene could be magnificently set up, dressed, executed and performed expertly. The next two could seem like they were designed, directed and dressed by 1st year theater majors doing a project. It gives a good *impression* of depth (seemingly done in post-production maybe?) but it's trying so hard to be a lot of things and as an audience member it's doing many of them magnificently... at first. Then it inexplicably gets gimmicky. Then something else is awesome, but gets spoiled by bad acting, or something that breaks the immersion (are the bricks on that wall *drawn*?).

If I didn't know better, I'd think each story beat was shadow-directed and shadow-produced by a completely different crew.

I winced a lot, and for reasons good and bad. The main actress is fantastic and totally carried the movie, but she was not enough. If the rest of the actors were able to perform at her level this would've been really good. Sadly, the other actors either weren't given enough quality direction or just weren't up to their respective tasks.

Nosferatu is a unique tale told in a novel way, especially for this day and age. For this reason it is worth exactly one ride at the theater. Use that gift card and see "something different"

reviews.author: adamb-49813
reviews.body:
If you're there to marvel at excellent cinematography and set design you'll love this film. Truly blown away by some of the often haunting and dreamlike shots. The set design offered absolute immersion in the period it was set and didn't betray it at all while simultaneously helping set the tone the director was going for which I didn't much care for.

As a movie on the whole it felt absolutely devoid of any allure or enjoyment. I'm the first person to go on pedantic rants about how regular movie-goers are spoilt by mainstream media and can't just sit and enjoy a serious or "slow" film. In spite of that I found Nosferatu much too bitter to swallow. It wasn't slow, the pacing wasn't the issue, it just wasn't enjoyable and I suspect the majority of the audience who see this will echo the same sentiment from either side of the fence.

I don't get to decide what makes a film a film, but It feels like an artistic portfolio trying to convey how impressive a shot and moody a tone Eggers could achieve.

I enjoyed seeing some excellent interpretations of the scenes from the book, that felt like they hit the nail on the head if Bram Stoker were to have showed us what he wanted the reader to imagine. The village folk in the carpathian mountains felt that way, as did the victorian streets with rain bouncing off black umbrellas. Delightfully morbid and at times beautiful. Eggers always really nails the historical settings he's going for every time. I was however totally unimpressed by the castle which looked like an empty building site and beyond unimpressed at the appearance of Nosferatu himself. What compelled anyone to to make him 7 feet tall with a giant moustache?

The acting to me felt lacking, but I think the script was the main fault there. William Dafoe impressed me though. In comparison to The Lighthouse I think the method acting there worked so well because the roles given were so vibrant and lively whereas the script here felt flat and the characters weren't at all brought to life no matter how well the actors performed.

This is the utter antithesis of Francis Ford Coppola's dracula that at times was so vibrant and colourful it was cheesy. I see that movie as a work of art, I also see Eggers version the same way visually. Both extreme ends of the spectrum come with their own faults, namely pretentiousness for this one.

reviews.author: jordandf-81572
reviews.body:
Robert Eggers celebrated for his atmospheric storytelling, takes on the classic Nosferatu but struggles to breathe new life into the gothic tale. What could have been a visionary reimagining instead becomes an uninspiring rehash of a story audiences have seen countless times before.

Eggers' passion for the material is undeniable, and his deep research into Dracula folklore shines through. Yet, his reverence for the original films appears to hold him back from shaping a bold, distinctive vision. Homages to earlier iterations are plentiful, and while they exhibit his respect for the source material, they overshadow his creative contributions. Folkloric elements are scattered throughout the film, but their impact feels superficial, often more gimmicky than innovative. The film's tone wavers between gothic period horror and ritualistic folk horror, leaving its direction confused and its execution underwhelming. This lack of focus becomes even more apparent with the film's slow pacing, emphasizing its linear and predictable storytelling.

The performances further hinder the film's impact. Nicholas Hoult and Lily-Rose Depp, as Thomas and Ellen Hutter, deliver underwhelming portrayals that feel inconsistent-veering between exaggerated hysteria and emotional detachment. Bill Skarsgård commands attention as Count Orlok, yet his zombified portrayal feels mismatched with the gothic ambiance, lacking the sinister elegance of previous iterations. Willem Dafoe shines, as expected, and demonstrates Eggers' ability to extract compelling performances even in minor roles. Aaron Taylor-Johnson's character suffers from excessive screen time with little narrative clarity, making him feel misplaced-a problem that extends to other cast members. Despite a strong ensemble on paper, their performances fall flat and fail to bring the story to life.

The film's true strengths lie in its visuals and atmosphere. The meticulously crafted sets and costumes transport the audience to a hauntingly authentic Victorian period. Eggers' use of dim lighting, long uncomfortable shots, and his signature sound design creates a gripping tension that lingers throughout its runtime. Robin Carolan's haunting soundtrack blends seamlessly with the dark world Eggers has created, and a handful of standout shots-particularly at the film's opening and conclusion-are breathtaking, destined to become iconic in gothic cinema.

As a fan of Eggers' previous work, particularly The Witch, I wanted to love this film. However, its safe approach and confused direction left me disappointed. While Eggers captures the oppressive atmosphere of gothic horror, the film lacks originality and coherence, feeling weighed down by its homage-heavy approach. For fans of gothic horror, Nosferatu (2024) may still become an enjoyable classic, offering a moody and visually stunning experience. But for general audiences, it may feel like a movie you want to enjoy but are relieved to see the end.

reviews.author: online-30
reviews.body:
There were some nods to the past and visually some sections of the film were amazing, but for the most part, it was boring, needed music to try and make things more exciting, had a vampire that looked like a bad Frank Zappa (sorry Frank RIP) and just overall a bunch of stupid people denying reality and getting killed.

reviews.author: facundos-12543
reviews.body:
This is the first time I've left a cinema bothered enough to sign up to IMDB and leave a review.

Robert Eggers' Nosferatu is a film with enough interesting technical premises to make you want it to succeed, but fails miserably on each of these and more.

The film begins with an absurd amount of noticeable CGI for each of the sceneries as well as most of its objects, making them annoying to see.

In its defense, it does get better throughout the movie but it's a poor job mostly and leaves you unengaged in some of the long takes that occur at the beginning of the movie.

Throughout the entire movie, the director HEAVILY INSISTS on using a fixed camera that tracks actors and more without any acceleration to give a feeling of "uneasiness" to the viewer, which only works at one point in the film and ruins the pacing of most scenes only to honor this poor attempt at the said technique.

In addition to it, the script is filled with poorly written characters with barely any depth, which is a shame because of the talented cast brought together in the film. These are some of the worst performances of almost the entire cast, I mean it. The biggest exception was Aaron Johnson - who is excellent, but also happens to have the only role with any depth in the film, so it's easy for him to stand out - and Lily Depp who does some great body-acting but otherwise fails miserably cause of her character's awful writing.

The rest only end up looking like themselves simply quoting the script because of their characters' poor writing - not to mention Simon McBurney who straight up did a poor job and makes you wonder whether his character is a comic relief or if he is that bad as an actor.

The editing is pretty bad and confusing - it doesn't handle the story's pacing properly and will leave you wondering what is actually occurring at times or will break the tension for no reason.

The most noticeable example occurs at the beginning of the film when Ellen and Thomas are arguing and a cut will make it seem as if they're going to embark together, when they're only heading to a friend's house. It's not that the cut works that way so you're meant to believe so, but that it's done so poorly that you don't know whether it happens by mistake or not.

It barely touches on some themes like humanity and sexual desire, so you cannot even pass it as a pretentious yet failure of a film.

I'm only giving it four stars because the production level is really good; the costumes are amazing, the sets are at worst decent and only fail during takes of massive scenery, and the SFX and ambient is good.

If you've yet to see it, go picturing that it'll be a comedy and you'll likely have a nice time. If not you will surely end frustrated by it.

reviews.author: aebs-44821
reviews.body:
Remakes are always beholden to their predecessors (or burdened by what has been, to re-use a political slogan), but surely it's no excuse to make such a boring movie. Here, everything is mostly played straight -- nothing is subversive of the original --, but it's still done in such a boring way.

The backstory is expanded a bit, but only to introduce plot holes. How come her husband just happens to work for this guy and this company? And how lucky is it that he chose the one job that could get him to the castle. It's all very unsatisfying, because for all that, character depth remains at the level of a puddle.

The presentation and acting is not that great, especially the latter. Eggers is known for the stilted and theatrical speech of his characters. For the first time, I found it doesn't work at all, as everyone sounds like a parody of themselves in a vampire movie. Dafoe in particular is massively underused. He just seems to have recycled his role from Poor Things without giving it any further thought. Some people praise the cinematography. On the contrary, I found the CGI to be fairly in your face, to the point of being distracting and looking overly sanitized. This ties in to everything feeling inauthentic.

But looking at the cinematography is the only thing going on for the majority of the movie. It is so light on action and actual events. The first half could have been done in 10 minutes in a film with regular pacing. The second half is even worse, however, with the majority of scenes seeming like useless filler of people lamenting how bad the situation is to each other, incessantly. Then the conclusion happens without any involvement of most characters. They were there only to provide commentary about what's happening, it seems.

This one seems like a half-spirited commercial effort. Eggers is at his best when he does unconventional stories, and this is as far from it as could be.

reviews.author: jinxedmihai
reviews.body:
Not what i was waiting for!!

reviews.author: jadejon07

reviews.author: Kostasqc
reviews.body:
Eggers continues the trend of directors who are in love with themselves rather than the audience. I went to the theater pretty excited realizing that I am not going to like the movie after the first 20 minutes.

There were literally 2-3 dialogues in the first 20 minutes or so with the rest of the time spend on visions or characters being delirious.

By the end of the movie I lost count of the times I saw characters being in delirium. If I would give a rough estimate I would say appx 20-25 times?

It's style, style, style, and no substance. The switch to black and white is overdone.

I really can't believe the average rating of this movie as everyone in the theater seemed relieved the movie ended.

Yet the hype is strong as even the ones saying that the movie was boring to death give the movie 6 stars.

Recommended only for people who love "art" made by Marina Abramovic, because the movie gives really similar vibes.

reviews.author: a-hilton
reviews.body: I give it two stars because Nicholas Hoult and Lily-Rose Depp worked really hard to try and liven this up, at times acting beyond their limits. Unfortunatley the film left me bored and unmoved. It was just too visibly dark, too slow, uninspiring and unoriginal. There were no shocks, I couldn't care less about any of the characters and the only way I could keep interested in the plodding script was to laughed occasionally at some of the absurd parodies that were lazily thrown in. In fact the only feeling I had throughout the film was - oh yes another creepy horrible bloke is preying on young vulnerable girls. This would probably have gone unnoticed a couple of generations ago but now it seems just gross. This for me therefore was an unnecessary, poorly written and directed remake of the classic tale. Sorry actors, I know you did your best...

reviews.author: ramirez13-2
reviews.body:
This film had its moments, but ultimately it fell short of reaching its full potential. Frankly, had it been directed by anyone other than Robert Eggers, it might have been far better. In my view, this critique extends to most of his work.

I'd rate this a C+, or perhaps a 5.5/10, primarily for the performances, which were the standout element. Both the original and Herzog's 1979 version surpass this one in every conceivable way.

Eggers' penchant for agonizingly slow pacing and his tendency to overinflate every scene makes even a two-hour film feel interminable. While he is often lauded as a visionary, I find him to be one of the most overrated directors working today. His overly stylized approach and excessive indulgence did a disservice to what could have been a flawless modern remake of Nosferatu. I struggle to see the appeal of his work, as it often undermines the material rather than enhancing it.

This movie wasn't an enjoyable experience, but it's hard to fault the film, story, or cast... they all had the potential to deliver something remarkable. Instead, it feels like the blame lies squarely with an overrated director whose pretentious and uninspired style continues to spread like a plague, draining life and energy from otherwise promising projects. It's a frustrating example of how a director's "elite" but uninspired influence can overshadow the true potential of great material.

Wow.

So... this had to be a winner, right?

Well... no.

Far from it, actually.

It was too long, too loud, too hysterical, just too much.

The story is actually quite small.

Yet Eggers drags it to no less tham 133 minutes.

After like 1,5 hour, I got really bored

And, as long as it is, I felt that certain important parts of the story, were done way too short.

His journey to the Carpatians, for example.

That could have been so much more interesting.

Same goes for the Demeters voyage.

No.

Just no.

The pacing was so slow that it felt like barely anything had gotten started by the time the film ended. The amazing cast had overly long and wordy dialogue that it took you out of the experience and made you not want to listen to them. And to top it all off, most of the characters just acted weird and horny most of the time that it either made you uncomfortable or roll your eyes. The one positive I can say about this film is the atmosphere, character and set design, and overall look of the film was immaculate. reviews.author: aaronstent-24124
