Sorry, I simply cannot comprehend all the positive reviews and a rating of 7.7?!!!

This is one of the most poorly written, cliche-laden films I have ever seen. It also features several hilarious way over the top performances where actors appear to fake eye rolling seizures *so*over-the-top people in audience erupted in laughter (one person even threw paper at the screen!) .

The dialogue seems like it was written by 9th - 11th graders with gems like "a FORCE worse than EVIL!" "You're a Villain" and tons of manic, panicked characters running around literally jumping "to and fro" yelling "He's coming! He's coming!"

Truly one of the slowest-moving dull plodding films I have ever seen. One can't help but feel bad for the actors.

This adds nothing new to the canon.

Save your money and see any one of the countless better versions of this same story, which most adults have probably already seen at least 7 times.

Oh...and it just kind of "ends"! (Not that your even paying attention at the end, but just sayin')

Imagine a movie worse than Nosferatu. Spoiler alert: you CAN'T!

You'll laugh out loud (but for all the wrong reasons).

reviews.author: RobinMahalla
reviews.body:
I'll start with what I liked. The acting of Lily-Rose Depp was pretty impressive. Getting gypsies (Roma) to do their acting was well-done. Nosferatu speaking reconstructed Dacian was original.

I'll continue with the aspects that fell short. Although the acting regarding Lily-Rose Depp was pretty good, the scenes of her being possessed were rather comedy than horror. They could have added the creepiness by panning out in those shots rather than giving a close-up of her tweaking, which was funny. The movie starts with that shot but it's her pleasureful, orgasmic moaning--which is a nice way to make the entire room uncomfortable.

The acting of the other characters, lacking substance and emotional backing, made them first and foremost feel like inbetweeners. Nosferatu's growling like he had survived dozens of lung-cancers in his long life was irritating since it took him exhaustively long to say a sentence.

The dialogue was really bland, and this can be used as criticism considering they were partially adapting the great writing of Bram Stoker.

The visual effects didn't really grasp the Gothic element they were attempting. Filled with fog, alternating from waking up from a dream to waking up from the dream within the dream altogether constitute a movie that must be watched with low expectations, otherwise you will be disappointed.

This is a hollow attempt to capitalize on a classic, failing to capture the atmosphere or essence that made Nosferatu timeless. A remake no one needed. Welcome to new hollywood, once again.

I had really high hopes for this film. It had all of the right ingredients (and I saw the the 1920's version years ago) - the story is a good one, Eggers as Director, Hoult, Skarsgard and Defoe in main roles.

Unfortunately I found it boring and over-long. It didn't involve me at all, there was no tension as the scenes just felt like a series of set pieces tacked together.

So detail? The Directing seemed too focussed on creating a gothic atmosphere, to the point that the darkness in some of the scenes was so Intense, they didn't need the actors.

The editing - felt like they were determined to put in everything they'd filmed - if there were 30 minutes cut, it would have been much tighter and more coherent.

The acting. Lilly-Rose Depp could have been anyone - the character just needed to look pale and wan. Skarsgard was in shadow so much that, again, could have been anyone. His spoken parts were almost in the form of a voice over. As for Aaron Taylor-Johnson, so over the top and hammy, it was almost a comedy turn. Defoe and Hoult, played Defoe and Hoult - you know what you're going to get.

This film was a real disappointment. Having said that, the person I went with, thought it was good.

reviews.author: devlamantia
reviews.body:
The 1922 Nosferatu is a classic, no question about it. It's one of the earliest and most influential films in cinema history, and its eerie atmosphere, haunting visuals, and Max Schreck's unforgettable portrayal of Count Orlok helped shape the horror genre. Even today, Nosferatu holds up as a masterclass in suspense and mood. So, when I heard about the remake, I was intrigued. It's a big name to take on, and I was hoping to see a fresh take on something so iconic. Unfortunately, the result didn't quite live up to the potential.

One of the biggest letdowns is how little the remake brings to the table in terms of innovation. It feels like the filmmakers were so focused on trying to recreate the original's aesthetic that they forgot to add anything new to the story. The pacing drags at times, and instead of feeling like a reimagining or something that pushes the envelope, it ends up feeling like a pale imitation. The original Nosferatu was groundbreaking for its time, and there was so much room for the remake to innovate, but it plays it safe and doesn't bring anything new or exciting to the table. It's a bit of a missed opportunity.

That said, one bright spot in the film is Lily Depp's performance. She really gives it her all and brings a level of depth to her character that stands out. There's a vulnerability and emotional complexity in her performance that gives the film a much-needed spark. It's clear that she was fully invested in the role, and her work is genuinely impressive. However, even though her acting is a highlight, it doesn't completely save the film from its other flaws.

The biggest issue is how slow the movie feels. There are moments when it feels like it's dragging on forever, and you start to wonder if anything's ever going to happen. The tension isn't built up in a way that keeps you on the edge of your seat, and instead, it just kind of meanders. I was honestly waiting for something to happen, but it often felt like it was just repeating the same things over and over. And while I get that Nosferatu is supposed to be atmospheric and unsettling, it's hard to feel engaged when the story doesn't really go anywhere.

Overall, this remake just doesn't capture the same magic as the original. While the 1922 Nosferatu is a haunting masterpiece, this version feels more like a rehash with no real sense of direction. Lily Depp's performance definitely stands out as one of the few bright spots, but even her talent can't carry a film that feels like it's stuck in the past. It's frustrating because there was so much potential here to reframe the story for a modern audience, but instead, it feels like the filmmakers just missed the mark. At the end of the day, it's a remake that doesn't do enough to justify its existence. If you're a die-hard fan of the original, it might be worth a watch just to see how it compares, but don't expect to be blown away.

reviews.author: levybob
reviews.body:
I should have known better than to see Robert Eggers' 'Nosferatu'. Right or wrong I did not enjoy his previous films, 'Witch' and "Lighthouse' and so the odds were that I wouldn't enjoy his latest. And ... I didn't. Truth is I wanted to walk out of the theater at about the thirty minute mark, but as there was still popcorn in the bag, I remained.

Let's get something out of the way. Eggers does a great job at creating a mood. The film is dark, the music chilling, the cinematic perspectives altogether perfect. For that I give him credit. What the film lacks is story (and no I have not seen the original silent version of this film). I was never altogether certain of what was going on, or why characters elected to do what they did or how they did it.

A young real-estate salesman leaves Germany for a small unnamed nation many hundred miles to the east. He goes alone, alone on a horse with no apparent baggage. He meets up with a village-worth of Gypsies who, for some reason, soon vanish (never explained). His client, a count whose accent is impossible to understand, and who remains only a shadow, attacks him as would a vampire, but for some reason (again unexplained), neither kills him nor turns him into blood-thirsty killer. Bad enough. But here's where the confusion really sets in; innocents murdered, townspeople turned insane, a rat infestation aboard a ship and then in town, contrivances impossible to believe (the world's foremost vampire-killer just happens to be in the small infested city), and on and on it goes.

I wanted a simple statement of intent. A simple theory of what the evil count might actually be. Now I know that it's usually better to show than to tell. But in this case, a simple one minute statement of (a) what's at stake and (b) why, might have gone a long way in helping me with this film. But, sadly, none came.

Finally, Willem Defoe. I enjoy him. Always. A fearless actor. But in this film I could not escape the feeling that he was ... gasp ....fooling around; like a mischievous high-school boy in a school play. His vampire-fighting warrior seemed always a second away from laughing at the ridiculous dialogue. And if not that, then the over-the-top intensity and staging.

And I guess that's that.

Like I said, I should'a known better.

reviews.author: deedeeallstar
reviews.body: Wow. Just literally left the theatre. This movie was SO LONG AND BORING! Loved The Witch and The Northman....so I was hoping the director would blow me away again. Sadly, not this time. Lily Rose Depp is lame in it. Just got the job becasuse she's yet another nepo baby. I just watched Juror 2 so I was hoping Nicolas Hoult would be good. Nope. reviews.author: brescd01
reviews.body:
I love the Dracula story and anything related, so I was eagerly awaiting this movie's release. I have not read the other reviews. First, what I did not like about this movie: I thought the script was very bad. The (German) characters all speak early 19th century prose English with English accents and even allowing for the archaizing, their speech was extremely stilted and unnatural. Meanwhile, Germanisms (like "mein herr") are inserted here and there, the Count speaks in a language I did not recognize, and there are a variety of characters who inexplicably speak Romani (I think), something else (Hungarian?), and of course Romanian. This makes the script both precious and jarring. The men's acting was a bit hammy at times and this didn't help things, for example William Dafoe who is otherwise such an excellent actor (or can be with better material). I found the movie slow and I had trouble staying awake, there was actually very little action, remember this is a remake of a film whose plot is well known, so that added to the tedium.

Insofar as things I enjoyed, the cinematography, costumes, and sets were fine, and I thought the Count was nicely portrayed and costumed. His blood-sucking was erotic and enjoyable more or less. There was a considerable amount of female nudity of course, what vampire film can exist without this? This might be a turn-off to some watchers because it so clearly suggests "the male gaze".

So finally I found the movie slow and unpersuasive, I could not really get into the "vampire mood", and I didn't enjoy it.

reviews.author: Hippo_on_trial
reviews.body:
My expectations before seeing this movie were sky high but I left the theater loving the original even more. Happily, for me I do love silent movies specially in the horror genre and I do believe that this remake could have accomplished more if they done the movie as silent as the original was, relaying exclusive on subtitles, music and imagery. You can't give a silent movie a voice and expect that it wouldn't demand rights. The perks of doing remakes of legendary movies like the many "King Kong" remakes are as follows. The film must feel accurate to a certain period of time, the manus must be carefully rehearsed and finally, the movie must relay on the original storyline and imagery. This remake follows its period of time to a certain degree and follows the original movie in a way that makes the film instantly forgettable. The manus inaccuracy is a conversation that must take place. In this remake the female roles are more prominent with the main change that they are, let's say, less eager to comply to the wishes of their husbands. The manus has many flaws. If the goal was to scare the audience, its fails mostly because it never really follows the visuals with accuracy and can be monotonous and tedious at time. The visuals look like paintings in a way that makes the movie feels AI, resting authenticity and casting a veil of stiffness over the final cut that takes the attention away from the original story instead of improving or resuscitating it. This movie wasn't the horror roller coaster I was expecting. It was darker than a cave but only with one blood thirsty monster lurking in the dark and he is taking Ozempic. The problem is that Nosferatu was too afraid of coming out to scare the audience. Giving a silent movie a voice challenges risking the soul of the tale. It's difficult to replicate old things. The art of film making changes constantly over time. Directors don't always have the luxury of adjusting to the tools of the past. That has a devastating impact on the dramaturgy of the remakes of silent movies. By giving Nosferatu a voice, Robert Egger, the director, made him unnecessarily human, relatable, vulnerable, less scary and even leaving the audience feeling sorry for him at the very end. We don't want vampires to die that easily we want them to hunt us in our dreams. That wasn't though the biggest problem this movie's main character has. Let's address the elephant in the room, Bill Skarsgård. If Bill Skarsgård was the right cast for this movie they just misused his undeniable talent. Let's be clear his physical features weren't the right ones for the bat-like Nosferatu of the original movie. Why cast a hunk as an actor to have him constantly hidden in the darkness making the worst horror version of himself. The makeup artist tried very hard to make him look like "Nosferatu" but they didn't succeed with it. If you wanted to know why you see so little of him during the movie or why every scene with him was so dark, here is the answer. The director wasn't thrilled with the results of how he looked. Why not casting someone perhaps less famous like Quinton Boisclair who played "The Angel" in the tv-series "Midnight Mass" or Jarred Germaine initially casted on "Alien Romulus"? Actors that might be not as skilled and accomplished as Bill Skarsgård indeed is but with they have the right features, the right proportions and complexion, the right eyes and the undeniable monstrousness of the original Nosferatu. Instead of those they casted the famous Bill Skarsgård and even dubbed and manipulated his voice so why misuse him that way when they couldn't even use his voice. Why not cast another actor with the right features? It's always harder to destroy a beautiful canvas like Bill Skarsgård to create a disfigured and disproportionate monster like Nosferatu.

Another mistake was the casting of Willem Dafoe. His character was like cut and pasted from one of Egger's previous movies. His acting was too predictable and even his makeup as a now older man felts too familiar for the storyline. Willem Dafoe is the kind of actors you really need to transform with makeup to make it work, otherwise his appearance will destroy the movie putting the audience to think about his other iconic rolls. His roles are as predictable as Marilyn Monroe roles were during her whole career and Ann Dowd still are in every movie she is on. Another issue with the movie was relaying too much on candlelights. The imagery was darker and less visible than the original movie. To make this kind of lightning effective you need to use another lightning and special effects. Audiences can't relate to candlelight as a source of illumination or element of horror anymore. This is something the majority of the world's population seldom use nowadays. But the worst scenes of the movie were the ones portraying the voyage of Nosferatu. Imagine how this movie could have improved with some of the scenes of Andre Övredal's "The last voyage of the Deméter"? Any how, I'm very disappointed with this remake, so much room for improvement. Robert Egger despite of doing brutal masterpieces like "The Northman" and "The Witch" made this vampire movie feel like Disney for adults and a horror fairytale where the female victim feels indeed like the real villain of the movie. This is a movie as expensive as "gone with the wind" but it's screaming desperately for a soul. This is definitely not the best gothic vampire movie ever done, nor is this better that the original or any of Robert Egger previous work. If you want to se a romantic gothic vampire movie, see Coppola's masterpiece "Dracula".

reviews.author: Gardenia-01
reviews.body: A terribly strained and tedious movie. Bram Stoker's Dracula was infinitely better and was as movies should be " Entertaining ". I couldn't wait for Nosferatu to end. The acting was mediocre, but maybe it was actually the direction which again made things quite contrary. Save your money. Give it a miss, go and watch Bram Stoker's if you have not seen it.

reviews.author: izabean
reviews.body: I was so excited to see this remake but it let me down. The cinematography and costumes were great, but it was slow and lacked potential for things that could have been added. reviews.author: drjgardner
reviews.body:
There are only 3 good films about Dracula. The 1922 silent version "Nosferatu" with the incredible Max Schrek, the 1931 "Dracula" with Bela Lugosi, and the 1992 "Bram Stoker's Dracula" with Gary Oldman. The 2000 "Shadow of the Vampire" in which Willem Dafoe transforms himself into Max Schrek deserves mention. After that there are a bunch of also-rans and, of course, the flops.

This one is a flop. For many reasons, it's too painful to remember them all. Suffice it to say that the attempt to translate German Expressionism into a 2024 film simply doesn't work. The makeup doesn't work and the language and gestures don't work. Simply making the film dark and having people move in shadows isn't enough to imitate the wonderful photography of the classics. Attempting it is misplaced hubris.

if you dislocate all four limbs at the same time then you would be less disjointed than this new Nosferatu movie. You can't call it a horror film. Unless you are describing Lily-Rose Depp's acting. Pretty sure the goths will scream bloody murder whilst eating glass and pretending to be undead, but this movie beat them to it. You are better off tracking down the original and giving that a look see, but if look you must, dont get mad as Bram Stoker's family cant sue due to any copyright claim has expired.

reviews.author: jrcicchino

Do not waste your time to see this movie. The original movie may have been good in its time, but this movie did not translate well as a remake. They could've adapted it to today's horror standards, but failed to do so in this reboot.

It dragged on and on, and it was super predictable (I never saw the original, as an fyi). It was painful to sit through the whole film, and I feel that the skeletal plot had potential, but the writing was awful. There was not a single moment throughout the entire film that was even slightly scary.

reviews.author: mohabshalaby-54341
reviews.body: Very very verysilly and a complete waste of time. This is one of the worst movies I have ever seen. The plot makes no sense, the acting is either overdramatic or completely lifeless, and the special effects are laughably bad. There is no trace of horror in this so-called horror movie. The pacing is unbearably slow, and the jump scares are predictable and ineffective. The dialogue is poorly written, adding nothing to the already weak storyline. By the time it ended, I felt like my eyes were sore from enduring such a disaster. Avoid this movie at all costs; it's not worth a second of your time."

reviews.author: thechrisfigaro
reviews.body:
The inclusion of these explicit and unnecessary themes does nothing to enhance the story or pay homage to the original material. It's as if Robert Eggers used this project as a platform to explore his own personal kinks under the guise of art. The end result is a film that feels less like a reimagining of a classic and more like a vehicle for the director's own masturbatory creative whims.

The choices made here, particularly the overtly sexualised elements, seem to serve no greater purpose than shocking or provoking the audience. They lack narrative justification, leaving the film feeling hollow, exploitative, and far removed from the terrifying elegance that defines Nosferatu.

reviews.body: It gives fifty shades of grey meets nosferatu. I was expecting more horror but was instead met with over sexual possessions and a story with no real feelings. The movie drew on for far too long and wasted performances from great actors. If it would leaned more in the genre it was marketed as, horror, then there might have been something to look forward to in the movie. Some scenes drew on for too long doing too much and very little at the same time. The movie had great visual effects and music choice. The makeup department did great. reviews.author: danielcalegari
reviews.body:
This movie Nosferatu is bad in several aspects!

1) It tries to imitate the dark atmosphere of the old 1922 movie.

Almost all the scenes are poorly lit, at night!

Look, who stayed up after 8pm in 1850? Nobody!

In fact, they didn't even use that many candles to light up the rooms, that's just something in modern movies.

2) The movie is about a young woman who is recently married, hysterical, schizophrenic, with some disorders, which are poorly treated by the crude medicine of that time. She has night wet dreams about... for god sake!

3) The movie goes downhill and looks like the classic "Poltergeist" about demonic possession. But the demon is something more subtle and is only in the girl's subconscious... or he is an old creature from nowhere. Dracula is more interesing, of course!

4) The characters are irritating and very affected, exaggerated!

It gets to the point you wish the vampire would kill them all and the movie would end quickly.

5) All the good guys wear capes to protect them from the constant winter snowfall.

But no one gets a snowflake, ever!

6) The happy, sunny ending is so sugary that it made everyone who watched the movie get diabetic. Thank goodness there was a doctor around to treat us.

7) Rats and the Black Death in a German town... it sounds like something medieval, along with the crazy professor who studied alchemy.

reviews.author: secretnerdbatcave
reviews.body:
This movie has great cinematography, cannot complain about the visuals. The costumes were on point with the era. Lilly Rose Depp portrayal as Ellen was well done. The story stared off interesting then felt like I was watching your typical Dracula movie. Some of the acting was way over done, family called this an artsy movie.

Count Orlock's character was very disappointing in my opinion. They made him look like a character in the video game Castlevania and Skarsgard's portrayal felt a bit comical at times that the theater was laughing how bad some of this scenes were.

Overall I don't see why people are loving this movie. I think the main points could have been covered in under 2 hours without the exaggerated acting from other cast members in the movie. Even though it was a beautiful visual the lackluster storytelling and typical plot points makes this a non-recommendation to my horror friends.

reviews.author: lonzo95-940-300272
reviews.body:
Yes, the production values were excellent. The cinematography as well. And there were a couple of shockingly horrific scenes.

But there were several spots that really dragged. How many times did I have to hear about the Nosferatu character that "He's coming." ? Well get there already!

I can't say I'm an expert on the original story, but there was no reason for the director to stick to it faithfully. Was there this much of the Depp character in it? This thin sickly "girl" is the film's focal point? I was losing interest in her. Far better to focus on would have been her friend, the actress that played Diana in The Crown.

Ah well, me, a horror fan, got bored half way through. I so wanted to like it.

reviews.author: miaaaseth
reviews.body:
First off, obviously this is a gorgeous. The costumes, the sets, the cinematography .. All impeccable. I enjoyed every second of it with that perspective! I also really liked the actors. But, there's more to a movie, and it just didn't pull through.

My overall take away is that I didn't really feel it. I felt no relation to the characters (did they have personalities at all?), and when the movie ended I was like «meh».

I really liked the build up, which was creepy, eerie and everything one could hope for really. But then it seems like they just forgot that was the vibe they were going for? The last part was -really- intense, like «I felt overstimulated»-intense. And more ..modern, in a way. I can't quite put my finger on it, but my impression is that they couldn't decide between being close to the original Nosferatu or to have a broader appeal - and the result is that it's neither and just in a weird limbo situation. And, what's with the jump scares? They felt really out of place, and I feel like they cheapen the movie. Just lean into the weird, eerie thing - that's way more scary.

I really, really wanted to love this movie, but I probably won't see it again - there are better adaptations out there.

reviews.author: craig-snell-151-149427
reviews.body:
I read many reviews of this movie before deciding to go and see this at the cinema, the majority of these were either positive or very positive, and to be perfectly honest I have no idea why.

This is Dracula, but it isn't, it's Count Orlok. If you want to see this done properly watch Bran Stoker's Dracula with Gary Oldman. Yes you have Keanu Reeves rather pitiful English accent, and Nicholas Hoult nails that (it does help him being English) but the film is far superior, it evolves the 'Count' character much better than Nosferatu. You can empathise with him and his reasons for being what he is. Nosferatu does not evolve in any way, there is no origin story, he is just an evil being who likes the taste of blood.

Yes the effects were better in this new film, but that is just a matter of having better technology,

Don't take my word for this, read the book, watch both movies and judge yourself, if I didn't know better, I would have thought someone did a find and replace on the original screenplay, changing Dracula to Orlok and then asked ChatGPT, to take out all aspects of character development from the screenplay.

For what he was given Bill Skarsgard give a good performance as an evil blood sucker, he was believable, but the point of Dracula is that he is twisted from being a good all round bloke by the death of the love of his life, suggesting that evil is made not born. Nosferatu throws this in your face.

So to summarise my muttering, this is Dracula by another name, but they should have left well alone.

reviews.author: karachaliosx
reviews.body:
Few films in recent memory have left audiences as bewildered and disappointed as Nosferatu (2024). Billed as a bold reimagining of the classic 1922 horror masterpiece, the movie instead descends into a mire of poor creative choices, lackluster performances, and an utter disregard for its source material's legacy. While remakes often tread a fine line between homage and innovation, this film tragically fails to honor either, making it, in my opinion, one of the worst cinematic experiences in recent history.

A Directionless Vision

The first glaring flaw lies in the film's direction. Helmed by a director who seemed more interested in imposing their artistic pretensions than crafting a coherent story, Nosferatu (2024) meanders without purpose. Gone is the haunting atmosphere of F. W. Murnau's silent original or even the eerie gravitas of Werner Herzog's 1979 reinterpretation. Instead, we are subjected to a visually incoherent and tonally inconsistent film that doesn't know whether it wants to be a psychological drama, a gothic horror, or a satirical commentary on modern anxieties. This indecisiveness creates a jarring viewing experience, leaving the audience more confused than captivated.

Subpar Performances

Much of the blame for the film's failure must also be attributed to its cast. The titular Nosferatu, played by a prominent actor known for their roles in arthouse cinema, delivers a performance that is neither menacing nor tragic. Instead, the character feels like a caricature, devoid of the mystique or menace that made Max Schreck's original portrayal iconic. The supporting cast fares no better, with performances ranging from wooden to over-the-top. The lack of chemistry between the leads only compounds the problem, undermining any emotional stakes the film tries to establish.

A Script That Betrays Its Roots

The screenplay is arguably the film's weakest element. Instead of crafting a compelling narrative, the script opts for a disjointed structure filled with pretentious dialogue and unnecessary subplots. The decision to modernize the story results in a loss of the timeless quality that defined the original. Moreover, the attempts at social commentary-whether on capitalism, technology, or the environment-feel ham-fisted and out of place, detracting from the core horror narrative. By trying to do too much, the script accomplishes nothing, leaving audiences alienated and uninvested.

A Visual and Auditory Misfire

If there's one aspect of Nosferatu that should have been its saving grace, it's the visual presentation. Unfortunately, the cinematography is a chaotic mess. The excessive use of CGI robs the film of any authentic atmosphere, making the gothic settings feel artificial and lifeless. The over-reliance on dim lighting and shaky camera work further detracts from the viewing experience, often making scenes difficult to follow.

The soundtrack, too, is a major disappointment. While the original Nosferatu used silence and an evocative score to heighten tension, this remake bombards viewers with a jarring mix of discordant orchestral pieces and inappropriate modern tracks. The result is a film that is not only visually unappealing but aurally grating as well.

A Disservice to Horror

Perhaps the most unforgivable sin of Nosferatu (2024) is its failure to be frightening. The original Nosferatu is remembered not just for its innovative filmmaking but for its ability to instill genuine dread. By contrast, this remake relies on cheap jump scares and predictable horror tropes, failing to create any sense of suspense or unease. The lack of originality in its scares makes it feel like a generic horror movie dressed in gothic trappings rather than a worthy successor to a genre-defining classic.

Conclusion

In its ambition to reinvent a cinematic legend, Nosferatu (2024) manages to accomplish the opposite: it diminishes its source material while failing to stand on its own merits. From its muddled direction and uninspired performances to its lackluster script and shoddy production values, every element of this film feels like a missed opportunity. While remakes always carry the risk of falling short of their predecessors, this film's failure is particularly egregious, given the rich material it had to draw from. For those seeking a memorable horror experience, Nosferatu (2024) is best avoided. Instead, revisit the classics that remind us why this tale of terror has endured for over a century.

reviews.author: mentiramivida6
reviews.body:
I went into the movie not knowing much other than the silent classic version. So I was expecting something new, creative and completely different from the silent version. What we are given is a disastrous remake no one dared ask for. Sure the clothing and setting were era appropriate but that's about it. And whose decision was it to make the vampire of all vampires a pitiful rotting chicken legged oaf? This is from the perspective from a person who saw the original.

From the perspective from someone who didn't see or even know much of Dracula; "I just kept wishing for the end to come quickly".

If you can bare a silent film even a little bit that is 100% better than this drivel.

reviews.author: andrewhambling
reviews.body:
I'm a huge fan of Robert Eggers and I made my whole family (9) go and see this movie.

Its just so slow and I waited and waited for it to get better.

It was so boring and silly.

I've never in my whole life (50) wanted to leave the cinema before this movie and I've never seen as many people leave a movie in quite as many numbers as I saw with this movie.

Every single person in my family hated it and only stayed to the end for me.

It was a huge disappointment considering the high expectations I had. I'm gutted.

If your unsure about this but still just wait for the stream and you can't use just your remote when you're sickened enough.

reviews.author: alessiofast
reviews.body:
Review: The movie had a theatrical quality to it, feeling more like a staged play than a traditional film. While this approach offered moments of dramatic tension and intimate performances, the overall story didn't quite come together. Even knowing the narrative beforehand, I found it difficult to grasp the full picture, as the film seemed to meander without clear direction.

The slower pacing, while perhaps intentional, made it hard to stay fully engaged. I'll admit that I, and a few others around me, dozed off at times. When the lights came back on, the shared expressions in the theater suggested that others felt a similar sense of detachment.

That said, it's clear the film aimed for something bold and different, but it didn't quite resonate with me. For those who enjoy more experimental, dialogue-driven pieces, it might still be worth a watch.

reviews.author: gazottojr
reviews.body:
I don't get the current 7.8 stars (as of 01/03/25).

I give it 5 stars for the visuals and photography, but this movie lacks a soul. It was boring to the point of me snoozing every once in a while for the first half, and then struggling as hard as I could to stay awake for the second.

It's just too long and the story doesn't feel right in the realm of timing.

To put it in perspective, watch The Shadow of the Vampire, where the same Willem Dafoe that plays "Van Helsing" (same character, different name) in this movie, plays Max Schrek (aka Nosferatu) in the first one. It's night and day.

Don't waste your time and money now. Wait for it on streaming so you can pause in between scenes to drink a much needed cup of coffee.

reviews.author: soggybottom94
reviews.body:
It's quite a feat to remake a film from the 1920s and make it less entertaining. If you want a solid remake of Nosferatu with something to say, watch the 1979 Herzog masterpiece. That film beautifully tackled a story of tragic immortality and the power of true love that can validate the mortal experience. This movie is just an ennui-infused deposition of death and decay that uses the legacy of Nosferatu to pull out cheap and ineffective jump scares over and over.

You won't be scared. You won't be thrilled with the direction. You won't care about the plot.

I'm gonna to give it a 4 because I do love Dafoe and most of the costumes. Dafoe steals every scene he's in.

Also this version of the Count is a joke. The voice is silly and the mustache is even sillier. Kinski and Shreck were miles ahead. Somehow, the makeup adoring his body looks more fake than the effects used on Shreck in the 20s.

I really wanted to like this movie. But the longer it drug on, the more palpable my disappointment became. The worst sin of the entire film is what they cut. The cuckoo clock featuring a skeleton instead of a bird from the first two iterations is nowhere to be seen. That loss of macabre fantasy is a microcosm of this entire film.

It's Nosferatu without the soul. Enjoy your jump scares and tits.

reviews.author: atozser
reviews.body: For my people who are die hard Dracula lovers hoping the love story and haunting beauty of the originals would be recreated....don't plan on it. With Bram Stoker's Dracula affiliated with this, don't plan on the beauty of that film incorporated. This was a waste of talent and beautiful people. A waste of incredible cinematography and costuming and haunting sets, turned into a boring waiting game shot in the bedroom with the main girl crying half the time. The majority of it is freaking slow and omg just boring. No back story on the main creature. No transformation of the creature to showcase his intellect and power. Bill's talent is hugely wasted, Aaron's talent is wasted. The story jumps back and forth and is pointless and again, a waste. Dafoe was a bad cast. Could have been so much better. Utterly disappointed in this film.

reviews.author: TMAuthor23
reviews.body:
If you're looking for obscene gore, sexual perversion, and general nastiness...then this is for you.

There are directors who choose to direct because it gives them an outlet for their perverted fantasies. This is that kind of movie.

There is nothing socially or artistically redeeming in this film.

The stunning thing is, is that If this film were released thirty or forty years ago it would have received an X rating.

Oh, how times have changed.

No surprise that traditional reviewers (populated by thirty somethings) rate this so highly.

Forced to add a line or two to achieve the minimum characters required. Ugh.

Gross.

reviews.author: milicaradosavljevic-35770
reviews.body:
The movie has the most dull storyline and lead actress has some serious acting issues.

Ending of the movie feels like they couldn't come up with anything slightly interesting so they were like "Let's just let them improvise". Set and location is great and it really makes up for the whole vibe they were trying to achieve but everything else is just a waste of time, money and film tape.

The movie left us with thousands of questions - why and how did they have the connection, where is the story behind the cooperation of Nosferatu and Mr. Nox, how did the vampire left his castle when the nuns told that he mustn't leave the ground on which he was cursed etc.

Movie in a word - Abomination.

reviews.author: dobrasinovicdj
reviews.body:
Empty, boring, already seen, no magic, no idea. I stopped to watch, then next day thought maybe I should give them a chance.

Actors good, but in the wrong movie.... Nothing.. ...

We already know every scene, and even a place for people in the scene and we are ready and what.....instead of something new original we got the same.....so boring, slow, my God, I can't belive that this movie got good reviews.....

While the lighting gives the air of mystery, that it was dark throughout the movie was not just annoying but also took away from elements of surprise, fear and shock. It just made it difficult to hold your attention.

reviews.author: jflicks
reviews.body:
All and any stars go to the crew and artists who made the material aspects of the film...Costume, set, lighting, in camera and cgi effects. The story, script and most performances did not meet the calibre of those crafts.

I think Nicholas Hoult and Aaron Taylor-Johnson did their best given the script was really trite and story just so boring and superficial.

I'm sorry I wasted my money and time on this film.

It said nothing new. It lacked any kind of subtlety or intelligence. Completely vacuous.

Such a missed opportunity to progress the story and genre. Or say anything really. It'd be better as an editorial spread or picture book.

reviews.author: kaylarebecca-90102
reviews.body:
I'm actually so shocked by how many positive reviews I am seeing for this movie. It was beautifully shot and had strong actors but that was not enough for me. This movie draggedddd. It was very hard to stay interested and I felt very bored with the storyline. I honestly think it would've been better if it was a shorter movie but everything that happened was so spread out.

Also, it barely felt like a vampire movie to me and most moviegoers in my theater shared the same sentiments. They really should've scrapped the vampire idea and just made him a sex demon and it probably would've been better in the context of this film.

I don't know how to properly put this into words, but this movie felt like one of those bad movies from the past that becomes a cult classic and for whatever reason people are convincing themselves it is outstanding.

I would not recommend this movie to anyone. In fact, I will do the opposite.

reviews.author: BA_Harrison
reviews.body:
I've lost count of how many Dracula movie adaptations I have seen. I've seen some great versions and some fairly terrible ones, but none have bored me quite as much as Robert Egger's Nosferatu (a Dracula film in all but name).

The pace is leaden, the script is pretentious and the acting unimpressive (Bill Skarsgård, with his comical Transylvanian accent, being the worst offender); all of this might not have been so bad had the visuals lived up to hype - I had read that the film was a feast for the eyes - but somewhere along the line the decision was made to drain the film of most of it's colour, to the point that I think it would have been better if they had gone the whole hog and just filmed it in black and white.

The script delivers nothing new, content to retread the well-worn basic plot from Bram Stoker's novel - nothing wrong with that, perhaps, except that the sluggish direction, the pompous dialogue and the overlong runtime make it a chore to sit through. I would have preferred it if Eggers hadn't stayed so close to the source material and had just gone a lot crazier - it might not satisfy the purists, but it wouldn't have been so completely and utterly boring. Two and a quarter hours feels a lot longer.

2.5/10, rounded down to 2 for disappointing me with the rats: apparently, 5,000 live rats were used in the film but it doesn't look like that many.

reviews.author: etaylor-29731
reviews.body:
I've heard Nosferatu praised as a masterpiece of silent-era horror, so I went in with some curiosity, only to find myself grappling with boredom from start to finish. The pacing was excruciatingly slow, making it hard to stay engaged. For a film celebrated for its atmosphere, the tension often felt nonexistent, replaced by drawn-out scenes that did little to move the story forward.

While I can appreciate its historical significance and the haunting design of Count Orlok, the novelty of the visuals wore off quickly. The lack of compelling characters or a gripping plot left me checking the time more often than I'd like to admit.

Ultimately, Nosferatu may have been groundbreaking in 1922, but watching it now felt like a tedious exercise in endurance rather than an enjoyable cinematic experience. Perhaps it's better left to film historians and those with a strong appetite for antiquated storytelling.

reviews.author: richardoccleshaw
reviews.body: The worst vampire movie i have ever watched even old silent black and white vampire movies are better than this. I fell asleep twice, so did my daughter and lots of people started texting and being busy on their phones during the film, which I normaly detest people doing. Depp was uninspiring and wooden and dracula was laughable, a sad old man with Copd hiding in a corner! Can't see the point of the ending - why a creature who has lived hundreds of years would simply give up and die like he did was a massive anti climax - but then so was the whole film. Expected better from this particular director.

reviews.author: iamlalazarov
reviews.body: The film failed to transmit anything, but confusion. I wasn't scared at any point, I wasn't mystified, I didn't root for anyone. It failed to even make me curious about the origin of the demon. The performances were bland, the only character that spoke with any sort of gravitas was the vampire. The screenplay makes little to no sense - where was the hero's journey? What's the story - "evil comes to your town and will only leave after it bangs your wife, because it used to bang her, and you can't do anything about it"? Where is the audience to insert itself? Accents - set in Germany, but everyone speaks with a British accent, except the demon who speaks in the well known Dracula accent. On the technical side, it's way too dark and it doesn't sound good. There is not a drop of realism to allow for immersion. As we left the cinema, no one said a thing, no one looked like they enjoyed it.

reviews.author: stefanijakozic
reviews.body:
The first part of the movie is ok. At first it is interesting, the viewer thinks this is going somewhere. However, slowly as the film is coming to the end the viewer realises there will be no interesting plot. At some point movie just ends without a real climax. Furthermore, the entire plot is ridiculously simple and predictable.

The cast and acting is great but not put to a good use. Cinematography is also great, and costumes too. However, again, there is almost no plot and therefore it is excrutiatingly boring. This movie is more or less pointless, beautiful and visually well done but pointless.

reviews.author: Reels2Watch
reviews.body:
Director Robert Eggers is known for his meticulous style in classical horror films like The Witch and The Northman, both features receiving high praises. In Nosferatu, its obvious Eggers spent a good amount of time in the quality of the cinematic sceneries but fell short on the screenplay.

The first few minutes grabbed my attention but dimmed quickly like the darkness throughout the film. Nosferatu is a slow, sluggish burn drama, horror about Count Dracula - Count Orlok (Bill Skarsgård) and the young lonesome, depressed Ellen Hutter (Lily-Rose Depp) that falls into the desires of the Count. The majority of the story revolves around Ellen's husband Thomas Hutter (Nicholas Hoult) desperately trying to save her and the town from Count Orlok's macabre intentions. Thomas is joined by Friedrich Harding (Aaron Taylor-Johnson) and the eccentric Prof. Albin Eberhart von Franz (Willem Dafoe). The storyline gets lost in the extensive scenes of the immense gothic castle and stone tombs. Ultimately, the conclusion was exciting but not worth the wait.

Lily-Rose Depp had a bland performance. I did not find her Exorcist like convulsions one bit thrilling, much less the crotch shots. Lily-Rose did not present the aspects of purity and innocence the way Dracula likes them. She is definitely no Mina Harker.

The other performances from Nicholas Hoult and Aaron Taylor-Johnson were typical. Hoult was better as Renfield and Taylor-Johnson was better as Kraven. Willem Dafoe could have toned down the comedic sarcasm and added some Green Goblin madness.

Last, but not least, Bill Skarsgård earns my praise. He was fang-tastic! He rarely disappoints, especially when it comes to horror characters. He brought the chill factor with the dark creepy voice and haunting looks. I wanted to see more Skarsgård. If more quality time was put into Count Orlok, Nosferatu would not have ended up leaving me coals in my stocking this Christmas.

reviews.author: goregunn
reviews.body: When I first saw the trailer I had high hopes for this movie. It had an appearance of a very dark and brutal horror movie. But alas it was the complete opposite once I found out the cast I should have just stayed home and saved myself the complete and utter waste of time and money. It had no serious tone it at all it had an excruciating comical tone to it. The actors all seemed to be trying to hard with their abysmal actions and terrible use of Olde English. The monster makeup was the worst it looked like the creature effects from the newest it movie. I don't know if skarrsgard had something to play in that decision but terrible choice. Two hours of utter nonsense and bad acting!

reviews.author: rchalloner
reviews.body: There is much to appreciate in this film, including the cinematography, acting, sets, costumes and gothic atmosphere. Unfortunately as a horror film it doesn't work. When I go to see a horror film I expect to have a few shocks and scares and feel the hairs on the back of my neck stand up, but sadly, though beautiful to watch there was nothing to stir the blood in this version. This is the second remake of Murnau's 1920 classic which remains, in my opinion, the most frightening vampire film ever made and one of the great horror movies of all time. The 1979 Hertzog / Kinski version was an interesting and scary variation, leaning towards Count Dracula rather than Orlock. Why then make a third film which really adds nothing new and with a central character (Orlock) who is clearly based on Gary Oldman's Dracula, without being nearly as profound and frightening. There is nothing wrong with Bill Skarsgard's performance; it's just that he has nothing really different to work with and so his Orlock is just a rehash of past vampires. That is the real problem - we have seen it all before and the storyline is too familiar to provide any real chills.

reviews.author: kingricksimon
reviews.body:
Well, what can i say? This movie "zieht sich wie Kaugummi", after a couple of time i only thought: "is this film going to end soon?".

It felt like i watched a series about 6 hours -but it was only 30 minutes.

Seriously: if there is nothing else in your life -go get one. You wanna watch a "dracula movie"? Go see the Bram Stoker one.

Bill Skarsgård as Count Orlok at first i did not recognize. His voice sounded like Kayvan Novak in "What We Do in the Shadows". If you pitch up his speech to double speed... well this film could save like 45 minutes of airtime and might get a better rating by me.

This movie (without credits) is about 2 hours. It feels like 12 hours of art-movie without any twists or story (´cause u know it -dracula, nosferatu, penny dreadfull ...).

Don´t waste your time. Don´t go into a cinema. Maybe try it with a free stream -at least you don´t have to spend money and the staff will not have to wake u up and make u go home :)

reviews.author: pnguin911
reviews.body:
I forgot this movie was coming out and then today was surprised by the trailer plastered everywhere.

I watched it and all through it the same thing kept popping in my head, "I've seen this already".

'92s Dracula with Keanu, Wynona, and Gary Oldman. Literally every scene in the trailer was point by point identical to that movie. And yes, I know, Nosferatu is a ripoff of Bram Stoker's Dracula, but when the ripoff, seems to be completely ripping off one of the greatest versions of Dracula (Oldman embodied sensuality, pain, anguish, and Horror so perfectly).

I'll probably wait until this hits streaming. I know Bill Skarsgard is great...but When I heard Willam Dafoe was in it, I truly Thought he was going to be Nosferatu...to find out he's the equivalent of Van Helsing...a little disappointing.

Not trying to knock Eggers (never seen any of his movies), but just by the trailer...really missed the boat on this one.

reviews.author: craziebtch666
reviews.body: Heavy breathing, slow start, fairly adequate acting.... I was really hoping this movie was going to be an updated version of the B&W movie of the same name, but to my dismay, I was subject to almost an exact retelling of Bram Stoker's Dracula with Keanu Reeves. This movie was, at times, boring(I yawned quite a few times) & bland, sometimes too over-the-top for no reason. Throughout most of the movie, heavy breathing, rather than dialog was used to convey different scenarios....it became quite annoying. My husband's reaction was "this movie was an hour too long"....he's right...that's 2hrs & 12 min I'll never get back.

reviews.author: barryhastings-54288
reviews.body: As others have said a beautifully shot film, the setting is so vivid you can almost smell it, sadly it's out-stunk by wooden acting and lack of any sort of comprehensible story. This really is a bad film, which is a shame as a lot of effort has been put in but it just doesn't work, I was utterly bored within 30 minutes, and left about 30 minutes before the end. My lasting impression is that it was trying to be tongue-in-cheek, but took itself too seriously to pull it off (and very obviously that is not what they were going for). It felt in places like there was backstory that had been shot but subsequently been cut, and some sequences seemed brusquely short, Tom's escape from the Castle for example. Cannot recommend.

reviews.author: martyn-hardy
reviews.body: I was looking forward to this and yes the casting seemed promising and as we watched the film I agree with the comments about the filming and attention to detail. But it just didn't grab me. Nicholas Holt was good and Willem Defoe was over the top excellent but the rest was a bit disappointing and in some places just not very good IMHO. I hadn't seen the original so reading about it being like Dracula was strangely reassuring but it seemed to be trying a little too hard. Having said that the ending was quite emotional and well constructed if somewhat predictable (that's not a criticism, just a byproduct of the story as told). So, overall not particularly impressed ( yes I know I couldn't have done any better )

reviews.author: buirgejones
reviews.body: Ahhh man...why???? Pretentious and boring. What the hell Eggers? Go back to A24 as your films after leaving have "sucked". I am sad as he is a talented director and the acting was sooooo bad. The female lead Depp? Was such a bad actor and should take some acting classes. Is she just manipulating her name to get into film? Well we all know how Depp sold out and has had so many horrible films. The story is also horrible writing! What was he thinking? Orlock needs a respirator. The scary old dude with a scary mustache. I actually looked at my watch so many times and debated walking out! Don't waste your time and do not pay anything over 5 bucks to see it.

reviews.author: rubenssss38
reviews.body: Nosferatu had its moments, but overall, it wasn't what I expected. While the actors delivered solid performances, none truly stood out as Oscar-worthy. The film's pacing felt unnecessarily stretched, making it longer than it needed to be. Visually, it had its appeal, but the story failed to leave a lasting impression. Lily-Rose Depp is clearly on her way to becoming an It Girl, but she needs to be more selective about her projects. Her recent choices, including this one, lack the substance to match her growing star power. As for the lead male actor, his performance was forgettable and didn't elevate the film. Ultimately, it didn't feel like a must-see in theaters. In hindsight, I would have preferred to wait for it to hit streaming platforms. It's not a bad movie, but it didn't fully sink its teeth into me. Overall, it was a decent attempt, but it left me wanting more bite and less runtime.

reviews.author: bretfiona
reviews.body:
This movie tried to be artistic and visually interesting but ended up feeling long and mostly boring. The plot is quite poor, some things don't add up and we lack a back story.

Too many « possessions » scenes by the main actress and her theatric made me cringe at times. Her facial expressions were very repetitive and lacked emotions.

Some of the dialogue was hard to understand.

The Harding family and the sex scene were useless to the story line.

Was really looking foward to this movie, but got out of the theatre quite disappointed. This movie had so much potential but end up lacking substance.

reviews.author: ballardchristopher24
reviews.body:
When the first thing you say is, "well...it looked pretty I guess" you know it's a wrap. With bland performances, gimmicky jump scares, and horrible pacing, my wife and I were slowly bored to tears. Every scene was a poor copy of Coppola's Bram Stoker's Dracula, just made so much worse in every regard.

Lily Depp did have some amazing visual and physical performances that needed zero CGI to look creepy, unfortunately used so often it became repetitive. Aaron Taylor Johnson was completely wasted. Defoe did his best with what was given, a mediocre Van Helsing.

Just watch Gary Oldman in Bram Stoker's Dracula and you'll have a much better experience.

reviews.author: theromanempire-1
reviews.body:
What a waste as this film had a great potnetial as it had an epic cinematography the scenery was awesome and the gothic atmosphere was superb but the movie like others said too was so booooooring and slow that i'm sure i would have left the theater in the middle of the movie if it was not for that great cinematography which succeeded in keeping me in my seat until the end and thank the lord vampire i stayed cause at last i saw a great ending to a terrible boring film.

Really now besides the cinematography the ending is worth all your money and time.

The moment the vampire was united with the woman everything was perfect and the music theme played left you intense longing for that scene to never end.

Anyhow this version could have been way better if they have done it in a different way but anyhow is worth a view and then it's up to you to decide but u have been warned. A boredoom is very likely during most of the film.

Cinematography and gothic atmosphere grade A++++ Overall grade just a C and i'm generous.

reviews.author: alexabalint
reviews.body:
As many wrote before me, I feel nothing new to the Dracula but feel misleaded that they changed (only) the names and England to Germany (completely unnecessary though). Actors were extemely unprofessional for me, I've seen better high school peformances. It was over the top, unnatural and just simply awkward to watch. I think they also supposed to convey extreme sexual tension, even in awful situations . The constant moaning of the characters are very offputting too.

In addition to the above, the movie is extremely long, and fully uneventful in the first hour. There are random episodes, which, if you've left out, would not jeoperdize the comprehension of the movie or would leave out important information.

Some commented about the nice cinematography, which I coudnt appreciate, but if its for you, maybe you will.

I feel robbed about the 2.5 hours wasted.

reviews.author: Mia_Meri
reviews.body:
I had high expectations for the movie since I've enjoyed Eggers's previous movies. The beginning of the movie looks great and there was potential for something great, but unfortunately the movie loses its focus in Germany. We modern people know our vampires and therefore it felt unnecessary for the characters to spend so much time wondering what they were facing. It all felt very pointless and didn't move the story forward or add anything to it.

I also felt bad for Lily-Rose Depp, whose character didn't develop anywhere and neither did her expression. Same for Willem Dafoe's role which seemed detached from the rest of the movie and was a waste of good actor's skills.

I also felt very uncomfortable watching yet again women being sexually assaulted on screen for no purpose. Yes, classical vampire stories revolve around sex and violence and death, which I have nothing against. But in this case I was forced to watch Lily-Rose Depp's sexual encounters and assault from the vampire's perspective. As if I was the perpetrator of the acts. And these parts in the movie brought nothing to the story.

I truly had great expectations for this movie, but would have to recommend people to rather watch the original Murnau's Nosferatu (1922), Bram Stoker's Dracula (1992), and/or the undervalued Shadow of the Vampire (2000).

reviews.author: ryanjtongue
reviews.body: I hated this film. I hated everything about it. I only watched 40 minutes, then walked out and went to a Nando's. I'd read the novel, so knew roughly what I was in for plot-wise and had seen the trailer so knew it would be relatively artsy, but this made me feel a strange blend of miserable and irritated that only The Favourite has made me feel before. Lily Rose Depp was pretending to be a Victorian woman in an extremely irritating way, and nobody could like her character. Nicholas Hoult was playing a withdrawn polite guy who pulled some sort of anime-fear-face pretty early in, and I can't imagine why anybody would like him either. The count's voice was just deeply, deeply annoying, and it took him far too long to say anything, and was largely just a shadow lurking in the dark, such that whatever artistic quality that might have the main takeaway from it is: "I don't like this. I don't like the way he speaks. This feels like a waste of time, and I can't see anything. Let's leave" and that would be the sensible thing to do. No regrets. This was only irritating, miserable trash.

reviews.author: integratedzero
reviews.body: The acting felt stilted and the pacing was sluggish. Some scenes felt overly dramatic, with characters reacting excessively to minor events. The artistic choices, while aiming for an edgy atmosphere, often felt gratuitous and confusing. The narrative was undermined by the protagonist's inexplicable and repeated sexual encounters with the monster, despite her husband's presence and her own unsettling justifications. The woman's exposed breast's didn't hold up the execution which lacked the impact of a strong horror story. The lack of character development and the predictable plot twists further diminished the viewing experience.

reviews.author: jungletechno93
reviews.body:
It's hard to imagine a weaker version being made. Even Tim Burton couldn't have butchered it this badly (and there is a faint trace of his aura through the presence of Rose-Depp).

You know where you are from the very start. The jump scares, OTT sound design and severe gloom of the opening sequence are so overblown that all possible veins of subtlety are severed. There's no room from there to build atmosphere; only to pile on more affectless set pieces, and to continue making relentlessly, inexplicably bad decisions.

It doesn't matter how many Eastern European folklore experts have been consulted to best approximate ritual gestures; or how much lavish period detail has been deployed, getting the annoying hats just right; or how perfectly the colour palette has been matched to early Zulawski or Szulkin or whatever, when the end result comes over like a mash-up of David Copperfield with a bad teenage memory of the Coppola version, given a cinephile sheen. You can have all the 'real fake snow' you like and the effort will still be wasted when your film still somehow carries the vibe of a contemporary CGI mess.

In another move that feels (perhaps unwittingly) synchronous with our times, the thing is full of posh English accents. These might sound good to Americans or the politically heedless. To me they're simply a reminder of how comprehensively the upper classes have invaded popular culture in the UK. They are the true vampires of the piece. Netflix and the BBC have a lot to answer for in this regard; although the sections in the plague town also reminded me of Michael Apted's 1983 film Gorky Park - where cold war Moscow is populated almost entirely by English character actors - but with significantly less talent on display here.

The weakest figure is Nosferatu himself. This isn't the actor's fault. The design of the vampire simply doesn't work. Making him bulky and having him bite at the heart rather than the neck comes over merely as an attempt to be different. There are reasons he wasn't like that in the Murnau and Herzog versions. Eggers was obviously proud of his call, given how long the tease shots go on for before we actually see the guy's face - so when we do, the sense of bafflement and underwhelm really hits home. Why is he such a straight, unsensual vampire? It's as if all the potential eroticism and mystery and camp and transgressiveness and power to disturb has been drained away and replaced with Anonymous Horror Guy, leaving primarily a really stupid deep voice for us to focus on.

Most of the best bits from Murnau and Herzog are glossed or avoided or dispensed with fairly swiftly. Despite throwing in some folk horror stuff that doesn't really fit, the story rattles along. The ship docks - and suddenly we're wading through a treacle of Historical Drama. The second half of the film is freighted by pointless reams of extra plot. Willem Dafoe running around giving daft exposition and having arguments with non-believer townsfolk, as if performances like the one he gave in Light Sleeper never happened; the vampire and Rose-Depp over-explaining metaphors to one another; there is just way, way too much dialogue. By this time all the dreamlike beauty of the Murnau is long lost in the breeze.

I can see the cathartic benefit in constructing a Merchant Ivory town of posh twits, to then have them all brutally slaughtered by the invading other. But this is not what happens. In fact, it is not a spoiler to say that by the end, 'normal' life has weathered the storm; and the film emerges from all the gloom as a fantasy of survival for the liberal middle class status quo.

Sadly, I get a strong impression that thanks to his immersion in detail, the director was not even aware of this net result. He doesn't seem to have considered the big picture: politically, sexually, or even really as a film. I hope he gives up or is removed from this level of production, and returns to a small scale he can better handle. (I thought The Witch was ok, and I really liked The Lighthouse; although the existence of a Norse epic passed me by until the algorithm started hammering me with Nosferatu hype.)

reviews.author: Yasemin_Genc_1991
reviews.body:
Nosferatu had it's merits, but was ultimately disappointing.

Though it had a nice cast, it often felt like they were overacting and shouting.

It was cinematically beautiful in lots of ways, in fact there were a few stills that really took me.

But it was incredibly slow, and lacked substance.

There was so much talking, and not much being said.

The depiction of Nosferatu was one dimensional, and unnecessarily gross.

The theme of things being unnecessarily gross was pretty constant throughout.

There was a real lack of complexity to the characters and their relationships with one another.

There was a lot of time taken to show things that didn't add much, and no time taken to provide more depth.

Shame really, since it's a story with so much potential.

reviews.body:
My review: spoiler free.

With an over bloated run time, sub par acting(minus Dafoe and Hoult who carried the cast), and a once terrifying vampire nightmare now subjected to looking like a Russian Bond villain, this movie was a bore.

I will commend a fantastic soundtrack, and beautiful cinematography.

If you're into those weird over sexualized films that seem to try and "push boundaries" for that "critical acclaim", this flick is for you.

But even as most vampire flicks have a decent dose of seduction, this one decided to go full blow Euphoria with fangs, adding subplots that didn't need to happen, or just plots that didn't need to be.

This almost 2.5 hr movie could have been an Easy 90mins if Bills vetec leap frog "voice" wasn't so unnecessarily dragging.

reviews.author: theavalonsaysmoo
reviews.body:
Really wanted to love this movie. I'm not sure I even like it. Visually, it's perfect, everything is exactly right, rich and evocative. It is worth seeing for this alone. But at times, the overly-mannered and composed visuals skew towards 'spooky wes anderson'.

After a very strong, dynamic and deeply unsettling first act, the narrative shifts into an odd, stuttery, jolting gear. The pacing gets jumpy, syncopated, we leap from scene to scene. We are told that time passes, but we are not given the opportunity to feel this.

The best way that I can describe it is that it felt like the film was a rapidly moving flashlight beam sweeping through a dark room. We are shown just enough to understand the narrative, but the world beyond is unknown.

All-in-all, it's a fine outing. But there have been so many interpretations of this source material. So many writers and directors and production designers have brought this material to life. Sadly, when viewed among its peers, this interpretation is just a bit bloodless.

reviews.author: patrikmiranda
reviews.body:
Well, first of all, I have to say that the main highlight of this movie is its cast, which features many talented actors and actresses. In fact, I really think this might be one of the movies with the most Hollywood stars assembled in one place.

Lily-Rose Depp truly shines in her role and is undoubtedly a standout in the cast. Her facial expressions and performance convey the struggles of a woman tormented by a villain, and she successfully shows us the full range of her character's emotions and her own potential as an actress.

Nicholas Hoult is another highlight of the movie. I was deeply impressed by his character and his performance, which was outstanding. Everything I said about Lily-Rose applies to him as well!

Willem Dafoe delivered exactly what he does best: an amazing performance. He adds brilliance to the cast and pulls us further into the plot. Unfortunately, his character's development was squandered in the final part of the movie, which made all the build-up feel wasted.

Speaking briefly about Bill Skarsgård, Aaron Taylor-Johnson, Emma Corrin, and Ralph Ineson, they all did an excellent job in their respective roles. Each of their characters had unique traits that added depth to the movie and made it even more enjoyable.

Briefly I have to say something: Visually the film is very good, and that should be praised, and while the cast is undeniably brilliant, the screenplay is where things falter. I have to confess that I didn't watch the first movie, but I don't think that's necessary, as I'm reviewing this movie on its own. The movie started off great, and I was ready to give it a solid nine out of ten. However, it took a turn that prevented me from doing so.

One thing worth mentioning is that the movie builds up a lot of anticipation for the finale. I was expecting some truly epic scenes involving fights and intense moments, which would have elevated the movie significantly.

Unfortunately, the movie took a disappointing direction, featuring numerous inappropriate scenes, especially in the final moments. This completely undermined the well-crafted story that had been developed up until that point.

In conclusion, the cast did an exceptional job, but I feel the screenwriters failed to deliver. I'm not sure if the first movie followed the same tone, or if this was a specific creative choice for this movie, but it ultimately left me dissatisfied.

reviews.author: movie_buffalo
reviews.body:
So, I was finally able to watch Nosferatu, a film hailed as a reimagining of the classic Dracula tale, and while I appreciated certain aspects of it, I left the screening feeling it had fallen short in many ways. The movie, although visually intriguing in parts, seemed more like a series of Instagram-worthy moments than a project meant for the grandeur of the silver screen.

Being familiar with Dracula as a story that evokes nostalgia and dark charm, I had high expectations. Unfortunately, this adaptation struggled to reach the emotional depths or timeless appeal of its predecessor. The film moved at a rushed pace, failing to establish the tension and intricacies of the narrative. The central relationship between Orlok and Ellen, which had the potential to be a profound exploration of love, obsession, and doom, was underdeveloped. Instead of delving into their complex bond, the film spent too much time on extraneous imagery that felt more like filler than substance.

The production design also left much to be desired. For a story set in old Germany, the setting failed to transport me to the eerie and atmospheric world it was trying to create. It seemed as though the filmmakers opted for an overly minimalist approach, possibly constrained by a tight budget. As a result, the locations lacked the haunting beauty or historical richness I would have hoped for.

The portrayal of Dracula, or Count Orlok, was another disappointment. The makeup felt almost amateurish, completely underwhelming for a character meant to terrify and captivate in equal measure. Instead of a commanding and fearsome presence, Orlok's voice was oddly trembling and lacked the vicious gravitas one associates with the role. There was no sense of deep pain, no inner torment, which left the character feeling hollow and unconvincing.

That said, Nosferatu wasn't without its redeeming qualities. The music was a standout element-well-composed and perfectly matched to the tone of the scenes, enhancing the eerie atmosphere whenever it was needed. A handful of moments were undeniably cinematic, with beautiful visuals that lingered long after they ended. But these highlights were too few and far between to save the film as a whole.

Nosferatu is a film that shows glimpses of promise but ultimately fails to live up to the legacy it seeks to honor. It's a mixed bag of fleeting brilliance overshadowed by poor execution and missed opportunities. While it may appeal to a generation seeking aesthetic visuals over substance, it's hard to imagine it holding the same lasting appeal as its predecessor.

reviews.author: zwarriorultimate
reviews.body:
"Nosferatu" is a modern reimagining of the classic horror tale that dates back to the silent film era, but despite its striking visuals, it falls short of delivering a compelling cinematic experience.

The Positives:

Visually, "Nosferatu" has its moments of brilliance. Some scenes are shot beautifully, particularly Thomas's journey to the ominous castle, which captures an eerie, foreboding atmosphere. The gypsy encampment scenes, as well as the sweeping shots of both the castle and the ship, offer a sense of grandeur and isolation. The cinematography in these moments truly shines, making good use of natural landscapes and gothic architecture to create an unsettling mood.

The Negatives:

Unfortunately, the visual appeal does little to save the overall narrative. Having not seen the original Nosferatu, my comparison is drawn more to Francis Ford Coppola's Bram Stoker's Dracula (1992), a film that still outshines this latest effort on nearly every front despite being over three decades old.

The pacing of this film is one of its major downfalls. The story feels like a washed-up retelling of the same old vampire lore without adding much in terms of innovation or emotional depth. There's a noticeable lack of urgency in the progression of the plot, and the characters feel distant and hollow. The protagonist, Thomas, fails to elicit any strong empathy or connection with the audience, while the antagonist, Count Orlok, is barely fleshed out. We don't receive enough backstory or development for him to come across as a complex or menacing figure. He remains a shadowy presence without clear motivation, which diminishes the tension and terror that should be central to this story.

The abruptness of the film's ending is particularly disappointing. After an already thin narrative, the conclusion feels rushed, offering no satisfying resolution or meaningful takeaway. Count Orloks death seems so underwhelming that audience reaction is "that's it ????" For a story that has been told in various forms over the years, this retelling fails to add any new depth or layers to either the vampire mythos or the characters involved.

Final Thoughts:

Nosferatu (2025) struggles to live up to the expectations set by both its cinematic predecessors and the weight of its own legacy. While visually the film is occasionally impressive, with some breathtaking cinematography and well-constructed gothic sets, it ultimately falters in its storytelling. The lack of character depth, slow pacing, and a weak antagonist make for a frustrating experience. It's unfortunate, as there was great potential to reimagine this iconic horror tale for modern audiences.

If you're a fan of atmospheric horror, you may find enjoyment in some of the film's visuals, but if you're looking for a gripping story with engaging characters, Nosferatu may leave you feeling underwhelmed.

The movie starts off well, with some excellent atmosphere and cinematography. It seems to be going in a good direction for the first 45 minutes or so, until both the writing/story amd acting take a terrible turn. Ultimately the movie ends up well into the "cringe" zone and becomes almost a parody of itself.

The characters, while not often well-written, are acted well EXCEPT Lily-Rose Depp (who over acts more than a community theater novice) and Willam Defoe (who just doesn't even fit in to the movie). Ultimately, the film just came off as gross, weird, and laughable.

reviews.author: dasa108
reviews.body: Nosferatu is an unnecessary film with huge script weaknesses thanks to its lack of originality. What is saved is the technical effort that demonstrates the solvency of the director who as a scriptwriter fails miserably. Let's start with the problems: all the possible clichés are present but poorly organized. On the one hand there is an improbable love story with a deranged woman who has a key relationship with the villain which is not explored in depth and this is precisely the key point that sustains the film. On the other hand, need and greed are triggers for bad decisions that make you want everyone dead from the first minute. The first ten minutes are promising but then everything goes downhill terribly. Events rush and to confront evil, someone without firm faith in God is called upon in a novel and Luciferian way. The eternal battle between good and evil must be resolved in a new age way. Nosferatu has a villain design from Antropophagus and Aaron Taylor is the equivalent of Casper Van Dien in Sleepy Hollow. There are nods to Coppola and his Dracula and the few references to Murneau do not serve as homage. It is a bad story, unnecessary and Luciferian that is barely saved by the costumes, casting and photography. Compared to the works of Murneau or Herzog it is an abomination.
