You don't feel bored at anytime of the movie.

In fact that's the best horror movie i saw in the past 6 months.

I'm also glad Demi Moore is back to screen She was the diva of the 90s.

reviews.author: caitlinsmith-91491
reviews.body:
Okay, so I just stumbled out of the theater after watching "The Substance," and I'm still trying to wrap my head around what I just experienced. This movie is wild, folks. In a good way.

First off, don't go into this expecting your typical Hollywood fare. The director clearly doesn't give a damn about playing it safe, and thank goodness for that. This film is like a fever dream you can't wake up from - and trust me, you won't want to.

I've seen it twice already, and I'm still picking up on new details. It's the kind of film that'll have you and your friends arguing over theories for hours afterward. What was real? What wasn't? Was it all just a metaphor for... something?

Bottom line: "The Substance" is a trip, in every sense of the word. It's bold, it's weird, and it's exactly what cinema needs right now. Go see it. Then see it again. Just maybe lay off the caffeine beforehand - your mind will be racing enough as it is.

reviews.author: Padreviews
reviews.body:
I do find it annoying when you spend ages writing a review then it disappears into the ether & isn't published particularly when you put so much effort into it

I get that this will probably outlive both Demi Moore & Dennis Quaid & probably get a remake in 20 years with all the actors played by AI & Margaret Qualley making a cameo appearance

For the most part 75% of this film from start till 90 minutes it was brilliant, exceptional even. But its final quarter let it down badly it pushed the envelope too far bit we've seen this recently with Saltburn & Poor Things so it's not a bad thing it's just not my thing

The film is a great piece of art , it achieves what Tarantino has never been able to do & that is to properly parody violence & gore, he came close when Oliver Stone directed Natural Born Killers the satire worked well there

If I was to describe this film I'd say imagine the intermission film in Monty pythons meaning if life & Terry Gillingham's auteur style of Brazil with limitless starting Bradley cooper , a touch of Logan's run , a huge dollop of Mary Shelly's Frankenstein then add Quasimodo , Shrek , Cinderella , showgirls , John Merrick from elephant man , the Sid vicious surreal version of My way in The sex pistols great rock & roll swindle and you've got most of the influences

This will be the most talked about film since Saltburn and that's no bad thing

Using prosthetics in nude scenes is a first but perhaps that's what will happen more in the future instead of body doubles ?

More of this but maybe less gore !

Pad. A 7/10 it could have been 9/10.

reviews.author: thomvic
reviews.body:
I had been waiting months to see this since I read about it since it aired at Cannes. I kept reminding my friends about this movie telling them we have to see it. Might also be because I have a soft spot for Demi Moore as well and heard this is the performance of her career.

Regarding Demi Moore, she absolutely steals the show here. She makes her character Elisabeth very believable, and her acting range is on full show here, whether it's dramatic, sad, batshit crazy rage, she has it all here. I know there's a lot of people who think she isn't a great actress, but I don't think she's been able to prove what she can do. Well this film will show otherwise.

Margaret Qualley is also equally as good and is a good counterpart to Demi Moore and gave a good performance.

The plot is simple and easy to follow. While I had somewhat of an idea how the plot was going to go, I had no idea how it was going to end. The third act took me by surprise and had my jaw drop at the insanity of it all.

The make up deserves a huge accolade which is able to bring the events that unfold into life. Definitely deserves an Oscar nomination, and hopefully Demi Moore gets a nod.

This isn't going to be everyone's cup of tea, but for those who are horror fans and are sick of the lack of originality in movies nowadays, the Substance is definitely worth your time. It's something you will not forget!

reviews.author: ivington
reviews.body:
The film, visually always held my attention, and that was before the last 30 minutes which just went to a whole bonkers new level. I was a bit unsure though of how the trade off had any benefits for Demi Moore's character, as it didn't seem as if she was party to any of the experiences of the Ms Qua persona. At least, of there were, it wasn't obvious to the viewer. So I couldn't see why Elizabeth would have any qualms about ending the experience as there appeared to be no upside.

Despite this niggle, I did find the story held my attention throughout and although this type of movie is not what I would generally watch I would recommend it, just for the last 30 minutes alone. With the last 10 minutes being absolute hilarious.

reviews.author: kevin_robbins
reviews.body:
I watched The Substance (2024) in theaters tonight. The storyline follows an aging movie star who is advised to take a product that promises a younger, "new and improved" version of herself. However, the medication comes with strict rules-if not followed, the consequences become increasingly severe. As the movie star revels in her new life, it becomes harder to stick to the rules, and breaking them begins to unravel the world of both her selves.

Written and directed by Coralie Fargeat (Revenge), the film stars Demi Moore (Striptease), Dennis Quaid (Innerspace), Margaret Qualley (Once Upon a Time in Hollywood), and Gore Abrams (Hell House LLC).

This is one of the most unique horror films I've seen in a long time. The attention to detail and the horror effects are top-tier. Demi Moore delivers an outstanding performance-she looks great, has more nude scenes than expected, and absolutely nails the role. Dennis Quaid is perfectly cast as a slimy TV executive. The depiction of the era is spot-on, with fun touches like the attire, cars, colors, and furniture, which make it easy to get pulled into this universe. The horror effects are top-notch, making this a must-watch for genre enthusiasts. The initial transformation scene is incredible, and the use of needles is not for the squeamish. There's brilliant use of prosthetics and gore throughout, and one of the wildest blood-splatter sequences I've ever seen. The background score heightens the intensity and drama of each scene. The cinematography, camera angles, and lighting are excellent, giving the film a grindhouse vibe mixed with something out of Tromaville. Also, there's no shortage of butt shots! The ending is pure horror gold-absolutely amazing. That said, it did feel a bit over the top at times, and I thought the movie could have ended earlier, but the full-circle conclusion was poetically satisfying.

In conclusion, The Substance is a movie you'll never forget. The ending will stay with you-whether you like it or not. I'd score it an 9/10 and consider it a must-see for horror fans.

reviews.author: whitetowel-74786
reviews.body:
Oh boy - what have I just seen! :-p

What an insane, rollercoaster ride this dark comedy-drama/body horror quease-fest was. Eat your heart out Cronenberg and Lynch, there's a new kid in town and her name is (French director) Coralie Fargeat! This talented 48 year old somewhat newbie filmmaker clearly sets out to revile and shock... she certainly succeeds, and then some!

90's superstar Demi Moore takes the lead role here and she's excellent, as are her 'better self' Margaret Qualley and veteran hellraiser Dennis Quaid, hamming it to the max as a sleazy Hollywood tv exec.

The premise is simple enough - aging LA female tv fitness guru loses her gig (and self-esteem), and after a lucky escape car crash is given a mysterious package by a hospital worker which leads to Ms Moore injecting a life-altering 'substance' into her body. Though we never find out who, why and how much for this miraculous 'elixir of new life', the ensuing storyline just gets weirder, grosser and more extreme as things escalate to a truly violent and bizarre blood-soaked finale.

To its credit the film grabs you from the first frames and never lets go. The cinematography, editing, garrish LA colour schemes and gross out narcissistic performances from the 3 leads are top-notch... but alas there's a big drawback. The overblown Carrie-esque finale is simply way to OTT! It all becomes too much and should of ended at its more natural conclusion (no spoilers) about 20 minutes earlier. However it doesn't and just gets more grossed out, absurd and somewhat laughable by journeys end.

However, all in all, despite the ridiculous ending this is a movie set for cult status and will certainly propel Fargeat!s stock and resurrect Demi Moores career (oh the irony). She's brilliant.

In summation, if you enjoyed the likes of 'Death Becomes Her', 'Carrie', 'Videodrome' and especially the lesser known 1989 cult classic 'Society' then you'll certainly enjoy this wild, debauched social commentary on America's obsession with youthful good looks, body image and the desperate methods embraced to obtain them... just stay away from infomercials and promises of fountains of youth afterwards OK!

reviews.author: minij
reviews.body: A very unique film in more ways than one. The way it is shot and the sound editing makes it hard to ignore, it's so visceral and gross but also engaging. Both leads I thought were fantastic and I loved the message of the film, of chasing youth and beauty, days gone by and not appreciating what you have now. Definitely put me in mind of other so called body horrors (such as Titane) but it had a subversive and at times humorous quality to it. I would love to see it again. As other reviews have mentioned, if you are easily offended by female nudity, gore and surgical scenes just give it a miss rather than walk out the screen (as I heard several people have been doing)

reviews.author: CSMannUK
reviews.body: Grabs you from start to finish. An unforgettable experience. So many influences and themes littered throughout. From Cronenberg to Melies, Kubrick to De Palma, so many nods to great feature films of the past. Has a lot to say about society in general and our fixation with being our best. Perceptions, values, thought processes and desires all examined and tested throughout. Demi Moore with a performance of a lifetime. Dennis Quaid superb. Margaret Qualley perfectly casted. Edited in such a way that the tempo of the film never lags. Really don't think i will see a better film for a long time. Certainly up there with the greats for me. Bravo filmmaking kudos to all involved.

reviews.author: chosenf8
reviews.body:
Is it horror? Satire? Art House? Perhaps all of the above. But don't step into this film expecting your standard horror fare. Instead, be ready to laugh-because I did, almost from start to finish. This film playfully stretches the boundaries of satire, pushing them straight into absurdism.

The sound design is impeccable-10/10 for the production team, whose work amplifies the experience. Special effects are solid, and the makeup team excels, but if you're looking for intricate character development or groundbreaking plotlines, this isn't the film for you.

That said, Demi Moore is a force of nature as Elizabeth Sparkle, commanding the screen in every scene. Her performance alone elevates this film from quirky to unmissable.

reviews.author: mattatthemovies
reviews.body:
I had a lot of fun watching this. What an insane movie that takes you for a wild ride! The performances from Demi Moore and Margaret Qualley make the movie. The stellar work from makeup and effects artists make this a certified horror classic. This movie will make you gasp with its Cronenberg inspired body horror.

This movie is centralized around themes of beauty and youth. It follows a woman who is struggling with aging and the fading spotlight that has come with it, when she is presented with the means to regain her youth and stardom. I recommend anyone who is even slightly intrigued by this movie to give it a watch. People will be talking about this one for years to come.

reviews.author: nERDbOX_Dave
reviews.body:
"The Substance" is a horror film that dares to take a satirical bite out of Hollywood, delivering a biting commentary on the industry's obsession with youth and beauty. This body horror flick is a grotesque and unsettling exploration of the lengths people will go to maintain their appearance, even if it means sacrificing their humanity.

The film follows Elisabeth Sparkle (Demi Moore), a once-beloved aerobics instructor whose world crumbles when she is abruptly fired. Desperate to reclaim her lost glory, she accepts a mysterious offer that promises to transform her into a more "enhanced" and younger version of herself, Sue (Margaret Qualley). The one excpetion is that they essentially have to swap bodies every 7 days in order to maintain balance in order for the treatment to remain effective.

Demi Moore delivers a tour-de-force performance as Elisabeth, a woman desperate to cling to her relevance in a youth-obsessed industry. Her transformation is both shocking and unsettling, a physical manifestation of the lengths to which people will go to maintain their appearance. Margaret Qualley is equally impressive as a sinister younger body double who becomes obsessed with her quest to the primary host in the world. The two actresses share a palpable chemistry that elevates the film's tension and suspense.

Coralie Fargeat's direction is bold and uncompromising, delivering a visual feast of grotesque imagery and disturbing body horror as she makes a statement that she has arrived in the horror genre.

The practical effects are truly horrifying, capturing the film's themes of decay and transformation with visceral power. The film's pacing is relentless, keeping the audience on edge from the opening scene to the shocking finale.

All in all, this film feels like a spiritual sequel to the movie "X" crossed with David Cronenberg's "The Fly". If you are a fan of body horror, then this is one for you....however remember that this satirical film, otherwise the third act will lose you.

reviews.author: lord_orsum
reviews.body:
Fading film star Elisabeth Sparkle is given a chance to recapture her youth and beauty through the use of a drug called The Substance. Initially everything is wonderful, however as she starts to break the rules of using it, things rapidly spiral downwards.

Demi Moore, who is looking fantastic at the age of 62, plays the 50 year old lead. She gives a stellar performance, bold and nuanced, leaving the audience in no doubt about Elisabeth's inner turmoil.

Dennis Quaid is on top form, as the utterly repulsive TV executive producer. Margaret Qualley is perfectly portrays the superficial Sue.

For me, the message here was that Elisabeth had spent her whole life seeking love, but only the superficial fleeting love of the adoring audience. Thus her desire to reclaim her superficial beauty overwhelms her. She has learned nothing. She has nothing.

Full marks to the special effects team. The prosthetics are awesome and the direction makes full use of them. It is not for the faint hearted (or weak stomached).

I would have given this film an 8/10, if not for the ending. If it had ended about 20 minutes earlier, it would have been perfect. The horror would have been complete, the future for Elisabeth/Sue ambiguous. Unfortunately, the film doesn't know when to stop and devolves into ridiculousness.

Regardless of this, this is one of the best and original films that I have seen this year.

reviews.author: jp_91
reviews.body: "The Substance" is a tremendous film of body horror and black humor, the script is exceptional with a touch of David Cronenberg's cinema, in addition to the gore and eroticism, the film leaves a positive message of accepting yourself as you are, no longer boycott yourself. The editing is of a high level and fits perfectly with the colorful cinematography, production design and costumes. The director's work is elegant and grotesque, the performances of Demi Moore and Margaret Qualley stand out in every scene, both giving their best. The music composed for the film is hypnotic. The prosthetic makeup effects are incredible, being realistic and grotesque at the same time. "The Substance" is a great British-French co-production that becomes an instant classic.

reviews.author: thomasellery
reviews.body:
Firstly we can all agree that The Substance delivers on visual style, think Kubrick and Kronenberger meets social media music video with Brian DePalma style camera work.

Demi shines as she falls apart, physically and mentally. The haunting tears in the mirror do morph more into comedic old hag, the more she mutates, but she's giving it some guts, (literally!) and the resentment she has of it all feels real.

There's a ton of symbolism going on if that's your thing, right down to the egg white and yolk colours she always wears when picking up her supplies, so there's obviously been a lot of thought put into everything you see.

I get the point of showing off Sue's body, but it does sometimes feel like they linger on this a little to long without any real benefit to the film, but its all done in a neon pink dazzle I guess.

As the battle between the old and young Elizabeth intensifies, so does the body horror. Personally I didn't feel that grossed out, but the effects were really good and they went overboard in a way that works.

It was all going so stylishly well until the last act. It wasn't particularly shocking and just didn't give a satisfying or deep enough conclusion for what you think the rest of the film would create.

It's like they had a really awesome idea and premise, but without a clue on how to end it with a punch or purpose. It gives a neat conclusion and a weak metaphorical meaning I guess, but it's more reliant on splatter than meaning by this point. Which is a shame, as up to then, this movie had it all.

10/10 until "version 3" arrives knocking it down to a 7 overall. My score won't stop it becoming a cult classic and I'll still YouTube the stylish bits every now and then.

reviews.author: wross012
reviews.body: Good not great in my opinion. Requiem for a Dream meets The Fly as Nicholas Winding Refn stops by. The theme is as old as humanity but stands out now in our age of selfies, social media, unregulated supplements and GLP drugs. The acting was great. As the movie progresses I feel the genre bending begins. It felt like a movie with 3 acts and while each one had plusses, some other theatre goers commented that the final act lost them. I laughed and liked it, appreciated where it went, but also understand how you could feel that way. Perhaps brevity would have served the director best with the editing left for the extended edition. The comments about the gore are FAR overblown; fandango and rotten tomatoes "viewers" are trolling or something. The effects had an 80s feel which is a win for me. The Thing is one of my favorite films. It was nice to see something different. Refreshing. It's a good movie worth your view just don't lean on the hyperbolic reviews. Yes it has some gonzo parts but so did the Evil Dead. I will keep an eye out for this director moving forward. Ultimately I think with some tighter editing and I'd give a few more stars. Also if you do go see it just buy in, obviously the medical aspects have to be taken like the Force or Magic in other flicks.

reviews.author: bronascullion
reviews.body: Guys I grow up on nasty 80's horror, and am normally a huge fan. But I have to say this was something else. It started of great, the story was so original and fascinating, the acting was great. Demi Moore was as beautiful as ever, and then about 3 quarters of the way through, it kinda left planet earth and took my brain with it. This movies deteriorated into an absolute mess that was just so ridiculous and stomach churning, it was a complete car crash, Unfortunately I was invested so I had to finish it, but seriously WHAT WAS THE POINT......It just got completely ruined by the end 🙄 BIG YAWN FROM ME 👎👎👎👎👎

reviews.author: varuka-04268
reviews.body:
The story reminded of Oscar Wilde's The picture of Dorian Gray, with this being a feminist and science fiction reinterpretation of Wilde's famous novel.

Great acting performances from the two main leads and stunning esthetics, the cinematography is fantastic. I wasn't grossed out at all by the body horror, just by the scene of the big boss eating prawns. Very well done.

If you're very sensitive to blood and body gore l recommend you don't go see this. If you're into dark and absurd comedies, absolutely go see this. This is the art of horror at its finest!

Absolute highlight of the year for me!

reviews.author: anttilajulle
reviews.body:
I've seen many movies in the Horror/Sci-fi genre but this was a first.

I would recommend watching the movie in cinema. Everyone was in a complete shock when the credits started rolling. Me and my buddy just looked at eachother and said "What did I just witness".

This is also the first time I've seen people leave the cinema. The movie is truly disgusting and not for everyone. If you are sensitive to gore and bodily fluids I've would not recommend watching the movie.

The Substance is beautifully shot and use great camera angels. The storyline was also good and it was easy to follow.

To describe "The Substance" in three words.

Brilliant, Disgusting and Ambiguous.

reviews.author: gcraig12-985-641175
reviews.body: Demi Moore is back! She portrays the obsession of not wanting to age perfectly! I would have given it a higher rating had it not been SO over the top and gross towards the end! DON'T eat before watching the film! Margaret Qualley 's performance was great too as the younger version of Elisabeth .Her character "Sue" that she portrays as the elder replacement represents the greed and entitlement of the youths needing more and more. I found the concept of "body snatching" intriguing ,showcasing the lengths women will go to to stop aging and be young and beautiful again. The message is age gracefully!!

reviews.author: joel_steele
reviews.body:
A good movie elicits an emotion while a great one elicits many. It's safe to say that 'The Substance' is the latter, which speaks volumes given how the film's cast is not full of A-list actors or presented by a well-known director. It's nice to have forgotten actors brought back into the spotlight to join fresh faces like a changing of the guard.

If you don't know much about it, go in as "blind" as possible. It's a truly engaging and thought-provoking story that's very well crafted to ensure you're caught up in it all from start to end.

We must give credit where credit is due as you'll likely never forget this excellent, unique, and much-needed offering in a film year that's been mediocre at best.

9/10.

reviews.author: daoldiges
reviews.body: I saw The Substance in a sold out movie theatre with a mostly enthusiastic audience, which may have enhanced my viewing experience. It's definitely interesting and the level of violence, blood and gore immediately reminded me of Tarantino, but The Substance surpassed even him in this regard. Seems a lot of folks feel the last third of the film goes too far. I was also feeling that way at that time in the film, but I stuck with it and by the end felt that it all made sense. Two days have passed and I'm feeling even more up on this film. Yes, it's a lot to take in and process, and I don't think it needed to go as far as it did with the violence, but despite that I think the substance has some things to say and it does so in a new and mostly entertaining way.

reviews.author: jtindahouse
reviews.body:
Oh man, I loved 'The Substance' for 90% of the runtime. It was more or less locked into a 10/10 for me with half an hour to go. Then the film found a way to undo a lot of the hard work. The ending they went for didn't work for me, and it's a real shame because this is an otherwise excellent film.

This is some of the most relentless body horror I've seen. Three separate groups all walked out while the film was still going, something I have never seen before in a cinema. The film has no fears of going overboard or showing anything shocking whatsoever. I absolutely loved it in that regard.

The film has a clear message and for most of the run time it gets it across very effectively. I can't help wondering whether the 140 minute run time was a little too ambitious and it just didn't know how to keep the momentum going for all that time. Don't get me wrong, this was a very good film. But there's no doubt that with the icing on the cake it could've gone down as something truly special. 9/10.

reviews.author: TheVictoriousV
reviews.body:
Early reviews and festival coverages of The Substance came with some hefty promises. Here, supposedly, was a film that, even as you're watching it, you cannot believe is a real movie that actually got made; a film where, even if you were to watch every trailer and promo clip, you can't possibly predict where it goes.

And I must be blunt, even with all of this hype in mind, I still wasn't prepared for the dark, disturbing, wildly original journey of body horror and unbridled social critique that Coralie Fargeat (a student of New French Extremity) would take me on. Its themes of body dysmorphia and beauty obsession aren't unexplored territory but seem especially relevant in the semaglutide age and are handled with technical meticulousness, gut-wrenching performances, and first-rate gore effects the likes of which we've rarely seen.

As Jeff Zhang wrote in his review, it unapologetically throws subtext out the window (calling it a "hagsploitation sledgehammer of internalized misogyny and LA-brained self-loathing" that only plays one note at "the exact amplitude to blow out the speakers and bring the house down"). It is in-your-face and deliberately, aggressively so. The thing is, it all works for the tone of the film: a horrifying yet also over-the-top and hysterical satire about a top-secret, decidedly unrealistic beauty product that makes your old, "haggard" body hatch a young double that can go out and make it big in beauty-obsessed industries while you lay dormant for seven days at a time, eating through a tube.

The substance is called The Substance, the shows are called things like The Show, and The Show airs on The Network. It doesn't need to be more "clever" than that; that's not the point. EDIT: An alternative phrasing is that the point isn't to give you something to feel smart for figuring out, even as there are details in this film that those who dub it "too obvious" or "too simple" somehow managed to miss anyway.

The plot itself eventually takes several darker turns as the main character, an aging, once-successful movie star and TV host named Elizabeth Sparkle (Demi Moore), grows addicted to being in her younger body, Sue (Margaret Qualley) -- or rather, Sue grows to despise the older version -- and so stays in that mode for longer than recommended. (While the two selves live in symbiosis, they seem like distinctly different persons, even as the customer service line for The Substance insists to Elizabeth that "they are one".) This eventually has catastrophic consequences, culminating in a nightmarish climax that Rob Delaney aptly described as "operatically bloody and gross".

Sequences like that are among the main reasons to see the film in a theater, alongside a crowd of others to share in your bewilderment, amusement, and horror. The other reason to see it in a theater -- or at all -- is the performances.

Demi Moore is sensational, giving a performance whose shrieks and facial expressions will stay fresh in your memory after the screen goes black. Dennis Quaid, meanwhile, supplies a hilariously sickening villain (the obvious joke being that he's almost as manifestly evil as when he's playing Reagan) that sometimes plays like something out of The Cat in the Hat, and I cannot believe I am saying this as a positive.

And oh God, Margaret Qualley. If you somehow weren't sold on the idea that she is one of the great modern movie stars -- even after Kinds of Kindness, Once Upon A Time in Hollywood, and Drive-Away Dolls -- this will be the film that makes you an admirer. (There is, of course, thematic relevance to the Moore-Qualley casting itself: a sex symbol of the 80s and 90s transformed into one of the stars of today. Luckily, both will be Oscar winners after this.)

The way Fargeat satirizes what it means to be a woman -- not just in Hollywood and Hollywood-adjacent industries, but in the world at large -- retroactively makes almost all previous attempts seem weak and lame. (People who thought the Barbie monologue was somehow as scathing as it gets aren't likely to forget this viewing.) In terms of horror filmmaking, it takes numerous cues from the masters; in addition to the broader homage to the works of David Cronenberg (from Crimes of the Future all the way to the other Crimes of the Future; some evoked for a greater purpose while some are merely aesthetic), the film occasionally draws on the likes of Lost Highway, The Shining, Vertigo, Persona, and even Basket Case. Nevertheless, it is mixed into something unique that will no doubt inspire its own line of imitators.

For one thing, it is a distinctive film in terms of locations. Fargeat's use of bathroom settings (especially the great nemesis of those with body dysmorphia: the mirror) is both inspired and effective. The special effects are top-of-the-line and while the surreal body horror is a highlight, the movie proves that less is more when it comes to making us wince; the most horrific scenes are the relatable ones, involving teeth mysteriously coming loose and bloody pustules getting pricked (the Cronenberg-ian stuff is too abstract to make us "hurt", but is effective in a different way). As nasty as this may sound, it's all excellently filmed, going for some highly creative shots at key moments. The editing is oft clever and, the rest of the time, intense and rhythmic in a way that recalls Requiem for a Dream.

If I were to name any drawbacks whatsoever, it might be the fact that sometimes it's "obvious" in a bad way, communicating connections in the story as though we weren't paying attention to the setup (but once again, it almost always complements the eccentricity of the film). Other than that and a few moments that are goofy without meaning to, I adored every single element of The Substance -- the cinematography, the editing, the effects, the sound design, the makeup, the score, all of it simply "slaps" as the Zoomers say. When my friend and I left the theater, we were almost blown away that 2.5 hours had passed.

While I've sung the praises of 2023 (as have we all) and what it meant for movies, The Substance confirms that 2024 was even better, at least for me and my local release schedule. Between The Zone of Interest, The Beast, Dune Part Two, Challengers, Hundreds of Beavers, and now this, 2024 has turned out to be a year unlike any other. We didn't have anything like Barbenheimer, sure, but the fact that one of the big hype titles was a movie like The Substance is special in its own right. (Besides, we did have a "Megajokolis".) This is a ludicrously well-made film that won't soon be forgotten, though I am pessimistic about the right lessons being taken from it.

reviews.author: christopher-underwood
reviews.body: This has a brilliant opening. We start with an egg and then with a syringe and a second egg, then an eye, a close up, and then other eyes and it is rather worrying and scary but then a Hollywood style star on the ground and we see it gradually getting old and worn. We then get to see the exercise dancing by Demi Moore and she is rather amazing as she is over 60 and I'm assuming she does her own, and she is very bold doing this and much more. For some reason, as I go through my records, it seems that I have never seen any of her films. But in this Margaret Qualley, younger and really good and I have seen two of her's, Once Upon a Time...in Hollywood (2019) and The Nice Guys (2016). It is confusing at first but then we know what is going on, although there is lots more of exercise dancing but also some Cronenberg style body horror, which is really difficult to watch. It is amazingly well done but we spend too long in the white bathroom. It is also two and a half hours, maybe half an hour too long and I think it really could have been reduced down to 90 minutes and this might have been better.

reviews.author: ole_steam_shovel
reviews.body: Best horror film in years. This is why we go to the movies. When you think you've had enough, Miss Fargeat keeps her foot firmly on the gas and doesn't let up. Fantastic use of practical effects, bloody body horror that would make Cronenberg blush and excellent acting all around, especially Demi Moore.. Any horror/film fan will love it and all of its influences, from Lynch to Kubrick to The Thing, even Pulp Fiction, etc. Not to mention the scathing critique of beauty standards and the entertainment industry, really ANY industry that employs women. Absolutely bonkers piece of work that will no doubt become a cult classic!

reviews.author: natashafitzsimons
reviews.body:
I was expecting good things, but even so I was very surprised.

I will preface it by saying that I felt this film impacted me stronger as a woman - because I think as women, the fear of being invisible, overlooked, forgotten are very strong drivers - in no small part due to the daily misogyny experienced.

Elizabeth sparkle is so easy to identify with, and it's really commendable for Demi Moore to open up herself to a role like this - it's very exposing - both literally and metaphorically.

The casting and cinematography is first rate, and I was engaged at every moment. I loved the story - I thought it was really original, and unsettling.

The body horror is phenomenally done, and it is one of the only films where I have felt genuinely uncomfortable. I was engaged the whole way through, and it didn't feel long at all.

It's destined to be a cult classic, but will have a lot of people who won't understand it, or won't want to.

The ending is absolutely insane, and really makes the film a lot different than anything I've previously seen.

I have to say, it feels like essential viewing.

reviews.author: harishnj
reviews.body:
The Substance" (2024) is a bold and unsettling film that pushes the boundaries of body horror while offering a scathing critique of societal obsession with youth and beauty. Though its graphic imagery and disturbing themes may not appeal to all viewers, its unique blend of horror, satire, and psychological drama makes for a captivating and thought-provoking experience.

The film's visuals are striking, with director Coralie Fargeat crafting a world that is both alluring and repulsive. The special effects are masterfully executed, creating a visceral and unsettling portrayal of the physical transformations undergone by the characters.

Demi Moore delivers a powerful performance as Elizabeth, a woman grappling with aging and societal pressures in the entertainment industry. Her portrayal of desperation and vulnerability is both captivating and heartbreaking. Margaret Qualley is equally impressive as the younger version of Elizabeth, showcasing the character's internal struggle and the disturbing consequences of her choices.

The film's narrative, while occasionally veering into the surreal, offers a sharp critique of the entertainment industry and its exploitation of women. The themes of body image, self-worth, and the pursuit of youth are explored with a raw honesty that is both unsettling and thought-provoking.

While "The Substance" may not be for the faint of heart, its unique blend of horror, satire, and psychological drama makes it a standout film. Its disturbing imagery and thought-provoking themes will linger in your mind long after the credits roll.

reviews.author: GJVazquez
reviews.body:
The Substance is one of the most unique films I've ever seen-an absolute wild ride from start to finish. It's a movie that's definitely not for everyone. Some scenes are tough to sit through, but the visuals and special effects are truly stunning. It's one of those films packed with themes and messages, many of which could resonate with people on a personal level, depending on how you interpret it.

While I think it's an impressive film, even Oscar-worthy in some aspects, though I wasn't completely sold on the ending. I get why they chose the direction they did-it makes sense-but I couldn't help but wish for something a little different. (Like a simple conversation) That said, the movie still stands out as a unique experience. There are a few nitpicks, though, like some ASMR-type moments that can get annoying, but they still fit within the world of the film.

Overall, the acting, effects, SOUND and cinematography all come together to create an experience unlike anything I've seen before. It's a weird mix of gross, disturbing, yet interesting and unique. Watching it with a theater full of people really added to the experience-everyone riding the emotional roller coaster together. If you're up for something different and don't mind a few tough-to-watch moments, definitely give The Substance a shot. Just be warned-it's not for the faint of heart!

reviews.author: fasteposta
reviews.body: The Substance is a disaster, and anyone who watches it does so at their own risk. It's astonishing that this film has received such positive reviews. While cinema has long since strayed from its path, the fact that people actually support something like this is terrifying. Films once focused on a storyline, a message, or some intrigue. This, however, is so bad that it's like it should be watched on a substance. Movies like these seem aimed at audiences with an IQ of 2, and anyone looking for meaning has clearly moved on to find purpose elsewhere. Movie such a garbage please don't go to see this garbage if you have any dignity.

reviews.author: videorama-759-859391
reviews.body: As I'm writing this review, still getting over the last half hour of this amazing film, this is one insane movie experience, you must experience. It could very well serve as a poster child for self image, and an anti pill taking movie. Fading, as now in her fifties, our fading star, a present Aerobics instructor with her own show, and a once great acting career, prefore I presume, as seen from a award accolade, sported near the start, which you can see in the trailer, Demi, isn't happy with the here and now of her life. Risking a mysterious, life changing green liquid solution, by use of injectile, which you should only use once, and would be mad to try she injects, where she experiences her once more beautiful 20 something self under a different name and look (the hot Qualley, stealing the scene in a strong tour de force performance), but after misusing, or being greedy, the consequences, sort of two way streak, Moore's old self, starts to rapidly disintegrate. Most of the gore in the film, comes really in the last half, and when it comes, it comes, the movie going off the charts in stupidity. It works because we don't expect it, and we are taken aback. We can forgive it. The Substance too has some real good humor. Dennis Quaid, is really the standout, an underrated actor who should of been worthy, of an Oscar someone down his career. He plays the villain, heartless, eccentric, over the top, and he was born for the role, the late Ray Liotta cast. As we are almost seeing out this year, make The Substance your must see film, for a hell of a movie night, you won't forget, and be glad you went..

reviews.author: Vils1
reviews.body:
Substance - Love it or Hate it You Won't Forget It (Good, Until It Goes For Gore) This was a movie in two parts. For the first ¾ it was an interesting satire on the need to look 'young' and where it could take you. It's not perfect (it's a shame that they used prosthetics to enhance 'perfection', no diversity etc.) but it poses questions we will all need to answer at some time. However I could quite happily have left at the 'potential termination' scene. It would have been better if that stage reverted to the conditions at the outset and left a card saying 'Careful What you Wish For'. I would have given it a 9/10.

Instead the last quarter was a splatter-gore-fest that was a tough watch. It was comedy horror which washed away the previous satire.

Oh well. Love it or hate it, you won't forget it.

reviews.author: ooobe
reviews.body:
The Substance (2024) started off as a nearly perfect film, showcasing a brilliant blend of concept, acting, cinematography, and direction.

The storyline flowed seamlessly, creating a compelling atmosphere that gripped me from the very beginning. Up until halfway, or perhaps a bit further, the film maintained a strong focus on drama, science fiction, and technological advancement-an ideal mix for a truly engaging thriller. However, as the plot progressed, it unexpectedly shifted towards horror-comedy elements, which, to me, didn't quite fit the initial tone.

While some may appreciate this genre twist, I felt it detracted from the depth and intensity that the first half had so skillfully built. Still, despite the surprising shift and unconventional ending, I thoroughly enjoyed the experience overall. I'd rate it a 7 out of 10, largely due to the incredible first half. Had the movie maintained that initial approach throughout, it would have easily been a 9.

reviews.author: luvli-67696
reviews.body:
A good film tells a compelling story. It also presents the story in an alluring way. Coralie Fargeat certainly seems to have mastered the art of that.

The story has been told many times. Be careful what you wish for. As a society, we have become more interested in beauty through alteration. In the past, some things were taboo. This includes going under the knife. Investing in medicinal means to improve our appearance. However, now they are highly accessible to the general population. It has also led to an obsession with perfection on both sides of the equation, production and consumption.

The acting is phenomenal. Demi Moore impresses in her role. Mere movements and the way she uses her physical form speak volumes without uttering a word. Her face is expressive, and her eyes are emotive. She lives in the skin of her character. The strength of the screenplay enhances her work. The storyline is solid. The premise is hard hitting, powerful, and visceral. Cinematography drives home the nuanced aspects that pull us in. This prompts our subconscious to delve deeper and perceive the grotesqueries on a micro level.

reviews.author: Avwillfan89
reviews.body:
I can't believe what I just saw. This movie is a masterpiece in horror cinema.

This is essentially The Fly meets Cinderella, injected with drugs.

I adore a film that challenges the ridiculousness of beauty standards. This film does do that, but cranks it up to not 11, not 20, but 100+. It is absolutely effing insane.

Elizabeth Sparkle (a still gorgeous Demi Moore, let's not forget it!) is a veteran starlet who has been kicked out of her job due to ageism. After getting into a car accident, she is given an oppurtunity to literally transform herself into a younger, tighter, more beautiful version of herself. She reluctantly agrees. From the get-go, this is dodgy AF. But she is desperate, so she goes for it.

What emerges from this is Sue (Margaret Qualey) the version Sparkle wants to get back, and who ends up replacing her. There are so many shots of butts, boobs and thighs in this film, but it's not done in a way that is exploitative. It's all the parts that women want, and all the parts that men want.

Like in Gremlins, like in The Fly, rules are broken due to pride. And once the rules are broken, it begins to go south very, very far.

What I love about its Cronenbergian roots, is that, like Rachel Weisz's take on Dead Ringers, this is a feminist, female-driven version of Seth Brundle's quest for perfection - that goes horribly wrong.

It is also a massive big finger to the vacuous, youth and beauty obsessed nature of celebrity culture. The buccal fat removal, the Ozempic injections and all of the cosmetic surgery that high-paid celebs get to afford.

Also, like The Fly, it is an incredibly sad tale about loneliness, isolation and the pressure you feel to be a better version of yourself. One of the first things I noticed about the film, is there is very little dialogue. Because Elizabeth has no friends, doesn't talk to anyone outside of work and lives on her own. Even when the prospect of a date from a schoolfriend comes up ("You're still the most beautiful girl I've ever seen!") Elizabeth still doesn't feel worthy enough to match her former self.

Guaranteed this will not be for everyone. But for all the horror fans and masochistic freaks like me who love to challenge themselves, this is the long awaited film for you.

reviews.author: walhant
reviews.body:
I expected some kind of psychological horror, which is maybe a bit there, but it turns out the highlights end up being a lot of gore (at a crazy level by the end) and the farcical side of things (none of the side characters can be taken seriously, which is annoying and funny at the same time). It is entertaining but not very subtle.

The 2 main actresses are really good, the rest of the performances is either bad or cartoonish, but at least that makes it funny, sometimes.

The direction/photography is nice, but I think some scenes drag on for longer than needed.

The story takes a weird direction, but since the premise is already weird, I can accept it for what it is.

Given the level of gore, I don't know if I would recommend the movie, but if you're fine with that, it's somewhat entertaining.

reviews.author: BA_Harrison
reviews.body:
There's an old Hollywood adage about the five stages of an actor's career:

1. Who is X?

2. Get me X.

3. Get me an X type.

4. Get me a younger X.

5. Who was X?

Elisabeth Sparkle (Demi Moore) has reached stage four, the producer of her popular fitness show looking to replace her with a younger model. After a lucky escape from a car accident, Elisabeth is given the chance to try out a mysterious drug that promises to revitalise her life, but it comes with a strict set of instructions. The substance, as the treatment is called, divides Elisabeth's cells, creating a younger, sexier version of herself; they are two halves of the same person, sharing a consciousness, and they need each other to survive, but Sue (Margaret Qualley), as the new half calls herself, fails to stick to the rules with terrible consequences.

If you've already seen director Coralie Fargeat's Revenge, then you might have some idea of what to expect from The Substance: OTT comic-book violence, loads of shots of Qualley's butt, star-shaped earrings, and a blood-drenched finalé. But Fargeat's latest film is far from predictable: this wonderfully inventive film works as a satirical swipe at Hollywood's quest for youth, where aging stars go to great lengths to stay young, no matter what the risks, but it's not all high-brow commentary... The Substance doesn't hold back on the nasty stuff, delivering grotesque scenes of body horror to churn the stomach (the FX in this film are amazing), and a bats**t ending that needs to be seen to be believed.

Both Moore and Qualley put in excellent performances, and they are joined by Dennis Quaid who chews the scenery as comically repulsive TV producer Harvey.

I rate The Substance 8.5/10 (rounded up to 9 for IMDb). Highly recommended.

reviews.author: donmurray29
reviews.body:
Giving this an 8/10 rating

Coral Fargeat brings us viewers, a truly disturbing vision of what a product of the future can be and what it could do, in this brilliantly insane and gorgeous horror film. Demi Moore is the main centre character and revolves around her, Margaret Qualley is just the same, but sees things differently and that is where things go wrong. Both are just so excellent, I want both of them for an Oscar. Dennis Quaid is a vile TV man who clearly is written on someone in the industry and is rotten and he loves it, plays it, all the way.

The clean designer look of every location, clothes and props heighten the tension, helps the narrative particularly with the inspirational scenes from other classic horror films that you will clearly see. And blood, you get buckets of it. But not before the build up with the best VFX and make up you will see in a long while.

It's really Demi Moore that shines and holds it together with her on some really excellent acting, and with what she has to do, you can see why the reviews have been good. One film I am going to watch again.

reviews.author: subxerogravity
reviews.body:
Surprised how much I loved this one.

This movie was awesome in ways that i did not see coming at all. It was literally like looking into the nightmares of a Hollywood actress and it was so bonkers and so disturbing, and I loved every minute of it.

Demi Moore does some true acting in the film as she pretends that she's still not hot and opens herself up to show us those insecurities of aging.

I also, thought this movie did a great job with the metaphor of who you were as a young person and who you are as an old person. There was a pure honestness about how one does change.

I have to admit, I was not expecting such a horrific look at the situation. They went extreme with it. So shocking.

Anyway, best two hours and twenty minutes you can spend at the movies.

reviews.author: jeromesgabilo
reviews.body: No wonder this Coralie Fargeat masterpiece won Best Screenplay at the Cannes: this was original, spectacular and socially relevant. This shocking body horror feature by the innovative Fargeat shocked audiences around the world, including me, with its plot that was important during these times. The imageries and graphics were still freshly embedded to my mind. reviews.author: Xstal
reviews.body:
It's a role which you might find yourself assuming, as the toll of age looms large and starts consuming, with a chance to halt the rot, recapture something that's forgot, an elixir of youth, to start you blooming. But there's a price you have to pay to reverse time, it involves a split and suck as well as slime, plus there's teamwork, partnership, and some rules you cannot skip, if you're not careful parts may age - well past their prime. But what the hell, the road to wrinkles can't be worse, the path that's taking you away rides like a hearse, you'll make the call and overhaul, bits will stand proud and you'll stand tall, let's put this growing old thing back, into reverse.

Two wonderful performances from the two leading ladies in a macabre tale that may leave you slightly bruised at the end.

reviews.author: caritxrn-98745
reviews.body: I thought the first three quarters were great. To have one of the most beautiful women in the world, at any age, play the main character, was simply brilliant. I even have an appreciation for Chronenberg (sp) body horror. However to me there was a major disconnect like it was two different films. reviews.author: steveinadelaide
reviews.body:
Coralie Fargeat's The Substance is a jaw-dropping, audacious dive into the dark underbelly of beauty culture. The film follows Elisabeth Sparkle (Demi Moore), a fading celebrity who turns to a mysterious black-market drug that promises to create a younger, better version of herself. What unfolds is a grotesque, yet mesmerising journey that'll have you squirming in your seat and unable to look away.

From the get-go, Fargeat throws us into a world that's both familiar and nightmarishly distorted. The director's keen eye for satire is on full display, skewering society's obsession with youth and perfection with razor-sharp precision. It's a world where botox parties are as common as book clubs, and the pursuit of eternal beauty comes at a terrifying cost.

Moore's performance as Elisabeth is nothing short of revelatory. She brings a raw vulnerability to the role that's both heartbreaking and infuriating. You'll find yourself rooting for her one minute and wanting to shake some sense into her the next. It's a career-defining turn that showcases Moore's range and fearlessness as an actor.

The supporting cast is equally impressive, with Margaret Qualley delivering a deliciously unhinged performance as Sue, Elisabeth's younger doppelganger. Dennis Quaid rounds out the trio as Harvey, a sleazy TV executive who embodies every toxic male stereotype imaginable.

Visually, The Substance is a feast for the eyes-albeit one that might make you lose your appetite. Fargeat and cinematographer Benjamin Kracun have crafted a world that's simultaneously beautiful and repulsive. The use of colour is particularly striking, with sickly yellows and neon pinks creating an atmosphere of artificial glamour that feels like it could melt away at any moment.

The body horror elements are not for the faint of heart. Fargeat pulls no punches when it comes to depicting the grotesque transformations brought on by the titular substance. It's Cronenberg-esque in its unflinching approach, pushing the boundaries of what's acceptable on screen.

Where the film truly shines is in its exploration of themes surrounding ageing, self-worth, and the commodification of women's bodies. Fargeat doesn't just point out these issues; she takes a sledgehammer to them, forcing us to confront uncomfortable truths about our own complicity in these systems.

The pacing is relentless, rarely giving us a moment to catch our breath. This works in the film's favour for the most part, though there are moments where a bit more breathing room would have been welcome. The score, composed by Raffertie, is a pulsing, synth-heavy affair that perfectly complements the film's fever-dream aesthetic.

If there's one minor quibble, it's that the film occasionally teeters on the edge of being too on-the-nose with its messaging. However, given the subject matter, subtlety might be beside the point.

The Substance is a tour de force of filmmaking that demands to be seen. It's not an easy watch by any means, but it's one that'll stick with you long after you've left the theatre. Fargeat has crafted a modern horror masterpiece that's as thought-provoking as it is viscerally shocking. It's the kind of film that reminds us why we go to the movies in the first place-to be challenged, disturbed, and ultimately transformed. If you've got the stomach for it, The Substance is an experience you won't soon forget.

reviews.author: jacksonnjerii
reviews.body: This movie sticks with you. I watched this film a few weeks ago and I still think about it. The movie will make you feel disturbed, it just gives you the ick watching it, down to the cinematography, sound, and makeup/prosthetics. I watched the trailer expecting the movie to be about a simple misuse of a drug and her living with an alternate version of herself but it is about 10x crazier than that. Demi Moore is astounding in this movie, incredibly impressive acting. The social commentary is slightly confusing because it seems to contradict itself and the ending (last 30 minutes) is a bit disappointing and predictable but besides that, solid horror film.

reviews.author: pasleysharon
reviews.body: This had so much potential with a good start. Demi Moore looking stunning and setting the scene for something great and intriguing. I did not even mind the sexualising of women but about 45 min in it started to take a turn for the worst turning into the biggest load of rubbish, blood and gore and unnecessary violence. Horrible music, distasteful scenes like something out of saw, evil hell. This is where it lost the plot and the intended message of accepting age and beauty. Instead is shows the intense hate and self loathing we can put ourselves through in our desire to be an acceptable beauty.

reviews.author: athanasiosze
reviews.body:
1) Many reviewers said that they disliked the ending and it ruined (or harmed) the whole movie. That it should have been "more subtle" or less insane etc. I disagree. The ending is exactly what it should. I don't know what movie did they watch, but THE SUBSTANCE is NOT a subtle and "nuanced" movie. This is raw, wild, insane and a bit simplistic. Symbolisms are so basic that even a child will understand them. Coralie Fargeat is not Lars Von Trier neither Andrzej Zulawski etc. Her previous movie (Revenge) was visually great and entertaining but overall, a bad movie. She is not that skilled in order to create subtle movies. She's very good though when it comes to chaos, insanity, gore etc. And this is a very useful skill : When an artist knows his/hers limitations. THE SUBSTANCE ended exactly like it should and the whole movie is based upon its particular strengths.

2) Everything worked in this movie. At first, i was even distracted by all this sexiness. I have watched erotic films much more subtle and classy than this. But as this unfolds, i understood there was a reason. All this sexiness and the close ups in Qualley's body, had a purpose. Everything is happening in order to serve this movie's message, this is how it should have been played out. It looks like plain voyeurism but it isn't. The audience should feel fed up with all this stuff. Basically, this worked like a distorting mirror. I think Fargeat wanted to show how creepy/pervert have so many people became nowadays. And this was a clever decision. There is of course the obvious message regarding the hypocricy/perverseness/sickness of the whole entertainment industry and the pressure that stars feel as they get older. But there is a second layer also. So many creeps and weirdos and empty people nowadays. It's like Fargeat tells to them: Look, it's just flesh, this is what you have idolized, and you are feeding also all this industry sickness, as they feed it to you.

3) Demi Moore was indeed magnificent, believe the hype. Qualley was also very good. Quaid was over the top, this was definitely overacting but that's exactly what Fargeat asked him to. Don't forget that these characters are not "people", this is not a drama with everyday people. These characters are Symbols. There is nothing realistic here on the surface. These characters are just vessels, and even though they are not real people, everything that's being revealed through them, is real as hell.

4) So, THE SUBSTANCE is a bit BLACK MIRROR, a bit Possession (Zulafski), Cronenberg, Kafkaesque, a Faustian bargain and a Dorian Gray painting which came into life. It's flawed and i think that in the future, it will be viewed as overrated. Still, it's raw, honest, exciting, intense, powerful and its heart is in the right place. I was holding my breath during the last 30 minutes, it was shocking and tough to watch, and i appreciated it : With all its flaws, it doesn't get much better nowadays. THE SUBSTANCE is by far one of the best movies of this decade.

5) Best moment of this movie though was when Moore was looking herself in the mirror, moments before her date. This is one of the best scenes i have watched the last 10 years. And this, paradoxically, was subtle.

reviews.author: st8627
reviews.body:
This film feels like an homage to Stanley Kubrick with the set, limited locations, arty shots and the quirky story.

A fading actress is offered an opportunity to live life as a younger version of herself, but there are strict clauses to this opportunity and you just know this is where the problems are going to start.

As each character develops both Moore and Quallev are brilliant I become immersed in their character wondering what will happen next.

Quaids character is a cringe worthy as it gets and he pulls it off brilliantly.

The film moves through sequence to sequence seamlessly and builds up to the huge ending where you squirm but enjoy it at the same time.

I think if you aren't into Kubrick style movies this isn't for you, but what a great film.

reviews.author: lilianaoana
reviews.body:
So this is why I don't watch body horror movies, cause they don't do much for me, if anything, except for the sake of certain actors I enjoy. So Demi is really brave with this one and does a good job and actually looks amazing. Sometimes, from certain angles, she has that filler face and I don't know if that's by design or it's just her, but anyways, she generally looks natural, although I don't know whose blood she drank to still have that body. But I digress... I didn't get horrified, I've seen this stuff before and worse. But the ending was completely gratuitous and pointless and overall there's just no social commentary of substance. Pun intended. They could've made it about celebrity culture and celebrity mentality and body image and a woman's place in entertainment and so much more. I was hoping for some of that given that Demi herself has had some ups and downs in her career, but she never again reached the height of her success in the 90s and early 2000s and I don't think it's just cause she got old, but again, I digress.

So what I'm saying is I don't get the hype. It's shot well and acted well, but basically it's nothing more than body horror. Plus, as some have pointed out, there is no logic to the story, and there are some gaping plot holes. One minute she can barely move her decrepit legs, the next she is running for her life. Never mind the twist with the termination, which makes no sense without the stabilizer and the whole thing at the end. Plus, why would Elizabeth make that decision since she clearly couldn't experience herself what Sue was living?

Also, how popular can you get by doing a soft core exercise morning show? And Elizabeth was an Oscar winner, how come she had nothing going on in her life to fill the void of her beauty declining? But I'm taking this way too seriously. It's all a pretext for body horror. Only not that clever.

Dennis Quaid is appropriately loathsome.

Certainly not Cannes worthy for me. Maybe for acting and maybe cinematography, but that's a stretch really.

reviews.author: avenuesf
reviews.body:
I really enjoyed Coralie Fargeat's 2018 film "Revenge," but I think "The Substance" is even better. While the theme of seeking eternal youth and paying a high price for it isn't new in horror, the sheer outrageousness of this film sets it apart. What I loved most was its freakish, sarcastic style and Fargeat's use of wide-angle lenses, which deepened the film's brooding sense of alienation. It 's also commendable that two fairly well-known actors trusted the process enough to step outside their comfort zones, taking risks with the frequent nudity and extreme excesses.

Despite how much I was awed by it, the film felt about twenty minutes too long-some of the repeated aerobic TV footage of "Sue" could have been trimmed and long scenes of Demi Moore's character alone in her apartment became slightly tedious. There were also a few improbable details, like how the main character, a TV personality, is able to effortlessly find a vein to give herself an IV or stitch up a body with surgical precision. But this is a fever dreamed, metaphorical horror film so it's easy to overlook those minutiae.

I'll see "The Substance" again, just to re-experience the last thirty minutes; there was so much going on that I feel like I couldn't take it all in. It eventually became obvious to me how the film was going to end, but then it just kept going, outdoing itself in extremes and gooey, viscous gore (to call this a "body horror" film is almost an understatement). It eventually became so insane, cartoonish and excessive that I felt I was laughing along with a nightmare.

That "The Substance" stands out is a reminder of just how few films today possess an original vision. It rises far above the endless stream of safe, cookie-cutter superhero sequels that are being churned out purely for profit. I hope this film makes a sizeable profit -it's high time audiences show studios they want to see something fresh and unconventional for a change.

reviews.author: EUyeshima
reviews.body: It's a delicate balancing act between abject horror and black comedy, but in her sophomore effort, director/screenwriter Coralie Fargeat not only straddles the tightrope but upends it big time with this nightmarish, somewhat overlong 2024 film. The fact that Fargeat provides a distinctly female perspective adds a layer of self-hatred complexity and absurdist humor to the relentlessly gory scenes. The plot focuses on the fittingly named Elisabeth Sparkle, a former Oscar winner turned into a celebrity fitness personality. With her stardom fading, she turns fifty and gets immediately fired by her vulgarian network boss perfectly named Harvey. After Elisabeth gets into a car accident, a highly suspect male nurse connects her with a black market cell-replicating drug that promises to recapture her youth. What it actually does is produce a doppelgänger fully formed named Sue. The deal is that Elisabeth and Sue can't exist at the same time because they're the same person and must strictly trade lives in alternate seven-day periods. No exception - so the horror is borne from the inevitable conflict that occurs, and I was amazed how far Fargeat went with the violent consequences. Casting Demi Moore as Elisabeth was pure genius because her empowered Hollywood reputation and purported obsession with youth fits the role perfectly. She responds with a fearless performance that devolves into unrelenting desperation. Margaret Qualley also swings for the fences as Sue, initially vapid but speeding into Machiavellian menace. Dennis Quaid captures Harvey's tawdry personality with zestful disgust. Tweaking the popularity of "miracle" injection drugs like Ozempic, Fargeat was definitely inspired by American horror cinema classics from "Death Becomes Her" to "Carrie" to "Requiem for a Dream" to "Whatever Happened to Baby Jane?". Dazzling, absurdist, and stomach turning.

reviews.author: cinnoche
reviews.body:
If you've ever heard the expression "Be careful what you wish for," the plot of this film is a perfect illustration of it.

Speaking of the plot, I want to highlight its originality, something I find quite rare these days. From start to finish, I was WOW by the ideas of the director. The casting choices were perfect. The use of music with contrasting atmospheres reflected the mental health of the characters very well.

That said, I must admit the storyline was a bit predictable. Trusting someone experiencing the spotlight for the first time always comes with risks. I won't say more to avoid spoiling the movie.

In the end, I'd give the film a score of 7/10. The ending left me a bit unsatisfied, it felt a little rushed and gave an impression of disorder.

reviews.author: georgerennie-97328
reviews.body:
This film was very unpleasant to watch.

Simultaneously, it was brilliant and hilarious.

I don't particularly like body horror films -- and please be forewarned -- this is very much a body horror film in so many ways. But it's so much more.

At some deep level, this is a film about aging, decay, and death. Also, regret, and wistfulness for youth. It's brilliantly cast, with Demi Moore as an aging star, and Margaret Qualley as the alternative to an aging star. Both give fantastic performances.

Essentially, it's a story of how a narcissist might seek a return to youth, and how the younger version might not want to return to older age. But this film becomes wonderfully unhinged quite quickly and somehow manages to escalate from there.

I've seen a lot in my life, but literally found myself covering my mouth with my hand. It think this film is magnificent.

Very unpleasant, but magnificent.

Well done to all involved!

reviews.author: danamcrane
reviews.body:
As in her previous movie, Revenge, Fargeat once again takes aim at the patriarchy and it's omnipresent male gaze, but this time with a far less antagonist subject who appears willing to do anything for fame.

But The Substance has just as much (if not more) to say about mother daughter relationships involving a rebellious teen. It's a shock to see the mother figure of Demi Moore give birth to a daughter who is able to stitch up mom's c-section. It's less of a surprise when mom ages prematurely as she struggles against her daughter's growing independence.

But Fargeat applies this commentary most sharply to Hollywood nepobabies as the "daughter" takes over her mother's career. At first, Sue (played by Margaret Qualley, the real life daughter of actress Andie McDowell) is willing to acknowledge her mother to her producer (a scenery chewing Dennis Quaid), but is soon all too willing to abandon and even destroy her mom in order to further her own career. Meanwhile, torn between pride for her daughter figure and despair at the shrinking horizons of her own opportunities, Demi Moore's aging actress goes on a culinary binge which is inherited as a bizarre eating disorder in Sue (you'll know it when you see it).

The end of the movie goes off the rails in ways that only fans of body horror could appreciate, but suffice to say that third generation nepobabies are probably a bad idea.

The real takeaway though is that fame in the arts (like power in politics) is almost impossible to walk away from no matter how old or unfit for the role you may get.

reviews.author: exceladeogun
reviews.body:
The Substance

The Substance tells the story of Elizabeth Sparkle, a celebrity at 50 who's about to be washed out of the industry. An accident leads her to get a substance that can make a newer younger version of her. However, there's a catch: both versions of Elizabeth-the seasoned star and her youthful counterpart-can exist, but only one can be active at a time, alternating on a weekly basis.

At its core, The Substance delves into the theme of aging. As someone who often reflects on this aspect of life, I find it a fascinating and nuanced exploration. The plot of The Substance is bonkers, fresh, and singular.

The bonkers story of The Substance is elevated by its striking visuals. Here, the visuals are raw and obscene, and definitely not for the squeamish. The camera angles transport from jittery sequences to intimate ones, all enhanced by a gripping auditory experience that pulls the viewer deeper into the film's unsettling world.

The performances here are nothing short of splendid. Demi Moore anchors The Substance, and she's absolutely perfect in her portrayal. To start, Demi is a bombshell, and seeing the journey she takes in this movie one has to ask, if a character with the build and beauty that Demi possesses goes through this, what hope do the rest of us have? Margaret Qualley matches Demi breath for breath, stride for stride. Dennis Quaid's portrayal of a repulsive, horrible boss is nailed with an almost unnerving ease.

For all the praises that The Substance will garner, from the performances to the makeup and the cinematography, the ending is a letdown. Metaphorically, it's poignant and significant, but if we're judging the sequences based on the literal events that occur, the walls begin to crumble.

In all, The Substance is a thrilling ride and a grand entry for body horror.

8/10.

Supporting for Qualley. Best sound design. Costume design. Cinematography. Original script. It's goes all in and nails everything it was trying to accomplish. Do not watch this while high. I can't wait to see what Fargeat has one of the most distinct voices in cinema right now, and I can't wait to see what she makes next.

reviews.author: natsamp
reviews.body:
"The Substance" delivers a powerful commentary on society's tendency to value women primarily for their physical appearance. By centering the narrative around a woman in the entertainment industry-a field notorious for its harsh scrutiny of women-the film effectively highlights the pressures many face. The underlying message I took away is the dangerous nature of insecurity, and how far people are willing to go to alter their appearance, even at the risk of their own lives.

The film skillfully amplifies this theme through its use of exaggerated body horror and gore, creating a visceral experience that emphasizes the consequences of such societal pressures.

Visually, the cinematography was stunning, the story was both original and inventive, and the special effects were captivating. This is a film I would definitely watch again.

reviews.author: zkonedog
reviews.body:
About an hour and fifty minutes into The Substance, this was the thought running through my head: "Is this the best movie I've seen in 2024?!". An absolutely masterful sci-fi-/thriller/horror/drama genre-bender. Alas, there was 30 more minutes of runtime in which The Substance completely goes off the rails.

For a very basic overview, The Substance tells the story of Elisabeth (Demi Moore) a TV fitness star pushed to the sidelines by slimy exec Harvey (Dennis Quaid) after turning 50. Desperate to remain relevant, Elisabeth tries out a drug--known only as The Substance--which recreates her as younger self Sue (Margaret Qualley). The catch? They must switch back and forth between old and young every week. But what happens when greed and ambition enter the equation and The Substance's boundaries are stretched to the breaking point?

In terms of overall premise, this might actually be the best genre movie of 2024. For a large part of its runtime it hits all the right notes in terms of amazing cinematography, deep human thematics, and even tongue-in-cheek comedy. I was absolutely riveted to see where it was all going.

It helps that Moore & Qualley are amazing in their dual-ish role. Though rarely on-screen together, they perfectly embody the message that director Coralie Fargeat is trying to convey. It was even great to see Quad not in the ultra-religious roles that have composed his later career.

Truly, over an hour-and-a-half in I was thinking "I have to tell all my friends/family about this one!".

But then the ending transpires and most of the film's insanely interesting premise is squandered. Ironically, I'm usually one who doesn't get too fussed about endings. I don't need everything wrapped up in a bow and I often like some ambiguity that requires further thought as the credits roll. But the ending to The Substance isn't that tactful by a mile. Instead, it does an on-a-dime transformation from gripping drama/thriller to absolute splatter or body horror grindhouse work. I won't spoil it here, but suffice it to say the final 30 minutes almost feels as if it was a different movie from what had proceeded it.

Is it perhaps a little harsh to drop The Substance all the way down to 6 stars? Maybe. But I can't shake the feeling that the film's ending is not only an unexpected tonal shift but almost a bit dishonest to its viewers. It would be like attending a symphony orchestra concert and having Miley Cyrus come out for the finale. Neither are bad in their own right, but the incongruous nature is jarring. I absolutely could not shake that feeling when The Substance concluded, and that is why I ultimately (and sadly) cannot give it more than a "just above okay" final rating.

reviews.author: masonsaul
reviews.body:
The Substance isn't subtle in anything it does nor does it care. It's a scathing critique of how the entertainment industry refuses to let women age through an unforgettable body horror lens. The premise has simple rules that are explained succinctly and once it starts breaking them chaos builds, resulting in a jaw droppingly disturbing and darkly funny third act that has to be seen to be believed.

Demi Moore gives it her all in a lead performance that's funny, heartbreaking and gonzo when needed. The only thing working against her awards prospects is the academy's own snobbery against films that are as wonderfully weird as this. Margaret Qualley has the right amount of confidence and selfishness in an early career high performance and Dennis Quaid is having an absolute ball with his unrelentingly loud role.

Coralie Fargeat's direction is amazing, contorting the male gaze to be as uncomfortable as possible and packing the film with neat visual metaphors. The body horror itself has gnarly sequences throughout and a climax that just doesn't stop piling on the blood and mutations. The overall bluntness is enhanced by Benjamin Kracun's in your face cinematography which gets as close as possible to everything.

The sound design is ridiculously intense for every little detail and none of them are allowed to go unnoticed which means when it's something actually visceral like a car crash, the sounds are horrifically loud and detailed. Composer Raffertie brings a thumping score to the mix which has the same level of intensity as every other aspect and hits just as hard as the numerous injections of the substance itself.

reviews.author: imcookie-1
reviews.body:
Wow. Just... wow. I'm still processing what I witnessed in "The Substance," but I can say with certainty that it's unlike anything else you'll see this year. Coralie Fargeat has crafted a fever dream that's equal parts seductive and repulsive, often in the same breath.

Let's start with Demi Moore, who gives a career-best performance as Elizabeth Sparkle. She lays herself bare (literally and figuratively) in a role that feels intensely personal. The desperation, the vulnerability, the rage - it's all there, etched into every line on her face. And then there's Margaret Qualley as Sue, the younger doppelganger born from Elizabeth's twisted desire. Qualley nails the intoxicating mix of youthful energy and creeping horror as she realizes the true cost of her existence.

Visually, this film is a feast. The neon-soaked cinematography makes even the most grotesque moments weirdly beautiful. And oh boy, does it get grotesque. If you're squeamish, consider yourself warned - the body horror here makes Cronenberg look tame. There were moments where I wanted to look away but couldn't, mesmerized by the sheer audacity of what was unfolding on screen.

Fargeat's satirical blade is razor-sharp, skewering Hollywood's obsession with youth and beauty. Dennis Quaid's sleazy producer (aptly named Harvey) embodies every gross stereotype of the industry, and watching him leer at Qualley made my skin crawl in the best possible way.

Now, I'll admit the final act goes completely off the rails. It's bonkers in a way that will likely divide audiences. Personally, I was cackling with a mix of shock and delight, but I can see how it might be too much for some viewers. The metaphors get a bit heavy-handed, but when you're dealing with such extreme subject matter, subtlety kind of goes out the window.

Is "The Substance" a perfect film? No. But it's a bold, audacious piece of cinema that left me exhilarated and slightly queasy. It's the kind of movie that burrows into your brain and festers there, demanding to be discussed and dissected. Love it or hate it, you won't be able to ignore it.

If you're in the mood for something truly unique and aren't afraid to get your hands (and eyes) dirty, "The Substance" is a must-see. Just maybe skip the popcorn for this one.
