reviews.author: gobusardar
reviews.body:
**The Substance (2024) - A Riveting Psychological Thriller (9/10 Stars) 🌟

**The Substance** (2024) is a masterful psychological thriller that delves deep into the dark underbelly of the human psyche. Directed by Coralie Fargeat, this film combines stellar performances, an engrossing plot, and striking visuals to deliver an unforgettable cinematic experience.

**Plot and Direction**: The movie revolves around Elisabeth Sparkle, portrayed by Demi Moore, who navigates the treacherous waters of the Hollywood industry's obsession with youth and beauty. The storyline is intense and gripping, keeping the audience engaged with its unpredictable twists and turns. Coralie Fargeat's direction is impeccable, skillfully balancing the eerie and the elegant, creating an atmosphere that is both haunting and mesmerizing.

**Performances**: Demi Moore delivers a powerful performance, capturing the desperation and determination of her character with finesse. Margaret Qualley, playing the younger version of Elisabeth, brings a raw and unsettling energy to the screen. Dennis Quaid's portrayal of the manipulative Hollywood executive adds depth and tension to the narrative.

**Visuals and Cinematography**: The cinematography is a visual treat, with vibrant colors contrasting against the dark themes, enhancing the film's unsettling beauty. Each frame is meticulously crafted, contributing to the film's overall impact. The body horror elements are depicted with striking realism, making the transformation scenes both mesmerizing and disturbing.

**Themes and Messages**: **The Substance** explores profound themes such as vanity, self-worth, and the relentless pursuit of an idealized youth. It offers a scathing critique of the entertainment industry's beauty standards and the lengths to which individuals will go to conform. The film is a thought-provoking commentary that lingers long after the credits roll.

**Overall Impression**: This movie is a standout in the thriller genre, offering a unique blend of psychological depth and visual grandeur. It captivates the audience with its compelling narrative and leaves them pondering the implications of its themes. **The Substance** is a must-watch for anyone who appreciates a well-crafted thriller with a strong message.

**Rating**: 🌟🌟🌟🌟🌟🌟🌟🌟🌟 (9/10)

If you haven't seen **The Substance** yet, make sure to add it to your watchlist. It's an experience that promises to both thrill and provoke deep thought.

reviews.author: F_ormalin
reviews.body:
I am a man. I admit that I cannot fully appreciate this film as a feminist statement. But I recognize its activist value and do not criticize it, such films are necessary.

Except that I cannot agree that this is a "strong" or "deep" story. Still, inflated standards of beauty are pop feminism. So, Substance's activism would fit into several TikTok videos. It seemed to me that the Barbie film is stronger in this sense.

In general, after this film, there was a feeling that we can already distinguish a new genre - femsplotation. Which will include Substance, Barbie and other films with superficial but important messages.

As a body horror, the film seemed boring (not as boring as Titan). The third act pays for the entire film's involvement in the genre - it is beautiful. I do not agree with people who consider it too grotesque and "trash". On the contrary, without the monster act, the film would be completely bland and perhaps would not be remembered by the public as much.

It should be noted that given its genre, the film is shot very beautifully. This shows the dichotomy that we observe in the plot: "the beautiful coexists with the ugly."

Demi Moore is gorgeous, give her all the statuettes. I love Margaret Qualley, but in this film her role did not imply deep acting.

Overall, I can't say much about this film. I would say that it is overrated, but I will not, because I respect its significance for women.

P. S. The topic of gender dysphoria would fit perfectly into the body horror genre. It is literally a state of rejection of one's own identity and body. It seems that this could result in an equally powerful statement, but a much more interesting and organic film.

P. P. S. To everyone who saw the "activator" from the film Ozempik, I recommend watching the film Reanimator.

reviews.author: NateWatchesCoolMovies
reviews.body: It takes a lot of courage to put oneself out there in the sort of intimidating tornado of physical performance and thematic taboos that Demi Moore fearlessly undertakes in Coralie Fargeat's the Substance, a positively unhinged socially satirical body horror opus. Moore is Elizabeth Sparkle, a once radiant beauty queen movie star who is approaching the sunset of her 50's and is very unhappy with the perceived diminishment of her good looks, scrutinized under the ruthlessly shallow guillotine lens aimed at her by society at large (which includes us, whether we'd care to admit it or not). Also disappointed with her aging is grotesque network producer Harvey (Dennis Quaid like you've never seen him before), who fires her in favour of somebody younger and more... perky. As if listening in on the proceedings, a bizarre pharmaceutical corporation reaches out to her with their latest mad scientist concoction: 'The Substance,' a complex regiment of serums devised to give an aging body that much needed (or perhaps just desired?) nubile nitro boost. Ah, but not without its brutally karmic repercussions, mind you. Fargeat takes the sort of loony conceit one would find in a particularly imaginative episode of Tales From The Crypt and blows it up like a disgusting parade float with horrifyingly tactile sound design, glisteningly vile practical gore effects, crackhead sponsored editing and a trio of lead performances that seem ripped right out of a tongue in cheek nightmare. Moore is staggering and I'd spoil the best surprises this film has to offer if I mentioned the lengths she goes to in dedication to performance here, I haven't seen her chomp at the bit in her work since... well, since she herself was on Tales From The Crypt many moons ago. Quaid is on behavioural steroids here in a role originally meant for Ray Liotta (that would have been something), Harvey has one note and its 'hilariously despicable' whether he's screaming demands into his phone, changing from one Hunger Games level extravagant outfit to the next at rapid fire speed or devouring a plate of butter soaked prawns with fiendishly horrible enthusiasm. Margaret Qualley, the third musketeer in this casting spectacle, is also unbelievably dynamic and almost opulently hot as a character too fun to spoil with context in a review. Every artist involved gives it their career best all, right down to the B-cam operator tasked with haunting establishing shots of ominous palm trees to the FX team giving new meta meaning to the term "splatter zone." Something that truly has to be seen to be believed.

reviews.author: missreneb
reviews.body:
I had been excited to see this film after the previews and to see Demi back in her element. Her performance is brave and well done for sure. All of the acting is very good.

The problem I have is that the last third of the film is over the top grotesque and not in a fun Tarantino way at that.

The very last scene is how I think most people in the business of fame feel after their career has petered out. However the journey, again from the last third of the story, was an eye roll for me.

I appreciate the effort in making a film that centers around beauty and aging in our throw away / cancel-culture society today. Plus, many people do not understand how difficult it is to make a film altogether. Simple YouTube videos that flow well and hold attention is not easy.

It is a film worth watching in my view. I am sure I will rewatch it as well.

reviews.author: baharahdz
reviews.body:
Over the past few years, the horror genre has felt increasingly stale. As someone who enjoys watching horror films, I've noticed the same tired tropes and recycled storylines being used year after year. Whether it's the haunted house, the cursed object, or the possessed child, many horror movies have become predictable and formulaic. There's often a lack of innovation or creativity when it comes to storytelling, and for a genre that thrives on surprise and fear, that can be a big problem. This sense of repetition has left me feeling disappointed and, honestly, less excited about watching horror films in general. So, I usually approach new releases in the genre with low expectations.

That being said, I went to the cinema to see this particular movie completely blind-something I rarely do. I didn't watch any trailers or read any reviews beforehand, and I honestly had no idea what to expect. Typically, I like to know at least a little about the film before committing to the time and expense of going to the theater. But for some reason, I decided to take a chance on this one. I think it was partially because I was craving something new, something that might surprise me, and I'm so glad I took that chance. From the very beginning, this movie had a different feel, and it immediately set itself apart from the usual horror fare.

The first thing that struck me was the cinematography. In horror films, the visual style often takes a backseat to the scares, with dim lighting, shaky camera movements, and rapid editing being used to create a sense of chaos and tension. But this film was different. The cinematography was absolutely stunning, with a keen attention to detail and an emphasis on atmosphere. Every shot was carefully composed, and the use of lighting and color added to the mood without feeling overdone. The camera didn't just follow the characters-it became part of the storytelling, using angles and movements to build suspense in a way that felt fresh and innovative. It was clear from the beginning that this wasn't your typical low-effort horror flick.

What really stood out to me, though, was the subject matter. Horror has a tendency to rely on familiar themes, but this movie took a completely different approach. Without giving too much away, the film explored new ideas that felt both relevant and unsettling. It wasn't just about jump scares or shock value-it actually had something to say. The story was thought-provoking, and the themes lingered with me long after I left the theater. There was a depth to the narrative that's often missing in modern horror, and I appreciated that it didn't spoon-feed the audience. Instead, it trusted us to think, to question, and to interpret the events in our own way.

Another thing that made this movie a standout was the pacing. It knew exactly when to ramp up the tension and when to let things breathe. Too often, horror movies either drag in the middle or rush through the climax, leaving the audience feeling unsatisfied. But this one balanced everything perfectly. The buildup was slow and deliberate, which only made the payoff that much more effective. It kept me on the edge of my seat without feeling like it was trying too hard, and when the final act arrived, it was both shocking and earned.

To be honest, I don't always write reviews. In fact, it's rare that I feel compelled to share my thoughts about a movie, but this one was different. It reminded me that horror can still be fresh, innovative, and, most importantly, fun. I left the theater feeling energized and excited about the genre again, which is something I haven't felt in quite a while.

If you've been feeling the same way about horror lately-disappointed by the sameness and predictability-then I highly recommend giving this movie a chance. It's a fresh take on the genre with fantastic cinematography, an engaging story, and a truly unique subject matter. This film is proof that horror can still surprise us, and it's definitely worth watching.

reviews.author: Stay_away_from_the_Metropol
reviews.body:
This is the film I'd been waiting for most all year long, and I would say that it did fulfill my expectations. I had checked out writer/director/Frenchie Coralie Fargeat's previous breakthrough film, REVENGE (2017), which was a completely over-the-top, ultra-violent revenge thriller that felt like what you would get if you took the energy of the darkest Hard Summer Festival EDM tracks and adapted them into a horror-ish film. I don't think I've seen any other noteworthy films that felt so "EDM-drenched", outside of maybe Harmony Korine's SPRING BREAKERS; the main difference being that Korine did it in an entirely tongue-in-cheek way, while Fargeat's "living dubstep" vibe feels primarily sincere - typically I would think this would be a bad thing, but somehow with Fargeat it works and feels very right - perhaps it's one of those things that only a French person could get away with.

Once I heard how intense The Substance was supposed to be, and how many people "couldn't handle it" at its initial screenings, along with the synopsis, intriguing cast, and seeing who the director was, I felt very certain the world was about to have something of great note in its hands. I must say that I am a bit surprised just how many people seem to be in love with this movie, when it's so extreme. To me, it mostly blends Extreme French Horror with pure exploitation and, of course, body horror, but in the bigger picture, what it really feels like is the epitome of a B-movie that somehow managed to get made and widely released with an A-list cast and A-level production value. Of course, for me, these are all wonderful things. I'd say this is the greatest B-movie to be released since MANDY in 2018, and it joins a very small group of contemporary B-movies which manage to transcend all elements of cheapness that make most B-movies precisely that, and win over a larger audience.

It seems obvious to say this is an entirely unexpected and astonishing comeback role for Demi Moore. Who would have imagined an A-list actress gone for so long would make her return to the big screen after raising multiple daughters and having her legendary husband turn to a vegetable, in the most extreme and disturbing movie to see a wide release in years? I mean, at times The Substance almost feels like a BASKET CASE sequel. It has to take a lot to mentally commit to something like this. While I think the Oscar nod talk I've heard mentioned around her performance is a bit of wishful thinking, I do find her performance entirely worthy of celebration - she pulls no punches, and, man, her character goes deeper into an abyss than 99% of film characters could ever dare. While her performance was grade A, I would say that only Willa Fitzgerald's performance in Strange Darling is one that reaches a level worth noting above everyone else, this year. Considering Margaret Qualley is one of my favorite actresses overall at the moment, her involvement had me stoked from the start, and added much to enjoy throughout the entire film. Her umbrella of films is quite fascinating at this point, just as it's fascinating that she is allowing herself to become this staple of some sort of frighteningly hyper-sexual archetype. It's funny how her mom freaked out over how "crude" Drive Away Dolls was at the beginning of the year, then her dad was on his way to see Kinds of Kindness with a group of friends, and she told me him to turn around and not watch it. Can you imagine how they felt when they watched The Substance?!?!?! I think one of them might implode. This is probably her most lascivious role yet, aside from maybe SANCTUARY - though I'm a massive fan of the majority of her roles, I've gotta say SANCTUARY still takes the cake as her finest performance, but she is unabashedly diving headfirst into near-pornographic territory in The Substance, and it's very wild. Dennis Quaid was also perfect in this.

Without spoiling anything, I've enjoyed how polarizing the final act of this film has been. While some have said that it was the only part that didn't work for them, a greater quantity have stated the final act is precisely what elevated the film to be a new favorite for them. To me, the final act is exactly what the movie needs. While it was absolutely not what I was expecting, tonally, I welcomed it with a massive smile (while trying not to be fully removed from the finale as my girlfriend ran out of the auditorium amidst an anxiety attack during the ultra-violent "chase scene", and stayed outside for the last 25 minutes of the film). While I found the first 2/3 of the film to be rather repetitive in structure, it's not a bad thing as I believe that is how this story needed to be told. Much like Enter The Void, it is more of an experience you must live (or survive) through, rather than simply a story you are being told in chapters. The final act really breaks the formula up, and wraps things up in a glorious blast of hyper stimulation that is not often seen in movies this century. And, it really shines a light on how much nuanced humor is meant to be underlying through the majority of the movie that precedes it. I could never refer to this as a dark comedy - it is far too brutal for that, but it definitely has plentiful elements of humor. It really is quite a singular film; while the closest I could get to anything is like combining all of Frank Hennenlotter's movies (Basket Case, Frankenhooker, Brain Damage, and Bad Biology) with old school Cronenberg (The Fly, Videodrome, eXiSTeNz), but honestly, even that can't quite encapsulate what The Substance "has done". The only way one can understand what The Substance has to offer is by seeing it.

reviews.author: 121mcv
reviews.body: The Desperate Pursuit of Eternal Youth Leads to Nightmar : I found 'The Substance' to be a visually stunning and thought-provoking film that effectively explores the themes of aging, self-acceptance, and societal pressures. Demi Moore delivers a powerful performance, and the special effects are impressive. While I enjoyed the film overall, I felt the ending was unnecessary and detracted from the otherwise strong narrative. Despite this minor flaw, 'The Substance' is a unique and memorable cinematic experience that's worth watching for those who appreciate bold and unconventional storytelling...

reviews.author: paulfriedrichmoebius
reviews.body:
Story is simple: Demi Moore's character is getting older and loses her show doing aerobics ob television, until she gets her hands on an illicit substance that promises to change her life which it indeed does. The film is a satire of society, the media, social expectations of women and so on and so forth, but it's also a collage of references. It seems as though almost every scene is ripped from. 2001, The Shining, The Elephant Man, Naked Lunch, Re-Animator, The Fly, Fight Club, Mullholland Drive, Society (or Carrie, I am not sure), Vertigo and possibly Covenant. I think it also references La Haine, Irréversible and Le Pari, and in my mind also the video to I See You Baby by Groove Armada, but I might be imaging that. The point is it's fun to spot the references.

But it is also a clever film. It is basically the picture of Dorian Gray, but the picture is also alive. The two people depend on each other but do not share a consciousness and can not meet each other, which makes negotiating the interdependence difficult. This element that sets the film apart from all similar stories I know of is not a bug, but a feature: It opens up a whole set of questions regarding how the two parts of the same person see each other and what their relationship could be.

But it's also a film with blood a-plenty. Supposedly it holds the record for most fake blood used for a film production. I cannot say whether that is true, but it does not seem impossible.

And Demi Moore is fantastic in this film, I never thought I would enjoy any of her films.

reviews.author: Ray53
reviews.body:
High praise to the two lead actors for so completely giving themselves over to such difficult roles. If you are put off by nudity or graphic violence, don't see it.

The film operates as much on the metaphorical as the physical level, offering relentless, even enraged criticism of a culture that values youth at any price, particularly as shown by attitudes toward women and as shown by the extent to which people will do anything to stay attractive and relevant.

The actual process of "the substance" is ridiculous, so accept the metaphor. Same for the over the top sequences of violence.

The men in this film operate on multiple levels of venality, lechery, greed, insensitivity, or brute piggishness.

So, is it lecture on the horror of male hegemony? Yes, but the acting is excellent (though Quaid goes way overboard on the Hollywood male swine bit), and the passion of the director and the actors to tell a fable about the horror of exploitation merits a fair viewing.

reviews.author: alwinsup
reviews.body:
Good story line and a creative movie. Actress are great. Great body as well! Acting spot on. Script good. The motive is very clear and is a powerful message. Maybe with a little bit of more shots of how fun it is to be young in the open world would make this motive even better.

Sometimes it is a bit disgusting to watch. You do not want to watch this if you feel sick.

The white men and CEO of the news netwerk was a funny extra touch. As was the neighbor! A bit more jokes like these could have made the movie better. A missed chanced!

So.. a cool, weird, funny and a bit of a disgusting movie. Could have been better, but still very creative and original. 7 out of 10.

reviews.author: nashielly-36114
reviews.body: I has been a long time since I watched a tribute to David Cronenberg that well done. The monster gave me nostalgic remember the beloved Fly :') I also has an wink to David Lynch. And the social impact so important to say it out loud! Women and men are more than just age or a carreer. Also, I really liked the ending, again really Cronenbergish. The architecture on the film was right on point. Demi Moore performance was terrific. Close ups where needed, photography really well ejected. I guess for me it was awesome to see Cronenberg's legacy going through so many years, cinema owes a lot to David Cronenberg.

reviews.author: Mango-30793
reviews.body:
It's an original idea that seems to be going places for the first half of the movie.

Character development was poor, though. For such a long movie, very little happens. I think they could have developed the story a little better and filled out the characters experiences more fully. Parts of it felt flat and almost deliberately acted badly (Sue's character particularly but maybe this is to contrast the wisdom of age with the flippancy and shallowness of youth) Anyway, I'm rambling because of this ridiculous 600 word quota. Basically it's just one very long Twilight Zone episode and not very much happens.

reviews.author: denis888
reviews.body:
Okay, where shall I start? I like both Demi Moore and a very sexy Margaret Qualley, and also Dennis Quaid seems to be a very decent actor in his own right. The premises of the movie also sounds promising.

Sure, and then you start watching this... er... schlock and you understand that you don't understand.

There are nymerous plot holes which I am going to describe here to avoid spoilers, that I started to ask myself - why?

The turns of the plot also seem to appear out of nowhere and what is worse, all the characters lack both charisma, depth, humor, credibility or cleverness. They do what they do and there is NO solid ground why they do it.

The whole film looks as if it was made and conceived by a young teen who is preoccupied with nudity and some pseudo-scientific ideas.

I am sorry, who is that voice on the phone, why is that there is? There are unanswered questions, and not because the writers wanted us to guess and percieve but because they did not understand themselves! Truly so. There's no any substance (pun intended) to the basic premise, as well as huge plot hole in two heroes actions, as well as in the totally unredeeming final that leaves us all scratching our heads and puking.

Yup, the movie is way too disgusting for no reason at all. Way too sick and way too illogical.

The very last 30 minutes are a real carnival of poorest taste, huge plot errors and wrong decisions.

I watched and thought, why.

The filmmakers really wanted to look smart and wise, instead, they left a mess and ahuge pool of unnecessary vomit of silly ideas. Vomit for sure...

Believe me, this movie is THAT bad - overlong, overblown, overwrought and overtly insipid, vapid, languid, empty mess.

Rating --- ZERO, but alas, no zero here, so One as a must be.

reviews.author: SinceNovember2000
reviews.body:
*The Substance*, directed by Coralie Fargeat, is a vibrant, adrenaline-charged dive into 80s glamour, elevated by both stunning cinematography and magnetic performances. The film feels almost like a visual assault, packed with close-ups that put you right in the action, making it an "in your face" experience. Every detail is bold, raw, and visceral, immersing you in a colorful world that drips with a hyper-stylized 80s aesthetic.

Demi Moore delivers a powerhouse performance, embodying her role with a sense of urgency and intensity that makes you wonder, "What if she stuck to the plan?" This question lingers throughout the film, adding layers of complexity to her character. Moore balances the rawness of her performance with an undeniable air of glamour, perfectly in tune with the film's glamorous 80s style.

Dennis Quaid is equally compelling, offering a superb acting display that serves as the perfect counterbalance to Moore's intensity. Their on-screen chemistry pulls you deeper into the story, while the cinematography heightens every moment. The film's use of light and shadow adds a cinematic depth that feels both classic and innovative.

Margaret Qualley's Sue is a standout, as she embodies a character who is both fragile and fierce. Qualley carries the emotional weight of the film, making Sue's journey one of the most compelling aspects of the story till the end.

Adding to this immersive experience is the great score by Raffertie, whose soundtrack elevates the film with a mix of rhythmic beats that perfectly complement the film's narrative. The music captures both the glamour and grit of the story.

Fargeat's direction is masterful, blending grit with glossy visuals in a way that feels unique to her vision. Overall, *The Substance* is a must-see for its striking cinematography, intense performances, and unforgettable style and score/soundtrack.

reviews.author: danchilton-71955
reviews.body:
One thing The Substance is not, is subtle. It shouts it's themes loudly. It bathes the viewers eyeballs with beauty and then assaults them with grotesque body horror of the highest order. It infests the ears with horrible squelching, popping and cracking. It's quite an experience.

Demi Moore plays Oscar winning actress Elizabeth Sparkle, who now hosts a daytime yoga show produced by odious TV exec Dennis Quad. Deemed over the hill on her fiftieth birthday (despite looking like Demi Moore) and let go she turns to a shady procedure that involves injecting herself with "The Substance". This births the young and pristine Sue (Margaret Qualley) who picks up where Elizabeth thinks her life should be, becoming her own replacement on TV. The problem is, the two halves need to share, with each being awake for seven days at a time and like feeding your Mogwai after midnight, there are extreme consequences to not respecting the balance.

The Substance is a high saturation parable set in a showbiz world with the volume cranked up. The rules of science do not apply here, with the substance itself representing a deal with the devil more than anything else. It's a feminine story, but not really a feminist one. Quad is disgusting and every other male is lecherous, predatory or pathetic (often all three) but they only have power because Elizabeth/Sue is so desperate for their approval. The focus is on internalised misogyny, the resentments women can harbour to each other and the damage they inflict on themselves in the never ending battle for fleeting adulation. The phrase, "your own worst enemy", has never been more appropriate.

At its heart the film may have a simple message of enjoy the life you have but the way it shows you is anything but. The body horror on display is some of the most inventive in decades; wince inducing, thematically powerful and just slightly hilarious. The sound design is, if anything, even more uncomfortable. Every snap, tear and thud will have you gritting your teeth and it all sounds so horribly wet. You wouldn't think watching someone eat prawns could be an endurance test.

It's cliche to call performances like Moore puts in here "brave" but she certainly leaves it all on the line, both physically and emotionally (the hardest to watch scene doesn't involve body horror at all, just a women crippled by her own imagined inadequacies). The meta casting of her as a woman desperate to stay young and beautiful isn't lost on her but she gives a powerhouse turn, reminding everyone she is one of Hollywood's most underrated performers. Qualley is very much in the secondary role but she dazzles as walking Diet Coke commercial Sue. Hollywood producers will be pleased she already has a good body of work so over the next couple of years they can pretend they aren't casting her after seeing the film she is a sex object in.

The gnarly visuals and general ickiness will mean The Substance isn't for everyone and the deliriously over the top finale goes on a little too long but anyone with even an inkling to check this film out should do so. The effects work is a tour de force, there's a career best performance from Demi Moore and a declaration from director Coralie Fargeat that previous movie Revenge was merely a warm up.

9 full vials of stabiliser out of 10.

reviews.author: paulclaassen
reviews.body:
Once famous actress Elizabeth Sparkle (Demi Moore) now hosts an aerobics show for a television network, but on her 50th birthday she is dismissed by her producer Harvey (Dennis Quaid), who wants a fresh new young face for the show.

Upset, Elizabeth is involved in a car crash on her way home. At the hospital, a young male nurse hands her a flash drive. Once home, she watches the contents, which is an advertisement for a substance that will produce a younger version of yourself. She orders it, but the substance comes with strict procedural instructions she must follow without exception.

A younger, new version of herself literally emerges from within, and there are now two versions of Elizabeth Sparkle. As the young version, she decides to audition as replacement for her show, and introduces herself as Sue. Harvey - not realizing who Sue truly is - immediately hires her.

Enjoying her newfound youth, firm body, and success, Sue neglects the instructions, and things start going horribly wrong for both versions. 'The Substance' is an extremely well made film with a great soundtrack, photography, editing, and sound effects. Not to mention the insane practical effects!! Not since 'The Thing' and 'The Fly' have I seen these incredible practical effects.

Unfortunately the film completely falls apart during the final ten minutes. What the hell were they thinking? I'm not going to do spoilers, and all I'm going to say is that the reaction from the audience (in the movie) was not realistic and actually completely stupid. Even the photography was shaky and completely out of focus. Just why? The film had the potential for a much better ending... Even so, this was still an incredible watch and a very unique premise.

Demi Moore delivered a fantastic performance as Elizabeth Sparkle, and Margaret Qualley is perfectly cast as Sue. Ten out of ten for the make-up effects team!! The film teaches us a powerful lesson to accept yourself, and accept the fact that we all age.

reviews.author: Agent10
reviews.body:
I'm not a horror fan, not the least. I don't care much for slashers or jump scares or evil incarnate characters. What I do like is societal horror, where the machinations of our being are dissected and put on display. The Substance is just a massive, in your face tirade against a variety of social ills like beauty standards, self love and shallow entertainment.

We meet the venerable Elisabeth Sparkle, who is still vibrant and fresh but has the unfortunate issue of growing old. Despite being outwardly beautiful, she is still longing for the love and adoration she receives from her position in society. Like many women and older people alike, much of our society tosses these natural changing ideals down the street rather than embracing them. Who cares about experience, we need something new and shiny to get us away from our bright phone screens.

It's fitting Demi Moore plays the lead role, who 20 years ago lit up the headlines by spending millions to turn back the clock on her face and her body. These days, Botox and lip fillers can be done during lunch. BBL's are attainable by even regular women as opposed to just the elite with enough zeroes in their bank account. If Moore did what she did 20 years ago again, no one would bat an eye. Call it the Kardashian effect I guess, for there is never a price tag or punishment high enough that wouldn't be worth changing your appearance and looking more youthful. Our 4K world has made it tough for people to age, so to speak.

The story is simple enough. Take an elixir and for seven days, you can be a younger and more attractive person. The issue of course, every Faustian bargain comes at a price. As the movie moves along, Elisabeth's alter ego, Sue, becomes extremely popular and thus a war begins between the two women. How much do you sacrifice for popularity?

In this film, it's everything. And boy, it gets unsettling at the end. In fact, this whole film is a skin crawling foray into the insane. Every slurp, rip, drip and tear can be felt. Kudos for the sound team for putting this disgusting sound design to life. Never have I been more queasy by a film's sound design. If I have to describe it to anyone, I call it a David Cronenberg body horror film mixed with Showgirls, Barbie and techno music. Watch it if you dare.

reviews.author: henry8-3
reviews.body:
Demi Moore plays Elizabeth Sparkle, a stunning beauty in her day and still putting out a popular keep fit video each week. Over the top, effete producer Dennis Quaid tells her that her time is up and he needs to replace her with someone younger. After a car accident, Elizabeth discovers something called The Substance which when taken will reproduce you but in a better/ younger form. She takes the drug and creates the gorgeous Sue (Margaret Qualley) who takes on the top role at Quaid's studios. Elizabeth (and by definition, Sue) are reminded they must swap bodies back every seven days as they are still really just one person - Sue though starts to yearn for more.

Extraordinary, unforgettable body horror story featuring a great performance by Qualley and a quite staggering performance by Moore - surely she'll get awards for this. It is not though your typical movie - lots of clever, tricky photography, much in close up and the film pelts along at a hundred mph. There is humour and many clear messages about the obsession with tv, youth and beauty, but the big thing here though is the blood and goo. Make no mistake there are gallons of both and many numerous, visceral woundings all leading to an unbelievable last half hour that love or hate you won't forget in a hurry. If you like body horror a la David Cronenberg, The Thing etc you'll probably enjoy this, otherwise I'd steer clear.

reviews.author: justahunch-70549
reviews.body: A strange and unusual film, part drama, part horror, a little comedy with messages about vanity, Hollywood's obsession with beauty and simply being able to face the fact that we will all get old and appreciate what you've got when you have it because youth and beauty do now last no matter how hard one tries and no one tries harder for that than the Demi Moore character in this grisly and astonishingly bloody film with outstanding visual and makeup effects. I've never thought of Moore as being anything other than an adequate actress, but to say that this is her finest performance would be a massive understatement. She may very well get an Oscar nomination for this. Margaret Qualley as Moore's alter ego Is also very good and Dennis Quaid in an over the top role gives an appropriate over the top goonish performance who might seem more at home in a Terry Gilliam movie. This was mighty hypnotic, and certainly interesting, but it's for special audiences only. While it is essentially a horror film, it's not one created for scares. It's more a thinking person's type of horror film, but no matter, it is gruesome and mean. It's terrific filmmaking, some of it eye-popping, some of it quite unique, some of it truly disgusting.

reviews.author: mluinstra
reviews.body:
Greetings from the other side.

I had no idea what to expect from this movie, other then seeing Demi Moore's name. It didn't take long before I was totally sucked in.

This movie was something different, and it was so good, at least until then end. With so many prequels, sequels, and reboots, it was nice to see something new. It had elements of other stories, but the idea here was new, and entertaining.

Demi Moore did an excellent job here, making her character real. We empathize with her character.

Now, the downside is, as I mentioned, the last half hour or so. They had a great idea, but went too far with it. I can't understand why they chose to end it this way, but it was a bad decision. As others have pointed out, it went bad, then stupid at the very end.

Anyways, this is still a good movie. I highly recommend watching it. However, I think you will agree (as most do) that they should have done the ending differently. It could have been even better if they did.

reviews.author: nixy-caos
reviews.body:
The movie starts with a solid premise and develops well up until about two-thirds of the way through. Then things take a sharp turn in an absolutely unbelievable and chaotic way. It becomes incredibly bizarre and repulsive. Just bizarre and disgusting. They deliberately ruined a good story. It truly seems like the idea is to mock the audience and test how much absurdity they can endure.

To me, the message is very clear: movie producers can ridicule the audience and still make money and win awards.

I really think that writers in the movie industry want to prove that AI can't replace them, and ironically, this movie serves as strong, irrefutable evidence of that.

reviews.author: nievesl-02510
reviews.body:
Having heard the hype surrounding this film, I was excited to check it out. Thankfully, it not only delivered on my high expectations, it proved to become a favorite of the year.

Demi Moore really gives it her all in this unconventional film that understands when to be gross and is smart enough to be in on the joke of its absurd concept. The practical effects are worthy of awe and gave me hints of The Thing (1982) and Society (1989).

The entire film is beautifully staged and carries a dreamy, hazy quality that allows you to enter the logic of this world. Is it the most subtle satire on aging and beauty standards? Not by a long shot, but it is certainly one of the most engaging and entertaining.

reviews.author: Coventry
reviews.body:
For those also old enough to remember... I recall, in 1996, one of the most hyped and anticipated films of the year was "Striptease", and this for the sole reason that Demi Moore had a couple of topless scenes. She was in her early thirties and at the absolute peak of her beauty and career. In 2024, for "The Substance", Demi Moore does numerous full and very explicit nude sequences at the age of 61 (!) and after a long & difficult time in her life/career. Why am I writing this? Simply to emphasize what a phenomenally courageous and unique performance she gives here. Endless respect.

Demi Moore isn't the only (woman) who deserves praise, though. Margaret Qualley is extraordinary as well, and what to say of writer/director Coralie Fargeat? Practically out of nowhere (*), she comes up with the greatest and most astounding accomplishment in body-horror of the past 30-35 years! Infamous directors in this domain, like David Cronenberg or Frank Hennenlotter can only be jealous of "The Substance". I realize that's quite a statement to make, but it's pure truth.

It would be a shame to describe the plot too much in detail, but since it's so good and relevant I do want to reveal a little bit. Faced with the painful reality that women over fifty aren't welcome in the film & television industry, Elisabeth Sparkle sees her TV-fitness show cancelled because her sleazy producer wants someone fresh and younger. She stumbles upon an innovative but clandestine and highly secretive treatment. For seven consecutive days Elisabeth transforms into Sue, a ravishing younger version of herself, and builds out a successful new career. The next seven days, though, Elisabeth must recover and stabilize in her "old" body. It works amazingly, but there are strict set of rules to follow, and the most important one is balance, balance, balance...

"The Substance" is an all-round fascinating experience. The script is full of strong messages and biting satire, but Fargeat brings it imaginatively and doesn't shove any morals down our throats. Hollywood discriminates ageing women. TV-studios are still run by white & perverted elderly males. Strong women should support each other but don't. Popularity doesn't depend on talent but on looks and the willingness to show bare flesh. Etc. By the way, with all the nudity and numerous close-up of female bottoms in this movie, it simply had to be directed by a women. It's unthinkable that a male director could have made "The Substance" today! Apart from great story and stellar performances, the film also excels in the depiction of shocking images (the transformations) and outrageous gore. The final act, in particular, is something you won't easily recover from.

(*) Fargeat did direct the Rape & Revenge thriller "Revenge" in 2017. Haven't seen that one yet, but I heard and read great things about it as well.

reviews.author: Tom_Hofman
reviews.body:
The Substance is a visually captivating film with strong cinematography and impressive performances, especially from the two female leads. Their acting is believable and conveys deep emotions like relief and shame, adding beautiful layers to their characters. The female perspective is central to the story and will resonate with many female viewers, though I don't know for certain if it was an intentional choice to focus primarily on a female viewpoint.

However, the portrayal of the male character felt unbalanced. Although a "kind man" role was briefly introduced, it wasn't developed enough to add real depth. This left the overall representation of men feeling somewhat negative, even veering into a one-sided portrayal that came across as sexist and unpleasant. A more nuanced portrayal-balancing both the positive and negative aspects of the male character-could have added more depth and drama to the storylines of the female characters as well.

The film's pacing was also a mixed experience. Several times, it felt like the story was wrapping up, but it continued, which slightly diminished my engagement. The final scene, especially with the level of gore, felt excessive to me, and I even considered walking out at that point.

The music choices were intriguing but didn't quite reach their full potential. A stronger musical score could have amplified the emotional impact further.

All in all, The Substance is a bold film with strong female performances but would have benefited from a more balanced portrayal of its male character and tighter direction to create a more cohesive and impactful experience.

reviews.author: guillermo0552
reviews.body: The Substance is a raw and unsettling dive into the beauty standards of the TV industry. It exposes the toxic obsession with perfection and youth, capturing the dehumanizing pressures placed on women. The film's surreal elements and eerie atmosphere amplify the disturbing reality behind the glamorous façade. Performances are haunting, and the narrative, while often uncomfortable, forces viewers to confront the industry's dark underbelly. It's not an easy watch but serves as a powerful critique of how media shapes and distorts self-image. A bold, thought-provoking portrayal of the price of "perfection."

reviews.author: LegioXEquestris
reviews.body:
I'm writing this about 20 minutes before the end because I need a break. Like honestly I feel queasy and mentally exhausted. There is just so much to take in.

First the easy stuff. It turns out that Demi Moore can act. Like really act. She deserves every award she is eligible for in this. The make up person/team also did such a good job that I didn't think "oh look at that make up". Apart from the very beginning.

Demi Moore was authentic and gave something to the film showing her real body. Don't think for one second that the nudity in this is anyway sexual or erotic. Yes you get to see vaginas but you probably wish you didn't.

But the young boobs for. Margaret Qualley look fake and are fake and the bottom half of her is added to her real top half with extremely poor VFX. Given the nature of the film (it is entirely about women's desire for a younger body) it is galling that Demi did nude but not Margaret.

That said you will care for all of 5 minutes.

The outcome is obvious but so well directed and paced you can't stop looking. It doesn't get ten stars because I wanted to see what a person would do if they can be someone else gorgeous? Sex would be most obvious but with who? Why? Revenge? Fantasy? Etc.

OK just finished it. I need to lay down in a dark room for a bit and drink some Alka Seltzer. Good lord but wow.

Watch it but prepare.

reviews.author: joemosesleggett
reviews.body:
A surreal, satirical, dark comedy, body horror with a strong sense of duality. Gorgeous yet repulsive. I felt uncomfortable for the entire runtime but couldn't look away. The film is deep in theme but not subtle in the slightest. Genuinely disturbing yet absurd enough to be fun. Hyper sexual but somehow never inappropriate (for the protagonist exploits herself). Poetically book-ended but with many unpredictable developments along the way.

For me Infested is the scariest horror film to be released this year, but The Substance, so far, is the all round best. It's original, striking, visceral and perfectly acted by the whole cast. I lost count of how often the body horror made me flinch. Films like this and Godzilla: Minus One (which is basically the original but better in every way) are why I love going to the cinema.

Fans of Starry Eyes (2014), The Neon Demon (2016) and anything by Brandon Cronenberg need to watch this movie.

reviews.author: digraphic
reviews.body:
The movie is an absurd body-horror which ironically contradicts the message that it might be sharing.

That being said, a very fresh and unique movie that offers more of gross. The movie pulls out slowly and we get to know the protagonist. Demi Moore is amazing with the role.

I would have given it more rating but the ending was chaotic and I didn't understood the bigger meaning even if there was. Adding a new layer of the character was clumsy for me and I didn't get to understand that last bit. I would have liked something either-or related to just the 2 versions of the protagonist. Otherwise would have been maybe an 8 for me.

reviews.author: elenkhachatryan-16354
reviews.body: The idea of the movie in general is awesome. The acting cast is chosen very good. The visuals just wow i almost threw up on one of the scenes lol. Most of the movie is very interesting to watch. The way movie talks about toxic relationships with yourself and your body, and the way society treats you just because you are beautiful is something that most of us experience in our lives. Even though the movie itself is great i would not say the same about the ending. It was quite disappointing. For me it was kind of out of pocket. It felt like the producing team worked really hard on most of the movie and was like "well that's enough work". If the ending was a bit different i would probably give the movie 10 stars.

reviews.author: jamgood-842-448084
reviews.body:
I was actually really quite surprised by this little horror flick. I knew nothing about it, read the synopsis, saw that it had Demi Moore in it and thought I'd give it a go. She's not the greatest actress in the world but the idea of the story sold it to me. I'm glad I gave it a go.....what a great film.

The acting is solid all round, Demi and Margaret Qualley played their roles so well as did all the other supporting cast. The story line was very good and keeps your interest considering the 2 hour plus time.

The use of practical effects over CGI is also a massive bonus. This felt like watching an old school 80s movie rather than a lot of the modern rubbish we get nowadays.

Give it a go if you don't mind a little body shocker horror. Even if you really don't like that kind of thing, it's still a great movie to watch.

reviews.author: emdee40022
reviews.body: The first 75% of this movie was so good. Did a great job of demonstrating how image and beauty is viewed in society and what people will go through to keep up their image. The first chunk of the movie was entertaining and fun while at the same time accurately touching on how we view image and beauty in this time of social media and everybody trying to put on a front for the camera. I absolutely loved the first 75% of this movie. Problem is, the last chunk of the movie went from a clever and intelligent flick to a disgusting gore fest. I understand that they were trying to really "push home" the point of what people will do to stay attractive in the public's eye, but they went way over the top. To the point where people had to look away. Blood. Guts. Puss. Vomit. Give me a break. You could have made your same points without going that route. I understand that plenty of gore fest movies do exist, but this was a really good movie without taking that route. It was intelligent and smart. And then in the last 25% they just turned it into junk. I was so ready to text friends and family saying, "you all have to watch this movie" because I truly enjoyed the first part of it that much. It's almost like a brand new writer came in for the last 30-45 minutes though. All of that being said, it was still overall pretty good, but I was so ready to give this an 8.5 or 9 an hour and a half into it, only to drop it to a low end 7 with how it ended. Not that the point or theme of the movie changed, but how they just turned it into a disgusting over the top gore fest - that was truly not needed to make the point.

reviews.author: dcoke25
reviews.body:
I wants to be campy and absurdist but also pretentious and intelligent. Fails at both. The message is cliched, "gags" go on for way too long like a Family Guy bit, acting is terrible.

The idea of a "Better" you has been done to death, now that "Better" you doesn't want to just be a stop gap, but be the main you. HOW WACKY, it was novel when Twilight Zone played with this concept back in the 60s, now it's hack. This movie could have worked if it went for CULT status, you can tell the director is a MASSIVE FAN of Brian De Palma, Brian Yuzna, David Cronenberg and so on. She just doesn't understand why their stuff is a cult classic and this will fade into obscurity.

It needs that hyperbole, found in movies like "THE STUFF" or Star Ship Troopers. YOU KNOW the CAMP.

The thing that's the most shocking is the acting is terrible in this. It wants to be over the top and campy like a Jeff Goldblum but just goes more the John K route being more crass and loud. Which is ironic, since it's loaded with names, and I think that's the problem. These are names you know and know they can act, but the problem is they're classical actors with realistically very little range, and this movie falls outside of their range. Dennis needed to be replaced by his brother Randy, Moore needed to be replaced by... man, I don't know...

This was a dud of a movie, as I've said, I've seen it done so many times. OH NO THE CLONE GETS TOO FULL OF THEMSELVES, what a novel trope... This would have been a great Black Mirror episode since it's perfectly shallow and ironically just as SUBSTANCE-LESS as one of those terrible dollar tree wanna be Twilight Zone Episodes. This ain't made for intellects, this is a Millennial movie through and through, and it shows. Very decent shot composition, one annoying song they play ad nauseam, over and over again. Form without a function, the movie. Though, lots of nudity, kind of unnecessarily so. Made sense in the beginning, just gets gratuitous and since it's not campy nudity a la a bikini bimbo beach babe Andy Sidaris film. So close but not quite, the movie. PASS.

reviews.author: toyosibee
reviews.body: This film is unsubtle, yet dense with meaning for various interpretations. GORGEOUS cinematography, skin-crawling sound design, incredible performances (Demi Moore should be nominated for every possible award), wicked and unique humor, stunningly gross body horror effects-The Substance (2024) has it all! Only thing making this a 9/10 instead of a 10/10 is that I wish there was one other female character, maybe a friend of Elisabeth's who shows the aspect of women perpetuating harmful patriarchal expectations of other women (with or without meaning to). That being said, this is (to ME) a perfect film that I will be rewatching over and over until I can quote it.

reviews.author: TomTalksFilms
reviews.body:
By now you've probably heard about this years surprise success or if not you've in no doubt heard about this films shock value.

The Substance follows ageing film star Elizabeth Sparkle (Demi Moore). In her younger years she was an award winning actor who has now been reduced to making workout videos. She becomes aware of a new substance on effectively the black market that allows the user to become a younger version of themselves for 7 days at a time. In her desperation to change her current career circumstances she decides to go ahead with this treatment only for things to quickly get out of hand.

Right from the off something that was apparent to me was this characters deep depression to no longer be her current self. Everything about how she becomes aware of the substance to how she obtains it screams major red flag. Despite this she goes ahead with the treatment with fairly little resistance.

Most drug users are using to escape reality and yet Elizabeth is actually desperate to conform to the societal standards of what is and isn't attractive. Yet at the same time she's also escaping the realities of ageing rather than adapting to her current self. That's the big point this film is trying to make that actually ageing is a natural part of life and that any attempt to interfere with natures course will have consequences.

When she first transitions into her younger self there's a particularly poignant scene that may just be my favourite of the whole film. Before transitioning Elizabeth stands in the mirror in her bathroom and examines herself completely naked. The camera focuses on the parts that women often come to dislike about themselves as they grow older, The cellulite, the sagging bum etc. We then get the same sequence but once she's become her younger self and for me this scene really hit home just how much someone could grow to hate their own body. It's not often we see non-sexual female nudity and this film should be commended for being brave and giving us such a powerful scene.

In the second half of the film however the adulation Elizabeth initially feels about her new younger self quickly begins to dissipate. Then the film moved into body horror and with some to be fair really gnarly scenes but they didn't really add anything to the conversation around embracing your body as you get older. I love a good gory horror film but for me the second half of this film felt a bit out of place. I didn't feel it needed to go so over the top just for seemingly the sake of it.

As the film went on I also found the incessant use of shakey cam became headache inducing. By the time I left the screening and went out from the dark auditorium into the brightly lit corridor my head was absolutely banging. Perhaps this was an intentional part of the experience of watching this film however it's put me off wanting to watch it again.

In conclusion, The Substance is a horror film with a big point to make only it doesn't always quite get the balance right between making that point and it's over the top body horror elements. It's backed up with some really strong acting performances but isn't one I'd be revisiting in a hurry.

I'm off for a lie down.

reviews.author: FlickyM
reviews.body:
Wow!!!! What an absolutely incredible movie yet terrifying, horrifying and funny all once..

I did not know this was a horror movie but even if I had, I still don't think I could have been prepared for what I saw.

I thought it was meant to be a clever portrayal of the social stigma around women aging, which it was in fairness but what started out on that note descended into the most chaos I've seen in a movie in a very long time.

I got vibes of Peter Jackson's early works, Requiem for a Dream, Carrie... all rolled into one.

This movie is not for the faint hearted! I actually nearly threw up at one scene, something that a movie has never triggered in me before. I also spent a lot of time peering between my fingers then covering my eyes but even the sounds in some scenes, without looking, had the hairs on the back of my neck standing up. The end is gross but also hilarious - it's just the wildest ride of a movie and even though I was extremely stressed watching it and shook afterwards, I still loved it, how is that even possible...

Coralie Fargeat is truly an enigma of a writer / director. The cinematography, the wardrobe, production the whole thing was just mind blowing.

Hats off to Demi Moore, this role can't have been easy but she nailed it!!!

reviews.author: JasonHMA
reviews.body:
Very difficult movie to rate. I knew so much about the plot coming in and wanted to love it all the way through. Let's start with the fact that you must suspend reality of course. Would an even desperate Elizabeth take this substance she procures from a dark alley with nothing but a stranger's handwritten note as her research? Eh... forget about it. No need to get bogged down there. After seeing Dennis Quaid channeling his inner harvey weinstein, we want our heroes to see how disgusting he is and run away, but we only have a movie when one tries to placate this despicable creature and his minions. We know why she's doing it, we know she'll get hooked, we know things will go wrong, and we know they will go wrong horribly. Is the other self really just her, just high on youth and beauty? So much so that she forgets she can't eliminate her older self? It becomes hard to tell as the separate personalities start to play against one another, not realizing it's all an act of self-sabotage. There are rules for a reason. After leaving I was certain the movie was too long and the failure was certainly in a comically absurd final act (yes, absurd even in this reality) Could that "performance" have been just hallucination? The characters dreams were more disturbing and real as the movie progressed. Not sure.

Anyway, I just feel bad for Fred.

reviews.author: ruigomesit
reviews.body:
Honestly, I saw the reviews, noticed a 7.9 rating, and thought maybe there was some hope for this disaster of a movie. How wrong I was. It starts out passable, but from there, everything falls apart in the most mind-numbing way imaginable. If I could give it a 0, I absolutely would, no hesitation.

The plot is a chaotic mess, full of absurd decisions that make zero sense. What were the writers even thinking? It's as if they threw logic out the window and hoped no one would notice. The only explanation for this film getting a theatrical release is the cast; it certainly isn't because of the writing, directing, or anything else worth praising. This movie is an insult to anyone who dares to watch it. Avoid at all costs. You've been warned.

reviews.author: chntnsngh
reviews.body: A must watch SCI FI dark blender. The Substance (2024), directed by Coralie Fargeat, is a provocative and visceral exploration of society's obsession with youth and beauty. Starring Demi Moore and Margaret Qualley, this body horror film delves into the dark side of celebrity culture, following a fading star who turns to a black-market drug that promises to rejuvenate her. The film's graphic and grotesque imagery underscores its critique of impossible beauty standards, with standout performances from Moore and Qualley, and a disturbing yet artistic style that keeps viewers captivated through its horrors.

reviews.author: Anotherfilmfan
reviews.body:
Only films that I really feel strongly about do I think I'll write a review for. Nor for kudos, not for likes, I quite frankly don't care what for, I just want to get my thoughts down as soon I've seen something that makes me feel a certain way.

First and foremost, Demi Moore I thought was INCREDIBLE. I've missed her and hope, if anything, this brings her some more limelight, more great reviews, more films and hopefully some award nominations. She's great. Really brutally raw, and while the first half showcases her talent as an actress, the second half shows her ability to be grotesque and not shy with anything. I loved her in this.

Margaret is just as sublime, and deserves the praise (from those that are not easily offended) and like Demi, is not shy and bares all. Literally.

I love horror, and this doesn't feel like a typical horror as it's not scary, no jump scares, no sense of dread, just pure visceral grossness. It's by far the most grotesque thing I've watched. It reminded me of high society and the thing, but beautifully shot with such stunning set ups, I was annoyed many times I looked away. It's literally everything you will have heard. We did have walkouts, but stick with it.

Go in open minded and with a strong stomach. You'll need it.

Why 9 stars? It was twenty mins too long.

reviews.author: shdwfthsun
reviews.body:
For those on the fence, let me help you decide whether The Substance is right for you. If you are here for the body horror, there is ton of that and you will not be disappointed. Give The Substance a watch if that is all you care about. There are some very creative practical effects I have never seen before in this movie and it is all top-notch, vomit-worthy stuff. On the other hand, if you want a tightly written, intelligent allegory, you will be disappointed.

There are interesting ideas here about the entertainment industry and aging, but little else. If The Substance was truly hoping to be feminist, it missed the mark by a mile because the moralistic tone and extremely basic engagement with the subject matter it raises turns this movie into the horror equivalent of Barbie-all flash and no substance.

My biggest problem with The Substance is the treatment of its protagonist. While I cared about her in the beginning, she is portrayed as unworthy of that empathy by the midpoint. But by then, my trust in the filmmaker's vision was already lost because of the obsessive close-ups on female anatomy.

Look, I get it! You want the viewer to be grossed out by shoving porn in our face because that is supposed to make the ending more of a middle finger to objectification. However, the disgusting men who control her life are never made the butt of the joke. The joke is on our poor protagonist the entire time for ever wanting to be loved in the first place. What an idiot, right? But maybe I was an idiot for expecting more.

In conclusion, don't believe the hype. The Substance is made for horror fans only. There is no deep message, only spectacle. Demi deserved more.

reviews.author: joacoCritico
reviews.body: I have already watched this movie and it was incredible in every sense. I was tired of watching horror movies which were sequels, remakes or generic. So,I decided to give this film a try and I was amazing. Demi Moore and Sarah Margaret's performances were surprising and I liked every aspect of their characters. The photograph and scenarios were creative and spectacular with incredible music bands. I believe that the only things that I didn't like were Sue's scenes because they were too much long and a bit repetitive. I don't understand why some people say that the ending is bad when in reality, it was the best part of the movie. If you want to surprise and disturb yourself, this is the perfect movie.

reviews.author: TaylorYee94
reviews.body:
The message is loud and clear. Society is excessively obsessed with women's body image and is very harsh on women aging. Even so, the most important thing is that YOU love yourself and be gentle with yourself. YOU do not have to give in, and YOU can even choose to fight. Elisabeth was the one who locked herself in that apartment. Also, 'The Substance' portrays 'male gaze' more accurately than any other films. That nuance, atmosphere, background story.. That indescribable feeling that he's looking down without saying anything with a hint of sexual connotation. Dennis Quaid depicts men in the entertainment industry meticulously: language, contents they speak (mostly commercialization of sex), attitude, and manners.

Cinematography is awesome. Color, image, composition of screen, and editing. They are trendy and hip but not shallow. Elisabeth's blue and yellow and Sue's pink contrast each other. Just by color. I've never felt all sorts of 'the substances' this clear and tangible. Especially the texture, the sound, and the close-ups of food and flesh stimulate all kinds of senses while watching a film. A fresh cinematic experience.

I loved two thirds of the movie, but I did not like the Monstro Elisasue part. Before Elisasue, I can tell the director cared for every detail of the movie, every step of the way. However, at some point, she just let go of that delicate and detailed process. Some might say it's cathartic, but it is not my cup of tea.

reviews.author: marlenerehlers
reviews.body:
I kept seeing ads and promo content for The Substance on TikTok, and one bored day, I decided to give it a shot. From the very first scene, this movie reeled me in. It's an incredible mix of eerie, strange, dirty, funny, and downright captivating moments. The story was well-crafted and full of surprises, keeping me on the edge of my seat throughout.

The acting was top-notch, and the characters felt real in the most unsettling yet entertaining way. Just when I thought I had it figured out, the final act completely blew me away-it was unexpected and so satisfying.

I've been telling everyone about this movie because I simply can't stop thinking about it. It's genuinely one of the best films I've seen in a long time. If you're in the mood for something different, this one's a must-watch!

reviews.author: mungflesh
reviews.body:
The Substance allows an aging fitness icon to recapture her glory days - with a sinister caveat.

I don't like the subject matter very much. Actors and actresses are only under pressure to look good as they age because there are so many other, younger actors and actresses wanting the same thing that they have. It's not the industry that demands perfection, it's just young people also wanting a chance too. This happens in many professions. Athletes have it far worse than the beauty industry.

That being said, this film is otherwise really good, at least until the final act. I thought the whole premise of the way The Substance works was very original and executed brilliantly, both visually and story wise, like a Cronenberg take on the Cinderella story.

I think the decision to be a bit too comical in the last third didn't work for me but the rest of the FrightFest crowd loved it. It got a bit too silly and over the top for my liking, trying to be as gross-out as it could but for me was daft and started to drag on a bit.

I much preferred the 2014 movie Starry Eyes, which is less satirical and a lot darker, at least on the surface.

I've no doubt this film is going to be a huge hit. I love the fact that it will look like a mainstream movie to many and what they'll experience will be quite unexpected.

reviews.author: jgcorrea
reviews.body: Suppose the worst David Lynch and the best (which always means of course worst) Andy Warhol made a movie together. Imagine a pathetic blast!... Demi Moore, 61, splits into her younger doppelganger in this excessive body horror that weaponizes male gaze and body standards into an Over The Top gonzo comedy satire before a jaw-droppingly gory "holy latrine!" finale. I can confidently say that I have been horrified eye to eye & ear to ear during the last 20 minutes of the movie... Actually during the last 1h20min ... It's a pathetic ride, please do not eat either before or during watching it. Demi runs around looking like Spike Jonze in a Jackass Bad Grandpa skit. I cannot approve how gross it gets. I cannot applaud Dennis Quaid for releasing his chicken-comics in an extremely impure style of farce, even though admktting that he remained the less slimy thing in this movie. Scaroused is a word I would use to describe this film. The final act is among the wildest trash we've ever seen. It is indeed a ¨modern fable¨ that's as subtle as a nuke, as grandly screwed as anything ever put on screen. The Substance is a ride you only see once (like for instance Requiem for a Dream.) Demi Jeckyll and Margaret Hyde - i.e. Both halves of the main character - make the sexy portions as grotesque as in David Cronenberg's undertakings. Director Fargeat hasn't so far touched the so-called Seventh art.

reviews.author: georgebandofbros
reviews.body:
The movie rides on the perceived beauty notions expected in show business. An aging movie celebrity decides to get herself replicated and her youth regenerated. It starts out being very cosmetic in treatment but is really a mind-bender and makes you think. Demi Moore deserves an Oscar for her acting, if not for the display of her cellulite. It's assuaging to watch a movie being carried solely on the prowess of their female actresses and director.

Every department stands out in this movie. The herculean make-up dept, slick and snippy editing , avid cinematography and even, the eclectic electronic background music scores all come together to deliver a thought-provoking story on experimenting with our DNA in the pursuit of aging gracefully.

The scriptwriter does offer some genius strokes like the replicant drawing spinal fluid from the original host for survival. The science behind the replicant and regenerative process is hogwash and far-fetched but the story does pique your senses and intellect.

reviews.author: tubosun97
reviews.body:
You will know very early if you like this movie. If you make it past the first hour, and you're still invested - you'll probably end up enjoying this movie. The thing is there is so many great things about this movie and they severely outweigh the weaknesses.

The good: It's a reminder about self-love. Appreciating your imperfections and embracing that you are not perfect. Additionally, Demi Moore pulls out the performance of her career to show how even the most beautiful among us feel insecurity and fading beauty.

Telling the story in an extremely visceral tone. Loud, abrasive, in your face and unapologetic. Stylish as well.

The bad: The ending does drag, well after the story has wrapped. I felt like the last 10 minutes was insanely self-indulgent and probably could've been cut.

Overall, I was disturbed but entertained. I can never forget this movie and I never want to see it again. If you like it, you probably can't recommend it to anyone in public and if you hate it then I do feel bad for you because this movie will definitely be polarizing.

9/10.

reviews.author: bryan_baz
reviews.body:
I tried not to read up on this movie as much as I could before watching it which I think added to my shock throughout watching.

There are so many layers to this film, layers of beauty, campness, confrontation, hopefulness, sadness, loneliness and some completely grotesque.

The journey throws you back and forth and constantly keeps you on the edge of your seat until the final scene.

The final scene captures each and everyone of those layers all at once which I found absolutely genius.

I wouldn't be surprised if this film gets some oscar nods, particularly for it's unique way of story telling. The acting by Demi, Margaret and Dennis was superb.

I wouldn't usually give such a high score of 9, but this film is absolutely amazing in every element - acting, cinematography, music and script. It will keep you thinking about it for days after.

reviews.author: zsguerreiro
reviews.body:
I went to this with high expectations, lots of raving reviews, praise. Started watching and I think we are onto something here. It's mysterious, kinky and different.

Got to the middle of it and thought "you know what this is actually good, has a bit of a Twilight zone feel to it"..so far so good.

Then comes the 3rd act and is just to gory and absurd. It's a shame really, the girls put up a really good perfomance, I like the way its filmed, the film's soundtrack is quite good and well executed but I think they overkilled it in the end, it goes from kinky and mysterious to bananas in a blink of an eye. Its a 6 out of 10.

reviews.author: yoshimasu_k
reviews.body:
WHAT DID I JUST WATCH (LOL) 😳

Kidding aside, The Substance is an over-the-top body horror with fantastic performances from Demi Moore and Margaret Qualley!

As advertised, it's a scathing look at the entertainment industry's objectification, oversexualization, and ageism against women.

If the thought of commentary repulses you (AS IF the horror genre has NEVER been a platform to explore social and political issues and everything now is just pushing THE WOKE AGENDA 😑), you don't have to worry too much because director Coralie Fargeat pushes everything to its entertaining, stylistic, and gruesome extremes - Cronenberg and Tsukamoto would be proud!

I feel like the message sometimes does get muddled by the visual extremes, whether that be the hypersexualization of Qualley's character or the physical and psychological effects of The Substance itself.

The movie is of course not without its flaws, but director Fargeat should be commended for testing boundaries and taking huge creative swings all the way to the final shot.

reviews.author: reesecup101-422-756195
reviews.body:
Unsettling from start to finish. Nothing can prepare you for what you are about to watch. It does a great job of slowly easing you into the gore with close up scenes of things that make you mildly uncomfortable. Superb work from Demi Moore and Dennis Quaid. I've never seen him in a role like this and he really nails it.

If you love body horror, this is your jam. I haven't seen something that makes me squirm quite like this since Green Inferno. And I would rate this 10x worse than that. The close up shots are what really makes it.

Overall, it's a compelling film. I have never seen anything like it.

reviews.author: salemzin
reviews.body:
Very similar to David Cronenberg's works from the 80s, "The Substance" (2024) presents a striking and well-executed body horror, making it a strong contender for the title of "best horror film of 2024".

The production stands out for its creative and original approach, exploring themes such as the human desire to shape nature and oneself, as well as criticizing how women are sold and discarded as products by large industries. The body horror scenes, which provoke repulsion and agony, are impeccably realized, with makeup and practical effects that deserve praise. The detailed work raises the level of the film, delivering visually disturbing and impactful moments. The phenomenal performances of Demi Moore and Margaret Qualley are essential to the success of the work, being strong candidates for Oscar nominations in 2024. However, despite its many positive points, the script, which initially impresses with its psychological horror, loses a little of strength in the third act, which, although frantic and exaggerated, does not maintain the same level of engagement.

Coralie Farjeat, director of "The Substance", reveals a remarkable talent in directing this film, especially considering her short filmography. With this work, she highlights her career and raises great expectations for her future projects in the coming years.

reviews.author: laurenriding
reviews.body: Even from the first shot I knew the film was going to take me on a ride. And it sure accomplished that. It achieved it's screenplay award for a reason, however I did not vote it 10/10 simply due to some scenes near the end being perhaps less symbolic than others. In more of a sense as they were genuinely confusing from the plot and less open to interpretation. But nevertheless, the film is pure art and is definitley open to interpretation throughout (I know I certainly did). The music, the weirdness of it all is exactly what cinematography should be about just getting lost inside this weird world that actually represents a vast majority of our world today. You can really tell the producer had fun with this film and the blood bath scene was a total buzz to watch. I genuinley applauded and was left entirely satisfied with the film when the shot at the end conveyed how no matter how we look, earn or are respected in life we all get wiped away at the end into thin air. Bravo.

reviews.author: bingelytegoda
reviews.body:
First I'd like to point out, that I'm not the biggest fan of gore, as in, I see it more as something usually gross and unnecessary in most horror movies, but this movie exceeded my expectation.

The movie itself points out quite a few problems with today's society, especially pretty privilege and the huge fear of getting old and unwanted. The main character - Elizabeth Sparkles or "Sue" - shows us how easy it is to get lost in all the fame and love you receive from others that, once it's all gone - it's like your life is meaningless.

I don't want to get into too many details as not to spoil it, but it's definitely worth the watch, and isn't your run-of-the-mill gory mass-murder, but a well thought out movie with actually shock inducing gore scenes.

reviews.author: kkstewart-51912
reviews.body: The ending ruined it for me. I was hooked throughout the whole movie, even tho there were some holes throughout that made me question how or why certain things were happening. I think the ending could've went numerous ways, but they chose the worst ending. I get the message of beauty standards and media projections, but I believe that it was drawn out and was confusing in the end and most likely didn't make sense to some viewers. I watch a lot of horror and psychological thriller movies, I had high hopes for this one.. and overall I think i'm just disappointed. The cast choosing was perfect, and had so much potential.

reviews.author: nndmnairn
