reviews.body: One of the worst films I have ever seen and I have seen a lot...The film starts with over emphasised yuk...develops into bearable and ends in chaos...Why Demi Moore and Dennis Quaid agreed to this movie is beyond me. Only positive comments I would say is that Demi looks amazing and her acting was ok. The last half hour of the film should never have happened...If you must watch it at the very least don't pay for this movie. The entire movie theatre laughed in bewilderment at the end and many comments were passed afterwards as to how bad it was. I will finish by saying that I hope people don't get their hopes up by the reviews so far like I did.

reviews.author: jared-25331
reviews.body:
This was a movie that I found just by watching the trailers on YouTube and I decided to put it on my watchlist. So now I just got done watching The Substance (2024) and it was amazing.

Positives for The Substance (2024): First off, the practical effects for body horror in this movie is absolutely phenomenal. Similar to any of my other movie reviews on IMDb, I am one of those people who is really not a fan of modern day movies using CGI. I understand that it's cheaper to use, but it also one of those things that I can't stand because you know that what you will see on screen is something that was created by a computer and it sometimes takes me out of the movie. I will always champion people who go the old school route and use practical effects in their movie and that makes me so happy especially given that my second favorite movie is John Carpenter's The Thing (1982). It also goes without saying but both Demi Moore and Margaret Qualley are awesome. Despite the fact that they're suppose to be playing the same character, these two woman manage to make their versions stand out from each other. And finally, the movie did a fantastic job with its social commentary and I can guarantee that a lot of people will relate to it.

Negatives for The Substance (2024): The movie was way too long for the story it was telling. I understand that writer-director Coralie Fargeat wanted to do a deep exploration of the movie's themes and I respect her doing that, there's also a part of me that believe this movie could've gotten its message across with a shorter runtime. Also, the movie's message does get a little bit lost and the movie just becomes a little too bizarre for me.

Overall, The Substance (2024) was a fantastic body-horror movie with phenomenal practical effects and some good social commentary in the mix. While this might not be one of my favorite horror movies of 2024, this is definitely a movie that will stick with me for a long time.

reviews.author: MattyLuke-81663
reviews.body:
The Substance is a sickly and creatively over-the-top body horror flick where everything in this world is heightened to a ridiculous level, but it's incredibly well-made and a fantastic watch.

Its approach to its theme of insecurity and self-hatred that we have with ourselves was a compelling way of portraying it. In some way, it is a unique take on Dorian Gray.

The performances from Demi Moore and Margaret Qualley were superb, especially for Moore, who I'm thrilled to see again on the screen. And this might be the best work from Dennis Quaid I have seen. His character is disgusting and has this forced hyper nature that makes his presence uncomfortable.

I highly recommend watching this movie while eating.

reviews.author: HOLYDIVER575
reviews.body: My goodness what a great movie. The overlapping messages in this film. From the obvious aging gracefully (or not), public acceptance, needing the admiration of others, making a bargain that sounds to good to be true, and young people are irresponsible with any responsibility they are given (🤣🤣🤣🤣🤣). Our culture's need to be beautiful and voluptuous is on display as well. It's the heart of the movie. As well as the Hollywood's out with the old, in with the new mentality. Demi Moore is brave for taking this role. She is fantastic in this film. The ending was 100% over the top but on point and amplified the lunacy of this world. That's all I will say. Dennis Quaid is over the top, campy, and great in the role of TV executive. Purchased it on iTunes. It had a limited run in my local theater. Highly recommended!!

reviews.author: guillermomartingodoy
reviews.body: A feminist film, excellent choice of main conflict where the acceptance of one's own body is combined with gore body horror. Actresses, actors and performances incredible, they achieve the task of transmitting all the emotions to the viewer, a script that takes an unexpected turn in the last 40 min of the film turning it from a reflection of the body of each one to a film undeservedly gore from my point of view, partly losing the seriousness with which it began to narrate the story. From the soundtrack and visual effects of the film I was completely amazed, how well designed and developed everything is, making everything so graphic. The substance achieved its goal, to make me think about the acceptance of the human body and complemented with a completely disgusting gore style, in my opinion it is a good movie and I would recommend it.

reviews.author: tabuno
reviews.body: Demi Moore is back in a big way, literally, back and front. Female director Carolie Fargeat has created a bare, gritty, and raw movie that depicts male obsession with physical beauty that also greatly influences women, especially for popular actresses and female performers. Even with two significant logical flaws involving money and physical conditioning, this movie with its superior cinematography, eerie sound effects, and creepy musical melodies along with a convoluted plot that is a mesmerizing slow burn for the first half of this horrifying and riveting movie requires deliberate and slow reflection for some to comprehend what the director and scriptwriter are trying to accomplish and the stunning message that this movie incorporates. For some this movie is ultimately a crazed grossed out and over the top bloody mess for others however it can be seen as a redemptive acceptance of the inner turmoil that each of us faces in daily life, especially women. Either way, Demi Moore's performance and courage to lay herself all out there is beyond superlative along with the help of her younger self stylishly played by Margaret Qualley who recently also had another off-beat performance in Poor Things (2023) and the completely obnoxiously portrayed Dennis Quaid.

reviews.author: mesaxi
reviews.body:
The Substance is a surprisingly high budget horror comedy that was heavily influenced by the body horror genre of the 80's. But if you are someone who consumes Frank Henenlotter and Brian Yuzna films, this movie will not shock you like it appears to be shocking mainstream audiences.

Demi Moore took a big chance with this role and I think she did a great job. I'm a little surprised they were able to land someone with her clout for this kind of movie, but I feel like some actors are trying to stay far away from the superhero genre and they're not left with much right now. Margaret Qualley did well, but her role wasn't exactly the meatiest. Ironically, she was the pretty young face taking a back seat to the aging actress as far as the overall production goes. The film is done with minimal dialogue, choosing to tell the story through imagery and implication as much as it can.

It starts to get a little dicey around Dennis Quaid's character. Him and the neighbor were done a little too cartoonishly for my tastes. There were a few moments in this movie that I felt tried too hard to get a certain reaction from the viewer. Sometimes less is more, even in something like this. There were also a few inconsistencies, such as one character having trouble standing in one scene and then running like a lunatic a few scenes later. But suspension of disbelief is important in something like this, so nitpicking the snow on the walk of fame is not exactly necessary no matter how much that annoyed you...

Overall it's a fun movie, and I need to stress again it's done with minimal dialogue so it is done very creatively. Don't watch it if you're the squeemish type, but really it is pretty cartoonish which helps you get past some of that.

reviews.author: kerosin666
reviews.body: I can't get this movie out of my head. It was so beautifully shot and directed that I was afraid to blink, in the fear that I'll miss out on something. Even the ugliest moments (and it's full of those) were completely mesmerizing. Without spoiling the story I can just say that to me, personally, it's one of the most important movies made in the last century. It spreads on so many levels and touches so many themes: the beauty industry, Hollywood, youth, self hatred, loneliness, objectification, one's relationship with the world and self and the wish to be loved. It was interesting that all the men in the movie were portrayed as total creeps, but it felt believable. Both actresses did an amazing job and you could easily connect and relate to their characters, understanding their motives and actions. It's a hard movie to watch, often unpleasant but without a doubt - brilliant. The sound was insane. Every shot was just perfect - from the color choices and outfits to the food scenes. I will probably never look at myself in the mirror the same, and I'm grateful for that. A masterpiece in my book.

reviews.author: masonsteven
reviews.body:
I'm under a bit of strain right now, and that may have something to do with this review, but I'd give $100 not to have watched this movie.

The acting is good, if satirically over the top, but this thing is just ugly. It's foul. There's nothing here but bitterness, abject pride and avarice, and an absolute butchering of humanity as a concept.

It's also, perpetually, and frequently extraordinarily graphic, right down to the gut blooming audio effects of slithering flesh, splashing bodily fluids, etc.

It's over the top in its morbid and gross physical part of the result of "the substance" too.

And yes, I get it. It's a commentary on immense vanity, the disgusting nature of Hollywood, pride, greed, and the underbelly of the human condition.

Don't watch this. There's nothing here but bad.

reviews.author: asofdelgado
reviews.body:
Choosing Demi Moore to portray a character who once was an actress and currently suffers from the natural process of aging in the difficult-to-even-breathe entertainment environment is just wild.

Demi acts as Elisabeth, a star who was loved by many and now is getting close to being a no-one, completely forgotten.

When she discovers her career is reaching its final point, she finds a second opportunity to relive what was once her life, a few years ago.

In The Substance you get to see a depressing but also thrilling mix of fear of aging, desperation, anger but also self hatred and this mix is what made me want to stand up and applaud by the end of it.

The end scene left me and my friends thinking for hours. Amazing work.

reviews.author: GrantWTempleton
reviews.body: The Substance contains what is in its title. The film demonstrates the philosophical decay of us as humans and our worth to society as we get older. The twist is that you can now alter that reality. The film is obviously inspired by classics like Scanners, 12 Monkeys, slither, and most importantly Shivers. The body horror is slightly disturbing but nothing a veteran film goer can't handle. This film in terms of likablitiy is about a 6 but with the special effects and set design bumps it up to an 8. Dennis Quaid delivers a long awaited good performance and Demi Moore shines as always. Highly recommend to newer film watchers.

reviews.author: FerdinandoLM
reviews.body:
Grotesque, diving into the pitfalls of progress and the human obsession with perfection. Visually, it's remarkable - its uncanny imagery often leaves you questioning whether you're thrilled or disturbed.

However, while it's bold and at times deeply unsettling, it doesn't quite achieve that elusive "perfectly balanced (as all things should be, cit.)" quality.

The narrative occasionally stumbles, with gaps that detract from its overall impact.

It's thought-provoking but not groundbreaking - a film that's above average, yet just shy of excellence.

And I like to imagine that the director somehow died during the making of the movie and was secretly replaced by Yoshihiro Nishimura.

reviews.author: jack-davy
reviews.body:
There are two films my friend and I have applauded LOUDLY in the cinema when the credits have rolled.

The first was in 2013, and the second was November 2024. The Substance.

Needless to say, we gained momentum pretty quickly and the whole theatre joined in and we're clapping too.

What a film!

Demi Moore deserves all the recognition and whatever awards may come here way for this role.

I relished every scene with her in. And the same for Margarey Qualley.

Admittedly, the ending could have been shorter and less 'OTT' - and had it been, I believe we still would have got the message - but it did not diminish the enjoyment we felt watching that film in the slightest. Such a great analogy about the subject matter of women, celebrity culture, fame and ageing.

I really feel that any of those who don't 'get it' sadly don't possess the mental capacity to look beyond the screen and think more about the meaning.

Take it at face value only, and you won't understand the message.

A true 10/10. Have already watched a second time and will definitely watch a third when it comes to DVD. (Yes, I'm 30 and I'm old school!)

P.s. The soundtrack slaps and the editing is top notch, dahhling.

reviews.author: TheVictoriousV_Listicle_Blurbs
reviews.body:
When I first saw Coralie Fargeat's The Substance, I couldn't have dreamed that this would be the most controversial entry on my list. Surely it is obvious to everyone that this is about as good as it gets in terms of expressive/creative cinematography, set design, makeup, and acting -- even if you aren't as much of an irremediable fan of cartoonish gore as I am?

Alas, after a whole bunch of praise during its theatrical run, the film was met with scorn after it became more widely viewable. (Weird how certain movies get worse reviews when people who watch movies on their laptops instead of watching them in an auditorium start getting access to them. I suspect that's just as much of an issue as popularity making things cool to hate.) The big talking point has been the film's various horror homages, including call-backs to Cronenberg, Kubrick, Hitchcock, Bergman, and even shlock like Basket Case and Braindead, and the question was: Is there really a purpose to them?

I concede that some of them seem mainly aesthetic (even though I've come around on the call-backs to The Shining, which, according to one critic, seem to distill the entertainment industry into a sort of glammy Overlook Hotel with all its accursed "loops"), but why worry when the end result is this colossally gorgeous? As for the complaints about the subtlety and tact of the themes, I'd say those come down to an inability to "meet the film where it is", to quote a mutual on Twitter, instead of imagining what YOU think the film should be. This is a consistently over-the-top, purposely on-the-nose body horror comedy with French Extremist sensibilities; to whine about obvious, in-your-face satire is to complain about cats in Garfield.

A more understandable complaint regards Demi Moore's character; how the film seems to poke fun at those who try to play by the system's rules just as much as the system itself. But to acknowledge that shallow women exist isn't to blame women for the way beauty-obsessed industries operate. It is a film about self-hatred, and it captures self-hatred all too well.

And of course, I would agree that all the swooning and fancamming over the conventionally attractive Margaret Qualley -- instead of her just as monumental co-star Demi Moore -- is a sign that a lot of people missed the point. If you think that's Fargeat's fault and not the morons who missed the point, well, maybe you'll at least want to retract those "it was too obvious" complaints.

reviews.author: billington_daniel
reviews.body:
Demi Moore and Margaret Qually's fantastic performances help to contribute to an engaging story about vanity and selfishness over rationality. The movie followed an aging former-star who was facing imminent career pressures to look young. Due to this and her own vanity, she is desperate and willing to take any measure to look younger. The creative videography and contrast of clinical and vibrant styles make the movie visually compelling and compliment the themes of the movie. It raised fundamental philosophical questions on identity, self-image and obsession.

However, the overly satirical ending greatly detracted from an otherwise thought-provoking movie. Although I don't mind body horror movies, the shift in style at the end felt excessive, unnecessary and a bit silly. Despite this, I still found the movie worth watching due to it's creative and original plot, as well as the great performances.

reviews.author: Rachelle8765
reviews.body:
Overall i Can't say i loved this movie, because it made me feel uncomfortable and not at ease and distressed , which is exactly what it was supposed to do! Pure art.

The movie is not deep, it has a message , ok but nothing more.

But, it was simply a very good movie!

I was engaged and interested and as the movie progressed, i was disgusted more and more until i was left shocked.

It took me a few minutes to contemplate on what i had just watched after the movie was over. That doesn't happen often with movies lately.

I missed this feeling of being fully invested and having lingering feelings after the movie.

The acting was impeccable, Demi Moore was looking better than ever at 60! Margaret Qualley is reallly good as well, I loved her in Maid and this is totally different but she nailed it.

Definitely worth a watch.

reviews.author: mathazo
reviews.body:
The Substance is a film that stands out, not necessarily for being a masterpiece, but for its refreshing take on beauty standards. Unlike Hollywood's typical obsession with unrealistic ideals, this film embraces the natural look of its actresses, which makes the experience far more authentic and relatable.

The performances are strong, particularly from the two lead actresses, but some aspects fall short. The characters' decisions, at times, feel too realistic to the point of being mundane. It's hard to empathize with a character who's spent a lifetime as a millionaire, now struggling in old age due to unemployment. Additionally, it's puzzling why "the substance" is free, and the portrayal of the bosses is overly childish, clashing with the more serious tone. Despite these issues, the film is still worth watching for its unique approach.

reviews.author: p-49514
reviews.body: Too much ass in the first half. Too much gore in the second half. No acting whatsoever. Plot holes all over the place. This is what's wrong with the film industry. Where is the finesse? Just a cheap video with visual and audio stimuli. How do you call this a film? I almost threw up mid-film. The is by far the worst thing I have ever seen in my life. I wish I could un-see it. Utterly disgusting. Uhh. It's been an hour since I walked out and I'm still feeling sick. Absolutely disgusting. I can't find any other word for it. Please avoid this film like the plague. Director must be deranged. It will traumatize you. You have been warned.

reviews.author: NarryBorman
reviews.body:
I grew up in the era of visiting the video shop and hiring horror videos I that was too young to actually watch (by law), which itself added to the thrill of watching the films (not to mention dropping them back in the box after hours).

I am pretty sure I've watched every single (UK Censor determined) "video nasty" that ever got banned.

30-odd years on, when I thought I'd seen everything, this is on a completely different level

From the psychological aspect, to the effects (which are incredibly gruesome) the brilliant film work, and the pace of this film is perfect throughout.

This is definitely amongst the best horror films made to date in my viewing experience; I am still trying to digesting this all (not literally).....

Incredible work! Could this even get an Oscar nomination?

reviews.author: yogeshevolution
reviews.body: The movie like this with pecular concept in horror genre is what horror fans live for. This movie ticks all the boxes of horror with simple but unique storyline and the element of horror which is unique. The movie quite puts on impression. The story is pacy and the movie time is adequate though at the end feels like streched a little bit. Some scenes in the movie are very much gore or may be unwatchable to normal audience . The movie stand out uniquely and will surely be liked by horror fans. The acting is very good but what is more impressive is the concept itself without any jump scares movie gives experience of unique kind of thrill . Really enjoyed it.

reviews.author: Piffritic-Half-arsedproductions
reviews.body: Disturbing, sinister, surreal, absurd, and at times hilarious. The Substance is this generation's modern interpretation of "The Picture of Dorian Grey", but executes in a way, that is relevant, well timed, topical, and weirdly thought-provoking. Honestly, this is a great film for pub banter, offering plenty of shock and awe moments that I'm sure will keep people talking for a while. Among the weirdness however is the cast, everyone is fantastic, but I'm just surprised that a film like this would attract such high-profile actors, I'm rather astounded. Denis Quaid plays a wonderful satirical scumbag, who is appropriately named Harvey, Margret Qualley once again furthers her career by showing she can dance with the best, but all my appreciation goes to Demi Moore who gives the performance of a lifetime - an Oscar Nomination would not be such a bad idea. Furthermore, the movie has an incredible directing style, consistently invading the personal space of its audience, while slapping you across the face with an extreme satirical approach. I wasn't sure whether to contemplate or laugh, it's quite the achievement. Overall, I really enjoyed The Substance, it's not my personal favorite for 2024 but it is definitely the most memorable.

reviews.author: kosmasp
reviews.body:
It's not ... it's you! Or something along those lines - so no pun intended as always. This had quite the festival buzz surrounding it - so the bar was already high. And yet it still passed it. And Demi Moore is so good in this ... she does not even have too many scenes where she can ... shine through ... but they are more than enough.

There is a lot of nudity in this - but I doubt this will be what angers people ... there are a lot of things that will happen in the course of this movie ... crazy things, things that are quite visceral ... also things that are psychological ... Demi Moore getting ready for a date ... rethinking, re-doing her makeup again and again, to name one example ... may feel annoying! But it also feels very real ... so while this is fantastical in nature, it is also grounded in reality! Which is true for Dennis Quaid too ... he is almost comically evil ... but he represents a part of our society ... of the youth mainia/culture.

So some things may almost feel cringe to some ... but I feel the movie is able to hold its own and never drifts too much into any sorts of cliches ... this really goes all the way ... to really achieve anything, you have to be able to shed some skin ... to please others ... smile ... and be young ... and its a vicious cycle ... because it is not just society dropping this on us ... it is what we want ... sounds crazy ... and certainly is exactly that ... as is the movie! And as a last point, which I almost forgot: certain things may be too on the ... nose! But that does not make them less intriguing and amazing (also disgusting - they have to be).

reviews.author: geregertiny
reviews.body: The concepts and issues are actually quite straightforward and simple, yet the process of gradually spiraling out of control is presented in a rather fascinating way. The performances of the two actresses are quite extraordinary. The female characters' bodies are nakedly commodified, gazed upon, and turned into spectacles. Coupled with a large number of close - up shots and the bright, high - saturation environmental colors, it all proclaims the film's exploitative nature and satirical implications. The third act is indeed highly impactful, resembling a Brian Yuzna - style B - movie from the 1980s, provoking the audience both in and out of the screen with even more extreme body horror. The omnipresent discomfort in the first half is finally transformed into a different form of catharsis. There will surely be a lot of controversy, but it's a rare find to see a horror film that can achieve a powerful female expression through such bold genre elements and body - centered narratives.

reviews.author: slyromania
reviews.body: This movie is absolutely amazing, I have been stunned about the messages that can be digested in a million ways. The movie is so minimal, the message is so straightforward, yet it can be really interpreted in so many ways, depending where you are as a human in your level of evoluation. Exceptionally great and utterly simple. I have to say that this surely took a lot of courage from Demi Moore, she was soo perfect in this. Margaret's play was also pristine perfection. I love every character and the whole plot, it was perfect as it was done, I wouldn't change anything, really. It tied me to the screen, I couldn't take my eyes off of it, usually I'm not that captivated by a movie, but this one, oh my God. I don't want to ruin anyone's experience so I won't give any spoilers. This movie is a must watch for everyone. You can read a lot of complaints about the ending, well, I admit, it was really tough but I think that's also in the right place I got shocked and disturbed at the end. This is the perfect movie for self-awarness, I recommend it to everyone. Really, everyone.

reviews.author: t_g1985
reviews.body:
A standout entry in the body horror genre, The Substance delivers an unsettling and unique narrative that lingers long after the credits roll. With strong performances, particularly from its female leads, the film cleverly explores society's obsession with youth and beauty, delving into the extremes some may go to for perfection. Its disturbing plot, driven by addiction and vanity, is as thought-provoking as it is haunting.

Though the climactic final scene leans into over the top theatrics, it doesn't detract from the film's overall impact. The strong acting anchors the story, and with the gruesome the sound and effects, making The Substance a notable watch.

reviews.author: Stevieboy666
reviews.body: When fading TV star Elisabeth Sparkle (Demi Moore) turns 50 she is told by her agent Harvey (brilliantly played by Dennis Quaid) that she's too old and he looks for a new younger star to replace her on a TV aerobics show (which features a lot of groin and bum close ups!). Elisabeth obtains a black market drug called The Substance, not to make her younger but to make a new, younger version of herself (called Sue, played by Margaret Qualley). Sounds confusing but watch it and it all makes sense. I avoided all reviews before going to see this at the cinema last night and I am glad that I did, the incredibly crazy and over the top brilliant finale caught me totally by surprise. Demi Moore was 61 whilst making this movie but looks fantastic, well until things start going wrong that is! Both she and Qualley spend a lot of time naked, which is very nice. They also get to beat the crap out of each other. This film is awesome! It is horrific, shocking, funny, sexy and extremely gory. It is easily one of the best body horror movies ever made, period! The running time clocks in at 141 minutes but I was never once bored, quite the opposite. I absolutely loved The Substance and look forward to its future Blu-ray release.

reviews.author: akermanmax
reviews.body:
I thought this movie was ok to certain extent , both actresses gave good performances in their roles. However, I felt it was missing the background context to the purpose of the film . Who made it? Why make it? What was the sinister purpose and motive to giving people this vial or substance in the first place. The script was average and not that great , didn't highlight any significant emotional performances. Not sure why people think it's Oscar level , definitely not! Way over-hyped!

I felt the story was too confined to her flat , she did go out at times , but these were quick sequences. Trying to flesh out the story. It did change at the end, no it definitely changed up at the end . As it completely lost the plot and went whacky! I did enjoy this scene , but felt quite senseless over the top.

People are saying wow look at the sensations the film gave me! With all the close-up gore . Such an original idea.... Sorry but I have to roll my eyes at this, have those people actually ever seen a horror film or original saw film? Probably not . This is pretty standard theme in majority of horror films. My next question is what genre is this? It doesn't sit in science fiction. And the tone and plot doesn't quite fit into horror either. But It definitely has more horror elements than science fiction. I think it's more of a Dark thriller fantasy genre.

Thanks for reading my review and whoever said this is Oscar winning. I hope you read my review and make your blood boil!!

reviews.author: lee_eisenberg
reviews.body:
I would describe "The Substance" thusly: imagine if David Cronenberg got tired of the obsession with youth, beauty and perfection, so he made a movie about it. Coralie Fargeat's movie about an aging celebrity who takes a serum to be a younger version of herself has elements of "Dr. Jekyll & Mr. Hyde" and "Death Becomes Her", and even some Stanley Kubrick movies. The point (like in "Frankenstein" and "Jurassic Park") is that when you try to alter anything natural, you'd better realize that you can't foresee the results.

All in all, a lovably shocking movie. I'd go so far as to call it Demi Moore's best role ever (this is actually the first movie of hers that I've seen in the theater), with excellent support from Margaret Qualley and Dennis Quaid. I recommend it.

reviews.author: AJ_Nel
reviews.body: "The Substance", deserves its place as a body horror opus. Much like the master pieces by Cronenberg and Ducournau, there is a strong visual focus of style over substance whilst the end result (this despite), remains a well-considered and uniquely complex work of social commentary. Fargeat's writing prowess has come of age since "Revenge" and her characters and storyline flows naturally and are true to the lighter more tongue-in-cheek juxtaposition she creates viz the "heavier" underlying message. The three leads were phenomenal, with Moore probably giving the best performance of her career (thus far). Yes, it is a relatively simple storyline and in some regards it failed to effectively carry the film.... But Fargeat's final scene, which reminds of a Molière farce (and which will probably pick up some criticism) beautifully emphasizes her stylistic intent, making the film just a tad more special.

reviews.author: jbiii-666
reviews.body:
(Apologies if a lot of people are using that headline)

For most of the movie I kept wondering what all the fuss was about. I assumed that it was a Cronenberg work and everyone was just happy to see him returning to his roots. Then I saw it was a female director. And of course the entire thing was carried by two female actors. Ok, then everything made sense. Call me sexist all you want, but there was nothing groundbreaking in the flick besides being Kafka from a woman's perspective. You can be sure that if the leads were men everyone would be decrying the excessive gore and nudity. The effects were decently ghastly and the story was fairly original. But saying Demi Moore turned in the performance of her career? Not by a long shot. I'd say Margaret Qualley does just as well, but not anything worthy of awards. One thing I was gratful for was the complete lack of exposition or explanations of the whys or wherefors. You just get what you get and you must draw your own conclusions. Horror fans, don't expect anything grand, and cinema snobs, don't expect a feminist tour de force.

reviews.author: hoodie-71715
reviews.body:
This film is a roller coaster ride!

The cinematography, the vibrant colours, the sound and the decent into absolute horror is amazing. For a film that dark to have so much light was refreshing. And then it all goes mental! And actually dark.

Demi Moore's performance is outstanding, for her to agree to get THAT ugly gets a hat's off from me.

It won't be for everyone, there's a fair amount of nudity but it's important to the story.

It took me a few days to process what I'd seen and decide that I loved it.

It's still in my head now, I love it when a film does that, only Requiem For A Dream, Martyrs (the original French subtitled) and Hereditary have ever done that.

Definitely not for the faint hearted, but The Substance is a horror fan's dream come true 😁

reviews.author: chammouth
reviews.body:
Let them have cake.

This film was insanely done. Extremely gory but it's the perfect representation of Hollywood's standards, especially when it comes to women. The worst part, it's still happening today and I don't see it coming to an end anytime soon.

The acting of Demi and Margaret is PHENOMENAL. The film itself was well directed and had many hidden meanings that stacked into a masterpiece.

The length of the film was great, didn't drag at all!

Again, very VERY gory and disturbing, but very well fitting with how social media, Hollywood and fame works.

Ending reminded me of Carrie and Smile 2 combined.

reviews.author: kevinmbhc
reviews.body:
To say I enjoyed this would be an understatement. I am still having trouble even really conjuring up an adequate description of this movie.

To describe this film as just dripping in style and visual aesthetic would be a grotesque injustice to the product that has been produced here.

Acting, directing, art direction, music, cinematography are all 10/10. The script is a fantastic vehicle for the subject matter of this film. I wondered at times if I needed or wanted to see more of the inner psychology of the main character (played brilliantly by Demi Moore), I don't think it would have helped the story or in fact the movie overall, its just not that kind of film. This is partly due to the fact that it really is in just too much of a hurry to get on with throwing virtually every trope, hypocrisy and absurd standards we hold on beauty, both from women and men onto women into the woodchipper... with an axe.

A sensory overload that is still on my mind 24 hours after having seen it. Bravo to everyone who played a role in making this film. Really enjoyed it.

reviews.author: MovieOpinions
reviews.body:
The Substance is a captivating exploration of the human condition, blending science fiction and psychological drama in an intriguing, albeit uneven, narrative. It's the kind of film that leaves you thinking long after the credits roll, even if its execution doesn't always match its ambition.

The movie excels in atmosphere and concept. The premise centering on a mysterious, life altering substance raises thought provoking questions about ethics, power, and the nature of humanity. The performances are strong, with the cast effectively portraying characters caught between desperation and discovery. Visually, the film impresses with its minimalist yet haunting design, making every scene feel both intimate and otherworldly.

Where The Substance stumbles is in its storytelling. The pacing is inconsistent, with a slow middle act that tests the viewer's patience. Some subplots feel underdeveloped, leaving certain motivations and consequences frustratingly vague. While ambiguity can work in a film like this, here it sometimes feels like a missed opportunity for deeper exploration.

Despite its flaws, The Substance is a thought provoking experience. It may not fully deliver on its premise, but its ambition and strong performances make it worth a watch especially for fans of sci-fi with a philosophical edge.

reviews.author: ChuckleCritic
reviews.body:
Wow this film does a great job at capturing a real life issue at the moment, while cosmetic business is booming, this film captures something not too far fetched but even Black Mirror esq while we consume a fake reality on the screen.

Ford does a great job at a sleazy producer as he chases his next big beautiful thing for his new show as the great Elizabeth Sparkle is replaced with Sue who he wants to boost ratings for his channel.

All seems like a very normal storyline, but it's not. Wrap your self in for an all time body horror film. This had me looking away constantly as Fargeat enhances the uncomfortable points of noise for the audience and cinematography with blood, guts and some points dark comedy.

Demi Moore, Harrison Ford and especially Margaret Qualley all deserve their flowers for this picture. They were all excellent and hope the Cannes award is followed by more success.

reviews.author: germangarayadriel
reviews.body:
I have very mixed feelings about this film, but I must admit it's one of the few that kept me captivated throughout its entire runtime-achieving that through discomfort. It's a strange blend of suspense and horror that keeps you on edge constantly, never allowing a moment to settle into its world. Many questions are left unanswered, but that's not the point. Both Demi Moore and Margaret Qualley deliver incredible performances, and the music feels otherworldly. The aesthetics, pacing, effects, and tension make it a technical spectacle.

What broke me were the last 30 minutes. They're hard to process because the film deceives you-it sets up a moral about aging, the intertemporal use of life, or even beauty standards as hinted in the trailers, but by the end, the director essentially says, "screw it," unleashing something so drastic and grotesque that you're left unsure whether to laugh, cringe, or feel heartbroken. Your expectations and tolerance for gore will define whether you leave the theater thrilled or deeply uncomfortable. I left feeling profoundly uncomfortable; my girlfriend couldn't stop laughing. Over time, though, I've come to accept the orchestrated madness I witnessed. This is a meticulously grotesque film that refuses to be forgotten, and that's its greatest achievement. It's disgustingly memorable.

reviews.author: cubone-61310
reviews.body:
I watch ALOT of horror films, of all sub-genre. I love most of David Cronenberg's work so of course once I heard about this I went to see it, last week. My barometer passes the test if after seeing a film I immediately want to rewatch it again for various reasons.

I award plaudits to both Actresses on whom the success of this film lies, it could have quite easily slipped into farce and prevented me from suspending my belief in what was being portrayed as taking place.

Their triumph was in convincing the viewer that they both were one person of one soul, consumed by self-loathing for both its bodys aging process & for the shallowness of its youth.

I'm going to go see it again this week at my local Showcase cinema, if you like body horror I suggest you do too.

reviews.author: hntmymhdk
reviews.body:
To start, with this movie is not for everyone. If you get disgusted with body mutilation or have no interest watching someone to retain fictional perfection then this movie is not for you. This is not a limitless pill when consequences show up after feeling amazing, this is how far are you willing to keep that feeling with all the horrors up front.

This movie in my eyes is special, it's not a movie that blows you way with cinematography or amazing camera angles or shots. It makes you think about how much superficial stuff in our lives affects us and how far some people regain it.

This movie is about a successful tv fitness star that has a career running of 30 years. When an old producer who is so obsessed with youth being beautiful gets rid of her, her life comes unraveled. Once she was someone who people looked up too, obsessed over and now all of a sudden an after thought. The feeling of being forgotten is too much when she tries the substance, instantly she becomes beautiful and famous again but with a cost.

Not going to give spoilers, but if your going to get the true message and experience of this movie it's more than just the physical but what are we willing to do to have that special feeling you experienced before and what are you willing to sacrifice.

reviews.author: CinemaSerf
reviews.body: This takes a logical step on from Coralie Fargeat's earlier "Reality+" (2014) drama, only this time it takes a much more substantial swipe at all things vain. "Elisabeth" (Demi Moore) has been at the top of her fitness game for many a year when her boss "Harvey" (Dennis Quaid) decides that she's now too old and that a younger model is needed to present those programmes we all saw on the television of gorgeous, fit and healthy, people showing us how to exercise on a mat in from of our televisions each morning. Distracted by her imminent removal, she is involved in a car accident that introduces her to an handsome young nurse (Robin Grear) and then to a curious invitation to test out a mysterious fluid that can essentially give her her cake and eat it. In best "Jekyll and Hyde" tradition, injecting this quite literally creates a split personality. One is her current self, the other a perfect, younger specimen. They work in a rota system each gets a week of consciousness then has to take a week out. Thing is, the more vivacious character "Sue" (Margaret Qualley) is not so religious about sticking to these sharing rules and we quickly discover that what is "borrowed" can never been returned - with increasingly harrowing results. With the gushing "Harvey" determined to capitalise on his new ratings winner, things become decidedly irritating for the now marginalised "Elisabeth" - but shat can she do? There's no going back...! I think this is Moore at her best. Her palpable sense of evolving fury, exasperation and frustration is expertly captured as is the selfishness of her alter ego by an on form Qualley. Quaid steals his scenes as the truly odious epitome of corporate greed for whom it's all about the business, the money and never the actual people concerned. The denouement is reminiscent of something concocted by one of the David's - Lynch or Cronenberg, and allows the throbbing ghastliness of this story of vanity gone mad to demonstrate just how fickle life can be when there's little actual substance at all to their shallow and vacuous lives. A savage indictment of the short-term and unprincipled "beauty" industry that aims squarely at just about everyone and everything involved, is engagingly toxic and well worth a watch.

reviews.author: akoaytao1234
reviews.body:
I have a huge problem with the setup of Elizabeth's loneliness (regardless of the whole replacing her with a younger her) and how in the hell did she just know how to do 'the substance' steps (even with that short video introduction). The film glossed those over. The ending left me more to be desired. It was more splatter 80's film, but I wished it went full Lynchian fever dream. Though, the mid section of this film truly is tight AND makes up with all my mixed emotions. It was pointedly stylish, it was funny when it needs to be, and it was ruthless.

Performance, I think this might truly is Demi Moore's show of her stuff. She is sad, she is delirious and she just eats the screen. Never really seen her with this vestige of emotions. It can be a bit showy but she really help herself together in tight spots. Qualley was good but she was the foil IN THIS.

Recommended. Also BIG PLUS FOR A HORROR WITHOUT JUMP SCARE. This is pure 80s splatter body horror.

PS: I think watching Rejuvenatrix (1988),it really does have the same topics. I think that film does have a great setup to understand the lead's want for change AND her isolation BUT The Substance has style and that midsection.

reviews.author: I_Ailurophile
reviews.body:
I've been looking forward to this from the moment it was first announced to premiere at Cannes. The premise caught my eye, I love some good body horror, and I like Demi Moore and Margaret Qualley. That filmmaker Coralie Fargeat won Best Screenplay at Cannes further stoked my interest, and I was eager to see 'The substance' as soon as it was released - only the third film I've made a point to see in theaters in 2024, and only the eleventh total since the COVID-19 pandemic began. I had very high expectations. And I've been very disappointed. I question the praise and accolades this has been awarded, and I don't think it's nearly worth going out of one's way to see.

All the way through to the end there are strokes of brilliance throughout the film in various ways. It begins so very promisingly, with small touches of cringe-worthy body horror prepping us for more gnarly visions to come. There's a strong undercurrent of psychological horror on hand, too, as the connection between Elisabeth and Sue runs deeper than a one-line synopsis suggests, and the story is primed to explore the splintering of not just bodies, but minds. More readily evident are the themes on hand, and rest assured that this dives headfirst into the difficulties of aging in modern society, specifically as they apply to women, and even more specifically to women in entertainment: the way that anyone older than thirty suddenly becomes invisible; the way that producers, casting directors, and talent agencies are always looking for the hot young thing; the desperation to feel and remain relevant, outright vanity, and reckless and/or selfish impulses; how young stars are molded and affected by all these factors, potentially resulting in a proverbial monster far removed from the person they were before. And from the outset 'The substance' latches onto a tendency for extreme detail that dovetails neatly into all such big ideas and juicy potential: camera and microphone alike accentuate mundane minutiae that are jarring and off-putting when heavily spotlighted; the ordinary human body, and indeed undeniable beauty, has never been more repulsive; Dennis Quaid is so disgusting in this instance, owing to both audiovisual presentation and characterization, that he's almost as revolting as the figure he portrays in another current release, the biopic 'Reagan.' And that's saying a lot.

From the start this also had a couple issues that gnawed at me, including music that at the outset was unnecessary and which began at an 11, trying to artificially assert ambience before anything had happened. More substantively, details in the picture as we see it - or rather, a lack of rounding details - raise a skeptical eyebrow as Elisabeth is selected out of the blue; questions nothing about the offer that has been extended to her at no charge, nor the set-up that the mysterious, wholly unexplained organization has devised; and has been given no actual instructions or meaningful information about "the substance," but charges ahead while understanding perfectly what the procedure is. Now, I've seen it remarked that modern audiences are too obsessed with plot, looking for details (present or absent) that poke holes in one's immersion, instead of just enjoying the show. I've never understood so clearly what that remark is referring to, and all the same my viewing experience was tripped up by these details, and also by the fact that in no time at all our protagonist is so careless as to disregard the scant few instructions she was given. As a further demerit, an early sequence probably needed a disclaimer, for I worry about viewers with photosensitivity. And still these matters, and some others of a smaller and less overt nature, are nothing compared the most significant problems plaguing the feature.

I said that 'The substance' begins promisingly, and I truly mean it. Would that Fargeat had stayed the course. There comes a discrete point somewhere around the halfway mark where the measured, nuanced body horror and psychological horror are set aside, and the tone shifts significantly. The fact is that this tries to be about half a dozen different movies, and while some of the flavors ably mix, others do not. Body horror and psychological horror do not mix with the most wildly over the top acting and direction that takes over, suddenly and then periodically. The flick almost becomes horror-comedy as it irregularly slips into bare-faced satire that leaves behind the more deliberate sensibilities with which Fargeat first approached the material. At times this is so simple-minded in its ordinary horror-thriller ideations that it becomes dull; there comes a time when the growing darkness of the more subtle thoughts is just discarded outright, and we're now watching a pure monster flick. Before all is said and done, this also embraces a level of blood, gore, literal splatter, and outrageous visuals that one is reminded of Brian Yuzna and 1989's 'Society,' if not also Stuart Gordon with his own irreverent genre frolics. Through to the end there are strokes of brilliance in all these capacities, and even the body horror and psychological horror continue to rise and recede. But the amalgamation as a whole doesn't work, and the doing is instead so messy and aggravating that I came close to just walking out. I've never done that before, and I still haven't, but this was almost the first time.

In all other regards this is tremendously well made. The stunts and practical effects are stupendous, including instances of violence, blood and gore, and certainly special makeup and creature effects. Where computer-generated imagery is sparingly employed, that judicious utilization blends seamlessly into the filmed footage. The production design and art direction are impeccable, and the costume design, hair, and makeup (of all stripes) are flawless. I love Raffertie's music in and of itself, themes that resonate powerfully as they complement the sordid tale, and I take issue only with how it is employed at times. Moore and Qualley give fantastic performances of admirable nuance, range, poise, and physicality, ably bringing to bear all the turmoil of Elisabeth and Sue; Quaid is solid in his supporting part. The sound design is terribly robust in the best and worst of ways, Benjamin Kracun's cinematography is sharp, and the editing is keen. The very concept is outstanding, and the procedure that Elisabeth and Sue must maintain is kind of ingenious. Unfortunately, none of this matters so much when the storytelling swerves so inelegantly between airs that do mesh, that don't mesh, or which downright compete for dominance. At its best I can understand why Fargeat was honored with "Best Screenplay"; I can also understand why she won "Best Screenplay" and not "Best Film" or "Best Direction." At its worst, I think even that honor was undeserved.

I entered with very high expectations, and I've been very disappointed. 'The substance' could have been many things, but it couldn't be all of them. The best notions that it had going for it, the measured, mounting body horror and psychological horror, unquestionably represent the best possibilities for the concept, but the others might have been just as swell all on their own. All together, it falls apart, and it does so as a discernible juncture. I wondered many weeks ago how this genre piece could be a whopping two hours and twenty minutes long, and the regrettable answer is that it tries to do and be too many things. With all this having been said, while it's possible I'm being too kind, I'm not inclined to say that the title is altogether bad. I don't dislike it. But then, any broad words of positivity, extended to the entirety instead of to particular elements, also seem several steps too far. I suppose I'm glad for those who get more out of 'The substance' than I did, but I find it difficult to offer an especial recommendation.

reviews.author: HasankaDesigner
reviews.body:
The film's opening scene was incredibly effective-it gave me all the information I needed without explicitly saying much. It begins with a shot of the Hollywood Walk of Fame, zoomed in on the protagonist's star. We see the star when it's freshly placed, with crowds flocking around, taking pictures, and celebrating the protagonist's success. As the years pass, the star begins to crack, and people walk over it, dropping trash without noticing whose name it bears. This simple, visual storytelling brilliantly set up the backstory of Elisabeth, the protagonist.

Visually, this is easily the most striking film I've seen this year. Each shot feels meticulously crafted to serve the narrative, and honestly, it's so beautiful that every frame could stand on its own as a painting. The frequent close-ups were especially effective, adding a layer of intensity and creepiness to certain scenes. The color grading was perfect, enhancing the film's atmosphere. It's truly a visual masterpiece.

The story and writing are incredibly clever. I don't think I've ever seen a film with such a creative narrative. In an age where original ideas feel scarce, this movie felt like a breath of fresh air-gripping from start to finish. The way it tackles ageism in Hollywood, particularly how it affects women, through a blend of camp, horror, and dark comedy, was both smart and unique. Even though many of the characters didn't have much dialogue, they were all memorable and stuck with me long after the film ended.

The cast is fantastic, starting with Demi Moore, who likely drew on her own experiences with Hollywood's obsession with looks and aging. This is one of her best performances, and she deserves all the praise for it. There's a particular moment-without giving too much away-where her character ages further, and it was mesmerizing to watch. Margaret Qualley also shines in her role as Sue, a fame-hungry, egotistical character willing to do anything to get ahead. The contrast between the two characters, who are ultimately reflections of the same person, highlights how we can be our own harshest critics and how societal views on aging and appearance can deeply affect us. The rest of the cast delivers solid performances as well.

Overall, this is my favorite film of the year so far!

reviews.author: pinokiyo
reviews.body:
This movie is a dark comedy for sure.

The director is surprisingly female. But what's not shocking is that it's by a foreign director.

American directors can't make this level of over-the-top disturbing violence; it reminds me of the movies Paul Verhoeven used to make (Robocop, Total Recall).

I get it... this movie is supposed to be satire, extremely over-the-top fantasy world... but where do you draw the limit?

If you try to watch this movie logically, you will not make it through.

The storyline is generic B movie.

It's just all about the performances by the two veteran actors and "special effects" that has created the buzz.

The movie is full of plotholes and outrageous behavior that makes zero sense at all.

I found it really hilarious how the girl is so professionally handy, she drilled and built a perfectly functioning/seamless secret door in the bathroom.

And don't get me started on the whole shady Substance pickup location and how that whole thing works...

The only realism in this movie is casting Demi Moore for the role because her career/age in reality fits exactly the character.

There's also gimmicks like full nudity from both actresses, so of course that increases the rating for some viewers.

There's not that many characters in this film, but Demi Moore and Dennis Quaid performances easily steals the show.

I'm sure both or one of them will get some kind of award.

The ending is ridiculously disturbing and disgusting - if you love extremely grotesque material, then that's something you will "enjoy" about this film. I can see how people walked out or were offended.

I can appreciate that they didn't use full CG for it, practical effect/prosthetics work made it look way more traumatizing.

So basically, what I want to say is if you want a nice, warm family movie to watch, while eating dinner, check this one out....

reviews.author: korzeniowskir
reviews.body: This movie tells a shocking story. I would give it an adult rating (18+), because it contains scene of extreme violence. I am a middleaged man and I was shocked to the core by some frankly unnecessarily violent scenes. I would give "Sunstance" an "8" if the violence had been toned down a bit. This movie doesn't really belong in the sci-fi genre, it doesn't focus on futuristic technology, not really, the technology is only used to create a base for the story. Actually this movie concentrates more on philosophical and psychological issues. From the trailer we learn that the main character (50 years old TV star) desperately wants to recapture her youth. People all around her seem to idialize youth and detest seniority, especially in a woman. She uses this mysterious substance and for a while everything seems to work out for the better. However a little while later something goes horribly wrong. In my opinion the story revolves around the concept of perspective and subjectivity. The world is portrayed in a grotesque manner, it's definitely distopian. The main character struggles to keep herself relevant, to mean something, to keep from becoming obsolete. This movie portrays her internal struggle very well and her changing perspective caused by strong events. The grotesqueness is also very strong, especially nearing the end, sometimes pushing the action to absurdity. Overall, the world, the quality of acting, the story and the ambience are well defined and fit into a larger scheme. I would like to add that this movie is definitely a horror movie, but it also has elements of a psychological drama.

reviews.author: filmephile
reviews.body:
This film is wild, insane, and strange, as many critics have stated. Much of the time, film reviewers can be hyperbolic. But this is legitimately a shocking film through and through. It's also very unique in how its told, which is refreshing.

The story is quite simple: A fading, middle-aged celebrity, Elisabeth Sparkle (Demi Moore), an Oscar-winning actress known for hosting her aerobics TV show, is abruptly fired from her show on her 50th birthday by her boss (Dennis Quaid) and takes a substance that temporarily creates a younger, better version of herself (Margaret Qualley). While this could've easily been a very mediocre film, it managed be so much more. The beauty and the substance, pun intended, of this film lies in its searing, shocking execution. The film manages to be genuinely scary, discomforting, darkly comedic, and thrilling all at the same time, without feeling like it's trying to do too much at once. Moore is magnificent as the lead. And Qualley is a true revelation. Quaid is good and believable as the slimy, slick, glib boss.

During the first 30 mins of the film, I was scared that this would be a beautiful-looking but hollow depiction of the horrors of aging: a film that was style over substance. But that's not the case at all. The film has immense style and substance. Every shot looks like it could be a painting; and every shot contains such pathos and gravitas. The cinematography, framing, lighting, and use of color are just absolutely stellar. As is the acting, score, and the extensive makeup work later in the film involving the body horror. But it's the writing that is the real winner, and that's why this film is so excellent.

Many of the lighter moments are tinged with terror. And the darker moments are often tinged with a splash of levity. The nuance achieved here is something to behold. Whether director Coralie Fargeat intended to or not, the film is very reminiscent of the classic horror stories The Picture of Dorian Gray by Oscar Wilde, and Carrie by Stephen King. And, of course, much of the body horror depicted in this film brings to mind David Cronenberg's filmography. With the 2 hr 20 min runtime, it somehow manages to have a slow build until the shocking final act, while also never wasting a second of screentime.

My only small quibble is that this film can feel too on-the-nose and shocking for shock value, rather than adding to the story. This is especially true of the last section of the film. But I could just be a tad too prude. I know most critics seem to have really loved the ending. So perhaps it's subjective. But no one can argue that this film isn't well-made.

This film is best enjoyed blind, which is why this review is so sparse and vague. But do know you're in for a ride. Before you know it, aging hits you. And when it does, that discovery and the way your experience of the world changes can be deeply unsettling, confounding, and even horrific. That is precisely how I'd describe this film. It sneaks up on you and never really lets up. This is one of the very best films of 2024, and the most shocking film in recent memory. Do yourself a favor and check out this masterpiece.

reviews.author: afoteyannum
reviews.body:
The film is a bit of a fable, and an unofficial spiritual successor to the excellent Brian Thomas Jones film The Rejuvenator (also recommended, but not prerequisite viewing), and tells the story of a 50-year old fitness content star that nears the end of her career and takes drastic measures to extend said career by injecting a mysterious substance that promises to be a fountain of youth.

The titular Substance is a concoction that literally creates a younger, better clone of the user, in this story played by Margeret Qualley, with some caveats and strict rules.

Of course, those caveats and rules aren't strictly adhered to in this film, and the resulting complications are incredibly entertaining to watch, albeit very, VERY gross.

Without going into spoilers, I can say with full confidence that this is one of the grossest films I've seen in YEARS. A true gem in the body horror subgenre of horror, and definitely worthy of being mentioned in the same conversations as classic films in the genre like Videodrome, Basket Case, From Beyond, Possessor, and even John Carpenter's The Thing.

This film is really good at putting the viewer into situations where we can experience what the main characters do. Cinematographer Benjamin Kracun (Beast, Promising Young Woman) uses (non-anamorphic, for SHAME! LOL) wide angle and macro lenses to great effect, almost turning the film into found footage horror for a few beats. The way he uses incredibly short focal lengths to exaggerate features and paint very specific thematic narratives around certain characters is done rather well. A very good example of this is in the very beginning of the film during a meeting between Elisabeth and Harvey in a restaurant where Harvey is eating shrimp. The camera lingers and focuses on Harvey's mouth, fingers, and the shrimp themselves, painting an incredibly vivid picture of a person who is uncaring, oafish, and borderline porcine in the way he presents himself.

I'm pretty sure I'm not going to eat any shrimp any time soon after watching that sequence...

And to further compliment these intentional visual choices is some INCREDIBLE sound design! The way things SOUND makes them seem far more vile and disgusting than they are in reality, the aforementioned lunch scene being a great example. Every crunch, chew, bite, rip, and tear is amplified to very uncomfortable degrees. It's EXPERTLY done.

Most of the film does this, especially when the yucky stuff happens. Body transformations are shown in graphic detail with macro and wide lenses, accompanied by the sounds you would imagine someone literally ripping themselves from inside your body would make. It's very, very effective at conveying a sense of disgust. Bodies make noises when they change, ambient sounds are distorted at key points in the story-things sound off, but on purpose.

What's really interesting in all this is that even through all that really gross, nasty body horror, there's a TON of beauty juxtaposed. Bodies not only move in gross and disgusting ways in spots, but also in really nice, beautifully shot, composed, and framed ways as well. There's a sequence towards the end of the second act that looks like a really good music video, for example, and while being very beautiful (both in terms of framing, composition, lighting, etc. AND the actors involved) also highlights the sexist and somewhat lecherous nature of the type of content Elisabeth/Sue create. It's really well shot and when placed in context of the rest of the film that came prior to that scene, very depressing and almost horrifying.

This film is basically a scathing treatise on the way Hollywood eats up youth and beauty, then spits out depression, deplorability, and despair. Watching Elisabeth fall from grace in the way she does is very sad and depressing, particularly in the ending. And I personally think that having Dennis Quaid's lecherous, uncaring exec be named Harvey wasn't an accident...

This film was extremely entertaining, but I don't think it will resonate with everyone.

First of all, it's really gross. Like, "you might not want to eat while watching this" gross. This reviewer is a diehard, decades-long horror fan with a broken soul, so it didn't gross me out all that much. But other people who aren't as strong willed or as desensitized to body horror as I am will DEFINITELY struggle with watching some of the more intense body horror parts.

The practical effects on display here are top notch. At no point during this film did I wish there was more CG or felt like what I was watching wasn't real in-story. SFX makeup artist Olivier Afonso and rest of the team that worked on this did an amazing job in turning the always stunning Demi Moore into something WILDLY different from her normal, pulchritudinous appearance. I don't want to spoil anything, but what she becomes really reminded me of some of the stuff Rob Bottin did with The Thing!

One other thing that may not resonate with everyone is the fact that this film is kind of a fable, almost a fairy tale. It's not set in a real place, and people don't act like you would expect them to in the real world. It's a clearly stylized version of reality, particularly Los Angeles. This doesn't really become apparent until closer to the end of the film (at least for me), particularly during one sequence that is VERY reminiscent of a signature scene from the horror classic Carrie. It was clear to me by the the end of this film that it's totally a fable. If you're expecting a by-the-book, standard type of story, this ain't it, at least not fully.

All in all, this is definitely well worth a watch. A somewhat powerful, rather sad, and kind of depressing cautionary fable about the potential dangers of chasing youth in order to fit into a system of misogyny, set in a body horror film that apes some of the best work of Cronenberg, Henenlotter, and Carpenter. Oh, and Demi Moore and Margeret Qualley are fully naked for a lot of this film. Which ironically, serves to drive the point of this film home even more on a meta level-here we are ogling Demi's and Margeret's fully naked bodies (full frontal female nudity and everything) during a tale about the dangers of vanity, sexism, envy, and jealousy.

Rather brilliant, if you ask me.

reviews.author: rverdonschot
reviews.body:
Not the groundmaking movie some make it out to be, not by a long shot. It's basicly Jackle & Hyde, with it's feminist message hammered home with a wrecking ball. Yes, we get it. Men bad. Men sexist pigs. Make women sad.

Fortunately, the film is still extremely entertaining with brillaint set design, good performances and some excellent blood and gore effects that could have come straight from Screaming Mad George. It's a video nasty packaged as a classy movie. As if Stuart Gordon and Brian Yuzna made a Black Mirror episode together. It's not a horror movie, it's a wild and gross comedy. Just enjoy the ride.

reviews.author: robertrutledge
reviews.body:
Meet Elizabeth Sparkle (Demi Moore), a former Hollywood star facing the cruel reality of an aging body in a discriminatory industry. After being fired because of this, she falls victim to a new, mysterious drug: the Substance. Once injected, using her own genetics, the Substance generates a younger and sexier version of herself known as Sue (Margaret Qualley), to which her conscience is transferred. It comes with a catch though: she is only allowed to occupy either body for a week at a time, after which time she must switch bodies.

As a man watching this film, I thought the filmmakers did an excellent job capturing the uphill battle of an aging woman in an unforgiving industry. One can commiserate with the protagonist as she experiments with this drug she believes to be the answer to all her problems. The movie wastes no time exploring the backstory of the substance itself and instead focuses on Elizabeth's struggle to successfully lead a double life.

The two leads are perfectly cast and do an excellent job in their respective roles. It's great that the filmmakers opted not to use AI to de-age Demi Moore, which I can imagine may have been tempting. Qualley does an excellent job playing a somewhat ditzy Hollywood "it" girl desperate for her time in the sun. Moore's character, on the other hand, is an equally-believable jaded and cynical woman who some may say is "past her prime."

The movie's weakness is that it is too predictable. We know right from the start that Elizabeth will be unable to find the perfect balance and ultimately fail to use this drug safely and responsibly. Alas, such is human nature. What ensues is a tumultuous rollercoaster ride with its ups and downs but no real light at the end of the tunnel.

The movie at times feels like a stretched-out, R-rated episode of Black Mirror, especially toward the end. I wonder if this would have worked better as a short film to get its message across more succinctly. This would entail removing all the visceral bits, nudity, violence, etc., leaving it feeling watered-down. But these aspects feel somewhat excessive anyway and the intended shock value does not hit very hard in 2024.

In conclusion, this movie is a very riveting experience. While it is perhaps not a horror movie in the traditional sense, it makes for a great psychological thriller and a chilling social commentary. The movie serves as a mirror of sorts for the audience to examine just how outrageous beauty standards for women in (and out of) Hollywood have become. What's scary is that it feels like the Substance could be an actual product in the near future.

reviews.author: mrdupondishere-53470
reviews.body:
