reviews.author: ReadingFilm
reviews.body: Between this and the Terrifier series we have an impurity spiral, an arms race to what is the most grotesque and out of touch to try to win the trophy of who is the director of the moment willing to go farthest. Still it is ultimately just a cheap horror disguised as arthouse and, temporarily takes the trophy, until the next one tries it. It rips off so many directors without thought. It takes tricks specifically from Requiem for a Dream, here, Dennis Quaid's wide-angle showman surrounded by psychos, such things were in that film to depict drug-induced psychosis, but here, it's from the very start of the film before any drugs are even taken at all. I illustrate that the film is just thoughtlessly ripping off aesthetics from start to finish and not even considering them at all. It is one idea, one single half hour episode, repeated nonstop for over two hours with no variation or exploration. This is its fatal flaw. It is all so surreal that you are never able to take what is happening to Demi literally; see how David Cronenberg's the Fly begins with hard scientific realism, gradually descending into the grotesque, forcing the audience to wrestle with the feeling that it is happening for real. The Substance also commits the worst sin, audience flattery--the film must be about... beauty standards! Okay, that is the first 20 minutes, what about the next 2 hours? Oh, that is literally it. Welles once said any movie with a "message" is shallow as a thimble. In an interview director Fargeat said that she doesn't like homages, and yet this film is nonstop homages and cliches from start to finish, even down to direct musical quotations from other films. So many extended tangents could have been cut down, like the beat up scene and the blood soak scene that are just there to express a style rather than tell a story. Demi is able to elevate her scenes before they regress into one-note directorial show-off. Fargeat pushes her stars out of the way much like Qualley does Demi in the film; the center stage must be Fargeat the director first, even at the expense of the movie itself. It is sad because even when Demi was taking the various grotesque mutant forms you can still see her eyes and spirit, she can never be ugly even when they try. The director is just not interested in the story that is right in front of her: ending the experiment and accepting life as an old woman. The film is too desperate to make a mark and impress the wrong audience, like the first film of a director with an unlimited bankroll and total creative control. It is a Qualley when it should have been a Demi.

reviews.author: metaldumpling
reviews.body: This film has not only changed my perspective on myself, but on societal expectations on beauty. Not only does this film come with a perfect message, but it also shows it through the most incredible way. It was like watching a mash-up of Carrie, Re-Animator, The Shining, Requiem for a Dream, The Thing, Hellraiser, and The Blob all combined but in such a way that I feel like I'll never see a movie this incredible ever again. An absolute masterpiece. Demi, Margaret, and Dennis all exceeded my expectations beyond anything I could've possibly imagined. I also seriously appreciate practical effects, and these were the best I have ever seen. So real to the point where someone ran out of my theater showing to throw up during the scene with Sue's mouth. I can't recommend this movie enough, I really can't. I will forever treat myself with the love and respect I deserve because of this movie.

reviews.author: SlashedProductions
reviews.body:
I went into this knowing very little and I hadn't even watched the full trailer. The buzz around this movie seemed almost impossible to live up to, but I was still pretty confident I'd enjoy it. I had also seen Fargeat's other film, Revenge, from 2017. That's a good movie, but The Substance is on a whole other level.

A truly unique experience, that I don't see breaking out and reaching a wide audience. But for a certain type of horror cinephile, this will be a movie to remember.

The first 2/3 of the movie set up a great premise that feels like it's out of a Cronenberg movie, but looks and feels very modern. Then, the third act goes completely for broke, and feels like something out of an 80's Stuart Gordon or Bryan Yunza production. Even many who were with it for the first two acts might be disappointed with the conclusion. While it was unfolding, I was constantly asking myself if I liked what I was seeing or thought it was goofy. When it's all said and done, the answer is a resounding yes, because I cannot believe Coraline Fargeat was allowed to do that and get any kind of funding whatsoever. But I'm so glad she did.

There's so much more to say about this movie. I could go on about the score, cinematography, and performances. But I think for now I'll just say everything about The Substance is excellent, and I hope it does as well as a movie like this can do in its theatrical run. Demi Moore and Margaret Qualley kill it.

reviews.author: Vera_Felkina
reviews.body:
The Substance is a body horror with a relatively trivial plot, at least predictable for most body horror fans. Only a few twists are actually surprising, and yet it is not a thriller that entertains through them. It is a simple and beautiful satire on the modern Hollywood industry, taking the well-known concepts and ideas to the next level. And these concepts make it absolutely beautiful. This film is two and a half hours long, but because it plays with the expectations and literally has something entertaining in each scene, I really enjoyed watching it up until the last moment. Let me say without any spoilers that the ending is what we all love about the body horror genre, and even though it looks a little surreal and different from the rest of the film, it was still an amazing sequence to experience.

The thing about body horrors is that it's physically uncomfortable to watch them. I've had this issue with many of them, but it seemed especially difficult with this film. Gore and guts, rotting wounds, and decaying limbs are far beyond disgusting. However, the true horrors always take place in one's mind, and this film is no exception.

I must also mention how masterfully this film was produced and shot. It was a great pleasure to see something different from basic and uninspired Hollywood movies. I am a man of cinema, but I had to spend last 1.5 months watching literally all MCU movies with my girlfriend. Watching something actually inspired and thoroughly designed was a breath of fresh air.

reviews.author: Lord_Frog
reviews.body:
The Substance is the most insane and best movie I've seen in at least 10 years.

Do yourself a favour and run to the cinema to see this, and you'll thank me later.

Absolutely crazy, I've never, EVER seen anything like it.

Demi Moore deserves an Oscar for this!

I can't stop thinking about it. Hilarious and horrifying at the same time.

With a strong mix of influences from The Shining, Carrie, The Fly, The Thing, 2001 and many more classics, The Substance delivers a dark comedy/horror/sci-fi experience that HAS to be seen in a cinema with a big crowd.

I've seen it twice already and I'm still buzzing about it. It's already in my top 3 horror movies of all time.

Beautifully horrible. Don't miss it, really!! Not just a movie, it's an experience you'll never forget.

reviews.author: aghostofachance
reviews.body:
I like horror movies a LOT and although body horror is not my favorite genre, "The Substance" was really exciting, shocking and also VERY disturbing. First of all, congratulations Demi Moore, you have gone to such extremes for your performance in this movie so you totally deserve your Golden Globe. I don't want to sound ageist by saying Demi Moore was the star of my childhood (I will always remember her with "Ghost", which was the first VHS I had bought with my pocket money), but only to make it clear how proud and happy I am to see one of my favorite actresses winning Best Actress award. It was one of the boldest acting choices of the year. As aging and becoming a thing of the past is the ultimate horror of most Hollywood women, who could have been cast for this role any better than Moore? Moore has always been known for being a bold and beautiful woman, such as Sharon Stone or Robin Wright, only to name a few. But who would have thought she would accept such a demanding role...? While most aging Hollywood beauties would reject to act in The Substance, I bet Moore also saw the golden opportunity. Because not only she is a bold and beautiful, she is also an intelligent woman.

The story is pretty well-paced and as the tension and dread builds, you keep saying to yourself, "Okay, there should be a limit or reason to this madness". Well, there isn't. It literally goes all the way down to hell and drags you with it. The transformation in the movie is horrible but you know that if this thing was real, it couldn't get any better. I have watched quite many movies with body horror segments within, but this one was jaw-dropping. It is so disturbing to see the change and feel the character's emotional downfall, the psychological discomfort that it could well be traumatic for some to watch this movie. It seemed to me like practical effects and make up effects were heavily implemented to create a more realistic look and it surely does. So it's not tailored for a wide audience. You need to be able to hold your breakfast well enough... Not for the faint of heart, not for the younger audience.

The theme of dual personality, shedding skin, medical procedures and everything else do not try to establish itself on a scientifically correct or possible base. But the acting pretty much convinces you into believing the fear, torturous pain and rage. Margarette Qualley's portrayal of beauty slowly turns into a nightmarish monster. Instead of Qualley, if they had cast someone looking like the younger Moore or someone acting in the same body language, maybe it could be more effective to make the viewer believe that they were one and the same. Well, it didn't work that well but it could have been better. So I didn't like Qualley's acting much.

Denis Quaid was also portraying such an ugly, evil and disgusting character but on the inside, in order to create a contrast to the physical ugliness of the female lead. He did his best for sure.

Coralie Fargeat is a young and promising director. Her use of light,music and angles were quite good. The transition of the scenes were also well done. And the tone of the movie stays the same throughout the whole movie, which is something I really appreciate in directing which helps the viewer to stay focused. That ending (!), in every meaning, was like someone holds your eye lids with both hands and pouring all your nightmares in. Was it too much?.. Yes. Was it too dark?... Yes. But this is how you make horror movies, you need to be over-expressive, oppressive and crushing at times. But real horror fans will understand what I mean. I hope in the future, Fargeat tries other sub-genres too in the horror genre, who knows maybe she might continue to surprise and find new audience to explore her works...

I enjoyed the movie as a horror fan and I also advised to some of my friends. I didn't hear any feed backs good or bad yet... But like I already said that it is surely not for a broader audience but that doesn't mean it's bad or failing. It's a niche job well crafted which will probably be remembered in the future as a classic in its category.

reviews.author: jdonovansteele
reviews.body:
Everyone needs to see this film. Demi Moore just became my hero. And the writer/director, Coralie Fargeat, just delivered much needed shock treatment to the masses. Absolutely ferocious in it's message, 'The Substance' is the most fun you'll ever have finding out whether you're a monster-maker, or a monster yourself. I haven't been this scared to go to sleep in a long time. Make no mistake; though it is horrifying body horror, it is more aligned with 'The Shining', in terms of the haunting psychological impact every frame will have on you. The hypnotic design of the first half of the film lends to suddenly feeding on your soul by the end.

It's a masterpiece.

The intention and execution are married perfectly.

I love this film. And my heart belongs to Coralie Fargeat.

reviews.author: pranayjalvi
reviews.body:
The Substance is distinctive less for its nutso, over-the-top gore than for a single scene midway through the film that exposes a different kind of body horror-or, more specifically, the way insecurity can be its own kind of horror.

The most compelling parts of The Substance deal with how social conventions turn women against themselves. A stronger version of the film might have dug into the complexities of that truth, instead of simply arranging itself around it. With wit, style and ruthlessness, Fargeat has made a movie that's an example of the soulless pop-culture object she's spoofing.

Ultimately, The Substance isn't saying anything new, but the extremes to which it's willing to go make it unforgettable cinema.

My Rating : 7.5/10.

Wow!

reviews.author: jxxxxnhxxt
reviews.body:
Slick, stylish and grotesquely sexy, Coralie Fargeat's The Substance is a fearlessly bold sophomore effort which lays bare the fleeting nature of youth and the fickle commercial systems that promote and uphold impossible standards of feminine beauty.

Demi Moore headlines as an actress whose opportunities are rapidly escaping her grasp by her fiftieth birthday; fired from the aerobics show she hosts in favour of a younger lead in the 18-30 age bracket, the aptly-named Elizabeth Sparkle desperately turns to a black market enhancement product that, when activated, births a 'better version' of herself. Played with relish by a Margaret Qualley who chose the perfect project to showcase that sex appeal is amongst her repertoire of talents, Elizabeth comes to realise that her alter ego Sue isn't so much a better version of herself, but almost a different entity entirely. As Sue quickly cements her own star power, Elizabeth's original body begins to pay the price as the Substance is misused to feed her younger counterpart's rabid addiction to the limelight.

While not to undermine Qualley's excellent turn as Sue, it is Moore who truly sinks her teeth into every facet of the character and her dilemma, realising one of the most relatable performances in recent memory. Elizabeth Sparkle is not only a mirror image of many of us as individuals, but also of the material preoccupations of our culture. Moore shows no hesitation in letting the meta aspects of the role inform her performance; while her career has no doubt been successful and with much longevity, she plays those introspective moments of evaluating her own appearance with an almost touching sense of vulnerability, nostalgia and eventually frustration.

Though the film's themes - and what Fargeat wants to say about them - are conveyed clearly in the first two acts, the movie indulges its independence from studio notes in the closing salvo. Viewers will be pushed to their limits with a gleefully gory climax - indeed, The Substance will have viewers squirming throughout - that lets go of their hand and tests their comprehension of what they are watching in an elevation of horror that may push the envelope too far for some sensibilities. Fargeat definitely ends the film on a note that encourages viewers to question what they have just seen, but does so without the clearly defined satire of everything approaching these moments. As such, audiences may lose track of Fargeat's intentions in the chaos and mileage will inevitably vary with regards to how satisfied one viewer is from the next.

Releasing at a pivotal time in the future careers of both leading actresses, and with a mostly tight grip on a subject matter which pervades our societies on a global cultural scale, The Substance is a refreshing, confident take on beauty and the fickle nature of fame. In an age where many of us record and share our own image to chronicle our lives in the search of validation and recognition, it is a soberingly timely tale that reminds us how such an obsession can create an unstoppable monster of us all.

reviews.author: schaumie-35089
reviews.body:
In all the movie tells, it could have been the half of the time. An episode for Black Mirror (in it's better times) would have been the right space and time for this story. More than 60 Minutes is too much and the movie takes over 2 hours... Mrs. Moore seems to take face some of her own fears in her role.

reviews.author: Pumpkin_Man
reviews.body:
I drove an hour away to see this movie, and the last 30 minutes of this movie alone was worth the trip! At first, I thought it was kinda slow and a little confusing, but it goes hard in the last act. I'll try not to spoil too much, but if you love crazy weird disturbing gory body horror movies, please do yourself a favor and go see The Substance ASAP!

The movie stars Demi Moore as Elizabeth Sparkle, an aging award winning actress whose time to shine is past her. She's now forced to do exercise tapes that hardly anyone watches. After getting into a car wreck, someone offers her the chance to try 'The Substance'

When she injects herself, another woman is born from her back. She's younger and prettier and calls herself 'Sue' Elizabeth has to go into a kind of hibernation for a week while Sue is out living her last life. If one dose of the Substance is missed, they will be forced to deal with the consequences.

This film definitely grows on you, and the last 30 minutes are just so crazy bonkers that I dare not to spoil it for you! I would highly recommend THE SUBSTANCE!!!

reviews.body:

The acting is extraordinary. Oscar like.

But what started as a promising futuristic great movie, sort of modern Dorian Gray, evolved into a cheap horror movie which was even hard to watch. I think the movie should be re-edited, removing the horrifying scenes and by that becoming a classical.

I gave it a 7 but half. Ovie deserves a 9 and the other half a 5...

reviews.author: cindyacheney
reviews.body:
Demi Moore has made some flops in her time but this is definitely not one of them. What a surreal and modern paradox of the body beautiful yet as an aging actress Demi is completely at ease with all the graphic nudity required to pull this one off and quite rightly so.

Elisabeth's decay at the hands of her own vanity is portrayed with style and panache revealing a terrifying and utterly believable reality for many people who choose to live in that world.

It is twisted, incredibly graphic and brutal with great special effects, I hope it goes down as a cult classic in true Demi style. Well done Helga! I'll pass on you cooking for me anytime soon though.

reviews.author: yurotuIaida
reviews.body:
Review: Substance (2024) Substance is a haunting exploration of vanity, obsession, and the fragility of self-identity that defies the conventions of horror and drama. Directed with a calm precision and an almost clinical detachment, it's the kind of genre-bending narrative that leaves you thinking long after the credits roll.

A fading celebrity takes a black-market drug, a cell-replicating substance, that temporarily transforms her into a younger, more perfect version of herself. Sounds like your typical body horror setup, right? But Substance is much more than just grotesque transformation. This isn't about flesh-eating monsters or jump-scares; it's about the terrifying cost of chasing an idealized version of yourself, and the psychological unraveling that follows.

"The Substance," works like a dark mirror - it gives you a perfect replica, a more youthful, more beautiful version of yourself. But there's a catch: time is divided equally between the original and the clone, each taking shifts to live out their life. Seven days for you, seven days for the new, improved version. The rules seem simple enough - but in the hands of an ambitious , young star desperately clinging to her relevance, those rules prove impossible to maintain.

This film challenges our perception of horror, replacing gore with existential terror. What makes it so chilling is how relatable the fears are - the anxiety of losing one's beauty, youth, and fame. The actress, whose performance carries the film, is riveting. Her descent into obsession is masterfully portrayed, and the nuanced portrayal of her emotional and physical deterioration is heartbreaking. Watching her shift between herself and her clone, you can't help but ask: how much of us would we be willing to sacrifice in the pursuit of perfection?

The pacing is deliberate, even languid at times, yet this only heightens the tension. Every moment of calm feels like it's lulling us into a false sense of security, right before the emotional rupture comes. The aesthetic choices - muted, almost sterile lighting - give the film a detached, eerie atmosphere that mirrors the protagonist's unraveling sense of self.

It's almost shocking to think this is a Mubi production rather than A24. While A24 has become synonymous with visually lush, often surreal horror, Substance keeps its grounded, cerebral tone while still being absolutely terrifying in its own way. The film feels more like a dark psychological thriller, using body horror as a tool to explore themes of self-worth, desire, and the consequences of tampering with nature.

It's a reminder that horror doesn't always need blood and monsters to unsettle. Sometimes, the scariest thing is the idea that the version of you that you see in the mirror isn't really yours at all. And sometimes, the most horrifying monster is the one you create inside your own mind.

Substance is haunting in its simplicity, and while it may not have the visceral edge of more traditional horror films, its ability to make you question your own desires and insecurities makes it a standout in the genre. It's a slow burn that builds to a devastating conclusion, leaving you with a lingering sense of unease long after the screen goes black. This is horror for the modern age, and it's a damn good one.

reviews.author: littllepea
reviews.body: I was very excited for this movie and it lived up to the hype! It was absolute insanity, unhinged in the best way. Made my jaw drop on multiple occasions. You have to understand it's meant to be that way going into it and keep an open mind. It was beautifully shot and the acting was spot on. I loved the juxtaposition of modern with vintage touches/vintage feel. The message of the movie is something we all can relate to as humans and especially women with unrealistic beauty standards imposed on us. The Substance has been my favorite movie of this year and I think it's going to be a cult classic.

reviews.author: atch1983
reviews.body:
The first half hour of the movie draws you into the story of a once-great star who has aged and is now about to be replaced by someone younger. It's so well-crafted. The cinematography in the opening minutes is fantastic. All the close-ups, sounds, and camera angles are outstanding.

In the second half hour, as she becomes consumed by the idea of the substance, her desperate need not to fade away becomes apparent. The need to matter, to remain loved by the public, takes center stage.

Then comes the final hour. I still found the third half hour interesting, although I was a bit skeptical about the all the sexual scenes in the second half hour. Even so, you wanted to know what would happen next.

The last part of the movie... I got it. Especially the final scenes-I understood the point. I just felt that they really took it to the extreme, and it felt unnecessary.

The movie lost quality as it went on. Still, it's an okay film. But I don't understand the hype around it. It wasn't scary at all, more like... "Wow, what the hell was that?"

6 out of 10.

reviews.author: s-l-k
reviews.body:
Were all of you who rated this high actually high when you watched it?

I'm a horrorholic and can love just about any movie in the sub-genres of the genre for one reason or another. Especially the gross and out there but there wasn't anything plausible about this movie in the "horror/dark comedy/satire" etc...realm at all.

Not even in science fiction does any of this make sense. An alien plunging out of someone's stomach actually seems somewhat possible but this DIY duplication nonsense with no information as to how it works or what the consequences are is just not even ironic enough to work. And for FREE?

What the $"@# was Coralie Fargeat thinking or was she at all? I cannot believe that this is what she thought would be the best way to approach this subject.

I think of all the really out there movies that most people will question their plausibility and laugh if they find this is acceptable.

I will, however, say that yes some of the cinematography was beautiful and Demi did a great job though she looked a lot like Courteney Cox in a bunch of scenes but it was really hard to believe she could barely move with one leg messed up let alone run around with both of them destroyed (and looking almost normal in those scenes).

And in what world of this "beauty standard" did the "monster" think they should make a public appearance when Elisabeth couldn't even drag her beautiful tush out for drinks? It doesn't make sense at all. Such a disappointment.

So many errors, so many poor choices, so many "pretend you don't have a brain" moments that I am still trying to understand why I finished watching it all. But then again I finish every single movie I watch because I'm weird like that and like to try to find some redeeming quality about everything I watch even when I shouldn't.

I think I'll go back to watching horror movies done by people who actually know what they're doing.

reviews.author: markgorman
reviews.body:
The botoxed Trout Pout is, in my view, a mistake. Rather than enhancing beauty it destroys natural allure.

In The Substance Coralie Fargeat applies so much botox to her movie that what emerges is a trout pout of cataclysmic proportions.

To say The Substance is extreme is an understatement of quite considerable proportions. It takes anything David Cronenberg ever thought of and squares it. Indeed in the third act the monster that emerges from this excess of body horror is worse than anything you can imagine. Take the dog in The Thing and cross breed it with John Merrick and you start to get an idea of what a vivid imagination, and outstanding special effects technicians, can create.

It's a tale about beauty and the desperate desire to retain it in the relentless face of aging. Demi Moore (Oscar-worthy) is a fading Jane Fondaesque fitness show presenter whom her station executive (a wonderfully OTT Dennis Quaid) wants to replace with a younger model (Margaret Qualley). The thing is Qualley is actually Moore, at least every other week.

She becomes so after Moore injects "The Substance" a yellow liquid that creates cell duplication and leads to Demi Moore giving birth to Qualley, through her back. This is the first body horror scene of many that ramps up throughout the movie's 140 minute run time.

Moore and Qualley become a sort of Jekyll and Hyde who quickly resent each other. Qualley for losing her spotlight, Moore for sacrificing her beauty. Thus begins an internal battle which neither wants to lose and both resent.

French female director, Coralie Fargeat, makes a movie that lampoons the male gaze by amplifying it to an extent that no male director could possibly get away with, other than in the porn industry, and in doing so lands her point emphatically.

All this makes it sound like we are talking about a ham-fisted "strategy on its sleeve' B Movie.

Anything but.

This is horror of the quality of The Shining, which is frequently referenced in the hallway carpet and the bloody lift scene.

In the final act the horror reaches its zenith and is actually quite comedic. A New Year's Eve TV spectacular, to which the great and the good are invited, becomes a blood-bath of uniquely epic proportions. Hollywood may actually have run out of fake blood.

Everything about this movie is brilliant. Everything, including the soundtrack by French electronic composer Raffertie, is perfect.

It's stunning and I hope it goes on to reap the praise it so richly deserves.

Bravo Coralie Fargeat. Bravo.

reviews.author: ailynncarrizales

reviews.author: dweston-38669
reviews.body:
I'll admit I was apprehensive about this Cannes screenplay winner as I was expecting a 'tick box exercise' of pretty much the entire back catalogue of previous 'body horror' and 'transgressive' horror/thrillers- the entire oeuvre of David Cronenberg, obviously his son Brandon, Brian Yuzna's cult classic Society, Titane, to the underseen Starry Eyes.

However, writer/ director Coralie Fargeat creates a pointed and deeply hilarious spotlight on the fickle and plastic world of showbiz, body image and the callow inescapable affliction of ageing. She wears her influences well yet creates a bold style of filmmaking .

She gets outstanding and brave full frontal performances out of Demi Moore and Margaret Qualley, with able support by over the top queasy and greasy Dennis Quid ( great to see him again, though has he had work done on his cheeks?) At 2hrs 20mins it is too long and it does have longueurs in the final third when it cuts back to the apartment when it should be building up the tension for the 'New Years Party' It's a film I'll remember and it's good to see it on the cinema screen with an audience (albeit small)

reviews.author: TheDanishMovie-Nerd
reviews.body:
The Substance is a daring and intense film that doesn't hold back. From the very beginning, it dives headfirst into its narrative, which is both a strength and a weakness. While the lack of character development left me wanting more, the film makes up for it with its sharp commentary and breathtaking visual style.

Demi Moore's performance is exceptional, particularly as the story escalates. The makeup and costume work are astonishing, creating a unique blend of body horror and striking imagery. By the third act, the film becomes unapologetically graphic and uncompromising, delivering a memorable and shocking finale.

The score deserves special mention for perfectly complementing the film's themes and aesthetic. While The Substance may not be for everyone, it's a provocative, stylish film that true cinephiles shouldn't miss.

reviews.author: CatDayAfternoon
reviews.body:
I'm not even a horror fan and the only reason I went to see this was because the aging starlet playing an aging starlet part intrigued me. I didn't really know much more about the film, I basically just wanted to see Demi Moore's performance and figured I'd probably end up walking out if it was something stupid but I've never been so enthralled by a film in a very long time. The run time is 2:20 but there it flies by, there isn't a single draggy scene, in fact it's the opposite.

Every second of the film is captivating and other than a couple of times I had to look away due to the gore, I never took my eyes off the screen, in fact it felt like I didn't even blink.

I don't want to give anything away but Demi Moore gives a tour-de-force performance and if she's not nominated for an Oscar it will be downright criminal. But the entire film is utterly brilliant and for what it sets out to achieve it's about as close to perfection as it could be.

I know there is some controversy over the ending but I don't know how you could end it any other way. The film one ups itself with each scene so it had to end with something extreme and it does.

The Substance is the best thing I have seen in years.

reviews.author: ffidan
reviews.body: It is a movie that offers a stunning and unforgettable visual feast and attracts attention with its acting. Especially Demi Moore's performance and the 'male dominant - female sex object' messages given by the film are impressive. However, the ending of the movie is a great disappointment; as if the director could not collect the story and tried to impress the audience by drowning it with effects. I think it takes the audience away from the atmosphere of the movie and gives an intense feeling of artificiality. In addition, the nudity scenes that feel unnecessary and excess are also disturbing. In general, despite a strong start, it was a production that had difficulty in bringing the end. Still, I liked the director's and screenwriter's feminist perspective.

reviews.author: npjsnape-1
reviews.body:
Well it hooked me from the start. Great style, cinematography was brilliant. The editing and score is very impressive.

Demi Moore is at her best in this, Quaid was also brilliant along with the young sparkle actress.

It was really heading towards being a phenomenal film, a masterpiece, then the ending started to unfold and that's where everything that came before was quickly washed away. Such a shame the director headed this way in the finale.

It just became a stupid bloodbath that did nothing for the film. It should have ended at least 20 minutes earlier.

I certainly won't watch it again as I thought I would before the final act.

reviews.author: angolasunshine
reviews.body: I saw movie with no idea how crazy it was. Wow Sure! "The Substance" is a captivating film that showcases stunning cinematography and powerful performances from Demi Moore and Daniel Quaid. The visual storytelling immerses the audience in its themes, enhancing the emotional depth of the narrative. While the acting is amazing , some viewers might find the level of nudity excessive, which could distract from the overall message of the film. Nonetheless, the chemistry between the leads and the film's aesthetic make it a memorable experience. It's a thought-provoking exploration of complex relationships, balanced by its striking visuals. Definitely future cult hit . Thanks to all cast and crew for a great ride 😊

reviews.author: mfshbx25
reviews.body:
It's three days since I've seen this film and I'm kind of dumbfounded why I'm still thinking about it.

Maybe it's because I keep thinking about a film that in the hands of either Cronenbergs would not end up with an ending that killed the meaning with over the top imagery of what the film initially intended.

Wait, now I know Darren Aronofsky would have done a great job. Maybe I'm just jaded about horror as literally meaning showing gore. There are so many ways of making a horror film without it ending up being like this.

Kudos to both Demi Moore and Margaret. Qualley for their acting and courage.

reviews.author: davidmagowan-32996
reviews.body: A silly, ott combination of body horror and black humour that doesn't work on any level as it's neither scary nor funny. A fading Hollywood star takes a mystery drug to rejuvenate her appearance and it doesn't go well to put it mildly. It starts out interesting then gets mired in ridiculous gore for the sake of it. Hardly any dialogue, no explanation as to what the substance is or any even attempt at character development. The camp overacting by the support cast seems intentional and is cringy. Like a cross between Death Becomes Her, The Fly and Dorian Grey... Except utterly juvenile and downright dumb. Avoid.

reviews.author: ThatManFromRio
reviews.body:
IN A NUTSHELL: Instantly forgettable?: No.

One watch or rewatchable?: One watch.

Waste of potential?: Yes.

Worth the money: Yes.

IN DETAIL: As of late, a couple of films finally dare to take risks again. The Substance definitely is one of them. Half of the experience is equivalent to visiting a strip club. The other half is like the nightmare of a butcher dreaming of being a surgeon. This film definitely earns its rating and doesn't play it safe and this is its strongest asset.

Story-wise it starts out nicely: simple but gripping. However, the film's story dribbles away in its second half and loses itself in visuals, brutal violence and gore-galore without delivering - as others pointed out here - substance. The film probably would have gained a lot more gravitas if it had decided to spend more time with the Demi Moore character and focus less on the (uninteresting) escapades and rise of the younger version. Furthermore, I think, it left a couple of interesting questions aside, such as whether Demi Moore's "Matrix Self" has mental access to the "Younger Self" or if the Younger Self is just a (younger) clone that lives its own life disconnected from the memory of the original version. Does Elisabeth Sparkle experience "the experience" of Sue? According to the decisions made by the characters in the film my hunch is: probably not. So then, where's the point of using the substance in the first place?

I personally went to see this film to see Demi Moore and although she has a lot of screen time and you do get to see A LOT of her, to me there was not enough character-wise. Her character's inner conflicts were dealt pretty superficially (I want to be young again - that's literally all) and that character could have gone places.

The film occasionally is uncertain what it wants to be. It slips into different fields at times (e.g.: horror, satire, parody, comedy). Some people in the theater laughed during moments that for sure were not intended to be funny. In general, there's a silly quality to it at times with over-the-top, stereotyped characters and caricaturization.

You won't get jump scares here though it does sent shivers down your spine occasionally from all that body horror and from the film not shying away to show what it wants to show.

The heavy-on-the-extreme-closeups-and-wide-shots-cinematography is beautifully done though the rhythm of it quickly becomes formulaic and predictable.

The music is - as every score these days - a bunch of atmospheric soundscapes. Effective but not memorable.

And then there are the many Stanley Kubrick drawbacks (among others: The Shining's carpet and bathroom & 2001's stargate sequence & "Also Sprach Zarathustra"). The question I had to ask myself repeatedly was "how do they add value to the movie?" I can't answer that question. The film would have had enough to stand on its own feet and all the Kubrick elements were done much more satisfyingly by the man himself.

All in all good fun at the movies with no higher redeeming qualities. 6/10.

MOVIES THAT "THE SUBSTANCE" INSPIRED ME TO WATCH AGAIN: Meet The Feebles (Peter Jackson).

The Fly (David Cronenberg).

reviews.author: ykjdh
reviews.body: Hard to explain what exam this is because it reminded me of Jeckyl and Hyde but had a little bit of The Fly from 1986 thrown in. A better version of yourself is what the premise is here but at what costs?? Vane 50 year old seeking to be a more glamorous person starts playing around with a new drug and likes the new her. Except the side effects are a whole lot of what she wasn't bargaining for. That's good for you because this ride is unlike anything I've seen. It's like the climb up the ladder to fame is something the central character here is willing to do anything for. The third act alone is worth watching especially with some of the best gory make up effects I haven't seen since Tom Savini. It's hard not to feel sorry for folks whose mission in life is fame and fortune. This is definitely a cautionary tale of be careful what you wish for.

reviews.author: pawlitta
reviews.body: Personally, I quite liked the movie, even for me who is a very greedy person with the subject of blood, organs, etc. The two main actresses acted perfectly, they achieved what they wanted to convey to the public, it gave me the feeling of horror and that they were having a really bad time! I recommend this movie to see just once, since well, it's very original and very cool, but I wouldn't watch it again because of the whole blood issue. I have to say that the special effects at the end of the movie seemed very fake to me in terms of makeup, blood, etc., since it was very obvious that they were masks and the blood was fake. In general, apart from what I have already said, I have no other complaints, take advantage and watch it.

reviews.author: sipangulerr
reviews.body: I really liked the perspective of the movie. It is an extraordinary transmission with a powerful message. Everything about the movie, in which the female body and the coercive judgments on it are wonderfully conveyed, was not entirely to my liking. For one thing, I can say that there were some illogical scenes. Especially in the last 30 minutes of the movie, it feels like it belongs to a completely different movie. Even though it took me a while to understand what the director was trying to say in these last 30 minutes, I understood it. In fact, I respected it. But these parts were illogical and disturbing for me. I think the movie should have ended earlier. So that we could get the message directly instead of trying to understand it from a place that forces logic.

reviews.author: OaterALMIGHTY
reviews.body:
This film relentlessly grabs hold of the audience and doesn't let go-it's brutal, visceral, and unapologetically cultish. Imagine "Limitless" but pushed far beyond its boundaries, breaking new ground in ways you wouldn't expect. It takes what's familiar and reinvents it in the most intense, jaw-dropping fashion.

At its core, *The Substance* offers profound reflections that can be easily interpreted, while still managing to feel deep and razor-sharp. It tackles themes that anyone could relate to, blending accessibility with thought-provoking depth in a way that cuts through, leaving a lasting impact.

Visually and sonically, this movie is a powerhouse. The cinematography, editing, and soundtrack all come together to create a cinematic experience that's both fresh and raw. From the very first scene to the last, the film pulls you in, making sure you're fully immersed.

It masterfully plays on a wide spectrum of fear and discomfort. It's not just terrifying-it's the kind of horror that forces you to confront it, even if you're tempted to watch with your eyes half-covered. Its visceral moments are guaranteed to make you squirm.

Overall, *The Substance* is an intense ride that doesn't compromise in any area. But fair warning: if you're not a fan of horror that goes all the way, this one's not for you. Those who can handle it, though, are in for one hell of a ride.

reviews.author: N-whymark
reviews.body: After hearing so much after this film was so eager and excited to watch it. Demi Moore is brillliant .. the cinematography is amazing . Full of colour and some great scenes .!the story is true to life . Getting old and fearing being ignored and left out and striving for perfection and beauty. And some going to huge lengths to achieve this . Personally I think the last 20 mins of the film lets it down. I love Blood and gore but think the last section was silly and cheaply made compared to the rest of the film. But I would still watch it again and think it's a great film . Fresh and new and well Worth a watch.

reviews.author: ChetXBuck
reviews.body: I saw this after Demi Moore won Best Actress at the Golden Globes. It's an amazingly dark, realistic (mostly), satire. Worth seeing for a variety of reasons. But beware, it's EXTREME Alien-like odd at the end. The first hour is a crisp 10/10 for story and satire. You believe it. The next 30 min are odd, but interesting. The last 20 minutes go deep into sci-fi. The first hour is worth the outrageous ending. Margaret Qualley is charming and fits her generational voice. Demi puts it all out there. She brings a lot of heart to this movie that reminds you to remain sane about vanity and respect what you have. It's also a lesson in self-love and self-hate. Very polished and slick, but the message is quite human. It will have an impact.

reviews.author: TheManWhoDoesThings
reviews.body:
I went into the Substance absolutely blind, which is something that I believed enhanced my viewing experience, and is also something that I would recommend all people who want to see this film do. Without getting to much into it, The Substance is a film that goes completely off the rails in the best way possible. There are some visuals in this movie, especially in the third act, that are so shocking that I won't be forgetting them any time soon.

Demi Moore's performance as Elizabeth Sparkle in this movie is perhaps the best of her entire career. Hearing her vocal delivery transform from calm to spiteful over the course of the film is scary. She masterfully uses body language and unconscious communication to express her character's personality during long stretches of runtime where she doesn't talk. Her character's frustrated outbursts have true raw emotion put into them and are genuinely disturbing to watch.

Margaret Qualley is also absolutely phenomenal in this film. She not only has the perfect beautiful complexion for her "Sue" character, but also has amazing acting chops. Hopefully this movie will get her more roles in the future. Dennis Quaid also gives a great performance as the perfect terrible boss in this movie.

The cinematography and sound design craft an extremely unsettling atmosphere, often zeroing on specific sensory details to unnerve the audience, which become much more grotesque and hard to watch/listen to as the film goes on. The prosthetic effects in this film are so well-done that watching the various body mutilations in this film will make you cringe your teeth (in a good way).

The tone is a perfect balance of pitch black comedy and serious dramatic character development. For a movie that has a 2 hour+ runtime, this film never feels boring and it actually makes the most of its time to carefully craft a thoroughly disturbing narrative. The third act of this film, as mentioned earlier, goes to extreme places, some of which could disgust even David Cronenberg himself.

With amazing performances, masterful scene crafting, and top tier body horror, this film is certainly one with a lot of "substance".

reviews.author: roidaniduff
reviews.body: Loved the Idea ! It definitely kept me on the edge of my seat and must say , perfect energy and excitement flow through out the movie The Last 30 Min was what i was expecting to be the BOOM of the whole Movie But ... Left disappointed For sure disgusting and Bloody enough But Very disconnecting to How the first half felt First half Felt Real to me , Even though its an idea far off from real but at least i could feel Attention to the Story and it made sense But the last 30Min ... felt like a kid started writing it ... maybe i missed the message But as A viewer It left me Disappointed while the first half was Mind blowing.

reviews.author: theknownames
reviews.body:
There are fewer and fewer opportunities for shared experiences in this digital world. A night out at the movies has been replaced, more often, with home viewing . However, seeing this movie in a theater, in the company of strangers, reminds us what cinema is all about.

The runtime flew by. The laughter, gasps, and applause reminded me of the reasons why going to a movie has remained an American past time and how we still actual need people around to experience a film more profoundly.

The theatre could have hosted an after party for attendees to process what they witnessed.

The parking lot time that was , may indeed make a comeback.

The movie was complex, layered, shocking, honest and raw. The cinematography was stunning and the acting exceptional ( not to mention the effects being visceral and poignant)

Horror is often divisive making it difficult to discern ratings. I doubt this will be an exception.

reviews.author: bugsycline
reviews.body:
I saw "The Substance" today at my local theater. Essays can and will be written about this film for decades to come. The Essays will be written by wannabe filmmakers, Feminists, Anti-Consumer activists, And sloggy 80's B-Movie gross-out film fans.

Honestly, I've never seen anything quite like it. Everything you may have heard about this movie is true, and then some.

Its a Sci-Fi, Horror, Drama, Social Commentary, and Creature Feature B-Movie all in one.

The positives.

1. It is stunningly beautiful and simultaneously disgusting to look at.

2. Much of the film's visuals will recall The Shinning, 2001 a Space Oddesy, David Cronenberg and The 80's B-movie The Toxic Avenger.

3. The message about the horrors of self-image in the plastic world of Hollywood are intense and deep, for a film low in dialog.

4. Demi Moore gives the best performance of her entire career. One that is insanely personal and intimate. Almost entirely physical as the dialog is empty and surface.

5. Margaret Qualley performs her most shallow and sinister character to date, while simultaneously being the most strikingly perfect human ever to be photographed.

6. co-produced, written and directed by Coralie Fargeat. Who is a master at 4 genres at the same time, while blending them together.

7. When its all said and done, the film reminds you, this is a movie and not to take it all too seriously. I expected half way through that by the time this movie was over, I would feel bad and it would be a huge downer of my day. But the (secret) last 20 minutes takes such a dreadful and terrible situation and lets the audience laugh and reminds them, It's just a movie... The people who made it were obviously having fun doing a craft (practical effects) that is almost entirely gone for the industry.

Shot on a shoestring budget of under $18m it continues to be another recent film entry that proves it doesn't take Half a Billion Dollars to make great cinema. It only takes love, passion for the art and someone with a story to tell.

Negatives... 1. It will be impossible for this to reach mass appeal. For many reasons. Yes the surface is shockingly gross to look at, But it also has some seriolusly stark and beautiful cinematography.

2. the profound message might turn away people who see women as Trophies or Smiling objectified body parts for consumer consumption. The female-hating RIght WIng of American society will have many problems with this film.

3. This ain't Forrest Gump.... You won't have a lot of great positive feelings leaving the theater. But you will think about the movie for days afterward.

4. While every woman should see this film, Maybe it might be better to take little 12 year old Suzy to go see a Disney movie instead of this.... This movie will mess up up inside your brain. Don't subject kids to that.

5. The dialog in the first 1 hour could have been a little less sparse to match the world class visuals. I think if maybe the "Science" of teh Substance was discussed just a tad more, it would have put this movie in the 9's instead of the low 8's

Over all a great time at the movies, One that makes you want to discuss what you just witnesssed. As once seen, it can't be unseen. And its likely you will never forget some of the imagery for years to come.... 8.1 out of 10 stars (monster Score for a monster movie) One of the Best Horror movies I've seen in a Long long long time.

Ps... Somewhere I hear the sounds of 80s B-Movie fans/nerds cheering like The Substance is the second coming of Troma Entertainment and Lloyd Kaufman.

The Substance is what you get when you mix The Shining, The Handmaid's Tale and The Toxic Avenger all into one film.

reviews.author: the-unknwn
reviews.body:
The story revolves around a famous actress and TV host, Elizabeth Sparkle, who starts to feel uncomfortable in her own body due to aging and the studio's desire to replace her with a younger woman. These circumstances make her consider an offer she received-a way to become a younger and better version of herself. She decides to take it, leading to a series of wild and chaotic events.

The message this work aims to convey is the flawed beauty standards that are prevalent in today's society and how they push some women to commit harmful acts against their bodies, resorting to cosmetic surgeries in an attempt to look younger and more beautiful. It emphasizes how beauty standards are constantly changing and how women are under immense pressure from societal judgment and preconceived notions. It also addresses the inappropriate treatment of women who reach a certain age, and how society contributes to their feelings of depression by altering the way they are perceived.

There are brilliant scenes that capture the reality of celebrities, like the symbolic depiction of a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame deteriorating over time, representing the rise and fall of fame. Another powerful scene features a fly falling into a glass of drink, as if to convey the message that she has reached a point where she is nothing more than a lowly, drowning insect that no one cares about.

The concept is beautiful, and the cinematography is excellent, but the issue lies in how the story unfolds towards the end. The pacing becomes rushed, and the resolution feels lacking. A better, more logical, and realistic conclusion could have been reached.

reviews.author: LAHegarty
reviews.body: It started off strong, with a beginning reminiscent of Death Becomes Her (great film), but it became progressively unwatchable. Two people walked out of the cinema around 25 minutes in, which, ironically, was during the film's more tolerable moments. The last 15 to 20 minutes were entirely unnecessary-it should have ended well before that final stretch. The message lacked subtlety or nuance, resulting in a weak film that will quickly be forgotten. The current rating of 8.1 here is likely to drop substantially over the next year or so. Overall, it's just a dull experience, and one I wouldn't recommend wasting your time on.

reviews.author: kmkevinn-66699
reviews.body:
THE SUBSTANCE is a modern horror film that wholly lives up to it's promise and its premise. It's beautifully grotesque in all the right ways, with such bold artistic confidence on display that feels as if its creators had full control of this project - a singular, focused vision. This is a film i wager many will love, and just as many will reject, as it is definitely an acquired taste, but i feel it's destined to become a cult horror classic.

This was probably the most intense film me and the wife watched in quite some time. Never seen anything like it. Went without watching the trailer so was completely caught off guard. There is VERY close up nude scenes throughout out the entire film so just a heads up and can be quite grotesque at times. I love the meaning behind it and the artsiness. There was never a dull moment and demi moore killed it like always! I don't think I noticed any propaganda or lgbtq being forced as well.. We all are going to get old one day and we should embrace the beauty that comes with that before we let our insecurities/struggles of living in the pass kill us instead of staying in the moment living/enjoying our life. That is what I personally took from this film. Definitely worth a watch in theaters as I think the big screen made it even more visually intense.

reviews.author: a-j-kelly
reviews.body:
Before reading the rest of this review, there is one thing you need to know: if you are a casual moviegoer, this movie is not for you! You are almost guaranteed to hate this movie unless you watch experimental, boundary-pushing films often. If you need a movie this weekend, watch "Transformers One" or "Never Let Go," or rewatch "Beetlejuice Beetlejuice" and "Deadpool & Wolverine" for the second time. "The Substance" is a film you need to know what you are getting into, and if you are just casually checking it out, you went to see the wrong movie. Please heed my warning and proceed with caution. Let's now get to the review.

I wanted to see this film for two reasons. First, the news of MUBI's acquisition of the film brought it to my attention. The synopsis sounded interesting, and the trailers further intrigued me. Second, Margaret Qualley. "Sanctuary" and "Drive-Away Dolls" proved that she was an actress to pay attention to, and supporting roles in Yorgos Lanthimos' "Poor Things" and "Kinds of Kindness" further showed her talents. Also, did you know she was in Quentin Tarantino's "Once Upon a Time...in Hollywood," and I didn't notice until "Sanctuary" came out, maybe later? Those two reasons guaranteed me seeing it from the get-go, and I'm happy to say this experience did not disappoint.

To start, Margaret Qualley was fantastic as Sue, the younger counterpart to Demi Moore's Elisabeth. Her obsession and determination with fame and perfection were gripping, and you are always curious as to whether she will pay attention to the rules related to The Substance that gave her this youth in the first place.

Next, Demi Moore was also phenomenal. I haven't seen that many films starring her, just her appearances in "The Unbearable Weight of Massive Talent," "Austin Powers in Goldmember," and "Charlie's Angels: Full Throttle." "The Substance" was her comeback film, and even though I don't know her acting range beyond this, her portrayal of Elisabeth, the actress looking to reclaim her past success, is remarkable. When she learns of The Substance, she would, of course, be eager for a second chance, even with the life-affecting costs associated with it.

I also thought Dennis Quaid's brief role as Harvey, a snarky, egocentric executive who turns away Elisabeth because of her age, was solid. His performance showcases the film's message: how aspirations to be perfect are harmful and dangerous and can lead to someone doing incredibly unsafe things. It also represents a realistic mechanism the entertainment industry uses: sex sells. It is screwed up but true, and this film perfectly showcases it.

Additionally, the film's direction was stellar. It reminded me a lot of the direction of the film "Revenge" from 2018, so imagine my shock when, after the movie, I found out "Revenge" director Coralie Fargeat made it. If you need further comparison, imagine "Revenge" but with more focus on sex appeal. I can comfortably say Fargeat has outdone herself with this film!

I also appreciated the practical effects, which were both disgusting - intentionally so - and beautiful. I won't say which scene since it would be a spoiler, but you'll see once (or if) you see it.

If I were to give any semi-negatives at all, the ending does drag but also contributes to the film's messaging. I don't want to say it's terrible because it isn't. It just manages to be more over-the-top and goofy than the rest of the movie, so be warned.

In conclusion, "The Substance" was everything I was expecting it to be and more, except the best movie of the year. The dangers of high expectations rear their head again for me, as "Beetlejuice Beetlejuice" was ruined by that. The ending is my main complaint, which prevented me from loving it more than I did, but I loved it nonetheless.

For the technical score, potentially career-best performances from the entire cast, amazing practical effects, intense editing, and fantastic atmosphere add up to the score being a 10/10.

It's hard to determine the enjoyment score since I look for movies like these, but casual moviegoers don't. If I were to guess, casual moviegoers would rate this a 4/10 since it is weird and unexpectedly unique. Again, if you actively look for these types of movies, this is absolutely for you. "The Substance" was a 10/10 experience for people like us and more than worth watching!

UPDATE 9/24/2024: I want to apologize. It has been two days since I've seen "The Substance" and had written my review, to which I said prior that it wasn't the year's best film. Again, the ending somewhat perplexed me with its goofiness. However, after two days of thinking of this film constantly, realizing that despite being goofy, the ending is appropriate for the movie at hand, and how wrong it felt to say "Boy Kills World" is better solely on the fact that the ending surprised me (check my 2024 Movies RANKED IMDb list), I can comfortably say my opinion has changed. "The Substance" is the best film of the year so far, and I'm proud to say that. Sorry I led you to believe the past two days that it wasn't the best film out there, but again, I haven't been able to take it off my mind. A film that does that deserves credit!

reviews.author: george.schmidt
reviews.body: THE SUBSTANCE (2024) ***1/2 Demi Moore, Margaret Qualley, Dennis Quaid, (voice of Yann Bean). Moore delivers a career high, Oscar-worthy performance as an aging actress who faces being obsolete when she's bounced from her TV gig as an aerobics personality and discovers a new way of reviving her career in the titular, unknown source which results in birthing her younger, sexier 'self' (Qualley equally giving it her all) who takes up residence at her home while eventually replacing her on air. Filmmaker Coralie Fargeat crafts a truly horrifying sci-fi/body horror fable of be careful what you wish for with elements meets the trope of the doppelgänger mixing everything from FRANKENSTEIN to CARRIE to THE SHINING to DR. JEKYLL & MR. HYDE to THE FLY to THE THING yet making a miasma of it all in a high-octane cocktail of signing your soul to the Devil and getting more than one bargained for with pure dread resulting in a final, blood-drenched, gore-fest act of redemption of sorts. Quaid defines toxic masculinity to the nth degree as the programmer whose presence of being vile, vulgar and outrageous to the hilt resembling an over-ripe pumpkin about to burst its rind. Shocking and surprisingly poignant underscoring how female bodies are exploited by society's mores and ultimately what it means to be human. The synth sinister score by Raffertie & the jaw-dropping practical make-up/visual effects by Oscar Afonso and his team are worth the price of admission alone. One of the year's absolute best films. A must see.

reviews.author: watashinokokoronitenko
reviews.body: I think this will remind a lot of people of Refn's The Neon Demon. This is not body horror, more like psychedelic pop arthouse. Carefully! Lots of blood and internal organs outside the bodies. There is a little suspense, and if anyone has seen people die from cancer, then this film will have special associations for them. Some moments really make you panic, and an existential crisis permeates the entire film. But at the same time, I think it could have been done better. There's no need to flirt with the pop industry, especially when you're doing something outside of it. Oh yes, still, it's better not to watch this with popcorn.

reviews.author: fredrikgunerius
reviews.body: French filmmaker Coralie Fargeat (Revenge) is the woman behind this profound dive into the body horror subgenre, with a considerable satirical edge. Demi Moore gives a hauntingly bold performance as Elisabeth Sparkle, a faded 50-year-old film star who, in her struggle to still feel relevant and youthful, accepts an enticing offer from a black market supplier: a serum that promises to transform her into a younger, better, and more beautiful version of herself. The poised and enticingly structured build-up is the mark of a filmmaker with a clear and detailed vision. And although The Substance stands on the shoulders of a number of giants, it does so with confidence as the new torchbearer. Fargeat's tone is sharp, witty, and cold, and the film finds its footing as a curious cross between Cronenberg, The Shining, Frankenheimer's Seconds and Peter Gabriel's "The Barry Williams Show". The interplay between Moore and Margaret Qualley as her younger, idealised self encompasses a range of conflicts that will be recognisable for anyone who has experienced the loss of youth, even if Fargeat seems to think that it's mostly valid for women - and more specifically, women who are famous for their looks. Only towards the very end does the film run out of novel ideas and end up turning somewhat desperately to well-worn visual and thematic tropes in order to wrap things up. The suggestive score is by British electronic music composer Raffertie.

reviews.author: jorgesosadiaz
reviews.body:
Impressive.

As time goes by, we change but we are not someone else; we remain ourselves. And when we force the creation of a new identity to distance ourselves from the one we despise, it's an illusion, because the more we reject it, the less we care about hurting ourselves. The attention we want to maintain slowly devours us. Little by little, we transform into a monster that at first can hide behind a mask, but eventually, it emerges. There comes a point of such dissociation that we end up harming ourselves without even being aware of it.

There is no better version of us, we are always just ourselves. We must accept who we are; we should not define ourselves in relation to others' perceptions. We cannot become slaves to a past memory or seek to maintain an addiction to relevance out of fear of being alone.

reviews.author: Alexander_Blanchett
reviews.body: What a ride. One crazy mind f..... with a Lynchian twist. It was extremely stylish and original. Actually one of the most original films of recent time, if you look at it in total. There are scenes, ankles and twists that you have never encountered on screen before. It was brave in many ways and I applaud writer and director Coralie Fargeat for that. And of course Demi Moore. What.a.brave.turn! Its really something you would never had expected her to do or see her in. Its not only her best career best performance but Demi Moore also proved how she can disclosure herself not only physically but also emotionally. I am not sure if she will be respected during awards season, as this film will really divide the voters but she surely deserves to. And then there is a fantastic turn by Dennis Quaid. His character does not add a whole lot to the film, except being the embodied chauvinism which is one of the pillars the film criticizes, but what a performance. Many might call it over the top or a charicature or parody. But comparing to Quaids usually track record he really went out of his comfort zone with that and delivered one of the best supporting performances I have seen all year so far. Marageret Qualley was also fine and once again proves her status as one of the nest best things. I loved the cinematography and editing which was superb. The general look and growing uncomfortable feel was awesome. Really a new kind of movie - with a strong criticism on the worlds obsession with youth and beauty but also a film with a very simple moral: ALWAYS follow the rules....

reviews.author: davidallenxyz
reviews.body:
Watching The Substance is an intense experience.

It's told in three acts. The first act sees Elisabeth Sparkle (Demi Moore) getting pushed out of the limelight solely because she is over 50, dreaming of staying relevant, and being introduced to the mysterious "Substance" that will give her access to youth again as long as she follows some strict rules.

The second act sees the ascendance of her younger self, known only as Sue (Margaret Qualley), as she takes the media by storm.

The third act is completely mental and any attempt to describe it would spoil the fun. One thing is for sure - you'll need a strong stomach to get through it.

Moore is fantastic - bravely exploring the fragility of being an older woman in a world obsessed with appearances. Qualley also puts in a strong performance, adding a knowing, playful streak to the hyper-sexualisation of her character. Dennis Quaid is hilariously over the top as a sleazy TV producer.

The visuals, sound design and special effects combine to create a slick, stylised world with a heavy dose of body horror.

The third act might be divisive. Certainly you could argue that is goes too far. But you can barely take your eyes away from whats happening.

I don't remember a film prompting so many conversations between audience members after it ended. If you are brave enough, go and experience it for yourself.

reviews.author: davedroid07
reviews.body: The underlying & not so occult message of this movie was disturbing. It's a multilayered movie that explores several themes. At the lowest ( and most graphic level) is the faustian bargain of the trade of her physical body to extend her career. At the psychological level there is a schism between her somewhat true self and her false/narcissistic self. Then at the esoteric level we are asked the questioned of what did she lose/gain at a spiritual & soul level ' to reach for the stars'. Matthew 16:26 comes to mind 'What will if profit a man/woman if they forfeit their soul?'. A thoughtful movie of about Holywood & celebrity culture that truly makes us think what a lot of these 'stars' sacrficised to get where they are.

reviews.author: qhfnwfxju
reviews.body:
The Substance" is a film that starts with a promising premise, delving into the pressures of Hollywood and the lengths women will go to maintain their youth. The first two acts are compelling, with strong performances from Demi Moore and Margaret Qualley, particularly Moore's portrayal of a desperate actress clinging to her fading relevance.

However, the film takes a drastic turn in the final 30 minutes, veering into a surreal and over-the-top territory that doesn't align with the previously established tone. The descent into body horror and fantastical elements feels jarring and disrupts the film's momentum. While some might find this unexpected twist intriguing, it ultimately undermines the film's core themes and leaves the viewer feeling unsatisfied.

Despite its flaws, "The Substance" is still worth watching for Moore's powerful performance and its insightful commentary on aging and the entertainment industry. Just be prepared for a wild and somewhat disappointing ride in the final stretch.

reviews.author: Eclyse88
reviews.body: I just saw "The Substance" in theaters and it was incredibly weird and bizarre. I loved every minute of it, this is what the world needs more of. Holy hell was it an amazingly wild ride! Massive Cronenberg influence here from Coralie Fargeat, in the best way possible. Really dope movie if you're into the weird side of horror. All 3 main actors killed it, it has an atmospheric immersing sound design and the practical effects team needs an award.
