reviews.author: movieoperator
reviews.body: Well acted, perfect and snappy editing with great close-ups and make-up. Good supporting music score and great sound design that emphasizes the intensity of the movies most tense scenes (and there's a lot of them). Best horror movie in years. I saw it last night and it will stick to your mind for a long time. And it actually carries an important message about the ridiculous beauty standards in the entertainment industry. Even better than most Cronenberg films and that says a lot. Respect for both actresses Moore and Qualley for their outstanding and intense performances. Altough it's a gruesome horror movie it also made me laugh quite often. Fargeat is a director that I will certainly be watching closely in the future.

reviews.author: andre_apt
reviews.body:
There are three good things that can be said about this film: its 2.5 hours fly, it's definitely better than Fargeat's Revenge, and it's not meant for kids for a change. Everything else, however...

Have you seen that TV spot where audiences react to The Substance's most shocking moments? On watching the film you might wonder if they weren't just reacting to its abysmal concept, premise, and plot holes. Lots of things can be accepted within the parameters of a satirical parable -- or any parable, for that matter -- but its underlying idea and basic structure should still be there and make sense. Which is simply not the case here. To keep it short, here is just one illustration. Take a closer look at this affair Moore's character gets involved in, which, by the way, is repeatedly referred to as the "experience". Since those "new improved versions" (basically, clones) are neither avatars for the matrices' consciousness nor even ostensibly act on their behalf (like in Billy Wilder's Fedora that ventures into neighbouring thematic territories), there is no experience there whatsoever for the matrix versions, no benefits at all even on paper. At the same time, there are massive dangers that inevitably realise. So why would anyone want to sign up for anything like this? How could they wind up maniacally clinging to this arrangement having already been burnt? What's supposed to become the very foundation of the whole piece doesn't seem to make any sense. But the thing is, even if read in purely metaphorical terms, the premise is still null and void. Unless, of course, you are prepared to unquestioningly embrace the notion that all this youth/beauty psychosis is entirely on society. The rest of the writing is pretty much on the same level. And this kind of intellectual sloppiness is miles away not only from the sheer brilliance of something like South Park with its wildly imaginative, but immaculately structured and always right on the money grotesques, but even from any competently done average stuff. Fargeat's directing is better than her writing, but it's also overtly derivative. However, the audiences are indeed in for some experience here. Because all the film's 'little' flaws are unabashedly driven into the background by its shock value bonanza. And how that is gonna be perceived will probably depend on your cinematic history, aesthetic preferences, an amount of art-related knowledge under your belt, and the contents of your dinner in some cases...

All in all, this movie can be described as not a very original (Refn's Neon Demon, for example, explored similar subjects using similar means eight years ago and did it much better) and not very well thought-out instance of arty grindhouse that not quite successfully aspires to be poignant social satire. But if you ignore this ridiculous gushing over the "adacity" of the barely existing substance of The Substance on the part of the critics, lower your expectations, and decide that you are just after entertaining yourself for a couple of hours in all sorts of stranger ways, it may be moderate fun...

reviews.author: Hamstervert
reviews.body:
There was good stuff in the film. But it might have worked better as a music video, and been released 20 years ago. I was most offended that this was saying nothing new, and also seemed to be outdated. I don't think that attitude to age and bodies is quite right, we are now in the midst of a big transformation about bodies, gender, sexuality. This is archaic... but the first 30 minutes was really good, but then it lost any coherence and the characters were so vapid and as a result the body horror ended up being unimpressive as it was just too distant from meaning.

I think in part it is a smidge of Sunset Boulevard, and Possession crossed with the Fly... and there lies the issue. Nothing original in here. I thought all the actors were very good though, but they weren't done justice in the final product, and the audience wasn't respected.

reviews.author: ahmedfaragahmed
reviews.body:
Review of the film "The Substance" (2024)

The film won the Best Screenplay award at this year's Cannes Film Festival. It is directed by Coralie Fargeat and stars Demi Moore, Margaret Qualley, and Dennis Quaid. The story follows a celebrity who is fired from her popular TV show by the producer because she has aged, and they want younger talent. She then receives a message by chance about a mysterious product that helps people change their appearance and age, making them look younger and more beautiful.

The concept might seem fairly familiar, as it's not entirely new, but what makes this film truly good is the way the idea is presented. On the surface, the story seems ordinary, but within the film lies another world-a world filled with gory horror, psychological pain, and a presentation that is both intriguing and controversial.

The direction is very impressive. The film does not stick to a single theme or style; rather, it is visually diverse, shifting from stunning shots to mesmerizing symmetry with the use of colors through the film's set design rather than just editing.

The acting performances are remarkable. Demi Moore delivers a powerful and, at times, harsh performance, effectively portraying two different states: in the first act, a character trying to stay strong, and in the second act, her descent into a state of breakdown and self-loathing. As for the young actress Margaret Qualley, she is a winning bet as a future star. Her role almost outshines Demi Moore, offering a captivating performance. She plays the youthful version, full of vitality and arrogance, using her beauty to succeed.

The screenplay is the film's strongest aspect. From the first act, the theme is clear: the struggle of stars to maintain their youth at any cost. It is not a fictional story but a bitter reality that we witness among film stars, especially actresses who undergo excessive cosmetic procedures to maintain a younger appearance. This pressure stems from the demands of production companies and greedy producers, driven by society's standards. This obsession forces them to alter themselves to the point of becoming unrecognizable. The film successfully portrays the torment of artists obsessed with eternal beauty, which takes a toll on their lives, and it presents this struggle in a brilliant way.

However, there are two issues. The first is the lack of clarity in some moments regarding the rules and limitations of using the product, which was explained too quickly, leaving the audience to assume things. Additionally, it's unclear how the other character could live without an identity, as if production companies would accept them without any proof or identity, as though they were ghosts. The second issue, which isn't necessarily a flaw, is the ending. The film starts as a deeply artistic drama, but the problem lies in the fact that it ends in a genre that doesn't entirely match the type of film it started as-in simpler terms:

"The film starts with one genre and ends with another."

To clarify, the ending is good but seems suited for a different type of film. While the story begins as a psychological drama, it ends more like a gory horror movie. Although the ending is well-done, it could have concluded in a more dramatic way.

In conclusion, the film is truly remarkable in terms of its concept, storytelling, and performances, which makes the entire experience enjoyable. However, be warned that the film is extremely graphic and gory, making it not recommended if you're uncomfortable with visually intense content.

My rating for this film is 8.5/10.

reviews.author: ronwinnick
reviews.body:
This movie is Totally Insane & Bonkers!

It's like, Oh, you think This is crazy?... Well, how about THIS?!?

The Substance, shows its audience just how insane the world of showbiz is, in particular Women... In showbiz the "window of opportunity & acceptability" is not very long, especially for women!

And in the way of Dark Comedy, it reveals the desperation & insanity, someone may go through, just to try & stretch that "window of opportunity", a little bit longer... What you will see is absolutely movie madness, that makes the early works of John Waters, look like a visit to Mr. Roger's Neighborhood!

This is a complete story, that is, it ends, exactly where it begins!

The story focuses on the desparation an actress goes through when she suddenly realizes that she is now too old and no longer considered beautiful or relevant.

What will she do? What can she do?

Her world is about to quickly unravel and as she realizes this, she's ready to do anything she can to change the course of...nature... After a car accident, she is made aware of something called "The Substanqe", that just might be the answer she is looking for... but like all things that are "too good to be true"...there are Always strict rules, that must must be followed exactly or you'll pay the consequences... The important thing to remember though is, whatever The Substance makes you, IT'S STILL YOU!

And You Have to follow The Instructions exactly or you will pay the price!

The decision is yours and the price you pay could be a little inconvenience or... who knows?

Of course, what happens is nightmarish!

The movie is shot in ways that expose the audience to the ugliness and cruelty of "show business", as it is, to women... Your "usefulness" & relivane is only, as long, as you are "Pretty".

Just remember, "to Smile! A Pretty Girl Should ALWAYS Smile!" The Substance is absolutely crazy and has touches of Stanley Kubrick and David Cronenberg!

It is extreme and just when you think you've seen it all...the film goes Further!

If you're a Fan of Great Film Making and Storytelling, you will Love "The Substance!"

reviews.author: Ramon-V-M
reviews.body: I really loved this movie! You can tell they took a lot of creative liberties, which made it something very interesting, terrifying, and artistic. I also loved the simplicity with which the story is told. The cinematography and the focus on small details in objects, acts, and animals, like in the first sequence with the fly, were also aspects that draw you even more into the story. Also, it inevitably left me reflecting on various themes, including some personal ones. Without a doubt, as the days go by and I watch it a few more times, I will be able to catch more messages the movie has. Personally, it touched on sensitive themes such as how each person perceives "success" and "ambition," things that are present in all of us in one way or another. Other themes include "decline" and old age, which can undoubtedly terrify us or even cause panic, especially as we see them approaching in our lives. I also believe that one of the main messages of the movie is the mistake of trying to find answers to all these life problems with quick fixes that only lead to more issues. Additionally, the desire to achieve happiness and fulfillment in our lives according to our own rules or to combat the injustices we face as if we had some special power to make everything right.

reviews.author: snavej
reviews.body:
To begin with, the positives. The acting was excellent all round. The locations and sets were fantastic and appropriate. The motivation was all too real and powerful, with famous people and aspiring stars wanting to be perennially attractive and popular. The desperation was extreme. I often thought 'surely she wouldn't!' but she did. The theme was pushed to a very final conclusion.

Unfortunately, the writer(s) didn't always consider the practicalities. There were at least two characters who were often in comatose states. Those needed to have proper care. They should have been in bed and nursed constantly. Their major wounds should have been closed surgically, not with ordinary nylon string! There should have been regular disinfection. They would've needed blood transfusions. I work in a medical library, so this gory fiasco was ridiculous to me.

reviews.author: mpflipper-459-115255
reviews.body:
The movie itself wasn't all that bad... only the last 15 minutes are horrible. I wish I would have walked out just before that.

The movie gives a great insight into our society and it's silly beauty requirements, how a female tv show host is over the hill once she's 50 and on the other hand a male presenter in his 60's gets loads of praises.

And the lengths some people are willing to go to, to live upto the stupid expectations of others. Instead of living your own best life.

Off all the endings they could have come up with, this was the absolute worst imaginable!!!

Sorry this sucks a lot !!

reviews.author: stellaamanuel
reviews.body:
Never have I ever written a review before but this movie intrigued me & captured my attention in a way that I have never anticipated. It's mind boggling & jaw dropping. On one hand it gave me chills on the spine, yet the message it conveyed is one of a kind. The best version of you is, You alone. So, don't you ever try to intrude in God's workmanship & try to bring alterations to your precious self. God creates originals not duplicate carbon copies. Don't overwork yourself trying to be a beauty limelight. In a world where women are foisted to be someone they are not, this movie is an apt message. It's an impetus for every woman out there that even their carrier isn't a platform to flaunt a bogus version of themselves. Be you even at the expense of your profession.

The storyline was convincing & consistent. It was flawless & even hyperbolic scenes were credible.

reviews.author: lffonseca-1
reviews.body:
A really good, original and impactful film for 80% of it's length that's ruined by an incredibly excessive ending that ramps up everything to 200%. Way too much and surprisingly very poorly executed from a special effects standpoint, considering the impeccable visual quality of the rest of the film.

It's like you're watching a film wrote and made by an exceptional team until you get to the ending chapter and then a B-film team took over. Very frustrating and disappointing, could've easily been an absolute classic.

Still great performance by Demi Moore and Denis Quaid as well from the rest of the cast.

reviews.author: andrewmarshall-06163
reviews.body: This movie is without question the worst movie I've ever seen, and I've seen a lot of really bad movies. If this is the depths to which previously well regarded actors Dennis Quaid and Demi Moore have stooped, I feel for them. The fact that it has received so many very high ratings is perhaps an indication of just how depraved our world has become. To attempt to justify this garbage as satire or some pithy statement on the beauty within a person is grappling for positives. It started very badly and just continued to spiral further and further downhill. I kept thinking "it can't get any worse", only to be proven wrong time after time. The actors, writers and director ought to have a long hard look at themselves in the mirror. Absolutely awful in every respect.

reviews.body:

I mean if you're into that and want to see Demi Moore & Margaret Qualley nude this is a definite must watch for you. Plus Margaret Qualley twerks so like I can't not give this a 10/10.

reviews.author: djcolzz
reviews.body:
I don't understand the big excitement about this film. It's one of the most unusual, eerie (not in a good way), and perplexing films you've ever seen.

It's quite vibrant. Excellently directed. Demi Moore is a fantastic in this, yet not my favourite actor.

What kind of brain truly comes up with this is left to question. The story you may read above. It may be worth seeing, but definitely a one and done kind of movie.

Nice air brushing on Demi mind you.

It's not a horror film; there are no jump scares, blood, or moments where you have to hold your breath, but you watch it with an inquisitive curiosity about where it's headed, and when the climax comes, you're like, "what???"

More a psychological thriller, cinema noir. It does have a grotesque element. Though not in David Lynch's level, I would say there are some fans participating.

It's obvious that the lesson is to accept who you are, your imperfections, and the inevitable ageing process, but it's strange and only gets stranger.

It evokes the spirit of an 80s cult film.

reviews.author: lauramoolenaar
reviews.body:
To start: Moore and Qualley were amazing in this. I cannot imagine any other actress duo pulling this of as they did.

The story is a bit familiar in it's broad strokes: woman ages and no longer meets society's beauty standards, but in comes a 'solution' to make her regain her glory days. Of course, you can already tell from the beginning what sort of things will go wrong.

This is absolutely fine, the gore in this movie actually helps set it apart in that it really shows what is at stake and how far the characters are willing to go. I found the gore very functional in that way and thought it added to the story, though my viewing did have a few walk-outs from people who were less comfortable. It definitely checks the body horror mark, so keep that in mind.

It was only towards the end that the gore started getting gratuitous. Without spoiling anything: it is very obvious while watching that this was a very conscious choice by the creators. However, for me it kind of made it comical and killed the (assumed) intention that had been built up. In my opinion: if the story ended earlier, it would have been far more impactful.

reviews.author: griffithxjohnson
reviews.body:
Glamorous & disgusting. A very creative screenplay with deep themes of beauty. Really sharp editing, score, & makeup. It leans into the concept hard but ends a little heavy handed. Yet it achieved its goal of making me squirm.

reviews.author: r_manmdy
reviews.body:
Well, that sure was omething different by today's standards in Hollywood. The story has a nice build up, but you can already guess where it's going once the problems get started..And once it's started , it becomes what you've hoped for. And even some more. Comedically and grotesque body horror. I find it a mix between Society and Death Becomes Her. With some nods even to Kubrick and Cronenberg in some scènes.

But winner best scenario? I find that a bit much for something like this. An award for (practical) fx should be more in place.

All in all, the 2 main lead characters do a great job. Especially Demi Moore.

Dennis Quaid is sleazy and horrible, but funny.

Camera and editing are creative.

But the story hasn't got much to it. If you don't know what to expect it can be a surprise. I think that's what this movie hopes for.

reviews.author: ariellis
reviews.body: I only wish it had ended 30 minutes sooner. It would have been the movie of the decade had someone not lost their mind and absolutely demolished the ending. The point had been made, the meaning heard and understood clearly and beautifully, and bad writing and costume and makeup and special effects just blew the whole thing up. Like the budget got lost in the end. I couldn't believe what they decided to do with what was such a masterpiece. I feel tricked. I wish I had read the other reviews and cut the last 30 off so I could enjoy what a wonderful movie the first hour and a half was. I should have stopped. Which is ironic.

reviews.author: melcher-2001
reviews.body:
'Essential', 'Unforgettable', 'Body Horror Classic', 'Feminist Cult Classic', 'Dark Comedy', are some of the quotes being thrown around about 'The Substance', a new film by Coralie Fargeat, starring Demi Moore. The best description I've seen is the line in the teaser from New York Magazine, "An enraged scream in cinematic form". Having been released during the season of America's self immolating election, 'The Substance' is a testament to society's desire to go backwards into thin fantasy worlds created to protect us from looking at ourselves.

The film is relentless and brutal and without compromise. Many viewers may be repulsed, or even traumatized, although I question if anything on the screen matches the daily horror displayed on the evening news. The film juxtaposes the sleazy spectacle of Donald Trump style beauty pageants with explosions of rage that reminded me of the movie 'Carrie', as well as the tortured physical metaphors often portrayed in the films of David Cronenberg.

Blending horror and comedy in a surrealistic mix of 'pumped up' visual extremes we see in television commercials and popular magazines, 'The Substance' pushes up against cinema's most powerful operatic limits. The intent is to forcibly shock the viewer awake. Its images are grotesque and direct, and anyone not altered in their presence is either unconscious or braindead.

In the face of extremes of hate and violence pushed by those who wish to rule and profit, the floodgates of truly political art have opened in the mainstream. Films like 'Barbie', 'Women Talking' and 'Poor Things' speak directly to the atrocities of female oppression. 'The Substance' is one of those, and it isn't trying to be reasonable or gentle in a world where the spectacle of politics has taken us to the edges of absolute chaos.

During the drawn out, horrifying and over-the top final cataclysm in 'The Substance' there's a close up shot of a terrified little girl covered in blood. She's been dressed up to echo the exotic sexual fantasies paraded before her on the stage, and her face displays the full horror children witness everyday in a world trapped in its fantasies and dominated by its own irrational fears.

reviews.author: amir-moayyed
reviews.body:
The Substance delivers a bold and unique vision that challenges the typical conventions of horror and dark comedy. Directed by Coralie Fargeat, this film combines body horror with satire, exploring themes like ageism and beauty standards in Hollywood. Its striking visuals and grotesque yet creative sequences make it stand out from the crowd. However, its execution has notable shortcomings.

While the movie impresses with its technical brilliance-such as its unsettling music and symbolic cinematography-it suffers from an overindulgence in style. The excessive focus on shock value and repetitive montages drags down the pacing, particularly in its 141-minute runtime. The tonal shifts can feel jarring, and the chaotic, over-the-top ending sacrifices narrative coherence for spectacle.

Despite its flaws, The Substance does succeed in leaving an impression, but its muddled storytelling and self-indulgent finale may alienate some viewers. This is a film that prioritizes its message and aesthetic over delivering a cohesive experience, and the result is as divisive as it is daring.

reviews.author: joshwb-31737
reviews.body:
I'd say it's best to go into this movie without reading anything about it, just go into it and experience the ride. It's genuinely an insane ride the whole way through, you won't be able to look away, as much as you'll also want to at times!

The movie is very well made, on a surface level, you're getting very good cinematography, and the horror that you're signing up for, but it also works a very well done commentary on a number of important topics, again, I won't be going into it specifically, as I wouldn't even want to spoil it.

But I must praise the well done symbolism, and the way they got the message across to accompany the whole ride. Would watch again, but even just once was enough for it to stay with me, very well done.

reviews.author: daisukereds
reviews.body:
If you get queasy with body stuff.. don't even think about it! It reminded me of elements from the 1986's The Fly.

Anyway.. for what it is, it is quite good! If you like body horror, you'd definitely get a kick out of it. If you don't, this will certainly broaden your horizon! For my tastes specifically, I'd rate it lower.. as it is NOT the sort of thing I enjoy or would be capable of recommending to anyone I know. But I actually respect it a lot as it is inventive, creative, interesting and also very well made technically! From camera work, make-up, and more. So, it even won me over, even if I felt it's 2+ hour length and it is a bit shallow in dialogue and interactions (content I enjoy). Helped that it is so well casted (the two main leads)! Demi Moore deserves some sort of recognition for putting herself in such a role, doing so many things I would have never expected her to do, and doing it so well. Makes me ponder about her motivation..

It is also a bit over indulgent in some visual aspects, but manages to "set you straight" with its core messages.. stuff to be grateful for and lots to think about.

reviews.author: TakeTwoReviews
reviews.body: I used to say I didn't like horror. That's nonsense, I love good horror. The question is, is this good horror? Elizabeth Sparkle (Demi Moore) is a Hollywood starlet who's, lost her sparkle. This we learn from an amusingly inventive and stylish opening. In fact this is packed with surface level style, that's sort of the point. Make no mistake though, this has plenty under the hood. Turning 50 and quite honestly looking fantastic, she's lonely and being forced out of work by a patriarchal industry obsessed with youth. It's vicious. An accident leads to an opportunity to regain her stardom, via The Substance. Is it an opportunity though, or the start of a living nightmare. The Substance will create a perfect younger version of you. One that you're to share your time with. One week for you, one week for the copy that you're tied to, until death you part. It's all very Cronenbergian. Starkly shot in a hyperreal, sparsely populated world, little dialogue, just enough to guide us. Once signed up, Elizabeth receives her DIY box with instructions. You activate only once, you stabilise every day, you switch every seven days without exception. Remember you are one. It's simple, but ominous. That's a good summary, but it doesn't pull any punches, it's a body horror bonanza as Elizabeth activates and that's only the beginning. The new Elizabeth isn't a clone copy, she's Sue (Margaret Qualley). Who seems instantly to know what to do, but then she knows what Elizabeth knows. They are one. There are a lot of needles involved and plenty of gore as the pair navigate 80s America dominated by creeps like Harvey (Dennis Quaid)... who's also looking pretty great. I say pair, they're not. You have to remember it's the same consciousness in both bodies. Secretly living two lives in rotation. The obvious issue is all admin is on Elizabeth's time, while the excitement is in Sue's world of perfect bodies, having sex to a banging electro score. She's told to "Respect the balance", but the scales are already tipping. Qualley is great, Moore is great. They are one after all. Moore though, often without any dialogue, her role trapped in a prison of her making, portrays this psychological unravelling brilliantly. As balance goes out the window, Elizabeth finds herself having to face the horrifying consequences of her choices. For the faint hearted it is not. The pace is rapid, so much so that you're left wondering what fresh hell is there left to endure. The make-up department must have had an absolute field day, the sound department too. The score is wonderfully menacing and the foley work is packed with all kinds of visceral squeltchiness. It's a damning critique against ageism, not only in society, but in each of us, how we choose to deal with getting older. Addiction too, what we relate to a good time and what's more important in life. Be careful what you wish for. It's not perfect, but it's a very interesting premise, brilliantly executed right through to its gripping finale of pure nightmare fuel. Is it a good horror? No, it's a great horror.

reviews.author: osanchezpotter
reviews.body:
They didn't know how to end it. It becomes a moral about female beauty and machismo in the industry. In addition, it is a story that has been told and ended with better decisions in previous editions such as Dr. Jerkyill or Dorian Gray or even Requiem for a Dream

What is redeemable is the photography and the superb performance of Demi Moore who is personally playing a very personal role with Bruce Willis. On the other hand, Margaret Qualley is a star with a great future. What is Dennis Quaid doing there? LOL.

reviews.author: sharon6598
reviews.body: The movie starts like a really good "Black Mirror" episode, and slowly ratchets up the tension until it reaches a climax with an insane amount of gore. My friend thought it was too much, but I personally love that horror movies dare to go "all the way out." The plot is amazing, and I don't have a single negative thing to say about the movie. On the contrary, it gave me chills of excitement because of how good it was. I remember feeling exactly the same way when I watched "Joker" at the theaters. That's the feeling when a movie truly succeeds in surprising you (and in a good way). It's a true body horror film that everyone who loves gore or body horror films should watch.

reviews.body: I don't hate the film, I thought it was genius and came in expecting to be entertained, I was at some points and when the nudity was ramped up I didn't mind I didn't take it as lazy nudity seeing as it served to the story, but even as the story goes on still it doesn't slow down, it still keeps going and remains utilising sexualy implicit scenes and plain nudity, makes the past 40 minutes you spend watching feeling like it was a waste of time, all of that build up and pay off for what? reviews.body:
Movie The Substance is directed by a female director Coralie Fargeat. Elisabeth Sparkle ( excellent casting of Demi Moore) is a gorgeous health fitness coach/model/role model who is now past her 40s./50s and needs to be replaced. The premise of the story is if the substance is injected a younger version of ageing person can be created but at any one time only one form can exist. Younger version is Sue ( Margaret Quailey from the Netflix mini series Maid ) young and beautiful. The 2 forms have to alternate but just like anyone Sue wants to continue her existence which means less of Elisabeth time.

Scenes between 7.30 pm and 8 pm are excellent when Elisabeth is getting ready for a date .

Extremely difficult to let go of youth and energy and be replaced with frailty, old age and continuous disrespect of society for the ageing knowing that all have to go through the same process. reviews.author: JulesAndVincent6
reviews.body:
One of the films I was most looking forward to in this calm 2024. I feel like it was too much, and not in a bad way, but rather that a second viewing is necessary to finish processing all the information acquired.

However, I think the film was being spectacularly handled and suffered a slight derailment at the climax of the film, because it seemed like it was being just grotesque enough to meet the standards of the genre and still have some logic and coherence to shine through.

I don't think that necessarily affects my perception of the film, because beyond the creative differences in the resolution, I still appreciate and believe that the resurrection of cinema will come from original ideas, with precise pointed criticism, just as seen here and not from biopics, sequels, remakes, prequels or all the bad spectacle of current cinema.

reviews.author: MovieswDan
reviews.body:
Earlier this week I watched Coralie Fargeat's The Substance which is currently streaming exclusively on MUBI. This body horror drama/dark comedy shines a disturbingly raw light on the unrealistic expectations for beauty that Hollywood sets for women in the industry. The film stars Demi Moore as aging star Elisabeth and Margaret Qualley as her newer and "better" self, Sue. Dennis Quaid is also featured as the sleazy producer named Harvey, which is almost too on the nose, but it works magnificently.

I loved this movie and felt that it was extremely well done. The performances given by Qualley and Quaid were superb and should be considered for recognition during award season, but Demi Moore stole the show. She laid it all out there (literally) and delivered the performance of a lifetime and I really hope she gets the recognition that she deserves. The writing and visual aspects of the film was what stood out to me above all else. The lesson shared in the film is about body shaming and the lengths that people will go just to feel beautiful, coupled with the gross contrast between the expectations of men vs women as they age. This is the type of movie where everything falls into place the right way, and the result was a beautiful and masterfully crafted work of art. The makeup, cinematography, writing, sound, and acting performances were all incredible and this movie should receive lots of recognition come awards season.

This is a movie that everyone should see, especially men. I will warn you though, this movie is extremely graphic with tons of nudity and a whole lot of gore and crazy body horror. Put plainly, this movie is gross and hard to watch at times. If it wasn't, I do not know if the point that Fargeat was trying to make, would have been as impactful.

reviews.author: aegairsoft1
reviews.body:
This movie is a conversation piece, but not a pretty one. Unfortunately any lasting impression this movie could have had.. is nearly ruined in the final 10 minutes. Everything just unravels.

Invoking from the likes of modern classics like "Requiem of a Dream" and "The Fly".. it seemed "The Substance" was on to something incredible. With relatable themes and characters, along with incredible acting and imagery.. I was on the edge of my seat. The film constantly tugs at your emotions, just to twist them with non-sense a minute later. While an effective tool, it borders on being subversive for the sake of it.

Unfortunately producers could not contain themselves. The plot goes over-the-top.. and all "substance" (and realism) disappears. The movie had a strong enough story/theme to drive home an impactful ending without the over-done shenanigans. It's a shame producers couldn't take a more inventive and nuanced conclusion.

reviews.author: waldojefferss
reviews.body: The Substance has everything horror fans will like: it's gory, it's fun, it's sexy. But The Substance is more than that. It's a movie about the relationship one has with oneself, the choices made while being young, and how they impact our older selves. It's also a movie about fame and what we are willing to sacrifice for it. It's a film about pushing the limits and facing the consequences. It's about being content with what we have, even if it's not as good as what we once had. In short, The Substance offers 2 hours of great cinema with subtle messages that are not just mental gymnastics. I could not recommend it enough.

reviews.author: willphelan
reviews.body: The Substance is absolutely fantastic. This movie tackles the subject of beauty standards in such a cool way. The concept of this movie is so creative and I love when unique premises get to shine on the big screen. Demi Moore gives a career best performance in this movie and she absolutely nails this tragic character arc. Margaret Qualley also nailed playing her role in this movie. They play two sides of the same coin representing the pressure that is put on women and their appearance while they age and then the repercussions and consequences of that. Coralie Fargeat masterfully captured this story and made it so that the movie was consistently interesting and thought provoking. The messages are so well done because the story is genuinely really intriguing. The unique take of horror in this movie is pretty freaky but can also work in some more comedic ways when the story calls for it. The cinematography was beautiful and memorable and the makeup was on another level in this movie. The editing is also a standout. This is one of the best theater experiences I've ever had as everyone was witnessing how insane this movie was. The Substance is one of the best and most memorable films of 2024.

reviews.author: blackmoon-8263839
reviews.body:
Visually it's striking, the sets are original and creative, the colors amazing.

The problem with this movie is that it made me hate the disgusting old woman and I wanted her to finally die, so the young hot girl could take over and live her life. I totally rooted for her. I understood her lust for life, and why she wanted to take just a little more if the substance.

Was this really the intention?

Plus, the ending is just funny gore-fest and a bit boring. It doesn't add much to the themes of the movie.

I would have loved to see more scenes between the woman and her young clone, where they have some kind of real exchange, not just try to kill each other. I never felt they are two parts of the same soul. Why wouldn't the girl at least try to convince her *mother* to let her take over? You had your life, now let me live mine. I'll keep your name in honor. Or why couldn't they try to team up to get more stabilizer? Why didn't the mother try to talk some sense into the girl?

reviews.author: movieman6-413-929510
reviews.body:
The Substance is a new horror drama directed, written and partly produced by Coralie Fargeat, director of Revenge.

Elisabeth Sparkle (Demi Moore) was once a big celebrity, but has lost her fame over the years. Out of desperation, she decides to use a special drug on the black market. This drug is a special substance that can create a younger version of herself from her cells.

Her younger version goes by the name Sue (Margaret Qualley) and manages to regain their fame. The two now have to live in a balance next to each other for seven days and try to support the other. If one of them disrupts this balance, it can have consequences for both of them.

With this film they play a bit on current events where in the world of celebrities people such as the producers, the public and the fans often keep looking for a newer and younger celebrity. In this way, the older, previous celebrities are then more forgotten, or seek success in other ways. Director and writer Coralie Fargeat shows these aspects mainly from the female celebrity side. Where actresses, models, or singers always try to stay current for both their old fans and younger new fans. For this, some do go through some changes such as new, or different looks, or styles.

The figures above them, who for example arrange their financial affairs, or schedule, also try to piggyback on their fame and also earn money with it. For example, by using the celebrity to promote certain things. This also involves situations such as abuse of power, or abuse in other ways. Despite the fact that this unfortunately took place a lot hidden in the world of celebrities, this film seems to tar all stereotypes with the same brush from both the perpetrator and victim sides. Despite the good message of the film, this can also make the film a bit one-sided. Coralie Fargeat herself could have used a better and more realistic balance in this.

The cast members do deliver good and appropriate acting. Especially the two leading roles dare to give and show a lot with their roles in this film. If the film had been less one-sided, their roles in addition to the film itself could have been a classic.

reviews.author: profzjadljad
reviews.body:
The act of transgression-at least in theory-is meant to provoke shock, perhaps even catharsis, compelling the viewer to reflect, to contemplate who they are, where, how, why, and for what purpose they live. For many years, radical artistic creation has been diluted by successive apparent transgressions for publicity and money, and today-ultimately overdone and powerless-seems to have nothing left to reveal.

Coralie Fargeat's "The Substance" is an attempt to push boundaries, but stopped somewhere along the way, lost its direction, and instead of forging new paths, drowns in a sea of pretentiousness. This film is stark, bloody, and undoubtedly bold, but this courage does not stem from an artistic vision, but merely from the need to draw attention. What was meant to be transgression is actually a parody of transgression-empty, purposeless, and powerless in its grotesqueness. Where is the catharsis? Where is the shock that makes the viewer reflect on themselves? In "The Substance", there is not a moment for reflection; a film filled with emotional emptiness treats violence like cheap merchandise, scattering macabre scenes across the screen without any justification.

Fargeat tries to convince us that she is telling a story about female freedom, about the fight against society-imposed ideals of beauty, but this struggle is superficial and false. Demi Moore, subjected to grotesque transformations, becomes the object of pure visual spectacle-her body is exposed, destroyed, deformed, but all this is devoid of deeper reflection. This is not an act of liberation, it is not a manifestation of strength-it is only a shallow attempt to evoke disgust. The film opts for radicalism but does not understand that radicalism without purpose is merely noise.

It is becoming increasingly difficult for me to believe in cinema that provokes, that asks questions, that shakes the foundations of thought. "The Substance" is hyperesthetic literalness dressed in the guise of something that aspires to a universal metaphor, but ultimately remains only a shocking image devoid of any meaning. In times when transgression has become an industrial standard, Fargeat joins a long line of creators who believe that violence and grotesquery are enough to create the semblance of rebellion.

Ultimately, "The Substance" is like a paper tiger-it roars, shocks, tries to be unruly, but its claws are dulled and painted with varnish, and its teeth bleached solely for display. It is a film that wants to be dangerous, but in reality, it is safe in its predictable, pretentious structure. This is not transgression; it is an imitation of transgression-another example of how contemporary cinema has fallen into the trap of its own aspirations, offering the viewer cheap sensationalism instead of a true challenge. "The Substance" is meaningless noise-a stark, only posterishly "uncompromising" attempt to push boundaries, which as a result breaks nothing except the patience of the viewer.

reviews.author: bullet-myvalentine-353-90337
reviews.body: Absolutely brilliant and amazing! I haven't seen a good movie in awhile. Very original, the cinematography is striking, the visual storytelling complements the film's theme. The movie tackles self discovery, the impact of social expectations and the importance of embracing your flaws. The movie is a reminder that the journey to self acceptance is often fraught with challenges but ultimately it is worth taking. The only negative thing I can say about the movie that it is really disturbing, the violence and blood scenes were too much for me that I had to look the other way many times till the scene passes.

reviews.author: jit-23697
reviews.body:
This was one gory film, some of the scenes I had to look away they were so gross. Demi Moore is a great actress and she was outstanding and Margaret qually who played demi moores part was absolutely brilliant. From start to finish I was hooked.

This film is a stark reminder that you should age gracefully and not everything is about looks, however the world we live in is cruel. Today's society, social media, companies expect young women to sell products, shows etc therefore women taking drastic steps to look younger. No amount of lotions, potions, surgery will make you look younger or more beautiful, just look natural and age gracefully is the message here, can we applaud the person who came up with the idea of the film, thank you.

reviews.author: keithmwarwick-20497
reviews.body:
Despite a daft and inappropriate denouement; an ending so clunky it falls apart like a birthday cake in a torrential rain downburst, this movie is significant for it's fine lead acting, cut-to-the-bone script, good production values, tight direction, creative flair, daubs of satisfyingly grotesque moments, and a steady descent into celebrity hell, where borrowed tropes from The Thing, Frankenstein, and Countess Bathory, all combine and surface, as does the sub-theme of the ridiculous denial of the ageing process, which afflicts humanity, and the bizarre hinterland of celebrity bulldust. The judgement of a society that both dislikes and rejects the notion of ageing, is an indictment upon the human race that the movie picks out, firmly. Just observe!

A movie of to two parts, a little degraded by its wildly abandoned blood-fest ending, and it's orgy of irrational gore-feasting, that grates!

However, it's now in my top ten best horror movies of lo time. Result.

Not in any way suitable for the squeamish, it's a satisfying foray into an original take on astonishing horror.

Highly Recommended.

reviews.author: amandalhua
reviews.body: The bloated and beautifully mutated embodiment of true body horror-a masterful blend of plot, gore, and purpose that elevates the genre. It's a well-crafted cocktail for those tired of the bottom-shelf shots of meaningless splatterfests. Every grotesque detail serves a narrative function, making it a must-watch for fans who crave more depth behind the visceral imagery. While it's a little on the nose at times, its never too blunt with its allegory on women's struggles in entertainment and keeping current. It's a disturbing yet thoughtful experience that stays with you long after the credits roll.

reviews.author: zakharmaletskyi
reviews.body:
The Substance delivers an explicit message that our generation desperately needs as we chronically lose mindfulness. It is about finding the fragile balance to help us become happy humans. Such an aim is incredibly challenging to achieve in our modern life because we face too many obstacles, and The Substance highlights at least three of those.

The first is our obsession with fame and recognition, which drugs us into a dependency that's impossible to escape, even when opportunities for normalcy arise - like a regular person inviting us on a date. The second is our struggle with multiple identities, which are challenging to balance. We tend to favour one at the expense of consuming and damaging the others. When one identity dominates, it destroys the counterparts, which might be our better sides. This happens when we fail to maintain the boundaries between work and personal life, professional interests and hobbies, logical and artistic identities, etc.

The final challenge is the dopamine addiction that develops from overconsumption in our capitalistic society. This addiction can involve everything from extravagant luxury shopping to drugs and sex. The common thread is that we become social junkies when that fragile balance is lost. However, The Substance suggests another way - by giving preference to our better selves - which can help transform the Beast.

It is a timely reminder of the importance of mindfulness and balance in our lives. It challenges us to reflect on our dependencies and identities and encourages us to seek a healthier path.

reviews.author: savastosic
reviews.body:
The Substance is an incredibly disturbing movie that isn't for everyone, but within its niche subgenre of horror, it's an absolute masterpiece. Using themes of addiction, self-love, and modern beauty, it tells a uniquely personal yet horrific story.

The sound design is outstanding, heightening every tense moment and adding layers of discomfort. The scenes are also filmed in such a way that every frame feels off-kilter, creating a sense of unease that's hard to shake. Combined, these elements make the movie a grotesque and unsettling watch, and I'd easily rank it as one of the most disturbing films I've ever seen.

The last 30 minutes are an absolute treat for fans of the genre, blending comedic special effects with violent sound design that feels like an assault on your senses. It's surreal, chaotic, and at times almost absurd, but in a way that's incredibly effective. While I'm not sure I'd ever recommend it to someone who isn't prepared for what they're getting into, I have to admit that I genuinely enjoyed the experience.

reviews.author: dawnydd
reviews.body:
This film, from the very beginning, captivates the audience not only with its compelling story but also with its remarkable visual style. It's a work that rightfully earned the Best Screenplay award, as the writing is sharp, intelligent, and full of emotional depth. However, what makes this piece truly stand out is its impressive visual direction, which complements the narrative seamlessly. The director's visual sensibilities are evident in every frame, with each shot meticulously crafted to enhance the story's themes and character arcs. The use of color, lighting, and composition creates an immersive atmosphere that draws viewers deeper into the world of the film.

Whether it's through striking wide-angle shots that convey the vastness of the film's universe or intimate close-ups that capture subtle emotional nuances, the film's visual language speaks volumes. The visual aesthetics are not just supplementary; they are an integral part of the storytelling process. This combination of excellent writing and innovative direction makes it a unique cinematic experience that resonates on multiple levels. From the very beginning, this film proves itself as a masterful blend of narrative and visual art, making it a standout work that appeals to both the heart and the eyes.

reviews.author: boss-981-447297
reviews.body:
Jesus Christ, I just finished watching this movie, and OMG, Holy Moly, it's VERY disgusting.

It goes from a personal melodrama of getting old, to a very good suspenseful thriller, to a Cronenberg-esque fantasy finale that won't appeal to most people.

I'd say most people will be able to watch 2/3 of this movie. The last third, is not for the faint of heart. It is VERY grotesque. Do not have food around while watching it. You have been warned.

Apart from that, Margaret Qualley is stunning. This movie makes her look like the most beautiful girl ever. I was already a fan, but this movie makes her stand out so much, I need a full-size poster of hers now.

Demi Moore is a fantastic competent actress. She is the backbone of this movie, and it works because she is so believable in her suffering. I wouldn't be surprised if she wins an Oscar or two.

The story is very fantastical, but the rules of the game make it feel like a Saw movie. If you watched the best from that franchise, you know what you will feel. It has suspense, it has gore, it is disgusting. And the contrast between the stunning raw beauty of Margaret with the gore of the game, make everything even more difficult to watch.

The direction and cinematography contributes for the sense of claustrophobia. Super close ups to make you feel even more uncomfortable. Everything is shot in a way to make you feel very uncomfortable all the time. That's the whole point of the movie. There is no boredom, no still moments, no breathing. It's a rollercoaster.

Highly recommended if you feel like you can take some gore.

reviews.body: There's a reason this movie is getting so much recognition. Such a unique storyline focusing on everyone's biggest fear , the fear of getting old , of losing relevance. Women are particularly gonna fell this , especially beautiful women who know that there is a short duration where they are in their prime. Beauty dosen't last forever and the lead in this movie realises this the hard way and does everything in her power to get young again. But it isn't as easy as it seems. Great performances by Demi Moore and Margare Qualley both are amazing actresses and worthy of many awards especially for this work. The movie dosen't feel boring even for a minute and you are completely engrossed in what's gonna happen next. The ending is so unexpected. You are missing out if you skip this masterpiece.

reviews.author: MogwaiMovieReviews
reviews.body:
An aging actress takes an experimental drug that creates a second, younger and more beautiful body, but the two struggle to co-exist.

This new film is a clever but shallow take on Cronenberg-esque body horror: it's flashy and colorful, but never scratches beneath the surface of any of the characters; the gore is repulsive rather than frightening and, in the final moments, rather silly and comical. On the other hand, it starts out very strong, is technically dazzling, and has a good performance from Demi Moore, so even with its catastrophically bad finale it still remains one of the more interesting movies this year.

reviews.author: Godfather0219
reviews.body:
The Substance is one of the most vigorous sci-fi masterpieces this year. It is a body horror version of Cinderella and a glorious comeback for Demi Moore.

There are countless films and shows about rejuvenation. Tom Hanks took us to the future in Big. Matthew Perry turned into Zac Efron in 17 Again. Goldie Hawn and Meryl Streep took anti-aging potions in Death Becomes Her.

The Substance, which won Best Screenplay at Cannes and made waves among sci-fi/horror fans, has now joined the hall of fame of this genre. But unlike comedies commonly seen in rejuvenation stories, it chose to be a horror film - a subtype within horror known as body horror.

In film history, rejuvenation has been achieved through curses, magic, wishes, potions, time travel - simple procedures easy for the plot and audience to comprehend. But The Substance insists on complicating the process with more elaborate steps, detailed workings and side effects.

This isn't just for show or to be different. You may have that misconception at first, thinking it's unnecessary hassle. But as the movie progresses, you'll understand the rationale and even come to appreciate it.

The "rules" in The Substance are: After injecting a black market serum, your body splits into a younger double of yourself. You must take turns being conscious and share one lifetime with this double, switching within allotted times so the original has enough time to produce stabilizers to maintain the double's youth.

If the double stays conscious past the limit, the drug equilibrium fails, causing irreversible rapid aging of the original - the double has parasitically stolen beyond its quota of the original's lifespan.

These rules give The Substance a modern, dark Cinderella fairy tale quality - Cinderella must get home before the clock strikes twelve or her finery will disappear, exposing her as an imposter at the royal ball.

The female lead Elizabeth, restricted by a similar "spell", must pause her youth when time's up. The rules raise questions - what if Cinderella found loopholes to prolong the spell? What punishment would that bring?

The questions liken the movie's Cinderella to a symbol of plastic surgery addicts. Cinderella's class anxiety in the original story translates into contemporary physical appearance anxiety.

People want to break rules and indulge endlessly in pleasure. The reckless double exploits loopholes, causing imbalance until the original can't produce more stabilizers.

The utmost beauty spectrum's other end is utmost ugliness. As Elizabeth sinks deeper, she brings about increasingly hellish self-destruction.

Rejuvenation stories often conclude like time travel tales - move forward, don't dwell on the past. The Substance certainly does too, but in an exceptionally violent, bloody way, vividly showing the agony of "obsession" so viewers deeply feel the painful consequences.

Only body horror can profoundly convey this pain. The more shocking the pain is, the more likely viewers will take the lesson to heart and feel the regretful agony along with the protagonist - bringing tremendous excitement and impact.

But The Substance's true target audience is probably female performers. Elizabeth goes from Oscar winner to hosting workout shows on TV after fading into obscurity - easily reminiscent of some Hollywood cases.

Oscar winner plus workout guru easily recalls Jane Fonda. Elizabeth's fear of being outdated resonates with what actresses face or will face. To cling to her last shred of fame, she'd rather keep her fading job than slowly rebuild her career - showing how unwilling she is to step aside or let go of fleeting youth.

The Substance continues stylistic hallmarks from Karyn Kusama's debut Jennifer's Body: vivid color, giant title lettering, slow eating shots evoking unease. But it's even more vulgar, outrageous and direct.

The Substance depicts a fantastical, unrealistic Hollywood. The dialog is overblown, actors (especially Denis O'Hare) are absurdly hammy, some social situations are cartoonish.

This surrealism is deliberate, amplifying the discomfort and repulsion. The more vulgar it is, the more hard-hitting.

Moore and co-star Margaret Qualley fit right into this surreal world, especially Qualley who handles unhinged hysteria even more naturally than her veteran co-star.

But The Substance is more significant for Moore's career.

Playing washed-up performers often marks turning points. Michelle Pfeiffer had Dangerous Liaisons, Rupert Everett had My Best Friend's Wedding, Tippi Hedren had The Birds. These veterans regained popularity by starring in these films, revitalizing their careers.

It's hard to recall Moore's last widely discussed, well-received film. Recently she's been in acclaimed series Ratched. The Substance further amplifies her.

For Moore, this could mark a pivotal comeback akin to those films did for those actors.

reviews.author: marcverrier-70557

I have absolutely no words to describe this.... I just have no words.

reviews.author: paulnoku-6655321
reviews.body: It's in fact a good movie. However, the last 10 minutes monster section was very much unnecessary, I mean it was fun to watch, but being serious, wasn't in the peak of the road. On the other hand, I was really surprised on how this was transgressive in a good way, people like David Cronenberg already made a movie in the same psychological aspect, but a woman's vision on the subject added something in the gesture of the body horror sequences. And let's be honest, with a plot like this, you already know where this film is going to switch into, but even though, it's a fun and unique ride....................

reviews.author: rgandrade2000
reviews.body:
This film is one of those rare cases where all the elements for an artistic masterpiece are present, but eventually it stumbles in its execution and falls short of its potential.

The Substance begins with an impressive setup, conveying the promise of becoming a timeless work. From the intriguing premise and character development to the exceptional cinematography-each shot, color palette, and scene composition radiates brilliance, crafting a stunning visual spectacle.

However, as the story unfolds, a darker, twisted layer is introduced, marking the turning point where things begin to shift. Words like "bizarre," "unsettling," and "disturbing" best capture this phase. While the middle act retains a certain intensity, it feels less refined, gradually losing the balance that made the opening so compelling.

The final act, however, is where the narrative takes a nosedive. The plot veers into chaotic, almost gimmicky territory, resembling a low-budget horror film that prioritizes shock over substance. The sudden tonal shift felt forced and lacked justification, undermining the impact of what came before.

Despite these flaws, the movie held my attention throughout. I found myself glued to my seat, eyes wide open, completely immersed and unsettled by the experience.

In summary, what started as a potential 10/10 masterpiece devolved into something closer to an 8 or 9 before ending in disappointment. It is a shame because this film had the ingredients for greatness. Nevertheless, the ending does not erase its merits entirely; it is still worth watching, albeit with a warning: this is a disturbing piece that should not be taken lightly.

reviews.author: romhacked
reviews.body: The first half of this movie is pornography with no commentary of any meaning on its subject matter. What could have been a scathing bloody critique of beauty standards, the tv industry, motherhood and being replaced by ones offspring, or even simply aging is instead a mess of unexplored half-baked ideas. If this movie was half the length, it would still be an overbloated mess in need of editing. There is no true main character, there is no arc for them to go through. There are about 15 ending points, all blown past. Leaving us with an ending that drags on and mever stops while you dig into your seat begging for it to be over.

reviews.author: kristinaurania
reviews.body:
I was surprised when I saw the movie ratings. It seems to me that people have clearly missed the point because the message that director was trying to send was quite clear.

The ending of the film, which many complain about, is actually the reason here for a higher rating. Usually it is the ending that leaves me wanting for more, but this time I had the feeling that nothing was missing. Also, complaints about the display of nudity were a bit out of place in this one, considering the topic of the film.

I have no doubt that this film will be a cult classic.

Demi was excellent as usual, and the film is a serious award contender. Believe the hype.

reviews.author: cherubimette
reviews.body: I was stunned! I'm a huge fan of cronenberg, I love movies like Basket Case, Dead Alive & am in general just a huge fan of genuine SFX & body horror. I'm sure there are some recent things I've missed, but generally in the last couple years I've just been disappointed over and over again by the lack of this charm in modern horror films. Yes, I am also picky. This movie... insane. It's unique, disgusting, hilarious, emotional, just so one of a kind, but at the same time reminded me and I'm sure took inspiration from so many of my favorite films. The acting was incredible, actors were genuine and on the part with all they had. Bravo, I was so entertained and so disgusted! I loved it!

reviews.author: stefydd
reviews.body: I enjoyed the movie overall, as it had moments that truly captured the essence of a good horror film. The suspenseful atmosphere, well-executed scares, and intriguing buildup kept me engaged throughout most of the story. However, the ending was a major letdown and felt completely out of place. It undermined all the effort that had gone into crafting the earlier parts of the film. It came across as rushed, poorly thought-out, and lacking depth, almost as if it had been written by someone inexperienced, like a 10-year-old child. This ultimately ruined what could have been an excellent experience.

reviews.author: tomdevisser29
reviews.body:
The Substance is a fascinating film, especially for those familiar with The Picture of Dorian Gray. The movie carries a lot of the same underlying themes-beauty, vanity, and the nature of self-destruction-but it tells the story in a fresh, visually stunning, and incredibly creative way. The cinematography alone is worth the watch, as every scene is meticulously crafted, almost like moving art.

However, The Substance is a tricky film to review. About 3/4th of the way through, it felt like the tone and genre took an unexpected turn. It was as if the writers decided to stop taking things seriously and just have some fun with it. While this switch was jarring, I have to admit I laughed a lot at the ending. Still, the sudden change in direction kind of derailed what could have been an excellent film. It was heading toward a very high rating, but the ending left me a bit disappointed.

That said, I thoroughly enjoyed the majority of it, and the movie deserves a fair rating. But I walked out of the cinema with mixed feelings, wishing it had stuck to its original, more serious tone throughout.

reviews.author: driver-85165
reviews.body:
Good body horror film. Works great except for the last 20 minutes where it all goes terribly south.

The movie draws you in fast with its mysterious context, camera angles and sound design. Although not specifically mentioned, the style and the costumes seem to point to the 60s, where beauty was a prized possession and ugly women never got a fair chance.

I like how blunt this film is. There is no shortage of gore or nudity, no sign of political correctness. Every image, every concept and every dialogue is real, savage and completely unfiltered.

The movie does a great job at maintaining the fear factor and the intrigue but in the last 20 minutes the psychological horror element goes away and the ridiculous element steps in. After a certain point you are not afraid, you are disgusted. I don't know why the did that.

With a better ending and the same camera work and artistic direction they could have produced a classic film. But now, not so much.

reviews.author: psgorio
reviews.body: It is quite rare for me to watch a modern day movie and feel so fulfilled after watching it to the point of sheer satisfaction, albeit some minor quirks here and there in the final act that went off the rails a bit with it's message. But besides the last 25 minutes or so being quite the writer and director's self-indulgent freak show, the rest of the movie was simply astounding. For fans of body horror or even fans of watching a slow churn of self destruction will get hooked instantly here. The message coming across of simply how far one person will go to regain youth and beauty when faced with their own mortality as they realize they're way past their prime in a Hollywood style celebrity status world that demands beauty and perfection. It is quite genius really that something so simple can evolve then devolve so rapidly over the course of 2 and a half hours. I mean you could probably have shaved off the last 20 minutes or so and still had just a fulfilling a film but I digress. It is a small hindrance that is a drop in a very large bucket of sheer brilliant insanity. The casting director nailed it too as Demi Moore killed it as Elizabeth Sparkle, a past her prime actress turned into a morning fitness instructor for a tv show that is about to replaced by someone younger and prettier. But all hope is not lost it seems when an accident puts her in the hands of contacting an ominous company called The Substance, which offers her a second chance at being young and beautiful once more. All she has to do is follow the strict steps and she'll be able to live 2 lives in 2 separate bodies. You can probably imagine what could go wrong with this picture does go wrong. The Substance to me can best be described as The Nutty Professor meets Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde but having 2 separate bodies vying for control over the other which ends in such an over the top climactic experience minus a mildly questionable final act selection that while it makes sense is very disturbing to watch yet had me laughing at times for being so utterly ridiculous. Alas why I'm scoring this so high lies in both the acting and of course message that it gets across quite spectacularly. Those who measure their lives in outer beauty should have matching inner beauty this way it counter balances the other and doesn't make you pull a Demi Moore here and go ballistic on your body and sacrifice not only your outer physicality but also your soul. What it means to be who you are. The very fabric of your being consumed by greed, vanity and sheer pride. Overall this isn't just a movie for women who are into their looks or have a job revolving around appearances. It is really for anyone who wants or needs to be reminded that you simply cannot put a price on your exterior self worth, no matter how quick and easy it may seem. Granted there was no easy way about initiating and maintaining the Substance in this movie though. Believe that. Anyway, I highly recommend this movie to watch at least once and I predict it will clean house at the Oscars and even might take home best picture to boot since Hollywood cannot resist gettingg off and showering their own awards about films pretty much about themselves. Looking at you La La Land.

reviews.body: You know, I thought this was a really promising movie at the start and even throughout the middle. It sounds stupid, because I know the whole story cannot happen in real life, but the ending made it almost sci-fi like. Just didn't like it.
