reviews.author: SoumikBanerjee1996
reviews.body:
The Substance intricately weaves psychological drama with elements of body horror, serving not only as a gripping narrative but also as a poignant critique of the pharmaceutical industry and the entertainment business. It highlights their complicity in promoting untested genetic therapies and de-aging treatments with alarming fervor.

At the heart of the tale is Elizabeth Sparkle a once-glamorous star now in her fifties grappling with profound depression and a waning sense of self-worth. In her desperate quest to reclaim her former fame and vitality, she discovers a 'substance' that promises to restore her youth in the most outlandish manner imaginable.

This narrative is a masterful fusion of drama and visceral horror, destined to leave audiences reeling, especially as it hurtles toward a nauseating end where stakes soar to unprecedented heights, a moment of pinnacle.

The artistry of the makeup and prosthetics team deserves special recognition; as their work is nothing short of extraordinary, Cronenberg would be proud. Additionally, accolades are due to Moore and Margaret too, whose stellar acts significantly enrich the storytelling, adding much needed layers of complexity and emotion.

reviews.author: CrypticSceptic
reviews.body:
Universal and timeless message about loving yourself. It has been done too many times, but this is a surprisingly refreshing take.

Demi Moore is amazing. She has almost no lines, but manages to convey the emotions perfectly through body language and facial expressions. New actors should take notes...

Sound design is great at making each scene come alive and set the tone. Sometimes the sound goes into ASMR mode which in combination with the camera work and direction makes the movie come to live and you feel like you are there beside her or watching from behind her eyes.

Special effects are gross and very realistic looking for a monster movie. It really shows the work and talent behind the prosthetics, when we are treated to some beautiful and well lighted closeups. We even get moving stuff. I feel like I'm watching something from Stan Winston back in the days.

The direction and writing is top tier. The script and direction is clever and has a lot of subtle messaging and symbols pertaining the main subject, throughout the film. The message or morale of the film is told in refreshing way through special effects and the fate of our main character, rather than make the characters tell it straight to our faces like most films now.

The plot and character development are also on point. The plot sees our main character facing a crisis or challenge, which she then tries to solve, but she takes the shortcut and pay for it. We have a clear point of no return and we see the main character spiral. Throughout the main character's journey we clearly see the gradual evolution of the main character's mental state and physical state. Though it is not at pretty sight. In all seriousness though I think the plot is, yes the self-worth discovery trope, but done almost perfectly.

Finally, I think it should be mentioned that this film does not go for realism. I would place it more on the artsy side of the spectrum, but not so much it becomes hard to watch. There are only a few times where the film takes some liberties when depicting certain gory or grotesque elements, but this is definitely a choice of symbolism over realism. It did bother me, but I think the pros outweigh the cons of the style choice in this particular case.

I recommend this movie if you are ok with body horror and gross looking stuff, but also if you want a refreshing take on an old idea.

reviews.author: everdimension
reviews.body:
I get the references to David Lynch and the slashers of the 70s, but I just don't see how they fit here

Yeah, I've read the reviews praising the director for a "bold move" of skipping over the conclusion and instead turning a movie very suddenly into something else. In my opinion, it just ruined it.

It's almost as if the director didn't appreciate the base idea enough to finish it. But the initial premise is actually a refreshing look at the subject of aging, and if it was concluded in any meaningful way, I would be recommending this movie to everyone I know. The first two thirds of the movie are really worth it.

And then it's as if a second director came in to finish it. What's worse, the sudden switch of events is based on breaking the basic assumptions of the story, which were borderline plot holes anyway. Do the bodies share the same consciousness or don't they? The movie implies one answer but then the other.

The final act consists of gore that's too pointless even for the lovers of pointless gore. It's just sad. Could've been a masterpiece.

reviews.author: alexdiflip
reviews.body:
Disheartened by all these reviews stating the last 30 minutes ruined the movie, considering it was likely my favorite part of the film as a whole, simply for how downright insane it decided to go with the concept.

Don't worry, I won't be spoiling anything in this review, but just know that you are in for an absolute rollercoaster with this movie. I was completely tense throughout the entire affair, screamed several times, and had an absolute blast watching this with my friend!

This movie delivers on all it promises with its advertising. It will disgust you, shock you, unsettle you, and stay with you for weeks after you finish watching it. I simply cannot stop thinking about this film and all this it represents about Hollywood. It truly has so much to say about what media can to do to our perception of our own bodies and selves, and I think that the decision to go full-insane in the end was just how it needed to finish: completely ugly, overtly disgusting, and absolutely traumatic. It's what this industry does, and this movie is indeed a frustrated scream in film form.

This film also deserves immense praise for its blend of practical and special effects, as using a decent amount of both was quite effective in grossing me out. The concept of the drug is well thought-out, and seeing all different parts of the process really help sell this movie as being in the real world, even if it is ludicrous in nature.

reviews.author: gilbertofmottamaia
reviews.body: 70% of this movie is a pertinent critic of empowerment of women by putting beauty at a pedestal. It must be hard for an actress to live up to these standards. No chance to compete with a younger woman as beauty became a "weapon" in highly competitive fields. However, the last 30% of this fiilm resembles a B movie, kind of The Blob. Excelent performance of 61 Demi Moore. Perfect choice. Dennis Quaid again proves to act brilliantly in different manny roles. Prosthetics plays a central role to make all scenes up to the last part of the movie. I realized that there are more people working in prosthetics than acting or directing the scenes. Good movie.

reviews.author: Zett76
reviews.body:
Let me start by this: I grew up watching movies like 2001 or Once Upon a Time in America. I never had a problem with overlong or slow moving movies.

That being said: This movie could have been a lot better, if a lot of scenes would have been cut by 25-50%. Especially the horror scenes in the 3rd act. In my opinion, the shock value of quite a few ideas overstayed its welcome, by a mile. At one point, I even started skipping here and there. Not a lot, but still.

My second problem with the movie: the main point was quite obvious, for 50% of the movie - how far a woman is willing to go, to keep up with the beauty standards around her. But halfway through, that point got more or less thrown out, for "the conflict" of "the two"... but I still saw some point in it, like the inner battle between the part that loves to be beautiful, and the part that hates it... ...and then, the very end is just there for the shock value, I guess, because that last few scenes did nothing to drive any of these two themes home.

Well, that's my two cents. As there are 1.1k other reviews, already, I think I just wrote that down to get it out. I'm male, but I'm at that very same point where Elisabeth was, at the start of the movie. Not old yet, but far away from being 30. Would I give my savings to reset my body to 20?

Yes, I would.

Eat healthy, age in dignity.

reviews.author: mikehdtv
reviews.body:
While this might be horrific for the lead character and maybe as a refection of our societal value, it's not a horror flick. It's an amazing confection of social commentary, issues relating to age and gender expectations, and superficiality wrapped in a gloriously funny movie. It's visually great with a ton of Kubrick and other references. You know where it's going you you sit back and enjoy how they're going to get you there. As for Demi Moore's amazing, courageous performance - what can you say? As for the ending - WOW!

I've seen stories about horrified movie theater audience members quitting the movie, can't imagine why but I do believe the stories about audiences applauding when the credits role.

reviews.author: brenster-26348
reviews.body: I am not a horror fan nor a Demi Moore fan, but the concept of this film drew me in. Especially as the topic was an older woman being cast out after a certain age from the Entertainment business. Given that Demi Moore has been in this industry and has had her own ups and downs within her career and is no stranger to getting work done to keep herself looking youthful, I found the casting that bit more interesting. Ms Moore is not afraid to highlight imperfections in this film and the camera has some very close ups and unflattering angles on her. Which I applaud her doing. The film was a scary voyage down the path of one 'has been' according to Hollywood and the lengths people will go to stay relevant. I enjoyed it very much. However, it could have finished 20 mins sooner and I really wish it had. It went off on a tangent that completely was at odds with the rest of the film, and frankly was gore for the sake of gore. There was no need. The film stood up until that point. It would have got a higher rating from me had it ended at the final bathroom scene.

reviews.author: jameswnunn
reviews.body: It takes 100's of people to make a movie. Writers, producers, costume designers, director, stars and background extras. And at no point did anyone stop and ask what the hell are we doing here? What theme are we trying to convey? Do we need to see a zoomed in shot of Demi Moore's uterus for 45 seconds? How many times can we show Qualley's asshole before it becomes gratuitous and annoying? How much nudity is the correct amount to show that Hollywood is a cesspool and treats women like sexual objects while we treat the women like sexual objects for the entire film? Failure has hit an all time low.

reviews.author: mailsalmaan
reviews.body: This movie is not for the faint of heart. The visuals are so disturbing that you'll find yourself wanting to look away, yet unable to stop watching. The graphic and unsettling imagery creates an intense atmosphere of discomfort, keeping you hooked despite the visceral reactions it provokes. The film challenges your endurance and forces you to confront dark, uncomfortable themes. On top of that, the actors deliver powerful performances, with each one excelling in their role. Their commitment to the characters elevates the film, making it all the more gripping and haunting. This movie isn't something you watch casually. It requires a certain mindset to fully engage with it, as it forces you to grapple with your own reactions to the disturbing content.

reviews.author: kunjabihariji
reviews.body:
I don't write reviews here, but this movie compelled me to.

It is horrifying on multiple levels. In terms of gross factor it is just magnificent. I had to flinch through my fingers for many scenes, and often stood up out of my chair to watch from a distance.

The body horror doesn't overshadow the other qualities of the film though.

The Cinematography is unmissably impressive and mesmerizes you throughout the film.

The Characters have a balance between mundane gravity and caricaturist bordering on surreal

There is a meta horror to it as well, in the way that the grotesque events portray the kind of pernicious obsession people have about their appearance. How the desperate need for acceptance drives us to undergo horrible ordeals.

You just know that if this were a reality, there'd be shambling fleshheaps wandering around the tentcamps in LA

This was one of the more eerie aspects of the film. I kept thinking in the back of my head, ... people would do this

There's really so much to get into, but I'll leave that to the video essayists nerds

I thought the casting was great for this as well. That hot girl who was stuffed into a Tarantino movie, somehow fits the bill exactly.

Demi Moore, the highest paid actress of the 90s, playing a wilting superstar. Just perfect.

reviews.author: klastaitas
reviews.body:
Grotesque and surreal body horror has had a slight resurgence recently (the films of Julia Ducournau come to mind) but so far not one has managed to step out from the restrictions of it's own genre and create an original movie; one which doesn't hold back in it's goriness or it's scathing social commentary. It's safe to say that Coralie Fargeat has done that.

The stunning cinematography, which switches between a commercial "advertisement" style to a more subdued and dark atmosphere, hones in on the ideas of consumer culture and body image which form the core of what the film wants to say. The diet coke product placement was so in your face that it's clearly a joke and even reminded me of the pepsi advert that played before the film started.

The performances from Demi Moore and Margaret Qualley are phenomenal with Qualley delivering a terrifying idea of beauty and sex appeal.

The costume and make-up department went above and beyond to create a horrifying creature and even a sperm-like breast which got a few chuckles and gasps at the cinema.

There is only one thing for me which stops it from being excellent and that is the odd voiceover repetition of certain lines and the insertion of some random shots that didn't do a whole lot. The voiceover repetition technique seems stale and old now more relegated to cheesy detective stories and cartoons.

Definitely the most interesting film I've seen this year and it makes me want more from Coralie Fargeat as she has proven herself to be a boundary-pushing filmmaker. It is also, to be embarrassingly honest, the funniest film I have seen in a long, long time - if you're not prepared to laugh at a freakish creatures get ready with me, braindead cokehead Hollywood executives and a demented old lady eating enough food for a dozen people...well, I'd consider watching something else. Something that won't make you concerned that behind every young Hollywood actress is a Cronenbergian creature locked in a cupboard.

reviews.author: panta-4
reviews.body:
Dennis Quaid really stole the show as Harvey in this film, thanks to Coralie Fargeat, the talented French writer and director. "Harvey" truly captured the exploitation within the entertainment industry, while the rest felt like a facade for a troubled woman's fantasy. Instead of gracefully aging like fine wine, Demi Moore as Elisabeth Sparkle seemed like a mutton wanting to reclaim its youthful spring lamb days, and we all watched how that turned out! It's a disturbing and perplexing film with stunning visuals, plenty of twists, nudity, and some gore!

The French really know how to make an impact, and Coralie Fargeat made a strong return after her 2017 film "Revenge." She's always been a fierce advocate for gender issues, and this film pushes back against societal norms and stereotypes. However, it didn't quite hit the mark when it came to exploring themes like rebirth, female empowerment, and the intricacies of human nature. In her follow-up, "The Substance" (2024), she keeps her signature style of being "blunt, bloody, and stylish," but the blend of exploitation and feminism didn't resonate as well this time around.

reviews.author: fabiopetz
reviews.body:
Very original, beautiful and grotesque multi-layered dark science story that is so human. It goes beyond the obsession for youth, and also talks about balancing oneself. Lots of substance to reflect one.

Yet, it has so many great Lynch, Cronenberg and Kibrrick rerences, full of detail with forms, patternns, colours and soundtrack that build through the film and culminate in an epic ending. So if you like them definitely worth watching.

The ending, like the whole film, is grotesque and beautiful, sad and funny but on steroids. I still cannot believe how many references that scene has. It's like Black Swan meets Carrie, Elephant Man, Mulholland Drive, Alien, Joker and South Park in one scene. How is that possible? Fine work of art!

It's amazing to watch Demi More delivering precisely on every scene in such a challenging role, even as a crawling cockroach. Margaret Qualley and Dennis Quaid are also perfect.

Best film of the year for sure.

reviews.author: benjlinacre
reviews.body:
I came to IMDB after watching this movie with the sole intention of having a good laugh at some of the 1 star reviews, I love how we all fall apart showing our distaste for something as subjective as a movie!

But then I felt compelled to leave my own, to add balance, because I genuinely thought this was a brilliant watch. It made me think, it made me feel uncomfortable, it made me laugh, it kept surprising me, and it stayed with me for longer than five minutes - which is a great achievement for any modern movie.

I'm no film critic and require nothing else from my time in front of the screen other than to feel entertained and to have something to talk about at the end - but this delivered on all counts and looked great for extra credit!

Blasting this movie for being vile, disgusting and revolting (since when were they bad things in cinema?) does nothing other than pique my interest even more. Criticisms on the gory content make even less sense to me, like bashing Stevie Wonder based on the premise that you don't like Motown music, absolutely fine if it isn't your thing, but other genres are available people!

I enjoyed this movie more than any other that I've seen for a long while, you may enjoy it too!

reviews.author: idontknowiknowthatidontknow
reviews.body:
-Damn the main actress has got a tight and sexy body. I really love her big bubble butt. The director really understands one of the top essential needs of the modern male, and that's is an extremely f-able butt of the female persuasion to unload into on a daily if not hourly basis.

-the director really knows how to film those scenes of the exercise shoot, there's something about it, especially the close up shots, it's like Kubrick except it's not. Though I'm pretty sure she admires Kubrick based on the hallway design of the studio.

-i rate my movies based on scenes that elicit an euphoric feeling from me: Phoenix scene-3pts Her walking down the street with lollipop and First exercise shoot w/the closeup shots-2pts The shape and bubbliness of her butt-2pts

-i do have to say I didn't enjoy the second half of the movie when everything started going south, I understand what the director is trying to do, but it did nothing for me.

-in a streaming climate where movie goers are down and artistic movies aren't given a chance, where it's surprising to see movies last for three weeks even, it's interesting to see this movie is still at my theater going on its eighth week. I actually doubt any movie has lasted that long so far this year. This shows ppl will still come to watch a quality movie however begrudgingly they have to get away from their streaming.

reviews.author: snewkyblinders
reviews.body:
The Substance had the potential to be a gripping commentary on beauty and the grotesque, but it relies too much on excessive gore to deliver its message. The film's visual effects are impressive, but the horror becomes repetitive and gratuitous, detracting from the deeper themes it initially sets up. Rather than building tension, the shock value feels forced and overdone, leaving the story lacking in impact.

While there are moments of brilliance in its direction and performance, particularly from Demi Moore, the film doesn't capitalize on its strong start. The unnecessary violence overshadows the nuanced points about vanity and societal expectations, making the film feel hollow. A 5 out of 10 reflects its strong visuals but missed narrative potential.

reviews.author: sgildea-78306
reviews.body:
The Substance is gory, funny and entertaining as hell.

As a satire on stardom, TV, beauty and drugs offering youth and vitality this film hits all the right beats even if it's not at all subtle.

But screw subtle, I wanted this to be as mad as it is.

The body horror is top notch and truly gross. Not usually my kind of thing as it's usually unnecessary but here it's actually driving the story and the scenes.

I kind of guessed and hoped where it was going and that definitely didn't disappoint me because it was executed to perfection.

A horror story that nails the ending is rare but this one is dare I say actually perfect at the conclusion.

This film is so well acted from all involved and they gave others their all.

It's funny, sexy and gross, so very gross.

This is a MUST watch for any horror fan or any fan of fantastic cinema.

reviews.author: ElCinefago
reviews.body:
That was my thought while I was watching this film. Cronenberg and Kubrick had somehow met and smoked some ilegal (in most places) substances and decided they should co-write and co-direct a horror comedy.

This film is such a welcomed event in cinema, a brand new film with a bold idea that dares not to treat the audience as if they were five years old.

The elements of body horror marry beautifully with a superb analysis of our superfluous societies. Down with the old cheer the new!

My advice to anybody tempted to watch this film is DO NOT read reviews and dare to go to a cinema near you and just watch it.

Technically speaking the art direction is superb. The camera work is exquisite, the special effects, make up, "CGI" are perfect.

Demi Moore and Denis Quaid deserve an Oscar each, they do imbue themselves in their characters to a point that you stop seeing them.

Mostly Quaid becomes an almost macho cartoon that due to the lense used will make you feel you're inside a Terry Guilliam 90s film.

There's so much more to say about this film, but above all is a genuine experience and that alone in today's cinema is worth your money.

reviews.author: Lorelie123
reviews.body:
From the very beginning, I could sense that the film was directed by a woman. And I was right - the subtlety with which the themes are explored reveals a distinctly feminine perspective. The director masterfully captures and conveys the painful truth about the monetization of women's bodies in the entertainment industry. Whether in Hollywood or any other country, the pattern remains the same: women are placed on a pedestal of fame as long as they are profitable, only to be discarded when their star begins to fade - when ratings drop, beauty fades, or profits dwindle.

This film is a metaphor. It's not just about the industry; it reflects society as a whole. We see how success and fame, which seem eternal, are actually fleeting. And this is a lesson for anyone enjoying popularity today: success comes and goes. What do you do when it's gone? Do you accept it and step aside? Or do you stay and fight, risking becoming a "substance" - someone clinging to the past and losing themselves in the process?

The Substance is a must-watch for anyone living in a culture of success and striving for fame. The film poses an important question: what matters more - the external facade or the internal essence? Each viewer will have their own answer, but this film leaves no one indifferent.

reviews.author: Reviewer32
reviews.body: I'd give this movie a 10 just for the sake of being brave and standing out with something different while still being on track and proving points it set within the plot. You think you've seen everything that cinema can offer, and slight deviation is just a huge step forward for every movie fan. This one does exactly that while it maintained good acting, storyline and movie logic (which not necessarily corresponds to logic in general). Other thing I like about the movie is that it is not afraid to polarize and even make people hate it. That's just being honest in directing and it goes a long way for me. Bravo movie!

reviews.author: info-87434
reviews.body:
This is an insane movie and I can totally understand why people are giving it 8+. It is INSANE, and after going bat crazy at the half way mark, then makes the halfway mark look very sensible by the last act.

That said...I couldn't shake the feeling that it was trying to say something profound but utterly failed; hinting at depth and meaning, but containing none. Maybe that's the point.

It is very well acted and the last act will be like a wet dream to fans of Braindead etc, but the gratuitous leering in the first act is never really paid off and the bizarrely random Kubrick references...well, just why? It's nodding so much to so many films that it ultimately fails to be anything of its own.

Disappointing but definitely not boring. (Don't tell your partner that is a commentary on youth and beauty like I did.)

reviews.author: nicholafinnigan
reviews.body: Wow, I've just been to the cinema to see this today and I'm in shock. This movie is not for the faint hearted or weak stomached but wow, what an enjoyable wild ride. True horror fans will appreciate this. Yes the ending went a little bit OTT for my liking but overall, this was a crazy, thought provoking, visually stunning, unique and intriguing body horror movie. For me, the tone very much reminded me of American Psycho - it has that unsettling, dark humour about it. There were also nods to other iconic Stephen King horror movies in there (The Shining, The Fly, Carrie). Demi, Margaret and Dennis were all amazing in their roles, particularly Demi, and I loved even the neighbours performance too! Bravo to a new original, crazy, and I think what will be an iconic horror movie 👏

reviews.author: ygzjvrn
reviews.body: The montage at the beginning shows it snowing on the character's Hollywood star. Excellent foreshadowing. The movie has a premise and a plot at first, but the last hour devolves into utter nonsense. I'm really stunned that the scores are as high as they are. It's not worth spoiling, this is one of the worst things ever filmed. It's like watching Black Mirror in slow motion on bad drugs for the second half. I won't be watching anything by these producers, the writer, or the director ever again. Please, just don't watch this. Rewatch a Cronenberg film. If you crave freak show special effects, go watch Freaked. They did a lot better with a fraction of the budget.

reviews.author: banaitytepaulina
reviews.body:
The Substance offers a fresh perspective on societal beauty standards, particularly for women, delving into the terrifying insecurities that accompany the pursuit of those ideals. From the start, the film keeps viewers on edge with its unsettling narrative, though the lengthy final sequence might feel drawn out for some. This intentional pacing aims to underscore the scene's symbolism, yet many viewers could overlook its significance. Overall, the movie is a series of unexpected, disturbing moments that brilliantly captivate.

While watching with my husband, I noticed a fascinating contrast in our perception of the characters. As a woman with her own insecurities, I found the characters' actions deeply relatable, while he, whose value isn't tied to his appearance, found their choices somewhat foolish. The character development is compelling; both main characters spiral downward throughout the film, only to discover a form of liberation by the end. The performances from the cast are nothing short of outstanding.

The film's themes are hard-hitting and resonate profoundly, particularly regarding women's beauty standards, the loss of self-worth with age, and the desire to escape one's reality. These messages are presented in a gut-wrenching manner, forcing viewers to confront their relationships with their own bodies and appearance. I found myself reflecting on those themes long after the credits rolled.

Visually and aurally, The Substance excels with remarkable cinematography and a haunting sound design. The unsettling visuals are paired with a techno soundtrack that, while jarring, enhances the film's raw brutality. The audio, filled with disquieting sounds, lingers in mind, creating a confusing yet captivating atmosphere.

The pacing throughout the film is generally well-executed, aside from the aforementioned lengthy ending, which may feel excessive to some viewers. However, the emotional impact is undeniable. As someone navigating the transition from adolescence to womanhood, I found myself grappling with the film's themes during a time of personal reflection. It's remarkable how such a disturbing film can evoke such delicate emotions.

When comparing The Substance to other films, Requiem for a Dream comes to mind due to its strong themes and striking visuals. I would highly recommend this film to horror enthusiasts and those grappling with body image issues. However, it may not be suitable for viewers who are sensitive to body horror, as the film contains heavy imagery that can be difficult to stomach.

In conclusion, The Substance is a thought-provoking exploration of beauty standards that challenges viewers to confront their insecurities. Its combination of disturbing visuals and powerful themes makes it a must-watch for those willing to delve into its unsettling depths.

reviews.author: balscalatoosa
reviews.body:
Demi Moore for President.

I do believe this is the first movie that has ever made me 1 - squrim in my chair more than once 2 - gasp out loud several times 3 - cover my eyes and 4 - plug my ears. As soon as I left that theater I go on the internet looking for that yellow coat that Demi More wears so I could get cracking on my Halloween costume! You can bet your smash I'm trying to recreate that look for All Hallows Eve. My only gripe is that it genuinely could have been shorter, by about half an hour. I didn't feel the runtime until the last act when I was literally plugging my ears because that siren sound was just way, way, way too loud. Demi Moore for President.

reviews.author: henriquebfirmino
reviews.body:
Demi Moore does a fenomenal job, and so does Dennis Quaid and. Margaret Qualley, but please considerer just whatching 1h45min for the future sack of the movie's great upcome (lets let the downfall for others to see).

Now, cutting to the chase, the first three quarters of the movie are incredibly well pulled off, it would be and easy 8 out of 10. However, the last minutes, the "final chapter" per say, it's what dwells in my judgment. I totally understand the meaning of the end, but was it really necessary to finish in such a grotesque way? It just feels to much to unveil at an ending with "little" visual content such as that thoughout the film.

The movie is entirely based on self unappreceation and lack of self love, and the limits we croos in search for that willingness to live and be happy with ourselves, the ideia is that we are always looking for the perfect self and at end we end up losing what we had best.

It looks like The Shinnig (1980), Requiem for a Dream (2000) and Suspiria (1977) had a child with consanguinity issues, consequense of the "incest" between the above. It has the moral idea of Requiem for a Dream, the vengeance of Suspiria, and the suspense and thrillerness of The Shinning (and blood, to much blood).

reviews.author: maulcun
reviews.body:
The Substance encapsulates the idea your greatest enemy is yourself. It's a modern fable about the pressures we face from a society obsessed with beauty, youth, and external validation.

The quest for a ''better self'' slowly erodes the identity of several people when getting older. The way how main character self-loathed in the movie is indicative of how so many beautiful women tear themselves apart chasing perfection that doesn't actually exist. They are already beautiful in their own way.

It is very gory but the gore tells a story of self-destruction both physically and mentally.

In the end, you should learn to love yourself, and do not measure your self esteem from society.

reviews.author: micahbboswell27
reviews.body:
Interesting film, shot in a very interesting way. It includes a lot of great cinematography and some interesting acting. Dennis Quaid does a great job at portraying a creepy business tycoon who doesn't care about people's feelings. Demi Moore, of course, knocks it way out of the park.

Honestly, my only problem is that the new version of Demi Moore is relatively unattractive and has receding gums/horse teeth. I've seen her other things and have had the same issues with her there. If you're presenting someone as the ultimate version of someone else, this is stupid. It makes no sense. I may catch some flack for this, but I don't care. At the end of the day, solid film! Enjoy.

reviews.author: ppriest-3
reviews.body: One is hard pressed to find comparisons. The density of horror is relentless and cumulative. Demi Moore and Margaret Qualley give unique and brilliant performances. Beauty and the Beast takes on a completely macabre interpretation. The camera work close-ups are amazing and surreal . It shares some of the psychedelic and nightmarish revels of Clockwork Orange but goes well beyond. The juxtaposition of hypersexuality and the evolving underlying ugliness that is just below the surface is a repellent cocktail. Moore and Qualley lead one through a kind of gut wrenching aversion therapy as their remarkable bodies are wrenched into nauseating horrors that would have terrified Hieronymus Bosch. An instant classic for sure.

reviews.author: simeon-44214
reviews.body: Great script and story. Actors beautiful and great performance. At the end (last 45 minutes) I got uncontrollable laughter at the cinema because the movie turns into an absurd comedy. Luckily I was not the only one laughing! I wonder if laughter was the goal of the creators. If not than the movie failed it's goal. It sure is a mix between sort of not really horror and absurd comedy. Intriguing mix. The screenplay I liked as well nice close ups. The end is a part where a lot of people walked put of in the cinema but i think that was overreacting. Its not that bad. But overall because of the absurdity i have to give it a 6.

reviews.author: bobgio
reviews.body: What started out as a clever idea increasingly became grosser and grosser. The minute Margaret Qualley popped up, the grossness began. It's billed as horror comedy. This wasn't horror or comedy but what I would expect from a 12 year-old mind and an unlimited special effects budget guided by a mentally insane fx guy. The grossness turned into stupidity at the end so much so I was asking out loud "Why?" and "Really?". Save your money, watch it on cable if you must. But if you find that you can't take it anymore and turn it off before it ends, you'll understand what I wrote here wasn't wrong. You've been forewarned.

reviews.author: johannes2000-1
reviews.body:
This movie is definitely something else: a next-level (body) horror that is totally uncompromising, showing every gruesome and sordid detail without even the tiniest restraint! Combined with an intelligent story full of significant metaphors, some extraordinary photography and awesome VFX, it provides an extremely intense experience. It's definitely not for the tenderhearted, and even diehard gore-aficionados will at times be overwhelmed.

I totally agree with so many reviewers and the international press, that Demi Moore is outstanding, and one can only take a deep bow for her courage to comply with the director's need for unrestrained realism. Dennis Quaid as the slimy network manager is absolutely hilarious, and Margaret Qualley is perfect as the young alter ego of Moore.

My only (nitpicking) reservation concerns the duration of the movie: with almost two and a half hours I think it's overlong, it maybe could have used, especially towards the end, a bit sharper editing. But for the rest this modern Grimm-fairytale with echos of gothic tales like Dorian Grey and Jekyll & Hyde is close to perfection!

reviews.author: MikesIDhasbeentaken
reviews.body:
This isn't a good movie, it's not deep, clever, or anything it's desperately trying to be.

Yeah yeah metaphor after metaphor and whatever, i think there was a point being made, and actually there were times when i thought it made it well.

But most of the time it shoves it's point down your throat so much you know what is going to happen next. It was too blunt.

The last act seemed inevitable from the start, and maybe they thought it too so added a load of blood to try and surprise it up.

The best thing about this though, is that it did have a point, and was all a bit weird. I don't think it mixed the weird comedy in well, but at least it was weird. And will be something you'll be talking about after for a while.

reviews.author: pettitthomas
reviews.body:
At first I thought 'this doesn't seem as crazy as I've read about' and I like me a horror. But it really gains momentum and genuinely some people walked out before it finished. Apparently one lady freaked out so much she had a nose bleed in the female toilets afterwards. It lives up to expectations by the end and will go down as an instant classic and a very unique horror.

If you like horror, shock films, or want to see something genuinely memorable and different, see this. You best have a strong stomach and you've been warned in advance! Both Demi Moore and Margaret are great and Dennis is a great minor character. Big thumbs up!

reviews.author: A_Different_Drummer
reviews.body: Bottom line: in today's fast-moving world, where most people have the attention span of a guppy, if you are going to do a film that runs 2 and a 1/4 hours, it had better be something special. In this case, writer/director Coralie Fargeat delivers, bigtime. The core story, a horror tale, is relevant and clever. But the direction, the camera angles, the cuts, the way Fargeat takes a simple action such as eating shellfish and gives it gravitas, meaning, that takes the film to a whole new level. Also somehow reassuring that, when a Hollywood casting director needed to find someone who does not look their age, they went (again!) for Demi Moore. Ms. Moore is here 61 playing 50 and doing a great job of it. Overall style more Bob Fosse than Cronenberg. One of the best films of its genre in quite some time. ((Designated "IMDb Top Reviewer." Please check out my list "167+ Nearly-Perfect Movies (with the occasional Anime or TV miniseries) you can/should see again and again (1932 to the present))

reviews.author: galgusa13
reviews.body:
It took me several days to process what I had witnessed and to come to terms with my thoughts about the movie- the film and its concept were excellent, I felt that the graphic scenes were essential to demonstrating its idea and we could say that it raises a lot of problems regarding body image in particular and self-image in general, or even more than that, you could also interpret it as a fable about mother-daughter relationships if you'd like.

But! The film's finale was what ruined it for me. I don't get it; you had the intelligence to create such a fantastic film, but couldn't you come up with a less dumb ending?

So overall the movie was great, just a bad ending.

reviews.author: vqwcxsny
reviews.body: I just can't stop thinking about The Substance, it's stuck in my brain and will never fade like so many other movies do. Every minute felt purposeful, building to these moments of uncomfortable self-awareness where you realise you're also part of the problem. Demi Moore is exceptional in this biting exploration of how society vilifies older women as "monsters," while older men are allowed to thrive unchallenged. One moment that haunts me is the close-up of an Deinis Quaid gorging himself on messy prawns, so revolting yet perfectly symbolic of the double standards. He's still successful, still unquestioned, while women are punished for simply existing. And that ending, glorious, gross, hilarious, and cringe-worthy all at once, it packs a punch that stays with you. The underlying messages and sharp commentary on beauty, gender, and ageism are so well-crafted. This is the kind of film that makes you uncomfortable but leaves you better for it. Damn, it's good.

reviews.author: gpalkas
reviews.body:
Definitely the worst movie I've ever seen in my life.

The plot is pathetic and proves that even interesting and profound themes (vanity, self-love, the shared destiny of everyone in a society, the need to know how to grow old) can be wasted by a minor (?!?) artist. It's like expecting a two-year-old child to prepare a tasty meal just because they've been given good quality ingredients.

The beginning was interesting, but MANY points made no sense at all. She gets products that create a new body completely for free; there is no instruction on how to use the product; she leaves the bodies lying on the ground for a week and there is no consequence But the ending outdid itself as the most ridiculous sequence of scenes I've ever seen.

reviews.author: diegogue
reviews.body:
In my opinion, the main problem with *The Substance* is that Demi Moore is, and always has been, a very mediocre actress with a very limited range of expression. Margaret Qualley, on the other hand, is an excellent actress who can convey a lot even without speaking. It's awkward to see both of them playing the same character, especially since they don't look alike at all, not even in skin tone. The story is nothing special; it's almost like a weak episode of *Black Mirror*. I don't understand how it won a screenplay award at Cannes, since it's not particularly well-written, but anyway, it's a movie that aims to criticize and satirize the cult of beauty. However, it does so from a shallow, superficial point of view. Good cinematography, good art direction, weak script, and uneven performances (Dennis Quaid is neither good nor bad, just unpleasant).

I could say it would have been much more fun to cast Andie MacDowell, Qualley's biological mother, in Demi Moore's role because she looks more like Qualley and is also a good actress, but still, I think the story is mediocre. I know it's a movie that has generated a lot of buzz and been successful, but I didn't like it.

reviews.author: wet_bandit
reviews.body:
"The Substance" for the most part is a brilliantly original arty film. Part dark sexy satire, and wild body horror. Its really one of those creative horror films that gets into your head as opposed to a trashy horror.

The film makes realistic points about beauty standards and addiction. But at times does this in a hilarious way, and the performances in the movie are great. You've never seen Demi Moore like this, and Dennis Quaid is also a standout as a sleazy manager. The movies never boring with its wild imagery, and is genuinely jaw dropping when it gets to its horrific moments.

So far so good right. But does the last 20 minutes or so go overboard? I guess it would have been worse if they hadn't gone all in. But it made for awkward viewing watching the movie at an afternoon showing full of older cinema goers.

All i can say is "the Substance" is definitely original, and mostly excellent. Which is what most of us want. But you should also avoid the movie if you get freaked out by needles.

reviews.author: Messofanego
reviews.body:
"You are one. You can't escape yourself."

Like an unholy fusion of hyperpop and body horror, this Cronenbergian dystopia about unrealistic beauty standards, body hypercapitalism, pretty privilege's halo effect, desirability, mortality, and misogyny is intensely memorable, grotesque, and stylish. The in-your-face shot composition, fish eye lenses, and camera angles by DOP Benjamin Kracun often lay out the symbolism very quickly, without needing much dialogue or exposition. It's crude, campy, maximalist, and not subtle whatsoever which is an unexpected style change from Coralie Fargeat's previous Revenge which was more minimalist and realistic (if you told me Julia Ducournau directed this, I wouldn't have questioned). My wife didn't know the director was a woman cause of all the objectifying camera angles of Margaret Qualley's Sue, which I found to be an interesting comment. I would say that's the point, especially with the workout scenes where the camera ogles with intense butt closeups for the audience and shareholders who unsurprisingly are old creepy white men. The DOP being a man but the director and writer being a woman, it's an interesting juxtaposition and maybe it's meant to be the objectifying male gaze under Coralie's direction. I can't help but be a sucker for bookended full circle editing (Coralie Fargeat also edited along with Jerome Eltabet and Valentin Féron), and here it involves the star of fame plaque. Valerie Deloof's sound design and Victor Praud's foley work are the standout backbone of the squeamish, wince-inducing body horror and surrealism. The practical effects by Pierre Hugueny's team and Olivier Afonso's special makeup effects team are absolutely phenomenal in selling the grotesque body transformations and I won't get the visual of Demi Moore's agape face with pained noises out of my head. There are so many memorable visuals like that of teeth, tumours, and viscera that will stick with me.

However, it's not just an aesthetically rapturous work. Demi Moore and Margaret Qualley work brilliantly as they descend into madness and it works really well as a two-hander even if they don't share the screen often. The lengths they go to battle each other is excruciating and tragic. There are some cutting lines like, "You are the only lovable part of me, I need you because I hate myself". Their character motivations are believable even if unwise, when their career or will to live are on the line. Dennis Quaid, thanks to the sound design and intense closeups, is the most repulsive male character in recent history. The very first short of him is him peeing at a urinal with his face jammed uncomfortably close into the side of the camera and his next shot is him eating prawns with nauseating sound effects and closeups. The two main characters get introduced with huge title cards but the film does an awesome late stage addition that really takes the climax to the next level that speaks to homage of Requiem of a Dream, Carrie and The Thing. It's not the most complex of performances or character arcs asked of these actors but they sell it with such aplomb. There is a certain moment that speaks to the misogyny latent in a lot of horror films when it comes to old women and ugliness as being so horrific.

Fans of Cronenberg, body horror, surrealism, dystopian satire, anticapitalist critiques, and maximalist style, will be eating well here, but I can see others see this as gross and just a style exercise although I found plenty here to be thought-provoking. When I got home from the cinema, I was looking at myself in the mirror and wanted to avoid hyperfixating at my body just like the characters do here, picking out any imperfections and wanting to try quick fixes like Ozempic, fad diets, and surgeries. We are already living in a dystopia, it's just not as stylish as the movies.

reviews.author: jgrayman
reviews.body: So much homage here: The Shining, Carrie, Requiem for a Dream, Mulholland Drive, and most especially every single David Cronenberg film ever! I was too busy being reminded of these and other great movies to fully appreciate this one's also greatness. The cartoonish approach-it had a Looney Toons meets Twilight Zone quality-really took me out though. I loved and hated this movie simultaneously, but the fact that it *goes* *there* makes it worth watching. Superb cast. Over the top cinematography and script choices. If you like body horror, this is must watch! For those debating the ending, I come down on the side of loving it!

reviews.author: miningpoolhost
reviews.body:
This movie is truly a mesmerizing dive into the terrifying depths of human vanity, ambition, and the lengths people will go for a taste of power. Blending elements of horror, dark comedy, and psychological thriller, the film captures the essence of a society obsessed with appearances and quick success, and does so with a biting satirical edge that feels both disturbingly real and hilariously absurd. Moore's performance is powerful, anchoring the movie with a complex portrayal that holds the viewer's sympathy even as her character spirals deeper into the nightmarish world around her.

The plot follows a group of characters who discover a strange, alluring substance that promises to transform their lives and help them achieve success beyond their wildest dreams. As they become consumed by this strange elixir, their individual ambitions and egos take over, revealing the dark side of each character's personality. Moore's character, a woman with a sharp wit and a more grounded approach to life, initially stands out as a skeptical voice among the enthusiasts. However, as her fascination with the substance grows, she is pulled into the same descent as those around her, caught between her sense of self and the desire to transcend her limitations.

What makes that movie truly stand out is its innovative direction. Each shot feels purposefully unsettling, often with unusual angles and tight close-ups that reflect the characters' distorted perspectives. Director choices keep the audience off-balance, making them feel as if they, too, are being drawn into the eerie allure of this substance. The cinematography echoes the characters' internal struggles, creating a visceral experience that makes the viewer feel almost claustrophobic as they are pulled deeper into the story. In the quiet, suspenseful moments, the camera lingers on Moore's expressions, capturing every flicker of doubt, desire, and fear.

The film's soundtrack deserves equal praise, heightening the tension with eerie, minimalist notes that build a sense of dread. The music plays an integral role in the storytelling, underlining the haunting journey these characters embark on and amplifying the suspense in key moments. Rather than relying on traditional jump scares or overtly horror-tinged music, *The Substance* opts for a more nuanced approach. The soundtrack subtly shifts between suspenseful tones and ironically upbeat moments, playing on the dark comedy woven into the story.

Moore's performance is particularly captivating. She brings a grounded realism to the character, making her transformation all the more unsettling and tragic. She navigates the balance between the absurdity of the situation and the genuine horror of losing control, portraying her character's descent with a blend of vulnerability and intensity. Her ability to express the character's internal conflict without words speaks volumes, capturing the viewer's attention and empathy throughout the film.

*The Substance* also serves as a social commentary, exposing the dangers of a society obsessed with quick fixes, instant gratification, and the pressure to present an idealized version of oneself. Its darkly comedic moments make it clear that the film is as much a satire as it is a horror story. Each character's transformation and subsequent obsession with the substance is exaggerated, providing a disturbingly funny look at the lengths people will go to attain superficial success and validation. By the end, the film's blend of horror and humor leaves the audience questioning the very nature of ambition and identity in a world that values appearance over authenticity.

Overall, *The Substance* is a unique, genre-defying film that lingers in the mind long after the credits roll. It's a terrifyingly hilarious exploration of human nature, brought to life by outstanding direction, a haunting soundtrack, and a powerhouse performance from Demi Moore. It's a cautionary tale wrapped in dark humor and suspense, a movie that challenges viewers to reflect on their own desires and ambitions in a society that often prizes the superficial over the substantial.

reviews.author: ellsmellipad
reviews.body: Feel like there is a perfect balance of great writing, extremely talented acting (particularly from Demi and Margaret!)and slightly horrific twists n turns. The absurd moments in the film perfectly reflected the absurdity of todays incredibly difficult standards of beauty in the industry and how we struggle ALONE with that self hating voice in our head. It's also about the length that both these factors push us to. This film was extremely thought provoking and I loved every minute of its outside-the-box scenes; it is truly an assault on the senses (in a good way!). I have never seen Demi Moore in a role like, and I thought she played it beautifully; I can't wait to see what she does with her next role!

reviews.author: rscheetah
reviews.body:
This movie has the basic concept that women have to look good from the day they are born to the day they die, whereas men can get away with both looking bad and behaving badly.

The images are shocking from start to finish but the basic, main idea remains the same the entire movie.

As a die-hard horror fan, I'd say this movie is a cross between dark comedy and horror. Everything is both shocking and funny at the same time. It's like everything is put under a microscope and magnified a thousand times for the viewing pleasure(or disgust) .

The only bad thing about the movie, for me, is the very unnecessary ending, it sort of spoils itself, in my opinion..

If you want to enjoy this movie, don't take it seriously, just enjoy the ride.

reviews.author: NYCsOwnPiTO
reviews.body: I love the visual paradigms and ECUs. I would also like to point out that Coralie Fargeat is a master at the use of negative space. She freaking nailed the angles, close ups, colors and negatives. The movie is about the way humans (especially women but men included) are notorious for crisis mongering when it comes to aging. We all do it and we all fear it or begin to fear it at around age 25-30. It's at this point that we all want to slow time down or even rewind it although we can't. Well this movie explores the "what if we could reverse time" and in the process of doing so they are also conveying the struggle of having to accept that you are no longer the young and beautiful person you once were aesthetically speaking. It isn't enough for any human to remain beautiful on the inside. And that's something majority of people have in common so we are all already connected to the movie. I'm not going to spoil it but this movie was great because we would all probably do exactly what the main character did given the chance, the horror comes from the repercussions. Excellent movie and excellent timing for it.

reviews.author: josephbaggett
reviews.body: Look, only reason I give this a good rating is because it actually grossed me out. That is the only reason lol I like gory movies. Nothing really ever gets to me but I will say, out of who knows how many horror movies I've seen, this is the only movie that got to me and I've seen some incredibly messed up movies. The thing I didn't like was the story. The decisions are always the same in horrors majority of the time...terrible, so that I can live with. It's the story, It left me wondering. I mean she didn't even try to find out who these people were that were providing "the substance." It aimed all at just gore really and tbh, that made me ok with the fact of leaving me wondering. I wouldn't watch again though, not because it was gory, just cause it's a one time watch type movie. I could see why people didn't like it. I'm actually very surprised it got such high ratings. Another thing this movie did was shock me lol I mean, the actress got her first reward from this movie. Kinda of funny to me. I mean, there are a ton of corny bloody movies that are in elite able that just sucked cause it didn't have the actors or the budget for it. Anyways, watch it if your curious. My parents didn't like it.

reviews.author: Falkner1976
reviews.body:
Disappointing hodgepodge that entertains in its first half but ends up not taking itself seriously at all and wasting its undoubted possibilities.

The first part raises interesting ideas, but so many and so little compatible in a coherent development, that it immediately seems that the author does not know which ones to decide on and the plot loses focus. The interest of the story is immediately clear that it would be that Elisabeth and Sue are one, one mind in two bodies, as the messages from the substance supplier remind them. Assuming that it fulfills the pact, that Elisabeth continues to be alternately Elisabeth and Sue, the film could have delved into very interesting aspects of the story.

But the film immediately prefers that they be two minds, where neither lives nor remembers what the other does, and everything becomes a fight between selfish witches who decide to destroy each other without remembering that, in some way, they are the same, or by At least they depend on each other. The plot therefore ceases to make the slightest sense: assuming that the experiment could be of interest to some disturbed mind, what interest for an aging person is to alternate with another younger version of himself if he is not going to be conscious or enjoy the hours of that younger self? All the very complex logistics of living half the time and obviously isolated from everything?

The last half hour is already a nonsense that drags on unnecessarily (the film should have been much less than two hours by eliminating unnecessary, duplicated or simply eternalized scenes in repetition) and makes it clear that everything is quite disappointing and gimmicky entertainment. There is not even an attempt at any time to make the development of the plot minimally credible, not even within the rules of the science fiction story itself.

The idea comes from yesteryear of course (Stevenson and Jekyll/Hyde), and the main influence should be Carpenter, but it ends up being Aronofsky.

Good performance by Demi Moore and good special effects, the best that can be said.

reviews.author: alioncaci
reviews.body:
Though hard to watch, it was doing great for the first hour. Great, great concept. A new concept of Requiem for a Dream. But it lost me when it became too focused on the physical mechanics of it. We "agreed" to the paranormal, supernatural drug concept, but you can't become supernatural WITHIN the already existing supernatural universe.

It could have been 30 min shorter. We all knew where it was going to go. It wasn't sentimental any more. However, the extreme close ups really captured the concept. I would have appreciated it more with less showing of the metamorphosis process, unnecessary blood or violence.

reviews.author: gettodamoofies
reviews.body:
FILM: 9.0 The Substance is one of those films that really grabs you from the start and refuses to let go. I've always appreciated a mix of horror, satire, and black comedy, and this film delivers all three with a sharp edge. I was particularly impressed by Demi Moore, who absolutely nails her return to the big screen. It's hands down the best performance of her career, and watching her go all-in as a fading star is both captivating and heartbreaking.

Coralie Fargeat, the director, is really making her mark as the spiritual successor to old-school body horror masters. There's an undeniable 80s vibe throughout the film, especially with Elisabeth Sparkle's character. She's got that Jane Fonda, leg-warmer energy, and it feels ripped straight out of an 80s workout video, which only adds to the film's satirical punch.

I love how the movie pokes fun at Hollywood's obsession with younger models and "upgrades." Casting a 61-year-old Moore as the 50-year-old Sparkle is a stroke of genius, turning the industry's own weird standards against itself. And Margaret Qualley as Sue? Brilliant. Her character's journey of getting hooked on something she just can't quit is both relatable and horrifying. I'm also a big fan of Dennis Quaid's portrayal of a sleazy Hollywood exec. He's the perfect embodiment of superficiality, and Fargeat really leans into all his disgusting antics with just the right amount of flair.

I can't stop thinking about one particular scene where Moore's character is obsessively reassessing her appearance before a date. It's a heartbreaking but funny moment, capturing the pressure Hollywood places on women. It perfectly shows how external pressures can turn a happy life into one of misery. Fargeat's ability to balance these tones is impressive, especially as the film shifts from drama to full-on body horror and then into crazy comedy that feels like something Sam Raimi would love.

It's one of the most unique cinematic experiences I've had in a while, and I wish we got more films like this nowadays. Honestly, The Substance is a must-watch if you love horror with a sharp satirical edge.
