reviews.author: kluseba
reviews.body:
The Substance is a pitch-black satire, supernatural drama and body horror movie that has rightfully gotten much attention for its excellent acting, twisted plot and wonderful settings. Cinephiles will notice that this movie combines elements of supernatural dramas in the key of The Picture of Dorian Gray, psychological horror stories such as Carrie and body horror elements like The Fly. Even though the film's general idea is everything but new, it has been executed with such care that it might end up winning multiple awards now and in the near future.

Let's discuss the excellent acting performances in this film. Renowned actress Demi Moore, whose remarkable acting career started forty-three years ago, might be giving the greatest performance of her life. She incarnates a former Academy Award-winning actress with a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame whose career has been in progressive decline. When her aerobics television show is canceled upon celebrating her fiftieth birthday, she is afraid to disappear into oblivion. Obsessed with beauty, fame and recognition, she goes to great extremes to give her career another boost. Margaret Qualley plays the athletic, beautiful and talented young woman who replaces the aging actress in the aerobics television show. While she is careful, polite and even shy at the very beginning, she becomes arrogant, manipulative and self-centred as the story progresses. Her obsession with fame, money and sex takes drastic tolls upon her life.

The twisted plot most certainly deserves its own paragraph as well. The movie starts with a slow pace in its first third, develops steady pace in its second third and truly quickens up the pace in its most dramatic final third. The script combines numerous genres fluidly and logically. This movie is a pitch-black satire of ruthless Hollywood executives and fame-obsessed actresses. It's also a personal drama about the challenges of aging and the issues of achieving stardom at a young age. The film turns into a body horror movie by the end that might shock viewers upon first view who are unfamiliar with this particular genre. This genre however has an intellectual point and wasn't just thrown into the mixture to get a strong reaction from the viewers. The movie's devastating ending shows how some actresses and actors are willing to give everything they have and even are to achieve stardom.

Another element that deserves acclaim are the movie's settings. The beginning of the movie takes place in a sunny city and on luminous television sets to illustrate the idea of beauty in Hollywood. The exact contrast is however portrayed when the protagonist ends up going to the man's restrooms as she hears a dreadful conversation of a media executive who speaks of her as if she were worth less than a piece of meat. The same contrasts can be observed in the protagonist's condominium that looks costly, elegant and luxurious at first sight but gradually becomes dirty, messy and soulless. This contrasting guideline can even be found in the film's very ending as an ambitious New Year's show turns into shocking carnival of depraved behaviours. Let's also add that the visual special effects in this movie have been executed with great care and will most certainly leave a lasting impression upon viewers.

At the end of the day, The Substance might not be as innovative as some cinephiles claim but the movie certainly impresses with stellar acting, clever plot twists and most remarkable settings and special effects. If the mixture of a pitch-black satire, a supernatural drama and a body horror movie with intellectual depth and strong messages sounds intriguing to you, then do yourself a favour and watch this wonderful movie. Be aware however that the final third is graphically violent, so make sure to have a positive mindset and a strong stomach.

reviews.author: jamieastam
reviews.body:
Truly a work of Art that will haunt and be studied for a very long time. Astonishing Direction and innovative writing makes this a must see for lovers of graphic Science Fiction/Horror. It's disturbing and digs in deep, but very very clever - even when it plays with the genre.

Feint of heart viewers should run away. Those of us who like artwork to move us from where we are will find genius in this work.

This will quickly become a Classic that is both unsettling yet beautiful. And I guess that's an important objective here.

Hitch would giggle and gafaw with gasps of delight.

Special shout outs for startling and shameless nudity that is used here ingeniously and with stunning purpose.

reviews.author: cristinaaldoileacont
reviews.body:
So much potential and good acting, the entire buildup of the story were wasted on an ending that seemed like a bad LSD trip. I loved the acting, the way the movie was filmed, however it had too many scenes with the butt. Sometimes it gets tiring to see the same thing pointed out so obviously; try to show it in a different way, in a subtle way or through dialogue.

The ending was however, awful, it made no sense at all and it was just plainly disappointing. It makes the whole movie go under "plain, don't want to see something like this ever again". Some of the visual effects were also bizarre, like "low budget windows 98 screen".

reviews.author: hakimghelab
reviews.body:
I had high hopes for *The Substance*, but I made a big mistake. I heard good things, watched part of the trailer, and stopped to avoid spoiling it for myself. The IMDb rating was solid-an 8.0, which, these days, usually signals a decent film. Anything below 7.5 is often a red flag, but over that mark, you're generally in safe territory.

Unfortunately, I fell for the trap. I went in expecting something great, but let me tell you, I was beyond disappointed. The movie had potential, but it completely derailed in the final act. The ending felt rushed, ruined what could have been a strong story, and the blood and sound design in the final scene were just plain gross-not in a shocking, impactful way, but in a sloppy, unfinished manner. It wasn't just the visuals that left a bad taste; it was the way the film wrapped up that made it feel like they had taken what could have been a decent movie with a meaningful message and totally butchered it.

Honestly, I almost want my money back.

Rating: 2/10.

reviews.author: sammuels
reviews.body:
Not only the best movie I have seen this year but one of the best body horror movies I have ever seen!!! Absolutely INCREDIBLE!!!! I didn't know what to expect and the story, the visuals and the ending blew my mind!! I would recommend this to anyone who is into the sort of body shock or body horror movies like The Thing or other good old 80's movies that showed exactly why practical effects beat cgi hands down!

Demi Moore is absolutely incredible in this film as well as everyone else involved! I cannot get over how good this film is and how it went so far beyond what I expected. Definitely would recommend this to anyone.

reviews.author: olavovgent
reviews.body: "The Substance" is a stunning masterpiece that completely captivated me from beginning to end. The film dives deep into the complexities of human emotion and connection, weaving a narrative that is both thought-provoking and visually striking. What truly sets it apart, though, is its bold use of blood as a powerful metaphor throughout the story. The visceral imagery adds an intense layer of meaning, symbolizing sacrifice, passion, and the raw essence of life itself. The cinematography is breathtaking, making every scene feel alive and vibrant. The performances are outstanding, particularly the lead, who delivers an emotionally charged portrayal that left me in awe. "The Substance" is a film that I absolutely loved, rich in both visual and thematic depth!

reviews.author: Mypherium
reviews.body:
Unsettling is an understatement. It's as if the first two thirds of this movie have some sort of plot but by the remaining third of the movie it's as if they just didn't know what to do with it anymore. It's as if they stopped, looked at the first two thirds and thought, how can we make this any crazier. So, it just sorta takes this left turn and goes off the deep end like it's trying to compete with Quentin Tarantino or something.

I encourage every religious person to watch this entire movie with an open mind. There will be scenes at the beginning that will make you question if you should be watching it but there is a really great point to sticking it through and watching the entire movie and not skipping any scene. You have to see the whole thing to truly appreciate it. This should get an Oscar nom.

If this is Demi Moore's last movie ever, I think that would be the most iconic masterpiece ever.

reviews.author: salvadorheroe
reviews.body:
Coralie Fargeat's film has something special that I never thought I would experience again, disgust, repulsion and a lot of pity for the countless cases in women or even men where they have their identity crisis or when they are no longer the center of attention in Hollywood, The Substance manages to be a kind of tribute to several classics of cinema, especially the Body Horror of David Cronenberg as the Fly or the legendary Carrie by Bryan de Palma.

As for the actors, I can't say they are bad choices because I genuinely think they chose the cast well, Demi Moore is a versatile actress where she knows how to consume her character in despair, anger and imbalance as in the same case of Sarah Margaret who can consolidate with a very scary performance as tender and let's not even talk about the great Dennis Quaid, it would have been better to see Ray Liotta in the original script, but rest in peace they gave us another great actor.

Without going into spoilers the ending and those last 30 minutes were so bloody and brutal that it will be impossible for me to forget it for a while, under my own interpretation the film talks about the crisis of the forties or even how the standards of beauty have corrupted society with the facade of covering your true personality under a very pretty false mask, I have no doubt but it is a film worthy of all its accolades and for my taste demi Moore deserves to be nominated for the ocsars or the Golden globs.

reviews.author: jacquesnz
reviews.body:
Anyone can make scenes so real there is no distinction between the movies and real life. The real Art of cinema is in making you wonder and not showing it all.

What a disappointment.

The latest offering from Hollywood, "The Substance" starring Demi Moore and Dennis Quaid, represents a troubling trend in modern cinema - the seeming need to show absolutely everything on screen, leaving nothing to the viewer's imagination. This film takes graphic content to new extremes, apparently operating under the misguided notion that more explicit equals more artistic or impactful. The result is a vulgar spectacle that confuses shock value for substance.

From the opening scenes, it becomes painfully clear that subtlety and nuance have no place in this production. The camera lingers gratuitously on every intimate encounter, turning what could have been meaningful moments of connection between characters into voyeuristic excess. Moore and Quaid, both talented actors capable of conveying deep emotion through understated performances, are instead reduced to mere bodies on display. Their considerable skills are wasted as the film prioritizes titillation over genuine character development or storytelling.

The explicit sexual content goes far beyond what is necessary to advance the plot or provide insight into the characters' relationships. Extended scenes of nudity and graphic acts seem included purely for shock value, adding nothing of substance to the narrative. This approach not only feels exploitative of the actors, but also insults the audience's intelligence and imagination. A skilled filmmaker can convey passion, desire, or even the darker sides of sexuality without resorting to pornographic levels of detail. "The Substance" instead opts for the lowest common denominator, mistaking graphic visuals for emotional depth.

Violence is similarly handled with a sledgehammer rather than a scalpel. Every act of aggression is depicted in gruesome, lingering detail, complete with exaggerated sound effects and gallons of fake blood. While violence can certainly have a place in cinema when used thoughtfully, here it comes across as gratuitous and numbing. The constant barrage of graphic imagery desensitizes the viewer, ultimately lessening any intended dramatic impact.

Even in non-violent scenes, the film seems terrified of leaving any detail to the imagination. Every argument must escalate into screaming matches with explicit language. Every emotional moment must be punctuated with tears and overwrought declarations. The result feels artificial and melodramatic, as if the filmmakers don't trust the audience to infer meaning or emotion without having it spelled out in neon letters.

This ham-fisted approach extends to the dialogue as well. Characters state their motivations and feelings explicitly, rather than allowing the actors to convey depth through more subtle means. Exposition is delivered through clunky, on-the-nose conversations that no real person would ever have. Again, the filmmakers appear to have so little faith in their audience's ability to read between the lines that every theme and plot point must be articulated directly.

The film's visual style further emphasizes this "show everything" mentality. The camera work is aggressive and intrusive, constantly pushing in for extreme close-ups or employing shaky handheld techniques in a misguided attempt to create intensity. The color palette is oversaturated, and the editing is frenetic. There's no sense of composition or allowing moments to breathe - everything must be loud, in-your-face, and obvious.

"The Substance" is emblematic of a wider issue in contemporary cinema - the erosion of nuance and imagination. In the age of streaming and constant content, too many filmmakers seem to believe that the only way to capture audience attention is through extremes. But this approach ultimately does a disservice to the art of cinema and to viewers.

The greatest films have always understood the power of suggestion, of what is left unsaid or unseen. They trust the audience's intelligence and engage our imaginations, allowing us to fill in the gaps and connect emotionally with the story. By contrast, "The Substance" treats its viewers like passive receptacles, in need of constant stimulation and unable to draw their own conclusions.

In trying so hard to be edgy and provocative, the film paradoxically becomes boring. When everything is turned up to eleven, nothing stands out. The constant barrage of explicit content numbs rather than engages, leaving the viewer exhausted rather than moved or entertained.

"The Substance" represents a cinematic race to the bottom, sacrificing artistry and storytelling in favor of shock tactics. One can only hope that its inevitable poor reception will serve as a wake-up call to the industry. It's time to rediscover the power of restraint, of letting the audience's imagination do some of the work. Only then can we return to creating truly substantive and impactful cinema.

reviews.author: chenp-54708
reviews.body:
No joke, this is probably the most walk-out I have ever seen in a movie theater. Maximally around 25 people, pretty much everyone left and being only me was the last one there. And you know what, I can't blame them cause this....was insane.

Coralie Fargeat has just made one of the most unhinged and insane, over-the-top body horror movies I have ever seen with interesting writing choices explored, strong direction, production design, effects, and strong performances throughout. Having seen Revenge (2017), I quite expected insanity and craziness to occur, yet, I am still surprised how the movie really took itself out there.

Filled with gorgeous production, great commentaries, and writing, Fargeat offers something that's really unique that I can't imagine any other filmmaker is able to capture. Its gorgeous colors and writing offers great uses of its setting, providing interesting characters, wonderful performances from the entire cast members, and memorable dialogue moments that are still burned into my memory.

The practical make-up and effects are outstanding. I have to give props to the special effects team because the designs are purposefully gross, shocking, and fits perfectly int a David Cronenberg universal of a story. Alongside with a wonderful score, pacing that never leaves the breath away, and vibrant aesthetics that shines.

Obviously, general audience will have a hard time to stomach with this movie but one thing I could say, this will be an experience I will never forget.

reviews.author: benjaminnoceti
reviews.body:
A really good piece of body horror showing us how women in hollywood are treated after they turn "old" and how they lose their jobs and end up being a forgotten memory inside a 1990 kid's head and i LOVE IT!!

It really lives up to the body horror and like the title says MADE ME GAGGG i cant even with the makeup its so GOOD like, it served the purpose of being gross making me gag but it also lowkey made me wanna take the substance myself cause like who doesnt want a better version of themselves be serious i loved this movie and the poster was right this movie is already a body horror classic!!!

reviews.author: left_us_silent
reviews.body:
People have been taking this movie too seriously and trying to undress all the "not so hidden" meanings and deep truths etc etc. Then being disappointed by a chaotic end.

The whole movie was chaotic!!! So many wtf? Moments, and lots of body horror, but soooo many laughs. Demi Moore was fantastic and had me and my sister cackling with laughter as her character got more and more wild both mentally and physically. Margaret Qually did an awesome job too. A great pairing for this film.

Basically, just give the film a go as a fun watch. It's not a film I'd watch again but I'm glad I've seen it once.

Enjoy and have a laugh!

reviews.author: passtheoats
reviews.body:
The Platform 2 is nothing short of a cinematic revelation! If you thought the first film was brilliant, you're in for a treat that will blow your mind and elevate your standards for what film can be! This sequel is a bold, audacious masterpiece that leaves everything else in the dust!

Let's talk about the plot. The way the filmmakers delve into the origins of the prison is pure genius! Why settle for ambiguity when you can have a deep, intricate backstory that enriches the narrative? This film takes the bold step of expanding the universe and providing context that elevates the original concept to a whole new level! It's a refreshing take that shows the filmmakers' dedication to delivering something truly profound!

And the characters? Oh my goodness, they are the heart and soul of this film! Each one is so meticulously crafted that you'll find yourself emotionally invested in their journeys. You'll laugh, you'll cry, and you might even want to send them fan mail! The depth and complexity they bring to the table make them far more relatable than the original cast. It's a masterclass in character development!

The pacing is impeccable! Some might complain that it slows down, but that's just a chance for the audience to soak in the rich themes and messages. This isn't just a movie; it's an experience! You'll find yourself reflecting on the philosophical implications long after the credits roll. Who doesn't want to be challenged in such a thought-provoking way?

Visually, the film is stunning! The cinematography is breathtaking, with each frame meticulously designed to evoke emotion and highlight the gravity of the situation. It's a feast for the eyes! If you're not blown away by the visual storytelling, are you even watching the same film?

Let's not forget the powerful social commentary! This film doesn't shy away from tackling the pressing issues of our time. It's an important reminder of the inequalities in our society and how we can all strive for a better world. If you're not moved by its message, you might want to check your pulse!

In conclusion, The Platform 2 is a flawless masterpiece that deserves all the accolades it can get! If you didn't love it, maybe you just don't understand true cinema. This is a film that will be talked about for generations to come, and I'm proud to say I was there to witness its brilliance! Don't just take my word for it-go watch it and experience the magic for yourself!

reviews.author: gersontv
reviews.body:
"The Substance" is undoubtedly the best film of 2024. It is absolutely stunning in every aspect, from the cinematography to the horror sequences and the portrayal of multiple personalities within a single character-it excels on all fronts.

Demi Moore delivers a brilliant performance, shattering the feminine ideal in a raw and grotesque manner. The emotions run high from the very beginning, keeping you on edge until the end. The film resonates with everyone because, after all, who wouldn't want to become a better version of themselves? This is precisely what the movie explores: the obsession with perfection and the relentless pursuit of youth.

But don't be fooled-the script and story take the plot to completely unexpected and terrifying places.

reviews.author: UniqueParticle
reviews.body:
Such a magnificent example of appreciate your body the way it is or destroy the body image drastically in any form to me it's all fascinating!

I have the regal subscription this was among several movies I saw today first Never Let Go that was solid, then The Substance which was quite a shock value yet so damn well made and then Transformers One that lightened things up! This movie is basically a horror version of The Matrix where the Demi Moore character takes the rabbit hole down from a surprise drug with so many changes - Holy cow this is wild experience glad I saw with a fun audience!

I usually don't understand laughing at terror but in this case it's genius to laugh at the insanity that burrows into your skin. The directing, editing and style are all impressive genuinely deserves to be talked about in any type of way. I loved The Substance a lot and wish my views could be famous so much talent went into this whacky gem.

reviews.author: bangel3322
reviews.body:
So much hype surrounding this film, and I was so excited to watch it. And it actually was a decent film up until sort of halfway through. Then it got silly, got good again and then was ruined by an absolutely awful ending.

I think it was trying a little too hard with the shock factor and gory body horror, that it went way over the top and lost its way with story that it was trying to tell. Which is a shame because the storyline was great, the acting was great and it could have been a really good film. But the body horror made the film look cheap and comic like, and after I couldn't really take it very seriously.

reviews.author: theboss-11950
reviews.body:
All Sue had to do was follow the rules of the substance.

At first I thought the substance would be the problem after taking it. Turns out the serum doesn't have any negative affects, as longs as you follow the instructions correctly.

The younger version of Elizabeth Sparkle, who is called Sue disregards the rules. This leads to detrimental consequences for Elizabeth Sparkle's older body. Following the rules keeps the balance between the old and new bodies.

It's hard to watch this when you're rooting for the main character to win. But she is her own worst enemy. I feel for both characters. This is a great movie with a lot of important messages to consider for our own lives.

reviews.author: ajikude
reviews.body: SPECTRE DISTURBING KUBRICK LIKE. Excellent story, excellent dialogue, superb makeup and costume and special effects, excellent story, not a dull moment, disturbing, shocking and the cinematography is Kubrick like, excellent sound effects. The acting is good, superb casting. Really enjoyed this shocking movie. Th whole story is well made and many plot twists ....the special effects as good as THE THING. This movie is one of the best movies I saw this year. Almost clockwork orange+The Thing+Centepede+videodrome in one movie.. This is a must watch movie if you like shocking and disturbing movies with plot twists.

reviews.author: miroslav-nikolov
reviews.body:
It's a shocking movie, that much everyone knows. I needed a few hours before it settled and I could form an opinion beyond "what did I just see?!?". The first 2 hours were a 7.5*, the last 20 min... I can't say if it's 1* or 8*. What I for sure can say is that it was incoherent, the two pieces didn't fit together. As if written by the same screenwriter, but directed by two very different people, the second one of which reeeally wanted to make an homage to Cronenberg. That is a missed opportunity, it could have been a very solid movie.

I don't regret seeing it, but there are very few people I would recommend it to.

reviews.author: waynemcauliffe-74605
reviews.body: Just got out of this one and wow! What a experience. Not just made for shock value i don't think and the practical effects stand out over had its day CGI. This film has similarities with Carpenter's Thing, The Elephant Man,The Fly and a dose of Carrie at the end. Also it has touches of books like Frankenstein, Doctor Jekyll and Mr Hyde and The Picture of Dorian Gray. But its all well done with its own originality. Demi Moore is great as the ageing actress/fitness guru. Never better. Her younger alter ego Margaret Qualley is more than a stunning looker too. And how great is slimy Dennis Quaid. Great horror. Ageing get used to it folks.

reviews.author: bruninhhaalima
reviews.body: "A well-crafted film that delivers a solid mix of engaging storytelling, relatable characters, and polished visuals. The plot, while straightforward, is executed with care, keeping the audience invested from start to finish. The performances are authentic, bringing depth and emotion to the narrative, while the cinematography and music enhance the overall experience. Though it doesn't aim to break new ground, the movie excels in its simplicity, offering a heartfelt and satisfying journey. Perfect for those who appreciate a well-told story with a balance of entertainment and emotional resonance."

reviews.author: timlucaunger
reviews.body:
This is for 80% of its runtime an amazing piece of art, with amazing performances ( especially from Demi Moore, who plays on an alltime high with a stunning physical performance, but also a Margaret Qualley, who does a perfect job in depicting her characters innerconflicts and self hatred).

The characters are sharply drawn and illustrate the social criticism against insane beauty standards very naturally and in an interresting way, that still makes you feel with them on their interresting journey.

The sounddesign is amazing and draws you more and more into the uncomfortable atmosphere and tone of the movie.

But the last minutes, starting at a scene with a termination injection feel very random and unfitting.

The grounded horror of selfhatred and self harm in an unaccepting world with insane beauty standarts, suddenly becomes a monster-horror-flick that try's to keep up with its topic, but feels very unnatural und unfitting for both the story and the chracters.

Weather you like monsterhorror or not, this ending feels unsettling and unsatisfying, especially when you think about how great the movie was up to that point and how many great opportunities for a good ending it had up to that point, for example with just a simple fade into the black after sertain scenes.

If you are interested in watching the movie, because of its story, characters and message, i would highly recommend you to just leave the cinema after Margaret Qualleys character injects herself with the first injection (again), otherwise you'll risk ruining yourself the entire picture of this masterpiece by it's artistic monsterhorror ending. (And I am telling you this as a fan of body- and monster-horror)

reviews.author: GrassCrown
reviews.body:
Modern culture herds us toward destructive narcissism. In the end, that will cost you. Benevolence toward your family might (hopefully) create joy. Hostility toward your younger self will not be fruitful.

This obviously applies more to women, as their gifts are given and men gain value (if they are able). The protagonist here obviously fails to identify what is actually important.

That is obviously the point here. The protagonist is only seeking to maximize individualist benefit in the moment. She doesn't have any children nor does she want them or even think about them. You might think this is specific to Hollywood, but it is not. We can see craters all around us.

But, when she suffers, no one is there to care for her. No one is there to check her madness. Those who sought to benefit from her are nowhere to be seen when she suffers.

As a broader point, corporations will also replace you the microsecond you are no longer useful. So girlbossery is not an option either.

A few days, months, years, decades or centuries from now, the capitalists will not care.

You're done.

If you suffer a debilitating illness, your company will replace you in an instant. They won't put up plaques for you. At most, they might buy a cake from the cheapest place around and *poof* you're no more.

But if you have family and children, they will (hopefully) care.

Family is really the only thing you have.

reviews.author: Boristhemoggy
reviews.body:
Have you ever dreamt of a better version of yourself? You. Only better in every way. Seriously. You've got to try this new product. It's called The Substance. It changed my life. It generates another you. A new, younger, more beautiful, more perfect, you. And there's only one rule: You share time. One week for you. One week for the new you. Seven days each. A perfect balance. Easy. Right? If you respect the balance... what could possibly go wrong?

In the never ending quest for beauty a slightly jaded TV star risks a new procedure where she gets to be a better version of herself, but only for half the time. The better version of herself decides she likes the youthful beauty she has and tries to capitalise on the time she has, causing problems in the timeline. This film is of course an allegory of the never ending pursuit of youth and beauty, mostly by women. It's odd to note that they cast Demi Moore to play Elizabeth Sparkle, the jaded TV star. Demi is known for her surgical enhancements, fake hair, fake teeth, and all the other procedures that many film stars now go through in order to combat age. In a lot of cases the constant tinkering does more damage than it fixes and this is what the film is saying. In a hugely exaggerated way of course. Perhaps Demi regrets some of her procedures and feels emboldened to highlight this?

The film is vomit inducing in parts, the gore almost has no limits. The acting from the Qualley (Sue) and Moore is great and adds to the tension, even though both have parts that demand mostly outrageous make up and at times you would not even know who they were. Dennis Quaid (Harvey) also acts perfectly as the slightly manic, misogynistic TV director and he reminds me a little of Stanley Tucci's 'Flickerman' in The Hunger Games. I wonder if that's a comment about how people in his position are 'enablers' in these situations? The odd angle and close up and perspective distorting videography is absolutely brilliant. It's as distorted as the thoughts people have when assessing their own perceived beauty, and what they would like to aim for, but also what they think other people want in the seeming endless pursuit of physical perfection. Perhaps that's the thinking behind the sometimes garish sets, bigger than life characters and odd angles and perspectives: maybe it is all designed so we can see how the entire subject is distorted from reality and exists mostly in the minds of people who pursue such beauty?

At first I thought the ending was a bit silly and taking things too far. But I suppose in reality those who pursue perfection at any cost and age, do eventually implode to the point they cannot fix what they've done, to return to what they had before they started. It can't be ignored though that there are not just 'perfection pursuers' who want to be perfect. There are the 'perfection enablers' who want to see perfection and encourage people to pursue beauty to gain the admiration and adoration of the enablers. It's almost a symbiotic relationship and both involved seem to have a thin grasp on reality.

I dunno, it's up to you to see what you see in the film but I think it's a solid piece of movie making with some exceptional effects, some great acting and a great and relevant story. I give it a solid 8.

reviews.author: obito87
reviews.body:
Had high hopes from he start but got disappointed in the end. Feels like they dragging out the movie and it has little substans other then what i find interesting that the characters name is Elisabeth. In my opinion a reference to Queen Elizabeth I. That was famous for her beauty but then also went to long length to continue it.

This film could have delivered but instead continues to feed the same thing over and over again with small depths to the actual story. It focuses on body dysmorphia. This could have been left after a really good makeup scene.

But the actors delivered all the way. Giving a great performance. Its so nice to see Demi Moore again and i hope we see more in the near future.

reviews.author: andjosdin
reviews.body: Don't waste your time on this garbage; there are much better movies than this one. The film looks like it was shot with a $50 budget. Every set feels cheap, hastily thrown together with props that seem to be pulled straight from a Halloween store. I'm not sure if they were going for a certain aesthetic, but the result is something you'd expect from a poorly made high school play. The plot, if you can even call it that, though intriguing in concept, quickly devolves into a nonsensical gore-fest that feels more like a shock-value experiment than a coherent story. What could have been a thought-provoking exploration of identity and aging instead becomes a grotesque spectacle of cheap, nauseating effects. It is a chaotic mess that defies basic storytelling principles. Any notion of art or sophistication is absent, making this movie painful to watch. Demi Moore's performance is the lone bright spot, but even she can't save this film from its over-the-top, disgustingly cheap body horror scenes that drag on far too long. The special effects are cheesy, and the constant chaos leaves viewers more confused than horrified. Avoid it.

reviews.author: adelalgomaie
reviews.body:
The most perfect movie I have ever seen in 5 or maybe 10 years .

I give it 10 stars because I know it deserve them all.

Every frame prepared to serve the plot. Every detail was made with big effort.

Emotional, terrifying and a refresh of the cinema that gets boring every year.

Yes some scenes appeared disgusting, but needed to complete the movie and people who hate that kind of movies, simply don't watch it, it's not for you.

The movie learns us that you have to be you and enjoy your life as it is, live your live and don't ask for more. I loved the idea when the woman tried to return to it's original self that she hated before and tried to change it. No movie showed this idea better than this movie.

I hope to more works like this from the same director.

reviews.author: juaniarango-91082
reviews.body:
It started with incredible directing, incredible color contrast that clearly shows Fargeat admiration for Kubrick's filmmaking. You grasp the plot and reach a climax quite fast at the beginning of the movie that enhances your expectations for the story development. Fargeat came up with a unique, never seen before plot that lacks in todays pictures but she simply couldn't stand up for the job and make a story development that sustained the same level of delight. The ending was way out of line taking the movie from psychological horror to a Rick and Morty live action. To sum up, great idea, simply not a good story development that end was trash.

Impeccable acting by Demi Moore though.

reviews.author: itstommieboi
reviews.body:
I am absolutely obsessed with this movie. It is a whole experience. Demi Moore and Margret Qualley do a phenomenal job acting in this film. This is art, this is cinema, this is a masterpiece. I saw it twice in theaters and have gushed about it to anyone in my life who will listen. It made it's way into not only my Top 5 of 2024, but also my Top 5 of All Time!

The cinematography and the sound design really make you feel like you are in the main characters body experiencing what she is experiencing. It's a gorgeous social commentary on Hollywood, beauty standards, ageing, and society's relationship to those things as a whole. The story is compelling from beginning to end.

I see a lot of people criticizing the movie and specifically the last 20 minutes. The movie is billed as body horror so if that's not your thing you won't like this movie. While this film relies a lot on metaphors and imagery it all serves it's purpose in the end. There is so much symbolism here.

I am not usually one to act pretentious when it comes to movies. I love a shitty 1-2 star horror or romcom movie. I objectively have bad taste in media. However, I can still recognize when something is a work of art. I feel like the people who dislike this movie either didn't understand it or didn't engage with the message the director was giving. I can truly see this becoming a cult classic in future years or maybe even already is because I am on the subreddit that is specifically just for discourse and this film.

reviews.author: tusharkadian-36624
reviews.body: It's the most weirdest yet the most craziest movie I have ever watched. I'm in shock after completing the movie. This is one of those movies which will keep reminding me of itself for many days or even weeks after watching it. If you can take on body horror then do watch this movie, it's an exceptionally crazy experience. The cinematography is soo well done and the screenplay is just fabulous. The story idea is incredible and it takes really unexpected turns, it's even impossible to image. Demi Moore and Margaret Qualley have delivered arguably the performance of their lifetime. It's unbelievable how perfectly everything was executed.

reviews.author: Mikekay1000
reviews.body:
If a horror/sci-fi gets walkouts in cinemas, yet good reviews, maybe it's worth a look. This film has received decent reviews and even better word-of-mouth so i saw this today and was lucky to catch it before it disappears on the big screen.

It hits on many levels and I will not go on to bore you with details, but it's an amazingly great thriller/horror. The framing, zooms, editing, sound and set and costume design are amazing, and the film uses many practical effects, making one compare Frenchwoman Coralie Fargeat to great horror directors like Cronenberg, Carpenter, as well as Sam Raimi. She has definitely got the chops!

The cast and script are great and it is a real statement on the Hollywood "meatgrinder". The ending is a bit OTT, but so is the rest of the film.

Check your disbelief at the the cinema door and (as long as you are not too squeamish), you will love it.

I predict this to become a horror classic.

reviews.author: Mainecoon999
reviews.body:
First half of the movie is like a series of visuals and colorful eye porn for male audience with addition of extremely over caricatured symbolism and reminesent characters. Every single scene is a diss against Hollywood and its last decade especially after Me Too movement.

Second half rather contains some of real cinematic and genre elements that saves the package in a way. Art direction, VFX and make up are first class. Actings are over x 100 overacting which is not a problem in a satire comedy.

At last, The Substance delivers a cathartic final message in a bloody and messy way. Did Hollywood get the message? Or Did audience decide to protest the system? Or is it just a Cronenbergish body horror with some comedy in it?

reviews.author: antonistakas
reviews.body: The latest film starring Demi Moore was a true disappointment from start to finish. The plot was so predictable that the entire storyline became obvious within the first few minutes, eliminating any sense of suspense or excitement. Allegories and messages were presented in such a heavy-handed manner that even a child could understand them without any effort. The film also ran far too long, with several scenes that seemed unnecessary and only dragged the pacing down. The final thirty minutes were especially chaotic, taking away any chance for a meaningful conclusion. Overall, a tedious and unfulfilling.

reviews.author: paul-allaer
reviews.body:
As "The Substance" (2024 release from France; 141 min.) opens, Oscar-winning actress Elisabeth Sparkle gets her star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame. Years go by and Sparkle is now a fading star, doing a workout TV show. She is fired on her birthday for being too old. Desperate, Elisabeth tries the Substance to create a younger, better version of herself... At this point we are 10 minutes into the movie.

Couple of comments: this is the second feature length from French writer-producer-editor-director Coralie Fargeat ("Revenge"). Here she looks at what a person will do yo remain young and beautiful. The premise is quite simple. What follows after that is the exact opposite. I've seen the term "body horror" thrown around for this, and certainly there is that, but there is a lot more than that. As I was watching this, I tried to think of another film that "The Substance" reminded me of. I couldn't think of anything else quite like it. Demi Moore is nothing short of sensational. Truly a career-defining role and I would be shocked if she doesn't get a Best Actress Oscar nomination for this. Margaret Qualley is equally impressive as the younger version. You cannot anticipate what will hit you in the movie's last 45 minutes. I shan't say more. "The Substance" is (for me) the best movie of the year (so far).

"The Substance" premiered at this year's Cannes Film Festival to immediate and wide acclaim. The movie is currently rate 90% Certified Fresh on Rotten Tomatoes, and for good reason. The movie is now in theaters. The Saturday matinee where I saw this at here in Cincinnati was attended so so. I counted about 10 people at the start. When the lights came back on, we were down to 7 people. If you are in the mood for a body horror and psychological drama the likes that you have not seen before, I'd readily suggest you check it ou, and draw your own conclusion.

reviews.author: mrouttt
reviews.body:
The Substance is a film that will clearly divide viewers.

But one thing is certain: this is a prodigious cinematic tour de force.

From a purely aesthetic point of view, every shot seems to have been given the utmost attention, and the staging ideas are brilliant.

Without spoiler, the story is just as graphic as it is symbolic. The exploration of the human psyche is brilliantly staged, showing the conflict that every human being faces between his inner self and the face that we want to show in public.

The only default I can find with the film is that it runs a little long here and there, and gets a little artsy towards the end.

Watching it will leave no one indifferent and will certainly leave its mark on you.

reviews.author: bjorndelange
reviews.body:
This movie was absolutely amazing. From the phenomenal acting job by the entire cast, to the way this was filmed by the director. This film will take you on an amazing journey that showcases the harshness of being an aging star in Hollywood.

The movie does an amazing job at portraying what this would look like. Despite the Substance being a very unrealistic drug, the way the movie portrays it doesn't make it feel unrealistic. I can believe everything that happens within this movie up until the last 20 minutes.

From the decisions the actress makes to the unfair way she is treated by people around her. There are amazing scenes that do an amazing job at showcasing what this is like.

Unfortunately the movie drops from a 9/10 to a 4/10 in these final 20 minutes. The movie becomes completely unrealistic and me and my partner couldn't do anything but laugh. It's very unfortunate because the entire setup up until this point was phenomenal.

reviews.author: tyler-philco
reviews.body: Dude... most metal movie I've ever seen in my life. Satirical nonsense like "Death Becomes Her" but turned up to 11. I love going into a movie completely blind and then it end up being something like this. Totally insane and worth it. Body image horror highlighting the pathetic nuance of the old, white patriarchy as you live out a woman's Hollywood nightmare of becoming older while trying to stay relevant. Demi Moore delivers an insane performance, as always. Was told by staff at theater to not order food as it is a very gross film. Not gross in my opinion but I may be the exception. Goofy fun and not to be taken seriously even if it has a more serious message about society. Don't read spoilers, just go watch.

reviews.author: michaemia
reviews.body: I recently watched this and found it incredibly inspiring except for the end; I chuckled at the end. The film emphasizes the importance of loving yourself for your flaws and appreciating your unique beauty and inner peace. It encourages viewers not to compare themselves to others, highlighting the value of self-acceptance. The message is clear: celebrate your successes and enjoy the fruits of your labor, understanding that your time has come. This movie is a powerful reminder to embrace who you are and find joy in your journey. I highly recommend it for anyone seeking motivation and self-acceptance.

reviews.author: masonfisk
reviews.body: From earlier this year comes the other most talked about gut-wrenching body horror film (no, not Terrifier 3) to come down the pike starring Demi Moore, Dennis Quaid & Margaret Qualley. A fading star, Moore, who has made her bones being a fitness diva (think Jane Fonda & her workout tapes from the 80's) gets the news from her agent, Quaid, that her time has come & she will be put to pasture. After being involved in a car accident, she gets an aside from a comely attendant that her life is not necessarily over where she gets a flash drive. At home she finds out about the titular serum which she opts to get from a clandestine storage locker facility. The instructions to use the fluid are exacting where it implicitly says when her new body comes forth, she must switch between her & it every 7 days w/o fail. At first Moore's new younger persona, now played by Qualley, gets her life back on track even nabbing her newly vacated position becoming the toast of the town. However as bad must follow good, Qualley soon starts to want to stay past her 7 day limit out which causes some drastic physical problems for Moore culminating in a battle royale between both halves of the same person for dominance. Writer/director Coralie Fargeat (Revenge) does the house of Cronenberg (David) proud (even surpassing his son's work which tends to be, at least by his first 2 efforts, pale imitations of his father's lesser works) w/a thesis which is as timely as it is universal as the ultimate pursuit of young physical beauty seems to have no bounds (w/vicious consequences for those who partake) w/all the actors getting a set of unanimous kudos for playing along w/the material.

reviews.author: aronharde
reviews.body:
When the first trailer for The Substance was released, I was intrigued because it looked unique and different. It didn't reveal too much, but you got a hint of the film's premise. The cast also looked fantastic, featuring Demi Moore, Margaret Qualley, and Dennis Quaid. I had really enjoyed Coralie Fargeat's previous film, Revenge, so I was eager to see this one.

Now that The Substance is out, with impressive ratings and lots of buzz, I finally got a chance to watch it. Unfortunately, I didn't enjoy it as much as most viewers seem to. The movie has both style and substance (pun intended), and the performances, especially from Demi Moore at age 61, were incredible. She was a perfect fit for her role, and Margaret Qualley also did an amazing job, bringing real depth to her character.

The film tackles a topic not often discussed but one that plays a significant role in modern society, especially in Hollywood and the entertainment industry. Combined with striking body horror, fantastic practical effects, and intense gore, The Substance is truly unique. I've noticed that many viewers have criticized the third act's extreme body horror and gore, but as a longtime horror fan with a love for '80s body horror, I actually appreciated that aspect the most.

What I didn't enjoy as much was the overall plot. There's nothing wrong with it per se, but it's just not my favorite type of film. While some people don't enjoy creature-horror or slashers, I'm less fond of drama and psychological horror, which this movie leans into. Everyone has their own preferences, and I'm not a critic who rates movies on their technical merits-I judge based on my enjoyment after the end credits roll. For me, The Substance was decent but not the mesmerizing piece of art that many people are calling it. I liked it, but I'm not sure I'd watch it a second time, partly due to its long runtime. Personally, I prefer concise, 90-minute films; movies over two hours often start to drag for me, and this was no exception.

Overall, The Substance is a good movie and worth a watch, but be prepared for some intense and, at times, unsettling effects. [5.6/10]

reviews.author: knoxfan2008
reviews.body:
A crazy mix between The Greasy Strangler, Dead Ringers and Severance (The Adam Scott one).

There are parts of this movie that make the ending of "Society" look quaint and child-friendly. The substance starts as a satire, then becomes a cautionary tale, and ends up a total farce.

The editing and music are so in-your-face that they're often obnoxious and annoying, but the director does a fantastic job at justifying those choices with just how entertaining this movie ends up being. Throughout the last half of this flick, I was laughing consistently. This is a movie that horror buffs and pretentious film snobs can all love. Letterboxed knobs will love this movie.

This is the most interesting film that Demi Moore has ever been involved in, and Dennis Quaid is the best he's ever been, he gets to chew the scenery more than he's ever done before. Margaret Qualley must be the most satisfied person on the planet right now. She's the daughter of a movie star, has been in many critically acclaimed art films in the last few years, AND gets this role which shoots and idolises her in the single most flattering way I've ever seen an actress shot. She has it all. Could you imagine the ego boost being cast as the Sue character would be? There are objectifying shots so glamorous of her body, that they would honestly make me feel kind of sick if the director wasn't a woman.

I didn't like some of the editing choices that spelled-out the plot, like the viewers were total morons that couldn't put two and two together. Quite a few of the sound effects were redundant and unneeded. Also, the middle of the flick, while very fun, is inarguably repetitive.

Still, this will be looked back at fondly the same way Re-animator and The Fly are looked at now.

Wonderful, definitely gonna be a classic. Goofy, fun, hilariously, blunt, silly and obvious body horror classic.

reviews.author: kuckarutz
reviews.body: The Substance is a gruesome horror that pushes boundaries and then some. Just when you think it's hit the limit, it goes further, leaving you both disturbed and impressed. The cast delivers outstanding performances, with Demi Moore leading the charge into madness. The film blends intense gore with smart social commentary, a feat few horror films manage. The special effects are top-tier- graphic and stomach-turning in the best way possible. It's well-written, with moments of dark humor that catch you off guard. Visually stunning and psychologically intense, The Substance is a bold, bloody masterpiece that isn't afraid to make you squirm. If you're a fan of horror that makes you think while unsettling you, this one's for you. Just maybe skip the snacks.

reviews.author: bankofmarquis
reviews.body:
Hollywood loves a comeback story and with Demi Moore, they have a doozy on their hands.

A mainstay of 1980's cinema, Moore was a member of the famed "Brat Pack" and starred in such films as ST. ELMO'S FIRE, ABOUT LAST NIGHT, GHOST and A FEW GOOD MEN before fading from fame's spotlight as she began to age.

Always bristling at the derisive term that she was just a "Popcorn Actress", Moore took a swing at a "Body Horror" film that would showcase her acting talents as well as comment on Hollywood's obsession with youth and beauty.

And with THE SUBSTANCE, Moore has scored with a tempered, nuanced performance that is very deserving of every and any award that she is mentioned for - and that includes the Oscar.

Starring as Elisabeth Sparkles - a fading Hollywood celebrity - Moore decides to take "The Substance" to regain youth. What happens next is a clear commentary on the internal struggle that many have regarding their relationship with an aging body and a desire to remain young.

Writer/Director Coralie Fargeat - in her first American film - is unflinching in her view of this and, deftly (if heavy-handily) uses "Body Horror" to drive home her point.

And...drive it home she does...as Fargeat puts a Capital B and H in Body Horror, with the 2nd half of this film giving the audience clear reminders of Dave Croneberg films (like THE FLY) and, especially, John Carpenter's THE THING.

But...she takes it many, many steps further, so don't watch this film while eating dinner.

Margaret Qualley is the equal to Moore as the young Sue who takes Moore's place on the fitness TV show she had starred in while Dennis Quaid eats shrimp - and the scenery - as the Producer of the show with little to no morals.

A surprisingly entertaining and thought provoking Body Horror film that is unflinching in it's body horror (the ending will have you say "what did I just watch"), this film will reward the strong stomached with a stellar central performance and a topic that is one to chew on.

Letter Grade: A- (I'm as suprised as you are)

8 stars (out of 10) and you can take that to the Bank (ofMarquis)

reviews.author: danieljfarthing
reviews.body: Fans of tv's 'Black Mirror' will LOVE similarly themed hard-hitting shock-thriller "The Substance" - and those who don't love it sure won't forget it. Dismayed at how Hollywood (represented by Dennis Quaid's character 'Harvey') is dumping her, fading aging star Demi Moore (sensational) signs up to a mysterious service that spawns 'a better, younger' version of her: Margaret Qualley (also terrific). The two must co-exist via certain rules, but they don't, and the poop (and everything else) hits the fan. With her first English-language film, writer / director Coralie Fargeat KILLS it in stunning style, via analogies on aging, body image, misogyny, etc. It is an amazing movie. Wowza.

reviews.author: joymahidulmovierecaps
reviews.body: Coralie Fargeat's The Substance (2024) is a gripping satirical body horror film that explores the dark side of fame and the obsession with eternal youth. Demi Moore plays Elisabeth Sparkle, a fading star who turns to a mysterious drug to regain her lost youth, only to face disturbing and deadly consequences. The film's twisted narrative, innovative body-switching concept, and chilling visuals create a nightmarish journey into the price of vanity. Margaret Qualley as Sue, Elisabeth's younger self, gives a standout performance. The psychological tension between the two characters builds to a shocking, unforgettable climax. Thought-provoking and visually stunning, The Substance is a bold exploration of age, identity, and the cost of fame. JOYMAHIDUL.

reviews.author: info-13780
reviews.body:
The Substance is a film that tackles a pressing issue in our society: aging, particularly in the entertainment industry, where staying perpetually young and attractive is almost a prerequisite. This modern form of enslavement affects everyone to varying degrees, depending on one's moral compass. Director Coralie Fargeat, part of an intriguing wave of French filmmakers exploring horror (think of Julia Ducournau's Titane), crafts her narrative around an actress who has risen to fame and now hosts a successful morning show. However, she's unceremoniously replaced by a younger newcomer.

Elisabeth (an extraordinary Demi Moore) spirals into despair and turns to shadowy figures promising to restore her beauty and youth. She succeeds, but at a steep cost, creating a doppelgänger-Sue (Margaret Qualley, previously seen in Yorgos Lanthimos's films)-who is as successful as she is sinister.

Without giving away spoilers, the film shifts into splatter territory towards the finale, but along the way, it draws from a rich tapestry of references: Cronenberg's body horror, Wilde's *The Picture of Dorian Gray,* and Wilder's *Sunset Boulevard.*

This isn't a film for everyone-those with weak stomachs might want to steer clear-but it's a work that will endure. It serves as a powerful commentary on the spectacle-driven society Guy Debord critiqued, a world now amplified by social media, where the relentless pursuit of appearance consumes us all.

reviews.author: danielle_nathanson
reviews.body: Very original and unique movie. Creative and visually stunning. Great plot and story. Acting superb. Everything was absolutely perfect until the last 45 minutes or so. It was very hard to watch, got grotesque and more and more disturbing. It was a bit over the top to be honest. I think certain scenes were way too much and I started to squirm and feel sick. Regardless, the movie deserves a lot of credit. It really was a masterpiece. If the last bit wasn't so hard to watch, I would give this a solid 10. I want to say I love it but I felt icky and empty after watching the movie. I am particularly desensitized to blood and violence, however this maxed out my limit. There was only one violent scene but for sensitive viewers it may not be for you.

reviews.author: juraj-jerkovic
reviews.body: The film opened being intetesting although it took a while to develop the plot. At that point I was at seven. As the plot developed it started climbing and I was thinking of giving it a nine. The effect the substance had on Elisabeth due to Sue overusing was great to realise that any substance you take in order to be an artificial better you has a detrimental effect on the real you. Then the ending came with the monster that was just needlessly overdone and that part is a five at best. Therefore overall a seven. Excellent acting, particularly Demi Moore. Someone might object but I enjoyed the nudity scenes in the first half. Didnt enjoy seeing the boyfriends hairy ass though :). This is the kind of film about women that a male director can hardly pull off. Just to mention, this is not a comedy at all, so if you plan to laugh a lot, Im afraid you wont. Original and memorable, at moments excellent, the ending part not to my liking.

reviews.author: cody-28669
reviews.body: I rarely walk out of a movie, even a bad movie. This was an exception. The close-up views of the TV producer's disgusting open-mouth chewing at the start was an indication of what was to come. I still thought that it was going to get better, or at least be witty. Nope. Demi Moore's acting was good enough, but the movie quickly devolved into excessively gratuitous nudity for both actresses. Ok, maybe the plot device justified that, so I stayed longer. The "horror" just deteriorated into repulsive gimmicks involving food and overdone closeups of Magaret Qualley's derriere. I tried to force myself to stay to the end to see it was going to have a clever ending, but 1.5 wasted hours later, the scene with Demi Moore in the kitchen told me where it was going. I could not stand it anymore and left. With the 1/2 hour of previews, that's 2 hours of my life I'll never get back.

reviews.author: muhammadkhajouei
reviews.body: "Substance" is a sci-fi thriller that explores the profound implications of technological advancements, particularly in artificial intelligence and consciousness transfer. The film is set in a futuristic society where a group of scientists has developed a substance capable of uploading human consciousness into a digital realm, promising an escape from physical limitations. Dr. Elena Shaw, a lead scientist, faces ethical dilemmas as she questions whether such technology, which blurs the line between humanity and machines, is worth the risk. The movie provokes deep thought on the future is that.

reviews.author: bob-emms67
reviews.body: Really liked this film for 80% of the time, but unfortunately found the last 20% a bit ridiculous and needlessly violent. Great performance by Demi Moore, and a compelling storyline that draws you in from the outset. As the film progresses the development of the situation the character Elisabeth Sparkle has got herself into really has you thinking 'how is this going to pan out?'. Initially you get it and are hoping for 'happier' solution, but ..... The direction and cinematography is extremely impressive, but sadly I just felt the final quarter lets it down. But very interesting plot and worth seeing for sure.

reviews.author: Hakihiko
reviews.body:
"The Substance" is a masterclass in discomfort and fascination, striking a rare blend that keeps you glued despite its unsettling depths. Its narrative is a mix of the uneasy and the absurd, maintaining an enthralling balance between disturbing imagery and intriguing story progression. The film pushes boundaries in ways that are impactful and occasionally repulsive, yet it never feels gratuitous. It's precisely this mix of the grotesque and the absurd that makes it so compelling.

The script itself deserves praise, crafting a story that is haunting yet deeply thought-provoking. The themes are unsettling and sharp. Each scene builds naturally to the next, with a steady escalation of tension that drives the plot forward without ever feeling rushed. This intentional pacing allows the narrative's absurdities to unfold in ways that are both shocking and mesmerizing, challenging the audience to confront emotions they'd rather avoid.

The visuals are equally striking. Each camera shot is thoughtfully crafted, amplifying the tension and drawing you further into the bizarre world unfolding on screen. The soundtrack is seamlessly integrated, enhancing every scene and amplifying the emotional beats without overwhelming them.

The main actresses deliver extraordinary performances, grounding the film's surreal intensity with their powerful portrayals. Their nuanced acting brings complexity and vulnerability to characters that might otherwise be overshadowed by the film's eccentric style. Every subtle expression and raw emotion feels authentic, capturing a genuine humanity amidst the chaos. They manage to channel the discomfort and horror of their circumstances in a way that feels entirely immersive, making their performances unforgettable. It's through their skillful acting that the emotional weight of the story is brought to life, adding depth to a film already rich with complexity.

Having watched numerous films this year, I can confidently say that "The Substance" stands out as a bold cinematic experience. It's as hard to watch as it is impossible to turn away from-a hauntingly original film that leaves an indelible mark long after the credits roll.

reviews.author: r96sk
reviews.body:
Certainly an experience!

'The Substance' is a lot. It's one of those sorta movies that I needed to let settle in my mind before I even started to think about reviewing it. I'm not even sure where to start. It's insane from pretty much the beginning to the very end of its 140 minute run time, some scenes are particularly rough to watch unfold!

I think the only body horror flick I've seen up until this point is David Cronenberg's 'Crimes of the Future' from 2022, which I found to be solid enough but it came across, at least to me, as a bit too forced for shock value. This 2024 release has plenty of that, if not more, but it somehow feels totally at home with what surrounds it.

The story itself is fascinating, even taking out all the craziness with the gore et al. So by no means is this a film that is style over substance (sorry). It isn't anything actually overly original in terms of the base plotline, though the way it is portrayed and brought to life is astounding - every inch is expertly crafted.

Demi Moore is outstanding in this! I haven't seen her in much, at least anything released post-2002, but here she is top quality throughout. Margaret Qualley is obviously the opposite in terms of the former, though is just as fantastic in regards to the latter - great performance!

If you see anyone giving warnings ahead of watching this, they are very much warranted! Even with all the graphic twistedness, which will turn many away, this is an impressively enthralling picture. I may need a lie-down though.
