reviews.author: Nameiscensored
reviews.body:
Coming from all the corners of the internet, "Substance", especially in the way that its main theme was portrayed through the memes, at first glance, appeared to be just one of those flicks, that while being popular in media culture, were frustrating and hence not worthwhile in itself. Thus, watching this movie rendered me an unexpectedly good feeling, when it turned out to be nothing of this sort of films, refuting the given presumption. In fact, it's hard to believe, that they still can make good quality body-horrors in 2024. In my opinion, "Substance" fairly deserves to be, not just one of the best movies particularly in its genre, but overall in the last couple of years.

Despite all that, it's not impeccable - in my view, some moments rightly require to be spoken of in a criticizing way. The biggest complain of mine (which, I guess, many would find very subjective, but nonetheless) is the main idea of "Substance" - making a better and younger version of yourself. It's impossible not to see here a clear portrayal of a materialistic worldview, expressed in the form of a person's strong affection to corporeality, that is so pervasive among the majority of modern people. At the same time, it would be a mistake to think of this movie as an alleged propaganda of this view and the values that come with it. By any means I have no intention to claim it to be a propaganda; quite the contrary - for, the situation that main character ends up in - grueling and shocking for some, or incredible and brilliant for others (like me) - could be considered as the moral of the story, which makes you change the attitude to your body and embrace one of its main flaws - the aging. But regardless of its seemingly redeeming moral value, the whole portrayal of this truly detestable way of life could not but be a turn down for me, even it's just a picture.

In addition to that, there's also a couple of moments in this movie, that raise some suspicions - a scene, where a very feminine, sylphlike heroine destroys the wall and does a very professional job on making a clean secret door to a secret room; and that she manages to build very quickly a carrier of a big pop-star, seemingly not having any identification documents (There's no Sue in database). Those are some nuances that bereave "Substance" of flawlessness, but which do not so greatly effect an overall perception of the movie.

It's fair to say, that the film has a very good quality, so good - that you ask yourself ironically - am I not watching a high resolution body-horror from the 80s? And this is completely normal, since "Substance", in this sense, takes some elements from carpenter and cronenberg cinema, not to mention the final scene of pure rain of blood that resembles the opening scene of the first "Blade". For the matter of fact, you can justly go as far as to say, that it is "Substance" is homage to classical body-horrors such "The thing" or "The fly".

The movie's length is almost 2.5 hours, but its dynamism and extraordinary plot do not let the intrigue to disappear. It is an indication, that the film is really interesting, constantly serving you up with unexpected things. That is why "Substance" is great both as a horror and a movie as such, and must certainly become a watch for someone who likes classical body-horrors.

reviews.author: bradmichael-sewell
reviews.body:
This post-modern horror explores body image, misogyny and the media industry through an explicit yet thoughtful production.

Physical horror fans will appreciate the accelerating theatrical gore that accumulates to gruesome and extroverted ending. Although, the dramatics are not left behind; the somewhat uncomfortable physicality reflects the disturbing metaplastic sense of self that the central character ultimately loses.

Strong performances and cinematography and delivered throughout, although the balance of slap-stick characterisation with an insidious narrative is lost at times.

Overall, this film painfully reflects the human nature to focus on the past and the unobtainable standards that society places on itself with reflection of these consequences. The hybrid of drama and horror produces an intense watch that, whilst overdone in the ending, leaves you appreciating the physical horror and provoking dramatics.

reviews.author: ania-zielinskaa
reviews.body:
What started as a very promising, captivating story took a very wrong turn in the end.

The characters are absolutely mesmerizing and the storyline really addictive. Demi Moore and Margaret Qually are incredible, they deserve to be awarded.

While it all makes sense in the first half of the movie, by the end it becomes more and more unrealistic with every minute.

It just lacks consistency.

I wasn't scared at all, just disappointed and watching in disbelief of what is happening in front of me.

I don't really watch horrors, maybe I just did not get it, but this definitely did not make me want to watch them in the future.

I wish the ending did not get so crazy because this could'v'e been a really great movie.

reviews.author: simoneminotti
reviews.body:
There are movies that entertain you, movies that teach you something, movies that are shot spectacularly. This movie has it all.

First of all the photography. This movie has an astonishing photography. It is shot in an immaculate way. The colors and the objects seem all to be place with a goal in mind, everything has a purpose. It's at the same time modern and old, it has that 80' vibe but it's clearly set in the present and this helps to create a peculiar vibe.

The story is very, very simple but at the same time it allows for tension and build up. It's predictable but not in a negative way. You know what's gonna happen but not how.

In conclusion I think that the message is really what sets this movie apart. Beauty, judgment, bei satisfied with ourselves, to know where and when to stop,

reviews.author: hexx-52214
reviews.body: This movie stars of great. Some beautiful camera shots. Enough suspense to keep it going. Story was good. It was all okay. But in the second half it started to go off plot. It became inconsistent. Suspense disappeared. It became kind of like a shorter at some point. Then at the last act it became a kind of weird comedy that did not match the tone of the movie at all. And finally ended without tightening the loose ends. I mean it had the potential to become a great suspense horror movie but it just lost its way. Shame. Overall it's an okay movie but with a very inconsistent plot and uneven pacing. But I recommend you give it a shot. You may like it.

reviews.author: sogoodlooking
reviews.body:
The Substance might have been mildly interesting cut to 80 minutes rather than at its ridiculous, bloated 140 minute runtime.

Cliched throughout, it would have been stale a decade ago. What, aging male actors aren't thrown aside the way aging female actors are? What, it's not the case that even a movie's fourth male lead now needs a six-pack, biceps, and broad shoulders?

Then there's the director's delirious exploitation through camera crawls over beautiful female bodies, when those bodies aren't erupting into pustules and broken faces.

The Substance might have had something interesting and rare to say about the emotional pain and loss of aging thanks to the script's compression of time and transformation, where aging produces genuine horror in how a body can go from desired, a vessel for romance and enchantment, to something ugly and deformed compared to what it once was, compared to its youthful delights---but Fargeat's craving for shock after shock after shock overwhelms any interest she might have in the realities of aging and its losses.

The film also errs badly in making its protagonist an empty vessel, someone with absolutely nothing going on for her aside from being attractive. In that regard she's had all the advantages, but nothing is made of it.

reviews.author: ethanbresnett
reviews.body:
The premise of The Substance is so brilliantly simple and punchy. It follows ageing celebrity Elisabeth Sparkle who is presented with the opportunity to create a younger, more perfect version of herself. To the surprise of nobody, this is too good to be true and there are dire consequences as a result.

As mentioned the premise of this film is quite simple, but it is so effective. It dives into ageing, beauty standards, self confidence, body issues and more in such impactful ways. It's a great vehicle to explore these themes really inventively. My only gripe is that the film gets away from itself in the final 20 minutes almost to a comical extent. A different ending or perhaps trimming some fat on the runtime might have helped here.

Demi Moore is utterly absorbing as Elisabeth Sparkle. The emotion she puts into the role is fantastic and when she lets loose it's just brilliant to watch, particularly with the more physical aspects of her performance. Margaret Qualley plays the 'younger, more perfect' Demi Moore to a tee. It's perfect casting and two top notch performances.

The effects and body horror are all expertly done. I'd like to think I've been around the block and seen some intense body horror flicks, but a couple of scenes in this definitely had my toes curling. The body horror is more effective when it feels in the realms of possibility, and as mentioned towards the end it gets a bit too over the top to have strong impact, but for the most part it's grim to watch.

Aside from a slightly wobbly ending, The Substance is a brilliantly engaging film. Demi Moore is absorbing, Margaret Qualley is on fire, and the heavy themes are creatively explored.

reviews.author: BoBo_Goal32
reviews.body:
First Shot - it seems that we are going to be framed inside a square. Then it turns into a star and becomes one of the most beautiful scenes of the movie. The end scene will return to the same place and concept and will try to have some closer for the same idea. The thing that will stick at most of the stages of the movie will be its visual side. Brilliant, tight, very artistic and colliery. The best thing that Coralie Fargeat brings to the movie.

In between - the movie will demonstrate a lot of artistic abilities - whether visual filmed abilities or thematic concepts that will emphasize the psychologic side of it. This side is using and leaning heavily on symbolism and ideas about several themes in the movie - the main is the concept of aging, beauty and if we can through inside a little bit extremist misogynist treatment and behavior toward women. Why not?

I knew that the reviews and general atmosphere around this movie that it is artistic, that also includes body gore and horror in order to get to as a controversial film. I expected maybe to like it, for being artistic but also maybe hating it a little bit if I must, because it wants to be known as an acquired taste that is not for everyone to like.

It has a brilliant cast of two female actresses, that each represent accurately her age and era in real life also and it creates credibility. It is brilliantly shot, colored, directed and edited. I fell in love in the movie's design almost immediately. The theme, though it was pretty predictable, was also interesting and engaging and I tried to look for other hidden messages other then tight body that will replace the old and flimsy one. Didn't find it.

And then came the final act, that almost told me that if I liked the movie till now, I can let it go and start hating it a little bit. I didn't get the reason for body horror and use at the beginning, but it had artistic value - the last thirty minutes where so exaggerated that I almost wanted to look away.

Its concept is great, not the first time to deal with age and beauty issues and the price it costs us, as human beings. The trade-of for instant and un-natural beauty was very clear to me, without going to the edge. It has a lot of great symbols, every viewer can relate with, but a lot that almost deliberately pushes away other types of audience, just to spite and show that they can.

A lot of parts with Quaid's character where forced and didn't do the trick and just tried to make us sick from men, as a whole and men in the entertainment industry. Nothing was new here as a concept, not for the Misogynistic treatment of rich men, that are leaders in the industry towards women and not about the way the women see themselves as a whole by viewing themselves as sexual objects.

The way that that Fargeat showed the balance (or un-balance) between Qualley's and Moore characters was great and fresh, but didn't crash any glass sealing and mostly tried to make us sick - at several opportunities and especially towards the end of the movie - kind of ruined it to me, personally and probably a lot others.

reviews.author: miss_emmalicious
reviews.body:
I thoroughly enjoyed the first 2/3rd of this film and thought it presented a very interesting take on the concept of female beauty in film & TV.

Demi Moore as the protagonist bares all and it is a fantastic performance from her - even if a little ironic considering she has obviously 'had work done' in order to maintain her youthful appearance at her age. I thought she looked fantastic until compared against her 'younger, better self' where you start to really see the subtle signs of age. Although I am not a massive fan of gore I felt the use of gore and body horror in the first part of the film was effective and contributed overall to a feeling of unease.

However, what starts as a commentary on youth, beauty and aging and the effect it has on people and their behaviour deteriorates into a comment on society's expectations of beauty in such a ham fisted way I felt I was being slapped around the face with a wet fish. All of the films previous clever subtleties were obliterated in an over the top meaningless gore fest in the end. It was like the director wasn't sure how to end the film and just decided to hit the nuclear gore button. It was a shame as I felt the message about our own vanity and desire for youth was far more disturbing and powerful than the idea that it is all societies fault - which was the message the director pushed loud and clear.

reviews.author: outpix
reviews.body: Every film genre has either been flat or gone down hill in the last 10 years except for one. Bringing smarts to Horror is long overdue and something is happening in recent years. Should you watch this movie? Only if you're not squeamish and have an open mind. Yes there's lot of blood and nudity but it all fits and has a purpose. I loved all the homages to pioneer film makers here. Especially David Lynch; so if you're familiar with his work, you will recognize this along with an Easter Egg in the elevator scene. What has the entertainment business and the media created in our society? That's the question The Substance asks; and it's really quite ugly. Yes The Substance is over the top but that's the point after all. So sit back and float downstream.

reviews.author: babyjaguar
reviews.body:
"Body Horror" and the gendering idea of "transhumanism" has been explored within Canadian horror filmmakers from David Crononberg's Rabid (1977) including it's 2019 remake by Soska Sister. Its remake take on the idea of fashion world and the beauty ideal.

This film plays with what horror scholarship called "spectacle of the ruined body" looking at 80s "Body Horror" genre like Crononberg's latter films but also one can consider 80s U. S. films: "Re-Animator" and "Society". Thus "The Substance" continues a transhumanist pathway in a critique of beauty. There's much flatness in its narrative, nothin new.

It's premise is the same, the buzz is how it works visually, combining science and technology with an old battle: keeping your youth. It goes beyond one narrative, into a 3-part story - the last one being the shortest. And its last story as the most absurd and bloodiest.

The director freely plays with story structure as it begins with a strong, almost linear. Then as the 2nd part unwinds a loose end. The third part becomes an insane scenario met with an uncertain end.

This film can suggest a problematic discussion on the 21st century Feminist narrative. From conventional concepts from the tension and dialogue between characters played by Dennis Quaid and Demi Moore.

The strength of the story comes from Moore's performance as a middle aged celebrity which echoes maybe, Jane Fonda? A film actress who later became an physical fitness icon, Moore plays it with much pathos.

Almost doesn't work since Moore's presence has always been an earthy ine not a shallow persona. But nonetheless considering Moore's actual movie career, it is a strong comeback with this film. Horror and genre filmmaking has been restoring a lot of Hollywood's older actor's with new life these years.

Moore helped this film's credibility and restore her star power, although her appearance is almost gone after the 1st part and abit of the 2nd part. For me personally, the film's shallowness (which it's moral point) overpowered the 2nd part, making it very predictable as human nature unfortunately can be.

reviews.author: JaRo_1984
reviews.body:
As an old-fashion horror-enthusiast I was very skeptical about watching this flick. Horror without supernatural forces at work? Yes, just the fear of aging and falling into oblivion at work. Horror without monsters or slashers? Yes, just the monster everbody has inside her/himself at work. Horror without blood, gore and body parts? Definitly no! Director/Writer Coralie Fargeat manages to give the synopsis a steady flow without boring interruptions (where bad scripted movies/actors try to explain, why something's happening the way it is), mixing the typical emotions, wishes and fears with the resulting actions of the characters in one shiny masterpiece. Hats off for Demi Moore and Margaret Qualley for their intense acting!

Albeit one star less for the (in my eyes) too short medication description - you can't except ordinary people to use spinal syringes, the various sample containers and this "switching device" properly with just a (catchy) oneliner.

reviews.author: Halfstring
reviews.body:
If you're a fan of the Reanimator, Evil Dead 2 & 3 - then the Substance is right up your alley. It's relentless and absolutely disturbing once it gets rolling.

Incredible acting from Demi Moore and Margaret Qualley. Quad is annoying as hell but it's part of the story.

The cinematography reminds me a bit of Hardcore Henry with the wide angle shots and POV views. The soundtrack is eerie and in your face when it needs to be.

There's a lot of nudity and sexual induenduals but it's a large part of the story. And larger commentary on how people get trapped in the cycle and desparation to want to be young.

reviews.author: dzakiriyyasy
reviews.body: The Substance is a clever body horror film. The film contains themes such as ageism, beauty standards, self-esteem, and youth. The story in this film is very balanced, disgusting with neat writing. The drama experienced by Elisabeth seems to depict the world of celebrities who are required to always look beautiful and young, and it is depicted well. The horror is also slowly becoming more pronounced and continues to make us feel disgusted, and it is clear that the type of horror in this film is not for everyone. The pacing of this film is very suitable, so that we can get more into the atmosphere. The cinematography style is really beautiful, colorful but comfortable with amazing shots. The editing of each cut to the next scene is neat. Whoever designed the sets, costumes, make-up, etc., needs to be appreciated. The music is also thrilling and makes the atmosphere tense. Demi Moore and Margaret Qualley are a killer duo with their incredible acting, and Dennis Quaid steals the show. Overall, this film is worth watching in the cinema.

reviews.author: brimichgam
reviews.body: Extremely uncomfortable and grotesque, but as a "Body Horror" movie it is excellent: blood, gore, deformed bodies and more, make "The Substance" the most disgusting, bizarre and strange movie of the year. First of all, the performances of Demi Moore and Margaret Qualley are without exception the best of the movie, this film shows us a very clear message, however some grotesque scenes that should make you uncomfortable are somewhat strange and absurd (exaggeratedly much blood coming out of the deformed body as if it were a fire hose really?) in addition to an unconvincing soundtrack, but without a doubt the film fulfills its purpose: a bizarre disgust.

reviews.author: Maradey
reviews.body:
Where to begin?

Demi Moore's performance in The Substance is nothing short of extraordinary. Her portrayal is so intense and gripping that it's hard to imagine anyone else playing the role. She fully immerses herself in the character, delivering a performance that feels both raw and mesmerizing. It's the kind of work that demands Oscar attention-her presence throughout the film is a masterclass in acting.

While Margaret Qualley is impressive, there's no denying that this is Demi's show. She dominates every scene she's in, and it's hard not to be drawn to her every move. The director's vision brings this all together in a way that's both haunting and visually stunning. The cinematography, in particular, feels like a piece of art, each frame carefully crafted to pull you deeper into the film's eerie atmosphere.

The makeup and effects are on another level. The attention to detail makes everything feel disturbingly real, enhancing the overall tension and unpredictability. Everyone involved in the production deserves immense praise for their work, from the cast to the crew. They've created something truly remarkable.

There are brilliant homages to The Shining and other iconic films, which add depth for cinephiles, and at times, I felt like I was watching a David Cronenberg film-an immense compliment. It carries that same unsettling, body-horror energy that Cronenberg fans know so well.

reviews.author: gdougas1966
reviews.body: The message about the "monster" of "Egoismus" and "Narcissism" was very strong and clear. The first 3/4 of the movie were fun to look at. But, the last 1/4 was not. I am sure that the message could have been communicated otherwise, too. The ending of the movie was too intense, but not in a positive way. It was unnecessarily disturbing. Overall, I liked the movie, though. It had strong performances by Demi Moore and Dennis Quaid, and a creative shooting angle that was presenting the facts in a surreal manner. The young actress. Margaret Qualley was convincing in her role, and despite the fact that she was acting next to legends, she delivered the role.

reviews.author: IndridC0ld
reviews.body: I literally just watched this film (September 23, 2024) without the aid of subtitles, yet I was shocked by how well this story basically told itself with the aid of the performers emoting (Ms. Moore left me breathless) and cinematic craftsmanship that is top-tier. If performers could wish for a perfect role, and a writer could long for someone who would give everything they had to their story, you would have something like what the ensemble cast of The Substance delivers. Without the ability to understand the dialogue as it was written, you'd think I would be terribly frustrated. Not at all! The pure cinematic craftsmanship plays like one of the great Italian operas. Not once did it occur to me to abandon this showing. There is so much great storytelling going on in this film, and yet it never resorted to the kind of audience manipulation that has become the stock-in-trade of filmmaking.

reviews.author: cerysjharvey-75856
reviews.body:
What started off so good and had so much potential, turned into a cringe fest in the last half an hour... There were several points where they could've ended the film on a good note, even 1 star feels generous

The start of the film, the concept, the acting, the cinematography was unreal and there was definitely huge potential for the rest of the film.

However, the ending was an absolute car crash!!! It made you completely forget the original point of the film, not to mention how over the top it felt, when it could've been a much more sad and dark ending.

Definitely don't bother watching, or turn it off at the 2 hour mark if you do!

reviews.author: ryancollette
reviews.body: Well its body horror that somehow surpasses or at least stands side by side with all the greats. The movie itself is also sadly a relatable story i think that anyone could find some sort of parallels to their own egos and feelings of self worth, more so for women and society's perceived expectations for looks and youth... maybe pretty straight forward and predictable, but stands on its own in my opinion and is elevated 100% by the visuals. The pacing is great, the aesthetic of the movie is always visually interesting , the acting is solid, but obviously the body horror and practical makeup effects are going to go down in history as the biggest draw for this film. Coralie Fargeat was briefly on my radar with "Revenge" but after only seeing that, would have never predicted something like this. Id recommend to anyone as a movie in general, but if u cant handle body horror, then dont even think about it. And if u love body horror than u probably already know about this and can be super happy for its existence like myself. I need to see/hear Coralie and Cronenberg in a podcast immediately.

reviews.author: Reviews_of_the_Dead
reviews.body:
This was a movie that caught my attention when the trailer played at the Gateway Film Center. They've been showing it for a while and the music caught my attention. The bits of the trailer I saw intrigued me. Seeing that this featured Demi Moore and Dennis Quaid was part of it. I could also tell that this was going to be an arthouse film. The parts I saw were stylized which when managed correctly, I'm a fan. I did catch this on the opening weekend, the positive buzz I heard across the board sparked that.

Synopsis: a fading celebrity decides to use an underground drug, a cell-replicating substance that temporarily creates a younger, better version of yourself.

We start this off in an interesting way. There's a cracked egg. Someone injects a needle into it, depresses the plunger and then we see the egg separate into another yolk. We then see the creation of a Hollywood Star on the Walk of Fame being put in for Elisabeth Sparkle (Demi Moore). There is then the progression of time until it is cracked, dirtied and ignored.

Elisabeth is an actor that won an Oscar. She's approaching the end of her career where she does a morning aerobics show. She overhears a producer, Harvey (Dennis Quaid) saying unfavorable things about her when she uses the Men's Room as the Women's restroom is out of order. She is let go as the studio wants someone who is younger and prettier to take over her show.

Our lead gets in a car accident that day, which just happens to be her birthday. Luckily, she's fine. There is a young doctor who comforts her and then does an odd exam. She's confused as the other doctor cleared her. What she didn't realize was that he snuck a note into the pocket of her coat. It has a flash-drive about the drug from the synopsis, The Substance. She ignores it until she sees an ad in the newspaper, looking for her replacement. She calls the number and they give her an address. In the mail the next morning, there's a keycard. She goes to the location and it looks suspicious. She goes inside to find a box with her number on it. There's a kit inside. She takes this home.

The premise here is that you inject yourself with an activator. This creates a different version of yourself, the better version. The catch is that you have seven days in this new body and then you must shift back. It provides food for the body that is in the suspended animation. There is only oneself. These rules are strict, with no exceptions. There are injections that are needed, which are stabilizers. A small price to pay. Elisabeth does this, creating Sue (Margaret Qualley). We get to see what the effects are by not playing by the rules as both sides are punishing the other.

That is where I want to leave my recap and introduction to the characters. Now this is a newer movie and one that I don't want to spoil. To be honest though, this is more about the visuals and the acting performances than what the actual story is. What I'll say here is that we have an interesting blend of The Portrait of Dorian Grey with The Strange Case of Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde, plus a bit of Society mixed in there as well.

Now that I've set that up, let me delve more into what we're getting. I know that I alluded to the story not being deep, but there's social commentary throughout. It was managed well in my opinion. It is in the forefront and not all that veiled, I just don't think anyone watching this will disagree. The most obvious one is showing how Hollywood is constantly wanting new and younger performers. It is crazy how long Elisabeth was in the spotlight, but her time has come to an end. This version is also sexier and more provocative as well. It is also fitting that Harvey and all the shareholders are white males. This is a representation of not only industry, but just people in power. Not necessarily 100% like we're seeing here, but still a high number. Since this is a dark comedy, they're going over the top to make their point.

Where I want to go then is bringing back up something that I've said. This is a fascinating blend of Dorian Grey with Dr. Jekyll/Mr. Hyde. For the former, there is a large portrait in the apartment of Elisabeth of herself. She gets angry and throws a snow globe at it. It strategically hits it in the eye, spider webbing the glass. Once Sue separates, we see that her selfishness is reflected on Elizabeth in an interesting way. I liked how that was used as it makes her more monstrous. The other comparison is clearer. She isn't the doctor that created this, but we're seeing two versions of the same person. There is also the monster aspect. It is repeated throughout this that Elisabeth and Sue are one. They blame the other for things that they do, but the truth here is that both are selfish. We are also seeing their true inner self reflected physically by the end. That was a good touch.

The one last thing I wanted to bring up is that there's a commentary here on addiction. Not necessarily in the traditional sense. Elisabeth is addicted to becoming Sue since she has reached heights that Elisabeth hadn't for a long time. She never had a show as successful as this other version. The former did win an academy award though. Sue is addicted to her success. She is selfish in what she does by not adhering to the rules of The Substance. Even if this isn't drugs, alcohol or gambling, it is still in the same vein.

Since I've leaned into the characters and this is a study of them, let's discuss the acting. Moore is great here. It is great that we have an older actor like her who has been successful in her past. Then coupling this with an actor like Qualley who is up and coming. I've seen her in a few things, but she isn't a household name. They do look quite like the point where it could be passed off as one as the younger/older versions of the same person. Along with them, Quaid is great in his role. He's just gross in multiple ways. First his look at Elisabeth and her age. That also bleeds into his look at women in general. Plus, we see him use the restroom without washing his hands and a disgusting scene where he eats prawns. I was well played though for sure. Other than that, the rest of the cast rounded this out for what was needed.

All that is left then is filmmaking. This is where it excels as well. The cinematography from the framing to the angles is just amazing. I didn't realize this filmmaker, Coralie Fargeat, also did Revenge. That is another movie that is visually stunning. This can just look great from the colors to going trippy as a character is struggling to keep their hold on reality. Great across the board. The practical effects here are as well. This is from things like watching people eat in the grossest way possible. It also becomes brutal. It is bloody and just wild what we get here. There is also CGI, but it was used where it was needed. The framing helps here to hide the seams as well. The last bit would be the soundtrack. This has a techno/dubstep song used throughout that is great. It fits the vibe. This is one the best soundtracks I've heard all year. The sound design is on point as well. The only gripe that I have is that this goes too far into the comedy for its conclusion. After seeing it on, I see why but it still didn't fully work.

In conclusion, this is one of the best movies I've seen this year. It has social commentary that is relative while not being too in your face. I love the combination of Dorian Grey and Jekyll/Hyde. The acting from Moore and Qualley is great. The filmmaking is on point from the framing, effects, cinematography to the soundtrack. My only gripe here is that the comedy at the end brought it down ever so slightly. This is a contender for the top of my end of the year list. I want to give this another watch before finishing.

My Rating: 9 out of 10.

reviews.author: yamininbeto
reviews.body:
There are many things well done in this film. Nice prosthetics, makeup and photography, accompanied by a brilliant rhythm and compelling performances. Where it fails is in the fusion of dark comedy with horror.

You have the psychological impact of what happens to her until she is in this television company which should be more serious, the role of the director of the program should have had a different tone.

In the end it's like you took Carrie and put jokes in it, which just doesn't work.

In addition, the costumes, locations and some frames become repetitive as the film progresses and make evident what I believe is a lack of budget.

reviews.author: enviro-24507
reviews.body:
Not sure if the other reviews are stooges as there's absolutely no way on earth that this film could possibly be considered a 9 or 10.

Honestly the endless plotholes should render this film a 2 but the brazen Absurdity kind of saves it because it is genuinely funny and brilliantly shot.

The main gripe is that the Substance is supposed to offer you the chance to live 7 days at a time as a much better version of yourself with the constant reminders that you're still one person. However it's immediately apparent that this is not the case, neither physically or mentally. This seriously undermines the whole story and the whole film.

There's more but you'll have to watch to catch them all.

Demi Moore going from fading Hollywood Star to Tony Robinson from the Boosh is basically the film.

reviews.author: jochang-30856
reviews.body:
I wasn't expecting much outside of some generic, cookie-cutter flick you put on in the background while doing something else. Man, was I wrong. It's phenomenal. The story isn't just original and it's isn't simply well-assembled. There's intent and meaning behind every shot, every sound cue, every visual design and aesthetic. There's real vision for this project. I was also not expecting the horror elements to register but it does. Some scenes are terrifying, and not in the cheap jump scare way. You see these things unfold and settle while the reality of what's happening eventually lands. This is always the best kind of horror, with the idea of something playing out inspiring fear. It is a gross film as well. Lots of blood, guts, body stuff and squish. Shaky and uncomfortable camera angles. Close-ups for things you'd rather not see close up. They even made Dennis Quaid absolutely disgusting, which was fitting, hilarious and delightful.

There's some social commentary here that's adeptly conveyed. Most everyone is aware of the consequences of getting old. Becoming irrelevant. Going unnoticed. Even the best of us are guilty of engaging in this behavior at some point, and then eventually we experience it for ourselves on the receiving end. The filmmakers present this truth in sobering fashion, and they do it well.

It may sound silly, but I appreciated Demi Moore going nude. She's obviously still a very attractive woman, but the role she plays is a person at the end of that consideration and some scenes in which she pensively does this accentuates it perfectly. I heard her speak on past relationships in an interview once, and even though we all know acting is acting, somehow in this insane out-of-left-field fantasy horror the motivations presented comes across as very genuine. Being able to tap into real emotions while on display is true talent. If anyone forgot Moore is a serious actress, they should watch this film.

reviews.author: JackRJosie
reviews.body:
This film is intriguing and exceptionally well-made, though it seems more relatable to women. Its concept is compelling and full of potential, but the execution suffers from a heavy-handed pretentiousness. The story gets lost in an overly symbolic and metaphorical approach, making it difficult to connect with or take seriously.

That said, its exaggerated, metaphorical tone is unlike anything I've seen before, making it worth watching, at least partially, for its creative and unique language. However, this tone also comes across as trying too hard, overshadowing the message with excessive gore and sexualization, which can feel distracting and off-putting.

The final 30 minutes, in particular, unravel any semblance of a coherent message, devolving into chaotic and gratuitous mayhem that ultimately undermines the film's earlier efforts.

This film made me decide i probably don't want to see nudity in film anymore.

reviews.author: Rayve777
reviews.body:
A modern day Jekyll and Hyde, The Substance combines dark humor, sickening body horror, and great commentary on the state of modern beauty standards that creates an absolute gut punch of a film. While The Substance focuses specifically on a former female media personality in Elizabeth Sparkle, who creates Sue in order to remain a star, the message of the film does still apply to how men are expected to look. Hell, you only have to look at the MCU to see how steroids have negatively affected some of their biggest male leads in pursuit of having their supes look as jacked as possible.

The editing and cinematography make this film look especially nightmarish, as Elizabeth/Sue's grasp on reality begins to slip as they try to sabotage each other in order to take control. This eventually leads to an absolutely nightmarish climax, that I can only really describe as being darkly hilarious and extremely upsetting at the same time.

I definitely recommend you watch The Substance while it's still in theaters, it's an experience that you definitely don't want to miss.

reviews.author: DJPleum
reviews.body:
"In terms of acting, one must rise and applaud Demi Moore thunderously, as this may be one of the best roles of her acting career. We have been waiting for her to have the opportunity to tackle a role like this, and she handles it magnificently, as if this role was truly made for her. People often perceive her as the epitome of beauty, so her performance in this film is akin to channeling the pressures of real life into a powerful explosion of emotions. Despite the extreme and intense nature of the character, she delivers a remarkable portrayal.

Kudos to the production design of The Substance, which has crafted the sets and style, along with various sequences, with great attention to detail. Every scene in this film is filled with symbols that reflect the broader concepts of the characters. The vibrant and striking colors further enhance its appeal. Additionally, the cinematography by Benjamin Cracknell (from Promising Young Woman) elevates this film, bringing it closer to perfection.

reviews.author: appusnikhil
reviews.body:
The movie gets on weirder and weirder as the story progresses. Then comes the ending and the creators drop a banger element and that elevates this movie to another dimension.

Please don't read anything about this movie before you are going the watch the flick, most of the reviews contains spoilers, for 100% satisfying experience, don't read any reviews. People are comparing this film to famous 80s film and they don't realise, how comparing similarities spoil the watching experience.

The lead actors especially Demi Moore was spectacular on the screen. Two hours on the screen were executed flawlessly by the creators. Dennis Quaid also portrayed his role nicely.

A must watch movie of 2024.

reviews.author: Faristuta
reviews.body:
The first half was very well executed , the idea of the movie appeared to be original even though it has been played in previous movies one way or another, but the strong acting and sound effects made it enjoyable to watch.

I don't mind the bit of horror but it became so unnecessarily gory that it was just utterly disgusting toward the end. I lost any sympathy I had for the Sue and couldn't wait for the movie to end.

The characters were also very one-dimensional, unsophisticated and highly predictable. I'm not sure whose decision was it to make it a horror/gore film. They could've presented ageing as a scary thing without making it a horror movie.

What stands out for the movie is the strong acting of everyone in it.

reviews.author: trainman269
reviews.body:
Really enjoyed this, as others have said shades of Cronenberg, especially in the the third act. Loved almost everything about this film.

From the set up of the star, cracked and despoiled, to Demi Moores exceptional performance, to the supporting cast, especially the Hollywood sleaze bag and the share holders, man this was a show.

Not perfect. Kind of felt like it went into overdrive in the third act, which to me, had less impact than the original birthing of the double. Most of the unsettling moments were in the details. The over sexualisation of the TV show, and OMG Dennis Quaid eating prawns hit harder than the latter body horror. But in a way I assume that was the point. It's easy to throw buckets of blood around, but to genuinely unsettle the viewer? That takes a director to have skill, which is on display here. Couple of scenes felt a bit out of place. Most notably Motorcycle Guy disrespecting the original, who although more mature is still conventionally very attractive. I get the point that was being made but really felt that's not how actual guys work...Not a deal breaker, but between that and the tonal shift in the last act it just kind of jarred me to rate it 8 rather than higher. Well worth your time.

reviews.author: EdgarST
reviews.body:
This film won the Best Screenplay award at the Cannes Film Festival, but the distinction does not guarantee that you will see a good film. Logically, it is very appropriate that a satire on fame in the audiovisual industry receives such an important award at a festival that was once an absolute guarantee of good cinema. Not anymore. It is true that it reflects on the obsession of certain people with fame and exposure in traditional and new media, their terror of aging and the terrifying transformations of their bodies. However, the satire extends for 144 minutes, which make all its weaknesses obvious.

The fact that the director-screenwriter is Parisian, or that the production is British-French does not change the Hollywood formula at all, with its special effects and artificial blood (in this case, in spurts and gushes), an exacerbated cult of butts of all genres, and rubber monsters that add to this accumulation of never-ending excesses.

However, I would not tell you not to watch it. You will end up laughing at all the indulgence and alienation, but you will have to put up with endless scenes of mutilations, beatings, and bloody explosions. In past body horror tales, in the hands of David Cronenberg, this story would have lasted 80 minutes. What I regret most is that the filmmakers threw away what did have an attractive central idea (which owes a lot to Wilde's «The Picture of Dorian Gray»): a plan to create a clone by injecting "the substance", of which success will depend on respecting the rules of the game and giving fair care to the human matrix when he/she is in a comatose state, while the other half fully enjoys what life (and the television industry) has to offer, thanks to its beauty and youth.

As the aging diva in charge of a morning show doing calisthenics and other jumps, Demi Moore creates an admirable self-parody, based on her strong but aging face and body, unfortunately for her and the TV mogul (Dennis Quaid in a grotesque performance, in a role conceived for the late Ray Liotta). Suddenly, the diva receives information about the substance from a nurse and the idea of acquiring it grows in the woman. The curious thing about the script is that there is no explanation of the liquid, its added value, or its origin... In exchange for what? At what cost? There is no mad scientist to explain anything, as in the good old days, only a scathing and oppressive voice.

I do not think I will spoil the movie for you if I tell you that everything goes wrong, very wrong, so wrong that one starts laughing and there is no turning back. It was calculated that we would end up laughing, but director Coralie Fargeat falls into her own trap and does not know when to stop this story loaded with fluids of all colors, organs, and multiple endings. And believe me, 144 minutes is a lot of screen time and too much of your free time.

reviews.author: davidosullivan-dos
reviews.body: This is the first movie I have seen in a very long time that reminds me of to arthouse movies I loved as film student, like 'Delicatessen'. Like that, *every single* shot in this has been thought about, not just to tell the story, or move the plot forwards, but to SAY something, literally every shot! Story wise, its a pretty mental thrill ride, and I loved the journey, music, editing, all totally quirky, surprising and pitch perfect, just like the directing and camera work, constantly inspiring and mesmerising. Demi Moore, seriously deserves an Oscar for this, on so many levels. For me, the ending just pushed it all one step too far, and it started getting too shlocky and early Peter Jackson- but everything was so amazing up till then I'm still giving it a 9.

reviews.author: tigz-84115
reviews.body: What a brilliant concept! Brilliant acting and good story but feel the ending is disappointing and could be so much better. I am not a film buff can imagine so many different endings apart from the one I had to watch. I lost heart with the story and felt it would be better with the younger character realising she needed the other to reach her goal. If the two entities worked against each other in a more intelligent way may have made more of an interesting ending. Did the actual ending show a boring view that we are our own worst enemies to the detriment of the film. So many have that T shirt and wearing it with pride. The ending makes it feel like B movie.

reviews.author: watice-79513
reviews.body: As others have said, the first part of the movie had a really great social message that was portrayed fantastically. The last 30 mins though added unneeded gore that just didn't fit with the rest of the movie. The only movie I can think that really pulls off gore with a social message is perhaps the first Saw movie. It might've been better to simply disgust the audience once to prove a point but this movie continues to batter towards how disgusting it can get towards the end. I highly recommend not watching this if you're eating .. anything, or working up an appetite as you will lose it. The acting and actors in this were superb, but the writing was a miss.

reviews.author: steve-ruzicka
reviews.body:
First and foremost: three ladies showing a lot of courage to write, direct and act in this movie. Not easy. Demi and Elizabeth don't shy to show themselves inner and out. And how beautiful both are, whatever their age. Going to extremes to dive into the fountain of youth is what makes cosmetic and plastic surgeons nicely wealthy. We can of course elaborate on the story line and reference to Elephant Man, Carrie, Possession and more. A glory hymn to women and their eternal magnificence. An ode to love and not a shade of positivism for the males.

Again, kudos to all three et merci Coralie de nous apporter un vent de France.

reviews.author: inusia
reviews.body: The trailer was a bit misleading, suggesting this is some psychological thriller or drama perhaps, with a deeper meaning. Instead, it's very shallow gore body horror, with only one intention: to disgust. And as such, it's quite nicely shot. Will probably get some awards in the costume/makeup department. Very nice visuals and coherent aesthetic. Just don't expect more than gore gore gore - quite hilariously kamp at the end, guts, blood and all. If that sort of thing sprinkles your donuts - go for it. Good for weekend entertainment, but not a memorable masterpiece. Just wish it was advertised adequately, that's it.

reviews.author: horne_pete
reviews.body:
Strap yourself in for nearly every emotion that you can feel while watching this film! This film has so much on offer and great character development, conjuring grotesque scenes that will make you want to look away but at the same time you can't stop looking!

Speaking of can't stop looking, Margaret Qualley is simply breathtaking her acting screams quality and trust me you won't forget her. The scenes will leave a mark on you and maybe even scar you a little bit. Her relationship with Demi Moore, is so sinister and makes you feel so uncomfortable that it evokes sadness for Demi Moores character (Elisabeth Sparkle).

You will need to pick your jaw up at the end of the film because this film will certainly have that effect, if you can make it through!

reviews.author: hazeldanziger
reviews.body:
This movie had so much potential and an entirely intriguing plot. I had been excited to watch this movie for months, based on the casting and my own personal expectations. The movie started off great, and had us reeled in from the first 10 minutes. The cinematography was gorgeous, and the casting was perfection.

I felt as if the movie had the option to take a deeper turn, revealing a better sense of explanation as to why the substance worked, who was behind it, etc. I felt as if this would have added the necessary psychological aspect to make this a more worthwhile film for horror enthusiasts. Instead, the ending was thoroughly gross (not realistic, I might add), and contained overwhelming amounts of fake blood. This brought my rating down many points, and left me to feel empty and dissatisfied.

One more point I'd like to bring up - What is with all of the butts in this movie? Someone has a fetish?

reviews.author: jbrumley-65779
reviews.body:
I thought this would be an intriguing movie. Although I understand what they were trying to portray the execution is just bizarre. I love Demi so I'm surprised she would agree to do such a movie. It was hard to sit through 2hrs...It is very repetitive, predictable and plain cheesy. I do not recommend. If you pay money to see this you'll be mad you did.

This would have made a much better Black Mirror or Twilight zone episode rather than a movie. There's so much emphasis on the effects that the plot is just bland, you really don't end up having a connection to the characters or caring what happens to them in my opinion.

reviews.author: tessann-54186
reviews.body: I was definitely not expecting this plot after just seeing a little clip on TikTok. I'm a huge fan of both Demi and Margaret. I loved the makeup and costumes, loved the cinematography, and loved admiring two beautiful women! This movie is definitely worth a watch. It's unique and a bit quirky but I think it was in all of the right places. I think that this movie may be difficult for some audiences to grasp - as it really plays on the ideas and feelings of getting older as a woman and how the media, and life in general, always wants something new and shiny. This is my first time reviewing here - so much length..

reviews.author: Mohsennechaverdie
reviews.body:
Boa, my gosh, it is nice! It's a rare gem, the kind of film you don't often see anymore, where every aspect feels thoughtfully crafted. The acting, especially from the two lead actresses, is good to great-they bring an intensity and depth to their roles that keeps you hooked from start to finish. The cinematography is stunning, with vibrant, eye-catching scenes that feel alive. The close-ups, paired with an incredibly immersive audio experience, draw you right into the film's world, heightening the atmosphere. I recommend watching it in cinema!

It's not filled with traditional horror scenes, but the raw, brutal interactions between the characters and their alter-egos bring an unsettling thrill that's hard to look away from. In fact, it reminded me a bit of "Revenge" (2017), with a similarly gripping sense of danger and raw emotion.

The movie's "Shining" finish style, almost ethereal feel, is the perfect finishing touch-it adds a unique flair that feels both modern and nostalgic! In an age where it feels like quality is often sacrificed for mass appeal, "The Substance" stands out as a refreshing exception. If you're a fan of thought-provoking, intense, cinema with a bit body-horror spice, this one's not to be missed!

reviews.author: ghettoplex
reviews.body:
Have you seen Antiviral? Are you a fan of David Cronenberg? If that's not enough, the blood, tits and ass should be enough to keep you in the seat.

But in all seriousness, The Substance is a fantastic nightmare of a story that deals with mitosis, extreme responsibilities and the consequence that comes with the price of eternal youth.

The ending did seem very predictable, however as the climax approached they delivered that predictable ending in a brand new way.

Whether or not it this was the message of the movie, all I could think is "be grateful for what you have, cause buying back time comes at an extremely dangerous cost"

reviews.author: mmoradpor
reviews.body: So why 6 stars? THE ENDING. Took the believable and suspenseful story aspects and threw them out the window in favor of indulging the director's Cronenberg fantasy and desire to max out the special effects budget. Was an enjoyable watch but the last 20-30 minutes got kinda silly and dumb, it lost its intelligence and subtlety too say the least and went to pure dumb gross out scenery, completely unnecessary especially when the messaging wasn't exactly subtle and was evident throughout the entire movie, from the very premise itself tbh, point is they could a ended on a much stronger note before the final change as it added nothing too what it was trying to say or show, not that it should turn anyone off from watching it, it's a good movie that will keep you interested from start too finish but should've been 20 min shorter.

reviews.author: sinscopefilms
reviews.body:
The Substance is a standout psychological horror film, blending intense visuals and an exceptional sound design that draws you right into its visceral world. The sound design is impeccable, creating an eerie atmosphere that complements the visual storytelling beautifully. This film is filled with artistic cinematography - overhead shots, close-ups, POVs - that feel very Kubrick-esque.

The production design captures a mysterious, almost puzzle-like atmosphere, with practical effects enhancing the realism - another Kubrick-inspired touch. Even the CGI feels natural-like. The music amplifies the tension with a mix of dark cinematic electronica and beefy techno beat, making the experience intense and even unsettling in the best way.

The narrative message is straightforward: embracing one's natural beauty and limitations is essential. It's a theme that resonates through the sexy, provocative, and at times grotesque visual storytelling - expect shots focused on body and gore, skillfully crafted to stir mixed emotions. The parallel editing is also brilliant. The final act is a pure frenzy of ugliness and gore, accompanied by an explosion of rock music, wrapping up the story on a raw, intense note.

Overall, The Substance is a bold, heavily Kubrick-inspired yet original horror that dives into beauty, identity, and self-acceptance with a fantastic script. Easily the best horror release this year.

reviews.author: RezaGlobal
reviews.body:
The Substance (2024) is a visually striking film that explores complex themes with ambition. The performances, particularly from Demi Moore and Margaret Qualley, are strong and compelling, bringing depth to their characters. The movie raises interesting questions about identity and societal pressures, but its execution doesn't always land.

The pacing is inconsistent, and some parts of the story feel underdeveloped, which takes away from its potential. However, the striking visuals and thought-provoking narrative make it an intriguing watch. While not perfect, it's a film that lingers in your mind.

reviews.author: vitinhaoriginal
reviews.body:
With a central theme, such as the exploration of identity. Through complex characters, you question what it really means to be yourself in a world where the perception of everything can be manipulated.

Full of winks at pop culture, they invite the public to reflect on their own relationship with the media and reality.

The art direction is impressive, with an environment that demonstrates the duality between the real and the artificial. The music complements the narrative very well, with a mix of electronic and orchestral sounds that intensify emotions and tension at key moments.

Demi Moore and Qualley bring the film to life with good expositions of the ethical and emotional dilemmas they face, making the connection with the audience even stronger.

With profound questions about the nature of reality and identity in an increasingly complex world. It positions itself as one of the most intriguing films of the year. Although there could have been 10-15 minutes cut at a time which would have greatly improved the pace.

reviews.author: carriemorrison
reviews.body:
This was, without a doubt, the most sickening film I have ever seen. I am not a fan of body horror but I appreciated the message and love Demi Moore, so thought I'd give it a try.

This was far too much for me. HOWEVER I can see that was the point, as I feel somewhat cleansed of any fear of aging I might have previously had! The film-Logic did somewhat hold up too, even though it was a bizarre concept. It was very clever and very awful. I think if we all watch this, the collective trauma will cleanse society of it's anti-aging obsession... in spite of this fact, I wouldn't recommend watching it to a friend!!

reviews.author: claudiapaola
reviews.body:
The Substance left me shaken, and, honestly, physically sick by the end. It was disturbing, not just in the finale, but throughout, though the ending truly took the grotesque to a new level. At first, I thought it was a story about a Hollywood figure struggling with aging, but the extremes this movie went to were beyond unsettling. I'm genuinely puzzled about what kind of mind could conceive of such horrific imagery; it felt less like storytelling and more like a display of the writer's darkest fantasies.

As someone who loves movies and appreciates art, I can say that this isn't either. Instead, it feels like a horror fantasy born from a very troubling perspective. The film's obsessive focus on sexualized horror and graphic, dehumanizing scenes makes me question what kind of compensation would even feel adequate for the actors involved in such a demeaning project. I don't believe any amount of money justifies the level of exploitation depicted.

This could have been an intriguing story about fame, aging, and societal pressures, but it veered off into sexually explicit and gruesome territory that overshadowed any potential. There were endless close-ups of fresh wounds, needles piercing skin, and gratuitously drawn-out shots that seemed to exist purely for shock value. The food and "aerobics" close ups, analogies made no sense and felt like they were just there to satisfy some disturbing creative impulse.

In the end, The Substance is a horror film that leaves behind a lingering, nauseating aftertaste, and I would never in my life watch anything like that again.

reviews.author: warturtle-18664
reviews.body:
If you seen Midsommar you know it left you with a weird feeling after watching . This movie gives you that same weird energy but worse. I'm writing this at 2am so sleeping after this movie is going to be terrible . Off putting visuals in this film and i say that as a compliment , the sound kinda reminds me of upgrade . If you know you know .

The two female leads did fantastic I loved sue . Our main protagonist should've been less insecure we all get old there's nothing wrong with that, she was beautiful even at her old age so it's sad to see where her insecurity got her .

reviews.author: ankitoffical-52349
reviews.body:
So, the movie is a striking reflection of how today's world is obsessed with fake beauty standards, often leading us to reject our true selves. The film brilliantly captures the toxic chase for perfection, revealing the devastating emotional and psychological toll it takes on individuals who are constantly bombarded with ideals of flawless skin, bodies, and lives. It's a sharp critique of how we've lost the ability to accept our natural beauty, trading authenticity for artificial enhancements and filters. (wannabe be snapchater)

What makes this film stand out is how these themes are visually presented. The cinematography is nothing short of spectacular. The way the camera transitions from extreme close-up, almost macro-level shots, to wider angles emphasizes the distortion between what we see up close and the bigger, often harsher, reality. This technique is used beautifully to illustrate how our perception of beauty is warped and manipulated by media and social pressures. (wannabe be insta influencer)

From the first frame to the last, the visual storytelling pulls you in, making you feel the characters' insecurities on a personal level. The macro shots, in particular, are breathtaking, focusing on minute details like skin texture and imperfections, only to zoom out and reveal how society forces these to be "corrected" or hidden. The panning shots, combined with a surreal color palette, add depth to this story, making the audience question their own relationship with beauty.

While some might feel the plot could have dived deeper into the personal stories of its characters, The Substance excels in using visuals to tell its tale. It's more than just a critique of beauty culture-it's a wake-up call for all of us to embrace who we truly are beneath the filters.

If you're a fan of thought-provoking films with impressive cinematography, this one is a must-watch. The Substance not only holds a mirror up to society but also asks us to reflect on our own perceptions of beauty and self-worth. Also there is a lot of gore.

reviews.author: chryso97
reviews.body:
The Substance starts off with an intriguing premise and a strong potential to delve into the complex themes of identity, beauty, and societal pressures. The point of view the movie adopts is compelling, and the setup holds promise for a fresh take on body horror and satire. However, as the story progresses, it becomes clear that this potential is squandered.

It was an interesting scenario at the beginning, but then all the possible ways the movie could continue got wasted. The narrative choices felt repetitive and uninspired, leading to an ending that was overly dramatic and chaotic. The climax, in particular, felt like a strange mix of "Carrie" and a 90s horror movie - over-the-top and disconnected from the thoughtful tone the film initially hinted at.

While the performances by Demi Moore and Margaret Qualley were commendable, they couldn't salvage the film from its misguided direction. The exaggerated finale overshadowed any meaningful commentary the film tried to make, leaving me disappointed.

reviews.author: robinclima
reviews.body:
My opinion does not matter. It gives and gives and just keeps on giving. What the greats have brought before- we just got it today.

This film lives forever.

Well if you need more characters than what I gave, as a collective mindset we are headed the right direction and so stoked to see where we all go next. Hopefully it will as beautiful and grotesque as SUBSTANCE!

My god I don't have a lot to say but at 200 characters needed- Dear Demi, it so great to see you rock humanity- like the all greats! Marlon Brando-Picasso-President Obama- our future president- VP Kamala Harris-the GREAT man or woman we never met but we can feel them in our own hearts.

reviews.author: xuenylomluap
reviews.body:
I love trash movies. There has been a resurgence of body horror trash movies recently (a Street Trash sequel, and the so far unreleased Toxic Avenger re-boot) and The Substance fits right into that niche. The Substance owes a lot to previous body horror films such as Society, The Fly and even Australia's Body Melt in it's scientific experiments vs physical and mental mutations. To see Demi Moore lurking around in a mutated and bloated body was hilarious and it's funny to think that this is what it took to revamp Moore's somewhat failing career.

I expect to see Tom Cruise cast as a monstrous ogre hellbent on feeding his own ego to himself next. Or Jennifer Lawrence as a pulsing placenta, killing film execs for the perfect role. Etc.

The Substance is a fun expensive B-movie filled with enough over the top-ness to satisfy any trash movie fan.

Good move Demi.

reviews.author: edwardcandraa
reviews.body:
Been hearing all about good stuff people talked about this movie. Watched it last night and i thought it was such a fresh idea on the take of body horror genre. Demi Moore was amazing in it and the other new actress that ive never heard of was such an amazing new talent as well. Might have to check her out after this one!

The directing and editing is top notch. It was stylishly edited,slightly over the top but in a good way. Now lets talk about the story,i wont talk that much about it since other reviewers already covered that area very well. I'm one of those people who get bored easily and often stop watching movies if the story was uninteresting and this one is not one of them. I was glued to the screen from the get go and it tells a lot about The Substance. I really hope Demi Moore will get more appreciation she truly deserves from more people after this one. She's the backbone of this movie,no pun intended.

reviews.author: scrap-1
reviews.body:
Wonderful concept. Act 1 and 2 are brilliant, and bring up some really amazing questions about beauty and ageing, but when act 3 comes around, the director/screenwriter (Coralie Fargeat) didn't know how to answer her own questions to wrap it up in a meaningful way. Instead she just relied on shock value, torture porn, and horror much like movies did back in the days of Saw. However, she directed this brilliantly and everyone's execution in the film is great. The lack of an intelligent final act is what made this movie fall flat in my eyes.

Demi Moore is amazing and so is Margaret Qualley. Editing and Cinematography is incredible.

reviews.author: bookofromans116
reviews.body: Haven't felt this appalled and disgusted watching a film since the ending of "Men". What a movie to watch in the theater. Perfect level of humor, satire and shock to critique the exploitation and male demand of young, entertaining femininity. Of course the realistic portrayal of self-hatred and attempting to accept and love oneself was impactful as well even if it didn't end in a happy ending. It was more or less a predictable outcome but witnessing the downward spiral and literal decay of the character was tragic but gripping. Probably couldn't have cast a better actress than Demi Moore to play the lead. Shoutout Dennis Quaid too, played his role annoyingly well. This also the first movie I've ever seen where I noticed people straight up walking out the cinema lmao.

reviews.author: jaylynnr
reviews.body: I guess I missed the acting, was focused on the dozens of butt shots. Watched again, still missed the best actress according to the Golden Globes. Did they say Demi Moore?. My short lived subscription to shudder ended abruptly because I watched all the films worth watching in several months. This was not horror, just silly Then realized Demi was punked by Golden Globes and thought this truly is revolutionary. She was not the only one punked. I also take ownership begrudgingly. Destined to become a cult classic. May take a little longer than the usual B picture to reach that stature. But the ending will certainly be t elevate it to he crowning touch to elevate to that stature.

reviews.author: fulleralecia
reviews.body: I'm reading the other reviews to see if I missed something. Maybe I am just not artsy and creative enough to have enjoyed this. I'll say the first 80% of the film I would've given a 6.5..... Demi was great, Dennis always great, lots to look at, very Kubrick-esque feel to the imagery, bright colors, set design and wide shots....like, I was entertained. Even the gross, ASMR creepy eating scene with Dennis Quaid's character was...something. But then the last 30 mins, were just a big, Kill Bill/Evil Dead cacophony of alll the no. Like, come on, we get it. The obsessive greed to obtain unattainable lifelong beauty leads to way more than anyone would ever want to sign up for. At one point at the end, I will admit, I was laughing. But then, it felt like Terrifier 2 and I was wondering when in the hell this was going to end. Someone put me out of my misery.

reviews.author: Phil_M_A_Kerr
reviews.body:
Agree with most of the other reviews here but wanted to put my 2 cents out into the ether.

Demi Moore kicks butt in this one, for sure. Pleasantly surprised & happy to be reminded of her substantial screen presence I'd not seen in a good while (rewatched A Few Good Men a couple years back).

Margaret Qualley, who I eventually recognised from Once Upon A Time In Hollywood, was equal to the task.

Now, to the writer & director, well, full props for carrying the body horror torch with aplomb. A true cinephile wearing her influences - Lynch, Cronenberg, Carpenter - on her sleeve, brightly & boldly.

Some complaints about the ending but, hey, it's a genre piece. Dodgy endings are almost par for the course! In the overall body of the film is where ... the substance ... lies.

reviews.author: momenmohamed-27188
reviews.body:
So good and the ending was top notch.

Watch if are into black mirror series.

The acting of Both Demi and Margaret is so good. I think it is one of the best movies I have ever seen this year and maybe even the best so far. The transition between the characters was so epic.
