reviews.author: vithiet
reviews.body: I'm aligned with a lot of the reviewers: great concept treated in an original fashion supported by fantastic acting. First 2/3 of the movie are great, though I still have a few issues with some of the directing choices, but it completely goes awry in the final third part. Mostly though, I think it's the way the movie was presented and how it starts that do not prepare you for what I think is the intended experience. Most of us expected a rather serious movie with a sci-fi/horror premise while it's very clear that it's one of those movies that are pure allegory and metaphors and should absolutely not be taken at face value, but appreciated for its interpretation. It so happens that it's not the type of movie I like so I would have passed if I had known in advance. But if that's your cup of tea and you go in knowing so, you might appreciate it more than I did.

reviews.author: katalist420
reviews.body:
This movie was such a nice surprise and one of the best modern horror shows of the last 15 years.

If you love old Cronenberg movies like I do, you HAVE TO SEE THIS MOVIE!!! It is simply amazing. It is creepy as hell,

Demi Moore is flipping amazing in this movie to, I really had no idea that she could act this well, she was on fire in this movie and proved to me and many others that with the right role she can be topnotch.

The directing is also fantastic to, from Coralie Fargeat who directed the underrated flick titled Revenge.

This movie really is a Horror movie and Body Horror done very well during modern times.

Lastly, the audio is fantastic and so well done, it will have you squirming throughout the movie do to the wonderful sounds the audio team did for this movie.

The movie also look great to, there really is no negative aspects in this movie for me, its a near perfect modern Horror movie.

I can't wait to see what this director does next! The supporting acting is also very good to. This will be a day one buy for me on Bluray/Ultra HD when it comes out.

And I must say it once more, Demi Moore is simply amazing in this movie, I always thought she was an average actress, but she turns in one of my all time favorite performances from a female actress in a horror movie.

I have not talked about what this movie is about yet on purpose, as I had ZERO idea about what this movie was about before I saw it. I went in blind and didn't want to see the trailer and I didn't know anything about what this movie was about.

Just know that if you want an old school style, proper horror movie with very good audio and a wonderful and surprising performance from Demi Moore or i fyou loved old Cronenberg flicks you should really check this out!

reviews.author: crowdedsubways
reviews.body:
Incredible look at the pressures of trying to stay beautiful, and young, and relevant as a woman (in Hollywood, but also everywhere) as a replaceable cog an image obsessed machine that will quite literally use you up and spit you out. Demi Moore brings such incredible vulnerability and absolutely kills it in her role; alongside Margaret Qualley, the tension between the two is palpable and such a delight to watch. My only complaint is that Ray Liotta passed away before he could be here too!

Literally the only people I've seen complaining that the ending is bad or that it ruined the established tone of the movie have been men. So do with that what you will, my loves!

reviews.author: RivereyesGR
reviews.body:
Wow, just wow.

Demi Moore and the creative team behind 'The Substance' should win every category/genre award possible in 2024 for this dark, twisted, all-too-familiar and all-too-human gem.

Reading the description and watching the trailer, you might think 'Alright, Cronenbergian body horror with a twist, meh, I've seen it before, I wonder why Demi Moore's in it.'

Just do yourselves a favor and watch it. It's absolutely mesmerizing. It starts with exactly what you expect and then deviates deliciously. The final act goes all out gonzo and will not appeal to all, but what a ride.

After a lifetime of watching horror movies, I either tune out quickly or kinda watch with interest or artifically maintained suspense. This one though, this one.

Amazing, grotesque close-up photography, a hell of a dark take on TV execs by Dennis Quaid and Qualley is equal parts breath-taking and chilling.

Read this as parents vs children, boomers vs youth, TV-self versus the real, no matter your take, you are never forgetting The Substance.

reviews.author: Steve9920
reviews.body:
From modern culture satire to, well, whatever that ending was?

Cut the last 40 minutes or so, and this would be a decent satire on the pervasive female body image youth fantasy obsession. Featuring two generation spanning, talented actresses giving excellent performances, driven along by good production values, effective sound score, and decent script.

Unfortunately, the satirical pudding was seriously over egged in order to produce what finally became just another over the top body shock horror. Which is a shame, because the job was well on its way to being finished within the first 90 minutes or so. Messages heard, lessons learned, time to tie it up with a neat cut to black screen and credits rolling.

Its fine for a one time watch.

reviews.author: mhnyxht
reviews.body:
This film is an incredible mix of surreal Sci-fi, and a horrifying commentary on the surgery mutilation done to women, self hatred, and addiction.

By the time of the third act and what Demi Moore does to herself... then cannot stop and does worse, it was absolutely horrifying. I found it one of the most frightening films I've ever seen... because I've had moments in life when I've considered cosmetic surgery and imagined the living nightmare of what happens when that is botched.

This film is like a hallucinatory nightmare and is just jaw dropping. It's one of the best films I've ever seen, if you're a movie fan this is unmissable.

reviews.author: reviewerB
reviews.body: This movie is based on an intriguing premise, conducts an important discussion, and has interesting aesthetic decisions. However it's extremely gory. Over the top gory. It's gore galore. I get that everything is very hyperbolical, charicaturesque and nightmarish: art direction, character building, camera angles and even plot. But, for me, the extreme gore was a total buzzkill. Again, super important discussion about ageism and how consumer culture oppresses women and damages our mental and physical health. But I wish someone had warned me that this is a gory movie. Or better yet: I wish that the whole discussion had been conducted without the gore. My rating would probably be much higher. If you were disgusted by the lumbar plug in ExistenZ, like I was, do not watch this! It's a gazillion times worse.

reviews.author: ztpbrmhw
reviews.body:
If you relied solely on the trailer, you may have been deeply intrigued, but nothing could prepare you for this tour-de-force in filmmaking and body horror.

Ageless Demi Moore, in undoubtedly her most provocative role since Indecent Proposal and Striptease - both decades ago - dares to bare all of her vulnerabilities, as does her character, with mastery and precision.

Margaret Qualley, who I adored in Once Upon a Time in Hollywood, delivers a devilishly delightful star-making performance.

The use of the camera and camera angles and zooms and closeups and shakey camera were Kubrick-esque. And the use of bold titling throughout was fresh and innovative and quite intentionally "in your face."

Director Coralie Fargeat in her storytelling consciously gratifyingly spared us the minutia of the scientific backstory, the identity of the scientists, or their motives and rationale, or even instructional dialogue or video on how to "use the darn thing" - just the bare minimum of labeling and one's own intuition on what to do next. As with most movies in the body horror genre, medical and anatomical and scientific logic or accuracy take a back seat to thought-provoking themes and imagery.

There are satirical and gaudy wardrobe abound, and the movie features undoubtedly the most gifted foley artists and AMSR technicians on the planet. Who knew that pushing the plunger of a syringe has such a deafening audible sound? Though this is offset by the horrid sounds of Dennis Quaid garrishly crunching through shellfish.

In this movie, the movie explores "over-indulgence" on every level, and at every turn, and in the end outright unapologetically hyper over-indulges the moviegoer with body horror and ludicrity to the point of masterful absurdity

If you appreciate fresh, innovative movies that are willing to take risks, this movie will satisfyingly stick with you for a long time.

reviews.author: urikasei
reviews.body:
I enjoyed this movie alot but personally there was alot of issues that bothered me in the script

1- the ending. I know it was meant to be symbolic and surreal, but that swift change was not a good conclusion for the film. The ending was extremely unimpactful and ineffective.

2- Elizabeth. The character of Elizabeth was really rushed into conclusion. We didn't get to know anything about her personality at all. She was really dull as a character and i didn't feel bad for her in the entire movie. The premise of "Sue" was really awesome, but Elizabeth was just boring

3- alot of stuff in the movie don't make any sense. I get that it's sci-fi fantasy, but given the established lore and rules of the world, it was still pretty inconsistent. What im trying to say is that "the movie wasn't immersive" at all. To me it was just a porrly written Black Mirror episode

4- alot of stuff was really "on the nose" and it was trying really hard to guide the audience towards the message. There was no language of subtlety.

reviews.author: lenardhexal
reviews.body:
I understand what the movie is mostly going for. But the way it goes about delivering its message works directly against it. It feels as if The Substance is feeding into the stereotypes it aims to disparage. The oversexualization of the younger manifestation borders on a kind of exploitation the film relishes in, scene after scene. There's little nuance or subtext to any of this parody on human values.

Qualley's work on this film is uninspired and wooden. Moore delivers a commendable performance, but feels sidelined towards the end. Even as her talents are underused in the second half of the movie, she grounds the story in something real and honest, which I appreciate.

The film had me interested for the first 1/3. The second act faltered, and by the time the final twist came and went, I think the story was too far gone for me to take any of its messages to heart.

reviews.author: miklcats
reviews.body: When i first seen the trailer and clips i thought although interesting the sort of chasing your youth story had been done to death however in this movie they managed to make it a pretty unique concept. Demi truly gave one of the best performances ever and deserves an academy award. Margaret and Dennis were also great in the movie too. I also thought the movie was good although funny at times i always felt sympathy for Elizabeth and towards the end felt awful for her. I love that it wasn't fully just a vanity reason that made her take the potion like death becomes her. Its because of ageism and sexism and being made to feel worthless just because she has gotten older and how it eats away at her.

reviews.author: aolsucks-26137
reviews.body:
I don't write reviews too often, but good lord, I can't recall the last time a film had me walking out of the theater with my mouth agape. I finished watching it over five hours ago, and after running a bunch of errands and coming back home to do some chores, I'M STILL THINKING ABOUT IT.

As a woman who just turned forty, this film really resonated by touching on so many visceral themes with regards to the supposed horrors that come with visibly aging as a woman.

But all of that aside - WOW. Can we talk?? Firstly, it's stylish. So, SO cool looking. So many interesting shots, cuts, and camera angles. Demi Moore looks great, and she gives a performance that makes you wonder why she didn't do more horror throughout her career! Very sympathetic character, despite making some decisions that make you want to grab her by the shoulders and shake some sense into her. And when things start to get really bad, her desperation and panic are top-tier... Ugh, she's so very good in this!

Margaret Qualley also gives a great performance; by the time the third act rolls around (more on *that* part later!), she has successfully made you feel so much contempt for her character. Makes you want to wrap your fingers around her pretty little neck, lol.

The sound design and soundtrack are also very effective. Everything about this film was designed to make an impact.

The body horror this thing supplies is beyond anything I've seen in contemporary releases. Excellent practical effects... wonderfully gory and gross. You will think of David Cronenberg. You will think of Brian Yuzna. You will think of early Peter Jackson. Definitely not for the easily digusted. The first two acts are well-paced, tense, and effortlessly hold your attention. That third act, though??? Absolutely BANANAPANTS. UNREAL. I could not believe it went where it went. It takes a left turn. A *sharp* one. Like - some left turns are steady, and you feel nice and comfortable and safe in the hands of the driver. But the left turn in this film takes the steering wheel and violently jerks it so the vehicle rolls over and over into a bloody combustion. It is jarring, extreme, gross (in such a fun and over-the-top way), and insane. If you've watched and enjoyed 'Society' or 'Dead Alive,' you will feel right at home with this one. I LOVED it!!!

I won't spoil it, so all I will say is this: Expect a climax that beats you over the head and demands that you suspend your disbelief. Let it grip you by the wrist and violently yank you along to its final destination (which nicely settles back to the film's opening). You will leave the theater stunned and - if you're anything like me - laughing and excitedly saying "oh my god" over and over again.

Amazing work by Coralie Fargeat and the entire cast and production crew. GO SEE IT!

reviews.author: tammyd-72964
reviews.body: Growing up in a world of gore, it's nice to finally see something original. It was gross, funny, and imaginative. With Hollywood constantly rinsing and repeating old films from the past this film gives us something original with a story and a beautiful message. Madame Demi Morre, has always been a dream to watch on the big screen and let me tell you she blew me away. I honestly felt for her and wanting so much to just hold her and let her know things would be ok. So many times my friend had to close my mouth because i would watch with it gaped open. This story lets you know to be who you are love who you are. What this film has taught me was for the love of God cover your mouth when blood gushes around you.

reviews.author: arubachhh
reviews.body: Honestly, I don't even know what I expected from this movie, but it DEFINETLY wasn't that... If you have weak stomach, you better skip this one. Till today, even after watching The Human Centipede (It wasn't so disturbing actually for me as others said) I thought I could handle ANY movie, no matter of how much blood, people in pieces or other drastic scenes it has, but after that? It was the first horror movie to actually REALLY disturb me. The other half of the movie I watched with my mouth wide opened. Exept that it blowed my mind, I'm really itrigued just by the idea of this movie, the whole plot (thats what I value the most in horror movies) and also by how everything looked so real, every drop of the blood, every second of these brutal scenes was so horribly detailed. If you're a fan of interesting plot, drastic and psyhologcal horrors, you definetly MUST try this one. One of the best movies I have seen so far. Really impressed.

reviews.author: zeynepkocakli
reviews.body:
The film had a lot of potential, especially in its first three-quarters. The scenes were visually striking, the tension was well-built, and I was genuinely intrigued by the direction it was heading. However, the last 15 minutes were a major letdown for me. While I understand the director may have intended to disturb and unsettle the audience, it went too far for my taste, leaving me more uncomfortable than captivated.

The music in the movie is nothing short of extraordinary. It doesn't just accompany the scenes-it completes them, elevating the emotional and psychological impact of the film. Without such a cohesive and striking score, the movie would have felt bare, almost incomplete. The music amplifies the film's most intense moments, adding depth and resonance to its narrative. It's a rare achievement to see a score so integral to a film's identity, and for that, I give the composer a perfect 10.

reviews.author: valdvasdx
reviews.body:
I am not new to body horror. Demi Moore and Dennis Quaid raised this script to another level. I also like extensive Lynch styling and some taste of Kubrick.

Though I expected more twist or philosophy or moralization towards the end of the film. Here we - viewers - were left alone with our own thoughts and impressions.

I would like to see this movie to be pushed further, because some of the modern beauty themes are little bit outdated and somewhat localized to United States.

I like sharp, quick visual transitions between characters, though I think to much attention was given to premises and comparatively too little to character internals. I would add 30 mins to the movie on top.

reviews.author: extranicely
reviews.body: "Demi Moore shows off her talent, she is amazing, totally bought into her character. The plot moves along great until the final 30 minutes or so, where it went a bit far-fetched. With a small re-edit, this could have been left as a final scene in the bathroom, with a 'look what you've done to yourself' ending. Didn't need the Hollywood stage ending; in fact, cut that whole mess out. I get the person's ego was now so twisted she thought she could get away with it, but it just didn't work. The earlier parts of the film were gripping and well-paced, showcasing Moore's incredible range and depth. However, the climax felt disconnected from the rest of the narrative, undermining the strong build-up. A more subtle conclusion would have preserved the film's integrity and left a lasting impact."

reviews.author: drael64
reviews.body: I genuinely don't know. This film is basically close ups of skin, booty shaking and body horror. It focuses on the stardom of an actress, which you would know from the trailers, and he attempt to reclaim her youth. But I'm honestly not much sure what it's about other than that. reviews.author: mfwypm
reviews.body:
Wow!!!! You have to see it to believe it...Demi Moore is outstanding. Amazing, unbelievable, unforgettable.

I cannot stop thinking about this film, what an accomplishment-Jekyll and Hyde, Frankenstein with a full on tribute to The Fly ...in a squishy, succulent ball of joy.... This will be one of the defining moments of cinema ...whether you love it or hate it, The Substance is an unforgettably loud, brash, gross, beautiful film which I want to see again and again.

Qualley and Quaid were fantastic, but Moore should without doubt be up for the big awards (which won't happen as horrors rarely get even a nod)...but I just loved this film...did I say I liked it?!

reviews.author: grahamvandyke
reviews.body:
You know when you hear people hyping up a movie, especially with lines like "This move was CRAZY". Well, it was not overselling this time. This movie certified belongs in a mental asylum.

The true power of The Substance comes from the director having absolutely no qualms about pushing the boundaries of how far to take any given part of the movie, be it music, special effects, plot, dialogue, sound design, the list goes on. This really had the makings of a true cult classic and masterpiece.

HOWEVER.

Once the movie hits the last 30 minutes there's a noticeable decline. It feels like the movie begins to try to "1 up" what it had been doing the entire time, by making the ending so completely over the top it crosses into an indecipherable mess. Quite a shame considering I was close to putting this on my list of best movies of all time.

The real question is- is it worth the watch for the parts that are genius? The answer is a resounding yes.

9-10/10 for the first 1.5 hours, 3/10 for the last half hour.

reviews.author: tiaskyelandish
reviews.body: I knew little about The Substance. All I knew was that it was a horror film starring Demi Moore, Margaret Qualley, and Dennis Quaid and it was receiving high praise from the Cannes Film Festival. It's an understatement to say it caught me off guard. I went into it blind. I didn't know about the extent of the crazy setup which inflated my experience. So, I'm going to do my best to not spoil too much about the film. Right off the bat, this isn't a subtle film at all and doesn't leave anything to the imagination and that's before it gets to the body horror. As a satire, it's obvious what it's about. Many themes in this film can be seen with the obsession with beauty and self-image and treats women (especially older women) and how it can cause their bodies to a breaking point to hold onto their beauty and youth. It's a shockingly hilarious film. The dark comedy fits well in an otherwise intense film. In fact, some of the comedy comes from just how crazy it gets. It's a strange and unpredictable film that locked me in from start to finish. Even the slower parts kept me on the edge of my seat. I won't go into detail but The Substance is over-the-top insane, especially with its premise. It leads to a surprising amount of camp. I was flabbergasted with how things progressed; it escalated things to extreme degrees. Although it's 2 hours and 20 minutes, it's well worth it. It feels like it's going to end, it keeps going. Just when you think it reached its maximum point, 10 minutes, it reveals that it hasn't. The last 20 minutes is when everything ramps up to incredible levels and it must be seen to be believed. Demi Moore and Margaret Qualley deliver phenomenal and compassionate performances that marvelously complement and contrast each other and easily rank as the best of their careers. Even Dennis Quaid is excellent as a detestable and freaky producer. Visually, this is a beautiful film; it's incredibly shot with fantastic production design and a great use of colors. The editing and sound design are top-notch and chaotic and make certain scenes more severe and disturbing. The practical effects and makeup are terrific like award-winning stuff. The body horror is ridiculously bizarre and horrifying. There are moments that I can't help but look away from the screen. The score is phenomenal and moody. The Substance is the best horror film of the year and one of my favorite films of the year. Go into it blind just like I did.

reviews.author: darkonex-31666
reviews.body:
I never write reviews on here or anywhere but felt compelled to write one here. I just got back from seeing this in theatres, which I wasn't planning on initially but went ahead and ventured out today to see it and wow my mind is blown. I went in pretty blind, I didn't read the synopsis, I just saw an early teaser trailer for it and knew Demi Moore was in it and loved the look of it.

Speaking of looks, the cinematography is outstanding here. I loved the look of the film, the lighting and angles used, and costume design was on point. The acting from the leads were all fantastic, Dennis Quaid's character was very over the top sleazy and Demi Moore gave a great performance and you could just feel all her emotions. I wasn't familiar with Margaret Qualley but her character was great as well and she's incredibly gorgeous to boot, definitely need to go and check out her other work now.

This movie is definitely in the body horror genre and not for the squimish, so if you are not into tons of blood, gore, vomiting, and also has a lot of nudity, then this may not be for you. Otherwise, I highly recommend this film and I have been to the theatre more than usual this year and this is 100% my favorite film of 2024 so far and I really cannot see this being outdone anytime soon for me anyway.

reviews.author: gadielbritoalmonte
reviews.body:
Despite appreciating the movie's craftsmanship and the effort invested in crafting a compelling historical narrative, the conclusion left me feeling somewhat unsatisfied. While I can acknowledge the artistic merit and thematic purpose behind the conclusion, I found myself yearning for a resolution that resonated more with my personal preferences. Admittedly, my ideal ending may not have been the most appropriate choice within the context of the overall plot, as it could have deviated from the story's established trajectory or its intended message.

However, when viewed objectively, I would characterize the ending as tolerable. It was sufficiently consistent to tie the narrative together and remained true to the film's overarching tone and themes. Nevertheless, it lacked the emotional depth and sense of closure that I had anticipated. I respect the director's vision and the creative choices that led to the conclusion, but it ultimately prompted me to contemplate alternative paths the story could have taken.

reviews.author: meghbanerjeemusic
reviews.body:
This one of the best movies I have watched in recent times. THE SUBSTANCE is a modern horror film that wholly lives up to it's promise and its premise. It's beautifully grotesque in all the right ways, with such bold artistic confidence on display that feels as if its creators had full control of this project - a singular, focused vision. This is a film i wager many will love for its sheer audacity, and just as many will reject like a rotting chicken drumstick, as it is definitely an acquired taste, but i feel it's destined to become a cult horror classic.

Demi Moore, Margaret Qualley & Dennis Quaid deliver astounding performances alongside an impeccable supporting cast & cast of extras, each committing entirely to every moment they are on screen in this dark, twisted, human, cruel, beautiful, violent, absurdist, satirical tale about fame, hunger, greed, the ageing process and so much more, set firmly in an industry always in search of fresh meat for the masses - executed with surgical precision by a team that fired on all cylinders.

A stellar cast, a brilliant writer and director, sublime cinematography, aggressive compositions and sound design, exquisite set designs, costumes & make-up effects, and a world-class horror FX team all put in the work to make something greater than the sum of their parts, and it shows in every frame from beginning to end. They knew what they were cooking and let nothing go to waste. Waist?

This film wears its inspirations on its sleeve with zero repentance, giving sly nods to classics like The Fly, Carrie, Inland Empire, Dorian Grey & The Elephant Man, even a little of the old-school Troma films finds a place on Hollywood Boulevard in THE SUBSTANCE, without ever feeling like writer/director Coralie Fargeat was simply emulating or regurgitating ideas from other films, rather these threads feel like inspirations or prompts for her to launch into her own wild, unique story while honouring the genre and writers that have come before her - quite fittingly, i might add, given one of the many themes of the film itself.

It's a fable-turned-horror story that manages to shock, amaze, disgust and enrapture in equal measure, with unflinching writing & characterizations that are sharp, witty, heartbreaking, sinister, enraging, vile, absurd and outrageous without ever taking things too far - while also knowing just when to take everything so much further.

But one example of the latter - the "paper mask" scene had the potential to be utterly ludicrous, threatening to derail the tone and momentum of the entire film's trajectory, but the alchemy of the visual lunacy and the anguish of the moment underneath strikes the balance of fever dream and nightmare fuel, wordlessly breaking the fourth wall like nothing else - and this film is packed with unexpected moments & expectations flipped, so much so, the two-hours-plus running-time flew by because i was simply transfixed to the screen.

The increasing pace of twists and turns in the second and third act will surprise and delight fans of classic horror stories and allegories from the minds of artists like Cronenberg, Lynch, Kubrick, Oscar Wilde, Stephen King & Clive Barker - and you can now add Coralie Fargeat to that pantheon of rarified air - she has more than earned it with THE SUBSTANCE.

Thank you for your feedback!

reviews.author: johnwhittle89
reviews.body: Let's be honest. If someone is ugly or old, they're not wanted. And this film perfectly fits that narrative. Whether fictional or non we each live this way inside of our own minds. This is a true display of vanity, suffering with old age and coming to terms with feeling left out. The sci-fi aspect of this film works very well, yet I found myself extremely uncomfortable as a viewer. This is a horrific take on how desperate people are to be loved, cherished and wanted. Let's also take a look at a different point of view from it. This lady takes her career so seriously and didn't care to raise a family, marriage or real close friends. This character has 0 friends in the whole film except someone which wants to get into her pants. It's a crazy take on something which we all experience every day. Looking into a mirror is a difficult thing when aging. This film show is exactly that, but in a very bleak way.

reviews.author: ericmarchand-65052
reviews.body:
I can only surmise that the rather high ratings given are for 1 of 2 reasons: Naked ladies -or- a rather low budget fiesta of fake blood by the gallon and special effects that makes this feel like a remake of The Toxic Avenger. For me, it's about the second.

This movie is bad, I mean BAD. The plot is obvious, the acting is..well.. good enough, given the list of actors but most of all, the script is just trashy. How they got Demi Moore to do full frontal nudity while in her 60's is an achievement on its own I suppose, but then she really has nothing to be ashamed of. Was it necessary to the plot? Not really but what else is there in the first half of the movie? Unless you were hoping to see full frontal from Margaret Qualley as well? If so, you're in luck, oogle your little heart out. May as well, not much else going on.

So given all that, why am I giving it a 6? Well, despite all of the above, I miss the old "Attack of the killer Tomatoes" type of movies. Although the first 3/4 of the film are a 2, at best a 3, the last half hour is a solid 8 on the B movie scale. That's when I decided it was worth the time I wasted to view it.

reviews.author: heseinfathi
reviews.body: Not a Shakespeare, but I would think this is some conceptual motion picture are on materialism, how we dread the world moving on from us, and subsequently our craves to stay relevant, young, and desired. Also, maybe, alludes to the concept that a human being is a selfish being and, kind of, a parasite that will naturally feed off and drain the very life (or resources) to thrive. I could consider this partially true since a child does similarly drain their parents and locks them into hard labor just so they can feed their child. Quite the dark view if this is truly the concept, or I am messed up in the head and it's nothing like that. Would make a fine theatrical piece than a movie, still.

reviews.author: ccpdgyhfw
reviews.body: A masterpiece! This work should be viewed completely independent of imposed concepts such as "beauty" or "age" or "fame" or "popularity". Instead of horror with dramatic elements, I can say that it is the reflection of "science fiction" on art. The subject is so real and so close (I think it is more than close, it exists and is applied today). The best screenplay award is very well deserved. Those colors, images, art are so good that it immediately involves you and leaves you in awe. Yes, you will want to close your eyes in some scenes, it is disturbing yes, but you should definitely add it to your "things to see before die" list. Despite all that she has been through, Demi Moore, who is impressive with her incredible comeback and courage, Margaret Qualley, whom you will not be able to find words to say, and of course Dennis Quaid's well-deserved leading roles, and Coralie Fargeat's genius, pen and eye make this work flawless.

reviews.author: aprilsfriendorin
reviews.body:
This is a good movie, but I walked away feeling like it really missed its potential in some key ways. It follows the story of a woman who desperately misses her youth, which she links to her value as a person. She invests in a program that allows her to live as a younger version every other week. As she becomes obsessed with her youth, her older self suffers,

This movie has a lot of great things going for it. For starters, it's message about aging is very apt- it addresses real-world issues in a fun body horror format. The horror elements are also well done, and it's ultimately very entertaining.

Now, the problems: 1) The messaging is so on the nose at times. Some of the lines are just SO direct- it seems like they don't trust the audience to be intelligent. 2) Unnecessary nudity. We don't need a million ass shots- we get it. At some point, it starts to feel gratuitous (as opposed to necessary for the movie). 3) It seems like they didn't know how to end this movie. It devolves from insightful commentary to straight up shock value. Still good, but could be better.

reviews.body: Omg this film is incredible, if I could give it 20 out of ten I would, shocking, great soundtrack, amazing acting, effects are sublime. Makes u think, then kind of not care. Like the Thing on prom night. Deffo need this kind of entertainment. Got a bit of black mirror way to it. Demi Moore is fantastic. Anyone that like the Eric prydz video will love this . Erotic shocking blood mutation monstrous clinical mental claustrophobic. The sounds and shots are something else. It captured the essence of showbiz and the repulsiveness of showbiz. Can't wait for more of this style of cinema. After seeing MEN this has just just blown that film out of the water.

reviews.author: twelve-house-books
reviews.body: I really can't give this film more than six stars, and I am awarding them only because of the strong and in-your-face message to Hollywood and all who partake of its rotten fruits. The message? Age gracefully despite what the producers want, or maybe in spite of them. Demi Moore, Dennis Quaid, and Margaret Qualley--along with a fabulous supporting cast including Gore Abrams as the myopic and hilarious neighbor who represents every man who turns to look at a woman's derriere as she passes--all make this film worth seeing (for anybody who can stomach vomit, blood, the visuals of very old age, needles, and extremely fit scantily clad human bodies). Extra respect to Moore for not being afraid to make this film, and possibly even making it as one proof, to herself and others, that beauty is only skin deep after all. Cronenberg, Kubrick, and Lynch are all given homage here, but I hope that Joseph Merrick, the so-called "Elephant Man," is the forgiving sort. Maybe his real-life plight is plugged into this fantasy to reflect the abuse anybody who has "aged out" experiences in the film industry, but I would have been a lot more careful, maybe using Frankenstein's monster or some other recognizable horror from film or literature.

reviews.author: daijameswilliams
reviews.body:
If you have ever seen any of the classic 80s body-horrors, in particular The Fly and Society, plus thought about women in media for more than a minute, you don't need to see this film.

It is a confused, poorly-plotted mess. The messaging is heavy-handed and obvious. The male gaze pastiche is overdone to the extent that it becomes what it is parodying. The endless references to Kubrick are completely baffling. The Vertigo reference at least makes sort of thematic sense.

This is easily one of the most overrated movies I've ever seen. After all the hype, I was so excited to see it. Really disappointing.

Positives: Demi was very good.

reviews.author: mroseta
reviews.body:
It's very complicated to even attempt to write a review about such a complex and layered movie as The Substance. Where do I even begin? It tackles so many issues we go through as humans living in a frivolous society that cares way more about what you should be than the true essence of each one of us. The primordial issue is regarding the physical appearance of an ageing star who wants to retain her fame and popularity and is willing to risk some desperate measures to attain her goal. No one will dare judge us because all of us have in some way or another taken measures to look more pleasing in the eyes of society. You want to fit in, you try to follow the rules. But then again, in the movie as in real life, we see that humans are not so good at following rules! It is so hard to find a balance, of not going so far into what you wish you were that you literally lose your true essence!

The rules of The Substance were quite simple, as rules in general often are, but as the movie progresses, they become harder to follow and chaos ensues!

All the extreme visuals notwithstanding, and the gore and references to other major cinematic successes, the movie makes you THINK, and it makes you want to discuss wtf you just saw with those fortunate enough to share the experience with you. For once it's not just entertainment, although it most certainly entertains! It also forces you to watch the cruelties of our miserable existence, but also the creativity of the human spirit. It bonds you; it frees you, it's an extraordinary experience, best shared with others!

And a shout out to Demi Moore in what is probably the best and most demanding role in her career. I hope she's nominated for an Oscar and that she wins, giving a small even if dwindling hope to 60+ years old actresses.

reviews.author: ScorpioDog
reviews.body:
'The Substance' is explores so many themes in such a unique way. It offers you so much as an audience member, even after you leave the cinema.

The body horror in this was so visceral and harrowing. It will get you twisting and squirming in your seat, as you imagine similar events happening to you as an audience member! I also loved how this film was shot and edited, it has lots of memorable long takes.

Demi Moore was an astounding main character. You can tell so many of the main characters possible thoughts through her visual expressions or her character looking at objects. Additionally, Margaret Qualley was sensational as the younger counterpart character. She has some intentionally artificial and exaggerated mannerisms that is perfect for the narrative and themes.

This film will be an instant classic and will be remembered for years to come!

reviews.author: floresabnere
reviews.body: Owing more than a passing nod to great films and filmmakers such as The Shining (Kubrick), Elephant Man (Lynch), and Society (Yuzna), The Substance felt slightly derivative and at times mimicked. The story and allegory of superficiality and beauty is spot on an insightful criticism of modern culture. I would make this film required viewing for all of those influencers and selfie addicted folks that waste their lives on looks alone and waste our time in their attempts to hijack our attention. In that regard, The Substance stands out as a cutting contemporary critique of our times and a grotesque representation of how far we now go to capture beauty and looks in this transient world.

reviews.author: OMTR
reviews.body:
A hard-hitting satirical body horror film of incredible thematic richness, whose creativity literally explodes thanks to the perfection of Coralie Fargeat's writing and direction, the virtuosity of the performances of Demi Moore, Margaret Qualley and Dennis Quaid, as well as the masterful editing of Coralie Fargeat, Jérôme Eltabet and Valentin Feron, perfectly highlighted by Raffertie's atmospheric soundtrack.

Nominated for the Palme d'Or at the Cannes Film Festival, 'The Substance' ultimately won the Best Screenplay Award.

A cinematic gem, which has also been awarded at various other festivals around the world.

reviews.author: Lecinaste
reviews.body:
The film The Substance is a horror and thriller starring Demi Moore and directed by Corin Hardy. It tells the story of Elisabeth Sparkle, a once-celebrated Hollywood star who, on her 50th birthday, faces a major accident. After the incident, she discovers a mysterious serum that restores her youth, but it creates another version of herself, leading to an escalating internal conflict between the two. The film explores the obsession with youth and beauty and its psychological effects in a terrifying and bizarre way.

The film's premise is intriguing, and I was excited to see it, especially given the lack of new ideas in Hollywood. The film drew me in from the first moment with its mystery and deep psychology. However, its scenes are not easy to watch, featuring nudity and very grotesque body dissection details, so I advise those with weak hearts against viewing it.

At first, the film's climax was strong, but then the plot began to slow down. I felt it should have ended after an hour and forty minutes, as two hours and twenty minutes felt too long.

In terms of cinematography, it reminded me of Psycho through its bathroom scenes and camera angles, and The Shining, where psychological colors were used distinctively. Initially, I rated the film an 8/10, but the ending disappointed me, so I settled on a 6/10.

reviews.author: ANTICRST
reviews.body:
It's rare that I leave a 10 star review for anything in life but this masterpiece deserves one, for sure.

The only other Fargeat movie I have watched was Revenge, and, although I loved it, after seeing The Substance, I instantly googled the director to find what else she had done as I needed more!

Every aspect of this film had me so uneasy and anxious it was incredible, and it has been a long time since I've felt like this by film.

Moore wasn't afraid to jump into the horror box for this film and try something new and this part felt made for her. She did such an incredible job for this role and you've never seen her do anything like this before. What a pleasure it was to watch her.

The SFX and makeup team did a jaw droppingly impecible job too I had to keep reminding myself to close my mouth, as it was on the floor for most of this film.

I don't think I've ever been so glued to a film from start to finish like this, not for a very long time at least. I was desperate to look away but I couldn't. I didn't want to miss anything! I was anxious, disgusted, shocked and my eyeballs felt violated by what I was seeing and I will 10/10 be watching this again!

I hope to see more of Moore in roles like this and I cannot wait to see more from Fargeat. What a sick genious she is.

reviews.author: Ace9997
reviews.body: "The Substance" is a bold and unsettling movie that dives into society's obsession with beauty and staying young. Demi Moore gives a strong and memorable performance as a woman desperate to regain her youth, and Margaret Qualley brings a lot of depth to her role as the younger version. The special effects are really well done, making the transformations both impressive and disturbing to watch. While the story has some powerful moments, it feels uneven at times, and a few scenes are so intense that they might not be for everyone. Despite its flaws, the film has a unique and daring message that challenges how we view beauty and aging. It's a thought-provoking watch, even if it doesn't fully hit the mark.

It's well written, well shot a cool music mix, and a strong message about aging in Hollywood mixed with self doubt and anxiety and body dysmorphia in people who are beautiful being told they are not. A movie worth watching, and don't eat, 8/10.

reviews.author: taniostoledo
reviews.body:
The Substance is a film that deserves a 10 out of 10 rating for several reasons.

Directed by Coralie Fargeat and starring Demi Moore, the movie is a masterpiece of body and psychological horror that delves into deep and disturbing themes of identity and obsession with youth.

Demi Moore delivers an outstanding performance as Elisabeth Sparkle, a fading celebrity who turns to a black-market drug to create a younger, perfect version of herself.

Moore's performance is intense and convincing, capturing her character's vulnerability and desperation masterfully.

Coralie Fargeat's direction is equally remarkable. She builds an atmosphere of tension and horror that keeps the viewer on the edge of their seat from start to finish.

The screenplay, also written by Fargeat, is smart and provocative, exploring the psychological and physical consequences of striving for perfection at any cost.

Additionally, the film has been acclaimed by critics and audiences alike, receiving praise for its originality and technical execution.

The cinematography is stunning, with visuals that are both beautiful and disturbing, perfectly complementing the film's dark narrative.

In summary, The Substance is a film that not only entertains but also makes the viewer reflect on deep and relevant issues.

It is a work that combines powerful performances, skilled direction, and an engaging story, fully justifying a 10 out of 10 rating.

reviews.author: cecs95

A new horror classic is born quite frankly. Over the top, funny as hell and incredibly deranged, this just slams its point over your head over and over, each time with more blunt force.

I've seen some people criticize the mechanics of the substance, but i'd argue that drives the point even more home: women, and at this point in our ig crazed times, even men, will undergo surgical procedures that won't make them any younger and will disfigure them simply to belong again.

It's a simple concept of a harsh reality but a searing one. And it builds and builds to such a ridiculous height that u really feel this kind of culture is being poked fun the whole time. To me, this was a marvel to watch unfold until the deliciously over the top finale.

By the end you're a bloody pulp begging for mercy like our beloved Elisasue. But i actually wanted more and more of this.

reviews.author: digdog-785-717538
reviews.body:
Yep, you will see a lot of reviews that say "oh, the theme of getting old" or "wanting attention from others" but really, they are completely irrelevant - they are the very shell that the character portrays in this film.

What you do get, is by far Demi Moore's best performance of her entire career without exception. And, a masterful combination of visuals and sound, incredible acting from everyone involved, superb direction, and an excellent story that does not rely on moralisms or "themes" to be effective.

However, it's .. not perfect.

The film is WAY too slow. And it makes it always obviosu what part is going to come next in the script, it telegraphs its moves like an incompetent boxer. And it also takes so. Much. Time. To move to the next point in the script, together with the film being so high-intesity, that it can be agonizing to wait for it to progress, but we're still watching because of how incredibly well made it is.

I would recommend this film to anyone who can stomach the fairly intense horror aspect, but i also imagine that some time in the future some shorter-runtime fanedit is going to come out that will make this film substantially better.

My vote, despite the problems: 8/10.

reviews.author: treadstone-83088
reviews.body:
Astonishingly bleak observation of the shallow world of beauty, misogyny and the demands of television. This reminds me of 1970s Art House film. Shock jock images that reduce any storyline to the parking lot.

Demi Moore, who is 61 (and looks it), plays a 50 year old Morning TV fitness guru, who suddenly finds out that she is deemed to be too mature for the role, in a gloriously overacted performance by Dennis Quaid (now 70).

The Substance of the title (and story) is some sort of chemical cosh, that promises the user a 'different' and better (more youthful) version of themselves.

That it all ends in tears hardly matters. It is the inevitability of Dorian Grey. The make up is macabre but very much parcel of the piece. However the characters are too unattractive and shallow to bring any emotion to the party. That is it's flaw.

reviews.author: jesusmcy-58776
reviews.body:
I had written something about this movie before, but today I went to see it again with another group of friends who hadn't seen it, and I had to revise some ideas and details that I overlooked the first time because I was so focused on the story. The Substance is a marvel in terms of direction; each frame evokes an emotion, and most scenes are designed to make you feel uncomfortable. From the seemingly insignificant opening scene to the bizarre moment of a polisher vacuuming up what's left of Elisabeth, every detail contributes to the unsettling tone.

The fact that Demi Moore's body seems unappealing in some scenes is a directorial achievement, as it's nearly impossible for this woman not to look attractive from any angle (with all due respect). While the film isn't perfect, with several logical flaws that interrupt the story-such as the lack of explanation about the procedure to acquire "The Substance." Elisabeth enters what looks like a dangerous lair and exits without interacting directly with anyone, which is not very believable but still entertaining. Also, how does one pay for this substance? It seems to be an extremely expensive chemical that must be maintained somehow. However, that's not the main focus of the movie, and it's not really necessary to dive into the substance's background too much.

In The Substance, the main theme is beauty-our obsession with it and how far we're willing to go to meet society's beauty standards. It presents a struggle between youth and old age. The emaciated Elisabeth complains about Sue's lifestyle, driven by an envious obsession for not possessing Sue's beauty or youth, while Sue, in contrast, criticizes Elisabeth's sedentary habits. Although they should be the same person, Elisabeth and her counterpart are disgusted by each other. Each has developed a distinct personality shaped by their lifestyle and self-esteem. Elisabeth shows no self-love and continues to deteriorate, while Sue, who gains more acceptance and media attention each day, feels good about herself despite hiding deep frustration.

This could be seen as a reflection of mental health issues when people become unhealthily obsessed with superficial beauty. Certain scenes may be particularly triggering for women who are self-conscious about their bodies. The Substance is a film that should be watched with an open mind, as it offers many interpretations. Some scenes may seem nonsensical at first glance, but they almost always hide something deeper. The last 15 minutes of the movie are excessively bloody and grotesque, but in my opinion, this is intentional. The film aims to make you uncomfortable, culminating in a bloody explosion that feels like the release of the monster within Elisabeth. It certainly offers a lot of social commentary that feels relevant and timely. While The Substance is shocking, it may be even more traumatic for women.

reviews.author: Bands44
reviews.body:
Elisabeth an older star is set to be replaced by a younger, hotter girl she decides to take The Substance, a drug that can create a younger, perfect and beautiful version of you the catch is only one person can live for a week and then the other lives life. Can they live with the consequences of this action?

The Substance to me lives up to the hype. The storyline is quite a good one, however I never really get what were the benefits for Elisabeth (or in general the original person) doing this in the first place. They always get older; the new person does not carry on living the original lives thus really no benefits. Thus, this experiment is always guaranteed to fail and screw over the original.

Acting was quite good.

Direction was nice until the last 30 minutes, I think they did not know how to end it, so they just splattered blood all over - making it a bit unwatchable.

The music was good. The sound at the beginning that player when The Substance was brought up reminded me of Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse (2023) when Miguel was around so I absolutely loved it.

It very much body horror so I would not suggest if you are squeamish. If you want to watch a much funnier version of this watch Dead becomes Her (1992) by Robert Zemeckis.

Do heavily recommend watching The Substance.

reviews.author: topiben-97992
reviews.body: I was really looking forwards to this. Although the premise of nothing new, I thought it could be entertaining with potentially a new take. Instead we are treated to tedious groundhog day scenes which are drawn out to fill the time and make no sense. We aren't drawn to any of the characters as they're all so flat. Can't say that Demi's Elizabeth evolves in any way as she simply continues to be empty and craving. The worst bit for me is that there's nothing new here. However the supposedly gruesome is way sub standard, which reflects the story as a whole really. Can't even say it's chaotic as that would imply energy. reviews.author: DLochner
reviews.body:
*Rarely does a film captivate with such precision and intensity. With an impeccable screenplay, this film is a masterclass in efficiency-lean and razor-sharp. The performances from Demi Moore, Dennis Quaid, and Margaret Qualley are nothing short of breathtaking. Each actor delivers a powerhouse performance, elevating the story's tension and emotional weight. It's easily one of the best films of the year.

The story may not be entirely original, but it's told with such ferocity and relevance that you're hooked from the start. Every scene feels immediate and gripping, making it impossible to look away. The film's deep connection to current issues gives it a sense of urgency that feels especially relevant today.

Visually, the cinematography is a game-changer. The camera work is unlike anything you've seen before, moving with a fluidity and perspective that makes each frame feel alive. It's a visceral experience, pushing boundaries in both form and storytelling.

This film isn't just good-it's unforgettable. A true triumph in modern cinema.

reviews.author: Eclaire-seul
reviews.body:
Very much text book for the majority, the message is skewed as it's very much service level. The writing lacks depth which you can see just in the character writing, which misses the crucial balance and nuance to not come across as pandering.

It seems obvious they realised they don't have the talent for this nuance as writers so turned to shock and awe for the third act.

Was it decent? Yes.

Groundbreaking. No.

Writing let's down what otherwise is a competently made, well constructed film. For anyone looking for a balanced look at the world that forces you to think about the themes of ageism, beauty, and misogyny - you won't get it here.

If you're looking for a laugh and have a dark humour, you will probably have a good time.

reviews.author: flcntk3-856-986017
reviews.body: We all know "California Roll". As its name's sake implied, it is an amalgamation of "edible cultural substance" wrapped under a sheet of seaweed. This is how the movie was to me. Since we are onto food, I shall start with the most visceral chewing sequence of eating shrimp cocktail by Dennis Quaid, who played the very loud show producer Harvey and who was at a dismissal lunch meeting with Demi Moore, the lead character Elizabeth. In that scene, Dennis chewing was a total emancipation of any known social grace or table manners. In closeups, under Dennis grinding teeth, the shrimps are no longer part of a delectable starter of fine dining, but a swirling mess of unappetizing protein, or more precisely, to use the scientific detachment of non-judgmental to redescribe what I said, they were simply some protein SUBSTANCE. Now if we were to use the same non-judgmental scientific lens to interpret the entire movie, again, starting with the shrimps, which are protein being digested, assimilated and transformed by Quaid to become part of a newer Quaid on a cellular level, That is biology. As such, if you were to use the same metric to understand what happened to Moore, isn't that the same thing? Some evolutionary newer self from cell division? This is my point, and if you were to see it as a show about speculative science on evolutionary possibilities, that could well be a National Geographic show, but it isn't. The reason why it isn't is because the story is seen through the lens of social criticism. Here is why I used "California Roll" as a metaphor for the movie. Like California Roll, the amalgamation in this case is how science and accusative social context are rolled into one to form this. Another aspect of amalgamation here is of genre: sci-fi and very, very black "comedy". The comedy aspect is attitudinal and as a viewer, you need to find it somewhere swimming among the Mardi Gras of horror. From an entertainment point of view, Dennis, Demi and Margaret (Qualley) are just captivating to watch. Other delights for me came from a host of homages or references to classics. For example: The Picture of Dorian Grey, Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde and finally that very iconic scene from the movie "Carrie" . You will know what I mean if you have read either those books or seen those movies.

reviews.author: thesar-2
reviews.body:
I can see why this got the attention it so deserved.

Continuing into Ahhctober 2024, we come to a close. The End. Halloween Day 2024. I was supposed to watch the classics, Halloween (1978) and its first follow-up from 1981. But no. Facebook advised me "The Substance" was available (finally) on Streaming - via Mubi, included with a 7-day trial. I *knew* I had to jump on the bandwagon.

I was right. They were right. This movie will be talked about for years. Decades. Talk about an Instant Classic. It IS worth the hype. I *loved* this movie and need to own it.

Demi Moore, sorry, Hollywood-Has Been Elisabeth Sparkle is getting oust as a 50-year-old (Shoot, I can relate) and as her career is set to be behind her, she's given the "Substance" to rekindle her youth and continue on. Only, there's a catch, isn't there? Oh, yes, there's a catch.

As this movie neared its third act, but still within Act Two, I compared this to 1986's The Fly. This feeling only grew stronger as the finale drew near. This WOULD be a great double feature with that masterpiece from the mid-80s. YES, I would rate The Fly higher, but this was close.

There is no subtlety here. This is in your face. It's odd and off. Everything is very exaggerated. And it makes you know the rules of this universe. So, this causes stakes and you'll feel those so high. This was brilliantly spread throughout.

Speaking of which, I *did* think this movie was too on-the-nose during the first half. I never thought it was bad. It was just too obvious for what they're trying to convey. As it progressed, it didn't matter anymore. This felt like...a whole world I loved to be in. This was pure horror and I haven't experienced this in years.

Sure, it's not completely original in its minute/initial concept. It comes into its own. You Do know the rules, so you know what these dueling entities are dealing with.

100% I felt, in the final act, this movie will be studied for years. Sure, it's just another indie horror film in the 2020s. This one just feels special. Well shot. Well-acted. With Great locations, believable actors and situations. It IS fantasy, but you can still relate.

Let this be a lesson to you all. Accept your fate or face a worse situation.

***

Final Thoughts: If only you followed the rules...

reviews.author: santosrochamaju-31372
reviews.body: I simply decided to start watching this movie in the morning, and ended up finishing it at night. I'm a big fan of Demi Moore's work, I first met her in Ghost which made me cry a lot. But this movie made me want to just freak out!! Highly gore simply because it has more raw scenes and a lot of blood! reviews.author: phildeesnow
reviews.body:
It's a great 80's movie, unfortunately for everyone involved in the making of the movie it's almost 2025.

It's full of references of great movies from the 80's and great directors like everyone mentioned before, Cronenberg, Terri Gillian, Oliver Stone, Kubrick and by the end, even Troma...if you remember The Toxic Avenger... With references to Scanners and even Carrie. So it reminded me of a Saturday matine at my childhood's movie theater. Nostalgia, but it wasn't enough... reviews.author: Olona2018
reviews.body: I loved every second of the movie . The storyline, the characters, the visuals were impeccable. It's very hard to find a good horror movie in 2023/4 and this is by far the best. It's very gory and detailed in every aspect. The story behind the whole thing is relatable to what we see in Hollywood . It's relatable in the most scary way if you think about it . A gold medal to the writer and director! I hope to see more of your work!!

reviews.author: JTMokko
reviews.body:
Substance was a brutal and thought-provoking viewing experience. The main character of the story is 50-year-old Elizabeth Sparkle (Demi Moore), who is a fading Hollywood star. Her morning aerobics show suffers from declining viewership and the show's producer Harvey (Dennis Quaid) wants to replace her with a new and younger star. At this point, a mystical "substance" is added to the patterns, which promises to restore youth.

The subject of the film is very understandable. Aging is especially dangerous when appearance is a profession and at the center of the whole worldview, as is the case with the main character of this story. Elizabeth felt her popularity waning and for popularity she was ready to make any concessions. The story of Substance was reminiscent of Oscar Wilde's famous book "The Picture of Dorian Grey". In both, youth and success are not attainable without costs. And the cost is not a quantity that can be measured in money in either story.

While watching the film, I didn't know the director's name, and thus I hadn't realized that the director is a woman. When the strong images of the film hit my field of vision, I wondered why a man would go to such lengths when showing a woman's body and its changes, but it became clear when I saw the director's name in the closing credits - Coralie Fargeat. Based on the film, I can say that she is a rare auteur director nowadays. Fargeat also wrote the film's story, which makes the film feel like one person's wild fever dream. This in no way diminishes the film's profound message and effectiveness. Substance is the first film I have seen from Fargeat and I must say that based on this film we can expect more interesting and different films from Fargeat.

Substance is not an easy film. Several scenes at the end of the film were so brutal that it was hard to believe your eyes. Neither the producers nor the other members of the working group could or wanted to curb the director's vision. All the violence and detailed changes of the body were captured in embarrassingly long shots, almost as if the director wanted to go beyond the shock. I wouldn't be at all surprised if one of the viewers left the cinema feeling sick. However, this was not the case at the screening I was at, even though I heard disbelieving giggles and shuddering from time to time.

One slightly tiring feature of Substance was the music video-like shooting, which cultivated close-ups and fast cuts combined with sound effects. This created a nervous rhythm in the film at times and also distanced it from reality. Maybe it was a deliberate effect or the director's characteristic style.

Substance's male characters were exaggerated. They showed only basic desires and weaknesses - there was hardly any multidimensionality to be found. Especially Harvey, played by Dennis Quiad, succeeds in creating a stereotypical image of a slimy Hollywood television producer. The world and story of Subtance reminds me of an educational fairy tale, where the characters are not meant to be deep or relatable, but they represent archetypes that just drive the story forward.

Subtance is a critique of the attention economy. Elizabeth is used to money and popularity and does not want to live without them. Like in social media - A person feels appreciated according to how much attention they get. Attention becomes a drug. The film can also be seen as a criticism of the privileged rich social class. This is manifested quite juicily towards the end of the film.

Cinematic connections can be found in David Lynch's Eraserhead and David Cronenberg's films, but Fargeat goes a little further than them, at least in terms of shocking.

#Substance #TheSubstance #DemiMoore #CoralieFargeat #BodyHorror

SUOMEKSI (In Finnish):

Substance oli brutaali ja ajatuksia herättävä katselukokemus. Tarinan päähenkilö on 50-vuotta täyttävä Elizabeth Sparkle (Demi Moore), joka on himmenevä Hollywoodin tähti. Hänen aamuinen aerobic shownsa kärsii madaltuvista katsojaluvuista ja ohjelman tuottaja Harvey (Dennis Quaid) haluaa vaihtaa hänet johonkin uuteen ja nuorempaan tähteen. Tässä vaiheessa kuvioihin tulee mystinen "substance" eli "aine", joka lupaa palauttaa nuoruuden.

Elokuvan aihe on hyvin ymmärrettävä. Vanheneminen koskee erityisen paljon silloin kun ulkonäkö on ammatti ja koko maailmankuvan keskiössä, kuten tämän tarinan päähenkilöllä. Elizabeth tunsi suosionsa hiipuvan ja suosion takia hän oli valmis tekemään mitä tahansa myönnytyksiä. Substancen tarina muistutti Oscar Wilden kuuluisaa kirjaa "Dorian Greyn muotokuva". Molemmissa nuoruus ja menestys ei ole saavutettavissa ilman kustannuksia. Eikä kustannus ole kummassakaan tarinassa rahassa mitattavissa oleva määre.

Elokuvaa katsoessa en tiennyt ohjaajan nimeä enkä täten ollut sisäistänyt että ohjaaja on nainen. Kun elokuvan vahvat kuvastot iskivät näkökenttään ihmettelin miksi mies menisi niin pitkälle kuvatessaan naisen kehoa ja sen muutoksia, mutta asia kävi selväksi kun näin lopputeksteissä ohjaajan nimen - Coralie Fargeat. Elokuvan perusteella voin sanoa että hän on nykyaikana harvinainen auteur-ohjaaja. Fargeat myös kirjoitti elokuvan tarinan, minkä johdosta elokuva tuntuukin yhden ihmisen hurjalta kuumeunelta. Tämä ei vähennä yhtään elokuvan syvällistä sanomaa ja puhuttelevuutta. Substance on ensimmäinen elokuva, jonka olen Fargeatilta nähnyt ja täytyy sanoa että tämän elokuvan perusteella voimme odottaa Fargeattilta jatkossakin mielenkiintoisia ja persoonallisia elokuvia.

Substance ei ole helppo elokuva. Useat elokuvan loppupuolen kohtaukset olivat niin brutaaleja että oli vaikea uskoa silmiään. Ohjaajan visiota eivät tuottajat tai muut työryhmän jäsenet pystyneet tai halunneet hillitä. Kaikki väkivalta ja kehon yksityiskohtaiset muutokset oli piinallisen pitkillä otoksilla taltioitu melkein kuin ohjaaja haluaisi mennä shokeeraamisen tuolle puolelle. En yhtään ihmettelisi vaikka joku katsojista lähtisi pahoinvoivana pois elokuvasalista. Näin ei kuitenkaan käynyt näytöksessä jossa itse olin, vaikka välistä kuulin epäuskoisia naurahduksia ja kohahduksia.

Substancen yksi hieman rasittava piirre oli musiikkivideomainen kuvaus, jossa viljeltiin lähikuvia ja nopeaa leikkausta yhdistettynä äänitehosteisiin. Tämä loi elokuvaan paikoitellen hermostuneen rytmin ja etäännytti sen myös todellisuudesta. Ehkä se oli tarkoituksellinen tehokeino tai sitten ohjaajalle ominainen tyyli.

Substancen mieshahmot esitettiin liioitellusti. Heissä ilmenivät vain perushalut ja heikkoudet - mitään moniulotteisuutta ei juuri löytynyt. Erityisesti Dennis Quiadin esittämä Harvey onnistuu luomaan stereotyyppisen mielikuvan Hollywoodin limaisesta televisiotuottajasta. Subtancen maailma ja tarina tuo mieleen opettavaisen sadun, jossa hahmojen tarkoitus ei ole olla syvällisiä tai samaistuttavia vaan he edustavat arkkityyppejä, jotka vain ajavat tarinaa eteenpäin.

Subtance on huomiotalouden kritiikki. Elizabeth on tottunut rahaan ja suosioon eikä halua elää ilman niitä. Kuten sosiaalisessa mediassa - Ihminen tuntee saavansa arvostusta sen mukaan kuinka paljon hän saa huomiota. Huomiosta tulee huumetta. Elokuva voidaan nähdä myös kritiikkinä etuoikeutettua rikasta sosiaaliluokkaa kohtaan. Tämä ilmenee varsin mehukkaasti elokuvan loppupuolella.

Elokuvallisia yhtymäkohtia löytyy David Lynchin Eraserheadistä ja David Cronenbergin tuotannosta, mutta Fargeat menee heistä vielä vähän pitemmälle ainakin shokeeraamisen suhteen.

reviews.author: serge-tsv
reviews.body:
I quite anticipated watching this movie with a provocative title "The Substance" and potentially interesting plot (Best Screenplay at Cannes). I was intrigued to see a view on men's addiction to fame, glory and opinions of other people, and to what ends one would go to in order to retain this way of life.

And I wasn't disappointed. Although the narrative seemed quite slow at the beginning, it started getting a little faster and glorier with time. I wouldn't go into details, just put out my final thoughts - using substances devides human into two different parts. And, if not controlled, it causes inevitable destruction of both. And the movie depicts this very thouroughly.

The main actors were incredible - Demi's, Margaret's and Dennis's performances were outstanding. Most of the scenes felt disgusting, asexual, but I think that was the point, to show the duality of glamorous life. The ending seemed like it was directed for a different movie.

All in all, 8 out 10, which is great I think for a niche movie like that.

reviews.author: avalsmith
reviews.body: I don't even know where to begin when praising this movie! The camera work and directorship it was SO bold and different than you typically see but it worked so well. This movie was so raw and intimate you connect to the characters so much and you almost can't look away. The message of this movie was so incredibly touching and powerful. You literally watch this woman allow every ounce of her to be sucked away until she completely loses herself. All because she couldn't find her beauty in herself and tried to find an easy fix to be "perfect" and younger. This is the type of movie you watch once and it never leaves you.

reviews.author: larschristensen-99287

This wonderful different horror flick went from Bo Derreks "10" to " The Elephant man" and further to " Sunset Boulevard" or Sally Fields Oscar acceptance speech!
