reviews.author: farukallhossain
reviews.body:
"The Substance" is a cinematic disaster in every sense of the word. The plot is non-existent, the acting is wooden, and the direction is painfully inept. From the opening scene to the final credits, this film is a relentless assault on the senses. The dialogue is laughably bad, the special effects are amateurish, and the pacing is slower than a snail on sedatives. It's baffling how such a project made it past the initial pitch.

The storyline attempts to weave together complex themes but falls flat due to poor execution and a lack of coherent narrative structure. Characters are introduced without any depth, leaving the audience indifferent to their fates. The supposed twists and turns are predictable and do nothing to elevate the viewing experience. It's as if the filmmakers aimed to tick off every cliché in the book.

The cinematography is another major letdown. Shot compositions are uninspired, and the color grading makes the film look washed out and lifeless. The music score is equally forgettable, failing to add any emotional weight or enhance the scenes. By the end of the movie, I was left wondering how I managed to sit through the entire runtime without walking out.

In short, "The Substance" is an excruciatingly bad movie that fails on every level. Save your time and money and avoid this film like the plague. It's a perfect example of how not to make a movie and stands as one of the worst cinematic experiences I've ever had.

reviews.author: david_hutton
reviews.body:
I thoroughly enjoyed this film and was quite surprised to see Demi Moore involved in such a daring project. It's refreshing to witness a well-known actress stepping out of her comfort zone and embracing a role that delves into the darker side of human experience. The film appears to draw inspiration from a rich tapestry of body horror classics from the 80s and early 90s, such as Re-Animator, Braindead, and Society (1989). These influences are evident not only in the themes but also in the visceral imagery and unsettling atmosphere that permeates the film.

The editing style is reminiscent of Tetsuo (1988), adding a frenetic energy that amplifies the film's surreal and sometimes nightmarish quality. This choice of editing creates a sense of disorientation that perfectly complements the storyline's exploration of identity and the human psyche. The plot bears notable similarities to the Japanese film Perfect Blue, which also delves into themes of obsession, fame, and the disintegration of self. It's intriguing to see how the filmmakers have woven these influences together to create a narrative that, while familiar, feels uniquely compelling.

While the film doesn't necessarily break new ground in the body horror genre, its execution is commendable, and the performances, particularly Moore's, elevate it beyond mere homage. Her willingness to take on such a challenging role is commendable, and I genuinely hope to see more actresses following suit, embracing projects that push boundaries and explore complex themes.

One aspect that did detract from my overall enjoyment, however, was the film's length. At times, it felt overly drawn out, which slightly diminished the pacing and impact of certain scenes. A tighter edit could have enhanced the film's intensity and kept the audience more engaged.

Overall, this film is a fascinating amalgamation of body horror influences, and it's a testament to Demi Moore's versatility as an actress. It's a daring venture that encourages viewers to reflect on the nature of identity, beauty, and the sacrifices made in the pursuit of perfection.

reviews.author: TreeFiddy53
reviews.body:
This film..... I'll try and explain what I just watched. This was a movie experience like nothing else this year, like nothing else in a while. This is NOT for the fainthearted, NOT for the squeamish.

I'd heard a lot of things about this film....about the body horror, the mesmerizing....storytelling, the violence, the "don't watch while you're eating".....all of that is true. The best way to describe the film, not the best way, but the first thing that came to mind was....'Saw' with a social message, told in a way you didn't know it could be told.

The highlight of the movie IMO is what it's trying to convey and how it's told. The commentary on the society's beauty standards, validation, on Hollywood and the men who are in charge....ooof - expect award nominations. Demi Moore and Margaret Qualley both deserve all the praise they can get, expect nominations for the best and support acting categories. The set design, editing and sound-design deserve a special mention.

I sadly expect the film to not win as many awards as I think it deserves because other films that were more widely watched will beat this one to the awards, movies like Dune 2 (which was a snooze-fest IMO but OK). This certainly isn't for the kids. Given its genre, I bet half the adult audience won't watch it. The ones who do, I anticipate 90%+ giving you positive reviews, but I have a feeling that's not going to be mainstream enough for the awards. I hope I am wrong.

Regardless, this will go down as a cult classic at the very least. At best - one of the most memorable (notice that i didn't say best) movie experiences of the year/ of all time.

reviews.author: felipedehnthuring
reviews.body:
Provocative and visually striking, it's a feminist body horror film about youth and beauty obsession and its pressure on women in the entertainment world. Elizabeth Sparkle (Demi Moore), a former fitness guru, uses a drug that transforms her into a glamorous, young version- Sue (Margaret Qualley) -for the sake of revealing her above all the changes in their lives. The drug would begin a chain of reactions that would lead Elizabeth to a melodramatic fight with the altered self over who should rule their life.

Demi Moore does the perfect acting in career-defining fearless portrayal as Elizabeth: inner struggle with the fact of age compared with societal requirements. The result is a brutally raw, emotionally charged performance, particularly in parts where Elizabeth comes to grips with the reality of her own disappearance and physical decline. The grotesquely beautiful transformation scenes of Moore become even more chilling under Fargeat's surrealized lens and feats of body horror one might expect from a film made by David Cronenberg.

reviews.author: explorimentationist
reviews.body:
The Substance is undeniably STYLISH, with INCREDIBLE CINEMATOGRAPHY, production design, and MUSIC. The montage and camera work are great, giving the movie a slick, modern look that instantly grabs your attention. The story feels original in some ways.

However, this is a classic case of STYLE-OVER-SUBSTANCE. The movie is hollow and lacks depth. It relies heavily on SHOCKING BODY HORROR purely for hype, and these grotesque moments do little to serve the narrative or support the main message. The gross-out scenes, with excessive squelching sounds in nearly every shot, speak for themselves.

The PERFORMANCES by Demi Moore and Margaret Qualley deserve applause, but unfortunately, that's where the praise ends. The movie promised a lot in the first half but dragged into a ridiculous, gross-out climax that felt more DISGUSTING than clever, losing all potential and opting instead for a dumb, over-the-top final act that completely breaks the film's momentum.

The movie's messages about the objectification of women and the pursuit of beauty are clear within the first 15 MINUTES. Why, then, do we need to sit through TWO MORE HOURS of repetitive body horror?

What could have been a thought-provoking experience instead turns into a shallow attempt to disgust the audience. The Substance may be visually spectacular, but it tries too hard to shock and offers little beyond that, failing to deliver anything interesting or insightful.

reviews.author: vanderstamjeroen
reviews.body:
"The Substance" is a dark and captivating film that hooks you from the start with its detailed cinematography. Demi Moore's brilliant performance adds depth, showcasing her at her best. The film's use of gore isn't gratuitous; it builds tension and enriches the narrative. Overall, it's a must-watch that leaves a lasting impression.

The story stands out for its originality, tackling the theme of true beauty in a way that is both thought-provoking and unconventional. It's a narrative that dares to question societal norms and pushes boundaries, making the audience reflect on what beauty truly is and can be.

reviews.author: gregkae
reviews.body:
This movie is like a Picasso painting - misshapen, colourful, out of place yet somehow compelling to watch and weirdly beautiful. It doesn't make sense, yet is subject to interpretation thanks to the many layers

Excellent score and sound design, same goes for prosthetics. It's beyond good actually.

The pacing and acting is uneven, definitely overlong and needs editing. There are some loud echoes of Lynch to be found along with Cronenberg, Aronofsky, DePalma... which makes the direction derivative. It's also completely unhinged and the latter part may be too silly for some but it just continues the narrative, where do you think this movie was going? To play bingo?

reviews.author: insatiableaskeri
reviews.body:
Before reading any reviews or watching this flick, I had a certain preconception about the gist and the message this movie carries.

Strictly speaking, I think, we need to divide the general idea into 3 parts:

1) The sense of disgust and repulsion: apparently satisfying scenes of eating scrumptious foods and demonstrating female bodies deliberately were shown in an abominable and revolting way. To my mind, the director wanted to display how modern society objectifies beauty and trivializes human basic needs (specifically portraying it at the end of the film)

2) Psychologically related issues: The repugnant final scene, which is widely considered as the main flaw of the film, is technically the most striking and thoughtful moment of the whole story. It is believed that some people might feel uncomfortable while watching it, as bright and vivid colors do not evoke a cozy atmosphere, nor is the final bloodshed scene pleasing to an eye. Nevertheless, though the prism of deviated beauty standards and a constantly dissatisfied human nature, the film conveys the idea of our own mental issues and inner problems.

3) Grotesque embodiment: Unfortunately, this story tells about moral decay and societal collapse we are currently experiencing. Namely, people have lost humanity, which was perfectly depicted in Denis Quaid's character. Also, contemporary society does not want to work on their mistakes, but, instead, is eager to look for the easiest ways to perfection. To my greatest lament, most individuals would rather compare themselves with others instead of acknowledging their own strengths and unique qualities.

Even though the movie raised all these issues in a tremendously outrageous and appalling manner, it goes without saying that we failed to recognize our own perversive nature and intentions.

reviews.author: samircds
reviews.body:
This movie surprised me in ways I never expected. A story that is innovative and at the same time very inspired. It keeps you hooked from beginning to end, I couldn't get up from my seat at any point, Demi Moore's performance is undoubtedly the best performance of her career, and Margareth Qualley and Dennis Quaid shine throughout the film.

The film has a solid first act, starting with a very well-constructed introduction teaching us the Substance exercise, Elizabeth's personality and the functioning and rhythm of the film.

In the second act, we have a rhythm that escalates in a PERFECT way, building a slight tension and anguish in the viewer, but even so, it does not prepare us for the 3rd act, which I feel is exaggerated.

The third act is still at a very good pace, but now much more frenetic, and embracing the Body Horror genre, which works very well here, giving us a conclusion that works well, but it moved too quickly towards the end, which for me could have somewhat hindered the end of the experience. Watch it without knowing much about the film in order to have a better experience.

In conclusion, alongside "I'm Still Here" by Walter Salles, these are the best films of the year.

reviews.author: imdb-92083
reviews.body:
Without too many spoilers, it's a body horror, about an aging tv star, (Moore - obviously) who gets herself into something that she thinks will get her back on the hot list... And it kind of works, but there is a twist of course, and if you don't follow the rules, bad things happen. And they do.

This was a surprise treat for me, and reminded me of the old body horrors of Cronenberg and. Argento with a dab of Carrie in the final scenes. There's mutated "things" and scenes that might make you wince a bit!

There's a few questions to be answered by the viewer and left open? Most importantly - what is going on with The Substance and who is behind it? How many people know about it? Conspiracy theories abound in the absence of answers.

I found it paced well across a relatively long run time and was never really bored, with the tension building as Sue and Elizabeth have a few 'disagreements' which climax in the finale, where the desire for adoration and fame seems to overwhelm the horror.

I would expect to see some sort of sequel or "origins/prequel" at some point to answer some of the unanswered loose ends? Who made it? Where did it come from? How prevalent is it? Is Elon Musk a Substance clone?

Destined to become a cult classic, in a world where live on ad-heavy Netflix and now terrestrial tv, it doesn't interrupt the flow every 15 minutes with the same adverts you have seen a million times, probably during the same film.

A film that will stick with you and make you think about it again and again, a rare thing indeed at the end of 2024. And if you want to know what Demi Moore did next, this is the film for you 😀

reviews.author: arvindbalaji-75590
reviews.body: What a film !! Loved it completely. The setting up of the film in the starting few minutes is so brilliant and well written, without that strong setting up, the story would have felt half baked and utter tragedy. The music score was fantastic, CInemotography and the graphic designer did a fantastic work as well. The lead actresses was very good, The sue actor was felt wrong fit at the start and man of man i was wrong, she did her part exceptionally well and all the supporting characters did performed good. The only logic mistake i found was, I thought both characters were the same person at the start, as the story progresses that kindof differed and not properly explained who controls who , or they are completely different personas. All good other than that, I will surely recommed this film to the Filmbuff community.

reviews.author: jnizic
reviews.body:
"The Substance" is a 2024 horror drama movie directed by Coralie Fargeat. The movie stars Demi Moore as Elisabeth Sparkle, a fading celebrity who is willing to do anything to stay famous, and Margaret Qualley as Sue, a fresh and young face, adored by all, except Elisabeth.

The plot is original and pretty captivating as it shows to what lengths Elisabeth is willing to go to to remain a celebrity. The movie was definitely better because Demi Moore portrayed Elisabeth flawlessly, showing her self-hatred and her struggle with society's twisted ideas of worth as a women. The cinematography makes the story look very realistic which intensifies every scene, and some scenes were just downright revolting and nauseating, which I believe just further proves how determined Elisabeth is and how she would stop at nothing to achieve her goal. The movie tackles the problems such as self-confidence, which we can see with Elisabeth because even though most people could only hope to be as beautiful as she is, she wasn't satisfied because she could always be more beautiful and more perfect, and society's view on women.

In conclusion, the film is really well made, at least up until the ending. I would say I enjoyed it because I could never guess what was going to happen next, unlike in most horror movies which are very predictable. This movie is definitely not for squeamish people like myself as it contains a lot of gore, which I unfortunately wasn't aware of. But overall I'm glad I watched it and I would give it a solid rating of 4/5 stars. So if you are a gore lover and don't know what to watch, this would be a perfect movie for you.

reviews.author: icemen32
reviews.body: I hardly ever leave reviews on movies, I typically rate them and go on about my business. The movie just ended and my wife and I can't stop laughing about how unbelievably bad this was. How on earth did they get Demi Moore and Dennis Quad to sign off on staring in this. No idea how this movie has gotten such great reviews, but it is the worse movie I have ever seen in my life, and I'm not speaking in hyperbole. Then throw on top of that the movie is two and a half hours long. No idea how they convinced a Hollywood studio to sign off on this film. Do not watch three hours of your lives watching this. Literally watch anything else.

reviews.author: nyanbatcat
reviews.body:
This is one of those rare movies that exceed in every Level. Acting, visual Style, Sound, editing, Just everything flows into one cohesive, very competent and unique Film.

The whole movie has a fairy tale character. Many things are heightened, but never to a point where they movie loses me, the emotions always keep you anchored to what is happening. The two lead actresses performances play a vital role in this. Other characters are mostly heightened and can add some dark comedy, especially when they interact with our protagonists.

The cinematography and editing are amazing and not only are they beautifully done, they also create a unique look and tell a huge amount of the story. Poppy colours, quick, snappy editing and close ups are contrasted by colourless sets and lingering wide shots (although its never really dreary or smudgy looking). Nothing seems out of place, everything intentional. This strictness alone creates an atmosphere that makes the viewer feel trapped in what is going on on screen. It fits the narrative perfectly. A world pretending to be happy and healthy, that simply burries its unhealthy selfhatred beneath a bright, colourful veneer.

The soundtrack and soundediting are memberable and fit the overall style well.

Everything is topped off by some of the most insane and probably best body horror imagery every captured. The effects go above and beyond and are to a big amount practical. Everything keeps evolving and escalading juuuust in the right tempo. Only at the beginning of the third act i felt like I was ahead of the story, but thats very subjective.

reviews.author: jayycchen
reviews.body:
The Substance is not for the faint of heart, especially if you're unfamiliar with the body horror genre. Don't be misled by the presence of Demi Moore and Dennis Quaid into thinking this is a mainstream film with subtle gore, like Hannibal or Dexter. This is far from Death Becomes Her, though both films explore similar themes. The Substance is a true body horror film, featuring disturbing and even shocking scenes that might be unsettling for mainstream audiences. However, if you're a fan of movies like American Mary, SAW, or Malignant, you'll likely find The Substance to your taste.

Beyond the unsettling visuals, the film excels in its cinematography, pacing, storytelling, and intensity. It's undeniably a well-crafted production, though it's definitely not for everyone.

In terms of comparison, The Substance feels closest to The Fly (1986), American Mary, and Death Becomes Her.

reviews.author: JoeyBagOfDonuts
reviews.body: So I just finished watching this. I'm kinda numb. I mean I just don't know what to think anymore. I'm not sure what is real and what is delusional. Ok maybe not to that extreme but this movie went to a place that I only imagined to exist. I've been watching horror movies for over 50 years and in all that time I don't think I've ever witnessed anything so disturbing as The Substance. Let's start with a life lesson. You may not be happy with yourself, your life, etc. That is a far cry from where you could wind up though. There's nothing wrong with self improvement, but sometimes the price exceeds the reward. And that is where this movie has gone. I always thought that The Fly (the remake with Jeff Goldblum) went to lengths to gross out the viewer. That movie was a stroll in the park compared to this. Re-animator and From Beyond tried to do it as well, and they were good for their time. But this movie.... I don't have the words to describe the experience. I have a tendency to nod off while watching movies... but this one kept me awake and focused. Even The Human Centipede didn't reach the heights of gross out horror as this. I wish I could share the experience with someone but I don't know anyone who would want to watch it with me. Would you?

reviews.author: dstan-71445
reviews.body:
The Substance follows Elizabeth Sparkle, a narcissist who's overly preoccupied with her appearance to a point where she measures her self-worth solely based on how her physical features fit into the ideals of perverted men and sexist and shallow societal standards. The more she ages, the less she's objectived as a borderline sex toy by the production company that hires her and the sexist fanbase who follow her show solely to get either sexual gratification or some unhealthy and irrational contentment from watching her stretch and bend on TV. Elizabeth being a self-obsessed drama queen feels constant hatred towards herself because strangers don't adore her body (not her personality, interests and deeds) anymore. This stupid character of hers drives her into getting involved in a shadowy, back-alley treatment which promises to turn her young again with strict rules she and her other unpredictable and uncaring self must follow. Things spiral out of control and both her and her other young self start pissing off each other, slowly breaking the singularity that was expected from them. The Substance finally instructs it's audience to cherish whatever one posseses and how adoration from strangers is ephemeral and is never to be used as a scale to measure one's sense of worth.

I enjoyed this movie a lot and loved how the two main characters don't often speak their minds but effectively relay whatever is going on in their heads through their expressions and actions. Loved the intense atmosphere exhibited throughout and the discomforting body horror depicted. Movie is not horrifying whatsoever and would even say hilarious at times when the events and body gore pictured go over the top. Great performance from Demi Moore and especially Dennis Quaid (most entertaining Weinstein-esque character). A fresh, well-thought out and meticulously crafted movie that successfully delivered much needed entrainment to my night.

reviews.author: pedroquintaoo
reviews.body:
The Substance gripped me from the very first moment, starting with the trailer. Its sharp editing caught my attention, not only for its frantic pace but for the promise of something out of the ordinary. I can say upfront: the movie fully lives up to the hype. I dare say it's one of the best films I've seen this decade.

The narrative is brutal, packed with powerful symbolism and metaphors. Coralie Fargeat delivers a spot-on critique of the obsession with image, a patriarchal society, unrealistic beauty standards that suffocate us all (especially women), deep insecurities, and the fear of aging. It's a film about women, but also for them, addressing themes that go beyond the screen and resonate deeply in today's world. And all this without ever resorting to showy tactics like so many big studios.

Much like her last film, Revenge (2017), Coralie Fargeat gives us a feminist piece, but without following the usual shallow paths we often see in major studio productions. The difference lies in the depth with which she tackles these issues. The goal here isn't to provoke for the sake of it but to make us reflect on the many challenges and societal pressures women face, without resorting to the typical "mainstream" narratives we've become accustomed to from multimillion-dollar studios. These studios often offer surface-level treatments of serious social issues, just to get a few mentions on Twitter or TikTok.

At no point did I feel attacked as a man while watching the film. On the contrary, it made me reflect on the challenges so many women face regarding their image in a world largely controlled by a patriarchal system that pressures them in every way.

As for the story, I loved every second. From the first minute to the last, The Substance maintains a pace that leaves no room for dull moments. The editing is absolutely superb, and despite its 2h20 runtime, the film flies by. It's rare to find a movie that takes you on such an intense, frenetic, and utterly surprising journey. For me, cinema is about emotional experiences, and this film pushed me to the edge of mine.

The cinematography and sound editing are breathtaking. Every scene is visually rich, every sound seems carefully chosen to amplify the experience. The film begs to be seen in a cinema, on the biggest screen possible, with a sound system that can capture its unique atmosphere. The sensory experience is among the best I've ever had.

I can't talk about The Substance without mentioning the incredible performances by Demi Moore and Margaret Qualley. They are the heart and soul of the film, each driving the narrative in a gripping way, turning every scene they're in into something spectacular. These performances deserve to be recognized at every awards show.

That said, it's important to note that this isn't a horror movie. If you go in expecting that, you might be disappointed. It's essentially a drama with some thriller elements and a few graphic, unsettling images that might turn the stomachs of more sensitive viewers. But it's not the conventional horror some might be expecting.

I highly recommend watching it, and I genuinely hope this film gets Oscar nominations. It would be an outrage if it didn't. For me, it's not only the best film of the year but possibly the best I've seen this decade.

reviews.author: jfgibson73
reviews.body: I think that this will probably be my favorite movie of the 2020s. I gravitate towards well-told stories that include insane climaxes, and nothing will top The Substance in that department for a long, long time. I am hoping that I will continue to enjoy it and find greater appreciation as I watch it back. I know it's not the recipe for massive commercial success, but I am thankful that there are filmmakers who are willing to go this far off the deep end. And it isn't just one sequence--The Substance starts off wild, but continues to build all the way through. The final sequences go further off the rails than anything seen probably Malignant, so they definitely didn't run out of steam too early. Upon first watch, I had some minor nitpicks; there were definitely moments that went on too long, and some performances that didn't hit quite the right tone. Dennis Quaid in particular didn't work for me--his character felt like he stepped out of the Mike Myers Cat In The Hat adaption. But I think those things will bother me less over time. I will recommend The Substance to anyone who will listen.

reviews.author: bzxykcyk
reviews.body:
Good one actually not bad compared to all similarly based movies.

The film blends surreal visuals with gruesome body horror, influenced by the works of directors like David Cronenberg, to critique the obsession with youth and beauty. Its graphic depictions of body mutilation and extreme close-ups challenge viewers to confront their own complicity in upholding unattainable standards. While the horror is intense and unsettling, it serves as a sharp commentary on the pressures faced by women in a society dominated by patriarchal ideals of appearance and success. Fargeat's direction, combined with striking cinematography and powerful performances, makes The Substance both horrifying and thought-provoking, though some find its satirical elements heavy-handed.

It's a visually bold and thematically charged film, yet not for the faint of heart, offering a unique and disturbing exploration of societal vanity and the dark side of the entertainment industry.

reviews.author: jackiemalabugcalata
reviews.body: Wow. THE SUBSTANCE is a modern horror film that wholly lives up to it's promise and its premise. This is a film i wager many will love for its sheer audacity, and just as many will reject like a rotting chicken drumstick, as it is definitely an acquired taste, but i feel it's destined to become a cult horror classic. Demi Moore, Margaret Qualley & Dennis Quaid deliver astounding performances alongside an impeccable supporting cast & cast of extras, each committing entirely to every moment they are on screen in this dark, twisted, human, cruel, beautiful, violent, absurdist, satirical tale about fame, hunger, greed, the ageing process and so much more, set firmly in an industry always in search of fresh meat for the masses - executed with surgical precision by a team that fired on all cylinders.

reviews.author: interatlantica
reviews.body:
The Substance is one of those rare films that leaves you utterly speechless by the end. With its blend of dark humor, unsettling plot twists, and moments of pure absurdity, it is certainly not your typical cinematic experience. As someone who hadn't laughed so hard in years, I found myself equally entertained and disturbed-an unusual but exhilarating combination.

At first glance, the movie appears to be heading in a familiar direction. The premise-an experimental substance that grants extraordinary physical and mental abilities-has been explored before. However, the film takes a sharp turn into the bizarre and comedic, refusing to conform to any predictable narrative structure.

What makes The Substance stand out is its unexpected shifts in tone and pacing. Just when you think you've got a handle on where the story is going, it takes an absurd, often grotesque turn, leaving you off-balance and eager to see what will happen next. In particular, the final scenes-without giving too much away-are the perfect embodiment of dark, nihilistic comedy. The climactic moments left many of the moviegoers around me scrambling for the exit, likely overwhelmed by the sheer audacity of the film's conclusion. Yet, for those who stayed, the payoff was unforgettable.

The humor in The Substance is as dark as it gets. It's the kind of comedy that makes you wince before you laugh, and often, the laughter comes from a place of discomfort. The film does not hold back from poking fun at the conventions of both science fiction and horror, with exaggerated portrayals of human greed, vanity, and desperation. Yet, despite its outlandish scenarios, there's an underlying satirical commentary about the human condition that resonates deeply. The closing scenes were the perfect blend of hilarity and horror, a sequence so outrageous that it had me and others in the audience laughing uncontrollably.

The lead actors, particularly those playing the scientists and corporate figures behind the creation of the titular substance, deliver their lines with the perfect balance of seriousness and absurdity. Their deadpan reactions to increasingly bizarre events heighten the humor, and it's clear that the actors were fully committed to the film's darkly comedic vision.

Standout performances come from the main female characters whose descent into madness is both hilarious and terrifying. The ensemble cast also does a great job at portraying a range of bizarre characters, each one more ridiculous than the last.

Cronenberg, in The Substance, pushes the boundaries further, injecting his usual unsettling style with a healthy dose of dark comedy. The film's visual style is grotesque yet captivating, with scenes that are equal parts disturbing and funny.

It's worth noting that The Substance will not be for everyone. The film's abrupt tonal shifts, disturbing imagery, and grotesque humor may alienate some viewers, particularly those expecting a straightforward narrative. During my viewing, several audience members left the theater before the end, seemingly uncomfortable with the film's more bizarre and shocking moments. However, for those willing to embrace its oddities, the film offers an unforgettable experience that challenges expectations and leaves a lasting impression.

It's a film that defies convention, blending dark humor, horror, and satire in ways that are both hilarious and deeply unsettling. It won't be for everyone, but for those who enjoy films that push boundaries and embrace the absurd, it's a must-watch. I left the theater feeling entertained, challenged, and-most surprisingly-laughing harder than I have in years. This is a film that will spark conversation and, for those willing to take the ride, it offers a cinematic experience unlike any other.

reviews.author: davidforti-34443

reviews.author: saolivaresm
reviews.body:
Director Coralie Fargeat positions her film in the best Kubrick and Cronenberg style, giving us her own feminist body horror film that hits the ground running with a heart of its own.

With a striking and resonant script, defiantly grotesque and strangely funny, the presentation of The Substance becomes one of the most satisfactory bets of this year, establishing itself as one of the best films of the year not only for being excellently directed or brutally acted, but also for being one of the films with the most personality of this year, leaving its own and gratifying mark.

We are faced with the passage of time of an actress played in an amazing way by a Demi Moore who returns in glory and majesty to the forefront with her most outstanding performance of her career. Moore manages to take her character of Elisabeth Sparkle to the edge of decadence with a performance that feeds in an abstract way a bit on the Demi Moore persona to give us a sample of anger, terror, desperation and revenge. She lets herself be guided by a daring director and Moore enters that game and it turns out perfectly, the actress shines like we have never seen her before and simply gets fully into the big candidates for the award season. However, not only is Demi Moore amazing, but Margaret Qualley comes and tells you that she is also an absolute star with a masterful interpretation of Sue. Qualley takes on a character full of magnetism and confidence, handling it with the intelligence of knowing that she is an "Object", but knowing that it is a satirical style of what she represents in her director's version, where she wraps it with a successful style and adds that touch of mystery, because at the end of the journey it is a duel of egos of a character called Elisabeth, who wins absolute dominance.

The director does not shrink and goes straight to give an uncomfortable and brutally honest look at the sexualization of women and what beauty represents. She does not go with stories and her direction proposal reflects it with a range of camera shots that will make you uncomfortable, but she also does it without limiting herself in the excess of bodies, blood, liquids and brutality. The director gets the best out of great references of the genre, but she does not limit herself to only getting the best out of them, but the director gives it her own identity that allows you to always be aware that Coralie Fargeat is behind the cameras and is doing it with her own rules and her own ideas that do not seek to equal, but rather to present herself as an authority and quality of her own and that is from a director who is on her way to standing head-on among greatness.

We are in the presence of one of the best films of the year and possibly one of the great contenders of the awards season and it does so with its own arguments, because it is presented with intelligence, honesty and personality that goes directly to those who are not simplistic, it is a film that will give you a battle, it will give you suspicion, it will make you uncomfortable, but it is a satisfactory, overwhelming journey full of clear, direct and symbolic messages.

It's a film full of its own identity that doesn't try to please you with its simplicity, guys, we're far from that, it's a film made by women with personality and character that put feminism in you without giving you room to complain, because here it hits you where it hurts the most and leaves you simply covered in blood and unable to clean yourself.

reviews.author: MK_Ultra_
reviews.body:
Went in as blind as I could, but hard not to hear the murmering pre and post festival runs.

First off, the sound engineering, the practical effects and the just the pitch black writing is bar none, probably the most perfectly aligned film that is as perfectly sinister as it is sharp as it comes. Demi Moore and the "version" actress are individual forces in this. Quaid seems to have lost his way the last few years but his return here is perfect in as a sleazebag producer.

This is a film that has its tongue firmly inserted against its cheek the entire fever dream of ride.

Blown away. Probably one of the more memorable films I have seen in quite some time.

Prepare yourself for this one.

reviews.author: matepolcz
reviews.body:
The Substance is awesome, heavy and gross. It has a killer production design, cinematography, sound design and visual effects.

The writing is amazing, but it's style is not for everyone. The story is an exceptional cautionary tale about the power of compulsion to conform. Elizabeth wants to be seen, loved and approved by others, which leads her to use the substance. Her new form, Sue has her personalities, so she makes the same mistakes as the original version and if everything had gone perfectly, she would've had the same fate as Elizabeth. The people around her were all toxic old men, who only cared about her looks, so that's how she looked at herself, which is completely unhealthy. The writing is perfect.

The directing is also outstanding, with amazing cinematography, production design that uses colours and lightness perfectly and visual effects that looked flawless. Everything was in the face of the audience, which I personally didn't always like, but that doesn't mean it's not any good. The acting performances were spectacular, Demi Moore was unbelievable.

The Substance is provocative, visually stunning, perfectly written and directed, but I didn't enjoy watching it as much in the theater as much I like it thematically.

reviews.author: bercinerol
reviews.body:
Substance (2024) is an artistic tour de force that pushes the boundaries of both storytelling and visual design. The film captivates from the very beginning, blending a unique narrative with breathtaking cinematography that draws the audience into its surreal, dreamlike world. The director has crafted a film that challenges conventions, delving deep into themes of identity, transformation, and the human condition in a way that is both thought-provoking and emotionally resonant.

The performances of Demi Moore and Margaret Qualley are stellar across the board, with delivering a powerful, nuanced portrayal that leaves a lasting impact. The movie's world-building is also exceptional, creating a hypnotic atmosphere that immerses viewers fully in the strange and captivating universe of Substance.

However, it's important to note that Substance is not a family-friendly film, as it contains numerous nude scenes that may feel excessive to some viewers. While these moments serve the film's artistic vision, they make the movie inappropriate for younger audiences or those uncomfortable with explicit content.

Overall, Substance is a daring and visually stunning piece of cinema, perfect for those seeking an unconventional and immersive film experience-though it's best suited for mature audiences.

reviews.author: benjamingauvin
reviews.body:
After seeing an interview with Demi Moore about this new movie, some YouTuber who watched it, the trailer, my brother tells me to watch this movie, I was really intrigued. I knew that just with the trailer this movie would be different. Different means often worth taking the time to watch it in our busy life. Some of the new movies that they are making are sometimes a bit bland and unflavored. So if something goes in a new direction, I want to taste it as soon as possible.

The movie was really something else, an experience in itself. I can surely feel that some inspiration from Requiem for a Dream was taken in their ingredients. This was about a concept that maybe some people had thought about once in their lifetime; what would happen if I were in a younger body with all the skills I had learned in my life? It explores this subject with a touch of Black Mirror vibe. A sci-fi, horror, drama, suspense movie. Demi Moore was stunning; we really felt all her emotions that the characters had in the storyline.

We explore a subject about twins, how we can feel sometimes when the other is performing better than ourselves. They also go in terms of how career and work can poison our lives and how all that we do revolves around our performance level and the working industry. They always want us to perform better than yesterday, and if a younger version, a new person without any experience, can perform better than us, we are replaced.

The movie was more horror-themed than everything else, but they certainly had a lot of great things that can be taken away from the script and storyline. They pushed the extremes from A to Z about many things to make us realize how society can make us sick, really sick...

I really loved the style that the filming took, the zoom on ordinary stuff, the color of the clothes, the luxury of the apartment and the studio, the contrast of color choices that made it pop. The music also, and the bass from the sound effects, was on point. Like every good horror movie, that's a must. The girls also, they picked the right ones for the cast to make people jealous for the girls and for the boys, really sit thight to see everything. It was eye-catching for sure. On the other hand, some scenes were disgusting, almost making me want to vomit,the sounds of dead animal flesh and meat that was rotting and cooking, the un-freshness of ingredients, and the moisture of rotting bodies. God, it can make you not touch your popcorn in some scenes.

This one was really an entertaining movie, well done, definitely one of the best 2024 horror movies that I've seen. If you want to go into another dimension, another zone, if you want to escape and feel something, this is the place to go. I can guarantee you that you will feel something. Maybe you'll not love the feeling that it will give you, but at least you will feel alive and maybe even want to think about some stuff in your life after that. 8/10.

reviews.author: hazingsbookie
reviews.body:
The Substance is an intriguing mix of sci-fi and psychological thriller, with flashes of brilliance, but ultimately falls short of its full potential. The film sets up an interesting premise, exploring the dangers of scientific ambition and the ethical boundaries we cross in pursuit of progress. However, while the concept is promising, the execution feels uneven.

The visuals are sleek and unsettling, creating an atmosphere that's both sterile and foreboding. There are moments of genuine tension where the film shines, and you can see what it's aiming for-something along the lines of Ex Machina or Annihilation-but the narrative doesn't quite hold together. As the story progresses, it starts to unravel, with too many ideas competing for attention and not enough depth to any of them.

That said, the performances are strong, but the film's biggest flaw is its pacing. At times it's too slow, taking too long to build but overall a good watch.

reviews.author: cineculturist
reviews.body:
This film delves into how greed becomes a byproduct of fame. While other films often try to balance fame and greed, this one focuses intensely on the consequences that come with unchecked greed.

The runtime is 2 hours and 21 minutes, and it takes its time, never feeling rushed. In my experience, the real impact of the story begins around the 1-hour and 9-minute mark when the setups start to pay off.

While the genre is sci-fi/horror, to me, it felt more like a gore film. Demi Moore and Margaret Qualley deliver outstanding performances, bringing depth to their characters. Director Coralie Fargeat's writing and direction are impressive; she made the story feel so convincing that I found myself genuinely worried about her mental health.

Just when you think the film couldn't get more gore, it pushes the boundaries even further, it has fareshare of nudity too. For those who enjoy bloodshed in movies, the finale will be a thrill.

For more reviews follow me on instagram - @cineculturist.

reviews.author: RalphRahal
reviews.body:
A disaster from start to finish. This film is an insult to the illustrious careers of Demi Moore and Dennis Quaid, who both deserve far better than the material they were given here. It's frustrating to see such talented actors tied to a project that fails to deliver anything meaningful or memorable.

The story focuses far too heavily on the body of Margaret Qualley's character, Sue, rather than using her presence to tell a deeper, more impactful story. This overemphasis cheapens the narrative and shifts attention away from what could have been a more thoughtful exploration of the themes at hand. The gratuitous gore towards the end feels like a desperate attempt to follow modern trends, but it doesn't work. Instead of being shocking or engaging, it feels forced and pointless.

Coralie Fargeat had a chance to make something bold and meaningful, but the movie ultimately feels hollow and disconnected. There's no clear message, no emotional depth, and no sense of purpose in the storytelling. It's a missed opportunity for everyone involved, leaving viewers wondering what could have been if the focus had been on substance rather than spectacle.

reviews.author: wongkinglee
reviews.body:
In an era where CGI dominates filmmaking, enabling even low-budget productions to appear cinematic, filmmakers are increasingly rejecting polished artificiality in favor of raw, grotesque visuals and deeply unsettling themes, aiming to provoke thought and awaken desensitized audiences. So comes The Substance.

Visually, The Substance is as grotesque as it is fascinating. From the relentless poking of bodies to extract fluids to the surreal scenes of writhing organic forms that blur the line between human and monstrous, the film is a relentless assault on the senses. These moments are both horrifying and oddly satisfying, forcing the audience to confront their desensitization to violence and overused CGI tropes in contemporary cinema.

While the film's shocking imagery could have easily descended into gratuitousness, it's balanced by its cerebral underpinnings. The grotesque visuals serve a purpose, challenging viewers to grapple with themes of identity, aging, and the commodification of the human body in a world obsessed with perfection.

This is not a film for the faint-hearted. Its unrelenting intensity may alienate some viewers, but for those willing to confront its horrors, The Substance offers a bold and unforgettable cinematic experience. It's gripping and impossible to look away from-a film that lingers in your mind long after the screen fades to black.

reviews.author: scottiestill
reviews.body:
I knew nothing going in, so just went with it. Firstly, Demi Moore possibly puts in her best ever performance here. (Great performances by Dennis Quaid & Margaret Qualley too).

The subject matter reels you in immediately, and from there you pretty much strap yourself in for a journey of the bizarre, funny, tragic & several thousand other emotions & feelings. Been quite a while since a movie drew as many varied feelings from me, I gotta say.

Cinematography, score, pacing, narrative, dialogue all top tier. I feel exhausted after watching it, and among other things, nauseas.. Which is an achievement as I'm an avid horror fan & fairly immune to gore.

You could make a number of comparisons or influences from other movies, and despite that, it somehow still feels original. Personally, (and like my tag line suggests) it gave me similar emotions to what I feel when I watch The Fly.

I'll keep it spoiler free other than that, but to finish up, I take a point off for being maybe a tad too long. That said, I genuinely think The Substance could in time, become a cult classic.

reviews.author: ranwulfs
reviews.body: The first three quarters of the movie were decent, but the last half hour it became another film entirely. The term "body horror" doesn't cover the level of hideous, graphically disgusting sequences splashed across the screen like vomit. I don't care that the film is supposed to be a commentary on Hollywood, society's standards of beauty, industry misogyny, or whatever other buzzwords you slap on it. Nor do I care that Demi Moore is lauded as "brave" for making the film. The film became unwatchable in the last 30 minutes. It reminded me of a weird, 1980s movie with low budget special effects, like "Reanimator" or any number of films best forgotten. A statement could have been made regarding societal values, etc. Unfortunately, any possibility of worth is tossed to the side for cheap, gratuitous gore and the complete abandonment of a story line. A terrible film.

reviews.author: Mauro_Silva
reviews.body:
The Substance it's a great solid intervention film, but it ends up becoming somewhat outrageous in its construction, being gross, repetitive, disgusting and exaggerated but also remarkable and impactful for it's attention to explore the grotesque side of greed, beauty, self-care, and healthiness.

From beginning to end, everything is an authentic hyperbole, using brutality and bizarreness, to emphasize the central subject and it's message. Though it targets women, it also affects men, representing a human tendency to find flaws in oneself. People get entertained, frustrated, and feeling excluded for not looking like celebrities, the "improved" versions of themselves, causing them to neglect their own health, as shown in scenes of laziness and uncontrollable food consumption and constantly sacrificing pieces of the real themselves in the search for aesthetic beauty, as is the case with the liquid that is removed and turns them into a monster.

Furthermore, all that sacrifice is capable of destroying the integrity of the person and In this film, it's possible to see Elisabeth destroying her entire reputation throughout the narrative, where it was created a personification between her Hollywood star and her life, which deteriorates over the years, as she ages, until at the end, she stained it by the last sign of her survival.

The film's cinematography, editing, and sound are excellent, meticulously designed to hold the viewer's attention and provoke feelings of disgust and disturbance where Demi Moore and Margaret Qualley's great performances are crucial in making this even more provocative.

Despite tackling an urgent topic that impacts the minds of many people, the movie got lost, and almost consolidated itself into a masterpiece on his genre, but ultimately becomes a montage of gore that stays at the surface, becoming more of a freak show than a meaningful experience, where in the first half promises a strong approach, but it goes too far, losing track of the plot, repeating several shots/scenes, being predictable and stumbling to an unnecessary ending, epic and funny, perhaps, but without a real purpose.

reviews.author: snoducky
reviews.body:
Something new, something to stand out.

With all the new films coming out recently this one truly is different, it's so raw, so graphic, so out of pocket. It's almost refreshing in a sense, a breath of fresh air in modern cinematography. With little references to old films (Shining, Carrie, American Beauty) this film really mixes old with contemporary, and makes it work. The meaning behind this film is super unique, unlike any other film I've watched previously, it's all about self acceptance, lacking acceptance, blocking yourself out and living in the past. There's a lot of little details that symbolise various problems in life, feminine stereotypes, masculine stereotypes, and how people overthink their looks. Alongside the great music and plot this film really outshines many other films. This film makes you want to gag, literally makes you gag, it takes a lot to make a person do that, the sound effects, the costume design everything boils down into this one of a kind film. If you want something different, this film is it.

reviews.author: biba_yu
reviews.body:
This movie is quite different from any body horror movie I've ever seen and I've seen A LOT! It's a string of surprises from start to the end, which is what I like. It's also visually stunning, and chaotic, while quite unpredictable. I have short attention span but even for over two hours long, it kept my attention.

While the idea of aging in Hollywood is not really new, the way it was processed is, and body horror is always interesting to watch in this era of great special effects, if done right, of course.

On the good side, there are story which is processed in interesting and new way, stunning visuals, great actors (particularly Demi Moore and Dennis Quaid for very brave roles they both took), unexpected ways story took turns and unlike many, I actually thought the ending was perfect fit. I also like how you can interpret the story and visuals in many ways, with lots of small symbols and Easter eggs to find.

On not so good side, it was difficult to relate to main characters, even Elisabeth, which was supposed to be my age, I didn't really relate to her, maybe to some smaller extent. But then again, I am not any kind of star. Even less I could relate to Sue or any other character. Relatability is not something that is "must have" for good movie but it helps to relive it more.

And I notice that a lot of shots of young Sue, which were supposed to be on ironic side, of how showbiz exploits young people, kind of pushed too much and became what they were actually against. There is a subtle line when you want to show something ironically which is quite easy to cross. Sometimes, at least for me, there was "too much of Sue", if you know what I mean.

But in general, it was quite fan experience, and quite original, well made movie.

reviews.author: TheArisen

They're portrayed as horny losers, and there's not even one decent character here. Throughout the entire "story," you're presented with gross imagery, constantly shoved into your face. Save yourself the time and money and watch something else.

reviews.author: isantistao
reviews.body: This is the first real horror masterpiece I have seen in years, and it is a true work of art that will probably go down in history as one of the classic horror films next to Francis Ford Coppola's Bram Stokers Dracula and the other great classic horror films of all time. This movie is so artistic and well done, every single aspect of it is a perfect 10: The writing, the story/plot, the directing, the acting, the cinematography, the editing/production, the style, the monster...it is all just so awe inspiring it was hard to believe my eyes, especially given that this was made by a female and women are not known for making hardcore horror movies. Now granted this movie is not hardcore in the violent sense, there are very few kills in it so if you are a slasher movie fan and really only watch horror for the kills, you may be disappointed there. Similarly it is also short on violence, and other such themes like torture, so if you are looking for those you also will be let down. However it makes up for this by involving the same amount of blood and guts you'd see in any of these horror movies, so you won't be disappointed there as it definitely triggers a massive amount of disgust through the "body horror" theme/style. And it also places more emphasis on the psychological side, creating the sense of emotional dread like something ominous, grave and terrible is happening in every scene, so if you like psychological movies that really make you think and feel things, you'll love this. And while most of the movie is not "traditional" horror in the violent sense, the climax and end of the movie when the monster manifests really brings this movie into hardcore horror themes so just wait for it, it will be well worth your patience as there is a massive payoff. And even in spite of the lack of violence throughout every scene is really artistic, creative and engrossing. Every frame is visually stunning and could be taken as a still image and put on the wall as a piece of artwork. The dialogue and behaviors of the characters are all very compelling. The lighting and sound scoring is all on point. Every thing about this movie was done so masterfully down to a T, it really is the perfect horror movie, even in spite of there not being that many kills. But most of all that is because it does what most horror movies do not, which is that it has meaning. This is such a thought provoking, intellectual and meaningful movie. It really made me reflect upon how my younger self sabotaged my older self, and like as we get older it is like there is still this young self trapped within us wanting to lash out, like our old and young selves are two warring factions within us, just as how the young and old people in society often are at odds with each other these days, and yet those are still two side of the same coin and should really learn to get along. This is the type of movie that even though I saw it almost a week ago it has stayed in my mind and forced me to continue remembering certain scenes and imagines, and to contemplate its meaning - which I think is the mark of a true work of art. Therein I rate it as a perfect 10 and think that everyone should see it.

reviews.author: rahuldeep-37247
reviews.body:
"The Substance" is a 2024 satirical body horror film that takes a darkly comedic look at the obsession with youth and beauty in modern society. The film follows Elisabeth Sparkle, a fading celebrity who, after being fired from her job as host of an aerobics show, is introduced to a mysterious new drug: "The Substance." This drug promises to rejuvenate her, temporarily transforming her into a younger, more vibrant version of herself.

However, this "rejuvenation" comes with unforeseen and terrifying consequences. The film explores themes of aging, identity, and the lengths people will go to maintain their youth and relevance in a youth-obsessed culture. It features strong performances from Demi Moore and Margaret Qualley, and its unique premise and disturbing visuals make it a memorable and thought-provoking cinematic experience.

While some may find its satirical tone and graphic imagery unsettling, "The Substance" is a bold and original film that challenges societal norms and offers a darkly humorous commentary on the human condition.

reviews.author: meddlecore
reviews.body:
A still stunning Demi Moore plays an oscar-winning actress who is forced to confront her age, amidst an industry that values youth and beauty over everything.

So, when she is offered a chance to engage in an experimental regimen, designed to reverse the aging process, by "tapping into the matrix within"...she hops on the oppourtunity.

Not knowing what lies in store...

After going through the process...her first act is to audition for the part of her own replacement.

However, things don't come without a catch.

As she must switch back to her original self every 7 days.

Despite being one, her younger self starts to conspire against her...that is...until she realizes the repercussions that entails.

As the consequences they inflict on one another are irreversible.

Both versions quickly realize that a balance must be struck.

Until it becomes a cat and mouse battle to counteract the effects they have on one another.

As they each begin to value what little time they have to interact with the world.

And seek to punish the other for any of the moments they steal from one another.

With the whole thing acting as a metaphor for what Hollywood puts women through.

As they use them up and spit them out (pun intended).

With the young and beautiful being treated like Gods...while the old are thrown to the waste side and forgotten, once they start to lose their fleeting beauty.

It's a tale as old as Hollywood, itself.

A sort of modern retelling of Sunset Boulevard...with a body horror twist.

Which is something it doesn't shy away from...as it quite clearly contains a number of homages to the master of horror himself- David Cronenberg.

The fly in the glass of rose; followed by the car crash at the beginning of the film, for example.

Though also via more subtle influences from films like Dead Ringers; eXistenZ; A History Of Violence; Maps To The Stars; and even The Death Of David Cronenberg, where the director confronts his own mortality.

Not to mention The Shining; Elephant Man; and The Thing...among others.

Which isn't to say that this film isn't wholly and completely original in it's own right...because it is!

In the most masterful sort of way.

It is, hands down, the best horror film of the year.

With an oscar-worthy performance from Moore, specifically.

If totally twisted cinema is your thing...you are not going to want to miss this...because you will be disappointed if you do!

Having watched it myself, now...I can see why it was the big hit at TIFF this year.

Every accolade it has received, thus far, is very well deserved.

So just watch it.

Cause it is definitely worth it.

8.5 out of 10.
