reviews.author: itsputtipong
reviews.body:
The Substance kicks off easy, like a twisted Bible story meets makeover fail, and then takes a nose dive straight into horror territory. Elisabeth and Sue? They're all good with the rules at first, but then Sue starts craving more "alive time," and let's just say things go off the rails.

Meanwhile, Elisabeth's body issues? Yeah, they're not solved - they're just lurking in the background, ready to blow up. She's got this date lined up, and watching her panic over makeup and outfits is like a cringe-worthy beauty vlog. You think you know where this is going, but trust me, your worst nightmare isn't even close to the mess Fargeat delivers. The last 20 minutes? Absolute chaos - things literally slither across the screen.

They call it satire, but don't be fooled. This is pure horror. We're talking extreme plastic surgery fails brought to life. It's the kind of movie that makes you wish they had one of those "fright breaks" from old-school William Castle flicks, where you could bail out before the ending.

reviews.author: cfchusen
reviews.body:
The substance was an intense and powerful experience, delivering a heavy emotional impact. It was raw and unfiltered, drawing out deep feelings of pain and vulnerability. Every moment felt charged with emotion, making it impossible to remain indifferent. It took me on a journey through some of the most challenging and profound aspects of human experience. The weight of the emotions lingered long after, leaving a lasting impression that was both painful and cathartic. An incredible Movie.

The Substance is a gripping film that delves into themes of addiction, loss, and the search for redemption. It follows the journey of its protagonist, who struggles with substance abuse, highlighting the devastating effects it has on their life and relationships.

The narrative is heavy with emotional weight, portraying the protagonist's inner turmoil and the painful memories that haunt them. The film effectively captures the desperation and isolation that often accompany addiction, showcasing the character's battles with both external and internal demons.

Visually, the cinematography is haunting, using dark tones and striking imagery to mirror the protagonist's mental state. The performances are powerful, with the lead actor delivering a raw and authentic portrayal of someone grappling with their addiction. The supporting cast adds depth, representing the loved ones affected by the protagonist's choices.

The pacing is deliberate, allowing viewers to fully immerse themselves in the character's emotional struggles. The film doesn't shy away from the harsh realities of addiction, making it a painful yet necessary watch. Ultimately, The Substance serves as a poignant reminder of the complexities of human emotions and the difficult path toward healing and self-acceptance.

It's a film that lingers in the mind long after viewing, inviting reflection on the nature of pain, resilience, and the importance of connection in the face of overwhelming challenges.

reviews.author: davidwalker-94471
reviews.body:
This movie is very good indeed. At once a stingingly satirical fable and also an out-and-out body horror. It really is gruesome.

I found it interesting to consider who the villains of this movie are. The men, all the men in this movie are presented in a very clear and particular light. Rolled up with the Coralie Fargeat's previous work, the excellent 'revenge', and there is a very clear message there.

That said, the main theme here seems to centre more on what people are prepared to do to cling to fame and fortune so perhaps Elizabeth Sparkle is the real villain. I enjoyed the idea of two distinct personalities eventually being at odds with each other. That speaks to me of what it could be like to have to maintain a celebrity persona.

And behind it all is an invisible corporation prepared to cash in on that greed for fame so maybe they're the villains.

Or maybe everyone has their villainous part to play and this is more about how the whole culture and industry just creates a terrible environment filled with monsters.

Both leading ladies are excellent. Demi Moore in particular really plays sad to desperately unhinged very well.

The movie is shot beautifully. The cinematography and the set design make for a visually brilliant spectacle. The effects are also excellent.

It felt a little too long in my opinion but I did enjoy this a lot.

reviews.author: post-38549
reviews.body:
What an outstanding film in every sense. Visually, this film is a true masterpiece. The entire concept-the collaboration of camera work, lighting, and scenery-is, in my opinion, visionary. The director has done an exceptional job here. But the film is much more than that. It's an exploration of appearance versus reality, the desire to be loved, the fleeting nature of our media-driven world, superficiality, ego, and humanity's underlying addiction to wanting more.

Bringing all of this to life in a body horror film is an act of remarkable courage. The horror portrayed, along with the truly outstanding gore effects, elevate the story and its substance to a whole new level. The music, the set design, and the visual engagement with the themes demonstrate that we are dealing with an extraordinary film and an exceptional director. I truly hope we'll get to see more films of this kind in the future.

reviews.author: thomasshahbaz-52541
reviews.body:
Imagine that Guillermo del Toro and David Cronenberg had a baby that turned into a much better director than Cronenberg's real son, and then that baby teamed up with the Black Mirror writers to make a film, with some guidance from Takashi Miike, that's this.

It's stomach-churning and hilarious, and I have massive respect to both leads for letting rip like this (in fact, all three, because Quaid deserves a shout out too).

If you're gonna make a film like this it should be jaw-dropping, surprising, appalling, not take itself too seriously, memorable and original, and this meets the requirements!

For the record, the dénouement that everyone seemed to feel let down by had me howling with laughter and clapping, honestly for me it was a perfect ending for everything that went before and really cemented the spirit and tone of the whole film.

reviews.author: boycefactor
reviews.body:
The Substance clearly draws inspiration from the Ozempic craze in the U. S., the rise of social media influencers, and the lingering effects of the #MeToo movement, offering a biting satire on female beauty standards and misogyny. Using a unique blend of body horror and comedy, the film doesn't shy away from blunt, visceral imagery to tackle these themes, making its point with a punch.

With standout performances and sharp dialogue, it holds a mirror up to society's obsession with youth and perfection. One line, in particular, "Pretty girls should always smile," is bound to resonate with many female viewers, underlining the pressure and expectations placed on women. The Substance may not be subtle, but it's a bold and darkly comedic critique of the beauty culture of today.

reviews.author: laurentsaletto
reviews.body: Coralie Fargeat obviously loves Stanley Kubrick. Lots of those long corridor shots complete with wild colours and a vaguely threatening figure at the end of it. In 49 minutes this was done too many times. That said, once would be too many for me. Ludicrous plot and with the fact there is a cleaner shown to work in the apartment, why is that cleaner not seeing the bodies and bloody mayhem? Who has a bathroom like THAT bathroom? A washbasin, basic shower and 5 acres of white tiles? The Dennis Quaid character is a panto villain. 2 dimensions would have been nice. The whole thing is plain godawful and clearly thinks of itself as something new and exciting. Errr no..... After 49 minutes I decided not to waste anymore of my own life to sit through this twaddle. Avoid at all costs.

reviews.author: OniFR
reviews.body:
Watching The Substance feels like snorting a line of Kubrick, downing a shot of Cronenberg, and finishing with a slap on the back from Lynch. Coralie Fargeat doesn't hold back-she throws everything at you. Strobe lights, suffocating close-ups, and an aesthetic so intense it feels like an Ikea catalog on LSD. It's violent, unsettling, but damn, it's beautiful.

The idea of sharing your life with a younger, sexier, well-rested version of yourself? Tempting-until Fargeat reminds you that every deal with the devil comes at a cost (sometimes an arm, sometimes a leg). Imagine a Black Mirror on steroids, where utopia spirals into carnage. The concept is brilliant yet terrifying: what if your double stared back at you like a final boss from Resident Evil?

Here, gore isn't just for show (though ironically, it's stunning). Every burst of violence is a piercing arrow, every punch knocks you down. It's somewhere between the visceral horror of The Thing and the surgical body horror of The Fly. Fargeat doesn't let up-she pushes to the edge of what's bearable, and you'll find yourself craving more. It's a bloodbath, but haute couture style.

Demi Moore, as a chilling matriarch, is a revelation: she looks like she's stepped out of a dystopian novel where humanity plays Frankenstein with their own bodies. Margaret Qualley captures fragile humanity morphing into monstrosity with eerie perfection. Dennis Quaid? A kind of washed-up mentor, Breaking Bad meets Dior. The dialogue is razor-sharp, dripping with enough arrogance to remind you no one's getting out unscathed.

Visually, it's an eye-gasm. The interplay of light, the oozing textures, everything is saturated and over-the-top, yet somehow cohesive. Each scene hits you in the gut, balancing fascination with unease. The music? A dive into an electro-industrial nightmare where every note crushes your soul a little more. The result is raw, savage, and unforgettable.

The Substance is the kind of film that divides: you'll either walk out clapping like a maniac or demanding your money (and dignity) back. Coralie Fargeat delivers a manifesto of visceral horror, a shattered mirror where anyone could lose themselves. It's brutal, beautiful, and horribly mesmerizing. An experience that shakes you like a cocktail shaker and leaves you drained, yet strangely satisfied.

reviews.author: andreialiguerra
reviews.body:
I went to see this movie, without expectations.. usually, when there is a big "hype" on the media around a movie, it ends up (almost always) being rubbish.

Well, that didn't happened here. This movie has amazing shots.. i mean, even the atmosphere of the beginning is amazing. Captured all my focus, from the start untill the end.. wow!

The score of this movie is also well thought, and you can see the influences of other big movies in it. (you will realize it, pretty fast, it is very obvious).

The actresses were great role players, I think the choice of Demi and Margaret, to play those characters was awesome.

This movie shows how things are built in a decaying society, (specially if you are a women) making you think about many life issues, even after the movie.

The final, gore part, for me is the climax of the movie, with all the body horror elements. Have to say it was my favorite part of it.. But anyway, some people might find the movie hard to watch, specially if they have troubles watching bloodish scenes.

But, if you are used to (and like) watching stongly visual movies, I advise you to check this one out.

reviews.author: kayejchapman
reviews.body:
The Substance is a body horror fan's dream that unapologetically embraces its absurdity. Some critics here are whinging about the ending going off the deep end, but this movie was never about logic - it's supposed to be pure, gory fun. The whole premise is unreal, and honestly, it would be far less enjoyable if it tried to make sense. It's absolutely a black comedy too, and I was laughing out loud at moments like shoddy DIY leading to a flawless secret room, and the monster with Demi Moore's face glued on lurching onto the set like something straight out of South Park.

The editing style with its rapid close-up cuts gave me serious Requiem for a Dream vibes, all intensity and momentum, but I'm so glad it never went that dark. The prosthetic work here is next level - it's so rare to see a movie these days with next to no VFX, and The Substance has so much soul as a result. The sound design is phenomenal, shifting between pulsing workout music and all the gloriously gory squishing and crunching noises that any respectable body horror movie should have. The final scenes are a brilliant homage to horror classics like Braindead and Evil Dead, delivering hundreds of gallons of blood and over-the-top gore. All in all, if you're cool with style over substance and you want abundant butts, boobs, and blood, this one's for you.

reviews.author: ciberzole
reviews.body: The Substance is a mesmerizing dive into horror and psychological thriller territory, with Demi Moore delivering one of her most compelling performances in years. She brings an intense and magnetic energy to her role, holding the screen with both vulnerability and fierce determination. The film itself is a dark exploration of human desires and fears, blending eerie visuals with a suspenseful storyline that keeps you guessing. If you're a Demi Moore fan, this is a must-watch-she really shines here! Director Coralie Fargeat crafts a chilling, atmospheric experience that horror fans are bound to enjoy.

reviews.author: kingfishfilmco
reviews.body: Definitely Next Level. Great combo of Twilight Zone with Cronenberg and Kubrick. Stealing while Honoring, but doing Her Own Thing. This caught my Attention. Next time, do a more like There Will Be Blood. I could see it. She's onto something Next Level. I Was totally impressed with all of her different angles and next level attempts at something different. It's impossible to do something Totally Original anymore. But to Catch Anyone's Attention is Special. We're so used to seeing the same old thing. Kudos to Her and Her Whole Team. Obviously, some recognized something different was going on here.

reviews.author: mataghost
reviews.body:
If you're a fan of Cronenberg-style body horror, The Substance is an absolute 10/10 must-see. The plot may be simple, but it hits hard with a sharp commentary on our culture's obsession with youth and perfection. What really stands out, though, is the stunning cinematography-this film is a visual feast. The bodies on display are absolutely mesmerizing, toeing the line between sexy and unsettling, and will keep you glued to the screen. Each scene is a masterclass in blending sleek, provocative visuals with spine-chilling horror.

From the flawless physiques to the eerie transformations, the film makes you feel both entranced and uncomfortable in the best way possible. Coralie Fargeat absolutely nails it, delivering an unforgettable experience that manages to be both thrilling and visually seductive. This is horror that gets under your skin while seducing your senses, leaving you both chilled and dazzled. Trust me, The Substance will stay with you long after the credits roll.

reviews.author: iamsanthosh-03
reviews.body: "Coralie Fargeat's 'The Substance' is a riveting exploration of society's obsession with youth and beauty, set against the backdrop of the Ozempic era's weight loss craze. The film follows the faded star Elisabeth Sparkle, played by Demi Moore, who discovers a mysterious product that promises to restore her youth. As Elisabeth and her younger alter ego, Sue, portrayed by Margaret Qualley, delve deeper into the use of The Substance, they face the harrowing consequences of their pursuit. Fargeat's direction is masterful, weaving a tale that is both a critique of ageism in Hollywood and a body horror spectacle. The performances are compelling, particularly Moore's portrayal of a woman grappling with her fading relevance. The cinematography and score create a vivid, almost surreal Beverly Hills, enhancing the film's thematic depth. 'The Substance' is a thought-provoking film that challenges viewers to reflect on the lengths one might go to for eternal youth, making it a must-watch cinematic experience.".

reviews.author: sachin-73003
reviews.body:
The Substance is one of those films that is unflinchingly brutal and pulls no punches when it comes to rendering you shocked and unsettled.

With relatable characters and an intriguing premise and an impressive comeback from Demi Moore and an equally stunning performance from Margaret Qualley the film explores the showbiz's terrible sides like sexism, beauty standards and a general awful lens through which women are viewed.

The desperation for the need to connect and be wanted and loved whether its by a singular individual or by everyone is what drives Moore's character to commit the strangest deals and acts.

The self doubt, crippling anxieties which govern or destroy our self worth and force us into meaningless trivial ways of self validation are put on vivid display through mostly Demi's character.

With body horror being the medium of horror for this one. Both the women show amazing skills to pull off these difficult performances whether its the gross blood and bodies or the nudity.

The absolutely unhinged finale makes it even more shocking and the brutal the fate of our protagonist leaves us with our jaws dropped on the floor.

reviews.author: wyzarcompetente
reviews.body:
The movie gets the point across quick, aging sucks and in a world of apperance and celebrity being a woman this gets even worst.

The good part of the movie is the cinematography, the shots are dynamic and sells very well how nasty the higher ups are and you can really feel the tension every moment.

But that's it, after the good introduction they start with the absurd, with one of the worst gores i ever seen for no reason, and after that they enter in a strange place, trying to be funny, using gore but with no story, it gets repetitive very fast. The end is trash, they have no story left, the message of the film was already clear but was like more than half of the film to go, so they just went full on the absurd and shock value.

You will always get a reaction from this film, good or bad it is impacting, but it's far from good.

reviews.author: bradleygaryckforbes
reviews.body: I was captivated and was totally taken on a journey. The way I saw it was kinda like what the human race is doing to the planet, taking more and more for fame and fortune, however we are one with the planet. It was absolutely and amazed by this film. I was totally sitting on the edge of my seat. I really feel that Demi Moore should get an Oscar for her performance. She is really a master at her craft. The story line is so original and I am happy that the trailers didn't give away the twist and tuns. This is a film everyone should watch but you definitely need the stomach to handle some of those scenes.

reviews.author: andrewchristianjr
reviews.body:
This was a wild trip WTF. The creativeness of this film was captivating I do wish the ending was different though. My take away, you only have one life and one body. Treat them with respect and just love yourself the way you are.

Synopsis: Have you ever dreamt of a better version of yourself? You, only better in every way. You should try this new product, it's called The Substance. IT CHANGED MY LIFE. With The Substance, you can generate another you: younger, more beautiful, more perfect. You just have to share time -- one week for one, one week for the other. A perfect balance of seven days each... Easy right? If you respect the balance... What could possibly go wrong?

reviews.author: ave_claudiu
reviews.body:
This movies is based on an extraordinary well implemented idea To be honest, this movie restores hope when we think about the cinematography.

The actors are top notch, demi moore reinvent herself with this role.

All is well made, well synchronised. The story is unique but not because of the idea in itself , but thankfully to the genius of the director.

Well, if it was not about the last 30 minutes i would have gave it 10/10. But thr last 30 minutes are a complete fiasco.

But feel free to skip the last 30 minutes and i hope you will appreciate the effort made by this director who tried to depict, based on a topic which sculpt our society nowadays.

reviews.author: daryasopkina
reviews.body:
"The Substance" is a sci-fi horror film that delves into themes of vanity, insecurity, and societal beauty standards, especially as they relate to aging. It serves as a dark satire, critiquing the unrealistic beauty expectations and objectification of women in Hollywood and society. Demi Moore delivers a standout performance, adding depth and complexity to the story.

The plot centers around a mysterious substance that promises not just rejuvenation but perfection, reflecting the unrealistic demands placed on women to maintain youthful appearances. The film's advertisements for this substance boldly claim it makes you not just younger, but better, highlighting the societal obsession with youth and beauty at the cost of authenticity and individuality.

While the movie's gory and chaotic ending could have been more refined, the performances, particularly Demi Moore's, are compelling. Her ability to convey complex emotions and motivations makes the film a thought-provoking commentary on the pressures and dangers of conforming to societal beauty standards. The satire is clear: "The Substance" critiques the superficiality and cruelty of Hollywood's and society's relentless pursuit of youth and beauty, offering a stark and unsettling reflection on human nature.

reviews.author: Dolmen37
reviews.body: I enjoy reading reviews from people who failed to appreciate the ending of the film at its true worth. I find the screenplay absolutely brilliant: it's the first time I've seen a film that shares the same fate as its main character (even though there are two of them, they are essentially one). I'll let you reflect on the progression of the movie again, and everything will become clearer, allowing you to raise your rating. I usually avoid rating films unless I can at least give them a 5, which I was close to doing before finally grasping the genius of Coralie Fargeat! A week after watching it, I'm still thinking about the film and its originality...

reviews.author: daanimahesh
reviews.body:
"The Substance" is a film that tries to captivate its audience with striking visuals, but ultimately falls flat. The movie feels more like an extended 2000s MTV music video-heavy on style, but lacking any real substance. Despite Demi Moore's efforts to breathe life into her role, the characters are disappointingly one-dimensional and cartoonish, failing to evoke any real emotional connection.

The plot itself is uninspired and feels hollow, with a plastic, superficial narrative that offers little depth or intrigue. The movie had potential, but instead of rising to the occasion, it plummets in its final moments. The ending, in particular, is painfully unsatisfying, cheap, and almost embarrassingly bad, cementing the film as a major letdown.

Overall, "The Substance" is a visually flashy but ultimately soulless experience. It's a film that could have been saved by a stronger story or more developed characters, but instead, it delivers nothing but disappointment.

reviews.author: nrrngsm
reviews.body:
I LOVED this. As a serious horror fan it's hard to make me shudder and I rarely have the urge to look away... this movie nailed it and delivered an impeccable culture commentary that'll make you laugh when you need it most. It's a harmonious blend of beauty, imaginative color placement, wild camera styles, cringe, envy, raw emotion and " **** the absurdity of the patriarchy" - maybe a dash of nausea for some. Dennis Quaids performance hits the nail on the head; it's exaggerated but delivered in such a way that he's sadly familiar. The last 20 mins are an experience of their own, an ending I applaud. The female leads really raised the bar on the this one, it's a classic.

"Pretty girls should always smile!"

reviews.author: sarantis_r
reviews.body:
The Substance is one of those movies that lingers in your mind long after the credits roll. Coralie Fargeat has crafted a film that's visceral yet stylish, pushing boundaries in a way that's both bold and unforgettable. It's a wild ride through excess and artistry, blending body horror with dark humor in ways that keep you glued to the screen. Just when you think it's about to let up, it doubles down, creating an intense, surreal experience that's as challenging as it is compelling.

If you can look past the gore and focus on the layers beneath, there's a surprising depth here. The film tackles themes of self-worth, self-empowerment, and societal expectations of women, especially in the industry. It's a fierce commentary on how women navigate a world that tries to define them, and the satirical elements hit hard, shedding light on the brutal realities masked behind the absurdity.

reviews.author: danielwsimpson
reviews.body: It's got a great point that isn't hammered into your head like most movies nowadays, it's got great horror scenes, very good effects, and amazing acting. The sex appeal in this movie is on another level with Margaret Qualley and not to mention Demi Moore, both of them putting on the performances of their lives. Let me get this straight though, sex appeal doesnt mean sex scenes, they just knew exactly how to use the beautiful actresses in the perfect way, to create some very visually appealling scenes. I'm expecting to see Margaret in a lot more films in the near future, and i would love to see her win an oscar for this... overall, it was the best movie I've seen all year.

reviews.author: jmxjrsss
reviews.body:
The Substance is a cinematic tour de force that pushes boundaries in the most evocative, shocking way imaginable. It's grotesque, vulgar, gore-filled, and disturbingly visceral-but that's exactly what makes it brilliant. Few films have the audacity to delve so deeply into human depravity while simultaneously delivering a profound and thought-provoking message. This one does so masterfully, leaving an indelible mark on its audience.

From the very first frame, the avant-garde and futuristic cinematography captivated me, drawing me into a world that felt uncomfortably real yet nightmarishly surreal. It's not just a movie-it's an emotional and sensory experience that keeps you on edge. I can't remember the last time a film gave me goosebumps this frequently or transported me through such a dizzying array of complex feelings. There's horror, sadness, revulsion, and a deeply unsettling empathy woven throughout.

Demi Moore delivers a performance for the ages, portraying a woman whose suffering is both fictional and heartbreakingly rooted in real-life experiences for countless women. The parallels between her character's struggles and societal issues were unflinchingly honest, leaving me with a bittersweet mix of disgust, sadness, and reflection. It's a film that forces you to confront uncomfortable truths, holding a mirror to a world that is often as vile as the one on-screen.

The Substance is not for the faint of heart. It's grotesque and graphic, yes, but beneath the shocking surface lies a message of raw power and clarity. For those willing to endure its unrelenting intensity, the rewards are immense. It's a film that stays with you, gnawing at the edges of your mind long after the credits roll.

This is filmmaking at its most fearless. I loved it beyond words.

reviews.author: lordsoracle
reviews.body:
A fading celebrity takes a black-market drug: a cell-replicating substance that temporarily creates a younger, better version of herself.

That's the basic description from the cover. I'll be honest, when i started this flick, I had no idea what I was getting into and guess what, I am wowed!

Demi Moore plays a yesteryear Jane Fondaesque fitness guru for a morning show Elizabeth Sparkle who has just clocked fifty and her executive producer Harvey (Dennis Quaid) no longer thinks she has it anymore and needs a replacement.

Enter "the substance", a breakthrough generic engineering process that causes what I won't mention here so that I don't spoil it, suffice to say she gets a dose at stardom, being young and sexy once more (played by Margaret Qualley).

What follows is a bizarre journey into the darkest recesses of a hellishness and of vanity on steroids. And with each act you know this is headed into a dark place, but it's the last act that for me brought back my memories and fondness of movies like From Beyond and Society which deal with the Cthulhu Mythos and are steeped in classic Lovecraft tropes.

Suffice to say this for me was a fresh take on dark comedy horror. Very well done actually and gets a full ten out of ten for me.

reviews.author: HabibieHakim123
reviews.body: The Substance is the perfect definition of a once-in-a-lifetime experience, of course it's up to different people whether they would rewatch The Substance happily, but for me and i believe most viewers, once was more than enough, the film is chaotic, reminding me of Irréversible, though with a weirder, less realistic plot, it's bold, daring, and frankly, unthinkable at times, Coralie Fargeat's filmmaking is incredibly stylish and captivating, and the performances by Demi Moore and Margaret Qualley are exceptional, as far as i recall, the film offers no moment to catch your breath, it relentlessly digs deeper into your gut for the entire 141 minutes, although i felt it went a bit too far towards the end and could have ended anytime during that whole chaos sequence, the movie seems intent on ensuring that the audience leaves with the nightmare it conjures, and it certainly succeeded with me earlier, it's incredibly disturbing, horrifying, while it's perform and made incredibly well, overall besides The Substance definitely becoming one of the best films of the year, it's also one of the weirdest and disturbing film i've ever watch.

reviews.author: PotassiumMan
reviews.body:
Try as I might, I simply couldn't stomach this disgusting ordeal in the end. Actually at one point or another, I desired those in the audience to talk in order to distract me- that is quite unusual. Many horror aficionados will applaud how audacious and unapologetically explicit the film's style is. But I have my limits and draw a demarcation line between that which is thought-provoking and filmmaking that turns into simple torture. This would be the latter, regrettably.

It starts out intriguing and pulpy enough before nose-diving into nightmarish savagery. Demi Moore is a Hollywood superstar whose glamor and heyday has long faded into the past. She discovers a mysterious underground drug that enables her to return to her former beauty and relive the peak of her career. Dennis Quaid is quite good as the grotesque TV producer of her workout program that she does in the twilight of her career. Margaret Qualley is the younger version of Moore's starlet. Solid performances and flamboyant visuals draw us in before the film gives new meaning to heavy-handed depravity.

The best that I can say for this film is that it will be tough to forget. Whether you're mesmerized or repulsed, this film will leave its footprint on your psyche. It's too extreme to recede from one's consciousness. You'll either be in awe or need a shower when you get home. But for the record, not recommended. Not at all.

WTF. Having said that.

Here the core of the horror is the aging and the hatred of Elizabeth who hates Sue who hates Elizabeth. The idiosyncratic alternance between the two. A very old body is monstrous as almost never shown on a screen.

The special effects gives a touch of artisanal which is a fresh breath of good, old air.

There's a bit of all the biggest. References to Cronenberg (i.e.: The Fly and Shivers above the others). Dario Argento is also there: Did you remember Nadia Nicolodi in Tenebrae when she paints all those beautiful arabesques with the blood of her just ripped arm? And the colors of Shining, in the long corridor of the studio seen in the different sequences of the movie.

Dizzy and greasy, techno soundtrack, fast shots of camera, flesh and fat and wet noises. The movie of Coralie Fargeat is a bloodbath rave which starts like a gala. You can feel it inside your mouth, almost.

Funny and entertaining, paints the portrait of an entertained director.

reviews.author: felkyneye
reviews.body:
Very much worthy of the praise.

PLOT: An aging celebrity, about to be replaced, takes a chance on a fix-all promising a newer, younger, better version of herself. But only for every second week, & there are powerful consequences for not adhering to this single rule.

REVIEW: A deep, dark, clever exploration of fame today, where relevance is key, & some will go to any length to maintain it.

Personally, I've historically not been a Demi fan, but this has all changed with this (which I call a) seminal performance.

Captivating on every level, the simple imagery is intelligent, deep, well designed, & very powerful.

Truly well done.

I've also never been a pearl-clutcher, but in the first three quarters, (75% of the time at least), there I was; hand-over-heart, slack-jawed & mouth open, vacillating between sharp intakes of breath & long, & very conscious sloooooooooooow breaths out.

Would have been a 10 for me except for a very small lack of a detail or two, & I didn't quite feel so positively about the last few minutes.

Personally, it felt a touch unclear, unfinished, & a bit pretentious (you've already made your point Ma-am, & you killed it. Well done!!).

That said, almost a solid 9.5 for me.

reviews.author: penguin-65
reviews.body:
I saw The Substance when it was first in theaters. I put off writing a review at that time because it had elements that were insanely good and others that were insanely bad. I wanted to praise it for the good stuff without ignoring the rest.

Then I saw it getting nominated for awards and decided I needed to write that review.

First, calling it body horror is an epic understatement. This goes down as Existence Horror. Yes the two female leads are gorgeous and yes they spend a lot of time naked. But by the end you'll have no interest in seeing naked skin for quite some time. Similarly the way food is presented will put you off your dinner for a day or a week.

All of this is intentional and the Director gets big kudos for pulling it off mostly with innovative camera-work.

You know that scene in Clockwork Orange where Malcolm Macdowell is forced to watch videos as aversion therapy? This movie is like that except you're Malcolm and you're choosing to watch.

Now let's talk about the science of The Substance (not in a That Wouldn't Work sense but in a How Do You Want Us To Believe It Works sense). The opening scene uses a chicken egg to demonstrate. No voice. No music. Just a demo. And it's largely effective.

The movie is long (2:20) and fills it progressing characters slowly into using and understanding the nature of the Substance. Even so, a few things are never clarified. For example, we get that when the bodies split each gets full memories up to that point. From then on, it appears there's no mental link between them but it felt like there should be...or at least they should have left notes for each other. And why did the rejuvenated starlet decide to sign up for the same tedious cycle of stardom with the same boss?

With that movie length, each of the 3 acts gets plenty of time.

Act 1: fairly standard characters and difficulties leading to an aging starlet willing to try a back alley drug to regain her youth. Innovative presentation earns this act an 8.

Act 2: time swapping between the two versions, leading to inevitable conflict and a sense that one must prevail despite the ground rules requiring equity between the two. This act goes up to the moment an irrevocable decision is made. Everything about this part is top notch. A solid 10.

Act 3: an attempt to maximize body horror and come to some reasonable conclusion. This story goes completely off the rails with a live performance that would never happen and dialogue borrowed from any of several versions of Frankenstein. I'm scoring this act a 2. There is nothing good about it and I wish I had left after Act 2.

To be fair, the plot gyrations in the first 2 acts leave basically no story arc for act 3 that would be satisfying. However, I will close saying that those first 2 acts goodness far outweigh the stumble in act 3.

reviews.author: viagiator
reviews.body:
The Substance is a film that speaks through its visuals, delivering an experience that is as technical as it is emotional. From a cinematic standpoint, it's exquisite-beautifully shot, with strong directing and phenomenal sound design, music, and performances. The actors truly elevate the film, making it a standout work overall.

I'm not typically a fan of body horror or horror in general, but I wouldn't necessarily classify this movie strictly as a horror. While there are scenes that some might find disturbing, they feel more like the director's chosen language for storytelling. These moments are not gratuitous; they're purposeful and well-executed.

The narrative doesn't dwell on explaining every detail, like the origins of the mysterious organization behind the product or their motivations. That's not the point. The heart of the story lies in the struggle to accept oneself-particularly the process of aging. As someone who's recently been grappling with fears around growing older, this theme resonated deeply with me. For me, this emotional weight was the true "horror" of the film.

While many have labeled The Substance as a feminist film-and it absolutely embraces those themes-I found its messages to be universal. As a man, I connected with many of its ideas and emotions, which transcend gender. This is a film that speaks to anyone willing to listen.

The performances deserve special mention. Demi Moore is outstanding, especially in the scene where she attempts to go on a date-intense, vulnerable, and unforgettable. Dennis Quaid is equally brilliant, portraying his character with just the right amount of repulsiveness. Margaret Qualley also shines to her role.

If you're hesitant to watch this movie because of its horror elements, don't be. The Substance is so much more than that. And if you're drawn to it for the horror, you won't be disappointed either. It's a multifaceted work that deserves to be experienced, blending artistry and emotion into something truly memorable.

reviews.author: rgkarim
reviews.body:
LIKES:

The Artistic Message

The Unique Theme

Cinematography

The Sound Editing

The Makeup/Prosthetics

The Twists/Unpredictability

The Acting

The Horror At Times

SUMMARY My friend and fellow reviewers are correct in that the movie is certainly one of the more unique tails and takes on the Horror genre. Fargeat's writing loads the film with metaphorical content, all about the obsessions, vanity, and imbalance that humans have and the consequences that arise from it. Under his direction, the film is not afraid to show the hardships of life that come with the fickle approaches of fame and present a nightmare in manifesto form. Though we've had plenty of such tales, The Substance makes the material its own, taking familiar media and molding it into a unique story that is one of the more original films of the year. Powerful cinematography helps elevate that horror to new heights as it incorporates excessively long hallways of aggressive colors, dynamic movement that symbolizes the mind, and varying teases of shots that something is amiss. Even some of the aggressive changes were hit with the perfect sot that made my gut twist and bile rise in my throat. The effects are a gorgeous display of practical and computer meshing together to make the ugliness extraordinarily haunting, especially during the transition moments as the twists start to take the film to an aggressive level.

The horror aspect is certainly "elevated" in a manner that isn't traditional, relying more on sadistic material and unsettling body elements, all supported by a sound array that is much of the horror itself. A mind-bending, ear-splitting soundtrack accompanies cringeworthy, hyper-realistic sounds as bones crack, skin tears, and sinew is stretched. The twists and unpredictability help as well, sticking with the bizarre rules but pushing the boundaries with little apology to the audience. It's horrific, and the underlying messages only further amplify the things you are watching and the realization of what he means. And to seal everything up (so to speak), with performances that are quite stellar and some of the best I've seen in a very long time. Dennis Quaid is okay. He plays the extravagant role well, the magnified persona of an exec being satirically funny and purposefully over the top to hit the message hard. He plays that part well, but it's nothing blowing my mind. Qualley is a delight, bubbly and cheerful at one point, and then dives into the dark material the next. She is physically impressive for the role cast, but her acting skills show fantastic merit that is going to continue to bleed into a lot of roles if given the parts. Demi Moore is the star of this movie, though, and she has returned to the big screen with such style, authenticity, and compassion for the role it's like she is living the nightmare. Her screaming, her facial emotions, and the way she has to change so much in this movie are frighteningly spectacular and very worthy of recognition and awards. I loved her in this film, and she was a huge line that kept me reeled into the movie.

DISLIKES

The Artistic Approach At Times

The Pacing At Times Get Slow

Very Sexual To Pornographic Levels

Disturbing Content That Crosses A Line

About Thirty Minutes Of "Fluff"

SUMMARY And despite all the good of this movie, there are going to be things that I feel will not be as enjoyable as it is to a certain niche. Fargeat's artistic approach dives deep into the material, complex, bloated, and convoluted, leading to a semi-stagnant plot that feels like it will go nowhere for those who like a more linear plot. His vision is certainly a higher presentation, and the content that comes with it is going to turn many people away. The pacing got slow for me at points, material that is important but yet bloated, alongside material you might not be interested in, drew the movie out for me and made the movie a tad boring. Dark content as it is, I am not interested in a lot of sexual displays of the body that poke at the addiction to such content, but I felt it could make its point with a lot less aggression or at least fewer minutes dedicated to the visual. If that's up your alley and you love that heavy punch, this will do little to phase you, but for all his creativity, there could have been other avenues to explore. Past the hypersexuality, the material's darkness is already going to be more selective, but it really crosses lines near the end that are tough to watch. No spoilers, but The Substances effects are really disturbing and easily cross several lines that are excessive, ugly, and to many extent again unnecessary. Body Horror fans are going to swim in delight with the tricks at hand, which, combined with the impressive visuals, will make them grin a mile wide. However, a major warning to those with sensitivities is to avoid this movie and any pictures or clips if you can. Such excessive methods do little for me and again bloated the end that could have been trimmed away to help trim back the time limit. And for people like me, there was a lot of fluff that was not needed and, with a little curbing, could have elevated this movie to even greater heights.

The VERDICT: The Substance is a movie that is going to be the talk of the trade for a few weeks. It's a powerful visual essay on the frailty of the human ego and the horrifying elements presented are a powerful message on many levels. A powerful combination of visual and audio tricks alongside an original angle to present the material all work to make one of the scarier stories that I've seen in a while. Add in twists and a fantastic acting crew to unleash the full might of the character study in this dramatic entry. Yet, with such an artistic presentation comes a little more selective audience to enjoy it and I was not one of those who could not relish the entire movie. Fargeat's focus on hypersexuality, disturbing imagery that crosses lines I didn't want, and fluff that only drew out the film. Had the movie been about twenty to thirty minutes shorter, or if they substituted it with some other type of content would have gone very far to improve this movie. This is definitely going to check all the boxes for a lot of body horror enthusiasts who love such graphical prowess over a fully tight story. Is this worth a trip to the theater? If you are into this genre, yes, but otherwise a better use of time at home. Scoring this movie is tough, but factoring everything in, I'm giving The Substance:

Comedy/Drama/Horror: 8.0-8.5 Movie Overall: 7.0.

I'm still trying to wrap my head around The Substance! This sci-fi thriller is a thought-provoking, visually stunning masterpiece that will keep you guessing until the very end.

As someone who loves movies that challenge my mind, I was hooked from the opening scene. The cast delivers phenomenal performances, bringing depth and nuance to their characters. I found myself fully invested in their journey, questioning reality alongside them.

Rather than feeling engaged with the storyline or invested in the characters, I found myself increasingly uncomfortable and repelled as the movie progressed.

reviews.author: julieshotmail
reviews.body:
Demi Moore waited until her sixties to deliver a performance like this - a visually rich, darkly atmospheric exploration of ageism, sexism, and the struggle for self-acceptance. Opposite her, Margaret Qualley shines as the younger version of Moore's character, fierce and intense, holding her own with a rawness that cuts through the screen. Qualley's energy complements Moore's portrayal of a woman grappling with desperation and confusion, bringing depth to a story that feels part fever dream, part tribute to horror classics like "The Shining" and "Carrie."

This film isn't here to make perfect sense. It's science fiction in the truest sense, set in a surreal world where a reclusive aerobics star undergoes physical transformations beyond the limits of reality. Logic isn't the point here. It's about the visuals, the twisted artistry, and the unmistakable message hiding just beneath the bizarre. Let yourself be pulled into its world, let go of any need for answers, and immerse yourself. When you do, the film reveals itself, leaving you with the haunting satisfaction only true cinematic artistry can deliver.

At the same time i feel bad that i know nothing of any of these people yet am a big fun of creativity for sure am going to be looking out for them and for art work from the storyline to the acting to production both visual and audio, everything played out right.

I just hope and pray that one day i get an opportunity to share my script writing and story imaginations with such directors. I really enjoyed it...

reviews.author: sparrowbird529
reviews.body: Oh "The Substance" how I love you... kind of. The cinematography and social commentary in this film was actually very well done. reviews.author: aaliyahoneil
reviews.body:
The Substance, directed by Coralie Fargeat, is a chilling and thought-provoking sci-fi thriller that examines themes of vanity, identity, and the price of eternal youth. The story follows Elisabeth Sparkle (Demi Moore), a former Hollywood star who, desperate to regain her lost beauty, begins using a mysterious serum that promises to turn back time. However, as Elisabeth transforms into a younger version of herself (portrayed by Margaret Qualley), the consequences of tampering with nature begin to unravel in horrific ways. With strong performances, a unique premise, and effective tension, The Substance is an engaging and unsettling experience, though its final moments may leave some viewers disappointed.

Demi Moore delivers an exceptional performance as Elisabeth, portraying a woman consumed by vanity and fear of aging. Her portrayal captures the psychological and physical toll of her obsession, making the character's descent into madness both heartbreaking and terrifying. Margaret Qualley complements Moore's performance as the younger version of Elisabeth, adding a layer of eeriness to the transformation. The supporting cast, including Dennis Quaid, further solidifies the film's emotional weight, with their contributions enhancing the film's exploration of self-perception and inner turmoil.

Fargeat's direction is captivating, using a vivid colour palette and stunning cinematography to create a visually arresting world that contrasts beauty with grotesque consequences. The film's atmosphere is unsettling, with a sense of unease growing as Elisabeth's transformation takes hold. The body horror and psychological tension are amplified by the film's restrained pacing, allowing the horror to gradually unfold. The score, with its haunting melodies, complements the eerie atmosphere, keeping the audience on edge.

While The Substance builds an intriguing and terrifying narrative, its final 15 minutes detract from the film's otherwise strong execution. The resolution feels forced, rushed, and somewhat unsatisfying, undermining the emotional and thematic weight that had been carefully built up throughout the film. The conclusion takes a turn that doesn't quite match the tone of the rest of the story, leaving a sense of disappointment and diminishing the overall impact of the film.

In conclusion, The Substance is a film with strong performances, captivating direction, and a thought-provoking exploration of vanity and obsession. While the final act leaves something to be desired, the film's unsettling atmosphere, unique premise, and emotional depth make it a standout in the genre. Fans of psychological horror and body horror will find much to appreciate in The Substance, even if the ending doesn't quite live up to its potential.

reviews.author: martymladenov
reviews.body:
The Substance is a rare, thought-provoking horror film that transcends cheap scares to deliver a deeply unsettling exploration of beauty, aging, and society's obsession with perfection. Demi Moore is extraordinary, giving a hauntingly vulnerable performance that anchors the story with raw emotion and complexity.

The film's themes are woven seamlessly into every aspect of its chilling narrative, inviting viewers to question their own values and fears. The score is unforgettable-both haunting and unforgettable, it elevates every scene. And the cinematography is stunning, with each frame meticulously crafted to balance beauty and dread.

What truly sets The Substance apart is its depth. On a second viewing, hidden details and subtle foreshadowing reveal the filmmakers' incredible attention to detail. The ending, while polarizing, is perfectly suited to the film's themes-bold, thought-provoking, and designed to linger in your mind (even tho many people don't like it, I think it was the perfect choice).

One of the best horror movies in recent years, The Substance proves you don't need cheap jumpscares to terrify. It's a masterclass in atmosphere, storytelling, and emotional resonance.

reviews.author: akshatmahajan
reviews.body:
The Substance is a body horror drama with a theme of accepting yourself as you are. It also shows the reality if Hollywood and effect of fame on an individual and theme of greed and how much a person can fall into it until he/ she bears it's consequences.

The story was good and nicely executed, the screenplay was also good but it was slowly paced and it could have been shortened by 10-15 minutes, the direction was good and the performances were brilliant, they were the real soul of this story.

reviews.author: ssimonsays-95190
reviews.body: There has been quite a while since I saw such a textbook example movie. "Old school", so to say. The excellent Ms. Fargeat used and masterfully directed all elements of the specific movie language (as taught in schools/at the academy/college) - symbols, frames, shots, music, colors, light, hints, details, angles, lenses, focus, closeups, music, edits and so on, and masterfully so. She also told the story perfectly - it has a beginning and and an end, is rounded and whole. Casting and their performances are impeccable. Special effects are done and used perfectly and timely, with measure, emphasizing te points of the story. Ms. Fargeat deserves an Academy award, as an acknowledgement that the artistic creativity perfectly combines with the learned movie "tools", when done right. Regarding the story, it's a classic vanity tale, taken to the extreme as a caricature. Nothing special in essence, but outstandingly special in delivery. I truly enjoyed watching this. Yes, there are some minor flaws (some connecting parts missing), but that's why 9 stars instead of 10. Still, this movie is, as an art of visual telling a story, fantastic. Incomparably better than 99% of trash out there. However, its quality will recognize only people with a certain amount of film knowledge and education, but probably not wider (average and below) audience. For the latter, an advice: watch and learn (to appreciate). I strongly recommend using this movie as a didactic and educational material in art schools and colleges.

reviews.author: gonzothedog
reviews.body: What I liked was how the movie was able to portray the pain in how a beautiful woman feels as she ages and starts to lose the attention of others and no longer looks as beautiful as she once did and how devastating that feels - at the same time poking fun of people's vanity and obsession with youth and beauty. I didn't find the story interesting or enjoyable to watch in any way other than in regard to the positive points noted.

reviews.author: andreasgarbossasmk
reviews.body:
The Substance is a rare gem that unapologetically takes you by the throat and doesn't let go. Its ambition is evident in every frame, drawing from the psychological horror of Shining, the visceral body horror of Cronenberg, the tragic intensity of Carrie, and the stylized descent of Requiem for a Dream. Its visual language echoes the raw, industrial madness of Tetsuo, yet it's infused with a late '90s aesthetic-hauntingly nostalgic, painfully fashionable, and dripping with a disquieting beauty.

Anchored by two spectacular leads, The Substance explores the toxic rivalry of its central figures, who battle not just for dominance, but for an elusive, almost mythical concept of beauty and youth. In this horror-tinged narrative, the power struggle leaves no winner; the ideals they pursued crumble into nothingness, a devastating reminder of the fleeting nature of perfection and success.

The film's careful exploration of food as both alluring and repulsive is nothing short of masterful. Scenes play with food as an object of desire and disgust, weaving it into the twisted ideals of beauty and control. This interplay-where beauty alternates with grotesque depictions of consumption-adds a visceral layer to the characters' obsessive pursuit, one that's both sensory and stomach-churning.

Each shot is meticulously crafted, edited to perfection, and scored with anxiety-inducing intensity, pulling the viewer deeper into its lurid, grotesque spiral. The result is a masterpiece of discomfort, a horror experience that is as chilling as it is aesthetically revolutionary for its genre.

reviews.author: gutsmcd-42398
reviews.body:
I hope nobody would ever recommend this sort of movie to me, because this is not the sort of entertainment I normally choose to immerse myself in.

That said, everyone's different, so I try and rate a movie based on the sort of movie it is and the type of audience it attracts.

So while this was not my 'cup of tea' (to put it very mildly)... for the people who like this sort of thing, it's definitely a perfect 10.

It's a HORRIFICALLY disturbing psychological beating that somehow keeps getting more deeply and darkly sick.

It's been over 2 decades since a movie messed with my head so much that I was still thinking about it 2 days later, even though I didn't want to. It just stuck with me, no matter how hard I tried to shake it off.

This movie is utterly ubsurd in that what happens in it, could never happen in real life, but if it could happen, it would be a nightmare for most of us.

It made me terrified because it's an extreme version of what we all do, I think. We overinduldge, to our own detriment, as though our present self and future self are two different beings. But this movie speaks to many other points too. And it's so real in how people often don't think things through carefully, only to later realise - when it's faaaar too late - that they paid too high a price for something that wasn't worth that much, because that thing they sacrificed a great deal for was relatively momentary and perhaps superficial.

So I would recommend this movie to people who don't mind being visually or psychologically disturbed (and maybe even welcome it), and also appreciate the horrifically ugly depths to which a character (who represents all of us, I think) can fall when they don't realise they're falling.

I hope I haven't given anything away that you might not already guess at, but just be prepared that if you go into this movie thinking it'll be like a fun little car trip... then yes, it will be like a car trip, but through a seemingly never-ending hellish landscape, and the car will have no breaks, and it will be driven by a madman.

It painted the darkest side of the world... a world without hope for many of us if we're ever allowed the chance to go too far.

reviews.author: missaymoo92
reviews.body:
I love movies that are smart and have something to say, especially when they're stylish too. Really appreciated a lot of the camera angles and tricks throughout the movie, very clever cinematography, set designs, and costumes. Obviously the acting was incredible. It's Demi Moore, say less! Margaret Qualley was also great and I'd like to see her in more films.

As a woman, I related to so many things in this movie. The remarks and behavior of the men, especially when in front of a "pretty young thing", and also from the women's' perspective. Sometimes, it's just nice to see a movie portray feelings and emotions that can be hard to put into words.

The movie reminded me of a mix of "Neon Demon" and the original "Evil Dead". Probably not for everyone, but it was right up my alley.

Buckle up, this movie is a WILD ride.

reviews.author: hgrseattle
reviews.body: Ok, first I should start with the fact that I created an IMDB account just to review this movie. The most incredible depiction of self loathing, mother-daughter symbolism, Hollywood beauty standards, and new age feminism I have seen from a movie. Kind of like the Barbie movie but wayyyy darker and much more developed. Casting: absolute perfection, Demi Moore and Margaret Qualley made my jaw drop so many times in this film from how they play the characters of Elisabeth and Sue. The raw emotions portrayed by both made this film. Dennis Quaid was amazing too, whenever I hate a character with my entire soul it means the actor is doing amazing. Cinematography wise, the vision and execution was incredible. Everything in this movie is exactly how it's supposed to be, there isn't a line or scene or frame that is unnecessary. Every bit of the story is meticulously placed to be absolutely crucial in understanding the characters, themes, and symbolism. The editing of quick jumps combined with riveting sound design was perfection. Even the most mundane scenes were full of tension, and somehow watching TV and eating became disgusting and almost unwatchable in the most delightful way ever. I see a lot of people hating on the ending of this movie, and yes it is very much over the top but it's overdramatized in a way that adds so much beauty and symbolism to the story. Honestly the end almost made me cry, it was so sad and disgusting and I loved every single second of it. An absolute masterpiece. Absolutely gross and beautiful. Definitely not for the squeamish, I almost had to look away many times, from body parts falling off to items emerging from unexpected places in the human body, it WILL make you want to rip your skin off, but isn't that exactly the point? Respect the balance.

reviews.author: breenchris-98493
reviews.body:
I went to see The Substance partly on the strength of it getting 8/10 on IMDB, which couldn't have been more misleading. Ratings here are usually somewhere in the ball park, but maybe boosters and bots have taken over...ratings do seem artificially high when movies first come out.

The Substance, is a B Grade movie with a big budget (or Z grade, B doesn't fully capture it). It's supposedly taking on Hollywood, sexism, aging and the beauty industry, but has very long scenes entirely focused on women's body parts. It has tacky blood and gore, lots of rubber suits, and plot holes you could drive a truck through. I've read some reviews that say the film is supposed to be satire, or ironic, but it's just shallow.

The ending scenes combined with the way the rest of it is filmed perhaps implies the film maker thinks the audience is complicit, but this rubbish is a product of the director, not the audience.

This would have to be one of the worst movies I've ever seen. Dont watch it to see if you agree with me, don't bother wasting your time.

reviews.author: rikkisushaun
reviews.body:
This is old school body horror done in 2024 and it is EVERYTHING!! I'm almost 40 years of age and this may possibly be the BEST film I have seen in my entire life! It is so over the top, wild, funny, truthful, scary, and just plain freaking weird!!

This is be an entire story ark on "Dr. Who" or some other out of the box sci-fi concept show. But the way I see it sci-fi for the next 30 years are going to be stealing concepts from this film.

This is an instant cult classic. It's a modern tale of the cost of not loving yourself, all of yourself, for what you are. I will NEVER forget watching this in theaters. #chefkiss #soweird.

reviews.author: allyharvey
reviews.body:
Ok. So... I cried at the end of the movie. Not from sadness or horror, but from laughing so hard. The overall movie is supposed to be a drama? Right. 😂 Both Demi and Margaret Qualley are beautiful and amazing and neither are ashamed to be naked on screen.

I would consider about 80% of the movie to be drama. Definitely symbolic of the media and the pursuit of perfection. The movie had more than one place to end if it was meant to remain a drama. HOWEVER, things took a turn and the blood, oh my, the blood. Evil Dead or Kill Bill spurting style blood. And a boob the falls on the ground. Hilarity ensues. The very end was like starfish crawling to water.

reviews.author: freend-63197
reviews.body:
The Substance starts off like a typical B movie that might be shown at a fantasy film festival. To the point, without wasting too much time for the protagonist to doubt whether injecting a dubious substance in her body might be a good idea or not. That time is spent better by actually showing why Demi Moore's character wants to be youg again. So far, so good. It could have been a solid 8/10 star movie at this point.

Unfortunately, the movie does not really explain what is the advantage for the old self to give her lifetime to a younger self (which is a completely separate person that only shares her DNA), nor does it explain why they do not even attempt to communicate with each other. It still could have been a fun 6/10 movie.

But then it also made the turn to getting ridiculous, and trying to be as gross as possible (probably in the hope of achieving cult status). While it sort of succeeded at that, we all wondered why we kept watching. Not because we could not stomach it - it was more ridiculous than gross - but because it seemed so pointless.

The movie still gets a second star for the idea, and the beginning.

reviews.author: inspektorr
reviews.body: Substance is an unusual movie. It starts off very calm and even the first few hints of what's to come are so restrained that by the final act you're left wondering "why is this rated as a horror". But then the director lets loose and you're bombarded with grotesque scenes to the point of absurdity. But look past that and Substance pokes at many, many toxic beauty standards that we demand from others and ourselves. Meat. Fresh, young meat. That's what the audience wants! There are many innuendos at how Hollywood really works, how women are treated and how far some go to satisfy the market demand. You just can't look away. It's not a film you'll forget any time soon, that much is certain by the time the end credits roll.

reviews.author: sorearm
reviews.body:
Imagine a scene from a famous film e.g. The Godfather where Michael Corleone confronts Carlo about betraying his family. Now reimagine that scene but everyone gets a close up of their backside. That's The Substance.

When I left the cinema I was laughing about how bad the film was but over the next few days it filtered into my thoughts (usually a good sign) and it was still making me laugh. I don't think it was intended to be this funny because the exploitation far outweighed the metaphor and what you are left with is a children's sweets-coloured wet dream.

The Substance will definitely be in the collection of those who think Lifeforce (1985) is a good film.

reviews.author: Dupps
reviews.body:

A movie where we see this exposed as a social mirror, like this movie did for women, would (could) be so revolutionary and relatable for most men of our modern era.

It was seriously like the steep climb up the craziest roller coaster you've ever been on.. and then the most hardcore, awesome drop to the rest of the ride lol It not only was insane.. but it was so geniusly done..the storyline was very relatable had me in my feelins.. Idk how many times I said "omg, holy sh#t, no wayyyyy" haha Definitely surprised me.. I put it on to try and fall asleep..l needless to say, the complete opposite happened.

reviews.author: torrentfreak-10628
reviews.body:
This movie is amazing from the beginning to the very end. Never for a moment it feels boring. It has everything from horror to suspense to a shocking ending. Performances by Margaret Qualley and Demi Moore are Oscar worthy. I never knew they were such great actresses.

I also really appreciate the screenplay and cinematography for this film. The new and I dare say eccentric storyline that this film offers is like a refreshment from the repeated plots of horror and drama movies seen nowadays. Some people won't like the ending but I liked it as it shows there are always consequences to your actions.

If you are looking for something unique and interesting that blows your mind , this movie is for you.

reviews.author: hvwnqdp
reviews.body:
This movie is not overhyped one bit, it deserves all the praise and good reviews, I don't understand how people have voted it negatively.

The storyline is very interesting and the cast are outstanding. Demi Moore & Margaret Qualley both shine through their roles. This movie made me feel so many different emotions from start to finish, from sad to happy and everything in between.

I don't understand why this doesn't have higher reviews, it has been WAYY too long since a good horror film has graced our screens.

(The substance reminded me of requiem for a dream at times, is that the same with anyone else?)

reviews.author: eshghster
reviews.body: I thought I give this movie a chance since the previews seem like a predictable movie about our sad modern day cultural assumption about beauty and youth. But, no. This movie is not as boring as known Hollywood trash movies, it is actually worst than that. With gallons and gallons of blood, dumb unnecessary violence, stupid prop, unbelievable characters, the plot that just did not made sense... I don't really know where to begin. The story had so many holes in it from the beginning, it was just comical. I had to control myself when I started LOLing when the story turned from bad to worse in the theater. I just can't believe how bad this movie was made. Gosh. What a waste of time.

reviews.author: cwigtil-75624
reviews.body:
Demi Moore & Margaret Qualley do amazing jobs in their roles, and Quaid chews the scenery well as Moore's & Qualley's agent. The body horror is high but tolerable for the first 3/4 of the runtime, and the premise is very logical and flows from conceit to that 3/4 point very well. The direction, blocking, and understatement reel you in in a way I haven't seen in a movie in a very long time. Moore's performance deserves awards and Qualley will certainly have made a name for herself with this role. Overall, even when it's flawed, it's still well-crafted, blocked, acted, and has a style all its own. I was also fine with the voice on the phone basically serving as the screenwriter as the voice of God, explaining the rules of the main conceit to the main characters.

Now to the downside: at almost two and a half hours, you can tell that the director wanted to end on a bang, and couldn't decide how to do it. The movie definitively goes "off the rails" and the conceit that you have to go with at the beginning suddenly mutates into a literal albatross. Still, this is the necessary risk of an indie movie which breaks through-the impressive vision which makes it possible doesn't get the studio spending the money for reshoots for a better ending. Even if flawed (I counted 8 different endings), it's a movie you should still see.

reviews.author: 8bithummingbird
reviews.body:
Imagine Alphaville's "Forever Young" playing softly in the background, while you revel in the fantasy of reclaiming your youth and beauty. This film delivers a sharp critique, flipping the bird to the relentless promotion of self-improvement mantras like "Be the best version of yourself" or the mythical "youth elixir."

Armed with dark humor, the director pushes boundaries, mocking society's obsession with beauty and youth. Why are we so terrified of aging? We all have different answers, but at the end of the day, who really wants to rot away, right?

I wasn't expecting such an extreme take, but it was definitely worth the watch. If you're in the mood for body horror laced with biting wit, this film is a must-see-don't miss it!

reviews.author: kalebckaiser
reviews.body: I absolutely loved this film. I went into it expecting a strange experience and came out with one of the best film experiences I've ever had. Filmmakers like Coralie Fargeat are the reason I love this medium- the ones who are transparent about their inspirations but inject a certain "substance" of their own and change the way we experience cinema. Obviously, this film isn't going to be for everyone. It's absolutely disgusting. It's body-horror with a heart. Though, I feel this film may be many individuals first and best experience with the body-horror genre. Demi Moore delivers, perhaps, the greatest performance of her career as Elizabeth Sparkles. The Substance is bold, beautiful, ugly, disturbing, meaningful, funny, sad and important. This film made me want to be a little kinder to myself and give who I've become a little more love.

reviews.author: ceresmongrel
reviews.body:
I LOVED this film. I loved it for how it told this story, but for me it was based in reality, which for me is scarier since I don't believe in the supernatural so it doesn't scare me. It also wasn't holding anything back. Some scenes were so over the top, but what if it wasn't real? What if it was a hallucination? But I really enjoyed seeing that on the screen. They obviously had a fun time making this film.

And I cringed sooo hard at some of the scenes, they were acted so well. I was really impressed with this film! The only unbelievable thing I thought was that Demi Moore's character is ever thought of as someone who isn't beautiful. She just needed self-confidence!!

reviews.author: david_hollyfield
reviews.body:
A Cronenbergesque body horror about ideals of feminine beauty and ageing. Demi Moore's performance is a tour de force as an ageing star and I'll say no more to avoid spoilers. She deserves her Golden Globe award and should be up for an Oscar.

Forty years working in Hollywood and this is her first award for anything so I guess some would have thought she was a lightweight and she has done a few awful films but this is definitely not one.

Cronenberg's influence is all over this movie but that is a definite plus. It's great to see a horror film with subtext instead of all the empty dross around.

reviews.author: indyverstraete
reviews.body: I was sucked into this movie from beginning to end, it had me with the simple sweet premise and beautiful visually artistic shots. This movie is amazingly crafted. Every question the viewer has does get answered in full 4k. We see every gore scene in fascinating detail and feel the true body horrors through the amazing acting. Nothing is left to the imagination. This rabbittunnel of a movie sucks you in and makes the long runtime feel like a whiplash of an expierince. You will be left with the question "WTF just happened???" Because when you think it can't get any crazier it wil and it wil get BONKERS. My favorite movie of 2024.

reviews.author: mythbangla

This is one the best and disgusted movie i've ever seen in my life.

"Substance" is a captivating film that dives deep into the complexities of human nature and addiction. reviews.author: dromasca
reviews.body:
David Cronenberg and Quentin Tarantino have a heir and her name is Coralie Fargeat. Coralie Fargeat is not afraid to shock. In fact, I think the purpose of her films is to shock. She's doing it to get attention and maybe to attract an audience that wouldn't otherwise come to her movies, but it's just a tactic to gain more people watch for the message. And the message is shouted with the shrillness of 'horror'. 'The Substance' (2024) is her second film. The debut film made seven years ago, 'Revenge', managed to catch my attention in a genre that most of the time leaves me indifferent. With 'The Substance', Coralie Fargeat amplifies her means of expression. Apparently we are dealing with a film that combines the genres of horror and science fiction. For many viewers, that's all and enough. But 'The Substance' is much more than that. It is a film with a strong feminist message and is a scathing critique of misogynistic and ageist television entertainment. Everything is dressed up in the form of a movie with an 80s aesthetic, quoting and paying homage to the 'class B' movies of that decade. Viewers who can't stand violent films will do well to avoid viewing it, as it includes many scenes bathed in blood and a massive dose of 'body horror'.

Elisabeth, the main heroine of the film, is a former movie star with a star on Hollywood Blvd., whose youth and prime have passed. At 50, she has a fitness show on morning television, which is canceled because the producer (who happens to be named Harvey) wants a younger screen presence. Desperate because age is catching up with her, she cannot resist the temptation to respond to an ad promising a revolutionary genetic treatment, a kind of self-cloning into a younger version constructed from her own DNA. The procedure has restrictions and conditions that must be strictly followed. Everything that can go wrong will go wrong.

This movie could have ended about half an hour earlier than the 2 hours and 20 minutes running time. Many of the commenters have noted this, but in this case I think it's not just about conforming to a Hollywood trend, which I don't really like, by the way. It is precisely the last part that seems to me to have been most important to director Coralie Fargeat (who also wrote the screenplay). The sensation-seeking audience that gathers towards the end to see a New Year's show are us, the ones who have resisted the screening of the film in the cinema theatre or at our homes until then. We are hearing the desperate scream of the creature who was once a glorified star and then a woman who, in the eyes of the misogynistic society around her, was losing value as she inevitably advanced in age. As for the visual effects, I think the choice of makeup and prosthetics that could have been done in the 80s is intentional. In fact, the whole concept and cinematography are a tribute to the action, horror and sci-fi films of 35-40 years ago, but with a very different message, perhaps even contrary to the mentalities of that time. Although she has only made two feature films so far, it can be said that the director has created a recognizable visual style of her own, constructing sophisticated architectures for the buildings where the action takes place, where the modernity of the exteriors is combined with corridors that shrink the action in crushing perspectives. Some scenes quote the films that influenced her ('class B' films, but also Kubrick from 'Space Odyssey' or 'Shining' for example). More than once the director quotes herself, meaning scenes or details from 'Revenge'. Demi Moore plays with commitment and courage a role that she knows can bring her an Oscar or destroy the rest of her career. Dennis Quaid is also excellent as the obnoxious producer Harvey, who offers a counterpoint of sarcastic satire. There is, by the way, quite a lot of humor in this film, but the atmosphere is dominated by screaming and despair. 'The Substance' will become, I believe, a cult film, but there will always be a need for viewers to be warned about what they are about to see. For Coralie Fargeat, this is the second achievement in a career that promises to be formidable.

reviews.author: barrybush
reviews.body:
I saw an ad on instagram about this movie. I really don't buy into anything that advertises on any of the social media platforms, but something about Demi Moore in a movie about growing old and wanting to be youthful struck me as ironic in the best way. The three stars - Demi, Dennis Quaid, and. Margaret Qualley - all deliver stellar, if not campy, performances.

If you like David Lynch with a hint of pre-Lord of the Rings Peter Jackson, then you will find this film as entertaining as I did. The overt TV/Film commentary, music, and special effects work to make this film stand out as one of the strangest movies of the decade. The difference here is that it has the quality of a high Hollywood film, but could stand with the best of Troma films. I only wish that there were people in my personal network that I know would enjoy this movie. Kudos to writer & director, Coralie Fargeat, and her special effects team.
