reviews.author: FHTL0
reviews.body:
The worst shi I've seen in my life no story and it's all nude stuff that's why the rating is 8. Movie Review: "The Substance" - A Shallow Attempt at Horror That Fails on Every Level

Rating: 2/10

In the vast ocean of horror films, there are those that rise above to become cult classics, those that are forgettable but fun, and then there are the ones like The Substance-a movie so devoid of meaningful content that it becomes difficult to classify as horror at all. Released with much hype but delivering little more than a string of cheap thrills, The Substance is a film that quickly reveals its true aim: to distract its audience with gratuitous nudity, while offering nothing in terms of plot, character development, or genuine horror.

A Thin, Barely-There Plot The biggest flaw of The Substance lies in its lack of story. It's almost comical how little effort was put into creating a coherent plot. The movie revolves around a mysterious drug that supposedly unleashes a primal force within those who consume it, but even this vague premise is barely explored. Instead of delving into the potential terror or psychological aspects of addiction or loss of control, the film jumps from one meaningless scene to the next, offering little in the way of narrative continuity.

The film opens with a group of friends, none of whom are given any backstory or depth, deciding to experiment with the titular "substance." We never learn why they are interested in it, where it came from, or what it does beyond inducing strange and violent behavior. And that's pretty much the whole movie-people taking the drug and then either stripping down for no apparent reason or engaging in random, violent outbursts. There is no buildup, no climax, and certainly no resolution. It feels like a film cobbled together with a few disconnected ideas that never form a cohesive whole.

reviews.author: jakebunker
reviews.body: Yeah that's how I would describe this movie. Now keep in mind my subjective rating would be probably be more around 5 but I have to acknowledge that what the movie set out for it accomplished very very well. There were a lot of moments that I felt like wanting to throw up or turn my eyes away. It was just not appealing to me and I don't want to relive this experience again. This movie was a bit different in that while I'm happy never going back to it the crew behind it did their parts well enough. And while it's not exactly my cup of tea I will acknowledge that there were a couple extraordinary aspects to the film. The sound design and mixing was so grotesque matching the tone. The cinematography felt new but in a way that was still well shot and acceptable for the purposes of the movie. The acting was pretty good, especially Dennis Quaid as the manager. The effects department did a pretty good job on most things. The pacing was good up until the Substance started being used then it started to drag a bit. I scrunched my face at so many moments in this movie which was definitely the point. I think a lot of horror is pretty stupid but this was better than most because it wasn't trying to scare the audience per se, just get a disgusted reaction. I won't be watching this movie again but props to the team for accomplishing what they set out to do very well. The director had a pretty good vision for it and isn't ashamed what others think of it, as you can tell by the divisive reviews. Watch it if you want something fresh and different otherwise I'd recommend staying away from this one.

reviews.author: calummacleod-51310
reviews.body:
It's hard to know where to start with The Substance. Demi Moore plays Elisabeth, an ageing television fitness personality who finds her lucky rabbits foot in the form of a 'substance' that promises a transformation that will create a younger version of herself.

The complex rules surrounding the administering of said substance includes the idea that both young and old versions of the subject are allowed more than one week of freedom before they have to allow the other to come back out in public.

This is a film that gives a poignant message about the absurdity and fickle nature of celebrity. As Elisabeth sees her celebrity fade, her younger version, Sue (played with a mysterious and slightly unhinging nature by Margaret Qualley), sees her fame soar. As time goes on Sue wants even more limelight and this starts to affect how Elisabeth's physicality starts to mutate.

The Substance is grotesque, and brings the horror element to the fore as things spiral out of control. Dennis Quaid puts in a disgusting turn as the TV mogul obsessed with nothing more than to make money from his stars but this film belongs to Qualley and Moore, with the latter never being better and an Oscar nod surely on the way.

If you find gore uncomfortable in a film where anything goes, then maybe this is not for you but there is a deeper message to this that should not go unnoticed and for that reason The Substance is a very different type of horror than the mainstream.

reviews.author: hanneloreprinsen
reviews.body:
The very start of the movie had some cool shots, and that is the only good thing I can say about it.

The premise was weak to begin with. I feel like the pressure for women to keep up their looks as they age is mainly a first-world, mostly celebrity problem. I don't understand what modern woman can truly connect with this main character. I certainly cannot. Being in her shoes would be a dream.

The movie aims to shock, that much is clear. And I guess it does, judging from the press. I've seen plenty of body horror and I don't see anything new here.

Overall it feels pretentious, loud, obnoxious and tone deaf. I don't see the hype.

reviews.author: mullen1979
reviews.body:
Demi Moore is absolutely incredible in this movie.

I can say the same for the rest of the cast.

But I personally feel this should be the moment that Demi Moore gets Oscar recognition.

I grew up with her. She's one of the greats who fortunately was fated to collaborate with Coralie Fargeat (the films director and writer) in THE SUBSTANCE.

The film revolves around the idea of challenging one side of our consciousness to another.

The film feels like one big dream sequence. So enriched with vibrant color pallets. It makes it so easy to suspend disbelief. It's a surreal experience.

It's best seem in theatres because the color and sound is that much more intense.

I could go on about the movies concept and brilliance but I'm sure mosre most people get it. It's a ll a very symbiotic experience.

The pacing is amazing. It don't feel as long as it is.

Best film of the year for me.

This is is real cinema.

reviews.author: mrbeyondermcu
reviews.body: What did I just watch?! This film is a brilliant masterpiece of horror, blending psychological terror with grotesque body horror in ways I've rarely seen. As a die-hard horror fan who's watched films from the 20th century to modern-day, this one hit differently. It's a haunting reminder to love yourself and not care about others' opinions of your appearance. Salute to the writer/director-what he's crafted is remarkable, the best horror I've seen in years. My only gripe? I wanted more aftermath of the chaos and deeper exploration of the organization behind the substance. I would love to see a sequel.

reviews.author: jlani2
reviews.body: I didn't see the previews because it always gives away the whole movie and ruins the experience. I heard from people that it's a good movie starring Demi and have been a long time fan but this was not her best movie. So much nudity and unnecessary scenes that could've been done better. Yeah I get that "Bare-all" sells but this is so over the top and took away my experience in staying to finish the movie. We should have left an hour into the movie but wanted to see if it would get better. We ended up leaving when it showed a B- horror scene towards the end. Leave the nudity to streaming services.

reviews.author: malmevik77
reviews.body:
The Substance

The darkest comedy I've ever seen depicting a woman's need to restore her youth, The Substance is a science fiction story on how that youth can be restored literally.

This is not a unique story. Men are depicted as disgusting as they age without repercussions, but women become pariahs for daring to age. The film uses close up visuals and loud disgusting sound effects to heighten the viewer's senses of reality. We get it, men are disgusting. But with more subtlety, we see the same of women who use desperation to justify their actions.

However, the lengths Demi Moore's character Elisabeth Sparkle go to resuscitate her youthful career, with a new name Sue, are beyond funny. The grotesque method to switch between her ages comes across as hilarious but sad at the same time.

Elisabeth, while still in control of her body, tries to reassure herself that she matters even over 50, but can't accept that men could still find her beautiful. Men are disgusting, but she still craves their attention. Sue, when in control, revels in the attention, and starts to rob Elisabeth of her life. The body switching is where the sci-fi comes into play.

I won't spoil the full story, but my goodness does this film become gory and horrific. It goes on a bit too long, but the amount of laughter coming out of me increased exponentially as the film progresses.

Be aware that there is a lot of nudity in this movie, mostly female. And the sounds recorded might trigger those with sensitivity to certain noises. It didn't bother me, but an audience member left the theatre to empty the contents of their stomach.

The film also assumes that we have no memory because every time we had to remember something from earlier in the plot, we see a flashback. I get it, there were some "twists" but I'm not an idiot, and I saw them coming.

I loved this film otherwise. It's so ridiculous, and unbelievable, but I could not stop laughing. I want to even see it again to see if I missed anything told through nuance. Plus there are some hot men during the work out videos with Sue. I'm shallow. Men are disgusting. But I'm proud of it haha.

reviews.author: DollfaceSword
reviews.body:
I really enjoyed this even though I didn't understand certain parts or decisions Elizabeth Sparkle made. The premise of this movie is that men that run tv and movies will go only so far with actresses until they turn 50 in which they will be replaced with a younger model. I mean, this happens in marriages. It's not just the beauty industry or the exercise industry, or Hollywood, this is the real battle women face as we age, unless you get to that Nirvana state where you don't care and then you're really free and wearing a gold crown for real and achieved Queen status.

Personally I'm not there yet. My mother is who is my hero so I will probably get there one day.

Demi Moore is absolutely fantastic in this and deserves all the praise and accolades she receives, I'm so glad she's had this comeback because I've always liked her as an actress. She's not given the respect because of her looks but now I think that's finally changed and everyone sees how good she is.

There's a lot of nods to other horror films in this like the carpet in the studio she works at is the same as the Overlook in The Shining. Stuff like that adds some fun to it. I thought this was a creative movie and that's nice because most everything that comes out now is remakes and copies of other films from the past. This takes from some things but it's also so wild in other ways that's just, I don't know, it's really good. You just have to see it cos it's really hard to explain. It's impossible to explain really. I loved the ending even thought I see some say they didn't, they just didn't get the vibe. If you get it you get it.

reviews.author: mxbrecher
reviews.body: Coralie Fargeat's first film "Revenge" already solidified her to be a a phenomenal director and writer on the rise. Now this being her second film, "The Substance" is by far her best work. Coralie is an absolute masterpiece in class of professional development, dedication to developing one of the GREATEST films ever made, specifically for the Body Horror genre as the creator. The Substance really blew me away with the insanely stunning cinematography, to the color palette, and let's not forget a career defining achievement of a performance that is so beautiful, raw and daring yet very admirable from Demi Moore for her role as Elizabeth Sparkle. Not many female actors at her age wouldn't do such a daring role but she did it! Margaret Qualley is incredible playing her other self as Sue and also Dennis Quaid was the perfect example of how horrible men can be in the business and with power, very well done! Just everything about this film is incredible beyond words. The ending gets bonkers for those who haven't seen it, go in NOT READING ANYTHING but the IMDB plot that's it, best way to experience it. It's a message of what women or people, the violence or situations we can do to our selves and how men perceive women or any star. Just FYI The Substance is now the first horror film to make such an impact in years being the first horror film ever to be nominated for the Golden Globes and for 5 Categories and Demi Moore wining Best Actress for a Comedy/Musial, because it's a Dark Comedy, Body Horror, Si-Fi, Psychological Horror film! MUST SEE! My favorite film of 2024.

reviews.author: alexsvk
reviews.body: I was so happy with story and thought behind that. The whole idea behind it was good, finally a different presentation of horror. I was happy to finally watch a good movie. According to the reviews, it should have been great. I don't know but did we see the same movie? This was a disgusting disaster..all wrong. I didnt saw a movie with that bad ending. I don't know why the screenwriter thought that this would be a suitable ending to the film, but she completely destroyed the potential that the film had. It ended up being a completely different genre than one expected. I don't understand how this can get any positive rating and not some award. Total nonsense. I was disgust but not in a good way. I've seen an incredible amount of movies in my entire life, but I've only written about 3 reviews for them, and I'm sad that I spent my time on this movie and at the same time writing this review. Well, I have never been so disgusted and disappointed by a movie. I will recommend this movie to my worst enemies. 1/10 movie just for the begining and idea.

reviews.author: iamliamiam
reviews.body:
A truly epic cinematic experience that touches your soul before ripping it out with a gusto that is thorough unapologetic and torn through every available orifice. This is a film that seems superficial and playful upon first inspection, yet on closer review it is deeply symbolic and wrestles with many topics at once.

The Substance is sculpted to excite every sense; music challenges you, graphics assault you and cinematography disturbs you as much as the narrative and delivery of the actors. Nothing is left to chance.

It's wonderfully graphic and a horrifically watchable, darkly comedic feast.

reviews.author: siderite
reviews.body:
Satire is served best in small portions. Or at least in subtle ones. In this film, the plot is obvious from the beginning, maybe even before that, since it's being revealed in every trailer, as well as its aftermath. So what's left? To have a marvelous implementation of the concept.

The Substance mostly delivers, with great visuals, poignant design and shots and some absolutely brilliant scenes: from the Quaid's disgusting character to the almost pornographic "pump it up" aerobics. It also ain't afraid to show both Demi Moore and Margaret Qualley naked, and they both look amazing for their ages. The acting is very good, too. But then things start to falter a little.

As an engineer I always find it funny when the customer fails and/or refuses to follow instructions, then panics when things go wrong, but in this case, with so much to lose, the main character(s) just make the worse possible choices, goaded by the Apple design of their drug supplier. If anything, that should really make you pay attention, but I digress. And it still kind of works, only the last 25 minutes bring nothing to the story other than body horror and gore. You already know what's happening and how it's going to end, so you feel like wasting time. And then there is the ending, that fountain of blood thing and the final scene, which just eliminate any reasonable suspension of disbelief. It's almost like it's there for comic relief.

Bottom line: a simple story, with brilliant visuals and acting, but overdrawn and exaggerated to the point where the satire loses its grip and gives way to nastiness.

reviews.author: kindofplace
reviews.body:
This was ten times the movie I expected. I'm not a horror or gore fan, but in an era when social commentary is branded as "woke" by those who tend not to pick up on it, I'll lend my ears to a filmmaker with something to say through horror.

"The Substance" doesn't pretend to be "for everyone". I can hardly stomach needles onscreen, but it's the SOUND palette of this movie that might be the most disgusting sound design I've ever experienced in a movie, yet it's cartoonish at the same time. Kind of like the dessert wafer scene in Monty Python's "The Meaning Of Life" on acid. You'll know the basics of the plot by now, but the execution is centered in a feminist Cronenberg social critique and then skips numerous opportunities to just quit at any convenient ending point to take a detour from David Lynch's Mulholland Drive to his Elephant Man with John Waters' and Divine's middle fingers to society's relegating women to window dressing for the enjoyment of others, and still refusing to let up without a full on Gwar show finale (just as messy and just as silly) that generously delivers the gross-out spectacle while mocking our collective refusal to deal with seeing ourselves age.

Don't see it on a full stomach.

[PS: Props also to the dark techno angle of the film score. I'm sure the music supervisor(s) were aware of the track "Substance (Felix Da Housecat Remix)" by Dot Allison. While not as dark and heavy as the film's score, it seems a missed opportunity not to include it somewhere, even over the end credits. I recommend looking the song up wherever you get your music.]

reviews.author: Floated2
reviews.body:
Described as a horror sci-fi body swap type film, it is extremely creative with its concept and execution. At times it does feel rather confusing with the concept of both characters using the substance to change from one body of its older self to younger self. Both actresses pull great performances. The film certainly shows several explicit scenes of skin but it makes sense. Nothing too overly sexual for no reason.

Roughly the first hour and a half is certainly the stronger part where everything is interesting and we are seeing what is happening next.

Around the part where the title card reads "3 months later" (around 1:34:00) is when the film seemingly declines. It's still interesting and fascinating to start but it feels like different ideas were brought in. Then as it continues it transcends somewhere into a bizarre and gory monster mash film with Demi Moore transforming into a deformed older version then a combination of both actresses in one- of course signifying an underlying body image message.

Even with the flaws and bizarreness of the final act, there is still a lot to enjoy and be entertained by. It certainly is one of the more creative and thrilling films of 2024 and deserves its praise.

reviews.author: jojobru-56454
reviews.body: How they filmed it, how we can see every single gross detail was great, disgusting but at the same time addicting. I'm a horror/gore fan so I didn't feel the need to leave the room but my mom who hates these kinds of stuff was about to storm out but she still watched until the end. It was one of my favorites movies that got out this year particularly because they don't really make good thrillers anymore, in my opinion. The whole story was well written, I understand they wanted to make it the goriest possible but I must say that the last fifteen minutes are a bit exaggerated. Anyway the actors did a rlly good job and i hope you take the time to go watch it soon!

reviews.author: Badbadgery
reviews.body:
...the relentless exposition. How many times do you need to tell us what we have already worked out? Unless there's a meta-point being made here - "it's obvious but you don't see it!" - the film would just be much better if it was more subtle. The visual over-the-topness is good; the movie would be a lesser thing without it. But the sledgehammer-to-a-nut imagery is a distraction. This is s shame because the grotesque story is utterly compelling and the leads are both superb. At 62 Demi Moore is enough of a metaphor. You don't need cute camera angles and side-cuts to remind us of the point she's already landed.

Less direction please. Tone it down and this could be a classic.

reviews.author: DrDemento789
reviews.body: Very similar plot lines even up to the end when she loses herself to abusing the drug. For everyone who did not like the end I am convinced it was all in her head but you be the judge. Definitely has the body horror one would expect so do not go in if you are squeamish. The monster kind of also remindmed me of the 1990 film Society so this film as a whole was a great throwback of movies of old where you threw out disbelief and just enjoyed the movie without thinking about it too much like some kind of message you have to walk away with. Overall a pretty great film much better than the new joker movie by a mile.

reviews.author: raja_sarkar
reviews.body:
The Substance (2024) is a visceral and well-crafted body horror film that delves into the darker aspects of human nature - greed, ego, addiction, and vanity - ultimately showcasing how these traits can lead to self-destruction. It also satires Hollywood's obsession with youth and the extremes some are willing to endure to preserve relevance. It also lampoons the ruthlessness of the entertainment bosses to enhance show-ratings.

The story is a bit unique: Elizabeth Sparkle (Demi Moore), a fading TV aerobics star, undergoes a dubious rejuvenation procedure involving a mysterious "substance." This creates a younger version of herself, Sue (Margaret Qualley), who rapidly ascends to stardom, leaving chaos and destruction in her wake.

Director Coralie Fargeat's bold and stylistic vision brings this grotesque tale to life, with striking visuals, intense close-ups, body-play and a thrilling, gory finale.

Demi Moore shines as Elizabeth, masterfully portraying the physical and emotional unraveling of a woman trapped by societal pressures and identity crises. This career-defining comeback reaffirms her status as a fearless and versatile performer. Margaret Qualley's nuanced portrayal of Sue - a character grappling with duality - is magnetic, while Dennis Quaid delivers a standout performance as Harvey, a chronically repulsive and morally ambiguous studio executive.

The film is a must-watch for fans of experimental cinema. It pushes boundaries but comes with a hidden warning: you may lose your appetite-and perhaps start fearing aging!

reviews.author: jordanmartingill
reviews.body:
I just walked out of the cinema during last quarter of the movie as the movie was beyond gruesome, if I stayed any longer I was scared I would vomit.

First half of the movie was alright I guess. The character development as to why she went to these lengths was not believable or well written.

I just think some sick individuals sat around a writers table with a good concept to get people into the cinema and then just completely derailed to have the most shocking ending for people to talk about.

In my 30 years of life I have never walked out of the movies. So many stages I was not looking at the screen because of how gruesome it was and I thought it couldn't get worse but it did.

Don't waste your time or money on this.

reviews.author: peterbegran
reviews.body:
Squirm, watch thru fingers with a twisting smile at this gross ASMR-laden tutti-frutti filmed gore treat.

Very original (although echoes of the Fly) it kept me glued, but is too long. Stick with it though because around 70 minutes in the storyline eases up into full ghoulish comedy. It's gross, disgusting and poses all sorts of existential questions, but ignore all that and have a hearty laugh.

Demi seems to be enjoying the absurdity, and Margaret Qualley excel (Dennis Quaid just great "Isabel, who has time to say that? Your name's Chic"...something like that!).

Certainly not for kids as does have some memorable scary scenes, but no jump scares.

reviews.author: ancsdavalos
reviews.body: This is a really cool movie. The beginning is has you hooked immediately. There's a lot of nudity (sexualized for sure) per the beauty standards of the film world, but it really does have its place within the movie. If you're grossed out by bodily mutation, needles, or blood- I wouldn't watch this. But it was definitely a very interesting movie on the take of beauty and aging. Demi Moore is gorgeous, I just kept thinking how beautiful she was throughout the beginning of the movie and how sad it is that she felt "ugly" and worthless. It's sad to know many aging women feel this way, rather than leaning into their aging wisdom and beauty. It's a really weird movie but also very cool. Ending was not good at all, the beginning and middle were great then it just really went down hill at the end.

reviews.author: jamesmcmorine
reviews.body:
... It felt like they didn't really know how to end it.

I thought at the end Elisabeth was going to come out of all of that and almost be reborn, then she could live her life and be happy in her own skin. But instead it kind of just went off the rails a bit and they decided to go all out over the top bloody (literally) for no real reason.

Up until the ending it had been a somewhat based in reality, or at least plausible sci-fi type body horror film. Whereas the ending just felt like it was something out of an over the top b-movie comedy horror instead.

Despite the end though, overall I did thoroughly enjoy the film as a whole, and it certainly makes you think about the themes that it covers earlier on. If it hadn't taken such a hard turn right at the end, I'd probably have given it a 9 or maybe even a 10.

reviews.author: sowinator
reviews.body:
Is the keyword here, I think.

It fits well with the film's theme and style but takes a toll on the runtime and pacing. Many of the concepts and topics the film tries to explore are repeated so much that it starts to feel dull, even a bit patronizing.

On the technical side, though, it excels:

* The sound design is awesome, making everything feel more tactile and impactful.

* The editing has a strong, distinctive voice. It can be a little over-the-top at times, but it fits the overall theme.

* The cinematography is fantastic. There's a good balance between close-ups and wide-angle shots, creating a slightly nauseating, dreamy quality that heightens the mood.

Overall, it feels like a vivid description of that strange, desperate feeling you get about a week before your birthday.

Definitely worth a watch.

reviews.author: goshea-72306
reviews.body:
I haven't seen demi Moore in a movie in years so I was looking forward to this one.

It was good , I enjoyed it but so obscene i couldn't believe it was happening kind of feeling. It certainly was not like any if your regular demi moore movies this was way way different. The story is funny and as the movie goes on its absolutely crazy what escalates The ending of the movie I really didn't see it coming I was shocked at what I was seeing. It is definitely worth a watch . It's easy watching you don't need to over concentrate on this movie it's a horror / comedy in all sense . All is said I enjoyed it .

reviews.author: patricia-63097
reviews.body: Definitely a B grade horror film which will be a future Cult film due to its gore and special effects more than the message and Directorial whizz! Ofcourse there is an audience out there who are entertained by this genre, but the messages are too obvious and lost in the trivialisation & the extremities of such an important modern problem that seems to be plaguing the modern female which, btw, we are all guilty of perpetuating, including Demi Moore who has obviously had changes made to her natural body to please who? Herself? Other Men? Other Women? This aspect of the film is its only, substance!

reviews.author: sweetyraman
reviews.body:
Substance is a movie which is well thought of, and amazingly made.

For starters, the performances by both protagonists are remarkable. Aging is very tricky concept. Women and men both go through it, but very few grow through it. Tight boobs, slim waist line was you and so are wrinkles and gray hair. Acceptance or even acknowledgment of both versions is what women run all through their lives.. Not all but the majority of women do. For the main course, desperation leads us to do horrible experiments without analyzing the pros and cons. The scene where deme Moore gets ready for a date, reflects the so-called " self mirror theory"-which states one doesn't see himself in that mirror, but the perception of others in the mirror"

This movie is a must-watch for this day and time. The body is biological biological made a certain way,its so powerful that it heals itself, but alteration in it is playing with a billion complex processes within. If you are up for a game, then sometimes you play, and sometimes you get played.

Substance is such a good take on the entire body-shaping, and cosmetic bizarre industry..which is making money at stake because of insecurity and vulnerability.

reviews.author: hamiltonjeramie
reviews.body:
A close up look at aging and grasping at the straws youth with a new "Substance". The movie seems more like a metaphor for child birth and living vicariously through another vessel while it sucks you dry than anything else to me. It pokes and prods at beauty standards, sex, ambition, and dreams, and what someone would do to make it all come true.

A captivating visceral style meant to make you clench your cheeks. I could tell it was Coralie Fargeat with the overt eating scenes reminiscent of her other work Revenge.

Definitely worth the watch on big screen and look forward to more works from this director.

reviews.author: meinwonderland
reviews.body:
The coexistence of ugliness and beauty inhabits spaces draping everything in its wake and gives expression to the immanent tension between self-love and appearance, where everything known, no matter how mundane or extraordinary, nightmarish or heavenly, is utilized to further its extremity. The Substance examines our relation with body image, its effects on personhood and interpersonal dynamics. It expresses the self-inflicted, internalized violence through physical manifestation, thematically exploring body image and ageism as never before. Its inheritance of body horror and gore carries within a history on the search of the grotesque. Styles that break with convention and taste by finding in bodies perfect recipients to experiment and show their endurance but also their intrinsic vulnerability. Horror provides the security and comfort of facing our fears, a way to confront what nightmares are made of and find joy in the terrifying. Sometimes the terrifying is not a product of exogenic dangers like in films that explore torture but a product born from our inner selves. The first shots of the film encapsulate the passing of time and how what once shone like a bright star now lies forgotten in the shadows. Violence perpetrated by time is one we, as mortal and aging beings, cannot escape from.

Written and directed by Coralie Fargeat, she indicated to be inspired by her own life experiences when creating The Substance. How she learnt to be violent about her image and feel it was never enough led her to consider it absurd and question it now that she is approaching 50. The movie pays homage to all the movies she loves that had an impact on her life.

One reference that stands out is a literary one, naturally The Picture of Dorian Gray by Oscar Wilde, in which a man manages to elude aging by allowing the signs of the passing of time to appear on a portrait of him and not on himself. In The Substance, by making her pain invisible and her beauty visible, Sue is Dorian, while Elisabeth is the equivalent of the portrait, her body as the canvas in which every change manifests, reminding its subject of her true appearance. Violence externalized in visual elements that testify to our agency of societal beauty standards, where a failure to meet said demands is experienced as unworthiness. By reason of that agentic state, beauty standards are actively craved many times to the detriment of our self-worth, especially when comparison renders its endeavor a seemingly impossible one to achieve.

Coralie Fargeat creates a world where everything that can have the potentiality of being disturbing is used in extremes to achieve that end. No matter how little or insignificant, she makes the simplest of things, like eating, something grotesque, producing discomfort and disgust, and once you think the movie has exceeded the limits, it goes further and unleashes new doses of grotesqueness.

The Substance is impactful not solely by reason of its use of graphic and shocking imagery but also by how profound its message is. The beauty of what Coralie Fargeat created is in not subordinating the concept to gratuitous gore, and it succeeds precisely because behind all the body horror, she is telling us something important, and we should listen.

reviews.author: chrisalsing
reviews.body:
If I were able to give this movie negative stars I would! The first 2/3 of the movie are great. Actually probably one of the best movies of the year! But then comes along the final 1/3 of the movie. I don't know what on earth the writers and director were thinking when they decided to add this ending to the movie! It was almost like a bunch of stoners sitting around in someone's basement trying to come up with a hilarious, disgusting, gorey ending. They could have ended the movie 30-40 minutes earlier and it would have been perfect! But then it takes a horrendous turn for the absolute stupid!!

Demi performed great as always. And for being 61 years old, she is still sexy and gorgeous! Dennis Quade is a little over the top with his acting in this movie in my opinion. If you want the best advice you will get this year, watch the first 2/3 of the movie and then walk out. You will thank me.

reviews.author: drastarr
reviews.body: I totally see why people don't like the ending. I'm sure they're all lovely people but they're wrong (I'm sure our grandmothers would hate it too). It's perfect and the only way to end the movie (no spoilers). The core conceit of the movie practically demands it. It is thematically cathartic. But there is no denying it makes it a controversial movie as a whole and one only meant for certain audiences. Everything about this movie is done perfectly, but it does so in its own world. Whether you understand and appreciate the world it's in is totally a matter of taste. Other than that - casting, direction, screenplay, sound, editing, and all those things make it, at the very least, a visually incredible piece of art.

reviews.author: nyhph
reviews.body:
All the violence that you project on me, the monster, at some points, it's projected back on the audience," Fargeat says, "which is all of us.

reviews.author: Chucky_Farley
reviews.body:
F-cking Great Film, except for the ending which was bizarre. "The Substance" is a compelling reminder that the most terrifying adversary we face often resides within ourselves. As a no-nonsense horror film, it strips away the gimmicks and clever marketing ploys that many contemporary horror films rely on, opting instead for a rich exploration of the mind's darker corners. In a cinematic landscape crowded with overhyped spectacles, particularly evident in the marketing frenzy surrounding "Longlegs," this film carves out its niche by tapping into deeper, more personal fears.

I would have given it a prefect score if it were not for that last 15 minutes.

reviews.author: davidmunizhemet
reviews.body: Great premise, good message, great cinematography, spectacular audio. That said, it was great because I don't think I've cringed and covered my eyes more than any other movie. Get ready for some gore. Very hard to watch the first time I doubt I'll ever watch it again. As everyone else has pointed out, it starts out great, but the last 40 minutes or so become really hard to watch. I think they did OK job with character building, you do feel for the character and it creates tension in your body. Do not watch this while eating, right after you ate, or gonna go eat lol. It sucked me in to watch in the beginning and by the end I really want to take my eyes off of it all.

reviews.author: amyyoung-72082
reviews.body:
As a horror movie fanatic, I'm often surprised when A-list celebrities make the plunge into the genre, as we see a lot of great actors and actresses start their careers in horror, but rarely do they dip their toes back in once they reach A-list status. That's why I was a little shocked to see Demi Moore casted for this film. Demi did not disappoint and understood the assignment!

This ones for the body horror fans - fans of "The Thing"/"The Fly" will rejoice in theatres for "The Substance." If your not about the gore, I suggest sitting this one out. As a fan of "American Psycho", I think this movie is similarly a rare female directed horror that lends itself to the feminine eye.

It lost the two extra stars from me due to oversaturation of certain elements - nudity and the ending. Nudity felt essential to the concept and gravity of the film, but I just found it to be excessive at times. The ending (last 20-30 minutes) could have been chopped entirely in my opinion, but as a few reviews already stated, it seemed that there was a practical effects budget that had to be spent. The ending took the movie from a believable tragedy into a dream-state, looney crescendo that took away from the film in my opinion.

Regardless, this movie lingered with me for days after I left the theatre and I have a feeling horror fans will be talking about this one for many year's to come! Skip the spoilers and enjoy as the chaos unfolds!

reviews.author: The-honest-critic
reviews.body:
Like many others I was unsatisfied with the ending. The movie started great, and you immediately felt empathetic for the main character. The movie portrays extremely well how body dysmorphia affects us all, especially those of us for whom our appearance is a large part of our identity. It shows what kind of irrational and impulsive decisions we make to try and escape the discomfort of our own perception of ourselves. I was uncomfortable for most of the movie and also disgusted. The visuals are excellent and the plot was compelling and relatable, though anxiety provoking.

The ending was my only complaint with the movie, as it felt out of place and incoherent with the style and pace of the rest of the movie.

The acting was phenomenal and the actors deserve credit for their ability to make us empathise with the characters.

Overall a good watch and I think a 7.5/10 rating is justified.

reviews.author: mi_hau94
reviews.body: Now, throughout 90% of the movie I was wondering why it had such a high score. It seemed kind of generic, it was definitely predictable. And it wasn't too shocking. The grand finale, the explosion (literally) that took this movie from a decent thriller experience to one of the greatest gore movies since Braindead 1992. It transformed "just another horror movie" to a once in a lifetime experience. This is something I will remember to the day I die. I looked several times at the length and thought omg it's another two hours until the movie is over. But after watching the end I would not change a single thing about it. It's perfect, it's a classic. And f yes there's some good bootie/boobie shots in here too.

reviews.author: krytycal
reviews.body:
This film draws inspiration from unnerving classics such as Requiem for a Dream and 2001: A Space Odyssey. They share the unsettling and distorted visuals, the sensory overload, the increasingly nightmarish sequences, the social commentary on isolation, ambition, desire, and self-destruction. They even have the same musical scores.

The problem with The Substance is that they took all the substance out. It lacks everything that makes disturbing films good. All pain, no gain. There's no pay off. There is no take-home. The film delivers its message with the subtlety of a category 5 hurricane. No calm to be found here. It pummels the viewers and leaves them bloodied. The final scene perfectly summarizes how I felt as a viewer trying to drag myself through this film desperately looking for something to cling to. One star indeed.

Not being able to overcome her sense of pride, she used The Substance. A miracle drug which can produce a younger and better version of oneself. At least physically. I think you can already guess how this plot will progress, but the process is interesting to watch. Or more precisely, horrifying to watch! It's like an actual nightmare came to life. The message in this movie is very good. And Demi Moore's acting was superb! She's still amazing after all this time!

reviews.author: cosavostra
reviews.body: This is essentially feels like a Netflix Black Mirror episode that's been dragged out to feature length. The concept of the film is grounded enough but you can just tell it falls short of its potential and relies on the eye candy of attractive girls and the shock of excessive gore to smooth over the predictability of the "You vs. You" storyline that you see coming from a mile away. From there the story doesn't really go anywhere and in the end just feels like it resigns itself to simply delivering some lazily conjured up nonsense purely to end what has become a yawn rather than anything engaging.

reviews.author: mike-c-b
reviews.body:
It should have played like Total Recall.

People have enough dullness and sadness in their lives. Movies are an escape.

Much of the cinematography & camera angles focus on max sadness, max ass/boobs, max dennis quaid, max horror. No long-sightedness or story.

Demi Moore could carry a remake of Total Recall, scene for scene, and be as good as the original... but here she was used as "someone that just gets old" essentially.

There's little for anyone to care about what happens to any of the characters. - Except for the concept of being fired for your age, and cheating on your age. - Characters appear soulless.

Due to the characters being soulless, there's no drama about them being careful in any way. What friction is there if nothing impacts them...

Most of the drama is grinning and zoomed ass.

reviews.author: DiesIraeComing
reviews.body:
Are we really supposed to be rooting for the vain, egomaniacal actress with the condo overlooking the city and a giant photo of herself on the wall? Oh look, she feels lonely now that's she's over 50 and realizes she chose ego, money, and fame over starting a family. What an easily avoidable tragedy!

And of course, all the men in the movie are stupid pigs. I mean, it's a Hollywood movie post 2020. So all men are must be characterized as stupid and/or pig-like.

I think the issue with these new movies is that the writers don't know how to write likeable characters because they don't know how to be likeable. More and more I find myself rooting against every character on the screen. Once it's clear they aren't all going to die, I just turn the movie off.

I did enjoy the visual style. That's the only thing that kept me watching after I realized this movie is just a room full of profoundly unlikeable characters doing gross things to each other. I do hope the cinematographer and art department do more movies. Maybe the next one will have a likeable character?

reviews.author: abdotaha-67140
reviews.body:
As usual with these types of films, white characters just can't help but fall for the most obvious traps. Our MC doesn't hesitate to dive right into the madness, making you wonder if they're even aware of their surroundings or the consequences. It almost feels like the filmmakers are trying to make a point about how easily people lose themselves under pressure from modern success standards, but it ends up feeling like a tired trope.

And then there's this so-called existential crisis, which feels so fabricated-like the character is desperately trying to grasp at some grand meaning to justify their actions. Instead of handling it in a way that feels authentic, they jump straight into the most extreme and irrational choices. It's like they're trying way too hard to convince themselves-and the audience-that their inner turmoil is deep and profound, but it comes off as completely forced and unearned.

The writing? Lazy. The protagonist's level of naivety is just not believable. It's hard to accept that someone could be this clueless unless the script is forcing it. It's like the plot couldn't function unless the character made absurd decisions, so the writers just rolled with it. By the end, it's less of a psychological unraveling and more of a series of increasingly ridiculous choices that make you roll your eyes.

reviews.author: itskayroza
reviews.body:
The Substance is a film that seems to aim for social commentary, yet it stumbles in its attempt to convey a meaningful message, ultimately trivializing the very issues it seeks to address. The storyline begins with a promising premise that could dive into women's struggles, but as it progresses, it loses focus, resulting in a confusing and somewhat tone-deaf portrayal. Instead of delving into authentic experiences or offering insights, the narrative falls flat, missing the nuance necessary to handle sensitive topics.

The film's climax and ending feel dismissive of the women's journey, almost turning their struggles into a punchline rather than a point of empathy or understanding. This undermines any initial attempts at depth and reduces the complexity of women's experiences to surface-level tropes, leaving viewers feeling like the movie mocks rather than honors those issues. The lack of sensitivity in the story's final act is especially jarring, transforming what could have been a meaningful exploration into a frustrating and disappointing watch.

reviews.author: HeronMoon
reviews.body:
The Substance is a walking stereotype, incapable of making claims deeper than "beauty standards are ridiculous", lacking meaningful dialogue and plot, and featuring an ending 30 minutes that is so disgusting, useless, and repetitive that one would do a disservice to their life by spending any of their precious time watching it.

The positive reviews of this film are propagated by those who believe "taking a stand" and "sharing an empowering message" that can be summarized in 15 minutes is a sign of their virtuosity, while lacking any real appreciation for quality film and use of budget.

Do yourself a favor and skip watching this film.

reviews.author: drue13
reviews.body:
This review won't be helpful, it's my first after all. But the fact that this is my first review, should say at least something.

Plotless, plot holes all over, incoherent (the entire premise is forgotten after 45-60 min), senseless, terrible writing, zero character development, and absolutely vile (way past any limit or reason). Acting is good.

And yes, we get the message. It's powerful and needs to be heard. But that's not enough when making a movie. This one actually makes a disservice to it. If you can't make a movie that can enhance and powerfully convey the message, limit yourself to tweeting about it or something.

I absolutely don't get the high rating, I want to believe it is because of the message. Some points for the replete/cheap nudity? Maybe the extremity? Idk. Clearly not enough for me.

reviews.author: narmncfdmk
reviews.body:
Went to this movie knowing absolutely nothing about it. So no preconceived ideas. Started well with the idea that people aren't happy with what they have or what they've achieved. So good premise. I was excited to see Demi Moore and Dennis Quaid in this movie.

I could see it was going to be something quirky from the cinematic angles and lighting. Definitely had vibe reminding me of Evil Dead.

They absolutely missed an opportunity where they could have made Demi a ravenous monster after waking up from a long sleep.

The last 15 minutes were so ridiculous. I laughed so hard I was crying. It was like the writers just decided to throw the most ridiculous ending possible in.

No doubt will become a cult classic it was that quirky. Not for me though.

reviews.author: vialactea
reviews.body:
Before I give my opinion I must say I like body horror movies, The Substance though, it's on another level. It started really well and intriguing, the plot is interesting and if you like to read in between the lines you'll find some really good food for thought, unfortunately as the time passed by the mess and non sense stupidity takes the best part of the action. Half way through I could tell that the end would be chaotic to say the least and perhaps the best thing to do would be to stop watching it, but my curiosity to see how the disturbed and distorted mind behind the making of this film would take this didn't let me turn off the TV.

The chaotic climax in the end confirmed my worst fears. 2 hours of my life wasted.

Positives: Demi Moore and Margaret fully naked on screen.

Negatives: Everything else.

reviews.author: theethinethou
reviews.body:
By far, this is one of the most disgusting pointless movies I've ever watched. Seriously, who thought that this was a good idea? I think they could have exposed the darker side of the beauty obsession of Hollywood in a better less disgusting and physically abhorrent redundant manner.

In other words, this movie is extremely gory, and it doesn't seem to really have a point other than in and of itself to be gory.

No character development whatsoever! None! This should have been an amusing dark satirical exposé on Hollywood, beauty and darkness, but instead - it was just disgusting - and by the way, don't eat a while you're watching this movie.

The movie is deceptive in that you hear the score and you expect the amusing dark comedy part to come right around the corner to match up, but instead it's just more gore and pointless noises as the two bodies are performed on.

There's no way that all of these glowing reviews can be real.

reviews.author: srgymrat33
reviews.body:
I watched the first hour and then read the Wikipedia summary - I literally just could not stomach it - I fast forwarded parts within that first section - so full disclosure .

I love film and I love one that is willing to push the boundaries and prove a point . A film that makes you feel something - genuinely uncomfortable and disgusted . Film should make you question sometimes where the line is and if the movie has crossed it - the wondering keeps it good - to me - this movie officially steps far far over the line into something actually grotesque and completely inappropriate and unnecessary to prove the point they are trying to make .

From what I saw it was casted perfectly and both women and DQ executed well. The film certainly is aesthetically well thought out and helps to lead the viewer the direction they want you to go .

The message behind the film is good and important - the objectifying of women in media and in culture in general and how we all play a role in supporting that or at the very least turning a blind eye .

But there is a moral line for a film that isn't porn ( or maybe it is ?) and that line was crossed so that the viewer cannot focus on the point anymore because of the focus on the gore and the nudity . The shocking nature does not enhance the message and the film - it totally ruins it .

I rarely don't finish a movie but I just can't do it .

reviews.author: cheyannedriscoll
reviews.body: I was excited to see Demi Moore in a new movie, expecting something intriguing and special based on the reviews. Instead, the film relied heavily on shock value with drastic and disgusting scenes, offering little substance or depth. The storyline felt hollow, the characters lacked development, and the pacing dragged. While the camera work was decent, it couldn't save the overall experience, which felt like a disjointed mess. The ending was especially frustrating-confusing, unsatisfying, and leaving me wondering what the point of it all was. I expected more from such a promising setup, but this was a letdown. Super disappointed. Save your time!

reviews.author: kheterpalayush
reviews.body:
Probably one of the most boring movie I ever saw, devoid of any storyline. The big message is that we should love ourself for who we are, not let some selfish people dictate our lives and enjoy little things in life. That we should not eat away at ourselves and maintain balance.

Fine, we get it, it could easily have been a 5 minutes tedtalk.

Gore is fine if it has some substantial storyline, but this movie just use gore to mask its deficiency in the storyline and lazy writing. Never thought such a boring movie can be so acclaimed.

Rating it three stars instead of one because they tried something different, even if something different to make it worse. A lot of effort has been put up into how to depict gore. You might like it if you are into modern or abstract art, but I'm not that person.

reviews.author: ruble-huff
reviews.body:
I'm sorry, but this film was nearly too silly to watch. You have to suspend disbelief so intensely that literally nothing could possibly surprise you.

I think the actors did the best they could with the material they were given. They simply weren't given all that much. Every male character in the film was written to be an utter buffoon. The 'substance' was ridiculous in its concept. Be a more 'beautiful' you? DNA is clearly smarter than I imagined, it decides one eye color is better than another, yet not smart enough to purge birthmarks. Go figure.

Apparently, this juice also auto-bestows a sense of entitlement, greed, and the narcissist's full toolkit. If they advertised the negative side effects, it would absolutely scare people away.

'Use only once.' Not 'Use Once and Discard.' Who wouldn't see a recipe for disaster there? Also, it seems to be 'one dose fits all.' Yet they supply more than a full syringe could possibly hold. The whole process had me shaking my head almost constantly.

It was also way too heavy on social commentary and stereotyping.

Jekyll and Hyde and The Portrait of Dorian Grey did it so much better. High marks for SFX make-up and body prosthetics. I will grant that. The firehosing blood was ridiculous, though.

Don't waste your time on this film unless you like the actors for their talents.

reviews.author: ozsud
reviews.body:
"The Substance" began promisingly, exploring thought-provoking themes and boasting impressive performances. Unfortunately, the film's potential was squandered by a jarring, incoherent, and excessively gory conclusion.

Demi Moore's talent was wasted in the film's disturbing and gratuitous final act. While she remains a stunning and accomplished actress, her character's graphic nudity felt unnecessary and exploitative.

The film's abrupt nosedive into horror was off-putting, evident by the two couples who exited the theater 15 minutes before the end, unable to stomach the content.

The Substance's squandered potential and unpleasant conclusion left me underwhelmed and disappointed.

reviews.author: sswren1

The art of subtlety is gone. The thresh hold for shock has been moved into a dangerous red zone and like the substance, it's irreversible. Maybe the modern proclivity to violence, filth and sadism can be attributed to Hollywood's slide into whatever level you call this.

I care not for the cinematic credentials of anyone involved in this abomination but I pity their motivation.

reviews.author: hannahrosemishka
reviews.body:
The unnecessary amount of nudity and sensuality was tasteless, overdone and disctracted from the cool sci-fi concept which was at the basis of the storyline.

The concept of the substance walks the line between creative and just plain silly throughout the movie, and then the ending pushes it over to totally stupid.

I was dumbfounded. It felt like towards the end someone deranged had hijacked the script and scribbled on what was actually coming out to be a decent social commentary. I don't know what was the point of the childishly bizzare scenes, perhaps for shock value or to add to the beauty standards allegory, but it just made me wish I could take back the two and half hours of my time that I had wasted on this movie.

reviews.author: svarooom
reviews.body:
As a connoisseur of movies like this and with a list of 100's of movies watched over the decades I just don't get why in 2024 something as mediocre and bad as this gets praised and is award worthy?

This movie is in (3) Acts and the first two are watchable as the third is a complete waste and walkout worthy act. Cringe and laughable is even too nice. France as LA is CGI horrible.

Great to see Demi Moore as a gorgeous older actress as she performs well early on. The story of the Fountain of Youth is interestingly thought out here but executed badly. Story plot holes, continuity issues, cartoonish special effects etc. Anyone here seen the movie 'Thinner'?

Other similarities are from DePalma, King, Carpenter, Donner, Argento... Please people, try and watch what inspired this director and not this trash of a film.

reviews.body: The movie pretends to have some sanctimonious feminist message about how men are bad for craving female body and treating it as an object. Peak hypocrisy and glaring how the frustration and hate of writer/director comes through in a very obvious way. At every point it breaks the golden rule of show instead of tell and audio effects are laughable. Otherwise great acting but really not much to work with. I'm off to check my house walls for a spare room by randomly knocking on walls.

reviews.author: ditimurshin-236-726933
reviews.body:
It's like if the Thing, the Fly and Sunset Boulevard had a baby, a very freaky baby indeed. But unlike this hellchild, those 3 aforementioned classics are actually great movies.

The substance on the other hand (imo of course) is simply not a good movie, it's lacking any believability whatsoever, most of the dialogue, the story as a whole, people's motives and pretty much everything else in this movie doesn't resemble reality at all, it's way over the top (I know they've done this on purpose, so the movie would feel like a fever dream by the time the lights are on) but to be fair, the movie still delivers, because the body horror porn is so hardcore, it simply overshadows everything else, but take the shock value away (both Demi Moore's titties and the body horror)... and what you got left?

reviews.author: barcellosthaina
reviews.body:
The whole premise is interesting and the film starts well, by the middle of the film the audience has understood what the film is trying to say and what the protagonists are feeling, but the director doesn't realize this and continues to add unnecessary, repetitive and bad taste scenes. At this point, the movie begins to suck your energy and you just want the ending to come, and when we finally reach the long-awaited conclusion, it's just a gore show with a very obvious and unoriginal message behind it.

It has a message about how women are objectified and how this leads to an obsession with youth, but the movie itself spends much of its time doing just that with the young actress. Several close-ups of her ass that you can't convince me were necessary.

The use of exaggeration and caricatures (especially in male characters) really went over the edge, especially towards the end of the movie.

Overall, a movie that had potential but got lost in the middle.

reviews.author: riedel-50650
reviews.body:
Watching this movie was an experience I'd rather forget. From start to finish, it felt like a chaotic amalgamation of poor decisions, lackluster storytelling, and bewildering creative choices. To say that this film was bad would be an understatement. It is, without a doubt, one of the worst movies I've ever endured.

The story itself is riddled with plot holes so vast that even the Caspian Sea pales in comparison. Almost every scene leaves you wondering, "Why?" or "How?" Characters make decisions that defy not only logic but also basic human instincts. The motivations behind their actions are either poorly explained or entirely absent.

The central conflict of the movie is convoluted and, frankly, nonsensical. Important plot points are glossed over, leaving gaping holes in the narrative. There's no buildup, no emotional depth, and no reason for the audience to care. It's a stark reminder of how essential coherent storytelling is, and this film utterly fails in that regard.

Adding to the film's woes is the baffling decision-making in costume and production design. The costumes are not only unrealistic but also jarring. The characters are adorned in outfits that would be more suited to a fantasy cosplay convention and are not scary or even shocking or disgusting.

Despite the movie's heavy reliance on gore and shock value, none of it lands effectively. The special effects are subpar at best and laughable at worst. Scenes meant to elicit horror or discomfort are instead met with indifference or, even worse, unintended laughter. It's clear the filmmakers were aiming to make an impact, but the execution is so poor that it has the opposite effect.

The only saving grace in this mess is the performance by Demy, who, despite the absurdity of the material, manages to inject some semblance of depth and authenticity into the role. The final act of the movie, though still flawed, shows a faint glimmer of what could have been. There's a sense of urgency and coherence that was sorely lacking in the earlier parts of the film. While it's not enough to save the movie, it does provide a few moments of relief amidst the chaos.

Overall, this film is a masterclass in how not to make a movie. With a plot full of holes, illogical character choices, unrealistic production design, and unimpressive gore, it's a painful watch. I am happy I got to see it for free.

reviews.author: eduardomurphyperez
reviews.body:
On a general point of view, the message of this movie is something that we already know: "Understand that your body ages, and there's nothing you can do about it. Don't try to fix it, ageing is natural."

And that message is great, however, that premise can be said in what? 15-20 min? Instead of that, the movie overextends on itself, and the result is a boring, extenuating ad nauseam, which only leaves you with a feeling of anger of the fact that it was a waste of time.

The plot has many different things that are irrelevant, and don't get me started on the hole-plots, or just plain ilogical stuff happening on the movie, but the worst part is the ending that seems like a Hobo's drug-addict nightmare.

Probably the only good thing of this movie is that you'll get to see lots of boobs.

Don't waste your time or money with this film.

reviews.author: gamunro23
reviews.body:
What would you do to be a better version of you?

The messaging in the movie is great, if you could be a "better" version of you, would you? Would you still do it if it caused you pain? If you were the better version would allow someone else take the consequences for your actions?

By the end the overall message is everyone is beautiful and you don't need to change your appearance.

The movie is suspenseful and really well done for the first 75% and then just becomes a hot mess. If the movie had stopped with 30-40minutes left I think it would be a 8/10 but.....it didn't.

Instead you end up shaking your head for the finale while checking your watch and seeing if you can work out the runtime remaining.

Could have been brilliant instead you end up with this, maybe it's just me and I've missed the point but I certainly wouldn't be going back to try and find it.

reviews.author: fox9106
reviews.body:
Substance is a frustrating paradox that ultimately fails to deliver on its central premise. The film ostensibly critiques society's obsession with beauty, but instead ends up glorifying the very ideals it seeks to dismantle. Rather than exposing the dangers of this cult-like fixation, it revels in grotesque imagery and exaggerated aesthetics, making it impossible to discern any meaningful critique.

The plot meanders aimlessly, offering little more than a hollow spectacle. While it claims to challenge our perceptions of beauty, it bombards the audience with disturbing visuals that seem gratuitous rather than thought-provoking. The result is a shallow and contradictory experience that feels like an insult to the viewer's intelligence.

A complete waste of time, Substance is a film that doesn't just miss its mark-it completely misunderstands it. Save yourself the discomfort and skip this one."

reviews.author: tm-sheehan
reviews.body:
My Rating - The Substance Streaming on Amazon Prime My Rating. 0/10

The only reason I watched this grotesque monstrosity and waste of celluloid or cellulite was to see why Demi Moore won the Golden Globe award yesterday for Best Female Actor in a Musical or Comedy Picture instead of Cynthia Erivo's amazing performance as Elphaba in the musical Wicked ?

Demi Moore said yesterday in her acceptance speech that in her long career of over 40 years this was the first time that she has won anything.

I'm still in a state of bewilderment after seeing The Substance starring Demi Moore who is really only in half the movie because she shares her character with Margaret Qualley who plays her better self Sue .

In 1970 Joan Crawford at a similar age to Demi Moore made a horror sci fi movie titled Trog and got crucified by the critics and audiences but Trog as bad as it may be is a masterpiece compared to The Substance and has attained a sort of cult status.

IMBD gives Trog a rating of 4/10 and The Substance 7.4 /10 what am I missing?

The plot of The Substance has been done to death and far better it's basically Dr Jekyll and Mrs Hyde meets Sweet Bird of Youth and The Elephant Man.

I don't mean to insult Robert Louis Stevenson or Tennessee Williams because the creator and director of this trash Coralie Fargeat in my opinion has created a monstrosity and an insult to women.

If you enjoy lots of blood and gore insane dialogue a naked 64 year old woman writhing around a bathroom floor then transforming into a naked 31 year old woman both giving hysterical performances which to quote a critic who once accused Katharine Hepburn's famous early stage performance as She ran the gamut of emotions from A to B you might enjoy The Substance and, I hated it.

I'm sure this film will be nominated for the grotesque make up and special effects but credit should be given to the butcher shop that suppled the offal used to cover both Demi Moore and Margaret Qualley.

Surely Demi Moore will not be on the same nomination list for Oscar against Cynthia Erovo in May I certainly hope not .

In this case saying this movie I read sends out a message about ageing and negative body images for women .

Trog in 1970 could have been billed as a movie sending a message of acceptance and anti animal cruelty.

reviews.author: lucacommandeur-07461
reviews.body: "The Substance" is a film that, despite its ambitious premise, falls short due to a lack of coherent logic and character development. The narrative centers on Elisabeth Sparkle, a fading celebrity who resorts to a black-market drug to create a younger version of herself. However, the film fails to establish a meaningful connection between Elisabeth and her younger counterpart, Sue. The two characters exist in isolation, unaware of each other's experiences, which undermines the potential for a compelling exploration of identity and self-perception. This disconnect results in a disjointed storyline that leaves the audience questioning the film's internal logic and the motivations driving the characters' actions. Considering the critical acclaim it has received, I find it to be one of the most overrated movies ever. If this is considered one of the best horror films of 2024, it raises serious questions about the current state of cinema.

reviews.author: danekas-32156
reviews.body:
One of the worst movies I've ever watched. It was absolutely terrible: the idea behind it had potential, but the execution was so poor that it leaves you feeling disgusted and regretting the time you spent watching it. Incredibly dull, unnecessarily long, and filled with loud, meaningless chaos, it manages to be both pretentious and overly provocative in a way that feels pointless. Definitely one to avoid.

What's even more frustrating is that you can see glimpses of what could have been a truly compelling story, but they're buried under the direction that seem more focused on shocking or impressing the audience than actually telling a good story. The pacing drags on, making every minute feel like a chore, and even the moments meant to be impactful fall flat. By the end, it feels like a complete waste of time-time that you'll wish you could get back.

reviews.author: kadenbown
reviews.body:
The only thing keeping me from putting this as a 1 star is because for the first little while, I was invested. The idea was cool. It was intriguing. I really wanted to know where it went.

Now I love horror. I am a horror fanatic. One thing I CANNOT do though, is gore. Specifically body gore. It's more personal. About halfway (if even that) through this movie, they lost the plot, completely ignored the story, and made it NOTHING but gore. It was disgusting and inhumane, and I walked out of the theater before it even ended because I couldn't watch it, I couldn't LISTEN to it, and it hurt my soul to watch.

No sane person can watch this movie and think, "Oh yeah, this is the best movie ever." When I think of "horror," I think scary.

Nothing about this movie was scary. It was just gross. It is the worst thing I've ever seen, and they never finished the story.

I was expecting to find out who made the Substance and why. I was expecting there to be a solution, but all there was was disgusting nonsense.

I do not recommend this movie. Movies like this make me lose faith in humanity, and I have no respect for the people who made this.

Don't break your soul.

Do not watch this movie.

reviews.author: lhollan
reviews.body: After the Golden Globes buzz, I unfortunately rented this movie only to find myself back in the C-rated thriller genre of the last century--maybe with a twist of nudity and gratuitous gore. There's no good acting here. There's no good writing here. There are only exaggerated, grotesque characters that surround a woman faced with aging. Yet again. And how all the ratty men in her world are so mean and ruthless. This film is Hollywood penetrating its navel in a poor confession to the world that life in Bel Air is imperfect. The problem is that Hollywood has forgotten that a good film is just a good story. Enough with the dystopia, the sci-fi, the macabre, and the shock-value. What really scared me isn't the movie--it's the fact that it earned nominations and awards!

reviews.author: haidarkanaan
reviews.body:
The movie stretches to an excessive 240 minutes, dragging through trivial and painfully slow events that often feel like they're filmed in slow motion. With more focused editing, the entire story could have been told effectively in just 80 minutes without losing any significant content.

The genre itself is confusing. Is it horror, action, science fiction, or something else entirely? The film fails to establish a clear identity, leaving the audience unsure of its purpose.

The plot lacks logic and coherence. For instance:

1- Why did the doctor at the hospital choose this particular individual for the experiment?

2- Was the memory shared between them? Could the girl recall the old woman's past actions, or could the old woman experience the girl's life and emotions?

If not, what is the purpose of the experiment? If the old woman cannot truly live through the girl's experiences, feel her joys, or gain any connection to her new life, the entire premise feels pointless.

It's as though the old woman simply created a separate human being with no ties to her, who exists only to take over her life and house at her life, The reasoning behind this decision is entirely unclear and leaves the viewer frustrated.

In the end, the movie is not just illogical, it is overwhelmingly unpleasant. Its grotesque imagery and unsettling themes make for a nauseating experience that lingers for all the wrong reasons.

reviews.author: merskur
reviews.body:
And I've seen a lot. From Bad Taste and Braindead to The Fly and Tusk, I've watched a lot. Horror is one of my favourite genres, and I love when it's done well. I don't write reviews, but I'll make an exception in this case.

This movie doesn't have many redeeming factors. Besides the acting being mostly okay, and some of the makeup and effects being decent for the first half, well... Beyond that, it's a mess.

First of all, it's extremely predictable with regards to the major (and only) plot point - the hunt for beauty and relevance leading to the ultimate downfall. It's extremely cliche.

The movie contains several strange decisions, both small and large, from Fred not simply writing his phone number down again instead of picking a wet piece of paper up from the puddle, to the pointless return to the New Year's Eve Show in the final act - only included so the director could fulfil their apparent dream of "Yeah and then I want 500 litres of fake blood splashed everywhere!". It's been done countless times before, and every time more impactful than this. It's completely devoid of all imagination and originality. There is no climax here with any weight whatsoever.

The editing, which I see people praise, is just not good. Couple several weird cuts and choices with what I can only describe as horrible sound design, and you're left with a bad movie with equally bad technicals.

The irony of this movie though, is that it spends most of the far too long runtime of 2.5 hours on two things: Sex and gore. That's it. That's the whole content of this movie. It's apparently made to visually shock you, but it only shocked me in how poorly it was executed. Which leads me to my point of its irony: This movie has absolutely no SUBSTANCE.

You want a decent horror movie? Watch Pearl (2022).

reviews.author: NixSar

Maybe, just maybe, if the film were remade as a surrealist gorefest in the vein of Happy! Or Happiness, closer to its own last 30 minutes, we could talk about a solid and meaningful experience. As it is, it's a young teenager's rage against the machine without a coherent story, soul, humor, or point.

reviews.author: Hildebrando_Martins_Almeida
reviews.body:
"The Substance" (2024) is an experience that tests the limits of taste and patience. Marketed as a blend of body horror, the film is more of an exercise in extreme bad taste, with grotesque visuals and a narrative that borders on unbearable.

The story follows Elisabeth (Demi Moore), a fading celebrity who turns to an underground drug that creates a younger, enhanced version of herself, named Sue (Margaret Qualley). The concept, which could have been explored in an intriguing way, is lost in an execution filled with repulsive scenes, where the horror focuses more on visual impact than meaningful thematic development. Coralie Fargeat opts to emphasize every grotesque detail, from visceral transformation scenes to excessive close-ups that test the viewer's tolerance.

The film is not subtle in its critique of Hollywood's obsession with youth and unattainable beauty standards. However, its approach is so forced that it becomes irritating and exhausting. Themes of envy, self-image, and superficiality are handled with the delicacy of a hammer, turning what could have been a relevant commentary into something shallow and indigestible.

The performances of the actors also do little to save the film. Demi Moore and Dennis Quaid, both veterans with respectable careers, are trapped in shallow roles and embarrassing situations. Moore makes no attempt to bring dignity to her character. By accepting this role, knowing the type of grotesque narrative she would be tied to, she demonstrated an unforgivable lack of discernment. Beyond the ill-advised decision to join the cast of this deplorable film, Demi Moore had the courage to expose her aging body in nude scenes captured from multiple angles. This choice not only reinforces the overall discomfort of the work but also marks a lamentable decline in her career, leaving an impression so unsettling that, for me, it is hard to forgive. Quaid, on the other hand, seems lost in a grotesque, caricatured role. Margaret Qualley is reduced to a caricature of empty sensuality, reflecting the film's overall superficial approach.

The climax, described by some as "unforgettable," is a festival of blood and horrors that defies logic and common sense. For those who make it that far, the ending is a shocking display of horror that surprises and leaves a lasting impact, sealing "The Substance" as a work that fails on all fronts.

In summary, "The Substance" is a film that attempts to shock at any cost, but ends up being a combination of gratuitous vulgarity and narrative emptiness. It is not only a disappointment as a film but also a sad milestone in the careers of Moore and Quaid. For viewers seeking something more than gratuitous revulsion, it is best to look elsewhere.
