reviews.author: bertrandma
reviews.body:
Body horror is presently at its most fashionable and I am glad for it: first of all, because we are yet to realize quite how *weird* our embodied condition really is, and secondly because there is a tradition--a craft, really--to body horror special effects, lovingly hand-made with rubber moulds and cranberry juice, which today's ubiquitous digital gore never managed to equal.

The Substance was advertised as the next level in that field, and so I was quite receptive to its promises despite the mixed reviews. Ageing is a matter that preoccupies me, and although limiting the experience to physical change is probably quite reductive, I was nevertheless looking forward to this Verwandlung in reverse.

The first disappointment thus came with the treatment of 'body horror', which is far too abstract and digital to truly fits the bill. There are some good moments (the cumbersome materiality of the 'other self' is a great idea, for example), but on the whole the transformation is neither visually inventive nor particularly gripping.

The production is otherwise sleek -- good filming, nice sets, interesting props (the 'substance' kit and its marketing are delicious), and the sound is inobtrusive if also unremarkable.

But it suffers from the usual pitfalls of French conceptual horror: a sort of overconfidence in the profundity of its message, which in this particular case is really quite banal. (The montage of semi-surreal scenes reminded me oof Titane, without ever rising to its level.) Sparkle is willfully depicted as one-dimensional, and is therefore a difficult character to like: partly because of the agreeably sparse dialogues, but mostly because she has very little substance beyond here usage of substance. Because the protagonist is so hollow, the script has to make every other character into a caricature in order to get its message across. Although this is done with some measure of self-awareness, it still dumbs the whole thing down, and we end up oscillating between a fable and a music-video, whereas the director thinks it is a psychological drama.

The real problem however comes from the pacing. There's just not a great deal happening. Because it is a little self-important, the film is often quite predictable and even repetitive. It is in any case way longer than it needs to be.

reviews.author: natalilahidalgo
reviews.body:
The Substance takes on an important topic: the societal pressures and anxieties faced by aging women. It's a refreshing theme to see addressed, especially in a genre that so often ignores the real, lived experiences of women. This could have been a poignant and thought-provoking narrative.

Unfortunately, the execution misses the mark. Rather than exploring these themes with emotional depth or nuance, the film leans heavily into graphic and disturbing violence.

What saddens me most is that the film was both written and directed by a woman, which feels like a missed opportunity to challenge the more aggressive, stereotypically masculine approach to violence in film.

I believe that women filmmakers have the power to bring new voices, perspectives, and sensibilities to the industry. It's unfortunate that this film feels like a replication of the same shocking content that men often produce, rather than a challenge to it. Women need not imitate these extremes to make impactful, meaningful movies.

reviews.author: rebeccarush-48517
reviews.body:
The beginning and middle showed promise, but the end was absolute juvenile garbage. This could have been a powerful film with a message, but it devolved into a mess. This director had a chance to do something meaningful. Instead, she chose to spew a disgusting, dragged-out disappointment. The snake ate its tail here.

Demi Moore portrays a woman in her fifties who looses her glamorous job due to her age. She overhears her boss mocking her and referencing the audience as having lost interest in a woman who has, in his terms, lost her desirability. It is worth noting that Demi Moore, at her character's age of 50 something, is absolutely stunning. Still, the yearning for a return to youth drags her under.

This film could have challenged age discrimination, standards of beauty and the unattainable perfection we see in movies and even photoshopped selfies. Instead it took a wrong, amateurish gore angle and dismantled any credibility it had achieved.

reviews.author: jwcstorage
reviews.body:
I love horror. I love body horror. I'm a big fan of when actions have consequences. But I was quite unimpressed.

First, I agree with many of the things people say. Good casting for the two leads, great effects, interesting premise (though rather minimal).

However, I hated the "style" of the movie. It felt like someone fed "How to edit a movie like a Tiktok clip" into ai and then fed it the script and it dumped this out on the other end.

I dont care if a film has nudity or not, so long as its in service to this plot, which this was, and showing the change that happened was probably one of the best part of the film.

Unfortunately, the art direction, shots, and cuts were all very obnoxious and made me check the time to see how much of the movie was left. I didnt really notice at first but the movie is over 2 hours long, and before the midway point, I was expecting the plot to advance and things to begin to wrap up, but no, we were just getting started.

Much like this review, the movie overstayed its welcome and just kept going and going. About 70% the way through, I felt checked out and paused it for a while because it just wasnt hitting right for me.

I came back to finish it off, and was treated to some really great body horror, but it felt too little too late, and what followed felt ridiculous, and I'm not sure if that was a Deadpool reference right near the end or what.... and the ending felt gratuitous for gores sake.

I honestly dont understand the rave reviews of this flick, unless its due to the tiktok generation growing older and getting into horror movies and maybe thats why it didnt appeal to me.

reviews.author: hesnotdrunk
reviews.body:
This movie feels like a hollow, flashy shell of a Cronenberg film, stripped of all depth, realism, and character motivation. It starts with promise but quickly spirals into absurdity, each scene more nonsensical than the last.

The absurdity and over-the-top gore aren't the problem-it's the inanely repetitive visual motifs (eggs, food, over and over) and the emptiness behind the protagonist's baffling choices. Imagine experiencing only the downsides of "The Substance" without any benefits, yet still choosing to endure it. The story feels as if it was generated by an AI, concerned only with its glitzy concept of "accept aging with grace or suffer," but lacking any meaningful narrative or character development.

By the end, the film's central idea collapses into a shallow spectacle, interested in shock value more than substance. It's a frustrating reminder of the state of cinema when such poorly crafted work receives acclaim.

reviews.author: myburningplacenta
reviews.body:
Not great but acceptable build-up of 95 minutes but really destroying it in the last 45 minutes.

I cannot for the life of me find a reason for a director to take such a huge dump on his or - in this case - her own piece of art. And she did the same with her movie "Revenge". The general ideas and concepts in both films are promising but it seems as though the only way this director knows how to communicate trauma, fear of death, anger etc. Is through thousands of litres of fake blood and gore. Which is really sad because it feels like she wants to be "artsy" like Cronenberg or Lynch but she fails miserably. You don't become a great director by trashing your own work and spitting in the face of your audience over and over again. I'm not going to give anymore time of my life to anything this person does, it's simply a waste of time. I understand what she is trying to do and she fails to do it properly so thank you but NO thank you.

reviews.author: andraskallay
reviews.body:
The Substance is a film that manages to squander its premise with poor execution at every level. From the outset, the story feels disjointed, as though the filmmakers themselves weren't sure what they wanted to achieve. The pacing drags interminably, making its runtime feel like a punishment rather than an experience. The dialogue is stilted and often laughable, failing to evoke any emotional connection with the audience.

The acting is equally disappointing; the cast seems either under-directed or completely uninvested in their roles. The supposed horror elements lack creativity, relying on tired clichés rather than building genuine tension or fear. The cinematography and production design, while occasionally competent, can't redeem the glaring narrative flaws.

By the end, the film feels like an incoherent mess that offers neither entertainment nor insight. For anyone seeking a meaningful or thrilling cinematic experience, The Substance is an utter waste of time.

reviews.author: laradethomas
reviews.body:
Certainly! Here's a polished version of your review:

The Substance is a horror movie that lures you in with the promise of a Black Mirror-esque premise but quickly devolves into a baffling mess. The opening has a glimmer of potential, enough to catch your attention, but as the film progresses, you're left wondering: How did this movie get made? How did they secure funding and how did they get a studio to make it? And, perhaps most puzzling, how did they convince Demi Moore to sign on?

This is, without exaggeration, one of the worst movies I've ever seen. The ending, in particular, crosses the line into outright grotesque territory. It's beyond shocking-it's revolting.

I wouldn't recommend this movie to anyone. Spare yourself the time, the money, and the inevitable regret. Do yourself a favor and stay as far away as possible.

reviews.author: Humanesboy
reviews.body:
Watching this horrible movie is like going through some sort of descent to hell. The movie starts ok but there are some issues from the very beginning like the fact that its universe is a bit off (who works filming aerobic videos in 2024?) and it's over atomized, but the premise is interesting. You'll make the mistake of continuing watching.

Then worst thing that a movie can do is to create a universe that doesn't stand to itself. I won't criticize that the movie is not believable the same way I wouldn't criticize Star Wars because hyperspace traveling is not possible. The problem is that the movie doesn't make any attempt at creating any semblance of an internal logic. Who in gods heaven would subject itself to a procedure that creates a double of herself that has a totally independent life and takes 50% of your life? So her double is basically like any of the young actresses that are stealing her job! Well at least those don't steal days of her life.

Then, the science fiction is lazy and an Insult to any fan of the genre. Basically the procedure is done without any background or explanation and with instruments similar to a Covid test crossed with a juicero subscription.

After that we enter in the terrain of purely bad writing. Even the main character starts to become unlikeable and is basically impossible to empathize with anyone in the movie. The characters take utterly stupid decision that come from nowhere without justification.

It all ends in a one hour Cronemberg rip off mini movie that never ends and erases any semblance of depth or meaning from the movie. The saddest part is that the movie thinks it's actually being super hedgy and deep, when in reality is like if it was written by a 5 years old.

What bothers me the most is how the movie rips off other movies and styles, while pretending to be innovative and revolutionary. Maybe for someone who has never watched cinema.

The visual style is at times Kubrick and times like a rip of "Raw", a movie that its French director has probably seen. The body horror monsters are a copy of Cronemberg.

There are tones of movies that deal with these topics better!

reviews.author: sergiorossini
reviews.body: A dark comedy that overindulges in bad taste and leaves you questioning whether it's worth your time or not. reviews.author: shaunadam-39903
reviews.body: *The Substance* had potential, but it falls short. While Demi Moore and Margaret Qualley deliver strong performances, the film's bloated runtime of 140 minutes drags, with unnecessary scenes that add little to the plot. The body horror is over-the-top and often distracts from the more interesting themes of aging and identity. Inconsistent logic in how the "substance" works pulls viewers out of the story, making it hard to stay invested. Fargeat's stylish direction can't compensate for the film's lack of focus and coherence. Overall, *The Substance* disappoints despite its intriguing premise. Wouldn't recommend watching it, unless you have 2 hours to spare.

reviews.author: b_velkova
reviews.body: In just the past few years, movies like Pearl, Midsommar, and The Witch have brilliantly explored female-driven narratives within the horror genre, so this nonsense has no excuse. Even X (which, unfortunately, doesn't quite compare to its prequel, Pearl) offers more depth and manages to deliver at least a few scenes that resonate on a deeper level beyond mere shock value. The biggest delusion here, however, is the claim of an important, widely relatable theme. The film mocks women who are obsessed with their appearance and the fleeting admiration it brings, appealing only to self-satisfied audiences who want to demonstrate that this isn't a factor for them since they've supposedly discovered the true meaning of existence. But yes, in that sense, it really is a feminist movie, as promised, because that's what feminism does - it divides women and only validates those who live according to its rules.

reviews.author: moonspinner55
reviews.body: Upon learning she's being dumped from her weekly TV fitness program, aging Hollywood actress Elisabeth Sparkle (Demi Moore) is ready to try anything to get her youth and beauty back. She learns of a new, semi-secret program which promises the answer, "a better version of yourself" in the form of a cell-replicating liquid substance. When injected into the bloodstream, the substance produces (or rather, births) a younger version of the user--a curvaceous, wrinkle-free, buttocks-tight doppelgänger. There's just one catch: the user and the copy have to trade off their weeks of living on a strict seven-day schedule...with no exceptions. Perhaps taking her cue from 1988's "The Rejuvenator" (which in turn took its cue from 1959's "The Wasp Woman"), writer-director Coralie Fargeat has come up with a body-image horror story for the age-conscious 2020s. Fargeat, who appears to have been raised on David Cronenberg and John Carpenter movies, has the germ of a good idea here--and she's not without an over-the-top, cartoony sense of humor--but she's gross out-oriented instead of clever. As a result, "The Substance" is flashy and empty-headed, a splatter-flick designed to warn us *and* turn our stomachs. Moore and Margaret Qualley take some real chances here as actresses (Moore in particular); but, with limbs turning brown, teeth falling out, and blood dripping and spurting and spraying everywhere, this is not exactly a movie to show off your skills. *1/2 from ****

The bulk of the movie was a taut physiological horror story with an older star in conflict with a newer and better version of herself. The images pf her transformation are both shocking and realistic.

The movie lost me completely during the last 20 minutes. If you thought the projectile vomiting scene in "The Triangle of Sadness" was an artistic statement about modern society, then you will also appreciate the literal firehose of blood in this movie. reviews.author: Giuseppe_Silecchia
reviews.body:
The Substance (2024), directed by Coralie Fargeat, presents an intriguing premise that blends body horror with biting social commentary. The film follows Elisabeth Sparkle (Demi Moore), a former fitness icon past her prime, who turns to a black-market drug that allows her to temporarily transform into her younger, idealized self, Sue (Margaret Qualley). With a strict rule of alternating one week in each body, the story explores the pitfalls of obsession with youth and beauty. While the concept holds promise, the film's reliance on shock and gore ultimately undermines its thematic potential.

Demi Moore delivers a compelling performance as Elisabeth, capturing the desperation and vulnerability of a woman willing to risk everything to reclaim her glory days. Margaret Qualley brings an unsettling duality to Sue, embodying both the allure and the danger of the transformation. Dennis Quaid provides solid support, though his character's role feels underutilized in the broader narrative.

Visually, the film is striking, with Fargeat's direction leaning into surreal, grotesque imagery that mirrors Elisabeth's internal and external struggles. However, the excessive reliance on graphic violence and body horror overshadows the film's more thought-provoking elements. Rather than deepening the exploration of identity, self-worth, and societal pressures, the film frequently veers into gratuitous territory, leaving little room for subtlety.

The pacing also suffers from uneven storytelling, with a bloated runtime that dilutes the tension and focus. While the central concept is intriguing, its execution feels heavy-handed, missing the opportunity for a more nuanced exploration of its themes.

The Substance is best suited for viewers with a strong stomach and a penchant for provocative cinema, but its excessive truculence may alienate audiences looking for more balance between shock and substance. Despite its flaws, the film's performances and unique premise make it a memorable, if polarizing, experience.

Rating: 5/10. A bold but overly graphic exploration of vanity and transformation that sacrifices depth for shock value.

reviews.author: grinningelvis
reviews.body:
The Substance is meant to be a fable, exaggerating every beat for maximum irony and shock value. It doesn't really work as a satire or as a straight up horror movie and I'm not sure it's really trying to be either. It's simpleton body horror; a callback to lower-tier Cronenberg that manages to be more unappealingly preachy than contemplative, more sadistic than fantastical. It's obsessed with the grotesque because the construct is so thin that it has no other choice. A fable because, while the messages are quite clear, the execution is laughably broad.

The film is not particularly funny, insightful, or complicated and it begs the question as to whether it would merit much discussion at all were it not for the pedigree of its stars, Qualley and Moore. This is the type of torturous slog we expect from a director like, say, Lars Von Trier - the only difference being that Von Trier is often right on the nose with his targets. The Substance seems to think that the audience isn't able to see where its going, nor conceptualize complications beyond the obvious. So if this is meant to be a feminist screed or an ominous critique of self-obsession or the poisonous male gaze, The Substance seems to be a little naive about its targets. Anyone who doesn't get it will not be watching.

The Substance gets trapped by its own pretensions, existing neither in the real world nor the fantasy one it half-heartedly lampoons, so that by the time the audience turn into the villagers outside of Frankenstein's gates we find ourselves kinda understanding their point it view. There's nothing new here but the fact that a bunch of high-minded critics want to bestow praise on a lavish B-movie remake of Dorian Gray.

reviews.author: liakoos-ibiza-53226
reviews.body:
The Substance*, a film that attempts to explore themes of human obsession, body horror, and scientific ethics, left me utterly appalled and disgusted. While I appreciate the occasional unsettling film that provokes thought and challenges comfort zones, this movie crossed the line into pure exploitation. Its grotesque imagery, lack of coherent storytelling, and unnecessarily graphic scenes left a sour taste in my mouth. To say I didn't enjoy this movie would be an understatement-it was a truly horrendous experience.

A Weak and Confusing Plot

From the outset, *The Substance* struggles to establish a clear narrative. The story revolves around a group of scientists conducting experiments on a mysterious, gelatinous substance that seems to possess a mind of its own. While the premise could have been intriguing, the execution is chaotic and disjointed. Characters make inexplicable decisions, the pacing is uneven, and the dialogue feels forced and unnatural.

Instead of building tension or creating meaningful arcs for the characters, the plot devolves into a series of grotesque set pieces that seem designed purely to shock. The lack of emotional depth or relatability makes it impossible to care about the characters, their fates, or the supposed moral dilemmas they face.

Disturbing and Gratuitous Imagery

The film's greatest offense lies in its visual content. From the opening scene, it's clear that the filmmakers prioritized shock value over storytelling or artistic merit. The imagery is relentlessly grotesque, featuring scenes of body horror that are unnecessarily graphic and borderline nauseating.

The transformation scenes, where the substance takes over the human body, are particularly hard to watch. While body horror can be an effective tool in horror cinema, here it feels gratuitous and exploitative, as if the filmmakers were more concerned with grossing out the audience than delivering a meaningful or thought-provoking experience.

Themes Explored Without Nuance

The movie attempts to tackle themes such as scientific hubris, the consequences of tampering with nature, and humanity's fascination with power and control. However, these themes are handled with little nuance or depth. Rather than delving into the ethical questions surrounding the scientists' work, the film opts for cheap thrills and grotesque visuals.

The substance itself, which could have been a metaphor for addiction, power, or even the fragility of the human condition, is reduced to a plot device that serves no purpose other than to facilitate disturbing scenes. By the end of the film, the viewer is left wondering what the point of it all was.

An Unpleasant Viewing Experience

It's one thing for a movie to be disturbing-many great films are-but *The Substance* crosses the line into outright unpleasantness. The relentless focus on disgusting imagery and the lack of any redeeming qualities make it a chore to sit through. The film doesn't leave you with a sense of catharsis, reflection, or even a coherent message. Instead, it feels like an assault on the senses, leaving you uncomfortable and dissatisfied.

The sound design, which could have been used to build atmosphere and tension, is instead overly loud and abrasive. The score offers no respite, further amplifying the unpleasantness of the viewing experience.

Missed Opportunities

What's most frustrating about *The Substance* is that it had the potential to be an intriguing and impactful film. The concept of a mysterious, sentient substance is rife with possibilities, but the filmmakers squander this potential by focusing on shock value rather than meaningful storytelling. With a better script, more nuanced direction, and less reliance on grotesque visuals, the film could have been a compelling exploration of human ambition and the dangers of playing God.

Final Thoughts

In conclusion, *The Substance* is a film that I cannot recommend to anyone. It's horrendous, disturbing, and disgusting in ways that feel unnecessary and exploitative. While some may argue that the film is bold or provocative, I found it to be an unpleasant and hollow experience. There are far better films out there that tackle similar themes with far more sophistication and respect for the audience. Save yourself the discomfort and skip this one.

reviews.body:
This movie very obviously but very incompetently tries to mimic Stanley Kubrick in so many ways, that this ridiculous fact alone is probably the reason, why it is listed as "Dark Comedy".

However, in forcefully and constantly trying to achieve the unachievable, this movie falls short in basically every single aspect a movie could even become remotely worth watching.

The movie is repulsive to the extent, that one cannot even write a hopefully at least somewhat constructive review without the overwhelming urge to stop thinking about this movie immediately.

There seem to be some people who claim this movie to be art, because of the strong emotions this movie undeniably evokes. But seeing that literally the single emotion this movie evokes is disgust in its purest form, it would probably be fair to say that those are the same people that refer to "Two Girls, One Cup" as art.

In fact, it would be advisable to watch "Two Girls, One Cup" before or instead of watching this movie, as it offers a similar experience and conveys a similar message but without the dreadful "Wannabe-Kubrick" vibe.

In summary, "The Substance" is the movie that would have been made, if Kubrick with a very severe brain trauma would have produced "Two Girls, One Cup".

reviews.author: wellthatswhatithinkanyway
reviews.body:
STAR RATING: ***** Brilliant **** Very Good *** Okay ** Poor * Awful

Elisabeth Sparkle (Demi Moore) is an early morning fitness instructor on a national TV station, who's reached an age where she no longer fits the image of what the network chief, Harvey (Dennis Quaid) thinks the public want to see. When she learns of a mysterious serum called The Substance, she is given a number to phone and a place to go. After getting hold of the serum and injecting it, Elisabeth endures a supernatural transition into Sue (Margaret Qualley), a younger version of herself who takes over her spot on the morning fitness programme. Gradually, Sue takes over Elisabeth's life in a way she can't control.

There was a time, in the 90's, where Demi Moore and her willingness to bare herself on camera caused quite a stir. Comedian Paul Kaye, in the form of his comic persona Denis Penis, once memorably cornered her on the red carpet with the question: "Under any circumstances, if it wasn't gratuitous and was tastefully done, would you consider keeping your clothes on in a movie?" And now, after many years, she bares herself considerably again, in this wildly outlandish piece from writer/director Coralie Fargeat, that has gained some rave reviews for its wild outrageousness. But I have a feeling it's going to divide opinion.

The overriding theme seems to be of ageism in the world of the TV industry, and how women especially are made to suffer at the whim of always appearing young and appealing. The film also delves into the issue of the 'male gaze', with the key male characters appearing in close up through the lens of Moore's lead character. As the central character of the film, you just wish there was more depth to her beyond her surface level of 'wanting to look young again.' In his supporting role, Quaid (in a role intended for Ray Liotta before his passing) is a cartoonish obnoxious chauvinist, at times reminiscent of J. K. Simmons in Spider-Man. Qualley as her younger off-spawn feels the most natural, even in a fairly typical vacuous airhead role.

When the end (eventually) comes, it's all become a big far fetched mess, overlong and over-indulgent, with nods in set design and effects to horror classics like Hellraiser and The Shining, with arthouse pretensions to the likes of David Cronenberg. Its sheer outrageousness seems to have endeared it to many, but I think I need something with a little more 'substance.' **

reviews.author: minarandjelovic-41757

The plot is almost nonexistent, and disappointingly, the film seems to miss any chance at progressive themes, coming off as more outdated than empowering. Instead of exploring deeper ideas, Substance is all about shock, lacking any real substance to support it. I am extremely disappointed and I do not recommend this movie at all to anyone.

reviews.author: Kademan-02092005
reviews.body:
The Substance managed to give a strong setup, a darkly funny sense of humour, and satirically excessive tone. It also managed to be an over-indulgent, over-long, tonally confused, and blatant film.

From the opening shot alone the film introduces you to the premise, followed up by the lead as well, in mere minutes without having to exposit anything, and that efficient writing carries through for a large portion of the first half of the film. There's an excessive satirical use of contrast in physical attraction, mostly shown from Dennis Quaid's overly perverted perspective in Harvey on literally every woman he comes across. These are balanced out with uncomfortable close-ups of physical imperfections in several characters throughout as well. Moreover, the entire cast all provide extensively committed performances in matching the specific tone the film goes for in varying success. Demi Moore and Margaret Qualley are the easy stand-outs, with Moore being the more insightful and dramatic counterpart to Qualley's fantasy-like and dastardly manic performance. Furthermore, the film's structure was fantastically organised, split into thirds that get increasingly ridiculous in its messaging, acting, tone, and some really entertaining body horror that feels admittedly funny-yet-unnecessary-and-random in the third act. Also, the body horror is very much original and accomplishes building up an anxious amount of tension to its first effect, and then follows it up with build ups to excitement for the next twisted contortion to occur in practical gory glory.

However, it's the overall execution that really conjures frustrations against this movie's clear raw potential to be more effective. The transitions between thirds of the film feel more like jumping tones rather than logically shifting between them, especially in the third act. Elisabeth and Sue feel like they're capable of more than their characters or anyone else are really capable of, such as constructing a hidden room or figuring out extremely vague and almost non-existent instructions. And then there's also the runtime, which feels like it's more dedicated to hammering the obvious themes of male gaze and the cost of fame so far through your skull to a point where it feels unjustifiably lengthy, and could have really been a tighter, ever-so-slightly more subtle and effective film whilst still carrying it's blatant wit.

Overall, The Substance is a highly entertaining experience that promises much more substance than it ends up delivering, and on top of the distracting excessiveness, it results in a personally frustrating experience that I can't find as much enjoyment in as I'd like to.

reviews.author: piculiwar
reviews.body:
Watching The Substance (2024) is like being locked in a pretentious film studies class where everyone is trying way too hard to impress the professor. It's painfully clear that director Coralie Fargeat has binged Death Becomes Her one too many times, decided it wasn't "elevated" enough, and slapped a faux-intellectual gloss over the same general concept. But instead of being clever, satirical, or even remotely fun, we get two hours of self-indulgent drivel that looks like a final project from Film School 101.

The film practically screams its influences: every frame desperately apes the likes of Kubrick, Cronenberg, and Hitchcock. Except where those filmmakers brought nuance and innovation, The Substance brings... close-ups of gooey body horror that wish they were Cronenberg, symmetrical framing that begs you to think it's Kubrickian, and Hitchcockian tension so forced it snaps under the weight of its own try-hardery.

The dialogue? Imagine a bad parody of "deep" conversations but without the self-awareness to know it's bad. The pacing? Molasses in January. The characters? Cardboard cutouts of archetypes we've seen done better in actual films.

The worst offense is how utterly joyless the whole affair is. Where Death Becomes Her reveled in its campy absurdity, The Substance tries to smother you with its "message" about beauty and vanity-because apparently, we're too dumb to get it unless they beat us over the head with every shot and line. Subtlety is not in this movie's vocabulary.

I'll give it this: it's ambitious. But ambition without execution is just a waste of everyone's time. Watching The Substance was an experience, sure, but not the kind I'll ever want to revisit. If you're into pretentious student films with painfully obvious influences and zero originality, you might get something out of this. The rest of us will be rewatching Death Becomes Her instead.

The hype surrounding this production feels entirely manufactured, offering little substance to justify the attention it's received.

As for Demi Moore, the decision to award her a Golden Globe is baffling. While she's a talented actress, her minimal screen time-amounting to roughly 30 minutes-leaves her contribution feeling underwhelming and unworthy of such high praise. It seems more like a case of Hollywood politics and marketing spin rather than genuine recognition of exceptional artistry. Overall, this film is another example of style over substance, and it's best avoided unless you're curious to see what all the misplaced fuss is about.

reviews.author: shawnxfournier
reviews.body:
I kind of feel they 'yada yada-ed' most of the plot in a rush to get to the body horror. It feels more suitable as a longform YouTube project than a fully fleshed out film.

I don't think there's enough of a motivation for this character to be taking the substance at all. If her primary motivator is 'I feel I'm losing my luster with age', there's about 40 better alternatives before it would ever reach here.

I also don't feel enough performance coming from Demi Moore. I wasn't compelled to believe that this character even cares deeply enough about what people think of her now vs then because the 'then' was only a five second flashback in the intro that didn't even include her.

reviews.author: Rcketscientist
reviews.body:
I wish this wasnt rated so highly around Halloween. I would have missed it and been the better for it.

This has one of the best openings. A few poignant moments to silently set the stage for a concise horror-adjacent statement on Hollywood and the zeitgeist.

255 minutes later..wait two hundred and fifty f-n minutes? 255 minutes of my life?

Yah, this is a steaming pile of ----. Good opening, followed by odd fake hoo has. Lumbering, lingering. Confusing, meandering. Low budget, single set, groundhog-day plot. Wait, plot is generous.

It was brave of Demi Moore. I kinda, sorta guess. But don't do this to yourself. I went there so you don't have to.

reviews.author: aimtas
reviews.body:
The movie starts off great and I thought I was going to see a really good movie for the first time in a long time. Unfortunately, from about 45 minutes onwards it goes steeply downhill. The images become more and more disgusting, the atmosphere more and more unpleasant and I kept wondering whether I should switch off. Towards the end, the images are simply repulsive and sick. No "normal" person would want to see something like this. You have to have a taste for the disgusting.

I couldn't watch the movie to the end. Fortunately, I didn't.

Nevertheless, the movie is very well made. The actors and the pictures are great!

reviews.author: mustafaramiz
reviews.body: In the first 10 minutes, the movie manages to grab the audience's attention effectively, building anticipation and arousing curiosity about the unfolding story. The rapid pace and intriguing setup create a sense of excitement, drawing viewers in with the promise of an engaging plot. However, after this initial burst of energy, the film begins to slow down significantly, with the pace tapering off considerably. This shift leads to a noticeable dip in momentum, causing the narrative to lose its initial spark. As the film progresses, the plot becomes increasingly predictable, and the character development feels superficial and underdeveloped, failing to live up to the expectations set in the beginning. This dramatic shift in tone and pacing makes it difficult for the audience to stay invested in the story. Consequently, after the first segment, it becomes a challenge to maintain interest, and many viewers are likely to disengage or lose their connection to the film, as it no longer offers the same level of excitement or emotional depth that it initially promised.

reviews.author: terrylarosa
reviews.body: Let me start by saying that nothing affects me in movies with the possible exception when people drink coffee without sugar. So no the disgusting parts did not affect me. What did affect me was that anybody that's lucid and not into heavy drugs enjoyed this. I saw this at my wife's behest and we were unintentionally laughing at the end as to how ridiculous this was. The cinematography and editing were the most inept thing ever witnessed and this must be up there for worst directing. The award winning acting consisted of groaning in pain for most of the movie. If you enjoy closeups of Quaid's pores this is your dream movie. This movie has nothing to say except for people who need serious mental help or stop doing dangerous drugs. I'm astounded that this travesty is highly praised. Cronenberg would be horrified that this was given a green light and the people behind this should be ashamed. Absolute utter trash drivel.

reviews.author: Aiden_T
reviews.body:
This is why you should never trust imdb scores , this is the worst movie ive ever seen in every possible way and ive seen The room movie , this is worst than that avoid at maximum power youll thank me.

Well I'm rather speechless after seeing this horror, not in the sense scary but just plain horrible. Don't know why it won best original screenplay at Cannes, the story is terrible sorry to say. It starts off with a good premise but fails miserably at said execution. It is one of the worst movies I've ever seen, the ending is all together ridiculous and takes the cake for the dumbest movie endings of all time.

reviews.author: cheesebird
reviews.body:
I'd be lying if I said I wasn't actively sighing at certain points of the movie.

I think the technical work done to the movie is more than solid, the camera work, performances, music selection, is all well and good, no real complaints there.

The main issues I have are with the actual meat of the movie, the plot, dialogue, characters etc etc.

The concept and the ''commentary'' that the movie is going for, is far too basic for its own good. I get that the movie is a critique and satirical exaggeration of how people react to getting older. But it does almost nothing with it, you don't feel any real connection to the main character at all given that there was barely any build up to the actual ''Substance'' being provided to the mc.

To avoid going into deep spoilers, I was questioning the movie's own inner logics quite often and towards the end it just lost me completely. I'm not the first one to mention the ending. I went into the movie knowing the ending would be shaky, and uh.. yeah...

I'm giving it a 4/10 because its not completely awful, it does what it sets out to do, be a body horror movie about one's inner feelings towards getting older (particularly early seniors). But it barely does anything with it, and so a lot of the movie feels wasted. It doesn't convince you of its own rules which caused me to feel super indifferent towards it.

(for the record a 4/10 is not garbage, just means you don't think it's very good, but that there are qualities there. I know people nowadays think anything below a 7 is garbage but that's just not how ratings work)

reviews.author: zezgiacar
reviews.body:
Gaspard Noé, TEMU version. I wish I could give negative stars. The director attempted to mimic every major movie she's ever seen, only to produce pure nonsense. She might call it "inspiration," but I'd call it a failed attempt at imitation. What could possibly have been the purpose? I honestly doubt even the director knows. Simply disturbing the audience and evoking a sense of disgust without any story to back it up doesn't make for good cinema.

You leave the theater wondering, "What was that even supposed to be?" I seriously think you'd have to be 13 years old to appreciate this dumpster fire. What a shame-almost three hours you'll never get back.

reviews.author: criticcoleman-37694
reviews.body: As with most horror films of late, "The Substance" if a film that suffers from having a great hook with no follow through. It's simple tale of Demi Moore's aging actress seeking youth and discovering that true beauty has its own consequences takes what could have been a kick-ass thirty-minute "Tales From The Crypt" episode and turns it into an overblown two-hour and twenty-one minute uninspired mess of blood, bones and body parts. Plus the fact that this one was helmed by a woman may progressively bring the body image message home for some, but this one feels as surface and salacious as as ever. (And gonzo gore just for gore sake never feels fresh!) A film I don't fault folks for walking out of, this one is steeped in a substance called boring.

reviews.author: elmgee2008
reviews.body: This is undoubtedly the worst piece of modern cinema that I've ever had the misfortune to endure, and I've certainly seen more than my fair share. The leads must have been truly desperate to participate in this absolute travesty, as I can't see it doing them any real favours going forward. I'm at a complete loss as to how this garnered a single positive review, lethelone the majority. I suppose that just reflects the sad state in which the world as a whole finds itself in these days, psychologically. Absolutely no accounting for bad taste. I've seen much better films than this receive much less acclaim.

reviews.author: alexcuetodo
reviews.body: The movie premises are legit, but the development and the script lack common sense. As much as it is a horror story it would still need more logic in how the events came to happen. I'm not sure I liked it. Besides, the visuals are disgusting, and I can understand it has a purpose, but they're not made with that great quality as to amaze me. With this being said, the actors seemed to have delivered a serious attempt but nothing memorable whatsoever. In regard to the sound effect and music, it was nothing extraordinary although it added some novelty to the film. I assume the director was serious about this production, but it fell short to the expectations. Nice try!

reviews.author: csg-59027
reviews.body: I have been a fan of Demi Moore's since About Last Night almost 40 years ago. I thought this movie started off promising enough. Margaret Qualley is wonderful too but this film veers away from what could have been a study of aging and what choices women make to stay revelant and instead became a messy, gross horror film. Maybe I missed something the film was trying to say but I was so disappointed that Moore and Qualley were forced to show their bodies so frequently and gratuitously. For me, the film didn't care about making any statement about anything and just became a shock fest in the end.

reviews.author: blankyblank
reviews.body:
I do not understand why was there a need to make this longer than 2 hours. I don't think I've ever seen more unnecessary shots and scenes that drag on in one place. This story could've been told in 20 minutes. It's very predictable as well.

The message is ... you are beautiful as you? Accept yourself? The industry doesn't like women with wrinkles? Those concepts have been explored a million times already and in more interesting ways. Frankly I do not see the point of this film. And no, the technology wasn't explained at all. Who are these people? Why are they doing this? Nobody knows but look - a pair of breasts of a young woman, again. Psychological horror could've been interesting too but it's pushed to the side to make room for perky butts

I can see that this is a horror but it irks me when disgusting scenes are used just to be disgusting. There is no emotion nor impact other than 'ew' and that's cheap in my book. Even worse that the last 30 minutes are all pure disgust just because

In short - do not waste your time. It's not scary, it's not thought provoking, you will see the twist from a mile away.

reviews.author: bobjs36
reviews.body:
I was excited to watch this after reading the hype before it's streaming release. People were not walking out during the film because they were shocked. Thry walked out for other reasons. Read on.

First hour, amazing. Sucks you right in. Acting incredible. Demi on point. Soundtrack just right. Story odd but totally could imagine it. I can't even give more compliments because the ending just destroyed it.

The last 30 minutes or so just brought a major sense of let down. All the ways they could have wrapped this up it turned into an over the top gore fest. The story you get sucked into is gone and evolves into how much weirdness and gore can we pack in to the last 30 minutes. I know there are other reviews where people are grasping for some deep meaning in the end. As far as I'm concerned, there isn't one.

Such a let down and beyond disappointed. Wish I hadn't spent the money to rent it and glad I didn't force my husband to watch.

reviews.author: anotion
reviews.body:
A story that needed 15 minutes at most, stretched into a movie. The acting is great, as is the cinematography and visual design. The effects are OK. However, the movie neither disgusts properly nor connects. The "message" is overly simplistic and handled with very little nuance.

The premise starts of interesting, but quickly devolves into idiotic characters in an idiotic universe set against them. By the time it reaches its final 30 minutes it already overstayed its welcome.

I guess saying I was bored and unimpressed is an understatement.

It's all the depth of Barbie, but in a horror genre. Yaaaaaaawn.

reviews.author: GlamMetalHead
reviews.body:
This is another one of those movies that starts good...then goes off the rails. One of those movies wherein people are going to say how great it was and any of you idiots who are not smart enough to 'get it' are just wrong.

Yes...I got the Carrie influence.

Yes...I got the drug influence.

Yes...I got the societal issues nonsense.

This was just bad.

There is nothing else to say about the last quarter of this movie. The special effects are nonexistent (by design), the protagonist isn't believable, our feelings for the main character are not redeemed, nada...

One of the biggest disappointments ever.

reviews.author: deb-47040
reviews.body:
I didn't even know this movie was a thing until I saw Demi Moore get a Golden Globe award

So I decided to check it out. In all fairness, I have never really cared for her acting or persona, and although this started out strong it failed 1/2 through.

The premise reminds me of a Stephen King novel and then it just got stupid. I don't mind gore and violence but this movie just went all out to be gross. I really didn't identify with any of the characters, Demi was just so so and Her twin Qually? Was a but better but not much.

I really didn't have sympathy for either of the characters and Dennis Quaid and his over the top acting was just too much.

reviews.author: rogerioparra
reviews.body:
The story was well developed but the first 20 minutes and the last 10 minutes destroyed the work. The plot of the desire of an eternal life was well explored.

The practical effects and makeup would surprise in the 70's, but today they seemed ridiculous. The CGI was poor and it could be done by anyone's pc at home.

Demi Moore acting was good but we can clearly see how uncomfortable she was under those non-sense costumes, "The Substance" had a blood bath that was clearly fake and useless. Maybe the director was thinking about Carrie or Kill Bill, but the blood bath in those films matched the story. Here it served only to trash the film.

reviews.author: kaitlynnegibson
reviews.body: Please save yourself and your time.. I was so hopeful after the nominations but this is actually the absolute worst movie i've ever watched. It's one of those movies that just makes your scream at the screen with anger and doesn't even have a good plot halfway through. Spare yourself. The movie. Please spare yourself the money, time and interest. I legitimately could not rate this movie worse. PS- I never review movies and am going out of my way to review this one to save you and your loved ones time. I'm only still writing to meet the character limit for a review. This movie is terrible and I want my time back.

reviews.author: agibson-97396
reviews.body: This movie was probably one of the worst I seen in a long time. It started off with so much potential and then got ridiculously ridiculous. My husband kept looking at each other like "this cannot be the same movie that started." The last half was so hideous (and when I say hideous... it was hard to watch). I guess it's classified as a horror flick, but to me, it was so ridiculous I had to almost laugh. It was like a child wrote it and did the costumes/makeup. And the amount of nudity in the beginning was also ridiculous- like borderline you know what rhymes with corn. So I'd say out of the entire movie, I could only watch/stay entertained for like 20-30 minutes? Hot mess. Whatever you do, do NOT spend money renting it. If you really want to watch it, wait til it's free. And then get ready to wonder how they heck this movie is rated anything over a 4.

reviews.author: mark222-540-320903
reviews.body:
I'm so sorry. Admittably I'm not a horror film fan, but this was pure awefulness. Just lots of vanton gore in front of a simple idea that can be expressed very simply. Base a whole film on it just leads to something like this. I felt like I was watching a race for the stupidest idea and the most disgusting visuals. Yet not well made as the contraptions were clearly artificial and not very natural-looking. So "have a stupid idea, make present it badly and you win". I'm really worried about our world seeing that anyone rated this with more than 1 star. The minds that created this must be very sick.

I am not going to spend more time reviewing as it is not worth it, but I feel like a minority of seriously sick people of this world have rated this while the ones with average inteligence and more have been so disgusted that they would not even give a minute of their time. Well, I do want to warn others.

This film would not have made it to even a video tape D release in those days when video tapes were the rage.

Then again, maybe I'm just not understanding art...

reviews.author: happyjam
reviews.body: Themes, acting, visuals, even the blaring score, everything was over done- scenes drag on and on and onnnnn leaving you wishing it would just end already. The overall message is conveyed with all the subtlety of s sledgehammer. The acting is so overdone-again going for over-the-top instead of believability to ram home the "message" (we got it already!!!). The gross-out, repetitive "body-horror" visuals and wet squelching sound FX dragged on and on ending up being very dull. It's just nonstop and as a result becomes boring. I won't reveal any spoilers regarding the ending which dragged on for well over thirty needless minutes, but our audience was laughing and in not a good way. It was derisive, mocking laughter with a lot of shaking heads. The "new years show" left me feeling assaulted it was so gawd awful and tedious. I just wanted it to be over, but no!!!; here's another half hour of pointless grotesque mess masquerading as a movie with a "message". While I can admire Demi Moore's guts for taking on such a role in theory- this certainly didn't do her any favors in the end. It's Death Becomes Her meets The Thing (with none of their artistry) meets every schlocky poorly executed "horror" film from the 80's you can imagine. Visual "Nods" to much better films such as Carrie and The Shinning are again delivered with zero subtlety and are so blatantly obvious it's eye rolling. A tedious, horrible experience.

reviews.author: fsmith-32549
reviews.body:
This could have been an amazing movie about science and medicine and the ever-present issue with human morals. Indeed, for the first 70% of the movie, the story is quite good and very engaging. Then it seriously derailed into a D- attempt at being a horror flick, as if the script had been given to a middle-school aged kid with a head for gore to finish up. What a shame.

That means this is primarily a vanity piece for Demi Moore to.show off off her 62-year-old naked body over and over and over. Her body may be taut, but it still doesn't pass for that of a 50-year-old. That's the age of the character she is supposed to be playing.

Such a disappointing use of more than 2 hours of my time.

reviews.author: zorroaca
reviews.body: At first I thought it was a shallow movie... like even though Debbie is an older woman... she's not that bad for her age. Then I thought it was more about tits and ass in general and I was wondering what the value was since you can google all the tits and ass that you want these days that is a lot more graphic than what was presented here. Then I thought it was a parity on the women in our society today... I have never seen more makeup used in my life... you see a monster in the store and then... oh my god,,, is that the same cute girl I saw here the other day.... but now she is all made up... then I understood the movie. But why they made it so morbid at the end,,, I have no idea.

reviews.author: J_Andrew_Evans
reviews.body: This film had made its point within the first 30 minutes, certainly the first 60, and I felt from that point in it was simply (and rather gratuitously) working out the consequences which were blindingly obvious. In that it suffered from the problem with most films in the horror genre - it became boring and utterly predictable. One is then left with just enjoying (or suffering) the.superfluous and unnecessary voyeurism. Very sad working out of a film whose point was utterly valid and needed a more thoughtful and.constructive treatment. I was attracted by the implicit criticism of the "Beauty" industry and all I got was a voyeuristic journey which added little to its cure point.

reviews.author: kjohn-77891
reviews.body:
Now if i was going to score this movie for the first two hours it would get a 7 or 8 out of 10 but I was so shocked at how bad the last twenty minutes went, my score will be a 3.

Demi Moore was brilliant in it and it was good to see her in a horror film, maybe this is her new niche in the movies.

Then there was Magaret Qualley, hope i spelt that right, who was sexy with a capital S.

This film was so good that by the last twenty minutes I wondered what happened to the script and what on earth did they think that they were doing, really.

A person in a rubber suit meant to keep your attention and make you think this movie was still going to be brilliant, wrong.

SACK THE SCRIPT WRITER.

Whoever wrote this script needs to be sacked they ruined what could have been the best movies of this year.

3 stars for the last twenty minutes which ruined the whole movie.

reviews.author: movies_are_life_
reviews.body:
The Substance truly lacked substance. It takes a basic premise and chooses to ignore making sense in order to flail about for 90 minutes too long just for the sake of being adored as something more than it is. I think back to horror anthology films of the past and enjoy stories that felt perfect for having shorter runtimes. They didn't need to say much to get their point across. I got the point in this, but then had that point hit over the head scene after scene.

Starting off with the good, the technical aspects of the film were all very well done, especially that of the practical body horror effects. Acting is fine. The script is fun, albeit amateurish with its dialogue and predictability. I did find myself asking questions that the script never bothered to care about answering. A laundry list of questions could fill this entire review, but a few random ones are why did no one notice that Sue was Elizabeth from 40 years ago? Or is it 30 years? The exercise show seems to have come from the 80's, but the movie timeline suggests it's from the 90's. Harvey is the "bad" guy because he doesn't wash his hands and eats sloppily. Other than that, he's a saint for allowing a has-been star headline a show that assuredly has been at the bottom for years. I kept waiting for him to blackmail Sue, but he's as nice as can be. Sue is a master carpenter. Elizabeth becomes a stay at home recluse...because. No, I do not want the answer to these questions to be that I'm overthinking it or it's art that is saying something. I get what it's saying and I was bored since it couldn't say anything more.

There's a hidden 45 minute movie that would be a lot of fun in a Creepshow segment. I think anyone who praises the film is okay with the other 90 minutes being filler. This film wont work for an average audience who don't like things that get too exploitive, gross, weird, but that's not me. I love these types of films. But I also love when they know their limits and/or know how to keep a movie tight if they are willing to cross the basic grounds of the body horror aspect. This one meanders over the same plot and makes decisions that go off the rails without having reasons to back up these decisions.

reviews.author: Sancler
reviews.body:
This could've been great... if it weren't such man-hating drivel.

Chapeau to Demi Moore for exposing herself in such a vulnerable way. Really, that took some guts... pun intended.

Unfortunately, these days such a role can not come without the casual man-hating drivel. Oh, except of course for hotter young guys. Otherwise, it would've been a great flick. Movies like this always try to send a message, but end up making it way worse for those who they're trying to make a case for. To anyone with a brain at least.

Look, I get it, I as well feel 20 years younger than I look, but it's absolutely possible to make movies like this without alienating entire demographics.

reviews.author: huddleboardgolf
reviews.body:
This movie started off amazingly well. Very exciting and intriguing.

A note of Demi Moore, what an incredible career she's has and she is still smashing it, and looks unbelievable for 62.

In the first half of the movie, Qualley is great too.

The movies just continues to develop in utter, utter madness. It's like some one started with a script for a movie and had to quit half way through developing it. Then they decide to give it to the dog to finish off. Then they put that part of the script through a shredder. Then the decided to film it.

It is genuinely up there with the worst movies I've ever watched.

reviews.author: PeteRockCLSmooth
reviews.body:
This is my very first IMDb user review, I created an account here for this to warn you to not watch this movie.

I was aware of the mixed user reviews, but I wanted to make up my own mind. This was big a mistake.

Let's start with the positives: the old cinema popcorn and the advertisements prior the movie.

Story? None. Character development? Zero. Plot holes? Plenty. Gore level? Too much.

I think the worst of all was that I left the cinema in a negative mood, this never happened to me before.

Conclusion: It's the worst movie I've ever seen in my life. Any cheap horror movie is better than this one.

reviews.author: VinsendVega
reviews.body:
The first half of this movie is really good. I liked the story, the acting was very solid and the cinematography was looking great. (Halfway trough I would have rated this movie an 8/10) In the second half things start to spiral out of control, this is necessary and expected for the story.

However the the way they have chosen to portrait this go's from chaotic to absolutely disgusting, disturbing and somehow at the same time boring... It was not scary, not funny, not necessary and It made us lose all intrest in finishing this movie. We did finish it and and both of us wished we had turned it of halfway.

PS: I've enjoyed many horror movies with a lot of blood and gore, but none where as pointlessly over the top and stretched out as in this movie. Mandy (2018) comes close in terms of blood and chaos, but at least there, it some action going on.

reviews.author: dadadaaa
reviews.body: While attempting to pass as a commentary on modern society, this film feels like an undercooked idea rather than a fully developed story. The plot is cheap and predictable, with a script that lacks any memorable dialogue or moments that would draw the viewer in. The whole production feels more like an outline than a fleshed-out film, leaving much to be desired in terms of character development and depth. Robert Rodriguez's re-make, with european fixation on societal critique comes across as forced and superficial. For fans of B-horror, much better examples from the 80s come to mind, films that were campy yet managed to entertain and surprise with innovative storytelling and genuine thrills. In comparison, this movie feels derivative and lacks the creativity that once defined the genre. Overall, a disappointing watch. No.

reviews.author: indiana1981
reviews.body:
I feel so annoyed with this movie. The first 1 hr and 20 mins is great. Literally most of the entire movie, until Sue's fate is established. The acting, the story, the cast, the sets, the shots, the sound design, everything! Is a 7/10 for me.

And the movie becomes stupid, dumb and over the top in the last 20 mins. Why???! Why did you have to just ruin in? You could have ended the movie so much better, with less stupidity and more seriousness. There was no horror in the last act, just literally wtf. Ruined the entire film. I don't understand why so many reviews are just glossing over, how the movie just turned into dumb comedy at the end.

reviews.author: charleskwaters
reviews.body:
A Movie with Promise, but It Fell Apart

I was really excited to see this movie. The theme sounded right up my alley, and from the trailers, it looked like it would deliver something different. I had high hopes, and honestly, it started off strong. The cinematography was excellent-beautiful shots, good lighting, and a solid atmosphere. It felt like the kind of movie that would be deep, meaningful, or at least thought-provoking. For a while, I was hooked.

But then it all went off the rails.

What started as a promising film slowly turned into something silly, almost like the filmmakers forgot what they were trying to do. Instead of sticking with the theme and letting it unfold naturally, the movie took a hard turn into bizarre territory. Out of nowhere, there was graphic disfigurement and weird body horror stuff that seemed to exist just to shock the audience. Now, I can appreciate a movie that pushes boundaries, but here, it felt random and out of place-like the story got lost along the way.

At some point, I found myself thinking, What am I even watching? Instead of being clever or meaningful, the movie just seemed to rely on cheap tricks. It wasn't scary, emotional, or funny-just odd for the sake of being odd.

And let's talk about the ending. Imagine a movie that builds up to some kind of climactic moment, only to throw that all away with a scene that felt like it belonged in a David Cronenberg film. I won't spoil too much, but it ends with a solitary, disfigured face walking down the street, and... that's it. The whole thing left me confused, and not in a good way. It was more like the filmmakers ran out of ideas and decided to be weird just to leave the audience with something to remember.

If I wanted to watch something surreal like that, I'd just watch a Cronenberg movie. At least his films have some deeper meaning behind the weirdness. This one? It felt like the writers just threw stuff at the wall to see what would stick.

Who's This Movie For?

To be fair, I could see some people enjoying this-if you don't take it seriously. This might be a fun one to throw on if you're hanging out with a group of friends, especially teenage boys who don't mind goofy body horror and the occasional topless scene. The silliness, random violence, and shock value could make for an entertaining night if you're watching it just to laugh at how ridiculous it is.

But if you're looking for something serious or meaningful? Skip it. I went in hoping for a movie that would have some substance, something that would leave me thinking about it afterward. Instead, I got a mess of random ideas that didn't go anywhere. It felt like a bait-and-switch-the kind of movie that acts like it's going to say something important but ends up just wasting your time.

reviews.author: jcollum06
reviews.body:
"The Substance" (2024) is a disappointing and monotonous film that fails to live up to its ambitious premise. Despite the intriguing title and the potential to explore thought-provoking themes, the movie delivers a painfully boring and uninspired experience that leaves viewers feeling frustrated and unfulfilled.

First, the narrative structure of "The Substance" is deeply flawed. The plot moves at a glacial pace, with minimal character development and an overall lack of cohesion. The movie sets up interesting ideas regarding a mysterious, potentially world-altering substance, but instead of delving into the intricacies of its impact on society, science, or human nature, the script meanders through aimless dialogue and repetitive scenarios. The film drags through scenes that add little value to the overarching story, making it hard to stay engaged.

The characters in "The Substance" are poorly written and lack any real depth. The protagonist, who should be the emotional and intellectual center of the film, comes across as one-dimensional and uninteresting. We never truly understand their motivations or the personal stakes involved, leaving viewers with little reason to care about their journey. The supporting cast fares no better, with characters serving as mere plot devices to move the story forward without contributing any meaningful substance (ironically) to the film.

The pacing is another major flaw in "The Substance." Long, drawn-out sequences are padded with unnecessary exposition, and there's a noticeable lack of urgency in a film that should feel high-stakes. Moments that could have been tense or suspenseful are instead dull and predictable. The lack of a clear, engaging conflict throughout the movie makes the plot feel directionless, with viewers left wondering when, if ever, the story will pick up.

Visually, "The Substance" also fails to impress. While some sci-fi films manage to mask weak storytelling with impressive visuals or compelling world-building, this film does neither. The cinematography feels uninspired, relying on generic shots and a bland color palette. Any attempts at special effects or futuristic elements fall flat due to the film's apparent lack of creativity and production value. In a genre that often thrives on imagination and spectacle, "The Substance" remains visually unremarkable.

One of the most frustrating aspects of the movie is its wasted potential. The core idea of a mysterious substance that could change the world is intriguing, and in more capable hands, it could have been explored with complexity and depth. However, "The Substance" squanders this premise by opting for a bland, paint-by-numbers approach that leaves important questions unanswered and key themes underdeveloped. Instead of diving into philosophical or ethical dilemmas, the film takes the easy route, avoiding anything that might challenge its audience intellectually.

The dialogue is similarly uninspired, with characters exchanging lines that feel stiff and mechanical. Rather than fostering meaningful conversations or raising important questions about the substance's significance, the dialogue often feels like empty filler, further exacerbating the film's overall blandness. It's hard to stay invested in a movie when the characters themselves seem to have no interest in what's happening around them.

In conclusion, "The Substance" (2024) is a prime example of wasted potential. What could have been an exciting, thought-provoking sci-fi thriller turns out to be a dull, uninspired slog through a poorly executed story. With flat characters, poor pacing, uninspired visuals, and a script that fails to engage, "The Substance" is a movie that ultimately feels like a chore to watch. If you're looking for a compelling sci-fi film, this is one you should definitely skip.

reviews.author: brentsbulletinboard
reviews.body: There's a big difference between being funny and being laughable, yet the latest from writer-director Coralie Fargeat has somehow found a way to be both. After amassing a considerable amount of largely well-earned cinematic goodwill in the film's opening segments, the picture mercilessly squanders that support in the final act with an overlong, meandering, disgustingly gratuitous and grotesque exhibition of utterly bad taste. This story of an aging actress (Demi Moore) who seeks to revive her career by retrieving some of her lost youth with the aid of an enigmatic injectable follows her grand misadventures when the mysterious substance prompts the emergence of a younger doppelganger (Margaret Qualley), who becomes a Hollywood sex kitten sensation virtually overnight. To make this experimental venture work, however, the two individuals must follow a complex set of rules, dictates that become increasingly difficult to follow as they each vie for their respective shares of attention. And, as this scenario unfolds, tension grows between them, leading to complications and unexpected developments that become progressively harder to manage. But that's where what works in the film ends. As the story plays out from there, it becomes stupendously absurd, and, even though there are some hearty laughs in this, there are even more ridiculously implausible and unexplained occurrences that try audience members' patience and tolerance, so much so that I couldn't wait for this trainwreck to end. In addition to the foregoing shortcomings, the film includes myriad changes in tone, making it difficult to determine whether this is supposed to be a serious thriller or a campy road, very much in the same way as in the incomprehensible French offering "Titane" (2021). It also shamelessly "borrows" elements from other movies in various ways, most notably imagery and narrative references from "The Shining" (1980) and "Young Frankenstein" (1974), costume designs from the "Hunger Games" franchise, and bafflingly inexplicable soundtrack excerpts from films like "Vertigo" (1958). Then there's the picture's obvious, heavy-handed message about the perils of misogyny, observations that, as important as they are, could easily stood to have been turned down more than a few notches (yes, we get it already). At the same time, though, there are also some fundamentally innate questions about the narrative that go wholly unanswered, leaving us with numerous head-scratching moments. Sadly, these failings detract significantly from the elements that do work (at least early on in the film), such as the fine performances of Moore and Qualley, the picture's inventive cinematography, and a central premise that could have made for an engaging story if handled with greater finesse. But these strengths are effectively cancelled by what ultimately results when this release goes off the rails. Indeed, how "The Substance" captured the 2024 Cannes Film Festival award for best screenplay is truly mind boggling. I'm certainly a fan of the weird, wild and wacky, but this release undermines the virtues of those cherished qualities. Regrettably, I was seriously looking forward to seeing this offering, and I was decidedly impressed by what I saw in its opening acts, but that was all wiped out by how this one ultimately played out, a picture that, in the end, ironically relied more on style than "substance."

reviews.author: zubinmistry13
reviews.body:
This so called movie is not even worth my time talking about it. So many holes in the story. An insult to even the grotesque cinema.

Despite its ambitious premise of exploring society's obsession with youth and beauty, The Substance falls flat in execution, delivering a convoluted narrative devoid of meaningful depth. The plot, centered on Demi Moore's character, Elisabeth, an aging fitness guru experimenting with a black-market drug to restore her youth, is weighed down by inconsistent messaging and a script riddled with cliches. What begins as an intriguing commentary on ageism spirals into chaotic body horror that feels more grotesque than purposeful.

Director Coralie Fargeat attempts to tackle serious issues like corporate misogyny and societal double standards, but her approach is heavy-handed and tone-deaf. Critics noted that the film's portrayal of women often reinforced the very stereotypes it sought to challenge. The exaggerated body horror and over-the-top visuals lack nuance, culminating in a blood-soaked finale that feels like an empty provocation rather than a cathartic resolution.

Adding to the frustrations, the movie's setting and character actions often defy logic. From characters inexplicably walking everywhere in sprawling Los Angeles to bizarre, unrealistic depictions of the Hollywood landscape, the film frequently alienates viewers. Demi Moore's performance is one of the few redeeming qualities, but even her talents are undercut by the poor material.

reviews.author: louisemarieperry
reviews.body:
I really wanted to like this movie, but it ultimately fell flat for me. While visually striking, the sustained body horror was overwhelming and difficult to sit through.

The film relied heavily on long, drawn-out scenes and panning shots of semi-naked bodies, workout routines, and lingering stares, with very little dialogue to drive the story forward. While I appreciate the underlying message about aging gracefully and the impossible beauty standards imposed by Hollywood and society, the execution felt underdeveloped.

At over two hours, the runtime was excessive-what it tried to say could have been accomplished in 90 minutes. Unfortunately, the lack of character development made it hard to connect with the story. Characters escalated their actions too quickly, which might have been intentional, but it felt unconvincing and left the film feeling untethered.

Though the voyeuristic nature of the film might have been a deliberate commentary, it missed the mark for me. I'm still puzzled by the high praise it has received. Despite its ambitions, it left me feeling disappointed.

reviews.author: Sellenslave
reviews.body:
Review of The Substance

The Substance was hands down one of the worst movies I've seen in a long time. It's almost impressive how bad it managed to be, considering the potential it had. The whole thing is a chaotic mess from start to finish, with a storyline that feels like someone slapped together a bunch of random ideas and hoped it would work. Spoiler: it didn't.

What Was Even the Plot?

Let's start with the plot-or whatever that was supposed to be. The movie tries to do too much and ends up doing nothing well. You sit there, waiting for something to happen, something to make sense, and it never does. It's like they had a cool concept, then completely lost track of it halfway through filming. The scenes just drag on, with no point, no buildup, no tension. It's like watching paint dry, except at least with paint drying, you know what the end result will be. Here? No clue. I have no idea what they were trying to say with this movie.

Sue: The Only Good Thing

Now, let's talk about the one thing that made sitting through this dumpster fire somewhat bearable: Sue. She's literally the only reason I didn't turn it off halfway through. Her character actually has some depth and her acting is pretty solid, which is more than I can say for anyone or anything else in the movie. Sue is what kept this movie from being a total loss. It's like she knew she was in a terrible movie but decided to show up and do her best anyway. I'd watch a spin-off with just her, honestly. She deserves better than this mess.

The Special Effects Were... There

Visually, it's like they wanted to throw in some cool effects to distract us from how bad everything else was. But it didn't work. Yeah, there were a few moments that looked okay, but who cares when the rest of the movie is so painfully bad? You can't just throw a bit of CGI at the screen and expect people not to notice how terrible the story is. After a while, even the effects just get boring because there's nothing holding them up. It's like they spent all their money on visuals and completely forgot they were supposed to make a movie with an actual plot.

A Wasted Opportunity

What really makes The Substance even more frustrating is that it could have been good. The basic idea was there, but they did absolutely nothing with it. They could've explored some interesting themes or given us a story that made us think. But no, instead we got this hollow, confusing mess that doesn't seem to know what it's trying to be. It's one of those movies that just leaves you angry because you know it could've been so much more if they'd just put in a little effort.

Final Thoughts: Just Don't

Honestly, I can't recommend The Substance to anyone unless you want to waste two hours of your life. It's not scary, it's not thought-provoking, and it's definitely not fun. Save yourself the frustration and watch something else-literally anything else. The Substance is a total disaster, and I'm genuinely annoyed I wasted my time on it.
