reviews.author: johnnymartian
reviews.body:
No, it won't put Cronenberg to shame. It's way too dumb to do that.

No, it's not Demi Moore's magnum opus. GI Jane might be.

No, it's not the "most insane movie experience this year/ever". It's "insane" in an infantile way, without ever being truly disturbing. Its "insanity" is confusing at best.

No, the gore won't make your stomach turn. It's too cartoonish, mild, imitative, and unfocused for that.

I've read quite a few reviews focusing on the movie's messages, raising them above the actual qualities that make a memorable movie experience. The message is banal, and gets extremely repetitive.

My main gripe with the movie is that it's emotionally flat, primarily due to treating its characters as gross stereotypes. Demi Moore is heavily underutilized here, being pushed into an evil witch role half way through. The screenwriter did her a disservice by stripping here of any kind of palpable humanity. While the movie is a grotesque, it gives no inner complexity to the main actors, making them hard to sympathize with.

Stylistically, it's confusing, as the numerous close ups, macro shots and slow mos become overwhelmingly irritating and simply awkward. The several homages to other movies are just bafflingly out of place.

As much as throwing the right ingredients in a pot doesn't make you a good chef, casting good actors, and having an interesting concept doesn't make you a good filmmaker.

In short - this is a wasted opportunity.

reviews.author: foxtografo

I was so hyped on this movie, everyone seemed to be impressed and shocked by it. Some raving about it as a masterpiece, some said it was so "well rounded" as a film.

I have to say, I'm very disappointed on it.

Besides the shock factor (based on pure disgust), I didn't get much more from this film. The premise seems to be interesting, but it falls very flat as the movie advances.

The pace dragged big time for me, I know lots of people will say "whaaaat??!!" because the film feels intense at all times, but what made me feel bored is the repetitive scenes, so redundant, it could definitely lose like 40 minutes run and it would say the same, more efficiently.

Besides the bold roles the main actresses had to play, I preferred Moore over Qualley. Quaid was very good on his role, obnoxious but exaggerated to the point it was funny.

I didn't really enjoy the performances that much, maybe not because of their acting skills, but I found most of characters very obnoxious and unlikeable, but everyone pushed to the overacting side. Problem with the direction, I'd say..

The obvious hate for old white male in this movie is so annoying and insulting, I really can't take any more of this so called "feminism" extreme prejudice, in reality cheap, trendy misandry. Sure not that many know that word, the one everyone likes is misogyny.

Don't get me wrong, I've always respected and defend equality for EVERYONE, gender, race, sexuality, religion, etc, but this extreme, constant attack against all man is so tiring, specially in cinema, that has lost all my respect.

On the "positive" side, I have to say it really works on the gross shock of body horror. The practical effects and makeup are very well done.

The cinematography seemed uneven, good most of the time, with distorted wide angle takes and lots of lense effects, but more than a few shots looked quite cheap..

Quite a lot of inconsistencies in the story, one that bothered me is how the main character is able to move in certain points of the story, it really felt like the "realism" of the film was lost or forgotten and it took me out of the experience. But there are enough of these inconsistencies all along the movie which bothered me ruining the whole thing.

The ending felt like a massive cliché to me, almost a roll-eye one, bizarre yes, good? Not necessarily.

That actually apply to the whole movie, again: bizarre yes, good not necessarily.

Well overrated movie, I wouldn't watch it again, and I'll certainly avoid this director, since I neither liked her previous film.

reviews.author: SteevoCanuck
reviews.body:
*The Substance* is a movie that tries to blend genres but ends up feeling like a Frankenstein monster of mismatched tones, incoherent plotting, and a third act so absurd it feels like a parody of itself. The film's initial setup shows some promise-what could have been a compelling psychological thriller quickly derails into a muddled mess that doesn't know if it wants to be a horror film, a sci-fi mystery, or a dark satire. By the end, it's none of these things.

The tone shifts are jarring to the point of distraction. One minute, we're supposed to be invested in the serious, slow-burn dread of the protagonist's unraveling mind, the next we're thrown into goofy comedic bits or over-the-top body horror that feels entirely out of place. Instead of building tension, the film keeps undercutting itself with these bizarre tonal swings, leaving the audience confused about how they're supposed to feel. Is this supposed to be terrifying? Funny? Thought-provoking? Who knows-certainly not the filmmakers.

But the real crime here is the third act. It goes completely off the rails, abandoning any semblance of logic or narrative coherence. Characters make baffling choices, motivations that were previously hinted at disappear altogether, and the story seems to be actively trying to undermine whatever sense of tension it had built. By the time the film's big twist arrives, it's less shocking and more laughable, like something out of a bad student film. The climax, which seems to have been dreamed up in a late-night brainstorming session fueled by too much caffeine and too little thought, makes you wonder if the writers gave up halfway through and decided to just see how weird they could get.

The problem with *The Substance* isn't that it's trying to do something different; it's that it has no idea what it's trying to do at all. It's a mishmash of half-baked ideas and tonal whiplash, culminating in a finale that leaves you more annoyed than entertained. This is a movie that thinks it's being bold and provocative but ultimately ends up feeling like a joke-and not a particularly funny one. If you're looking for a film that makes you question your life choices, by all means, give *The Substance* a watch.

reviews.author: Cyns-Corner

I get what they were going for, but for me this film suffers from a few things that hold me back from rating it higher. It's a bit on the long side, which started to irritate me after a while (not a good sign), it's hard to connect on an emotional level with the main character after a certain point, writing issues in the final third/last act of the film were too glaring to overlook, and the climax of the story came across as just a shock value thing (to gross you out as much as possible). reviews.body: This movie definitely could have been 30 minutes shorter. There are multiple situations that happen over and over again, which makes it feel unnecessarily repetitive. That said, the film does have an interesting and unique premise that sets it apart from many others in its genre. It's also easily one of the goriest movies I've ever seen-there's absolutely no way the main character is getting her security deposit back after all that chaos! On a deeper level, it offers a slightly good message about Hollywood and vanity, though it takes some patience to sit through the entire thing to fully grasp it. Additionally, viewers should be prepared for an unexpected amount of butt shots, which might catch some off guard. Overall, it's a bizarre mix of thought-provoking ideas and extreme visuals, but it could have been tighter and more impactful with better pacing.

Absolutely worthless as a film. It has things to say about the commodification of youth for women in society, but doesn't have any original way to say them.

Visual it's entirely ripping shots and framing from more established film makers, primarily either Kubrick or Wes Anderson. Couple that with the sharp cuts and inserts in the style of a mid 2000s computer game cut scene and that's the visual style here.

The plot is meandering and utterly non compelling.

The practical effects and attempts at body horror fall flat entirely. When you're basing a movie around them, you have to make sure the effects are at least on par with body horror genre greats from the 80s and 90s, and these just aren't.

The actors aren't good or bad, but they service the shallow material as well as they can.

Can't recommend this from any angle.

reviews.author: ADAMO_ITALIANO
reviews.body:
It's noticeable how people with different opinions about this film are often dismissed because they don't "get" its message or atmosphere, but isn't that the whole point of opinions? If we all agreed on everything, we wouldn't be able to complement each other as humans-everyone would be the same.

In the film, there's something for everyone. People have long been drawn to controversial topics, and this production is no exception. The creators try to reach audiences just like "Terrifier" did recently, delivering a dose of absurdity for viewers who avoid sappy romantic films at all costs. Along with that substance, we get psychedelic sounds that seep through our minds, paired with the idyllic scenes on screen.

The beginning of this two-hour journey brings to mind the structure of the series Black Mirror. For a while, it even tempts you to lump it together with Netflix productions, but that would be highly unethical and inappropriate, especially in an era when politics strive to show a lack of barriers in casting roles. Not to mention the many moments in this film filled with eroticism.

To be objective, I admit the film didn't appeal to me personally. I wouldn't rank it among the best I've seen this year, nor would I play it at a dinner gathering with friends. However, I recognize that it will leave its mark in film history-if only for its controversial nature.

reviews.body: I've watched some pretty gory stuff in the past with no problem, but for the first time in my life a movie almost made me physically sick, to the point where I had to take a shower after watching it because everything just felt so wrong. Don't get me wrong, I understand why some of it was necessary to the storyline, I'm perfectly okay with that, but much of it was just so sincerely unnecessary. If they only kept the integral parts in, the movie would probably be around 1h40. It's honestly disappointing because this movie has such a great concept, but such a poor execution. It baffles me how its gotten such great reviews because I honestly wish I could go back in time to stop myself from watching it. The pacing is excruciating, they spend so much time focusing on just the wrong things completely, like I can't even tell you how many zoom in shots of asses there were, like okay we get it, she's got a great butt, but can we continue on with the story now? Overall I'd say it just feels very immature. I would most definitely not recommend.

reviews.author: mfdias2005
reviews.body:
The script and the direction treat the characters like a piece of meat. Elisabeth, for example, has absolutely nothing but her work, which is totally focused on her body. She doesn't have family, friends, not even a dog or cats or hobbies. And actually all the characters are treated like this, they have no depth at all.

So the movie becomes exactly what it was meant to criticize. If Elisabeth should be treated like a real human being, the script should be the first to do so.

If you really want to reflect on ageing, go read The Picture of Dorian Gray or watch Sunset Boulevard (the classic from 1950), they're much better.

reviews.author: orfan-masri
reviews.body: The Substance starts with a great idea, exploring the risks and moral challenges of a groundbreaking scientific discovery. It sets up an interesting story about human ambition and the dangers of playing with nature. However, instead of focusing on the emotional and ethical struggles, the movie shifts into a different category of horror movie. The characters lose depth, and the story becomes more about shocking visuals and wild action than the deeper themes it started with. What could have been a smart and dramatic sci-fi film ends up feeling like just another creature movie, wasting its potential.

reviews.author: gaussma
reviews.body: It had the potential to be a thought-provoking horror, but it ultimately devolves into a superficial spectacle of sex and gore. The premise-a mysterious substance with dangerous, mind-altering effects-is intriguing and could have led to a chilling exploration of human nature or moral dilemmas. Unfortunately, the film's execution prioritizes shock value over substance. Characters lack depth, and the plot becomes muddled, sacrificing coherence for gratuitous scenes of violence and sexuality. While there are moments of eerie tension, the excessive reliance on graphic content quickly overshadows the more interesting ideas at play. It's a shame that a concept with such promise ended up feeling like a chaotic mashup of overdone horror tropes rather than a meaningful story.

reviews.author: deboerr
reviews.body:
Brave, original, dynamic, courageous and then it all goes to hell.

I was very intrigued by the concept and really applauded Moore for stepping into it. All went well, if somewhat predictable, when the characters start to violate the 'golden rules' of Substance use. Much like Gremilins, 'Don't feed them after midnight and don't get them wet', the story takes off when you violate the rules.

The social commentary and observations are relevant and powerful in the first two thirds of the movie, but the third act stinks. Its like someone with too much money and not enough ideas wrote and directed the third act. Its gross and pointless and throws away any social commentary it wanted to make. What a shame.

reviews.author: mauicharmane
reviews.body:
The worst movie I have ever watched! Yes, We watched until the end. We were trying to figure out what the hype was all about. The movie became more absurd with each minute. Zero personality is revealed in the main characters...Was this the point? I'm no prude, but the exaggerated butt shots and nudity made me feel uncomfortable. It felt as a sick pervert was directing it.

To call this a horror film is an insult to horror films. It showed no horror, just horrible acting, horrible directing, horrible sets, horrible storytelling, horrible waste of time. The plot could have been good if it didn't go in the absurd direction. I paid to see this on streaming. They should have paid me to watch it.

reviews.author: Edge49
reviews.body:
The three things about this movie that intrigued me were the IMDb rating, the premise, and Demi Moore. Those were three things that the movie really pulled me in with. And wow, did I get suckered.

It starts off pretty good. You're kind of curious about this actress and her getting old and what's gonna happen to her. And then this massive awful snowball just keeps getting bigger and bigger all the way up until the final act. Of course I can't spoil anything here, but wow, what a terrible ending.

The plot was actually kind of cool. Why rely on all these weird grotesque body things? I actually had to turn away at the end.

Another reviewer said that this was all in her mind after she took the substance. If that was the case, the movie was not that terrible.

You know what even if that was the case just avoid this altogether. I think anyone who gave this over a five is on drugs.

reviews.author: elizabeth-10237
reviews.body:
Definitely one of the worst films I've seen. The first 30 minutes had my attention but then it slid downhill and then finally fell off a cliff careening into a total abyss of meaningless imagery that lacked any substance whatsoever.

The topic of beauty is fascinating and it's a shame this filmmaker didn't have the guts to really explore why we prize it the way we do, especially in the United States and with an icon like Demi Moore. I feel bad she wasted her talent on this mess.

Finally, if you want a classic that's fun and entertaining, do yourself a favor and watch "Death Becomes Her," which is not only set in Los Angeles but includes an entire buffet of film greats delivering their comedic best.

reviews.author: TiredOldMan13
reviews.body:
Let's start with all the buzz regarding Demi Moore and her acting in this movie. Demi does very well but it's another case of an actress playing a character her own age and using special makeup effects to enhance their performance (think Nicole Kidman in The Hours). Any award she receives should go to the makeup people not her.

The movie itself is a big deal about nothing. 2 and a half hours of nothing to be exact. I was on the edge of my seat in the hope something exciting or scary was going to happen but it never really did. The last 30 minutes or so really sucked and were unnecessary.

Just another perfect example of a movie that gets so glazed by the movie industry and online critics that all the sheeple out there actually believe it is worth an 8 out of 10.

The highlight of the movie was Dennis Quaid and his performance, which should be the one spoken about. Margaret Qualley is there purely for her looks and isn't really given a lot to work with besides showing off her bum in every second shot.

reviews.author: daxbyrne-03460
reviews.body:
I don't know what on earth possessed Demi Moore and Denis Quaid to be in this film, but they want to take their agents and ship them off to a Cambodian prison with nothing to eat but gruel.

Without a doubt, had those 2 names not been on the listing, this might've not even made straight it to dvd. And it has done neither of them any favours. Quaid's attempt at the crazy OTT show producer is more akin to a turd in a glass of Buck's Fizz. Moore couldn't be flatter if she was on the surface of a black hole. And her minimal script seems to have come from a similar place.

A ridiculous story with a nonsensical ending. The "characters" are about as deep as a coin, the writing and dialogue seem to have been dug up from the bin of a sixth form common room after a heavy freshers week.

The cinematography is abysmal, visually all over the place with splashes of colour and fish lense photography in some attempt to provide an artistic element.

Watch it at your peril. I am almost offended at the existence of this vacuous bucket of fish skin.

reviews.author: amberstacy-01692
reviews.body: No spoilers/short review-This movie was a good watch as a horror fan. However, it's terribly overhyped. If you like horror then it's worth making a movie night out of it but it's not something that left my jaw on the floor or something that I believe to be a masterpiece-Just a typical body horror movie, but a decent one. My only criticism is the prolonged shots of butts, twerking, etc., it was super uncomfortable watching, even by myself. I found myself fast forwarding a lot of the first hour due to this. The amount of exposure wasn't needed to get the point across. It's almost like they are doing exactly what the movie portrayed and it definitely got uncomfortable and stigmatizing for women. Other than that, it's okay-if you like horror then it's worth your time.

reviews.author: antony-1
reviews.body:
That should have been the title of the movie.

Perhaps it's "meta", but in a movie about an aging celebrity whose career is past its best getting an aging celebrity whose career is past her best to degrade herself including cavorting about fully naked is kinda appropriate? Maybe?

And the really, long, drawn out scenes focusing on the female body is... some commentary on the male gaze or something?

To be honest if Demi Moore wasn't the lead this movie would have been forgotten what it is: a niche horror movie.

And it's quite good at times in doing that. And it has some interesting concepts. But it also has concepts all over the place, it felt like an experiment of ideas.

Even down to people eating, it tries to be grotesque. It's like a movie that is trying constantly to push your buttons, but to what end?

That's what it lacks most, any subtlety. We'll use dialog from the beginning of the movie and pair it with nightmare scenes at the end JUST IN CASE YOU DON'T GET IT. Are you listening view to OUR MESSAGE?

Not terrible by any means. And I actually quite liked the very end in contrast to other viewers as it ramped up the absurd humour.

The trouble is what is the movie? Absurd humour? Horror? Shock factor? Commentary? A bit of everything, but not really anything in particular.

reviews.author: GrumpyMovieBuff
reviews.body:
Oh boy, where do I even start with The Substance? You know, they're calling this movie "thought-provoking" and "reminiscent of The Fly," which is hysterical because the only thing it provoked in me was the urge to turn it off. Comparing this mess to The Fly is like comparing a dollar-store knockoff action figure to the real deal-it's embarrassing.

The plot is basically this: Demi Moore plays a washed-up celebrity who decides the best way to deal with aging is to take a shady drug that creates a younger, hotter version of herself. Because, of course, that's how science works. What follows is a smorgasbord of gore, nudity, and "symbolism" so ham-fisted it should come with a side of eggs. And don't even get me started on the logistics of her younger self suddenly being a functioning adult. Did the serum also create a fake identity, a résumé, and a social security number? Guess we're supposed to just roll with it.

The movie doesn't bother explaining how Elisabeth and her younger clone can live in the same house without anyone noticing-or, better yet, calling the cops. I mean, come on, you're telling me no one, not a neighbor or a nosy paparazzo, caught on? But logic clearly wasn't on the table here. The filmmakers were too busy cramming in gratuitous gore and awkward nudity to bother with pesky things like consistency or plot.

Speaking of the nudity, let's not pretend this movie isn't aimed squarely at horny teenagers. Sure, it wants to be deep, with its commentary on Hollywood's obsession with youth, but all it really says is: "Look! Gore! Naked people! Art!" It's all surface-level nonsense wrapped in a sticky, self-important package.

The ending is the cherry on this incoherent sundae. Without spoiling too much (not that there's anything to spoil), it's the kind of "artsy" conclusion that screams, "We didn't know how to wrap this up, so here's some vaguely disturbing imagery. Now clap."

In short, The Substance is what happens when a movie confuses shock value with quality. It's gross, stupid, and full of itself. If I had to rate it, I'd give it a generous 3/10, mostly for the effort of the makeup and effects team. Everyone else involved should probably try harder next time. Or not. Maybe just don't make another movie like this at all.

reviews.author: tuanaaaadeniz
reviews.body:
I have seen 10 minute YouTube films more complex and thoughtful than this movie. There were so many questions the team didn't even bother to answer, they added almost no mystery or emotions in the movie. The entire movie is wrapped around the closeup shots of gross things combined with the ASMR voices, the only novel experience you'll have if you watch the film.

There would be nothing interesting you'd take out of this movie, neither mind puzzles nor emorional attachments. The movie is HOLLOW.

In the media, aged people don't disappear like this. Because there's an aged audience that wants to relate and find a connection to someone. An aged audience that can take an aged woman as a role model. In fact this would be especially true for a dance/exercise program on a network TV. Aged people want to look younger ang get in a better shape, and they're more comfortable with network TV than with paid online platforms like Netflix. No one even offers this idea in the movie. Even in porn, aged people have a place. Duh.

Elizabeth Sparkle, someone seemingly famous suddenly disappears and no one questions it. Even if she had no friends, there would be paparazzis trying to capture her. A sudden disappearance and no reaction.

I get it, Sue is youthful and beautiful. But in what world beauty opens all the doors for you, allowing you to skip work 7 days in a row every other week? Unless you're in a middle eastern place full of woman-deprived men, you can't have too big of a number of men instantly falling for you!

And what about the sudden appearance of Sue? Since she looks young, I wonder how she'd buy alcohol without an ID. No one asks her for any sort of identification during the hiring process. What'd they tell the social security I'm curious.

Other than the logistical holes, there's no character to anyone. There's no personality or backstory. So whether you're someone who searches for intellectual stimuli in a movie or an emotional one, you'll be left with nothing you looked for.

reviews.author: kvfqfyc
reviews.body:
I felt like I wasted my time watching the movie. The first half showed potential, building up an interesting premise with hints of solid storytelling and engaging character development. However, the second half quickly unraveled into a chaotic display of gratuitous gore and mindless violence that felt completely unnecessary and added nothing to the plot. The sudden shift in tone was jarring, making it feel as though the film lost its direction and resorted to shock value rather than meaningful storytelling. The blood-soaked scenes seemed to drag on without purpose, turning what could have been a thought-provoking narrative into an incoherent mess.

Watching from home was, at least, a relief, as it gave me the freedom to skip over the excessive parts that felt both tedious and uncomfortable to sit through. Demi Moore's involvement felt like a mismatch; her talent seemed wasted in a role that didn't do her justice and should have been turned down in favor of more substantial material. Overall, what began as a promising experience turned out to be disappointing and left me feeling unsatisfied.

reviews.author: tgwvzd
reviews.body: I had a bad feeling from the time the Dennis Quaid character was introduced. Cartoonish extreme close-ups, leering directly into the camera - all that was missing was a skinny, curly moustache for him to twirl. The initial premise requires suspending a lot of disbelief, but it was an interesting idea. Demi Moore did a creditable job portraying a TV fitness personality who is being squeezed out of her featured role by an evil network executive who is preemptively heading off declining ratings. In more skillful hands this story could have been much better told, minus the absurd fantastical elements and excessive gore.

reviews.author: jenniejones-75346
reviews.body:
Tricky one this, not sure if it's actually a good film. It reminded me a little bit of Requiem for a Dream and the fly. Some nice nods to the shining.

But, it's a bit silly towards the end. Kind of ruins the cinematography (like requiem). The final, final scene is quite powerful. I guess.

The beginning is good, and half way, maybe that's good too. The end? Seemed like it was a different film.

I wouldn't watch this again, or recommend it. I'd say if someone asked me, "yeah, it's weird, you might like it". I guess I'd say that to all of you as you're reading this.

Giving it a five star rating as that's midway and I think that's how I felt about it.

reviews.author: faridb2000
reviews.body:
When the movie started, I expected a drama or dark comedy. However, as soon as the gore began-starting with Demi Moore's back being grotesquely opened I found it revolting. The longer it went on, the more I hoped it would end. Yet, my habit of watching films to the end, even when I dislike them initially, kept me going in the faint hope it might improve. Unfortunately, this one only got worse as it progressed.

I fail to understand why a director would rely so heavily on excessive gore and absurdity to explore the theme of aging actresses resorting to drugs or falling victim to scams in their pursuit of youth and relevance.

Compare this with the classic Sunset Boulevard-a film that tackled the issue of aging and its impact on performers with far more depth and significance.

If this movie deserves any recognition, it would solely be for its special effects.

However, even that feels more like a technical showcase of CGI rather than genuine artistry.

reviews.author: jdring2007
reviews.body:
Apart from the makeup effects, and Dennis Quaid's performance (as a despicable scumbag albeit), this movie falls flat in every regard.

It's a laundry list I'll sum up for the TL;DRs: obnoxiously annoying music, predictable shock-plot, boringly overt fixation on Margaret Qualley, flashing colors, gaping plot holes and time leaps, OVER 2 HOURS OMG HOW AND WHY, characters you can't relate to or feel for (literally everyone in the movie sucks, especially the 2 main characters).

That's about it, and but for a little clarification:

Again, the makeup/practical effects for Monstro ElisaSue (I didn't make that up; 2:05:00 into the movie, it becomes a satirical comedy) were great. It's just a shame that we had to wait literally 2 hours for something befitting of a "body horror," which I've relentlessly seen this labeled as, not to mention in many "top 5 of all time" lists. Puh-lease.

1:28:00 or so was when we get our first glimpse of something eerie, only to be shed as a dream sequence. 2 more of these before Monstro ElisaSue makes an appearance. By which time my brain has melted from the wretched soundtrack and Barbie-music-video visuals, while trying to piece together disjointed sequences thanks to time jumps to circumvent immense plot holes, like critical wounds with no treatment. If someone defends this by saying "the movie is a metaphor, not to be taken literally" I can excuse it to a degree, but not when the other flaws are jarringly unavoidable.

Of course, if this movie wasn't being lauded so much and didn't have a higher rating than other genuinely terrific movies such as Cure For Wellness or (different genre I know, but still criminally underrated) The Creator, then I'd be less affronted by how trash it is.

I only thank the gods that I didn't have to pay a penny for this, only my time. People giving it anything above a 6 need a brain scan, or maybe just have extremely shallow/sensitive taste in movies, especially horror. Body, psychological, whatever. Unfortunately, there are also people on here giving it a 3-6 and STILL praising "the first hour." If anything, that was the worst part of the movie. At least the last 45min felt tolerably jarring, albeit so dumb and comedic that it was like digging its own grave, with a shovel nicknamed Shock Value.

End of the day, if you watch the trailer and expect it'll be good, you'll probably like it. There's a word for that: it rhymes with people.

reviews.author: ktwbw
reviews.body:
Honestly... I like it, but didn't love it.

reviews.author: iamronin
reviews.body:
A putrid incoherent cacophony stumbling from one incongruous chunk of horror porn to the next. Rarely do I rant in such a way about any attempt at filmography however poorly conceived it may be. But this is without doubt the most psychologically harmful two hours and twenty one minutes I've ever subjected myself to. The first twenty minutes or so intrigued me to the point of wanting more. The remaining two hours found me exponentially want less.

If there was an explanation as to who was behind this "substance" or why, I missed it.

Never have I so desperately wanted two hours and twenty one minutes of my life back.

My advice: Save your money and psychological well being and skip this one.

reviews.author: DrumheadofSpace
reviews.body:
People giving this a good review are easily amused by nudies and blood. Besides the very stylish cinematography this movie, ironically, has zero substance. I can see how very hard the director was trying to make his own version of The Fly, but it fails on every level.

The acting is farcical, the script is putrid and the performance from the two leads... holy hell it's like Power Rangers level acting.

But where it truly fails is the story. The Fly was a stunning piece of body horror with an extremely engaging story that tied in well to the horrors presented on-screen. The Substance tries to ape this but it's a poor clone that won't last long in your memory banks. Avoid it, rewatch The Fly rather.

reviews.author: marijatattooink
reviews.body:
The film starts with an intriguing premise and benefits from a solid foundation built on a commendable core idea. The performances, especially the lead actors' portrayals, are worthy of praise, demonstrating a level of skill and commitment that adds depth to the storyline. Yet, despite these positive elements, nearly all other aspects of the film falter. As the story progresses, the once-promising setup begins to unravel, giving way to a series of increasingly exaggerated and misplaced narrative choices.

The final act is where the sense of imbalance and excess truly takes hold, and here, the directorial vision seems to waver. It becomes increasingly difficult to tell whether the director has lost control over the story's arc, or if perhaps he grew indifferent toward crafting a coherent and satisfying conclusion.

When the film reaches a natural point for closure, one would expect a thoughtful resolution. However, it proceeds to meander for an additional forty minutes, a stretch that feels largely unnecessary and begins to detract from the impact of what came before. This prolonged denouement dilutes the potency of the narrative, stretching the viewer's patience and disrupting the rhythm and cohesion that could have brought the story to a satisfying end. Instead of the intended dramatic or emotional climax, the film's resolution feels extended to an exhausting degree, casting a shadow over an otherwise engaging initial experience.

reviews.author: rajkumar-kannan-276-940987
reviews.body: As a sci-fi enthusiast, I went into this movie expecting an exploration of a futuristic theme like cell division and replication of self, but it turned out to be more of an abstract metaphor brought to life. The premise - the idea of creating a younger version of oneself to relive experiences and create new opportunities, however this is as a separate individual who lives a parallel life - is intriguing. However, despite some stellar acting that kept me watching, the story itself starts strong but quickly spirals into a muddled mess of absurdity. The script takes a sharp turn downhill, leading to an over-the-top, almost 25-minute finale that feels unnecessarily drawn out. While there's a hint of "Black Mirror" inspiration here, especially with the thematic elements, the forced humor and absurd plot twists leave much to be desired. If you're looking for thought-provoking sci-fi, you'd be better off revisiting an actual "Black Mirror" episode.

reviews.author: OzoFriendly
reviews.body:
Here was an oppurtunity to tell a tight twilight zone morality tale about our dark obsession with beauty.

Leaving aside the heavy-handed implication that men alone are responsible for this, the story, and it's take-it-or-leave-it premise, begins very well.

Demi Moore and Margaret Qualley are both very good and the confrontational visuals, from grotesque wide-angle close-ups, thru uncompromising nudity, to the Junji-Ito-worthy body horror are genuinely exciting and fun.

In fact, until the trolley left the tracks at the 100 minute mark, I absolutely loved this movie. Then incredulously the story becomes an inconsistent, incoherent mess, undoing all the great storytelling up to that point.

For the next 40 minutes or so, the movie is just offensively bad with almost nothing to recommend it, making no final, insightful statement about beauty or obsession, or ending with a clever, savage twist, but instead leaning on horror cliche and spectacle to see us out in a frankly ludicrous final scene that will make sense to pretty much no one.

My theory is that Coralie Fargeat's original ending was rejected and in a fit of pique, she replaced it with a ruinously terrible one.

Very disappointing.

reviews.author: Taaneekaa
reviews.body: Let me first start by saying that the cinematography was great. I'm not used to seeing this type of cinematography and direction so it took me a while to settle into the movie. The movie has a good message. But it's v long unnecessarily. The message gets lost during the climax and stupidity takes over. The protagonist is one of those people who don't learn from their mistakes- very realistic actually. But like I said, the ending is v stupid. It makes you feel like you're watching a movie made by some amateurs. I understand it's a dark comedy but the entire movie didn't feel this over the top ordeal with heightened nonsense that the end felt like. The ending wasn't written well at all. It was super bad it makes you feel like a different writer has written the ending. The movie should have ended when Sue finds out what's going to happen to her. Or it could have been a total different ending altogether but they decided to ruin the movie with this ending. You basically start thinking you're watching something with substance but then after the movie ends you'll think that is really shallow.

reviews.author: li0904426
reviews.body:
The movie 'The Substance' exemplifies the new trend in French extremism cinema, similar to 'Titane,' where every scene is exaggerated, pushing boundaries and shocking viewers in ways that often feel excessive and uncomfortable. Writer and director Coralie Fargeat uses horror in this movie to powerfully critique and challenge societal perceptions of the female body. The concept and idea behind the movie are excellent, but the script has significant flaws.

Until the final 30 minutes, the director's flaws are largely forgivable. For example, I only recognized that the movie was set in the 21st century when I saw messages on Demi Moore's character's cell phone; until then, I believed it was set in the '80s, similar to the popular Jane Fonda exercise videos. Interestingly, even today, there aren't well-known morning exercise programs for women on television.

Unfortunately, Coralie Fargeat derails the movie in the last 30 minutes. It feels as if she rushed to finish the story, abandoning her original vision and resorting to clichéd Hollywood conventions to wrap it up. The movie's standout feature is its casting, especially Demi Moore and Margaret Qualley. Qualley excels in her role as Sue, radiating talent and depth, while Moore is a reflection of her own mirror. Dennis Quaid, as Harvey, perfectly captures the essence of his personality in real life, a fool and disgusting man.

reviews.author: nfsrykjvm
reviews.body:
Great movie till the end. Passed out, hit the ground, and EMS took me to the ER! Don't recommend.

It needs to cool off with the gore!

reviews.author: Jim_Screechy
reviews.body:
Came upon this one as it was listed as a 'watch' on my list. Well, nothing could have prepared me for the crazy way it was dipicted. It has a guy richie feel about it having many of the styles he employed particuarly in some of his earlier famous stuff like 'Lock Stock & Two Smoking Barrells, but this film has it dialed up to 10. It's like Guy Richie on Crack.

It's defintely intruguing though I don't think it worked particularly well with this screenplay, it does make the movie iconic. I think if it had been scaled back it would have brought a rich flavour to the movie rather than drowning it in a flavour so strong that's all that stands out.

The movie itself has an interesting premise. There are some issues with it, but for the most part its certainly thoughtfull enough to make an intersting plot, and again this works quite well till things become a little ridiculous toward the latter stages of the movie. I get the impression that this was done deliberately and preciesly for the response it gets. It sort of puts the movie into a rhealm of 'crazy' where it can't be taken too seriously but again, I think this is by design.

The cast does a great job with the meterial. I didn't even realise Demi Moore until the credits rolled, and she really is great with her role. Dennis Quaid does well as Jim Carely (for the most part) but there aren't a lot roles of note outside the main cast to mention. Margaret Qually is miscast here in my opinion. She simply isn't good looking enough to carry off the role she's playing convincingly. Normally this wouldn't be an issue, but here since her very existence is dependant on her being the pinnacle of what Moore's character is supposed to reprisent... she falls drastically short, particularly when you consider that Moore is sixty and looking this good. Pehaps Mia Goth was unavailable, or turned down the role.

I certainly likee the first part of the movie, the concept is an interesting one and as I said, thought things are a little wild it certainly holds your attention. I did find my interest wanning a little by half way, and truthfully only really watched to the end to see how things would tie up since by half way the more familiar tale of two halves has levelled the plot to something much more familiar. The movie is a little long and does drag in places, but its not too bad.

Overall I've given it 5/10 becuase... Just because of the entertainment value. Most all reviews I've read are correct about whats on offer here, but all that said, I just didn't really enjoy it enough to give it more than a passing grade.

However I would absoultely recommend you watch it for yourself because I think this is one of those Love it/hate it type movies and the only way to know which way you'll lean, its to give it a go.

reviews.author: nameoh
reviews.body:
The film and the plot line are pretty good. I enjoyed it up until the last 30 minutes. Demi Moore and Margaret Qualley and Dennis Quaid all played their roles brilliantly. Things started going south when it became obvious that Margaret's character and even Demi's where willing to behave in a manner against their own best interests. The instructions were clear, easy to follow and would have been to the advantage of all. But to want to destroy the other and thereby oneself or to want to sacrifice oneself for another just didn't cut it with me.

That aside, the movie was quite good until the last 30 minutes when whoever conceived the story completely ran out of gas and went bizarre on us. It is either that or for reasons best known to them they decided that whack ending was good. Pretty much spoilt the movie for me.

Be your own judge. Give it a watch!

reviews.author: ferdinand1932
reviews.body:
In ''Ulysses'' Joyce's uses the phrase 'ineluctable modality of the visible' to state that there is a reliance upon vision in perceiving the world. A sort of ''Esse est percipi''. This movie expresses that to the nth degree. But it is not interesting in anyway at all and its length elongates the torpor of its mediocrity to a degree that Joyce and Berkeley might have groaned at.

The Substance expresses Christopher Laschs's 1978 book ''The Culture of Narcissism'' quite perfectly. That is to say, that the torments of aging and the loss of physical beauty are the ineluctable anxiety of the narcissist and of the narcissist culture that fostered it: in other words, those that live by the sword, die by the sword. The nature of narcissism is manifold and has been in articulated in great and analytic detail, and it is accepted as a commonality of modern life, at least since it was empirically documented over 40 years ago. (Lasch uses statistics in the US to show that the increase in narcissism is a quantitative fact. It rise everywhere since is demonstrable)

As such, and without deviance from the logic of that argument, The Substance uses horror tropes and a simplistic deterministic linearity to drive its dramatic point home with the same spirit that a dull-witted student had used AI to write a paragraph. This aspect is manifest in the coy depiction of the multiple ''butt'' shots, whereas the loss of youth, and with it, fertility, ought really to be expressed in the transformation of the sexual organs, but because of censorship rules, and the obvious refusal by actors to do such scenes, cannot be done in a film. Thus, the impotence of the thesis is clear in the film medium.

That the camera work, the direction and editing are of singular point of view does not elevate the piece to anything of note. It does, if anything, underline the gruesome idiocy of its own narcissism.

reviews.author: ftack-84704

In fact, so many scenes seem to be a male fantasy, that I thought the movie was written and directed by a man. Other reviewers have said if one is uncomfortable watching this movie they should take a hard look at themselves. What I would say is that the writer/director needs to take a hard look at herself. She fell victim to the same low forces that she was attempting to have us look at, and all for profit. Oh, the irony.

reviews.author: raminamintafreshi
reviews.body:
The concept is exciting, and the buildup is phenomenal. However, the experience was ruined toward the end. It felt like the plot was forced to be shocking, but it failed to give an impactful conclusion.

It feels similar to smashing bubbles with a heavy hammer-overly exaggerated ations with no impactful sound.

In my opinion, and as opposed to many reviews here, many references and intertextual connections with works like The Elephant Man and The Shining seemed just like a cover-up for the story's lack of coherence, which lead to a rather disappointing ending. The conclusion of the movie just felt like an attempt to shock the audience-a strategy that worked really well in marketing terms and generated lots of hype around the show, but greatly lacked substance in story.

reviews.author: tabsischaeffer
reviews.body: Just a movie based on a basic plot, which doesn't allow any deeper character development. The videography is interesting but also as much on the nose as all of the characters. The movie has great audio quality and effects but the dialogues are meaningless and superficial. Visually this film is interesting, but lacks a certain edge to make it a timeless cultural addition. The movie would have been much better as a shorter Black mirror episode. The length of this film mostly consists of two things: the horror-imagery of body manipulation, extraction of fluids and wounds as well as the way-too-often-used sexiness/attractiveness of the two main actresses. In my humble opinion there is no need for these many close-ups of boobs and curves. The movie had potential to reveal so much more about our society's connection to commercial beauty ideals but fails to meet any emotional depth.

reviews.author: ThereelscoopwithKK
reviews.body:
The premise of the movie is simple and is satisfactory for the most part. However, it didn't even come close to living up to the hype that is going around movie circles right now. The acting is fine and both lead actors play their parts pretty well. The story that's told is a theme of wanting to be your best/ improved/ younger self and willing to go to whatever ends to achieve it, even if it means obvious self destruction. This theme has been often used and this storyline doesn't really offer much that is new to it.

During many of the scenes that feel overly extended I was thinking to myself that it felt like what Black Mirror would put out if they sent something to theatres. Using Black Mirror as a reasonable comparison I would say this film just lacks the same punch. Even the cinematography and shots included that many are raving over feel forced and included for the sake of them rather than to enhance the story, which should always be filmmakers top priority in my opinion.

I applaud the effort of at least trying to make this movie special up until the last 15 minutes. I'm usually willing to accept a lot of chaos on the screen but the conclusion of the film was almost insulting. They completely throw out any message or theme the movie is trying to explore by just overloading your brain with grotesque imagery. The audience in the theatre was laughing but in a weird , uncomfortable way.

Just because you don't know how to complete a piece of art work doesn't mean you throw the paint bucket at the easel and call the work abstract. Filmmakers should avoid doing this also.

reviews.author: bedpilled
reviews.body:
The three acts of this movie reminded me a lot of the Godfather trilogy, wherein the first one lays amazing groundwork and the second somehow outdoes it while the third one leaves you with a distinct "ehhhhhh" in your mind and while it's not terrible, you kind of wish it stopped at the second one.

What I will say to people going fresh into the movie is to bolden expectations. What I went into the movie for- and what it did indeed somewhat deliver for the first two acts- was a kind of Requiem For A Dream/Perfect Blue hybrid. The movie unfortunately devolves into some weird rejected entry for an ABCs of Horror film by the last half hour or so and the shift in tone is about as jarring as you can expect.

It really does feel a lot like Saltburn's spiritual successor in that they're both movies that I feel wanted to say a lot and people overhyped but really don't leave you with that poignant of a message once you leave the cinema and you're mostly there for the gratuitousness and shock factor anyway.

At least Saltburn didn't take itself too seriously social commentary-wise whereas the same cannot be said for this movie and the people who made it, who no doubt thought they were producing the second coming of The Shining.

And as far as the social commentary element of this movie which feels more like a comically large spoon someone is trying to force-feed you with....yes, people have a complex with aging, yes this feeds into self-destructive beauty standards imposed by advertising and media and this has adverse consequences on everyone but much in the same way that you don't need to watch a 10 hour compilation of gazelles being devoured by lions to understand that nature can be cruel, this movie's gratuitousness to hammer home a kind of superficial message makes the whole thing feel really cheap and has me thinking maybe the intended demographic is kids who never before in life considered these ideas and would no doubt be impressed by their delivery and who also consider comically excessive blood spatter to be the pinnacle of what makes something scary instead of well....funny, since oddly enough I spent more time laughing at what went on in the movie than I did being genuinely unnerved or frightened.

It's not a terrible movie, just don't go into it expecting too much except for a slightly better produced Grindhouse flick.

reviews.author: venegas-richard
reviews.body:
Horrible ending. Pretty good but the last 30 mins.

My wife and I end up on the verge of vomiting.

I couldn't recommend it.

reviews.author: wellingtonmtr
reviews.body: This movie could've explored *many* interesting themes and social commentaries. Instead it focuses exclusively on one (the prejudice and hostility women must endure emotionally, mentally, and professionally as they age) and just repeats it over and over and over and over and over and over again. Then it repeats it over and over some more. Moore is excellent! Cinematography and sense of tension really great. Otherwise, the story is one dimensional and feels barely fleshed out. The result is a repetitive, ultimately uninteresting and tiresome plot. The first act leaves you with anticipation of what's coming next, that slowly morphs into boredom across act two as yet more blood splatters and scene after scene after scene simply depicts variations of the old Lizzie descending while the young Lizzie rises (Old bad. Young good. We. Get. It!). The third act goes off the rails (in this case over the top is just over the top and not "artistic") and feels like a potpourri of alternative endings they just smashed in there one after another. Just when you think/hope it's finally wrapping up, nah. Twenty minutes to go. Lots of untapped potential here, surely a missed opportunity for Fargeat. And truthfully, Moore carries what is otherwise a tedious watch.

reviews.author: parhamkazemi-30716
reviews.body: The film had a very good idea, and the cinematography was great. The story progressed well up until the middle of the film, but then a poor idea about how to continue ruined it. I would give the first half hour of the film a 7, but for the rest of the story, I'd give it a 2. Overall, Demi Moore's performance in the film, as well as her co-star's, was very good. Even though the film has received high ratings from others and is praised a lot, unfortunately, in my opinion, at least in the second hour, it is not an acceptable piece of work.

reviews.author: edesio
reviews.body:
It lasted only half an hour. It introduces interesting ideas about accepting aging and the search for recognition and love. However, the main protagonist's decision to undergo a procedure with minimal information seems implausible. The egotistical behavior of the copy, seeking all the 'wake' time for herself, is frustrating, and she never notices the damage caused by delaying the switch.

The lack of communication between the characters is a missed opportunity. They never leave notes for each other about their feelings or activities, which is a concept explored more effectively in Philip José Farmer's Dayworld series, where characters live one day a week and leave notes for each other, including complaints about household chores.

There was a lost opportunity at the café to gather information when the protagonist meets the master of pair 207. They seem to abide by the rules, but even so, the master is depressed and feels no longer relevant since the copy is a younger and better version of himself.

The bloodbath sequence reminded me of the duel between the Black Knight and King Arthur in Monty Python and the Holy Grail (1975), as well as The Bride's fight against the Crazy 88 in Kill Bill.

reviews.body:

reviews.author: jasminesingh-86988
reviews.body: Unpopular opinion here but I didn't like the movie at all. Absolutely wouldn't recommend it to anyone, except those who are certified psychopaths who might enjoy the absurdly unnecessary and mindless gore and nudity in almost every scene of the movie. I'm all for blood and sex when it fits the narrative and the story seems gripping. In this case it was not. The story went from mildly interesting in the first 30-odd minutes (with us hoping it would get better) to slightly twisted in the next 30ish minutes and on to absolutely ludicrous and unbearable for the rest of the 80 or so minutes. It is clear that the director and scriptwriter were going for extreme shock tactics to get a reaction from award bodies (which seems to be a trend and clearly working even for this movie which is getting awards left right and centre). But to the average viewer it was just a disgusting and traumatic waste of their time and mind space. In the second half of the movie, I looked around to see people either walking out or just scrolling on their phones/ closing their eyes. And not because it was scary but it was just plain idiotically disgusting. Honestly don't see why one would want to spend 2.5 hours of their lives subjecting them through this torture. If puking out intestines and spraying blood like a hosepipe on a stadium full of people is your type of fun, please do go ahead and watch the movie. Just don't forget to book your therapy sessions for the next 2 months in advance.

reviews.author: harwood-68876
reviews.body:
Really? A 50 yo actress, with a star on the Hollywood Boulevard of Fame, beloved by all for her masterful talent as an...aerobics instructor named Elizabeth Sparkle?! Was her original surname 'Spackled'? Then I might understand the name.

Is it of any coincidence the female director of this cartoon of a movie has a last name that reads at first glance to spell 'Fartgreat'? It's actually 'Fargear'. OK, I'll stop obsessing because there is a lot of ground to cover. The Substance could make the top three in a show devoted to 'bloopers'. For both logic and visual oversight.

Skimming through the plot, Elizabeth ( Moore) is being booted from her decades long aerobic show and replaced by a younger version. Anyone with sense would think this is a terrible idea. As it's said, the proof is in the pudding, and Moore's unbelievably youthful body ( in reality she is 62) would be enough incentive for a fictional audience to remain loyal to her show.

But no. Damn show biz and its youth obsession! The network producer demands change and Liz needs to be replaced by a twenty- something year old. In perfect sync with this devastating news, some random staff member at a medical facility Liz is at, discreetly presses into her palm, cryptic instructions for obtaining a mysterious 'substance' offering a formula for reverse aging. Think Meryl Streep in Death Becomes Her.

But there is a caveat for sustaining the effects, much like the one featured in Stephen Spielberg's Gremlins, for keeping the titular characters adorable. Only messier.

So about the bloopers- then I'm out of here.

There is a break in location continuity that annoyed me.. Liz lives in the most spectacular spacious apartment imaginable. Evidently, squatting - the exercise- really does pay well. But in a tight, controlled shot of the building's public hallway, that we see when Liz opens her door to her geeky, male neighbor (dressed in sweats and shirt and looking like he was retrieved from a dumpster), reveals a shabby glass block window - obfuscating the view to outside. Odd because, from inside Liz's apartment, the view is spectacular. We also notice the public hallway has shoddy finishes, reminiscent of a father's attempt to build his kids a recreation room.

And who allowed that creepy tenant a lease, anyway?

The younger version of Liz enjoys the popularity of performing on the most leering, uninstructive aerobics show ever. I expected Liz, as the instructor, shouting in appropriate verbiage synchronized with the camera work, commands like, " Thrust! Crack! Bend! Spread! Crack again! Use those fingers!". The closeups are so tight, you don't know if you are watching exercise to tone thighs or a challenge to pick up loose change using other body parts, repurposed. Never mind; they all explode over the course of 2 hours, 20 minutes.

The movie leans into a familiar subtext of 'woman old, bad', 'woman young, good': It isn't a heavy message.

There must have been some tantalizing perks delivered following the extravagantly good reviews of some professional critics.

That's all I'm saying.

reviews.body:
