reviews.author: shuabones
reviews.body:
I get it - sex sells. But, it felt like this movie was an excuse to show gratuitous amounts of nudity because they are hot women... I'm fairly certain there was less nakedness in Demi Moore's "Striptease". Add to that the weird almost obsession with Dennis Quaid's mouth, and ridiculous ending (no spoilers),I can understand why this movie is "controversial" to say the least.

This idea had so much potential, but I feel like they were trying too hard to pander to a "man's man". When you have a good idea or story, just stick with that - no need to try and "reel in" a specific demographic. Very disappointed.

reviews.author: daniellanovak
reviews.body: Raw disappointment. I completely understand movies that are art pieces but this was beyond lost. I wanted to love this movie the same way I loved the fly...awkwardly mesmerizing. Sadly, at some point the lot shifted and frankly I have zero clue what this movie was about. Is it about beauty? Aging? Doctors pushing medical procedures? So much potential yet so many different routes this movie could have taken. If I can make dinner, paint the house and mow the lawn and I'm still able to figure out what's going on in the movie...well it's not a great film. The actors themselves are spectacular, the script ....well what the heck???

reviews.author: jorlawson
reviews.body: This film is laughable. The "message" is nothing new nor fresh. I had zero sympathy with any character. We are human. We get old. Accept it. I will say Dennis Quaid stole the movie with his over the top performance. Moore was adequate but not mind blowing and Qualley. Whom I love gave a very monotone performance. So, it as a lot of nudity....my goodness, how shocking!, This is a far cry from Cronenburg and films like In My Skin by Marina De Van. Simply do not understand the big deal.... I found it absurd. I must write more, so...many who watch this no very little of horror or what is being made independently or in foreign countries. Go what a Buttgereit film from 40 years ago and get back to me..

reviews.author: noharonk3
reviews.body:
I can't believe the reviews: How can so many pros review this grotesque farce as a legitimate intelligent " masterpiece".

This is clearly a very simplistic view of the subject it's trying to address. I'm sorry, but it's not enough to film an old actress to pass on a message about vanishing beauty.

Without Demi Moore, Denis Quaid and Margaret Qualley, this would be nothing more than an horror movie not unlike Human centipede: if you want to lose your appetite, it's perfect. If you want something that gives you substance to think, I'm afraid you are going to waste your time.

I have to admit that the realisation is mastered. Too bad the screenplay and the subject is so poorly treated.

reviews.author: gspencley
reviews.body:
A bit of context about myself and where I'm coming from with this movie. My wife and I are huge horror movie fans. We were married on Halloween and every year on our anniversary we pig out on candy and binge watch horror movies.

This year we included The Substance in our list of movies to watch.

We went into this somewhat blind. We knew the cast and the basic plot / premise and that was it. We didn't read reviews and we didn't even watch trailers. Based on what we knew, we were both really looking forward to this.

Being children of the 80s, we remember Demi Doore being a sex symbol in the early 90s. We also fondly remember many of Andie McDowell films (Margaret Qualley's mother) from the era as well. So the idea of casting these two women in a horror movie that is fundamentally about the insecurities that women face with ageing and becoming "washed up" in an industry that is youth-obsessed sounded amazing on paper!

And there was a very good movie buried within The Substance. Unfortunately it was a confused mess and that good movie gets diminished by a lot of utter pointlessness.

The first thing that I really disliked was that Dennis Quaid's character was mostly useless. He was needed for the inciting incident, when Demi Moore learns that her TV show is being cancelled, but after that point there was not a single purpose for any of the scenes that he was in. They could have cut them all and the movie would have been unchanged and better off for the shorter runtime.

Instead Quaid's character was treated like the villain. However, the real villain of this story (or at least the good story that was buried in this movie) is the actress herself and her inner demons and insecurities. The writer kinda sorta got this at times, but it seems like they were wanting some kind of a "good vs external evil" dynamic that this story simply did not call for.

I don't want to talk too much about the ending because I don't want to include spoilers in this review. What I will say is that there was a scene that immediately preceded the ending that would have been the perfect way to end the movie. My wife and I both gave each other a look of surprise when the film continued on beyond that point. This is to say that what the filmmaker was trying to put forward as the grande finale / climax was completely unnecessary!

If I had to guess, some decision maker(s) wanted this film to play up the practical fx for marketing purposes so they went full "Rick Baker American Warewolf in London" to flex the practical fx muscle and show off.

The only problem is, it hurt the story... something I say even as a huge horror movie and gore fan!

At the end, "confused" is the best word to describe this movie. It was starting to touch on a story that is very worth telling and could have been told clearly and to great dramatic effect, even with many horror devices applied. Instead they tried to cram in a bunch of unnecessary drivel and the movie suffered because of it.

4/10 because there were redeeming qualities but the execution on the story telling was weak and we won't be watching this one again on future anniversaries.

reviews.author: artopolha
reviews.body: From start to end full of holes in the story, horrible plot, weak directing. Zero respect for the audience. Absolutely worst movie I've ever seen. And i watch A LOT of movies. The movie is rather confused and does not make meaningful points. It is a mildly developed idea poorly executed throughout the movie. Desperate attempts to attract people by sexual content. Non the less a horrible movie with bad editing. Stretched in the last 40 minutes only to serve no purposes at all. I don't have a problem with slasher movies so thats not the source of my disgust. It is because i wasted more than two hourse watching a meaningless, pointless and horrible film.

reviews.author: aimeeshannonk
reviews.body: So... I loved the trailer. I loved what was showing on TikTok and yes! YES I ADMIT... I was influenced. And I really, really liked this movie until a specific point and then it became just this: Pointless. I don't know why they chose the last half an hour as they did but I wasn't a fan of it and it pretty much destroyed this otherwise really great movie and good idea. When I read the reviews tho - people say we just -don't get it-. And that it's -way more deep.-. While I think it has a deep meaning, this one got deeply buried in all. That. Blood. Sometimes we do get - we simply just don't like it.

reviews.author: carlitos-23
reviews.body: I had high hopes for this movie based on word of mouth. But after watching it I have to say, I don't think we watched the same movie. This movie rips off Aronofsky in such a way that a third of the movie is basically Requiem For a Dream. The movie has no direction. It feels like there's three different directors trying to do three different things. The social commentary feels like it was pulled straight out of a Twitter spat with such poignant one liners as "pretty girls should always smile!" Towards the end it devolved into a David Cronenberg film and swaps it's feeble attempts at subtlety with over the top shock and gore, that comes off as trying to hard. The ending is quite literally the ending of Requiem For a Dream where Jared Leto's mother gets to live her a fantasy in a hallucination. Skip this movie and watch Requiem for a Dream or Scanners if you're looking for something more Cronenberg.

reviews.author: imdb-392-492467
reviews.body:
The concept is interesting but grew old quickly. The body horror stuff doesn't really do it for me. It was quite obvious where things were going and where they would end up. The only surprise was not knowing what abusing the substance would do to them.

I found it impossible to have any empathy for either of the jekyll or hyde personas. They each knew what they were doing to the other but chose to stay the course regardless. The one being negatively affected had the option to stop it at any moment but chose to say the course week after week.

Ultimately just another movie where the main character would have been better off with therapy.

reviews.author: info-43154
reviews.body: Happy in the beginning, lovely acting and great message to the audience. Movie could and should have stopped minimum 30 minutes before. In these times of war, misery in the world and all the unnecessary bloodshed I found it embarrassing and way too much how they kept going on with violence and blood scenes. After she hits the "ugly" version of herself with the head into the mirror, it wasn't necessary to hit her 8 more times.. Until now I still don't understand why I didn't leave? It's something I regret. Never a movie made me feel so uncomfortable afterwards and not in a good way. I feel bad for the actors and the people that watched the whole movie. I'm kind of amazed how this has a 7.4 in IMDB? Anyways .. I ll get over it one day..

reviews.author: mssef
reviews.body:
This movie was so wonderfully made, until the director/writer decided to drag it into a ditch. The casting, acting, cinematography was all A+ but for whatever reason (I suppose to really force the body obsession theme down your throat..) the movie makers decided to make it a complete joke at the end.

The movie starts as a Black Mirror/Black Swan squirmy thriller, and slowly transform into a fun disturbing gore fest. Brilliant performances by Qualley, Moore, and even Quaid. I wish they stopped the movie several times towards the end and I would've been extremely satisfied with the finished product. I am insanely angry they decided to run this brilliant movie into the ground and then continuously insult us as a viewers at the end. The end is so bad, that I would've given this movie a 9/10 but instead I had to TURN IT OFF. That bad of an ending. 1/10 ending and 9/10 otherwise leaves me at 5/10. So so disappointing, the most disappointed I've felt at the end of the movie in my life.

reviews.author: lesdroits
reviews.body: Just finished watching, and the concept of the movie and the action kept me watching (and so many movies do not). There were a ton of realism problems which, of course, has to be totally suspended very early on, and just pretend. But even pretending couldn't help me as I got to the last third or so, when the main action has already happened and repeated itself so the script, for me, rather jumps a shark. This last portion has its moments of suspense but also a lot of time spent just in (relatively tame) repeated violence. Boring. At the end was where it especially jumped the shark and, tho there were a few really funny moments, the whole thing became just nonsensical and, well, silly (where did the tons of blood and/or other stuff being sprayed all over come from). So, for a movie I make it through, I give it a 5. The woman playing the younger, "prettier" version had a certain nastiness to her that reminded me of a certain disliked slanderer, which meant she did a good job. Demi, I no longer can recognize as Demi but she too did a fine job.

reviews.author: Allvgretto
reviews.body:
"The Substance" caught my attention with its intriguing premise, but it didn't quite deliver what it promised. The film felt long and dragged out, with characters that sometimes seemed silly or poorly thought out. This was likely meant to highlight their insecurities, but it ended up making them come across as just not very smart.

Despite these issues, it's worth noting that the actors did a great job. Their performances were solid, and the makeup effects were impressive, adding a lot of depth to the visual experience of the film.

However, as the movie went on, it relied too heavily on squishy sound effects that aimed to gross out rather than scare, and the excessive use of butt shots and nudity felt unnecessary and overdone.

Overall, "The Substance" had the potential to be something really special, but it got lost in its own gimmicks. The great acting and makeup couldn't save it from becoming a bit of a letdown.

reviews.author: NewSkol
reviews.body:
There is a lot to love: the acting, the cinematography, the social commentary.

Unfortunately, the delivery of the message was done in such a grotesque, distasteful, and ham-fisted way, relying on simply shocking the audience. This annihilated all of the artistic beauty in the film.

Watching this movie is akin to observing a world-class fine art painter creating a delicate master-piece using the gentlest of strokes, only to take a huge bucket of old paint and splashing it across the canvas, just to prove a point.

Perhaps the movie is also a commentary on the audiences of our time, given the high ratings, as it feels as if to get through to people - we need to scream, shout, shock and disturb them.

It feels as if creating the art of delicate meaning will simply not get appreciated. The music industry gets louder, faster and more bizzare. The art industry - more abstract, more colourful, more shocking. So do movies such as this one, where we lose the art of storytelling, subtlety and care.

Is this still art? Sure. It created emotions, it created hate, disgust, disappointment. It moved me to write a review for the first time in a decade. It made me scream and shout about the state of our society. It made me complain to friends and family. It made me act.

Is this the kind of art we want in our world? Should this be the only kind of art that is able to make us move? That is up to you, but I will go and try to rekindle my love for the classics.

reviews.author: forgiven1
reviews.body: I saw the trailer and I knew I wanted to see it. As I am watching it, I too was thinking enough with the butt shots. It was unnecessary after like the 4th time. There were a few scenes that were disturbing, but still had new liking it. Then the last 30 or so minutes, was just stupid!! It was disgusting and very unrealistic. It had a good point and could be applied to real life, but then they ruined it with the ending. The writers could have written it with the same intensity, without the ridiculousness of it. Could have had somr ending to realize that all the hype of being skinny or beautiful is not worth going through all that. The fact is we all age and get old, so teach us how to do it gracefully and accept the changes that happen. So disappointed!! Waste of time.

reviews.author: scarey91457
reviews.body: I'm sorry I spent the $ to buy this after all the hype. I was expecting some real scares but got NONE! If you get squeamish over what amounts to Hollywood puppetry, than this will work for you, but this was a real let down for me. That being said, it did give some thought into what lengths some people will go to in order to regain what they have lost to the natural aging process and most find that in the long run, it only makes things worse. You see that every day with women who have become botox junkies and their faces wind up looking like a bad comedic caricature of their original selves. BAD!

reviews.author: gdleonq
reviews.body: Okay, let's get to the good stuff. The movie started off incredibly strong-the beginning was one of the best I've seen in a while! I was completely hooked, as everything fell perfectly into place with a seamless blend of drama and thriller. It had all the makings of a masterpiece, and for most of its runtime, it delivered. But then, the last 30 minutes happened-a complete disaster. It felt rushed and nonsensical, like you ran out of ideas and started improvising. The film overstayed its welcome, and those final moments ruined what could've been a 10/10 experience. If it had ended sooner, I would've loved it. As it stands? A 2/10.

reviews.author: hitman_1980
reviews.body: I can't explain how dissapointed I felt at the end of this movie, it started out strong and had so much potential! The leading actresses are great, the cinematography and pacing outstanding, but then all of a sudden it al goes downhill. But not just downhill, it sinks to unimaginable levels of bad taste. I get the message and the point it struggled to make, but the final 30 minutes are simply bad and unwatchable at times. I really thought I'd recommend this but it took me from enthusiasm to plain disgust. The final act is simply unexcusable and turns the entire experience into one you'll basically find yourself struggling to forget, and I don't mean that in a good way. Avoid.

reviews.author: davewaughwaugh
reviews.body: This movie is awful. How anyone gives this a 10 is beyond me. If it wasn't for the nudity it would be a total waste of time. It drags on far too long. Do not watch under any circumstance. I wish I had never wasted my time watching this pile of garbage. If only I had an alter person that I could make it watch for me. I'm only writing this review to try and warn other people but I have to use 200 more characters. Do not watch this film. Please do not watch this film. If me watching this has done anything it is to help you avoid watching this garbage. Do not watch this. Do not watch this. For the love of god do not watch.

reviews.author: paulcoman
reviews.body:
"The Substance" clearly tries to channel Quentin Tarantino's unique style, with its over-the-top bloody scenes and moments of absurdity.

However, where Tarantino masterfully blends violence, wit, and storytelling to create movies full of substance and flavor, this film lacks the same magic in execution.

It feels like an imitation without the soul, struggling to capture the depth or cleverness that makes Tarantino's work so compelling.

Ultimately, it comes across as a hollow effort... a poor man's version of the real thing, missing the charm, energy, and finesse that could have made it stand out.

reviews.author: timkwarcinski
reviews.body:
The first two acts of the film are 7.5/10. I thought it had a distinctive flair in terms of the lighting, colors, set design that created a cohesiveness that was on theme. Bright colors, shiny colors, modern set design all had verve and energy that screamed youth and vitality, which is an underlying theme in the movie of course. It was slightly too self-aware of itself at some points, like during calls between the manufacturer of the substance and the lead character--something in the dialoge just felt a bit too much like a cheesy scene from a bad Bond movie.

Then, in the 3rd act, the whole thing falls apart. It's a shame because the movie could have been one of the best of the year for me.

reviews.author: xxmelmothx
reviews.body: I would suggest watching the first 20 minutes and see how good Demi and Denis are...then stop. This film is too long, it could have been a short. The concept is interesting and the points taken but it doesn't know if it wants to be a horror, comedy, serious of funny. Should I be "Basket Case" (movie), should I be "Dead/Alive" (movie), can I be a Cronenberg film? It tries way too hard even though it says the basic points in the first hour or less. Then it breaks it's own story rules and rides off the handles for another half an hour trying to be shocking. One other thing.....the fight scene....did we then try to be an over done action film at one point? I will not explain specifics because I don't want to make any spoilers.

reviews.author: johnebailor
reviews.body: This movie started off strong and was very interesting for the first half of so. The last act really turned me off with enough body horror to make David Cronenberg sick. To justify my purchase of this movie I'm going to believe we have enough clues to assume this was all in Elizabeth's mind after she injected herself with The Substance. Although the movie appears to want you to believe these events all occurred, there are some specific reasons I will continue on with my theory. First, I can't imagine what would happen to someone's eyes if they stay open for seven days. Second, the character appears to hear dialogue that she wasn't there for. Third there is a superhuman kick in a fight late in the movie. Definitely not a movie for the squeamish. I'd skip it due to the third act, but maybe that is why some like this movie?

reviews.author: juxxxlio
reviews.body:
I love Demi Moore with all my soul, I really wanted to support her in this movie but I didn't like it. The beginning is actually good... But after 30 minutes everything starts to go wrong. Disheartening to think about what this film and this idea could have become, I can't even express my disappointment.

It's unbelievable that the film was directed and written by a woman, Margaret was extremely sexualized the whole time. It seems that the film that was supposed to criticize aesthetic standards was more of a fan service for the unbelievers to see a female body being exposed for free. It's like, let's give men and lesbians what they want: hypersexualization.

reviews.author: joannakarolinalaszczak
reviews.body:
I really got bored pretty quickly, but for once I did not fell asleep in the cinema... Mostly because of the drill sound used as soundtrack.

Huge part of it looks like 'Call on me' clip and I do fully understand why. Highlighting the youth and body cult in opposition to aging, by this also loosing your value, was pretty literal and predictable.

I loved the yellow coat and the way it morphed it's usage purpose trough the timeline. From 'Look at me' statement, then 'hide in' cape, to beggars layer in the end.

But tbh I was kinda disappointed with the finale. While most part of the movie looked like peak into the 'Shinning' , the end was more like 'Brain-dead'.

reviews.author: davy-31708
reviews.body:
Although I praise the film for camera work, special effects and great sound and music it lacks in some vital areas.

The characters have zero personality and zero story, which might be intentional but in a movie this long it gets kind of boring. They never try to develop the characters either.

The plot is presented in the first 30 minutes and then it's just not really going anywhere in my opinion. Of course things escalate but the story is not going anywhere. You don't really get a lot of answers here.

The ending was interesting but a little too much and disappointing. Same here, no twists, no answers, no conclusions. Just a violent escalation.

Maybe I had a hard time for this film mainly because it tries to hard to make a point. In this case about beauty, showbiz and vanity. It stomps this message in to your brain over and over again and don't really care for anything else.

I left the theatre with a bit of the same feeling as after seeing "don't look up". A great film that was also stomping in the message a little too hard.

reviews.author: onur-buyukceran
reviews.body:
"The Substance" had a lot going for it, but unfortunately, it lost its way by the end. Demi Moore's performance was easily the highlight-possibly her best ever. I never considered her a particularly talented actress before, but she completely changed my mind with this role. Her portrayal was gripping, and she carried the movie in a way I didn't expect.

The movie had some really creative ideas, especially in how "the substance" works to create a "better version" of a person. It was weird, but in a fascinating way. I also appreciated how the film subtly convinced me that aging isn't something to be feared. The focus on greed and how far people will go for fame, youth, or success was well-executed, with plenty of suspenseful moments and twists to keep you on your toes.

However, things took a downturn towards the end. While the first half had the makings of a solid psychological thriller, the conclusion devolved into a bizarre, blood-filled mess. It felt like the film shifted from being thought-provoking to simply aiming for shock value. The excessive blood and gruesome scenes didn't add much to the story, and the final moments felt over the top-almost like they lost the plot. It could've been so much better if it had stayed focused on the psychological thriller aspects instead of diving into a bloodlust-driven climax.

By the end, the movie started discussing something entirely offbeat, which threw me off. Had they kept it more grounded, I might have rated it higher. As it stands, my score is 5/10. It had potential, but the ending just took it too far.

reviews.author: manos_paterakis
reviews.body:
This one's gotta be split into two parts.

First, a totally nonsensical sci-fi conception that's a mockery to the genre ("Severance" is a good example of a self-against-self story making actual sense), full of plot holes. It also thinks it's dropping truth bombs about shallow people-big deal.

Then, out of nowhere, we get this gloriously grotesque, almost poetic climax with Anna von Hausswolff's "Ugly and Vengeful" (fitting name, right?) from her 2018 album, which almost saves the day.

P. S.: All those paranoic wide-lens nods to Terry Gilliam and Jean-Pierre Jeunet are a nice touch, rarely encountered these days.

reviews.author: fredniang
reviews.body: Great topic. Very contemporary and relevant to our western societies. Great acting from Demi Moore, who gives a great partition in a role rhar makes me think she should have had better characters to play in her career. However, this film is way too long. 1:45 minutes would have been more than enough. 2 and half hours is VERY LONG, especially the last hour which does not bring anything to the story or its characters. Think Requiem for a Dream. Was this over 2 hours? Probably not. Gore scenes should either be fun, scary or provoke an emotion. Disgust is not one of them. I gave it a 5, but it could have been a 7 with better editing.

reviews.author: farbodderawz
reviews.body:
The movie revolves around the main character, Elizabeth, as she comes to realize that with aging, a sudden existential threat of losing her identity befalls her. This feeling of being rejected for the natural behavior of her body, puts Elizabeth in a dreadful situation of having to accept her fate or use an anonymously recommended drug that offers the promise of a better life, but at a very high cost.

Overall, the movie has an interesting plot but fails to harmonize the themes of the movie and feels a bit scattered as a whole.

On a more serious concern, it seems to rely on unnecessary eroticism to gain viewership since this amount of erotic scenes seem futile when they could have been replaced by scenes that help better communicate the plot.

Small details in the movie weren't thought for and created gaps in the viewers mind.

The visual considerations of this movie are more acceptable and seem to be well thought for. A cold and harsh living environment that is complemented by excellent lighting helps convey the absurd conditions of Elizabeth's life.

The CGI was also helpful in giving the audience something to look forward to.

reviews.author: cassidyleelawrence
reviews.body:
Pros:

Okay first off, This was a very intriguing movie.

It was defiantly a "horror movie" in the sense it will keep you up at night.

Great actors and acting (all relatively well known) In addition, Very interesting almost in the moment theatrical camera views.

If you like strange total mind bending movies, this one's for you!




I don't regret watching it but I did not Love It.

It had a great story line and it does keep you watching for more.

Cons:

reviews.author: matthewshribmanimdb
reviews.body: It's really quite miserable to watch over 2 hours of someone who hates themselves so much / sees no worth in living if they're not beautiful. The endless close-ups of sexy humans are surprisingly boring, because they over-play the license of the narrative and so generally feel gratuitous and lacking in purpose. The portrayal of Harvey, the studio boss, is good - well script, well acted. But besides that, there isn't much by way of engaging story. It's just shock-value meted out as disturbing sounds and general gore. The cinematography, grading, costumes, set-design, sound engineering etc. Are all good, but wasted on a topic that lacks subtly or substance. If you're someone who likes to think, this probably isn't for you.

reviews.author: fabio_tamayo
reviews.body: It could be a Black Mirror episode and it would certainly be good, but just one more. For a feature-length film it is basic. Surely some will say that it is intellectual, even philosophical and a work of art, but it is a disgusting film. I feel like it is a modern copy of the Portrait of Dorian Gray, The Wild Ass's Skin or The Devil in the Bottle, but extremely poorly done, a fraud. Nothing new, where the subject is addressed in an extremely predictable way and also contains a lot of filler, especially at the end where it is exaggeratedly prolonged, repeating the subject that has been made clear in the first 30 minutes. Not recommended.

reviews.author: elmoutesidi
reviews.body: Tarantino but for butts. It starts off so well, it's obviously a metaphor BUT boy oh boy that ending was bad. Clever to a point but it went way to much. I don't care that it was gory, that's it's genre, but there was no logic way to end it or they simply didn't know how to end it and did what they did instead.... This is a movie about butts and boobs. And full frontal nudity obv by both protagonists... That is all... What kind of prime time 9pm new years eve show has boobs put???? Honestly the last 15 mins or so just don't watch it or do so at your own risk of seeing something more weird of an ending than from dusk till dawn. Extremely Tarantino-sequel but failed to capture the meaning behind it...

reviews.author: joao_m_neto
reviews.body:
...possessed someone to allow for this aberration to be shown to people?!??!?!??!?!!?

What was this woman (the director) thinking?!??!?!??!

What was she on?!?!?!?!?!?!

My guess is that the lady got really drunk (or high... OR BOTH!!!!!), then binge watched "The Elephant Man", the opening scene of "Blade", "Alien" and "Kill Bill", and the day after, suffering from a massive hungover (or stroke... OR BOTH), regurgitated this... I don't even know how to call it, in order to avoid censorship (it happened 3 or 4 times already).

Dennis Quaid is BRILLIANT for what the part demanded (apparently it was going to be Ray Liotta, but God rest his Soul), he passed away before. The change was for better, I think.

Demi Moore plays, in my opinion, a very sober and vulnerable part (that's what she called it in some statement, and I agree). She looks stunning for her age, and she was very brave to appear this bare on camera (assuming it's her body, and there is no photoshop).

The idea is not bad, but the movie becomes so unnecessarily gore, extremely gross and visually unbearable at times...

This is just plain nonsense...

reviews.author: sabasgr-26959
reviews.body:
Despite all, I liked the visual effects of body transformation, needle shots and the such, sometimes I actually didn't want to watch and I usually am not affected with those scenes, I actually like "good" scenes like those, but some of them on this film were a little over the top, meaning, they worked fine!

The plot, as I see it, is basically how alienated are people with the good looking appearance and trying to look "young" even if they are well in their 70s or 80s, no matter the final cost. Botox and implants are the curse of this century. Media industry is almost sick.

What I really dislike was the excesive nudity here. Really, nude/sex scenes are 100% unnecesary in movies. And the too "up and close" camera takes on butts and boobs were really annoying, even if they were intended to show that it is what most "media consumers" want to watch. I actually turned my head many times because I didn't really wanted to see Moore and Quayle naked. Remember, before artists, they are persons, they are daughters, sisters, mothers, aunts; they are coworkers, they are clients, they are public persons, and they, or we, or people in general don't go around naked to work and do errands, right? So, why is it "ok" that they have to make nude or sex scenes for a movie? There´s really no need for that, IMHO.

The final part of the movie is way over the top, but I think I got the message, or better, the picture they wanted to show to the show industry and people. But maybe I'm wrong, who knows?

reviews.author: jasmanie
reviews.body:
The plot is fairly simple and clever but the movie dragged on with long scenes of nude actresses staring at themselves in a mirror for far too long.

The movie make some clear messages about how we prioritize beauty and youth and tend to undervalue women as they age. It also takes a clear shot at people who still decide to play the game and will literally eat each other alive (and themselves apparently) to stay on top.

The final scenes of the movie, the whole thing jumps the shark and descends into a mashup of the Elephant Man meets Carrie. It was complete mess and pointless and you won't be able to stop watching as your brain tries to process what it is seeing.

Cult classic material - maybe. I'm still trying to process this one. Don't think I could sit through a full watching again however.

reviews.author: winkhugkiss
reviews.body: I'm pretty tolerant and open minded when it comes to art, literature and film but this one was super disappointing in the end. It starts great and I love Moore's performance. Demi earned her award. Something about her performance reminds me of Glen Close in her more mature roles. Both actresses carried their roles well it's just too bad they had such a ridiculous ending to work with. The movie has such a strong, emotional, sobering message about societies view of beauty and aging. It also revolves around how far one will go and the risks they will take to be accepted. Unfortunately it turns a little cartoonish. I would still recommend it but prepare for a very different kind of ending.

reviews.author: francinecoleman
reviews.body: "The Substance is the worst movie I've ever seen. It revolves around two deeply unlikable characters caught in a bizarre, toxic dynamic that leads absolutely nowhere. The film heavily sexualizes the actress, reducing her to an object rather than a meaningful character, while grotesque and gratuitous scenes are included purely for shock value, failing to add anything substantial to the narrative. The story is shallow and uncomfortable, lacking depth or purpose, and ultimately feels like a pretentious waste of time and talent. Offering nothing of value, it ironically lives up to its title. Avoid this film at all costs."

reviews.author: TopReviewer
reviews.body:
The general premise of the movie is good. An aging Demi Moore wanting to retain her youthful look, since she's at a more advanced age.

I think Demi was the best part of the movie and legitimately out-acted everyone else. It was almost like the rest didn't belong in the same movie as her.

The move has a nice balance of reality, slap-stick humour, horror & extreme horror. The reality mixed with subtle horror was fantastic. Unfortunately, the slap stick humour and extreme horror cuts were forced and really took away from this being a GREAT movie.

It felt like the writers didn't know how to end the movie and just made it silly at the end. It doesn't need to be over 2 hours long.

Film is good and worth a watch yes, but is NOT and should NOT be a high rating film alongside legit classics. I gave it a 5, but a 4+ would have been enough.

reviews.author: katiekatelady
reviews.body: Ok, I'm not really sure what I just watched? The movie started off interestingly enough and I was really hoping that the plot would continue to deepen...but then it all took a very odd turn (to say the least) It was entertaining on some levels, and I found that I couldn't stop watching it. I am not sure if that is because of my disbelief in where the movie was headed, or the fact that it was this bad, that they had to go there? I am pretty sure it could have had a much better ending that didn't include the obscene amount of blood??? I didn't read any reviews before watching this movie, possibly I would have had a different expectation. Enjoy!

reviews.author: lwugoqc
reviews.body:
The Substance is nothing short of a cinematic revelation. From its opening moments, the film grips you with its stunning visuals and masterful storytelling, taking you on an emotional journey that lingers long after the credits roll.

The film seamlessly blends drama, suspense, and thought-provoking themes, crafting a narrative that feels both intimate and universal. The characters are richly developed, with performances so raw and authentic that you can't help but feel deeply connected to their struggles and triumphs. The lead actors deliver powerhouse performances, carrying the weight of the film with incredible nuance and charisma.

The direction is a standout, with every frame meticulously crafted to enhance the story's emotional resonance. The cinematography is breathtaking, with a palette and composition that draw you deeper into the world of the film. The score is equally haunting and beautiful, perfectly complementing the film's tone and elevating its most poignant moments.

What truly sets The Substance apart is its ability to challenge and engage the audience. It's a film that doesn't just entertain-it makes you think, feel, and question. This is a movie for anyone who appreciates storytelling at its finest, a rare gem in today's cinematic landscape.

Bravo to the entire cast and crew for delivering such a profound and unforgettable experience. The Substance is a film that deserves to be celebrated and remembered as one of the most remarkable achievements in modern cinema.
